Title: KINETIC MODELING OF CHLORANTRANILIPROLE AND LAMBDA-CYHALOTHRIN IN NON-FLOODED SOIL SYSTEMS USING GC-MS/ MS
Abstract: A pot culture experiment evaluated the dissipation kinetics and ecological risk of a ready-mix formulation of chlorantraniliprole (9.30%) + lambda-cyhalothrin (4.60%) ZC in sandy loam soil under controlled non-flooded conditions. Soil residues (0-10 cm) were monitored up to 90 days using GC-MS/ MS. QuEChERS outperformed MSPD, giving >85% recoveries. Both pesticides dissipated via first-order kinetics (R2 >0.97), with half-lives of 1.65-2.84 days (chlorantraniliprole) and 2.47-4.52 days (lambda-cyhalothrin). Residues persisted up to 60 and 45 days, respectively, depending on dose levels. Initial RQ values for Eisenia fetida (>1) indicated high risk but decreased to <0.1 as residues degraded. Overall, the study reveals rapid dissipation, short-lived ecological risk, and provides essential data for environmental safety evaluation and optimized pesticide application strategies. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. Authors: Miao W.; Shang T.; Wen Y.; Ye C.; Zhang C.; Qiu C.; Jin Z.; Quek S.Y.
Title: Engineering dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes for enhanced astaxanthin stability: Effects of beeswax and β-sitosterol crystal networks
Abstract: To improve the stability of emulsion-templated oleogels and enhance astaxanthin protection, dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes (OS/CS) were fabricated by incorporating crystalline networks formed by beeswax or β-sitosterol. The effects of different crystalline networks on the microstructure, stability, and astaxanthin retention of OS/CS oleogels were systematically investigated. The incorporation of both crystalline networks significantly (p < 0.05) enhanced the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels under various processing and storage conditions, with beeswax exhibiting the most pronounced improvement. After storage at 25 °C for 56 days, astaxanthin degradation was observed in all oleogel samples; however, the OS/CS oleogels containing 6% beeswax or β-sitosterol showed relatively lower astaxanthin degradation of 19.32% and 21.05%, respectively. In vitro digestion revealed that astaxanthin bioaccessibility in the dual-network oleogels (23.92-43.04%) was higher than that of bulk oil (20.97%). Overall, beeswax exhibited superior synergistic effects in promoting the formation of a dense dual-network structure and enhancing the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving oleogel stability and astaxanthin retention. Authors: Yan R.; Zhu X.; Dong Q.; Zhang M.; Yin Z.; Zhao Z.; Chen X.
Title: Industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis for intelligent maintenance: A review of data, methods, and emerging trends
Abstract: Industrial robots are widely used in intelligent manufacturing due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and repeatability. However, long-term operation under complex working conditions inevitably leads to performance degradation and various faults across mechanical, transmission, and electrical subsystems. Owing to the structural complexity of industrial robots, strong coupling among subsystems, and heterogeneous monitoring data, fault detection and diagnosis has become a challenging yet crucial task for ensuring system reliability and enabling intelligent maintenance. Despite considerable progress, existing studies remain fragmented across different robot subsystems, data modalities, and diagnostic paradigms, and a systematic review dedicated to industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis is still lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a comprehensive and structured review from three complementary perspectives: fault characteristics and data resources, diagnostic methodologies, and emerging trends. Specifically, the review summarizes typical fault types and data acquisition strategies, organizes existing diagnostic methods into a structured taxonomy, and discusses key challenges and emerging directions such as multimodal fusion, trustworthy deployment, and digital-twin-driven diagnosis. This review provides a structured reference for advancing both theoretical research and engineering applications of industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis in intelligent manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Lattice-electron dual regulation enhances oxygen-redox reversibility and structural stability in cobalt-free lithium-rich manganese-based cathodes
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The cobalt-free lithium-rich manganese-based cathode (LMNO) has attracted much attention due to its high specific capacity, low cost, and environmental friendliness. However, irreversible oxygen loss and transition-metal migration hinder their practical deployment. Herein, a lattice–electron dual-regulation strategy based on Na/Y co-doping was introduced to modify LMNO cathode materials. Theoretical and experimental results confirm that Y doping reduces the Mott-Hubbard splitting energy (U) and irreversible oxygen loss. Furthermore, the Na/Y co-doping optimizes the lattice structure, improving the transport kinetics of Li+ while enhancing the stability of the material structure. The modified cathode achieved an excellent capacity of 302 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and 2–4.8 V (compared to 268 mAh g−1 for pristine). After 200 cycles at 1 C, the modified material retains 90% of its capacity, with a voltage drop of 0.34 V (compared to 55% and 0.50 V for Pristine). This strategy provides a new approach for regulating oxygen redox behavior and enhancing structural stability. © 2026

Authors: Mao Z.; Liu J.; An K.; Zhang Y.; Shi X.; Yang X.; Lin X.; Xu J.; Shao L.; Hang L.; Li P.; Sun Z.
Title: Breaking the limitations of ZnSe anodes: Boosting sodium-ion kinetics via electronic structure regulation and morphology design
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Transition metal selenides have garnered considerable attention as promising anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their practical application is hindered by intrinsically low conductivity and sluggish conversion kinetics originating from strong metal-selenide bonds. Herein, we propose an innovative electronic structure modulation strategy to overcome these limitations by doping Cu into ZnSe particles anchored within a hierarchical porous N-doped carbon (NC). Experimental results and density functional theory calculations reveal that Cu doping induces charge redistribution, narrows the bandgap, and elongates the Zn-Se bond, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier for the conversion reaction. Moreover, the NC framework and Cu-induced morphological optimization accommodate volume expansion and promote electrolyte penetration, enhancing cycling stability. Kinetic analyses reveal a dominant pseudocapacitive contribution and reduced charge transfer impedance. Hence, the optimized Cu2-ZnSe@NC delivers exceptional rate capability (240.3 mAh g–1 at 30 A g–1) and outstanding cycling stability (389.5 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 2 A g–1 with a capacity retention of 82.9%). In full-cell evaluation, the device maintains stable electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from −20 to 25 °C, highlighting its potential for practical applications. This work establishes a structure-property paradigm in which heteroatom doping weakens metal-chalcogenide bonds, offering a generalizable design principle for high-performance conversion-type anodes. © 2026

Authors: Benkhira E.L.H.; Yamouni O.E.; Fakhar R.; Mandyly Y.
Author full names: Benkhira, EL Hassan (44460930300); Yamouni, Ouiame El (59780942300); Fakhar, Rachid (44461128300); Mandyly, Youssef (57208573772)
Title: Mixed double-hemivariational analysis of piezoelectric contact with multiplier-coupled nonmonotone friction
Abstract: We introduce and analyze a static piezoelectric contact model for Hencky-type materials in which the nonsmooth interface response depends on the tangential displacement, the electric potential jump, and a regularized representation of the normal contact reaction through the Lagrange multiplier. This yields a genuinely multiplier-dependent double nonsmooth coupling on the contact boundary. The model is formulated as a mixed problem in which a Lagrange multiplier is associated with the unilateral Signorini-type contact constraint and, through its regularized representation, also enters the nonsmooth interface response. The resulting boundary functional is expressed in hemivariational form through Clarke’s generalized directional derivative with respect to both the primal interface variables and the regularized multiplier variable. Under standard assumptions on the constitutive operators and suitable growth, compactness, and upper semicontinuity conditions on the coupled superpotential, we prove the existence of weak solutions. The proof combines a truncation procedure, a Fan–KKM argument with a Minty-type reformulation, a uniform multiplier estimate based on an inf–sup property for the normal trace, and a weak compactness argument. We also establish a sequential stability result showing the robustness of weak solutions under perturbations of the loadings and of the foundation data. Finally, a numerical illustration is provided to highlight the influence of the regularized normal reaction on the effective frictional and electrical interface responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Layered Defect-Filling co-Assembled Carbazole-Based SAMs Deliver 20% Organic Solar Cells and 17% Mini-Modules
Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-transport layers (HTLs) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet conventional single-component SAMs often form quasi-monolayers with incomplete coverage and interfacial defects that become increasingly detrimental upon device scaling. Here, we develop a co-assembled multilayered SAM (coSAMu) strategy that combines two SAM molecules, 2PACz and 2Cl-4PACz, with distinct dipoles and steric configurations through blend casting and sequential casting. Photoelectron spectroscopy, X-ray analysis, and molecular simulations support a layered structure in which a chemisorbed, 2PACz-rich bottom layer primarily sets the indium tin oxide (ITO) work function, while a 2Cl-4PACz-rich upper layer fills interfacial voids, improves molecular packing, and passivates defects. Consistent with this picture, coSAMu promotes a more favorable vertical composition near the ITO surface and suppresses trap-assisted recombination, enabling more efficient charge extraction and collection. Consequently, a representative D18:L8-BO OSC incorporating the sequential-cast coSAMu HTL achieves a power conversion efficiency of 20.1% (0.042 cm2), outperforming pristine 2PACz. Importantly, when scaled to a 17.14 cm2 mini-module (six serially connected subcells), coSAMu delivers 17.0% efficiency versus 12.2% for the 2PACz control. This work demonstrates controlled multilayer co-assembly as an effective strategy for scalable OSC interface engineering that is broadly applicable to multiple donor–acceptor systems. Title: Comparative Analysis of Mathematical Models of Drilling in Heterogeneous Geological Sections; [Біртекті емес геологиялық учаскелерде бұрғылаудың математикалық модельдерін салыстырмалы талдау]
Abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of four main types of well drilling models in heterogeneous geological sections: mechanical-mathematical, energy, kinematic, and empirical. It is shown that each group of models focuses on different aspects of the process: the physics of bitrock interaction (mechanical-mathematical approach), the energy efficiency of rock mass destruction (energy), the trajectory and movement of the tool (kinematic), as well as statistical patterns and the prediction of complications (empirical). The interaction between the bit and the rock is considered depending on their physical and mechanical properties. A comparison of the rotation speed of the rotor and bit is provided depending on the rock hardness. Based on a review of modern publications and the practical experience of leading service companies (Equinor, Schlumberger, Halliburton), the strengths and weaknesses of each approach are identified, and the need for their integration is substantiated. It is established that the integrated use of models of different classes allows not only to describe and explain phenomena but also to manage the drilling process in conditions of high geological variability. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Authors: Li H.; Chen Y.; Wang D.; Qi W.; Zhang Y.; Lu J.
Title: Atomic coordination engineering for overcoming the selectivity-durability tradeoff of carbon-encapsulated metals towards sustainable wastewater purification
Abstract: Breaking the selectivity-durability tradeoff of carbon-encapsulated cobalt/peroxymonosulfate (C-Co/PMS) remains challenging. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) derived from C-Co/PMS shows high selectivity toward electron-rich pollutants, it is readily quenched by water, which impairs catalytic durability during repeated operation. Herein, we rationally construct copper single atoms on C-Co (CuSA-C-Co) to trigger the formation of additional high-valent copper-oxo species (Cu(III)-OH) during PMS activation, which compensates for the intrinsic defect of sole 1O2, overcoming this critical tradeoff. On Co sites, adsorbed PMS undergoes O-H dissociation to form peroxomonosulfate radical (*SO5•-), which self-disproportionates into 1O2. Meanwhile, strong orbital hybridization between the Cu 3d orbital of CuSA and the O 2p orbitals of PMS induces heterolytic cleavage of peroxide O-O bonds, facilitating oxygen atom transfer to generate Cu(III)-OH. Benefiting from these complementary oxidation pathways, CuSA-C-Co/PMS retains high selectivity toward electron-rich pollutants while achieving catalytic durability during repeated cycling compared with pristine C-Co/PMS. Beyond the sole 1O2-mediated mineralization of bisphenol A (BPA), Cu(III)-OH converts BPA into oligomers via proton-coupled electron transfer, and these oligomers spontaneously accumulate on the CuSA-C-Co surface, which simplifies subsequent water treatment. Continuous treatment of BPA-containing wastewater over 240 h shows that the CuSA-C-Co/polyvinylidene fluoride/PMS system sustains > 91.4% BPA removal. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Feng W.; Fang Y.; Zhang S.; Xiao Y.; Zhang J.
Title: Thermal stress mitigation via synergistic dual-interface reconstruction in Si3N4/Cu joints
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Severe thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) mismatch in brazed Si3N4/Cu joints frequently induces interfacial stress concentration and ceramic cracking. Herein, a (Cu20Sn)100−xTix/Nb/Ti multilayer composite filler is proposed to achieve dual-interface reconstruction by simultaneously tailoring the Si3N4 and Nb interfaces, thereby synergistically regulating residual stress distribution within the joint. At the Si3N4 interface, the filler constructs a Si3N4/TiN/Cu6−xTixO+(Nb, Ti)5Si3 architecture, establishing a smoothed CTE gradient and relieving interfacial stress. At the Nb interface, Nb-Sn interactions generate a hierarchical architecture comprising a continuous basal layer and micron-submicron (Nb, Ti)3Sn particle band. Thermodynamic and kinetic analyses reveal that restricted Ti activity allows Nb-Sn/Nb-Si reactions to dominate, wherein (Nb, Ti)3Sn growth obeys a parabolic law governed by a transition from reaction-diffusion to dissolution-precipitation mechanism. First-principles calculations demonstrate that strong Cu-3d/Nb-4d orbital hybridization endows the Cu(111)/(Nb)Nb3Sn(111) interface with excellent interfacial adhesion to establish reliable metallurgical bonding. The in-situ (Nb, Ti)3Sn/Nb composite serves as a stress buffer to mitigate the von Mises equivalent stress near the Si3N4 interface. Driven by the dual-interfacial strategy, the joint achieves a maximum shear strength of 163.2 MPa under optimal brazing conditions (930 °C, 5wt.% Ti). The fracture path migrates from the Si3N4 interface to the (Nb, Ti)3Sn particle band, which confirms effective stress redistribution and improved joint reliability. This dual-interface reconstruction strategy may provide a general approach to residual-stress mitigation in ceramic/metal joints with severe thermophysical mismatches. © 2026

Authors: Li D.; Xu H.; Cao G.; Liu F.; Ban J.; Zhang S.; Fan L.-Z.; Hu J.
Title: High-Conductivity and Moisture-Tolerant Sulfide Electrolyte Enabled by Bifunctional Coating for Practical All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
Abstract: The pursuit of safer and higher-energy-density batteries has driven the advancement of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Among various material systems, sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SEs) stand out as highly promising candidates owing to their exceptional ionic conductivity. Nevertheless, their extreme sensitivity to moisture results in the release of toxic H2S and rapid structural degradation, which severely impedes their scalable manufacturing under ambient conditions. A bifunctional (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) coating strategy is herein presented to shield Li5.5PS4.5Cl0.8Br0.7 (LPSCBr) from moisture-induced degradation. The MPTMS layer forms a hydrophobic barrier of approximately 10 nm, which reduces H2S emission by 93.0% after 35 min of exposure to 30% relative humidity, while maintaining 83.1% of the initial ionic conductivity (10.8 mS cm−1). This approach tackles the core challenge associated with sulfide solid-state electrolytes: the realization of compatibility with controlled ambient air without sacrificing critical electrochemical properties. The modified electrolyte maintains a high ionic conductivity (> 5.7 mS cm−1) even after 10 h of air exposure. When applied in all-solid-state cells paired with LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.06O2 cathodes, it exhibits remarkable electrochemical performance, delivering a capacity retention of 84.6% after 1000 cycles. By enabling moisture-tolerant processing, MPTMS-modified LPSCBr SEs lay a solid foundation for the scalable, high-performance, and cost-effective production of ASSLBs. Title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, legality, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Multiphase synergistic strategy enabling flexible ceramic fibers with electromagnetic stealth capability for thermal protection up to 2000 °C
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Next-generation aerospace vehicles demand thermal protection materials that can withstand aerodynamic heating achieving 2000 °C, while concurrently maintaining structural flexibility and electromagnetic stealth capabilities—a synergistic performance portfolio that remains largely unattainable with conventional ceramic materials. To address this exigent requirement, flexible multiphase SiC-ZrC-C fibers are designed and fabricated in this work. In situ-formed ZrC nanoparticles preferentially nucleate at SiC grain boundaries and act as pinning phases, suppressing SiC grain coarsening at ultrahigh temperature, while the continuous porous carbon scaffold accommodates mechanical deformation. The resultant fibers demonstrate exceptional thermal stability, characterized by phase stability following exposure at 1600 °C for 50 h, as well as retained flexibility even after annealing at 2000 °C for 1 h in an Ar atmosphere. Concurrently, the fibers exhibit potent electromagnetic wave absorption capabilities, achieving a minimum reflection loss of −52.60 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 5.56 GHz. Besides, continuous fabrication yields large-area fibrous membranes, highlighting the feasibility of large-scale production. The results of this work provide new insights into the design and development of structure-function-integrated thermal protection materials for extreme environments. © 2026

Authors: Duan T.; Ye L.; Zou G.; Li J.; Peng S.; Bian B.; Hou L.; Liu Y.
Title: Achieving exceptional superplasticity in Al0.5CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloy via partial recrystallization-induced heterostructure
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Heterogeneous microstructures are generally considered detrimental to uniform superplastic deformation. However, a partial recrystallization behavior is observed in the Al0.5CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloy, leading to the formation of a heterostructure—comprising both fully recrystallized and retained unrecrystallized regions—following annealing at 800 °C. This heterostructure achieves an exceptional elongation of 1720% under deformation conditions of 1000 °C and 0.005 s−1. In this heterostructure, the recrystallized regions rapidly accommodate superplastic deformation at the initial stage, promoting uniform superplastic flow. Meanwhile, the stored strain energy in the unrecrystallized regions is released during superplastic deformation, activating dynamic recrystallization and further refining the grains. The refined grains, in turn, better accommodate grain boundary sliding. Consequently, the alloy with an initial heterostructure maintains a high strain rate sensitivity (m value) throughout the superplastic deformation process, enabling uniform superplastic deformation and ultimately achieving significantly higher elongation than that of the initial banded-grained structure and the initial equiaxed-grained structure. © 2026

Title: Template-induced assembly and in situ polymerization for constructing uniformly distributed molybdate-secondary-doped polyaniline toward self-passivating and self-healing epoxy coatings
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Conductive polymer coatings show great promise for the passivation protection of metals. However, the aggregation of conductive polymers and the gradual deterioration of electrochemical activity still limit their long-term protection in harsh marine environments. In this study, plasma-modified basalt (MB) scales were employed as two-dimensional (2D) templates for the induced assembly and in situ polymerization of aniline (ANI), followed by secondary doping with molybdate ions (MoO42−). The resulting P-Mo/MB filler was incorporated into an epoxy (EP) resin to construct a multifunctional coating for Al alloys. The uniformly distributed polyaniline (PANI) improves filler dispersion within the EP resin, increases the accessibility of redox-active sites, and helps alleviate localized electric field concentration. Additionally, MoO42− secondary doping enhances the electrochemical cycling stability of PANI and enables pH-responsive release of the inhibitor. The P-Mo/MB/EP coating maintains a |Z|0.01 Hz value of 2.46 × 1010 Ω cm2 after 150 days of immersion, approximately 10 times that of the MB/EP coating. Surface and cross-sectional analyses reveal the formation of a compact protective film with a thickness of approximately 450 nm on the Al alloy surface. Moreover, no obvious corrosion is observed in the scratched area of the P-Mo/MB/EP coating after 120 h, accompanied by the gradual formation of a continuous protective film. These results demonstrate that the synergistic integration of physical shielding, self-passivation, and self-healing provides an effective strategy for developing long-term multifunctional anti-corrosion coatings. © 2026

Title: Fracture propagation law of shale rocks using pre-fracturing technology with supercritical CO2 fluids of different volumes
Abstract: Shale reservoirs are intrinsically tight, and conventional fracturing generally induces substantial reservoir damage while only simple fracture geometries are generated. This study investigated the effects of supercritical CO2 (Sc-CO2) volumes on artificial fracture morphology and propagation law during Sc-CO2 pre-injection gel fracturing. A true triaxial fracturing apparatus, combined with micro-CT and coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-damage (THMD) numerical model were applied to elaborate characters of fracture initiation pressures and geometries after using different volumes of Sc-CO2 during pre-injection gel fracturing. The physical and numerical simulation analyses revealed the fracture propagation law that is associated with Sc-CO2 pre-fracturing. The results are as follows: (1) Sc-CO2 pre-injection effectively reduced the fracture initiation pressure by 12.7% as the pre-injection volume increased from 0 to 88.61 mL; (2) greater pre-injection volumes of Sc-CO2 enhanced fracture complexity degree, reflected by that the indexes of fractal dimension, tortuosity, and volume of the induced artificial fractures; (3) the THMD model was successfully validated, which can accurately predict fracture propagation morphology, fracture area ratio, and fractal dimension; (4) both the physical and numerical simulations indicated that, the fracture apertures increased from 0.09 mm to 0.15 mm, as the pre-injection volumes of Sc-CO2 increased from 14.53 to 88.61 mL; (5) fracture propagation exhibits a nonlinear dependence on Sc-CO2 pre-injection volume, characterized by weakly activated, effectively activated, and saturation-activated patterns. These findings provide systematic guidance for optimizing the process parameters of Sc-CO2 pre-fracturing in shale reservoirs. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Liu X.; Chen Z.; Zhou D.; Zhao Q.; Feng H.; Cui Y.; Ding C.; Gao Y.
Title: Breaking the Specific Capacity Limit: 409% Boost in Manganese-Based Redox Flow Batteries at High Current Densities with a MnO2Semi-Solid Slurry Electrolyte
Abstract: The common-ion effect of SO42− limits the solubility of MnSO4 to ≤ 1 M in conventional H2SO4 electrolytes, resulting in low specific capacity of manganese (Mn)-based redox flow batteries (RFBs). Although MnO2 semi-solid RFBs are expected to improve the specific capacity, the sluggish electrochemical reaction kinetics leads to low operating current densities (≤ 1 mA cm−2). Herein, we employ a reverse-design strategy by introducing additional high-concentration MnO2 into the conventional Mn-based electrolyte. Leveraging the MnO2/Mn2+ electrochemical reaction successfully circumvents the common-ion effect, raising the concentration of soluble Mn species in the electrolyte to 3.76 M and achieving a specific capacity of 156.2 Ah LCatholyte-1 —a 409% increment over reported MnSO4-based electrolytes. Subsequently, the reverse disproportionation of electrolytic MnO2 generated during the second charging cycle shifts the redox mechanism from the MnO2(s)/Mn2+ couple to the solution-phase Mn3+(aq)/Mn2+ pair. This transformation not only elevates the discharge voltage but also enables stable operation at 30 mA cm−2, representing a current density 30-fold higher than reported Mn-based semi-solid RFBs. This work demonstrates a rational design strategy for semi-solid slurry electrolytes to enhance the specific capacity of RFBs, thereby advancing their applicability in grid-scale renewable energy storage. Authors: Zhang Z.; Xie J.; Fu S.; Du J.; Gu Y.; Yang X.; Lv J.; Yang X.-S.; Lin J.
Title: A critical review on the formability and improvement strategies of wrought magnesium alloys
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Wrought magnesium (Mg) alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for transportation vehicles, yet their limited formability, especially at room temperature, remains a major barrier to broader applications. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in technological development for improving the formability of wrought Mg alloys, focusing on the mechanistic origins of poor formability, assessment methodologies, alloy‑ and process‑specific improvement strategies, and the engineering validations and gaps for secondary-formed Mg sheet components. The limited formability of Mg alloys is primarily attributed to the intrinsically low number of readily activated independent slip systems in hexagonal close‑packed Mg, coupled with the propensity to develop strong basal textures during thermomechanical processing. For coarse‑grained Mg alloys, introducing pre‑existing twinning via pre‑compression can enhance subsequent formability by facilitating detwinning‑dominated deformation. For fine‑grained alloys, weakening basal texture and promoting non‑basal slip via targeted alloying and optimized processing routes are central to achieving higher ductility and stretch formability. Additional approaches, including engineered heterogeneous grain structures and the introduction of deformable second phases, primarily aim to increase work‑hardening capacity and uniform elongation by stimulating geometrically necessary dislocations and improving strain accommodation. These potential strategies are often applied across different grain-size regimes, depending on the specific alloy and processing conditions, rather than being strictly limited to a particular grain-size range. Finally, Mg alloy sheets have certain weight reduction potential under the condition of meeting specific stiffness requirements, but their widespread application in automobile body structures still needs to undergo rigorous multi-constraint verification. © 2026

Authors: Hu J.; Han F.; Guo W.; Ren J.; Wang Q.; Zhang Z.; Ali M.; Zhang Y.; Yuan F.; Liu C.; Gu H.; Li G.
Title: Nanoprecipitate assisting HCP→FCC phase transformation in Zircaloy-4 alloy under multiple micro-indentation loading conditions
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Stress-induced HCP→FCC phase transformation in zirconium has been well documented, yet its activation by secondary phase particles (SPPs) remains underexplored. Here, we report that Zr2Fe SPPs can promote this phase transformation in a Zr-4 alloy under micro-indentation loading. Specifically, the applied stress stimulates extensive {101‾0}<12‾10> dislocation slip in the Zr matrix. These dislocations interact with the reinforced Zr2Fe SPPs, which barely deform plastically at room temperature, thereby generating localized stress concentrations at the SPP/matrix interface. Due to specific crystallographic orientation and rod-shaped morphology of the SPPs, the stress concentration is lower along the lateral (long-axis) interfaces but significantly higher at the two ends. This stress disparity accounts for the distinct shell structures around the SPPs: the ends preferentially develop a P-type FCC-Zr phase, whereas the lateral interfaces are dominated by (0001) stacking faults without B-type FCC transformation. Our findings elucidate a novel mechanism by which SPPs assist local phase transformation to accommodate deformation stress. © 2026

Authors: Cui X.; Xu L.; Wang Z.; Yu Z.
Title: An AFM DNA image-segmentation method based on random height mapping and a Sobel-guided attention module
Abstract: DNA conformational analysis requires accurate molecule-level delineation, meaning that segmentation is a prerequisite for quantitative analysis of atomic force microscopy (AFM) height maps. Although AFM provides direct height imaging, in grayscale renderings, DNA boundariesare often obscured by limited contrast. Salt deposits and scanning artifacts can produce fragmented traces and cause DNA to be merged spuriously with nearby salt deposits in the segmentation results. AFM images acquired under different scanning conditions often vary in contrastand sharpness, and the resulting degraded appearance challenges the robustness of segmentation. We propose a framework that integrates (i)quantile-bounded RGB mapping, (ii) Sobel-guided attention in UNet skip connections, and (iii) random-mapping training for robustness.With all components enabled (quantile-bounded RGB mapping, Sobel-guided attention at Skip1, and random-mapping training), the finalmodel achieves an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.74 and a Dice score of 0.85 on the AFM test set. To assess robustness to boundarysmoothing, we further applied post hoc Gaussian blur to the test inputs. At a Gaussian blur standard deviation of 3 pixels, the model trainedwith random mapping retains an IoU of 0.46, whereas the counterpart trained with fixed mapping drops to 0.26, an absolute gain of 0.20.Additional Gaussian-noise experiments on raw AFM height maps confirm that random-mapping training improves robustness to stochasticheight-domain perturbations. Together, these results indicate that combining imaging-aware height-to-color encoding with training-timerandomized mapping and lightweight, gradient-guided reweighting of skip features offers a practical route to robust and stable AFM–DNAsegmentation, with potential transferability to other AFM image-analysis tasks. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Spongiatia-inspired pore engineering strategy for phase change material encapsulation and all-day freshwater-electricity co-generation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Integrating interfacial solar steam generation with phase change materials (PCM) has emerged as an efficient approach for all-day solar-driven freshwater-electricity co-generation. However, building those multi-functional evaporators requires complex materials design and leakage-free PCM encapsulation. Herein, we develop a simple, one-step pore engineering strategy to synthesize carbon nanotube microspheres (CNM) with rich nano-/micro-scale pores using waste polypropylene as raw materials and subsequently construct persistent PCM@CNM composite-based multi-functional evaporators. The synergistic effect of multi-level pores significantly promotes PCM encapsulation, realizing an extremely low PCM leakage of < 0.4%. The high thermal conductivity of PCM@CNM (0.547 W m−1 K−1) enables fast thermal energy transfer and utilization for improving water evaporation and thermoelectricity generation. Under 1 sun irradiation, the evaporator delivers an evaporation rate of 2.7 kg m−2 h−1 and a voltage output of 217 mV, surpassing the state-of-the-art PCM-containing evaporators. During outdoor tests, a voltage output of 3 V is achieved, which can charge a mobile phone. Technoeconomic analysis results indicate that the cost-effectiveness of PCM@CNM stands at 209.30 g h−1 $−1. This work offers a cost-effective, sustainable platform to produce multi-functional evaporators for all-day freshwater-electricity co-generation. © 2026

Authors: Deng D.; Li J.; Wang Y.; Chen J.; Liu B.; Feng Z.; Zhang Y.; Dong Z.; Chen X.; Pan F.
Title: Deformable Ti particles regulating strain partitioning and microstructural evolution in a high-yield-strength Mg-Gd-Y-Zn composite
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: A Ti-particle-reinforced Mg-9Gd-4Y-1Zn-0.5Mn (Ti/VW94) composite with excellent yield strength was fabricated via near-recrystallization warm extrusion at 340 °C followed by aging treatment. During warm extrusion, trace Mn atoms dynamically segregated toward the Ti/Mg interfaces, leading to the in-situ formation of a low-mismatch interface layer of MnTi intermetallic compound. This robust metallurgical bonding facilitated coordinated elastoplastic co-deformation between the Ti particles and the Mg matrix, thereby effectively governing local strain partitioning within the composite. Meanwhile, the coarse deformed undynamic recrystallization (unDRX) grains retained extremely high stored strain energy and dense dislocation structures, while the dual-source particle-stimulated nucleation mechanism induced by Ti particles and intrinsic long-period stacking ordered (LPSO) phases promoted the formation of ultrafine DRX grains (∼350 nm). After aging, nanoscale β′ precipitates and lamellar LPSO phases preferentially formed in high-defect-density unDRX grains, while β phases preferentially formed along solute-rich DRX grain boundaries. These precipitates constructed a hierarchical multi-scale obstacle network that effectively impeded dislocation motion. Owing to the combined effects of grain refinement, dislocation strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and load transfer, the composite achieved a high yield strength of 535 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 549 MPa. These findings demonstrate that deformable metallic reinforcements can fundamentally regulate strain partitioning and thereby govern recrystallization pathways, dislocation density, and precipitation behavior in Mg-rare earth-Zn alloys, providing a new strategy for designing high-strength magnesium matrix composites. © 2026

Authors: Zhang X.; Zhu Y.; Bai R.; Mao R.; Yan Z.; Du X.; Zhou R.; Tang Y.; Li H.; Sofer Z.; Wang W.; Ma H.; Song C.; Jiang C.
Title: Valley polarization boost enabled by interfacial exciton-magnon interaction in TMD/CrSBr antiferromagnetic heterostructures
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Manipulating valley pseudospin in two-dimensional materials using antiferromagnetic proximity remains a significant challenge, as the zero net magnetization invalidates conventional magnetic proximity based on spin-polarized carrier hopping or effective magnetic field. Here, we overcome this limitation by harnessing a distinct mechanism, strong magnonic excitations in antiferromagnets, to achieve valley control without relying on net magnetization. We demonstrate a boost of valley polarization in MoSe2/CrSBr antiferromagnetic heterostructures enabled by the interfacial exciton-magnon interaction. This boost appears exclusively below the Néel temperature of CrSBr, directly correlating with antiferromagnetic order. Optical excitation and magnetic field dependence exclude the conventional mechanism of the magnetic proximity effect. We attribute this antiferromagnet-driven valley polarization boost to the interfacial scattering between photoexcited magnons in CrSBr and excitons in MoSe2, which effectively suppresses the exciton spin precession, thereby reducing the intrinsic electron-hole exchange interaction that dominates valley depolarization. Our work demonstrates interfacial exciton-magnon interaction as an effective approach for valley manipulation and bridges the gap in antiferromagnet-controlled valley degree of freedom. © 2026

Title: Coordination-locked metastable zirconia from MOF pyrolysis drives enhanced metal–support interaction for high-performance formic acid dehydrogenation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Palladium catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation (FAD) are profoundly influenced by the crystal phase of the support, yet the phase-dependent electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) remains mechanistically elusive. Herein, we craft a metastable tetragonal ZrO2 (t-ZrO2) support through the confined pyrolysis of an NH2-UiO-66 metal-organic framework (MOF). The in situ formed O–Zr–N coordination network kinetically locks the t-ZrO2 phase, preserving abundant defects and enabling robust EMSI with Pd nanoparticles. This results in exceptional Pd dispersion and interfacial electron transfer, a remarkably high turnover frequency of 11088 h−1 for FAD at 323 K, surpassing the performance of many recently reported Pd-based catalytic systems. By integrating in situ spectroscopy, synchrotron radiation analysis, and PALLAS machine-learning path searches, we unveil that the O–Zr–N network kinetically stabilizes t-ZrO2 by raising the lattice reconstruction barrier. Furthermore, the gradient acid–base sites on t-ZrO2 synergize with Pd–O–Zr interfacial charge transfer to substantially lower the energy barrier for HCOO− dehydrogenation. This work establishes a new paradigm for engineering metal–support synergy via precise crystal-phase control of oxide supports. © 2026

Title: Combinatorial metabolic engineering of Mycobacterium neoaurum LY-2 for efficient androstenedione production from phytosterols
Abstract: Androstenedione (AD) is an important precursor for the synthesis of corticosteroids, sex hormones, and other high-value steroid pharmaceuticals. Microbial conversion of phytosterols provides a sustainable route for AD production, but current production levels remain insufficient for practical industrial application. In this study, a modular metabolic engineering strategy was developed to improve AD biosynthesis from phytosterols in Mycobacterium neoaurum LY-2. Competing C19 and C22 steroid pathways were first blocked to attenuate AD degradation, generating the AD-accumulating strain Mbn12 with a titer of 5.14 g/L. Sterol catabolic flux was then enhanced by relieving transcriptional repression and improving acetyl-CoA and propionyl-CoA utilization, which increased AD production to 6.08 g/L. To support high-flux sterol oxidation, cofactor regeneration and oxidative stress resistance were further strengthened, raising AD production to 6.67 g/L. Finally, moderate cell envelope remodeling improved substrate transport and increased AD production to 6.98 g/L. The final engineered strain Mbn30 produced 20.55 g/L AD from 30 g/L phytosterols in a 5 L fermenter, representing a 48.6% improvement over Mbn12. This work provides a scalable engineering framework for AD production and offers guidance for the microbial manufacture of other steroid intermediates. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Short-term emission pathways in India's iron and steel sector: A hybrid framework combining quantitative methods and bottom-up modelling
Abstract: This study presents a hybrid assessment framework to quantify current greenhouse gas emissions and evaluate decarbonization pathways for India's iron and steel industry up to 2030. The framework establishes a sectoral emissions baseline and examines the impact of alternative mitigation scenarios, providing a foundation for long-term decarbonization planning beyond 2030. The industry was categorized into two segments: major integrated steel producers, representing more than 57% of national crude steel output, and other producers, comprising predominantly electric-route and small-to-medium-scale operations. Emission intensity estimates for major producers were derived from reported production and emissions data, whereas emissions from other producers were assessed using a bottom-up, process-based estimation. The study estimated the baseline emission intensity for financial year 2023–24 at 2.31 tCO₂/tcs, with major producers averaging 2.53 tCO₂/tcs and other (secondary) producers operating at a lower intensity of 2.02 tCO₂/tcs. Six scenarios were modelled through 2030, revealing that a combination of 30% scrap use and 50% renewable electricity offer the most effective short-term mitigation, reducing intensity to 1.66 tCO₂/tcs. While emissions from major producers remain largely stable, most reductions are driven by secondary producers, highlighting their greater decarbonization potential. Despite these improvements in carbon intensity, projected growth in steel production is expected to increase total sectoral emissions by approximately 20–74% by 2030, depending on the scenario considered. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Dipole Field Engineering in Ni(II)‐Acetylide Frameworks under Mechanical Activation for Enhanced Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
Abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction offers a promising route for solar-to-chemical energy conversion, yet its efficiency remains limited by inefficient charge transport within two-dimensional organic frameworks due to rapid intralayer recombination. Here, we develop a dipole-field engineering strategy in a nickel(II)-acetylide framework, TP(NH2)-Ni-AF, in which polar –NH2 groups enhance piezoelectric polarization and regulate intralayer charge kinetics. Under visible-light and ultrasonic irradiation, the TP(NH2)-Ni-AF/Na2SO3 system delivers a CO production rate of 125.2 μmol g−1 h−1 with 88.36% selectivity, outperforming the non-aminated analogue. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that TP-Ni-AF exhibits a dipole moment of 175.49 D under 2 GPa, whereas –NH2 increases structural asymmetry and raises the dipole moment to 192.01 D. Consistently, piezoresponse force microscopy confirms a higher piezoelectric response, with a d33 value of 16.56 pm V−1. This internal polarization field promotes charge separation and electron migration from the photoactive ligand to the catalytically active –CtbndC–Ni(PBu3)2–CtbndC– sites. Mechanistic studies further show that polarization-assisted charge migration facilitates CO2 adsorption through a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) pathway and lowers the energy barrier for *COOH formation. These results establish polar-group-induced internal electric fields as a powerful design principle for controlling photogenerated carrier dynamics and advancing piezo-photocatalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Pyrolysis/non-thermal plasma/catalysis of waste plastics with bimetallic catalysts: Control of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites to improve production of BTEX aromatic hydrocarbons
Abstract: Pyrolysis-catalysis of waste plastics is an endothermic process that suffers trade-offs between diffusion limitations and rapid catalyst deactivation due to catalyst coking. Title: Synergistic Effect of Dual Ionic Liquid PVDF-HFP Polymer Inclusion Membranes: Linking Mechanical, Chemical, Microstructural and Gold Recovery Performance; [PVDF-HFP полимеріне екі иондық сұйықтықты қосу арқылы мембраналардың синергетикалық әсері: механикалық, химиялық, микроқұрылымдық қасиеттер мен алтынды алу тиімділігі арасындағы байланыс]; [Синергетический эффект мембран с включением двух ионных жидкостей в полимер PVDF-HFP: связь между механическими, химическими, микроструктурными свойствами и эффективностью извлечения золота]
Abstract: Poly (vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) polymer inclusion membranes (PIMs) are widely used across separation industries because of their ability to selectively separate ions or molecules, their chemical stability, and their mechanical flexibility. Still, improving how the membrane performs without making the membrane material properties deteriorate remains a challenge. In this study, Aliquat 336 and Cyphos IL 104 were blended with PVDF-HFP and fabricated through the solvent casting method. The main objective of this study is to understand how the ionic liquids can affect the membrane’s chemical properties, physical properties, mechanical stability, and its ability to recover gold through an H-cell setup. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of Aliquat 336, showing bands associated with quaternary ammonium groups, while Cyphos IL 104 displayed vibrations related to phosphonium-related P–C. SEM images further revealed clear differences in how the membrane morphology looked. Pure PVDF-HFP alone had compact surfaces; Aliquat 336 membranes appeared to have smoother features, and Cyphos IL 104 membranes developed rougher surfaces with micro-voids. The addition of ionic liquids also increased membrane porosity from 25 % in the pure membrane to 45 % with the addition of ionic liquids. At the same time, the contact angle dropped from 90° to 58°, indicating improved hydrophilicity. Mechanical testing showed that pure PVDF-HFP had the highest tensile strength (30 MPa), modulus (450 MPa), and tear resistance (2.5 N/mm). Membranes with higher Aliquat 336 content retained better tear resistance, close to 2.0 N/mm, while maintaining smoother membrane surfaces. In comparison, the addition of Cyphos IL 104 adversely impacts the mechanical properties. Gold extraction experiments showed promising performance. The PVDF-HFP/A15C20 membrane achieved 76 % recovery within 12 h. The combination of both Aliquat 336 and Cyphos IL 104 improved ion transport while maintaining acceptable membrane stability properties. Overall, the results showed that the ionic liquid composition has a strong influence on both the membrane’s durability properties and separation performance. These findings provide a useful approach for developing membranes in precious metal recovery applications. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. All rights reserved.

Authors: Yan Y.; Wang P.; Chen M.; Li Q.; Ran Y.; Peng H.; Chen D.; Jiang X.
Title: Formation mechanisms of a nanocrystalline-amorphous hybrid interface in Al-Cu impact welding
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: This study systematically investigates the interfacial evolution mechanisms of Al-Cu joints fabricated by electromagnetic pulse welding. Transmission electron microscope (TEM) analyses reveal a gradient-refined interface comprising three distinct regions: central impact zone characterized by a nanocrystalline-amorphous structure, impact-affected zone with sub-micron grain refinement, and non-impacted zone showing only minor lattice distortion. The central impact zone contains a ∼1.3 µm transition layer exhibiting an “amorphous sea-nanocrystalline islands” structure composed of amorphous regions, Al2Cu nanocrystals, and residual Al/Cu nanograins. A phenomenological ΔC–Rc framework is proposed to describe the competition among compositional driving force, deformation-induced disordering, and kinetic arrest, in which high compositional gradients favor Al2Cu nucleation while rapid cooling restricts subsequent grain growth. The amorphous phase is attributed predominantly to deformation-induced solid-state amorphization, as supported by its heterogeneous morphology, the limited liquid-state diffusion length, and intense shear-driven atomic mixing. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal a strong velocity dependence: An intermediate velocity of 500 m/s produces coexisting ordered and disordered structures consistent with experimental observations, whereas 2000 m/s velocity produces predominantly disordered configurations. Semi-quantitative high-resolution TEM/ inverse fast Fourier transform analyses also yield local dislocation-density estimates on the order of 1016 m−2 in highly deformed regions, demonstrating substantial defect accumulation during impact. These findings establish a coupled mechanism linking deformation, atomic mixing, and phase evolution in non-equilibrium Al-Cu interfaces and provide insights into controlling nanocrystalline-amorphous structures in high-velocity impact welding. © 2026

Authors: Fan J.; Wu Z.; Nie Q.; Nie L.; Tan F.; Wu C.; Deng M.; Sun H.; Zhou G.; Qian L.; Zhang T.; Xiang C.
Title: In-situ photo-patternable ZnO via dual-functional surface engineering strategy for high-resolution QLED devices
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Benefiting from the adjustable emission spectrum, high color purity, wide gamut, and solution-processability, quantum dot light-emitting diode (QLED) is considered one of the most promising next-generation display technologies. As a prevalent electron transport material, ZnO plays a crucial role in enhancing the efficiency and long-term stability of QLED devices. To promote the development of high-resolution QLED displays, this study proposes a dual-functional surface engineering strategy for achieving in-situ photo-patternable ZnO with enhanced electrical properties. Physicochemical characterization revealed that surface defects of ZnO were significantly reduced via direct photolithography, thereby decreasing non-radiative exciton recombination at the QD/ZnO interface. Particularly, the red QLED devices based on photolithographic ZnO exhibited remarkable performance, achieving a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.5%, a brightness of over 140,000 cd m−2 at 5 V, and an alleviated positive-aging effect (i.e., anomalous brightness increase). Concurrently, the operational lifetime T95 (the time for the device luminance to drop to 95% of its initial value) was also improved from 1,036 h to 2,084 h. Furthermore, by modulating the morphology of ZnO films, we successfully fabricated pixelated QLED devices, laying the technical foundation for commercializing high-resolution QLED displays. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Authors: Xu Y.; Liu Y.; Wang X.; Wang M.; Tan W.; Peng Y.; Yang H.G.; Hou Y.
Title: Energy-level engineering of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite for efficient photocatalytic C(sp3)–H bond oxidation
Abstract: Photocatalytic selective oxidation of aromatic C(sp3)–H bonds represents an appealing strategy for producing value-added chemicals and enabling solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Despite rapid progress in halide perovskite photocatalysts, their practical performance remains fundamentally limited by inefficient charge separation and rapid photocarrier recombination. Herein, we demonstrate a quasi-two-dimensional perovskite platform, (C4H9NH3)2(CH3NH3)Pb2BrxCl7−x (BMPBC-x, x = 0–7), in which structural anisotropy and electronic structure engineering are synergistically integrated to regulate photocatalytic reactivity. Precise modulation of the Br−/Cl− composition enables continuous tuning of the band structure while simultaneously activating a local polarization-related electromechanical response associated with the quasi-2D framework. This dual regulation established a cooperative mechanism that enhances both light harvesting and charge separation, thereby significantly improving photocarrier utilization efficiency. Hence, the optimized composition delivers up to a 17-fold enhancement in activity relative to the Cl-pure phase and a 1.5-fold increase compared with the Br-pure counterpart. Emphatically, the optimized BMPBC-4.7 nanosheets exhibit a benzaldehyde formation rate of 19.1 mmol·g−1·h−1 under light irradiation, representing one of the highest reported performances for single-component perovskite photocatalysts. This work highlights halide-mediated energy-level engineering coupled with facet junction as an effective strategy for manipulating charge-carrier dynamics in quasi-2D perovskites, offering new opportunities for efficient photocatalytic organic transformations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Radioactivity as a prospecting indicator of rare earth, gold and polymetal deposits in eastern Kazakhstan and an indicator of increased radioecological hazard during their development; [Шығыс Қазақстандағы сирек жер элементтері, алтын және полиметалл кен орындарын іздеудің белгісі ретінде радиоактивтілік және осы кен орындарын игеру кезінде радиациялық-экологиялық қауіптің жоғары деңгейінің индикаторы]; [Радиоактивность как поисковый признак месторождений редких земель, золота и полиметаллов Восточного Казахстана и индикатор повышенного уровня радиоэкологической опасности при разработке этих месторождений]
Abstract: This study evaluates the role of natural radioactivity as an exploration indicator for rare-metal, gold, and polymetallic mineralization in Eastern Kazakhstan, as well as its significance as a factor of radioecological hazard. The analysis is based on the results of regional radiohydrolithochemical surveys conducted at a scale of 1:1,000,000, including bottom sediment sampling within microbasins. The study focuses on key natural radionuclides (U-238, Ra-226, Th-232, Ra-228, K-40) and their spatial distribution. Factor analysis was applied to identify anomalous geochemical associations and to assess their relationship with metallogenic structures. As a result, 80 potentially radioecologically hazardous zones were identified across Kazakhstan, including 5 zones within Eastern Kazakhstan. Within the study area, 12 anomalous sites were distinguished, characterized by 3–5 factors with cumulative explained variance ranging from 62.8% to 83.6%. The identified anomalies show spatial correspondence with major metallogenic zones, particularly the Rudny Altai and Kalba-Narym regions, which are associated with polymetallic and rare-metal mineralization. The results demonstrate that natural radioactivity can serve both as an effective exploration indicator and as an important factor of environmental risk. The study highlights the potential of integrating radioactivity parameters into exploration criteria and emphasizes the need to consider radiation safety in geological exploration and mining activities. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Authors: Lu J.; Chen X.; Aziz M.; Yu Y.; Zhang C.; Huang Z.; Chen F.
Title: Architected NiTi alloys with elastically dominated regions for efficient and stable elastocaloric cooling
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Elastocaloric cooling based on stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) in NiTi alloys shows great potential for low-carbon thermal management, but the functional performance–cyclic stability trade-off remains unresolved. Here, an integrated strategy of macro–microstructure fabrication is proposed to mitigate this trade-off by architecting the NiTi alloy into elastically dominated buffering regions and phase-transforming regions. In situ experiments confirm that the designed structure spatially distributes stress and temperature. Microscopic analysis further reveals that preferential longitudinal-direction martensite growth and regular secondary twins can effectively suppress plastic damage accumulation and improve reversibility. As a result, the NiTi structure exhibits significant elastocaloric performance, with a stable coefficient of performance of ∼18.7, a mechanical loss factor (ζloss) of ∼0.11 over 103 cycles, and a first recovery strain of 7.3%. This study demonstrates that macroscopic structural programming can improve elastocaloric functional performance by regulating local stress distribution and transformation behavior, offering a new approach to solid-state cooling materials beyond micro-control material optimization. © 2026

Title: Self-rotating wood sphere evaporator enabled by flame-induced carbonization for high-efficiency solar desalination
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Self-desalting solar evaporators have exhibited remarkable potential in enhancing interfacial evaporation stability and mitigating salt accumulation, although most existing systems rely on chemical modifications to optimize photothermal performance or surface wettability, which leads to intricate fabrication procedures and additional environmental burdens. In this work, a flame-carbonized wood sphere (CWS)-based self-rotating floating evaporator was developed to overcome these limitations by employing natural wood as a renewable substrate and fabricating it through a facile, chemical-free flame treatment process that simultaneously enhanced light absorption and surface hydrophilicity while preserving the intrinsic longitudinal vessels and multiscale porous architecture. Such structural integrity enables a synergistic regulation between efficient water transport and localized heat confinement, ensuring stable and continuous evaporation. Experimental evaluations revealed that the optimally carbonized sample, CWS-2, achieved an evaporation rate of 2.05 kg m−2 h−1 under one-sun illumination in 3.5 wt.% saline solution and maintained a high rate of 1.20 kg m−2 h−1 even in 20 wt.% salinity, displaying exceptional long-term operational stability over 8 h of continuous testing. Centered on natural, eco-benign materials and featuring a chemical-free, low-energy fabrication route, this self-rotating evaporator demonstrates superior environmental adaptability and scalability, offering a high-performance and sustainable strategy for solar-driven desalination and water purification applications. © 2026

Authors: Wang J.; Lin D.; Yuan X.; Zhang Y.; Zhang W.; Feng Y.; Yimin R.; Gong W.; Li Q.
Title: Synergistic electrode/electrolyte optimization enables efficient dissolution-deposition chemistry in Zn-MnO2 batteries
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Electrolytic Zn-MnO2 batteries based on the MnO2/Mn2+ dissolution/deposition reaction have attracted considerable interest due to their high redox potential and exceptionally high theoretical capacity. However, such systems typically require an acidic environment to initiate the one‑step MnO2/Mn2+ conversion. Herein, high-performance cathode-less Zn-MnO2 batteries are designed. Benefiting from its high surface area and manganese affinity, the aminated Prussian blue analogues (MF@NC‑HA) seed layer provides extra active sites, inducing uniform MnO2 deposition and improving its charge structure. Meanwhile, amino‑acid additives with chelating ability toward Mn2+/Zn2+ are introduced to optimize the cationic solvation structure. Asp lowers the Gibbs free energy of the MnO2 dissolution reaction, thereby enhancing reaction efficiency. The MnO2@HA‑Asp delivers a high areal capacity of 0.53 mAh cm−2 after cycling at 0.5 mA cm−2 and maintains nearly 100% CE over 300 stable cycles at 1.0 mA cm−2. Importantly, Asp can preferentially adsorb on the Zn (002) plane, guiding uniform Zn2+ horizontal deposition and effectively suppressing dendrite growth. Ultimately, the Zn//MnO2@HA‑Asp pouch cell exhibits a high discharge plateau of ∼1.5 V and a capacity of 11.7 mAh. This work provides an efficient strategy for realizing the two‑electron transfer process of Zn-Mn systems. © 2026

Title: Optimization of Aluminum Casting Process Using PLA-Based Casting Patterns and Analysis of their Thermal Behavior; [Оптимизация процесса литья алюминия с использованием литьевых схем на основе PLA-материалов и анализа их термического поведения]
Abstract: This paper presents the results of experimental and numerical studies of the casting process of 99.85% pure aluminum using investment-casting technologies with patterns produced by additive manufacturing. The influence of pouring temperature, mold-filling time, and gating-system design on porosity formation and casting quality was analyzed. It was established that increasing the pouring temperature within the range of 700–800°C leads to increased porosity due to higher gas solubility and intensified turbulence of the melt flow. It was shown that the separating gating system ensures a minimum number of defects compared to top and bottom metal-feeding systems. In addition, thermal analysis of PLA and a glass-fiber-reinforced PLA composite was carried out. Pure PLA was found to burn out almost completely (residue about 2.4%), whereas the composite was characterized by a high residual content (~43.6%), which may negatively affect mold quality. The simulation results obtained using the AutoCAST software package showed good agreement with the experimental data and confirmed the effectiveness of numerical modeling for optimization of casting processes. It was established that the optimal pouring-temperature range for aluminum is 720–760°C. The obtained results confirm the potential of using PLA in investment casting technology and make it possible to improve the quality of aluminum castings under industrial production conditions. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: Descriptor-based plasma-regulated ultrafine high-entropy alloy supported on vertically aligned carbon nanotubes with enhanced bifunctional catalytic performance for excellent direct methanol fuel cell
Abstract: This work proposes an efficient strategy for screening high-entropy-alloy (HEA) dopants using atomic radius and electronegativity as principal criteria. Multi-metal precursors, screened via descriptor-based methods and density-functional-theory calculations, are reduced using low-temperature radio-frequency plasma technology to obtain defect-rich PtFeCoNiCu HEAs anchored on vertically aligned-carbon nanotubes (P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC). The synergistic effects of the ordered HEA structure, plasma defect-engineering, electronic-structure modulation, and the vertically aligned-carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) significantly enhanced the electrocatalytic performance and stability of P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC for both the methanol-oxidation-reaction (MOR) and oxygen-reduction-reaction (ORR). Electrochemical analyses reveal that the P-PtFeCoNiCu@VACNTs@CC delivers outstanding bifunctional activity, attaining a peak-current-density of 2.44 ± 0.067 A mg−1Pt at 0.93 V for MOR (0.5 M H2SO4 + 0.5 M CH3OH) and a half-wave potential (E1/2) of 0.761 ± 0.006 V for ORR (0.5 M H2SO4). This work presents a novel strategy for efficient screening and fabrication of high-performance HEA based electrodes and highlights promising applications in direct methanol fuel cells. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Hydrodynamic characteristics of a pump as turbine under periodic inflow fluctuations
Abstract: In seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) systems, the pump as turbine (PAT) recovers energy of high-pressure brine by coupling with high-pressure pumps. This can significantly reduce the system’s specific energy consumption. However, the upstream flow rate to the PAT is not constant during operation. It typically fluctuates within a certain range, thus affecting the stability of the PAT during actual operation. Therefore, this study uses computational fluid dynamics to investigate the transient flow behavior of a PAT with a fixed-axis and constant-torque connected load pump under periodic fluctuations in the incoming flow. To simulate the fluctuating flow process, user-defined functions are implemented to describe the instantaneous flow variations and capture the transient hydrodynamic characteristics at various fluctuation frequencies. The numerical simulation results are validated against experimental data. The results indicate that when the PAT is subjected to periodic inflow fluctuations, the rotational speed, torque, and internal flow field of the impeller vary significantly with the flow rate. This will exert a significant impact on the efficiency and stability of PAT operation. Meanwhile, the external characteristic parameters (head, power, and efficiency) and stability of the PAT are also affected by the inflow fluctuation frequency. At higher inflow fluctuation frequency, the PAT system exhibits higher average efficiency and a small axial force fluctuation in the impeller, but the radial force fluctuation is more intense. The results obtained in this study can provide theoretical support for the anti-interference design and operational optimization of PAT energy recovery systems in SWRO systems. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: AI-Driven Surrogate Modeling and Inverse Design of Type-II Superlattice Infrared Detectors
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: The conventional design of Type-II superlattice (T2SL) infrared detectors relies on iterative physics-based simulations, which can make broad exploration computationally costly. Here, we develop an AI-driven surrogate workflow for InAs/GaSb T2SL detectors. Two separately trained Transformer regressors with the same layer-token architecture predict dark-current-density curves and quantum-efficiency (QE) spectra from layer thicknesses, doping concentrations, and operating temperature. On fixed held-out test sets, the dark-current model achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.7332 A/cm2, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.7913%, and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.998103, while the QE model achieved an RMSE of 0.005104, MAPE of 1.6417%, and R2 of 0.999231. Controlled comparisons on identical data splits showed that the Transformer obtained the lowest RMSE and MAPE and the highest R2 for both targets relative to multilayer-perceptron and Random-Forest baselines. Using the two surrogates, we evaluated one million uniformly sampled candidates at 77 K and identified 83 structures meeting the target requirements: dark-current density below 5 × 10-6 A/cm2 at -1 V and mean QE above 56% over wavelengths from 3.03 to 3.42 μm. Six selected candidates were subsequently compared with Crosslight simulations. By combining surrogate prediction, high-throughput target-driven screening, and Crosslight simulation verification, this framework shifts T2SL detector design from repeated trial-and-error simulation toward intelligent prediction and verification, offering a practical route to accelerate the exploration of high-performance infrared detector structures.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: Taming the boundary effect: Femtosecond laser slicing of 4H-SiC enabled by side scribing for improved processability
Abstract: The 4H polytype of silicon carbide (4H-SiC) has excellent properties such as high electron mobility and high saturation electron velocity; ithas therefore become an important material for high-power and high-frequency devices. In the slicing step of wafer fabrication, however,conventional wire-saw cutting is constrained by the inherent high hardness and brittleness of 4H-SiC, causing excessive material removal andsurface and subsurface damage. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a femtosecond laser slicing technology combined with sidescribing. A simulation model of the boundary effect in internal laser processing was established to analyze the optical energy distribution underspherical aberration. The simulations revealed boundary regions that resist laser modification because of the coupling between asymmetricfocusing and spherical aberration, which degrades the slicing quality of conventional laser processing. Systematic parametric experimentswere then used to investigate the influence of the laser processing parameters on the formation of the modified layer. Targeted experimentsperformed using the optimized processing parameters provided a quantitative characterization of the hard-to-modify regions and guided theapplication of the side-scribing process. The peeling results demonstrate that the proposed side-scribing-assisted femtosecond laser slicingprocess effectively reduces the peeling stress and the cracking that occurs during slicing, achieving a 68% reduction in peeling stress and a 27%reduction in the arithmetic mean roughness Sa of the peeled surface, together with the formation of laser-induced periodic surface structuresthat are better suited to subsequent processing, compared with conventional laser slicing. This study improves the processability of 4H-SiCwafer slicing and provides a new approach to substrate preparation for wide-bandgap semiconductor materials. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Ultralow Noise Orthogonal Fluxgates Enabling Weak Magnetic Field and Biomolecular Detection
Abstract: Noninvasive detection of ultra-weak biomagnetic signals is crucial for modern biosensing, but conventional magnetic sensors are fundamentally limited by intrinsic noise. Orthogonal fluxgates (OFGs) enable high signal-to-noise-ratio detection of weak magnetic fields, yet their performance is still constrained by intrinsic 1/f noise and Barkhausen-related magnetic fluctuations. This study reports a low-noise orthogonal fluxgate in which a newly designed magnetic core and circuit mitigate existing noise limitations. The CoP/Ag composite core, featuring an amorphous-nanocrystalline dual phase, is associated with reduced low-frequency magnetic loss and improved noise performance. Title: Synergistic heterointerface engineering and atomic Co-Nx coordination doping in carbon-intercalated MXene for enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Heterointerface engineering and atomic doping are recognized as core strategies for the development of high-performance electromagnetic wave-absorbing (EMA) materials. The carbon-intercalated heterointerface provides abundant Co anchoring sites, while Co-Nx coordination configurations introduce numerous dipolar polarization centers. Co-Nx atomic coordination and interfacial charge redistribution synergistically enhance interfacial polarization, dipole polarization, and defect-induced polarization, and effectively balance the dielectric and magnetic responses of the composite, further optimizing its impedance matching. The CoSA@MX/C composite achieves an outstanding minimum reflection loss of −54.42 dB at only 1.72 mm. Density functional theory calculations show that uniformly dispersed Co-Nx doping disrupts the local symmetry of the electronic structure, thereby increasing the electrical conductivity loss and enhancing electromagnetic wave absorption performance. Authors: Gao H.; Li R.; Feng Y.; Wang Y.; Li S.; Wang Y.-D.
Title: Bulk stacking fault probability as a diffraction-derived metric for quantitative planar defect kinetics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Quantitative descriptions of defect-accumulation kinetics require a physically meaningful defect metric that can be continuously measured and compared across different deformation states. Such a metric remains unavailable for many diffraction-derived defect descriptors because existing quantities are either model-dependent or lack a rigorous bulk-scale interpretation. Here, an orientation-corrected bulk stacking fault probability (SFP), reconstructed through orientation-weighted integration of in situ synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction measurements during tensile deformation of a stainless steel, is proposed as a diffraction-derived planar defect metric. The measured SFP exhibits pronounced orientation dependence and is therefore better interpreted as a directional defect descriptor than as an intrinsic scalar quantity. By correcting the directional faulting field for texture-induced orientation bias through pole-density-weighted integration, a bulk measure of the overall degree of faulting is obtained, enabling the transformation of a directional faulting field into a physically interpretable defect metric. The resulting bulk SFP enables direct quantification of stacking fault accumulation kinetics, revealing rapid initial fault generation followed by progressive deceleration at larger strains. A strong linear correlation between SFP and diffraction peak broadening further indicates concurrent evolution of stacking faults and defect-induced lattice distortions during deformation. Unlike peak-width-based quantities, which generally lack a rigorous averaging property and contain contributions from both Type II and Type III stress fields, the proposed bulk SFP retains both a rigorous averaging property and a direct crystallographic interpretation. The resulting framework enables quantitative characterization of planar defect accumulation kinetics using experimentally measurable diffraction data. © 2026

Title: Engineering high coordination shell of single-atom Fe-N-C to enhance electronic push-pull and oxygen reduction performance
Abstract: The development of iron single-atom catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is hindered by the strong adsorption of oxygenated intermediates on the Fe-Nx active sites and the sluggish kinetics of ORR. In general, the intrinsic ORR activity of Fe-N4 sites is constrained by their plane-symmetric D4 h coordination environment. Herein, an exceptional Fe-N4OP configuration is proposed by constructing an outer coordination sphere consisting of Fe atom coordinated with four in-plane N atoms and one axially oriented O atom in the first shell, together with the simultaneously incorporated P in the second coordination shell. Benefiting from the coordination shell engineering, the ORR activity and stability of Fe-N4OP/NPCS catalyst are significantly improved compared to other Fe-N-C counterparts and approximate to Pt/C. Experimental results and theoretical calculations reveal that the electron-donating P species and electron-withdrawing O species triggered a synergistic push-pull electronic effect. As a consequence, the Fe-N4OP sites with suitable electron density and D-band center can effectively regulate the intermediate adsorption and alleviate the energy barrier of the rate-determining step. This work expounds the significance of push-pull electronic effect on electronic structure and the local environment in high-coordination single-atom electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Achieving thermally stable subgrain microstructures with superior strength-ductility synergy in dilute Al-Mn alloys via a low-temperature homogenization strategy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: To address challenges associated with coarse-grained microstructures and inadequate mechanical properties in conventional dilute Al-Mn alloys, the present study has designed a low-temperature homogenization strategy aimed at generating a higher volume fraction of α-Al(Mn, Fe)Si dispersoids within the Al matrix. Owing to the strong Zener pinning pressure exerted by these dense dispersoids, long-range grain boundary migration is effectively suppressed during extrusion, thereby promoting the formation of a fine subgrain structure. Remarkably, this subgrain structure demonstrates exceptional thermal stability even after exposure to elevated temperatures as high as 500 °C. During plastic deformation, the abundant low-angle grain boundaries continuously emit dislocations, while the α-Al(Mn, Fe)Si dispersoids pin dislocations and hinder dynamic recovery, thereby enhancing both dislocation multiplication and storage. Compared with its conventional coarse-grained counterpart, dilute Al-Mn alloy fabricated via the novel low-temperature homogenization strategy exhibits an excellent synergy of strength, ductility, and thermal stability. This study offers an innovative perspective for the advancement of dilute Al alloys with superior comprehensive performance. © 2026
