Title: Bioinspired lightweight para-aramid/SiO2 aerogel thermal insulation materials for firefighting protection
Abstract: Protective materials used in high-temperature environments often suffer from reduced thermal insulation performance under open-flame exposure, sustained heating and repeated compression, increasing the risk of thermal injury. In this study, a feather-inspired lightweight para-aramid/SiO2 aerogel thermal insulation composite with a fluffy porous structure was developed for firefighting thermal protection. Poly(p-phenylene terephthalamide) (PPTA) fibers were used as a heat-resistant fibrous skeleton to construct a porous insulation network through fiber carding, impregnation and aerogel compounding processes. Among the tested samples, the composite prepared with a nominal SiO2 aerogel addition of 1.5 g has exhibited the lowest surface temperature under a thermal load of 100 °C. Repeated-heating and cyclic-compression tests were conducted separately. The composite exhibited a relatively stable thermal response during repeated heating and a repeatable mechanical response during cyclic compression under the applied test conditions. At the fabric-assembly level, the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 29% for the PPTA fabric-only reference to 35% for the PPTA + PPTA/SiO2-1.5 assembly, indicating improved flame resistance. A simplified PPTA-based protective assembly containing the composite filling has demonstrated a remarkable thermal-barrier behavior under direct-flame conditions with a flame temperature of ∼600 °C. The feather-inspired porous structure provides lightweight, fluffy and deformable filling characteristics while improving the thermal-protection performance of the composite. This work provides a potential structural design strategy for lightweight thermal insulation materials used in firefighting protective equipment. © 2026 Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Title: Structural engineering of carbon-based nanofibers via electrospinning for enhanced electromagnetic functionality
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Carbon-based nanofibers (CNFs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high electrical conductivity, large specific surface area, superior mechanical strength, and excellent thermal stability, making them promising for applications in energy storage, sensing, catalysis, and environmental remediation. Electrospinning, one of the most effective techniques for CNF fabrication, enables the continuous production of high-performance carbon nanofibers with operational simplicity and excellent controllability. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in electrospinning-derived CNFs. First, the fundamentals of electrospinning and the structural characteristics of CNFs are introduced. The microwave absorption mechanisms of CNFs are then comprehensively discussed. Subsequently, the structural design strategies of electrospun CNF microwave absorbers and the corresponding performance enhancement mechanisms are systematically reviewed. Finally, future research directions are highlighted, focusing on multispectral response, advanced structural design, scalable electrospinning technologies, and integrated device design. This review provides theoretical guidance and technical insights for the fabrication of high-performance electrospun CNFs and offers perspectives for the design and practical application of CNF electromagnetic functional materials. © 2026

Title: Dual role of oxygen vacancies in Mn0.3Cd0.7S/WO3−x S-scheme heterojunctions for strengthening internal electric field and extending light harvesting toward efficient H2 evolution

One is to modulate the electronic structure of tungsten oxide, thereby enlarging the Fermi level (EF) difference relative to Mn0.3Cd0.7S, and consequently strengthening the IEF to accelerate directional charge transfer. The other is to induce localized surface plasmon resonance, which broadens the light harvesting range of M/OV photocatalysts into the near-infrared (NIR) region for more efficient solar energy utilization. The synergistic effect endows the M/OV heterojunction with a H2 evolution rate of 1600 μmol g−1 h−1 under visible-NIR irradiation, which is 2.4 times as high as that of the Mn0.3Cd0.7S/WO3 counterpart derived from air-calcined WO3−x. Title: Microwave-thermo-electrical energy recycling via thermally conductive absorbing network and entropy-amplified ionic thermoelectrics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Converting the ubiquitous microwave interference into electrical power allows simultaneous electromagnetic protection and energy harvesting, which is technologically important yet challenging for the ever-compacting electronic devices. Herein, a cascaded microwave-thermo-electric transducer (MW-iTE) has been designed with enhanced electromagnetic attenuation and amplified thermoelectric conversion. A thin and flexible FeCo/CoFe2O4@reduced graphene oxide/waterborne polyurethane sheet combines multiple electromagnetic loss mechanisms for microwave dissipation with a percolated conductive network that contributes to the conductive loss while delivering the generated heat to the thermoelectric layer. The resulting MW-iTE exhibits an architecture-level thermopower of 77.86 mV K−1 and delivers a reversible voltage of 0.30 V under 17.9 GHz irradiation at 0.625 W cm−2. Title: Impact of Unauthorized Vehicles on Road Safety Using Machine Learning in Bangladesh
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: The rising number of unauthorized vehicles in rural Bangladesh has led to an alarming increase in road accidents, particularly on rural highways. Despite a significant body of research on road safety in developed countries, limited studies have focused on road safety in Bangladesh, especially concerning unauthorized vehicles. This study applies machine learning to analyze road traffic accidents involving unauthorized vehicles using data collected between 2018 and June 2023 from high-risk regions in Bangladesh, including Pabna and Sirajganj. A total of 72 accidents were examined and classified into head-on, rear-end, and pedestrian-related collisions. The traffic accident data was categorized into four distinct classes based on their causes: overspeeding, overtaking, reckless driving, and unknown causes. A total of 179 accidents were reported during the study period, with unauthorized vehicles contributing to 41.00% of the total incidents. Among the machine learning models tested, the CatBoost Classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 89%, with strong performance metrics, including an F1-score of 0.8457. The study also incorporated SHAP values to identify key predictors of accident severity, with vehicle type, weather conditions, and driver behavior being the most influential factors. Head-on collisions were the most frequent accident type, with auto vans accounting for 22.2% of cases. Reckless driving was the leading cause, primarily affecting individuals aged 25–44 years. Unauthorized vehicles, particularly auto vans, CNGs, and motorcycles, were involved in most incidents, with the Pabna-Natore corridor accounting for 56.5% of cases. These results highlight the critical role of unauthorized vehicles in traffic-related fatalities and underline the urgent need for stricter enforcement of regulations. This research provides valuable insights into the role of unauthorized vehicles in road safety and offers actionable recommendations for policymakers to reduce accidents and fatalities. The findings emphasize the need for improved legislative frameworks and better road infrastructure to enhance road safety in rural Bangladesh. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Electrochemical reconstruction-confinement coupling of defect-rich V2O5 nanowires enables ultralong-life zinc-ion storage

Abstract: Vanadium-based oxides with multiple redox states are promising cathodes for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), yet their practical application is hindered by sluggish Zn2+ transport, structural degradation, and vanadium dissolution during prolonged cycling. Moreover, electrochemical reconstruction generates abundant oxygen vacancies and structural water, leading to a highly active yet structurally resilient Zn-storage framework. Comprehensive experimental investigations combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that the reconstructed architecture simultaneously optimizes the electronic structure, strengthens Zn2+ adsorption, lowers the Zn2+ migration barrier, and promotes pseudocapacitive-dominated reaction kinetics. Title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. Each city separately trains a local deep learning model using local traffic, environmental, and disaster-related data, while only privacy-protected model updates are exchanged with a central aggregator. The results also validate enhanced anomaly detection and disaster-caused traffic disruption prediction performance across cities with limited local traffic data. The obtained results validate the effectiveness of the proposed PP-FL framework as a scalable, secure, and efficient paradigm for next-generation intelligent transportation systems. © 2027 The author(s). Abstract: The presented literature review contains the results of the analysis of scientific articles for 2000-2026 years, considering the use of blast furnace slag in various areas of road construction. It has been established that there are clear differences between the application options for different types of blast furnace slag. Air-cooled blast furnace slag (ACBFS) is more often used as a coarse or fine aggregate for cement concrete and asphalt concrete, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) is used as an additional binder or as a mineral/reactive filler. When using blast furnace slag in the production of concrete, the highest results in a number of studies were achieved when replacing 20-40% of the aggregate with slag, although this indicator was not a universal optimal value. In some articles, it was pointed out that the use of blast furnace slag as part of the base of a highway or for soil stabilization was associated with an increase in CBR. Some authors point to a reduction in the consumption of Portland cement when using complex binders containing granular blast furnace slag. Data on the improvement of water resistance, fatigue resistance, Marshall stability, and rutting resistance of asphalt concrete with the introduction of ACBFS and GGBFS in various proportions are also presented. Pretreatment of porous ACBFS was also important: selective crushing and related separation methods reduced water absorption, crushing value, and the proportion of weak porous particles. The main practical conclusion is that BFS should not be treated as a single interchangeable material. Its use should be selected according to slag type, particle quality, the component being replaced, and the required pavement property. Title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. However, conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face inherent limitations at low temperatures by intrinsic hurdle of poor ionic mobility in liquid electrolytes. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), which replace liquid electrolytes with non-flammable and non-freezing solid electrolytes, are considered promising alternatives because these solid electrolytes provide high ionic conductivity at low temperatures, superior temperature stability, and exceptional safety. ASSBs still face practical limitations at extremely low temperatures due to degradation caused by interfacial side reactions and mechanical instabilities that increase resistance and polarization. Addressing these challenges is critical to realize the advantages of ASSBs and enable their practical deployment in low-temperature applications. This review provides an overview of historical developments, critical challenges, and recent progress in advancing the low-temperature performance of ASSBs. The key components of ASSBs, including solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, are systematically investigated to develop strategies for improving ASSBs at low temperatures. By highlighting future perspectives, we emphasize both the potential and necessity of ASSBs to overcome the intrinsic limitations of LIBs and ensure reliable energy storage in harsh environments. Title: Finite element approximation of a hemivariational inequality for steady-state heat conduction: double-limit convergence of penalization and discretization
Abstract: In this paper we study the numerical approximation and convergence analysis of a steady-state heat conduction problem with mixed boundary conditions. The physical model is governed by a hemivariational inequality depending on a heat transfer parameter α > 0. We consider the finite element approximation of this penalized problem, as well as its corresponding limit problem with a prescribed constant temperature on a part of the boundary. The main theoretical result establishes the strong convergence of the discrete solutions. Specifically, we prove the double-limit convergence of the finite element approximations to the limit solution as the mesh size h tends to zero and the penalization parameter α tends to infinity, independently and simultaneously. We further complement the convergence analysis with an error estimate of optimal order for the discrete limit problem, and we explain why an estimate uniform in the penalization parameter cannot be expected. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical simulations on four examples verified by the method of manufactured solutions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: He K.-N.; Kong X.-S.; Hou J.; Zheng X.-R.; You Y.-W.; Liu C.-S.; Xie Z.-M.
Title: Physics-guided multiscale modeling of hydrogen trapping at rhenium-decorated nanovoids in Tungsten
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Understanding hydrogen-isotope trapping and release at irradiation-induced nanovoids decorated by rhenium (Re) is critical for tungsten plasma-facing materials, yet atomistic adsorption descriptions become intractable with increasing nanovoid size and hydrogen (H) loading. We develop a physics-guided multiscale framework linking density functional theory (DFT), high-throughput analysis, the sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO), and object kinetic Monte Carlo (OKMC) simulations. DFT shows that H trapping is governed mainly by the local coordination environment of surface adsorption sites, while Re generally weakens H binding with little effect on short-range H–H interactions. High-throughput calculations using a DFT-informed local-environment model generate > 6.1 × 105 H-adsorption configurations, whose energetics collapse onto two surface-scaled descriptors for H loading and Re enrichment. SISSO yields a compact analytical expression that reproduces these energetics and extrapolates to larger nanovoids within the model framework. OKMC predicts lower deuterium desorption temperatures with Re decoration when small vacancy clusters dominate, with a weaker effect after cluster coarsening. This work establishes a compact two-descriptor representation of H trapping and provides a general multiscale modeling framework for irradiated materials. © 2026

Authors: Edwin E.; Jayaprakash N.
Title: Inflammation-driven multiorgan Dysfunction: Biomarker-Guided diagnosis, mechanistic insights and emerging precision therapeutic strategies
Source title: Advances in Biomarker Sciences and Technology
Abstract: Inflammation-driven multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (MODS) represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients and arises from a complex interplay of dysregulated immune responses, endothelial injury, microvascular dysfunction, metabolic disturbances, and maladaptive organ crosstalk. Although traditionally associated with sepsis, similar inflammatory pathways contribute to organ dysfunction in trauma, pancreatitis, severe viral infections, autoimmune disorders, and other critical illnesses. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying inflammation-driven MODS, with particular emphasis on cytokine amplification, innate and adaptive immune dysregulation, immunothrombosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and barrier failure across multiple organ systems. Emerging biomarkers, including inflammatory cytokines, endothelial injury markers, damage-associated molecular patterns, and organ-specific indicators, are discussed for their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. However, significant challenges remain, including biomarker variability, lack of standardized thresholds, and the absence of universally accepted diagnostic panels for routine clinical use. The review further examines organ-specific manifestations and evolving therapeutic strategies, including anti-cytokine therapies, immunomodulation, endothelial protection, extracorporeal blood purification, and metabolic-targeted interventions. Importantly, many promising anti-inflammatory therapies have demonstrated limited success in clinical translation due to patient heterogeneity, inappropriate timing of intervention, and the dynamic transition between hyperinflammatory and immunosuppressed states. Advances in precision medicine and artificial intelligence offer opportunities for individualized risk stratification and biomarker-guided treatment selection, supporting improved health outcomes, quality of life, healthcare innovation, and sustainable healthcare systems. Integrating biomarker-driven insights with mechanistic understanding may improve clinical outcomes, reduce mortality, and facilitate the development of targeted therapies for this complex syndrome. Addressing these challenges will be essential for developing phenotype-driven therapeutic approaches and improving outcomes in patients with inflammation-driven multiorgan dysfunction. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Regulating high-sodium P2 layered oxides through rational lattice modulation for fast kinetics and superior structural stability
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Layered Na-based oxides with the general formula of NaxTMO2 (TM: transition metal) have attracted significant attention due to their high compositional diversity, which enables tunable electrochemical performance as cathodes for sodium-ion batteries. However, their practical applications are often hindered by the irreversible structural transitions leading to capacity fading during cycling. Herein, we synthesize a high-sodium-content layered oxide Na34/48Ni17/48Mn24/48Ti7/48O2 (NNMTO) via the precise substitution of manganese with titanium, thereby realizing enhanced structural stability. The increased sodium content lowers the average oxidation state of the TMs, reduces the O(2p)-TM(3d-eg*) band gap, and thereby enhances O(2p)-TM(3d-eg*) orbital hybridization. The introduction of Ti4+ ions disrupts the Na+/vacancy ordering and effectively mitigates the detrimental P2-O2 phase transition during prolonged cycling. Consequently, the NNMTO cathode exhibits exceptional Na+ mobility and superior electrochemical stability, maintaining 94.8% of its initial capacity after 600 cycles under high-rate 5 C cycling within the voltage window of 2.2–4.2 V. All in all, this study provides critical insights into the rational design of high-performance P2-type layered cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries. © 2026

Title: A four-shank 32-channel microelectrode array integrated with FPGA-based online processing for multichannel neural recording
Abstract: Multichannel neuralrecording requires not only microelectrode arrays(MEAs) with sufficientspatial coverage but also stable front-end acquisition and online signal processing hardware. In this work, a four-shank 32-channel MEA and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-basedonline processing module are developed for multichannel neural recording. The four-shank structure is designed to provide broader spatialcoverage while maintaining a compact probe footprint. Platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) are modified on the electrode surfaces to improvethe electrical interface of the recording sites. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that PtNPs modification significantly improves theinterfacial properties of the electrodes. An FPGA-based module is employed to enable communication with the front-end chip and performonline signal processing. Post-implementation verification further demonstrates that the FPGA design satisfies the timing constraints whilemaintaining acceptable power consumption. The end-to-end performance of the electrophysiological recording chain is evaluated throughgain/bandwidth testing and simulated neural signal detection. The system exhibits an average gain of 45.57 dB within the main passband, witha bandwidth ranging from 4.28 to 2.36 kHz. In addition, simulated spike tests demonstrate stable online detection and waveform extraction.In addition, in vivo recordings from the hippocampal CA1 region demonstrate that the proposed system simultaneously acquires clear spikeand local field potential signals from multiple channels, with representative spike waveforms exhibiting good consistency. The combinationof a four-shank MEA with PtNPs-modified recording sites and FPGA-based online processing supports stable neural signal acquisition bothin vitro and in vivo and provides a useful foundation for future neural interface applications. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: From Screening to Site Control: Phytic-Acid Mediated P-Tuning of M–N Coordination to Balance Iodine Adsorption and Stability in Zn–I2 Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (AZIBs) show promise for grid-scale energy storage, but they are hampered by polyiodide shuttling, sluggish iodine redox kinetics, and irreversible active-site poisoning caused by uncontrolled adsorption. We provide a comprehensive screening of M1 (M1 = P, S, B) heteroatom dopants, and P is identified as the best candidate for achieving coordination-tuned, moderate adsorption that balances adsorption and catalytic activity while mitigating site poisoning. Using phytic acid as both the P source and an etchant, we create a universal in situ approach to core–shell single-atom catalysts (M2-P-CSNC, M2 = Fe, Co, Ni). The unique core–shell structure achieves stable confinement of polyiodides, rapid ion transport, and protection of active sites, while in situ P doping precisely regulates the local electronic environment and d-band center of the Fe–Nx active centers. In situ characterization confirms that Fe–P-CSNC has a strong reversible anchoring ability for polyiodides, which can significantly accelerate redox kinetics. The optimized Fe–P-CSNC/I2 exhibits almost no capacity decay after 20,000 cycles at a current density of 2 A g−1. This work’s facile heteroatom doping strategy for electronic modulation offers a reference for high-performance catalyst design in conversion-type energy storage systems. (Figure presented.) Authors: Xie L.; Yang J.; Song B.
Title: Exploring 2D Isotope Heterostructures for Atomic-Scale Control of Thermal Radiation
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials with their characteristic layered structures and weak van der Waals interlayer interactions provide a versatile platform for manipulating emergent phenomena and engineering novel functionalities in the thermal near field. Recently, it has been revealed that the energy-momentum dispersions and photonic density of states of 2D materials can be effectively modulated by isotope engineering. Here, we explore the impact of isotope composition on thermal radiation for 2D heterostructures based on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By systematically varying the number of layers, we discover that few-layer hBN amplifies the isotope-induced spectral match and mismatch between the hyperbolic phonon polaritons. The largest isotope effect is observed in monolayer hBN, where the ratio of the heat transfer coefficient between isotopically identical and maximally distinct hBN pairs reaches approximately 300. Interestingly, for emitters and receivers of different layer counts, the heat flux between isotopically distinct hBN pairs can surpass that for identical pairs. Furthermore, we reveal that thermal transport is highly sensitive to the stacking order at sub-10 nm gap sizes, as demonstrated by bilayer isotope heterostructures. Finally, to facilitate experimental study, the substrate and temperature dependence of the isotope effect are investigated. Our findings highlight the unique potential of 2D materials for isotopically engineering near-field thermal radiation with single-atomic-layer precision.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: LiMn2O4-centered manganese-based cathodes in aqueous lithium-ion batteries: Material genealogies, degradation mechanisms, and design strategies
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Aqueous lithium-ion batteries (ALIBs) represent highly promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage due to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. Concurrently, manganese-based (Mn-based) cathode materials align exceptionally well with these natures and the electrochemical stability window of aqueous electrolytes, which makes them the most extensively studied cathode materials. However, the underlying degradation mechanisms of Mn-based cathodes in aqueous systems remain to be fully elucidated. Focusing on spinel LiMn2O4 (LMO) as a quintessential model material, this review summarizes the development and material genealogies of Mn-based cathodes in ALIBs. Furthermore, both classical and emerging degradation mechanisms are scrutinized in depth, as these insights guide both contemporary and future design strategies. Under specific conditions, LMO can exhibit a kinetically maintained, metastable interfacial buffering regime in which compensating processes temporarily reduce the net degradation rate. However, continued species accumulation and interfacial heterogeneity eventually destabilize this regime, highlighting the need for precise interfacial regulation. Ultimately, this review bridges the degradation mechanisms of aqueous Mn-based cathodes with targeted modulation strategies, enabling high-voltage and long-life Mn-based cathodes for advanced ALIBs. © 2026

Title: Amplified strain partitioning driven by multiple heterostructures enables superior strength-ductility in Ti-reinforced Mg composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The strength-ductility trade-off remains a long-standing challenge for magnesium matrix composites (MMCs). Herein, we develop a novel strategy to fabricate multi-heterostructured MMCs with simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement, using a Ti/Mg-6Zn-1.5Mn composite prepared via ultrasonic-assisted semi-solid stirring, homogenization heat treatment, and hot extrusion. The constructed multi-level heterostructures consist of three key features: (i) non-uniform coarse/fine grain (CG/FG) mixed structure, (ii) nanophases with density differences between FGs and CGs, and (iii) Ti particles preferentially distributed adjacent to the nanophases. The composite exhibits exceptional comprehensive mechanical properties, with an ultimate tensile strength of 366 MPa, yield strength of 239 MPa, elongation of 20.6%, and a superior strength-ductility product of 66.29 MJ/m3. The excellent performance originates from multi-heterostructure-driven amplified strain partitioning, which induces hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening and hardening via geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation. Meanwhile, activated non-basal slip systems enable efficient intergranular slip transfer for uniform plastic deformation, and CGs effectively delay plastic instability and suppress crack propagation. This work provides new insights into the deformation mechanisms of heterostructured MMCs and offers a feasible pathway for developing advanced lightweight structural materials. © 2026

Title: Spectrally Partitioned All-Optical Memristors for Highly Linear Neuromorphic Vision Systems
Abstract: All-optical control of synaptic weights offers a promising route toward low-power and massively parallel neuromorphic hardware. However, existing optoelectronic memristors often require electrical assistance or exhibit nonlinear and asymmetric conductance updates, limiting their energy efficiency and scalability. By contrast, visible illumination activates VOx and promotes interfacial hole-assisted recombination, leading to reversible depletion of defect-state electrons and conductance depression. This wavelength-selective carrier-transfer process enables highly linear and symmetric all-optical weight updates, achieving a linearity of 0.9994 and an effective 8-bit conductance resolution. The electrical energy consumption per optically induced synaptic event is calculated to be as low as 0.63 fJ under an ultralow probing bias. By integrating the devices into a 32 × 32 all-optically programmed array, we further demonstrate hardware-based BloodMNIST microscopic blood-cell image classification with an accuracy of 96.5% and strong noise robustness. Title: Vanishing viscosity method for a class of second order Clarke subdifferential inclusions
Abstract: We study a coupled system consisting of a second-order subdifferential inclusion, in which the multivalued term is given by the Clarke subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz function and an ordinary differential equation (ODE). The studied system arises from a contact problem involving a viscoelastic body and involves two operators related to viscosity and elasticity effects. The coercivity of the viscosity operator plays a crucial role in establishing the existence result for the viscoelastic problem. In addition, we consider an elastic case in which the viscosity operator is absent, leading to a loss of coercivity. To address this difficulty, we introduce a vanishing viscosity regularization and analyze the associated approximating problem. Using known results in the coercive setting, we establish existence for the regularized system, derive uniform a priori estimates, and pass to the limit to obtain a solution to the noncoercive problem. The approach extends previous results on hemivariational inequalities (HVIs) to a coupled HVI–ODE system and provides an alternative to discretization methods, with applications in contact mechanics and systems with evolving internal state variables describing adhesion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A Manganese-Chlorella Hydrogel for an Integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” Strategy in Pancreatic Cancer Therapy
Abstract: Pancreatic cancer faces the challenges of tumor progression and postoperative pancreatic fistula during the perioperative period, which severely affect patient prognosis. In this study, an injectable self-healing multifunctional hydrogel (CMCGel) was developed based on dynamic cross‑linking between manganese ions (Mn2+) and carboxymethyl chitosan loaded with chlorella extract (CE). This platform implements an integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” (3R) strategy for comprehensive perioperative management. CMCGel exhibits distinctive pH/laser dual-responsive behavior: In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the accelerated release of CE and Mn2+ enhances photodynamic therapy and chemodynamic therapy (CDT). This combination, activated by laser and gated by endogenous pH, achieves remarkable tumor suppression rates of 85.81% in vitro and 96.01% in vivo. As pH normalizes, Mn2+ shifts from CDT to activate the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, remodeling the immune microenvironment. Crucially, CMCGel’s adhesion strength in artificial pancreatic fluid at 48 h was 4703.80 ± 50.36 Pa, only 8.17% lower than that at 10 min. This enzyme-resistant property enables durable mechanical sealing at the fistula site, reducing amylase leakage by 55.71% and creating favorable conditions for tissue repair. By integrating pH/laser-triggered combination therapy, immunomodulation, and enzyme-resistant barrier functionality into a single platform, CMCGel presents a clinically promising strategy for perioperative management of pancreatic cancer. Title: Lightweight broadband transition-metal microwave absorbers synergistic engineering of multi-interfacial polarization and hollow conductive networks
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Collaboratively constructing a three-dimensional hollow conductive network and multiple interface polarizations can simultaneously enhance the conductive loss and polarization relaxation efficiency, which is an important direction for the research and development of lightweight, wide-band, and high-performance electromagnetic wave absorption materials. Transition metal sulfides have attracted much attention due to their adjustable electronic structure and excellent intrinsic conductivity. However, single-component materials have shortcomings such as a lack of polarization sites and insufficient continuity of the conductive network, making them difficult to meet the requirements of practical applications. This study proposes a stepwise preparation strategy of etching, modification and sulfidation, using cobalt-nickel Prussian blue-like analogues (CoNi-PBA) cubes as the precursor, and preparing morphologically controllable hollow CoNi-PBA cubes by regulating the ammonia water etching time; subsequently, in situ growing NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH) nanosheets on the surface to construct a CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH core-shell structure; finally, using thiourea as the sulfur source, through hydrothermal sulfidation treatment, obtaining the CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH/FeNiS4 composite material. The final test results show that the prepared CoNi-PBA@NiFe-LDH/FeNiS4 series composite materials have a minimum reflection loss of −56.6 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.04 GHz, demonstrating excellent microwave absorbing performance. This study provides a new strategy for constructing high-performance microwave absorbing materials with multiple interface polarizations and hollow conductive networks, further deepening the understanding of the structure-performance relationship, and has very important significance for promoting the practical engineering application of transition metal-based absorbing materials. © 2026

Title: Techno-economic assessment of a solar-powered absorption air-conditioning system for a commercial building in Sudan
Abstract: This study evaluates the technical, environmental, and economic feasibility of solar-powered air conditioning (AC) systems in Sudanese buildings. Sudan’s high ambient temperatures make AC a major contributor to electricity demand. The Bank of Khartoum is selected as a case study, with an 83.4 TR solar cooling system modeled in TRNSYS (latitude 15.6°N, longitude 32.6°E). The system comprises a lithium–bromide absorption chiller, evacuated tube collectors (ETCs), and thermal energy storage (TES). The system achieves a coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.7, primary energy savings (Formula presented) of 212 MWh, and a payback period (PBP) of 13.2 years—strongly influenced by local electricity tariffs. Title: Active harmonic filters: Evolution from classical to advanced engineering practices - A comprehensive review
Abstract: The rapid growth of power-electronic converters has elevated harmonic mitigation from a secondary power-quality concern to a core requirement for grid compliance, reliable operation, and stability. Passive filters remain attractive for their simplicity and low cost, but suffer from detuning, resonance, and poor adaptability under varying conditions. Active harmonic filters (AHFs) use controlled converters to deliver adaptive, broadband compensation suited to converter-dominated grids. This paper reviews active harmonic filtering from a system-level perspective, covering shunt, series, hybrid, and unified configurations; two-level, multilevel, and modular converters; and resonant, predictive, nonlinear, and data-driven control. It treats DC-link energy, thermal stress, grid interaction, and component aging as first-order constraints rather than secondary concerns. Particular attention is given to high-power applications—most notably fast electric-vehicle (EV) charging— where compensation capability may be constrained by thermal and energy headroom, semiconductor current rating, modulation-voltage margin, DC-link ripple, and other operating limits. Performance metrics, benchmarking, and validation practices are consolidated into an AHF Minimum Reporting Set that extends comparison beyond total harmonic distortion (THD) alone; the limits of simulation-only studies are highlighted. Open challenges include weak-grid operation, wide-bandgap reliability, coordinated multi-converter control, and intelligent reliability-aware AHFs. © 2026

Authors: Jiang H.; Wang J.; Chen P.; Xu M.; Sun Q.; Hu B.; Wu N.; Zou Z.; Zhou J.
Title: Sulfur-vacancy modified hierarchical hollow Ni2CoS4 nanospheres boosting electrochemical kinetics and stability for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The sluggish reaction kinetics of positive electrode materials limit the rate performance of supercapacitors, which has become a bottleneck restricting their large-scale energy storage applications. Herein, hierarchical hollow nanosphere H-Ni2CoS4 with sulfur vacancies was prepared via hydrothermal synthesis and calcination using nickel-cobalt glycerate as the template. The H-Ni2CoS4 material exhibits an exceptional specific capacitance (Cs) of 2162 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1. The as-fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (H-Ni2CoS4||activated carbon) delivers an energy density of 63.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 384.1 W kg−1 within a voltage window of 0–1.6 V. After 18,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 in 1 M KOH, its capacitance retention reaches 80.71%. Experimental investigations in conjunction with density functional theory calculations uncover that the integration of sulfur vacancies and a hierarchical hollow structure can expose richer active sites and sustain effective redox processes. Compared with single Ni- or Co-based sulfides, the d-band center of nickel-cobalt composite sulfides is effectively regulated, which optimizes the adsorption of hydroxyl ions on metallic active centers, improves electronic conductivity, accelerates ionic mobility, and enhances interfacial charge accumulation. The present work simultaneously boosts the electrochemical reversible capacitance and structural stability, demonstrating great application potential as state-of-the-art electrode materials toward supercapacitor applications. © 2026

Title: Engineering W/Mo-modified Ni3S2 with local crystalline/disordered interfacial domains for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
Abstract: The rational engineering of crystalline/disordered interfacial domains with tailored electronic properties represents a promising strategy for developing high-performance electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, a three-dimensional self-supported W/Mo-modified Ni3S2-based electrocatalyst with local crystalline/disordered interfacial domains (Ni3S2@W:Mo-0.2:0.2) is fabricated through a facile hydrothermal strategy. Structural characterizations support the coexistence of crystalline Ni3S2 domains and adjacent Ni-containing W/Mo/O-associated disordered regions, while the combined experimental and theoretical results suggest interfacial electronic regulation and enhanced alkaline HER kinetics. The local interfacial structure is associated with interfacial charge-transfer behavior. Consequently, the electrode requires an average overpotential of 101.00 ± 1.73 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH, together with improved apparent kinetics, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and stable operation at 100 mA cm−2 for 100 h. The enhanced activity arises from the combined contributions of accessible surface area, ECSA-normalized apparent specific activity, and charge-transfer kinetics. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest modulated H* adsorption energetics and a lower water dissociation barrier. Gas chromatography (GC) analysis quantitatively confirms sustained H2 generation. This work provides insights into interfacial engineering and electronic structure regulation for advanced electrocatalyst design. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Thermal atomic migration for contact doping in scaled carbon nanotube transistors
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Single‑walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are considered promising candidates for next‑generation transistors owing to their atomic thickness, high carrier mobility, and dangling‑bond‑free surfaces. However, as technology nodes continue to scale down, achieving reliable electrical contacts between SWCNTs and metal electrodes at the sub‑nanometer scale remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on localized thermally driven migration of physically encapsulated iodine inside SWCNTs to improve the contact performance and overall device characteristics of individual SWCNT transistors. Spectroscopic characterization combined with theoretical calculations confirms that the strong charge transfer between the iodine crystal and the SWCNT transforms the nanotube in the contact regions into a degenerate semiconductor, thereby significantly reducing the contact resistance at the metal electrode interface. By applying Joule heating to drive the migration of iodine atoms, in situ dedoping of the channel region is achieved. The contact resistance of film‑based devices is reduced to 1.7 kΩ μm. For individual SWCNT devices, the on‑state current increases approximately 40 times, the on/off ratio increases 37 times, and the contact resistance decreases by a factor of 5. This work presents a proof-of-concept contact engineering strategy for high-performance SWCNT transistors. © 2026

Title: Heavy-atom node engineering in perylene diimide-based MOFs for efficient singlet-oxygen-mediated aerobic oxidation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Efficient singlet oxygen (1O2)-mediated selective oxidation requires photocatalysts capable of promoting intersystem crossing and enriching triplet states. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a multifunctional platform for photocatalytic detoxification, yet how metal nodes regulate excited-state dynamics and triplet exciton formation remains insufficiently understood. Herein, we construct two isostructural perylene diimide (PDI)-based MOFs to systematically elucidate node-dependent spin-orbit coupling effects. The Hf nodes promote spin-related excited-state evolution through a heavy-atom effect, favoring triplet-state formation and 1O2 generation. As a result, the Hf-based MOF PDI-MOF(Hf) exhibits outstanding performance in mustard gas simulant detoxification, achieving a half-life of ∼ 4 min while maintaining high selectivity, and exhibits wide-ranging applications in the selective oxidation of aromatic sulfides into sulfoxides. Phosphorescence and in-situ electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy measurements corroborate the enhanced triplet-state processes and dominant 1O2-mediated pathway. This work establishes a clear correlation between heavy-atom node engineering and spin-dependent photophysics, providing a general strategy to overcome intersystem crossing limitations in organic chromophores and advancing the rational design of MOF photocatalysts for detoxification and selective oxidation. © 2026

Title: Tailoring strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloy thin sheets via asymmetric extrusion and two-stage cross rolling: The effect of hot rolling temperature
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Mg alloy thin sheets have broad application prospects, but conventional rolling processes often fail to achieve both high strength and ductility, and the scope for property optimization is limited. In this work, ZE21B Mg alloy thin sheets with a thickness of 0.2 mm were fabricated by asymmetric extrusion combined with two-stage cross rolling. The effect of hot rolling temperature (350, 400, and 450 °C) on the final microstructure and mechanical properties was investigated. The results show that the asymmetrically extruded sheet exhibits fine equiaxed grains and a weak basal texture, providing a favorable microstructure for subsequent rolling. As the hot rolling temperature increases, the grain size of the hot rolled sheets grows from 7.75 to 48.76 μm. Under the same subsequent warm rolling and annealing conditions, the sheet hot rolled at 350 °C undergoes pronounced recrystallization, forming a mixed structure of recrystallized and deformed grains with high dislocation density, achieving an elongation of 28.03% ± 2.1% and an ultimate tensile strength of 356.7 ± 5.3 MPa. In contrast, recrystallization is strongly suppressed in the sheets hot rolled at 400 and 450 °C, and the microstructures are dominated by irregular dislocation walls and regular sub-grains, respectively, resulting in the ultimate tensile strength increasing to 387.6 ± 4.3 and 405.3 ± 6.9 MPa, respectively, but the elongation dropping to 18.60% ± 1.3% and 6.50% ± 2.6%. Simply by adjusting the hot rolling temperature, the strength and ductility can be continuously adjusted, enabling on-demand tailoring of mechanical properties within a certain range. © 2026

Title: Assessment of asphalt pavement segregation under varying construction conditions via multi-scale 3D texture analysis
Source title: International Journal of Transportation Science and Technology
Abstract: Asphalt pavement segregation, characterized by non-uniform aggregate distribution, detrimentally impacts pavement performance and service life. Conventional two-dimensional (2D) image-based approaches are limited in quantifying three-dimensional (3D) texture geometry and multi-scale features, with environmental factors introducing evaluation uncertainties. This study proposes a framework to quantify segregation by decomposing it into two morphological types: surface aggregate clustering (assessed via 2D-entropy coefficient of variation for planar uniformity) and vertical stratification (evaluated using coarse-to-fine aggregate ratio derived from multi-scale relative energy for gradation deviation). By leveraging 3D laser scanning and 2D wavelet decomposition across nine scales, this research investigates five asphalt mixtures (AC-13, AC-16, AC-25, OGFC-13, SMA-13) under varying temperatures (95–165 °C) and compaction passes (12–24). Results reveal that temperature influences fine aggregate surface uniformity in dense-graded mixtures, while compaction enhances uniformity in SMA-13. Vertical segregation in dense-graded mixtures decreases with elevated temperatures, unaffected by compaction intensity. The study provides new perspectives and methods for assessing asphalt pavement segregation in pavement construction quality control scenarios. Copyright © 2026. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Post-combustion carbon capture in the cement industry: A critical review of its decarbonization potential
Abstract: The cement industry is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, accounting for nearly 7% of global anthropogenic CO2 emissions. As cement demand continues to rise, rapid and substantial emission reductions are imperative to keep global warming close to 2 °C by the end of the century. Extensive research over the past decade has explored multiple decarbonization pathways—including alternative low-carbon clinkers, process optimization, and the increased use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). Although such strategies offer meaningful reductions, their overall impact is constrained by limited material availability, performance challenges, slow commercialization rates, and the difficulties of scaling manufacturing solutions within established production pipelines. In this context, post-combustion carbon capture (PCC) has emerged as a particularly versatile and high-impact pathway for mitigating CO2 emissions from both existing and new cement plants, offering a scalable and technologically compatible route to rapid emissions reduction. This review critically examines the CO2 challenge in the cement sector and evaluates currently available mitigation strategies. The review subsequently elaborates on PCC as one of the fastest and most practical solutions by presenting its key technologies, contemporary applications, and associated limitations. Overall, the literature indicates that while PCC is considered among the more viable options, it still faces significant challenges that limit its large-scale deployment. © 2026 The Authors. Title: SPATIAL MODELLING OF DENGUE OUTBREAK RISK BY INTEGRATING LARVAL DENSITY AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS IN AN URBAN AREA
Abstract: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia. Effective prevention requires moving beyond reactive case-based responses to proactive, spatially-targeted interventions based on comprehensive risk factors. This study explores a spatial model to assess DHF outbreak risk in the working area of the Somba Opu Health Center, Gowa Regency, Indonesia. Primary and secondary data were integrated through GIS overlay analysis. Key parameters included larval density (House Index, Container Index, Breteau Index), microclimate (temperature, humidity), socio-environmental vulnerability (population and building density), and community capacity (implementation of the PSN 3M program). Results: Spatial analysis revealed significant heterogeneity in dengue hemorrhagic fever risk across the study area. High-risk clusters were identified in Katangka, Tompobalang, and Tombolo villages, associated with high larval indices, optimal microclimates, and high population density. Larval density showed a significant positive correlation with these optimal temperature and humidity ranges. In contrast, villages with consistent Mosquito Nest Eradication implementation, such as Kalegowa and Bonto-Bontoa, exhibited higher larva-free rates and lower overall risk. The integrated spatial model, incorporating entomological, climatic, and socio-environmental data, successfully categorized the region into low, medium, and high-risk zones. This precise mapping enables targeted, cost-effective vector control and allows health authorities to prioritize interventions in high-risk areas for sustainable dengue prevention. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. Title: Atomistic origins of the sluggish cathodic reduction of α-FeOOH in atmospheric rust layers: A first-principles study
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: α-FeOOH is the predominant protective phase in atmospheric rust layers, yet the atomistic origins of its sluggish cathodic reduction remain unclear. Here, first-principles calculations elucidate its preferred surface state, electron-accepting ability, and reduction pathway. Dissociative water adsorption is favored over [H+/Cl–] and [H+/HSO3–] adsorption on α-FeOOH(110), yielding the lowest surface energy among the examined states (0.602 J/m2). The resulting hydroxylated surface has an electron affinity of 3.928 eV, lower than those of representative β-FeOOH·[H+/Cl–]0.167 (4.886 eV) and [H+/HSO3–]-modified γ-FeOOH (5.228 eV), indicating weaker electron uptake. Upon electron injection, charge localizes on Fe sites, causing Fe(III)-to-Fe(II) reduction, FeO6 expansion, and Fe-OH weakening. OH− removal, adjacent-OH condensation, and lattice rearrangement then drive transformation toward inverse-spinel Fe3O4. Adjacent-OH condensation to form H2O* is the rate-determining step, with a barrier of 1.227 eV. Thus, the stable hydroxylated surface, weak electron uptake, and hindered dehydration explain the sluggish reduction of α-FeOOH. © 2026

Title: An integrated framework of emergy analysis and LMDI for assessing sustainability: a case study of tobacco production system
Abstract: To tackle the challenges of resource consumption and environmental pressure in agricultural production systems, quantifying sustainability performance and identifying its driving mechanisms are critical. This study introduces an integrated framework based on emergy analysis and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI), covering production investigation, system analysis, sustainability evaluation, and driver exploration, and ultimately guiding targeted production recommendations. The results reveal that tobacco energy output rose from 3.5 × 10^16 J in 2004 to 5.1 × 10^16 J in 2013, before declining to 3.3 × 10^16 J in 2021. From 2004 to 2021, the environmental sustainability index increased from 0.46 to 0.54, while the environmental loading ratio decreased from 3.36 to 3.00, indicating a steady improvement in sustainability. Significant spatial variability was observed across provinces. LMDI decomposition revealed that economic efficiency contributed significantly to the sustainability improvement (0.53), while changes in renewable resource dependency offset -0.52 of this gain. Title: Chemical doping and crystal-facet engineering synergistically enhanced resistivity and piezoelectricity in Bi4Ti3O12 high-temperature ceramics

Abstract: The low resistivity (ρ) and inferior piezoelectricity of bismuth layer-structured Bi4Ti3O12 (BIT) ferroelectrics hinder their application in high-temperature electromechanical coupling. To address this challenge, a synergistic strategy combining W6+/Nb5+/Zr4+ heterovalent co-doping with crystal-facet engineering is proposed. This dual modification elevates the high-temperature resistivity by nearly an order of magnitude (∼106 Ω cm at 540 °C) and yields a large piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 40.8 pC N−1) together with a considerable Curie temperature (TC = 653 °C). Furthermore, the modified ceramic exhibits excellent thermal stability, maintaining a low d33 fluctuation (∼16%) at RT-540 °C alongside high ρ (>106 Ω cm). The enhanced resistivity is attributed to the widened bandgap and suppressed oxygen vacancies brought by W6+/Nb5+/Zr4+ co-doping. The improved d33 originates from the fine domains with flexible polarization caused by the local structural heterogeneity. Crucially, the crystal-facet engineering approach exposes the highly active polar pseudo-perovskite (a-axis) facets of the ceramic grains. This exposure effectively releases the clamping effect from the insulating (Bi2O2)2⁺ layers, dramatically facilitating domain switching and further amplifying the piezoelectric contribution of the fine domains. Title: Hydrophobic Eutectogels Reinforced by Zn2+-Coordinated Lignin Nanoparticles for Underwater Wearable Electronics
Abstract: Wearable flexible sensors for underwater communication and biomotion monitoring are gaining attention. However, developing gel-based strain sensors with high toughness, anti-swelling performance, robust underwater adhesion, and long-term stability remains challenging. Herein, we present a hydrophobic eutectogel (DPF-Zn@LNP-HEG) fabricated via the assembly of a polymerizable hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (PHDES), 2-phenoxyethyl acrylate (PEA), and Zn2+-coordinated lignin nanoparticles (Zn@LNP). The resulting structure, composed of hydrophobic polymer networks and metal-phenolic complexes, forms hydrophobic microdomains that disrupt the hydration layer and prevent water penetration. Meanwhile, Zn@LNP serve as dynamic sacrificial cross-linkers, enhancing the material’s mechanical strength, energy dissipation, and anti-swelling properties. The resulting eutectogel exhibits remarkable tensile strength (1.14 MPa), superior toughness (3.15 MJ m−3), excellent anti-swelling properties (< 1% after 30 days), and robust underwater adhesion (1.07 MPa on glass). Based on these properties, we demonstrate an underwater strain sensor with high sensitivity (gauge factor = 8.12) and long-term stability, enabling underwater Morse code transmission, biomotion monitoring, and Bluetooth-based tracking of swimming movements. This work not only provides a versatile design paradigm for multifunctional underwater sensing platforms but also advances the high-value utilization of bio-based materials in next-generation flexible electronics. Authors: Dai J.; Zhang S.; Fu W.; Shi J.; Li X.; Mei H.; Hu S.; Song X.
Title: Mn powder-assisted interfacial reaction engineering for high-performance FeCoNiCrMn HEA-SiC brazed joints: Microstructure, properties and mechanism
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Reliable joining of SiC ceramics to metals is a critical technical approach to expand the engineering applications of SiC. However, the brazing of SiC and metals has long been plagued by three fundamental challenges: poor wettability of liquid metals on SiC, uncontrolled formation of brittle intermetallic compounds, and large residual stresses induced by thermal mismatch. In recent years, face-centered cubic (FCC) structured high-entropy alloys (HEAs) such as FeCoNiCrMn have exhibited exceptional high-temperature mechanical properties, good ductility, and a thermal expansion coefficient well-matched to SiC due to their unique “cocktail effect”, making them ideal structural materials for joining with SiC ceramics. The multiple active elements dissolved from the HEA can promote the wetting of SiC, but uncontrolled dissolution of the HEA will lead to more complex interfacial reaction issues. To address the above problems, this study proposes a novel strategy for indirectly controlling the interfacial reaction on the ceramic side by pre-placing homologous elements to regulate the dissolution of the base metal. The results show that the addition of Mn powder alters the dissolution mode of the HEA, enabling precise regulation of the active elements dissolved into the filler metal. An ordered gradient compound layer with the sequence of Ni2Si/Mn3Ni2Si/Ni16Cr6Si7 from the SiC side to the brazing seam is formed on the SiC interface. This multilayer structure transforms the crack propagation from straight propagation along the Ni2Si layer to tortuous propagation across multiple compound layers, and the fracture mode changes from pure brittle fracture to ductile-brittle mixed fracture, significantly increasing the shear strength of the joint. This study provides a new idea and feasible technical strategy for the reliable joining of ceramics and high-entropy alloys. © 2026

Authors: Gao M.; Sun X.; Huang Y.; Fa Z.; Wang S.; Lu J.; Lu H.; Guo A.; Mao X.
Title: Residual nitrogen aggravating hydrogen embrittlement via boron grain-boundary depletion in press-hardened martensitic steel
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The increasing use of scrap-based electric arc furnace routes inevitably introduces elevated residual nitrogen into press-hardened steels, raising concerns regarding their reliability in hydrogen-containing environments. In this work, the effect of residual nitrogen on hydrogen embrittlement (HE) in press-hardened martensitic steel was systematically investigated using steels with controlled nitrogen levels. Slow strain rate tensile tests after hydrogen pre-charging reveal that increasing nitrogen content markedly aggravates HE susceptibility, with the HE index rising from ∼43% to ∼61%, accompanied by a transition toward intergranular-dominated fracture. Microstructural characterization confirms that both steels exhibit fully martensitic structures after hot stamping; however, higher nitrogen deteriorates hardenability and promotes the formation of coarser and more numerous TiN particles. Thermodynamic calculations and inclusion analyses demonstrate that elevated nitrogen enhances TiN precipitation, which modifies boron partitioning. Atom probe tomography provides direct atomic-scale evidence that boron segregates to prior-austenite grain boundaries in the low-nitrogen steel, whereas such segregation is absent in the high-nitrogen counterpart, indicating nitrogen-induced boron depletion at grain boundaries. First-principles calculations show that boron segregation strengthens grain-boundary cohesion (Estr ≈ −0.3 eV), suggesting that the loss of boundary boron reduces interfacial stability and facilitates hydrogen-enhanced decohesion. The combined results establish a mechanistic framework in which residual nitrogen aggravates HE primarily by suppressing boron grain-boundary segregation rather than by altering the martensitic matrix itself. These findings provide critical guidance for nitrogen control in sustainable electric-arc-furnace-produced press-hardened steels. © 2026

Title: Knowledge-grounded multimodal cognitive decision-making for aerospace machining: A physics-aware reasoning framework for generative process planning of special-shaped features
Abstract: Complex aerospace products encompass numerous special-shaped features (SSFs), whose machining processes rely on highly customized process planning. Traditional data-driven discriminative models predominantly operate as physics-agnostic "black boxes." Moreover, applying general-purpose Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to manufacturing often causes "physical hallucinations", generating linguistically plausible but mechanically infeasible process plans. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a Knowledge-Grounded Multimodal Cognitive Framework (KGMCF), which extends discriminative feature recognition with physics-aware generative reasoning for machining decision-making. First, an Aerospace Multimodal Process Knowledge Graph (Aero-MPKG) is constructed to formalize manufacturing constraints. A cross-modal visual anchoring mechanism is introduced, enabling the MLLM to precisely map unstructured engineering drawings to discrete symbolic nodes via topological embedding retrieval. Second, a KG-guided Symbolic-Neural Synthesis (SNS) strategy is developed to construct a multimodal instruction-tuning dataset, thereby driving a multi-stage physics-aware Chain-of-Thought (CoT). Finally, a symbolic verification loop with semantic traceback detects constraint-violating parameters and triggers self-correction through natural language feedback. Extensive experiments on an aerospace vortex shell benchmark demonstrate that the KGMCF effectively suppresses the Graph-based Physics Violation Rate (G-PvR) from 24.52% (vanilla MLLM) to 9.62%, while simultaneously achieving a Tool Selection Accuracy (TSA) of 93.12% and a Machining Parameter Selection Accuracy (MPSA) of 91.44%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li N.; Wu L.H.; Wu H.; Li F.S.; Zhang H.; Xue P.; Liu F.C.; Ni D.R.; Xiao B.L.; Ma Z.Y.
Title: Fabrication of a large-area, uniformly fine-grained high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance by collaborative friction stir welding and processing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Fabricating large-area, uniformly fine-grained high-entropy alloy (HEA) remains challenging because welding can introduce microstructural heterogeneity and degrade material performance. Here, a new approach, termed collaborative friction stir welding and processing (C-FSW/P), was developed by integrating FSW and FSP, which share the same basic principle. The approach eliminated weld-induced microstructural heterogeneity during the fabrication of large-area fine-grained sheets and transformed cast-alloy slices into a large-area CoCrFeNiMn sheet with a uniform equiaxed fine-grained microstructure (∼2 μm). The resulting fine-grained HEA exhibited an excellent strength-ductility synergy, achieving tensile strengths of 724 and 1150 MPa at 293 and 77 K, with elongations of 34% and 45%, respectively. The critical twinning stress in the fine-grained processing zone (PZ) was determined experimentally and theoretically to be 957 ± 27 MPa. Deformation twins were first observed at true strains of ∼8.4% at 77 K and ∼27% at 293 K. At 293 K, the work-hardening rate (WHR) decreased continuously with increasing strain because deformation twinning was activated only at a late stage. By contrast, the higher WHR at 77 K resulted from the earlier activation of deformation twins, which acted together with stacking faults and secondary twins to provide additional work hardening. Relative to the values at 293 K, the tensile strength and elongation of the PZ at 77 K increased by 37% and 24%, respectively, owing to twin-boundary strengthening. The PZ also exhibited superior corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, as evidenced by its higher corrosion potential (−0.225 V) and lower corrosion current density (0.084 μA/cm2) relative to the base material. This improvement arose from the formation of a stable, dense Cr2O3-rich passive film. This study establishes an efficient short-process route for fabricating large-area, structurally uniform ultrafine- and fine-grained materials without size constraints. © 2026

Authors: Yan Y.; Lun A.; Gao B.; Liu Y.; Jia D.; Zhou Y.; Huang X.
Title: Advances in TMDs-Based Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers: From Structural Engineering to Multicomponent Synergy
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered considerable attention as advanced electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) materials due to their unique layered structures, tunable electronic properties, and intrinsic defect-induced polarization mechanisms. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes recent advances in TMDs-based absorbers, with particular focus on two fundamental development strategies. The first involves multiscale structural design of pure phase TMDs spanning from atomic to submillimeter dimensions, achieved through precise defect regulation, phase engineering, and sophisticated morphological manipulation to optimize electromagnetic parameters and attenuation capabilities. The second strategy focuses on constructing multicomponent composite systems, incorporating dielectric matrices, magnetic elements, and multicomponent hybrids to achieve synergistic enhancement through interfacial polarization, conductive loss, and magnetic dissipation mechanisms. The review critically analyzes pioneering research achievements across various subfields while identifying specific challenges and opportunities within each domain. Future perspectives highlight emerging frontiers including atomic level interface engineering, inverse design of multicomponent and multiscale architectures, sustainable large-scale synthesis techniques, and development of multifunctional smart-response systems. This work aims to establish fundamental principles and provide forward-looking guidance for designing next-generation high-performance TMDs-based EMA materials with tailored functionalities. Authors: He W.; Mou B.; Qian C.; Li T.; Song J.
Title: Tight sandstone gas exploration potential of the Upper Triassic Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin, SW China
Abstract: The Xichang Basin, excluding the Sichuan Basin areas, is an important strategic replacement zone in Sichuan Province. Given the variability of continental oil and gas exploration conditions, the entire basin must be considered as the study area. The geological conditions of tight gas in the Baiguowan Formation were systematically analyzed using extensive core, logging, and field outcrop data to assess the exploration and development potential of continental Baiguowan Formation tight sandstone gas (hereafter referred to as tight gas) in the Xichang Basin. The results indicate that the Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin can be vertically divided into three complete third-order sequences. (1) The channel sandstones deposited in low-stand system tracts of the first and second third-order sequences contain thick, laterally continuous sand bodies with well-developed joints and fissures, forming excellent reservoirs for tight gas accumulation. (2) The tight gas of the Baiguowan Formation in the Xichang Basin is mainly concentrated in the Bai 1 and Bai 2 Members, which exhibit favorable hydrocarbon source conditions, moderate thermal evolution, high hydrocarbon generation intensity, broad reservoir distribution, excellent reservoir properties, favorable early structural settings, and vertically stacked multilayer gas storage. (3) The Baiguowan Formation experienced rapid burial and subsequent denudation, and the tight gas reservoirs underwent two hydrocarbon charging events followed by two accumulation periods, showing a characteristic pattern of accumulation controlled by source, structure, and sedimentary facies. (4) Based on the source rock quality, reservoir type, and hydrocarbon generation intensity, the Jiatie–Sikai zone is identified as the most favorable exploration area, covering 1860 km2 with a tight gas resource of 6756 × 108 m3. Further investigations should focus on five promising tight gas sweet spot areas: Southern Zhaojue, Northern Zhaojue, Lieridi, Tiejia, and Sikai. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Shankar D.; Nouri J.; Ho S.; Hitesh B.; Sankaramuthukumar M.
Title: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer municipal plastics for enhanced environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical recycling of municipal plastic waste can reduce landfill burden, energy demand, and environmental impacts while recovering reusable polymers. The study objectives were to assess the performance of polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene using polymer-specific pre-processing methods, shredding, thermal consolidation, and compression moulding. The assessment focused on waste minimization, material recovery, energy requirements, estimated carbon dioxide emission reductions, sustainability, and mechanical and thermal performance. METHODS: A total of 37 kilograms of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene was separately processed using polymer-specific treatment and compression moulding. Environmental performance was evaluated within a cradle-to-gate framework using secondary emission factors, and the Sustainability Index was derived from predefined parameters. Recycled materials were evaluated for mechanical and thermal properties. Exploratory one-way analysis of variance assessed polymer differences, with probability values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. FINDINGS: Waste reduction and material recovery rates exceeded 95 percent for all polymers, with low-density polyethylene achieving the highest recovery of 99 percent. Low-density polyethylene also showed the lowest energy consumption of 0.95 kilowatt-hours per kilogram and the observed sustainability index of 82.6 ± 2.1, although polymer-specific differences in the Sustainability Index were not statistically significant. Polyethylene terephthalate showed the highest tensile strength (55.2 megapascals), compressive strength (83.4 megapascals), density (1.36 grams per cubic centimetre), and carbon dioxide emission reduction (2.10 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilogram). High-density polyethylene showed intermediate performance. Analysis of variance indicated polymer-specific differences, with F-statistic values of 1.72–412.3 and probability values of <0.001–0.27. After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, most physical and mechanical properties, energy consumption, and carbon dioxide emission reduction showed significant differences, whereas landfill diversion and the Sustainability Index did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene achieved high material recovery while maintaining mechanical and thermal properties. The polymers showed differences in material recovery, energy consumption, carbon dioxide emission reduction, and evaluated material properties. Further evaluation using heterogeneous municipal plastic waste and larger-scale processing is required. © 2027 The author(s). Title: SHAPE OPTIMIZATION FOR PIECEWISE PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION IN INVERSE DIFFUSION PROBLEMS WITH A SINGLE BOUNDARY MEASUREMENT
Abstract: This paper proposes a unified shape and coefficient optimization approach for inverse problems governed by diffusion equations. The associated forward problem is considered with a Robin boundary condition, physically motivated in diffuse optical tomography to model partial reflection of light at tissue boundaries. The main objective is the recovery of the piecewise-defined absorption coefficient together with its underlying interface from a single boundary measurement. To this end, a shape-based reconstruction approach is formulated in which the interface is introduced as a geometric unknown governing the piecewise structure of the absorption coefficient. While classical approaches rely on the Fréchet derivative with respect to spatially varying parameters, the Eulerian derivative with respect to the interface is additionally exploited. This leads to a unified framework for the simultaneous recovery of the coefficient and the geometry under the single-measurement setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, even for complex and non-convex interfaces. © 2026, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. All rights reserved.

Abstract: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) is a liquid waste from coal mining by-products. AMD is a highly corrosive liquid (pH 1.5 – 4.0) and contains heavy metals, which is one of the problems in coal mining. Therefore, the study aims to fabricate and characterize composite ceramic membranes made from silica extracted from rice husk ash (RHA) and modified with high-performance activated carbon (Maxsorb III) to boost heavy metal adsorption capacity. The membranes are produced through extrusion molding and stepwise sintering processes. The results were analyzed using SEM-EDS, XRF, XRD, and BET. SEM-EDS revealed the formation and distribution of pores, with Si, O, and C as the main elements. Increasing the activated carbon content from 10 to 20 wt% increased the BET specific surface area from 238 to 412 m²/g and the average pore diameter from 16 to 25 nm, indicating increased pore development and surface area. Authors: Du P.; Li Y.; Yu H.; Qiang Y.; Deng S.; Li X.
Title: Substituent effects of thiourea derivatives on steel corrosion inhibition in 1.0 M HCl: An experimental and theoretical study
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Carbon steel corrosion in acidic pickling media remains a critical industrial challenge. Herein, thiourea (TU) and three substituted thiourea derivatives, including phenylthiourea (PTU), allylthiourea (ATU), and methylthiourea (MTU), were investigated to clarify substituent-regulated corrosion inhibition and adsorption behavior in 1.0 M HCl. Weight loss, electrochemical tests, SEM, AFM, XPS, and TOF-SIMS analyses were integrated with quantum chemical calculations, first-principles calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations to establish the relationship among inhibition efficiency, interfacial film structure, and molecular adsorption mechanism. The results show that all four thiourea derivatives effectively suppress the corrosion of carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl and behave as mixed-type inhibitors. At 20 °C and 100 mg L−1, the inhibition efficiencies of TU, PTU, ATU, and MTU reach 88.1%, 87.8%, 89.1%, and 89.8%, respectively. Surface analyses reveal that MTU forms a more continuous, homogeneous, and compact adsorption film on the steel surface. First-principles calculations demonstrate pronounced coupling between molecular orbitals and Fe surface states after adsorption, with evident hybridization of S 3p and N 2p orbitals with Fe 3d orbitals. In particular, Fe-S interactions dominate interfacial bonding and charge transfer. These results show that inhibition performance depends not only on single-molecule adsorption strength, but also on orbital coupling, film coverage, interfacial homogeneity, and thermal stability, providing molecular-level guidance for designing efficient thiourea-based inhibitors for acidic media. © 2026

Title: Tailoring precipitation and thermal stability through pre-forging: High-density T-phase precipitation in a heat-resistant Al-Cu-Mg-Mn alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Pre-forging before homogenization was applied to an Al-Cu-Mg-Mn-based heat-resistant alloy to improve elevated-temperature strength and post-exposure stability. XRD shows similar overall diffraction features in the two samples, whereas SEM and TEM reveal that pre-forging fragments coarse intermetallic compounds (IMCs) and promotes a finer, denser T-phase dispersion retained through extrusion, solution treatment, and T6 aging. The average T-phase size decreases from 233 to 148 nm, and the particle count in the same observation area increases from 444 to 851. The improved stability is associated with suppressed Cu-rich grain-boundary precipitate coarsening and retained fine, dense intragranular T-phase dispersion. Authors: Xu Q.; Yuan R.
Title: Existence and Hausdorff convergence of sliding phenomena in traveling waves for a fast-slow Keller-Segel equation
Abstract: A one-dimensional Keller-Segel equation with a piecewise-defined reaction term depending on the density gradient gives rise to a nonsmooth fast-slow system. Using Filippov convexification and geometric singular perturbation theory, we prove the existence of sliding traveling wave solutions for sufficiently small ε > 0 and characterize the corresponding sliding region. In the singular limit ε=0, we construct a singular sliding heteroclinic orbit on the critical manifold and show that it persists for sufficiently small ε > 0 under appropriate conditions on the wave speed and model parameters. The family of perturbed orbits converges to the singular orbit in the Hausdorff distance as ε → 0. These results provide a rigorous construction of sliding traveling waves for a chemotaxis model with gradient-dependent switching. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
