Title: Advances and perspectives in genetically encoded biosensors for biomarker detection and theranostic circuits
Abstract: Effective biomarker detection is critical for timely and accurate clinical disease diagnosis. However, conventional analytical methodologies are often constrained by laborious procedures, reliance on specialized equipment, and an inherent inability to perform continuous in situ monitoring. To circumvent these limitations, synthetic biology has pioneered the development of genetically encoded biosensors as a rapid, highly sensitive, and cost-effective alternative. This review specifically focuses on transcriptional regulation-based biosensors, primarily those utilizing allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) and two-component systems (TCSs). By integrating these regulatory sensing modules into engineered microbial chassis, researchers can achieve continuous, real-time biomarker monitoring even within complex and otherwise inaccessible physiological environments. This review particularly focuses on microbial chassis rather than mammalian systems due to their highly tractable genetics, rapid response kinetics, and their unique potential to be deployed as autonomous living probiotics for in situ theranostics. Furthermore, coupling these sensors with engineered actuator genes enables the construction of intelligent therapeutic genetic circuits. This closed-loop theranostic paradigm facilitates simultaneous, real-time diagnosis and autonomous, localized therapeutic interventions, paving the way for personalized and dose-adaptive precision medicine. Finally, we summarize recent advancements in these biosensor platforms, explore their applications in targeted disease interventions, and discuss the contemporary challenges alongside future perspectives for their clinical translation. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Design of strong anti-corrosion and high electrical conductivity protective bilayer coatings on bipolar plates in PEMWE cells by machine learning
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Bipolar plates (BPs) are crucial components in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis cells, demanding protective coatings that simultaneously possess strong anti-corrosion and high electrical conductivity to ensure long-life durability. In this work, a machine learning (ML) method is established to accelerate the design and development of protective bilayer coatings on Ti BPs. Firstly, comprehensive datasets on corrosion resistance and electrical conductivity of metal/metallic carbide (nitride) bilayer coatings are compiled from published articles. Based on the optimized subset and regression algorithms, ML models for coating performance are trained and validated. The ML screening identifies TaC/Ta and TaN/Ta bilayer coatings as primary candidates, which exhibit strong anti-corrosion properties and good electrical conductivities. To experimentally validate the ML predictions, TaC/Ta, TaN/Ta, and NbN/Nb bilayer coatings are deposited on Ti BPs. Title: Continuous Fabrication of Bioinspired All-Biomass Aerogel Fibers for Thermal Insulation
Abstract: Aerogel fibers have been considered as a promising solution for thermal protection textiles due to their high porosity and low thermal conductivity. However, the scalable production of sustainable and mechanical strong aerogel fibers remains a critical challenge. Here, inspired by the porous core–shell structure of polar bear hair, we report a continuous strategy to fabricate all-biomass aerogel fibers featuring an encapsulated core–shell architecture using silk fibroin as the core and cellulose as the shell. This tunable structure, with radially aligned sheet-like pores and adjustable shell thickness, is achieved through hydrogen bond-driven cellulose contraction and alcohol-induced curing of sheet-like silk fibroin. Such a porous architecture effectively suppresses convective heat transfer and promotes a multi-reflective effect for infrared radiation. The resulting fibers exhibit good mechanical robustness with a tensile load of a single aerogel fiber is up to 200 g without reinforcement. Meanwhile, the aerogel fiber maintains high porosity (79.78%), low thermal conductivity (52.4 ± 4.2 mW m−1 K−1), and low density (0.193 ± 0.01 g cm−3). Furthermore, an aerogel glove fabricated from these fibers demonstrates good thermal insulation. These results provide new insights for the design of biomimetic aerogel fibers with core–shell architecture, offering a scalable and eco-friendly pathway toward advanced wearable thermal management. Abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have drawn considerable interest in photocatalysis owing to their π‑conjugated networks, large specific surface areas, and adjustable pore structures. Constructing S‑scheme heterostructures by coupling COFs with suitable semiconductors can facilitate charge separation and boost both oxidation and reduction capacities. This review first outlines the evolution of S‑scheme heterojunctions and the regulation principles of interfacial charge carrier migration. Title: Wearable Electronics for Precision Diagnosis Through Advanced Manufacturing and Integration
Abstract: Wearable electronics are rapidly transforming healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and molecular signals directly at the point of need. This shift supports a transition from episodic, generalized care toward precision diagnosis, where individualized, longitudinal data guide early detection, risk stratification, and treatment decisions. Central to this transformation is the convergence of advanced manufacturing and heterogeneous integration strategies, which enable the development of compact, multimodal, and highly conformable diagnostic platforms. In this review, we examine how advances in materials engineering, micro/nanofabrication, and system integration have transformed wearable devices from single-parameter sensors into fully integrated, multimodal diagnostic systems. We outline key architectures and transduction mechanisms and highlight manufacturing approaches such as printing, 3D fabrication, photolithography, and laser writing. We emphasize heterogeneous integration strategies that combine sensing, electronics, power, and communication into skin-conformal platforms for long-term use. These advances enable precision diagnostics through continuous monitoring, multimodal data fusion, and individualized baselines. We also outline key challenges to clinical translation and discuss future directions toward robust, scalable, and clinically actionable systems, providing a strategic outlook for next-generation wearable electronics in precision diagnosis. Title: MS2RSHAT-Net: A hybrid Shoebill optimized deep learning framework for accurate electrical fault prediction
Abstract: Electrical faults arise from insulation failure, aging, and disturbances, causing instability, traditional and deep learning methods show limitations in performance. For efficiently represent the data, feature engineering techniques applied Min-Max scaling and feature extraction are applied. The proposed model is executed by Python and evaluated using Electrical Fault Detection and Classification dataset. Title: Dual-Ion Co-Storage via Solvation Structure Tuning Toward Ultrafast and Durable Zinc-Organic Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous Zn-organic batteries are promising due to the sustainability and tunability of organic cathodes. Experimental and density functional theory mechanistic studies unveil a new reversible Zn2+/K+ co-storage mechanism in the PTCDA cathode, where K+ acts as a charge shield and structural pillar, synergistically decreasing the ion migration energy barrier, enhancing reaction kinetics, and stabilizing the cathode structure. Title: A temperature-coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Stokes-heat model for thermally driven phase separation
Abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for thermally driven phase separation in viscous incompressible mixtures. The system couples a convective Cahn-Hilliard equation for the order parameter with a Stokes subsystem for the velocity-pressure field and a heat equation for the temperature. Temperature enters the bulk free energy through a Landau-type coefficient, while the phase field feeds back on the flow through concentration-dependent density and viscosity, yielding a phenomenological temperature-coupled Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes–heat system. The model serves as a proxy for temperature-triggered condensation-like phase separation and does not include humidity, latent heat, vapor pressure, or capillary forcing; these effects are absorbed into the choice of the threshold temperature Θ S . We motivate the chemical potential by a temperature-dependent Landau free energy and derive a priori estimates for the regularized subproblems. On the analytical side, we prove local-in-time existence of weak solutions for a regularized auxiliary model of the coupled system. This regularized formulation serves as an auxiliary analytical model for establishing local existence. On the numerical side, we use a first-order sequential finite-element discretization of a simplified quasi-static formulation. The heat equation is advanced by an implicit diffusion step, the variable-coefficient Stokes problem by a Taylor–Hood discretization, and the Cahn–Hilliard bulk derivative is evaluated at the previous time level, so every algebraic subproblem is linear. An isothermal diffusive test confirms mass conservation to roundoff and exhibits monotone discrete-energy decay for the tested parameter set. Time-step and mesh-refinement studies show first-order temporal and approximately second-order spatial behavior. The remaining computations are qualitative, parameter-specific illustrations, and no global discrete energy law is claimed for the non-isothermal sequential scheme. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A coupled oxidation-damage model for cross-layer ablation failure in HfC/SiC bilayer coatings on C/C composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: HfC/SiC bilayer coatings provide exceptional ultra-high-temperature ablation protection for Carbon/Carbon composites. However, the complex cross-layer chemo-mechanical interactions, specifically between the oxidation-induced cracking of the HfC outer layer and the active oxidation of the SiC inner layer, remain poorly understood. In this work, a comprehensive oxidation-damage coupling ablation model is proposed based on continuum damage mechanics and chemical reaction kinetics. Oxyacetylene ablation experiments were conducted to characterize the ablation depths and layer-specific damage evolution. To handle the severe material discontinuity at the bilayer interface, an interfacial node-decoupling method is implemented, ensuring multiphysics continuity while preserving the independent chemical kinetics. The proposed model is successfully validated against experimental results with an average relative error of 15.7%. The numerical results clarify a mutually exacerbating failure mechanism: Stress-driven HfC cracking creates preferential oxygen pathways that accelerate localized SiC depletion, while the resulting material loss undermines the mechanical support of the overlying HfC layer. Furthermore, parametric analysis uncovers a non-monotonic evolution of the anti-ablation performance when varying the SiC layer thickness (10–30 μm). A thicker SiC layer imposes a more severe mechanical constraint that prematurely drives outer-layer microcracking, whereas it provides a superior secondary oxygen barrier during extended ablation. This chemo-mechanical trade-off offers crucial guidelines for the structural optimization of advanced multilayer anti-ablation coatings. © 2026

Title: Similarity solution and asymptotic analysis of a multi-phase Stefan problem with a convective boundary condition at the fixed face
Abstract: In a one-dimensional multi-phase Stefan problem occurring within a semi-infinite, homogeneous material, a convective (Robin-type) boundary condition is applied at the fixed boundary x=0. Title: Synergistic bulk-gradient and surface-dual-doping design for Co-free Li-rich cathodes

Title: Integrated wind uncertainty and incentive-based demand response framework for electricity market operation using probabilistic, robust, and fuzzy optimisation
Abstract: The greater the integration of wind energy, the more uncertainty is introduced into electricity markets, affecting dispatch decisions, price formation, and system reliability. At the same time, incentive-based demand response provides a flexible means of dealing with imbalances between supply and demand. Yet, most of the studies currently available examine uncertainty modelling and demand response in isolation, leading to only a limited understanding of how different ways of representing uncertainty influence market results when combined with demand-side participation. This study proposes a hierarchical, multi-stage optimisation framework that includes wind generation uncertainty in the energy market and involves independent system operators, load-serving entities, and consumers. Probabilistic, robust, and fuzzy wind uncertainty models are incorporated into a multilevel modelling structure to allow for consistent comparison. The proposed method is solved using a hybrid technique that combines linear programming with Stackelberg particle swarm optimisation and is tested on the PJM 5-Bus and IEEE 118-Bus systems to examine both operational performance and scalability. The results show that combining uncertainty modelling with demand response results in significant improvements in several key market indicators. For the PJM 5-Bus system, the probabilistic approach reduces generation cost by 9.6%, increases demand reduction by 21.2%, and boosts LSE revenue by 9.5%. In the IEEE 118-Bus system, generation cost is reduced by 12.1%, total demand is decreased by 18.3%, and LSE revenue rises by 9.6%. The results demonstrated that the probabilistic model achieves lower locational marginal prices and higher demand flexibility by effectively using forecast information. The robust model produces more conservative but stable results under adverse wind conditions, while the fuzzy approach shows intermediate performance in situations where data are constrained. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wang X.; Zhai H.; Gu D.; Wang Y.; Gao J.; Du L.; Zhuo L.; Li X.; Wang Y.
Title: Strategy for enhanced production of A40926B0 in Nonomuraea gerenzanensis using an efficient CRISPR/AsCas12f1 system
Abstract: The global emergence of vancomycin-resistant Gram-positive pathogens underscores the urgent need for efficient production of novel lipoglycopeptide antibiotics. Dalbavancin, a last-resort therapeutic agent, relies on its key biosynthetic precursor A40926B0, whose industrial manufacture is severely limited by the low yield of wild-type Nonomuraea gerenzanensis and inefficient genetic tools for this rare actinomycete. Here, we developed a high-efficiency CRISPR/AsCas12f1 genome editing system and applied systematic metabolic engineering to boost A40926B0 biosynthesis. First, conjugation conditions were optimized to elevate the transfer efficiency in N. gerenzanensis D11. The hypercompact AsCas12f1 nuclease showed markedly lower cytotoxicity than SpCas9 and enabled 100% gene deletion efficiency with preferred PAMs (TTTG, CTTG, GTTG). Second, we strengthened the shikimate pathway via multiple genetic strategies: overexpressing feedback-resistant DAHP synthase (aroG  fbr ) and chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydrogenase (tyrA  fbr ), as well as knocking out pheA . This manipulation blocks the phenylalanine synthetic branch and redirects metabolic flux toward the l -tyrosine branch. Third, we engineered the branched-chain fatty acid (BCFA) pathway via promoter replacement of bkdA2B2C2 , LipAB , fabF and deletion of acdH to enhance isododecanoyl side-chain supply. The combinatorial engineering yielded strain B-13, which produced 1740 mg/L A40926B0 in shake flasks. Finally, 50-L fed-batch fermentation with continuous maltodextrin feeding further increased the titer to 1817 mg/L, the highest reported titer to date. This work establishes a robust CRISPR editing tool for N. gerenzanensis and provides valuable engineering references for precursor-oriented strain improvement targeting lipoglycopeptide antibiotics, offering insights for the industrial scale production of A40926B0. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang S.; Zhang Z.; Zhou H.; Yu Z.; Zhao F.; Yu S.; Wan Y.; Wang L.; Wang Y.
Title: Nanoscale surface of a blade induced by novel immersed polishing assisted by ultrasonic and photocatalysis and elastic abrasive polishing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Titanium (Ti) alloy has extremely low thermal conductivity, low elastic modulus, and high chemical activity, making it prone to deformation, scratches, and abrasive embedding on Ti alloy during traditional polishing. Therefore, surface roughness (Sa) of Ti alloy is usually > 0.2 μm after polishing. To solve this challenge, novel combined polishing is proposed by immersed polishing assisted by ultrasonic and photocatalysis and elastic abrasive air jet polishing (EAAJP). The immersed polishing was performed using a developed setup, under irradiation of ultraviolet ultrasonically in a new environmentally-friendly slurry. The slurry consisted of ceria, nicotinic acid, and deionized water. After immersed polishing, hardness, Sa, and tensile strength on specimens of Ti alloy decreased from 392.23 HV, 532.18 nm, and 1080.01 MPa to 280.44 HV, 402.27 nm, and 1022.41 MPa, respectively, reducing 29%, 24%, and 5%, correspondingly. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy show that hydroxyl radicals were generated during photocatalysis, oxidizing the surface of the Ti alloy and forming a titania layer. Nicotinic acid dissolved the titania layer and complexed Ti ions with carboxyl and pyridyl groups. This is in good agreement with the calculations of density functional theory that the electrostatic potential of nicotinic acid is distributed in the range from −39.4 to 54.76 kcal/mol, and the complex occurred on the oxygen and nitrogen atoms derived from carboxyl groups and pyridine rings, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that tangential force, normal force, transmitted depth of von Mises stress, and thickness of damaged layer on pristine Ti alloy are 207.34 nN, 143.92 nN, 41.33 Å, and 39.62 Å at a scratching depth of 15 Å, while those with titania layer are 166.76 nN, 85.41 nN, 18.14 Å, and 30.71 Å, respectively, decreasing 20%, 41%, 56%, and 22%, correspondingly. Core-shell structured elastic abrasives of ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymers@silicon carbide (EVA@SiC) were prepared using a custom-made stirrer with controlled temperatures. EAAJP was conducted on a self-made four-axis polisher. EVA@SiC abrasives have a lower Young's modulus, varying from 0.2 to 1.0 GPa, measured by atomic force microscopy. After EAAJP, Sa, tensile strength, and hardness reached 12.57 nm, 1231.56 MPa, and 426.33 HV, respectively, improving 98%, 14%, and 9%, correspondingly, compared with those prior to polishing. Transmission electron spectroscopy confirms that the thickness of the damaged layer decreased from 723.91 nm prior to polishing to 9.59 nm after EAAJP, reducing 99%. Sa on a blade with a complex surface decreased from 569.87 nm before polishing to 13.96 nm after EAAJP, improving by 98%. Our outcomes provide new insights to get nanoscale surface on a blade of Ti alloy with a complex surface using both immersed polishing ultrasonically under irradiation of ultraviolet and EAAJP. © 2026

Title: A green molecular gel nanocomposite: Structure, rheological properties and tribological performance
Abstract: Molecular gels are a new class of lubricants that offer many advantages over traditional lubricants. However, developing molecular gels that combine environmental sustainability with high lubrication performance remains a significant challenge. In this work, a green molecular gel lubricant using cottonseed oil as a low-cost and sustainable solvent and N-lauroyl-L-glutamic acid di-n-butylamide (GP-1) as a green gelator has been developed. The thermal stability, rheological properties and lubrication performance of the gel are further enhanced by reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanosheets. At 1.0 wt% of rGO, the onset decomposition temperature is increased from 335 °C to 365 °C, and the storage modulus (G′) from ∼4.05 × 10 ³ Pa to ∼9.35 × 103 Pa. Correspondingly, the coefficient of friction is reduced by approximately 4.62-fold. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations in combination with Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy indicate that the reinforcing effects of rGO are attributable to its physical interactions with GP-1. The interactions also promote the primary nucleation of GP-1, leading to the formation of smaller GP-1 fiber network domains that help distribute GP-1 nanofibers more homogeneously in the gel. The gel network restructuring and reinforcement by rGO may work together to contribute to the high lubrication performance of the gel nanocomposite. Apart from the sustainability design of this molecular gel, the mechanistic insights provide guidance on the selection of nano-additives for designing a high-performance molecular gel lubricant. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Topologically crosslinked molecular intercalation enabling strain-resilient EMI shielding in an n-type conducting polymer
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Maintaining stable electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performance under large deformation remains a major challenge. The n-type conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) exhibits excellent electrical conductivity. However, strong π-π interactions lead to severe intrinsic brittleness. The incorporation of flexible polymers can alleviate brittleness, yet the resulting improvement in deformability is still limited. This work, by grafting 3-isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane (IPTS) onto both ends of polyethylene glycol (PEG) to synthesize a flexible, both-end IPTS-grafted PEG (BIP), proposes a strategy based on molecular-level intercalation and dense hydrogen-bonding interactions. BIP is intercalated into the interlayers of PBFDO, increasing the free volume of the system and forming a high-density hydrogen-bonding network with PBFDO. The resulting increase in deformation freedom enables the composite film to achieve an elongation at break of 580%. Under strains of 100% and 500%, the EMI shielding effectiveness retention of the composite film reaches 93% and 65%, respectively. Moreover, a fully connected neural network is constructed to predict EMI shielding performance, achieving an external-validation root mean square error of 2.429. This work provides an effective strategy for alleviating the brittleness of n-type conducting polymers and achieving stable EMI shielding performance under large deformation, demonstrating great application potential in flexible electronics. © 2026

Title: Sulfur-driven in situ oxygen vacancy engineering in TiO2 enables efficient photocatalytic transfer hydrogenation of furfural
Abstract: Photocatalytic transfer hydrogenation (PTH) of biomass-derived furfural (FF) to furfuryl alcohol (FA) using methanol as a green hydrogen donor represents a sustainable route for producing value-added chemicals, yet developing robust noble-metal-free catalysts remains challenging. Herein, we present a sulfur-doped TiO2 photocatalyst exhibiting exceptional activity and selectivity for FF hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst delivers an impressive space-time FA yield of 44.0 mmolFA·gcat.−1·h−1 with 99.5% selectivity under 500 mW·cm−2 irradiation, surpassing most state-of-the-art systems. Comprehensive characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that lattice-substituted sulfur atoms form surface S–O species, driving oxygen vacancy formation and modulating the electronic structure of TiO2. The synergistic interaction between S species and VO sites regulates the electron density at active sites, thereby markedly promoting FF adsorption/activation, charge separation, and targeted hydrogenation. This work establishes a strategy for constructing high-efficiency, non-precious photocatalysts through sulfur-mediated oxygen-vacancy engineering. © 2026

Title: Covalent Organic Framework Membranes through Sequential Imine Exchange for Precise Molecular Separation
Abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with high crystallinity hold great promise in precise molecular separation, but often suffer from the intercrystalline defects and thus poor membrane-formation ability. This study reports a sequential imine exchange strategy to fabricate highly crystalline, defect-free COF membranes for precise molecular separation. Two functional amines (aromatic and aliphatic amines) are employed in highly reversible imine exchange reaction to separately conduct crystallization and defect remedy processes according to their different energy gaps. Aromatic amine, which serves as COF framework building unit, undergoes the first-step imine exchange for high crystallinity because of its lower energy gap. Afterward, the hyperbranched aliphatic amine with abundant amino groups undergoes the second-step imine exchange, affording the tight connections between adjacent crystals and the excellent membrane-formation ability. Accordingly, the COF membrane exhibits high permeance (344 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for water, 462 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for methanol) and rejection (> 99.9% for Congo red and Alcian blue). Meanwhile, the membrane is endowed with an ultrahigh separation factor (> 528) for mixed dye aqueous solutions and large-scale processability (> 290 cm2). This work offers a new strategy to fabricate highly crystalline and defect-free COF membranes, revealing their large potential in diverse practical applications. Title: Strain-engineered FeNi@SDC heterointerfaces for durable high-temperature seawater electrolysis
Abstract: Hydrogen production from seawater using solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) offers a promising pathway towards a sustainable energy future. However, severe Ni catalyst coarsening and chloride-induced surface poisoning under high-temperature steam conditions still limit long-term operation. Herein, we develop a reduction-driven strategy to construct strain-engineered FeNi@SDC heterointerfaces by infiltrating an FeSDC (Sm0.2Ce0.7Fe0.1O2-δ) precursor into a commercial nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia (Ni-YSZ) fuel electrode. Partial Fe diffusion into the Ni lattice during reduction drives the in-situ formation of FeNi alloy nanoparticles, simultaneously generating lattice strain and a robust metal-oxide heterointerface. Theoretical calculations show that these coupled structural features regulate the electronic structure of Ni, thereby promoting water activation, optimizing hydrogen adsorption and suppressing chloride adsorption. As a result, the modified electrolysis cell achieves an electrolysis current of 52.7 A at 1.5 V, while maintaining stable operation for 645 h with an ultralow degradation rate of 8.4 × 10−4% h−1. This work establishes a general strategy that integrates alloy-induced lattice strain with heterointerface engineering for the development of durable fuel electrodes for high-temperature seawater electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Modulating localized microenvironments via construction of CoS/CN heterojunction to strengthen hydroxyl adsorption for efficient 5-hydroxymethylfurfural electrooxidation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) provides an efficient route for the production of value-added chemicals. However, the slow oxidation of the hydroxyl groups in the HMF molecule limits the reaction rate. Herein, a CoS/CN with a p-n heterojunction structure was designed and successfully synthesized. Among the prepared samples, the optimal current density of CoS/CN-4 is 2.5 times that of CoS at 1.47 V vs. RHE. Machine learning (ML) was used to optimize the experimental parameters (coulombs, potential, and stirring rate) to achieve nearly 100% of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (FE), and FDCA yield remained above 95% after 25 cycles. Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) combined with theoretical calculations indicates that the superior performance is attributed to the redistribution of interface charges, forming positively charged CN centers, which enhance the adsorption ability for electron-withdrawing hydroxyl functional groups. Different from CoS with 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanic acid (HMFCA) pathway to produce FDCA, CoS/CN with 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) pathway exhibits a faster HMF oxidation rate. Finally, 72% yield of higher-value product named 5-formyl-2-furancarboxylic acid (FFCA) was achieved by tuning the base concentration, outperforming most previously reported electrocatalysts. This work provides important theoretical and experimental insights for rationally modulating HMF adsorption behavior to alter the reaction pathway and accelerate biomass conversion. © 2026

Title: A SIMPLE RANGE CHARACTERIZATION FOR SPHERICAL MEAN TRANSFORM IN ODD DIMENSIONS AND ITS APPLICATIONS
Abstract: This article provides a novel and simple range description for the spherical mean transform of functions supported in the unit ball of an odd dimensional Euclidean space. The new description comprises of a set of symmetry relations between the values of certain differential operators acting on the coefficients of the spherical harmonics expansion of the function in the range of the transform. As a central part of the proof of our main result, we derive a remarkable cross product identity for the spherical Bessel functions of the first and second kind, which may be of independent interest in the theory of special functions. Title: Optimal G2V/V2G fleet scheduling under uncertainty using a quadratic interpolation supercell thunderstorm algorithm
Abstract: This paper develops and applies a Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm to electric vehicle fleet charging scheduling optimization under uncertainties over a 24-h horizon, through smart coordination between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid operations. Validated on the Congress on Evolutionary Computation 2022 benchmark, Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm balances global exploration and local exploitation through a supercell-inspired population structure combined with quadratic interpolation, navigating multi-modal solution spaces and accelerating convergence toward locally smooth cost regions without requiring gradient information. The addressed electric vehicle scheduling problem is an inherently non-convex, high-dimensional, due to coupled fleet constraints, stochastic operating conditions, and battery degradation dynamics, which limits the applicability of classical deterministic optimization methods. In addition, a state of health based adaptive C-rate control mechanism is introduced, in which charging and discharging rates dynamically adjust according to battery health and state of charge conditions, keeping the operation electrochemically safe and limiting accelerated wear. Five case studies are investigated, including a deterministic baseline, thermal excursion battery degradation uncertainty, day-ahead price uncertainty, arrival/departure uncertainty, and scalability testing. The Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm is benchmarked against five competing metaheuristic and two deterministic approaches under equal computational budgets across 30 independent runs. Comparative results show that the improved approach achieves up to 20% lower operational cost compared with the baseline approach, while also obtaining the lowest cumulative cost across all scalability scenarios. Statistical validation further confirms its superiority, with significant differences in 50 out of 56 Wilcoxon pairwise comparisons and the lowest average Friedman rank (1.71). In addition, the Quadratic Interpolation Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm consistently satisfies target state of charge constraints with zero violations and demonstrates strong scheduling robustness across all investigated scenarios. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Defect-driven construction of fully exposed Ru clusters on CeO2 for efficient low-temperature CO2 methanation
Abstract: High-density oxygen vacancies were constructed on the CeO2 support via H2 prereduction, and the loading of Ru in the form of two-dimensional fully exposed clusters was successfully induced thereby, rather than conventional three-dimensional nanoparticles. The directional injection of charge into Ru clusters was driven by oxygen vacancies, resulting in an upward shift of the D-band center and an increase in electron cloud density, and the activation of CO2 molecules was significantly enhanced. In addition to the direct CO* dissociation pathway, the presence of a parallel HCOO* pathway on the catalyst was revealed by in-situ characterizations and calculations. The energy barrier of the rate-determining step was reduced from 0.75 eV to 0.56–0.65 eV by the synergy of the two pathways. Consequently, a CO2 conversion of 32.3% was achieved by Ru/CeO2-Ov at 150 °C, and the TOFs value was enhanced by nearly two orders of magnitude compared with the reference sample. No deactivation was observed during 400 h of stability testing. This work provides a new strategy for constructing efficient methanation catalysts through defect engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Decoupling Ion–Dipole Interactions via Competitive Coordination for Durable Dendrite-Free Zinc Metal Batteries
Abstract: Abstract: The aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are famous for high-safety and high-energy-density, but limited by severe challenges around the Helmholtz plane layer such as the strong ion–dipole interactions between Zn2+ and H2O, resulting in slow desolvation processes and limited transport kinetics as well as corresponding higher barriers. To reconstruct the ion–dipole surroundings, the interface chemistry of employing a high permanent dipole moment of L-Carnosine (L-CN) has been proposed, weakening the interactions between Zn2+ and H2O to realize a crowded Zn2+-conductive structure, accelerating the desolvation kinetics. As revealed, the strong affinity between L-CN and Zn2+ enables the L-CN molecules to repulse H2O, reconfiguring the inner Helmholtz plane layer, thereby inhibiting the active water molecular to form hydrogen evolution reactions. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells with Helmholtz plane modulation achieve a long lifespan up to 7000 h, a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.72%, and a high stabilization at high depth of discharge (85.4%). The assembled Zn//V2O5−x full cell with optimal electrolyte delivers the capacity of 289 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g−1 under an N/P ratio of 3.98. Impressively, the large-scale pouch cell with optimal electrolyte stabilizes for 200 cycles, offering the bright future of reconstructing Helmholtz plane for achieving high-performance AZMBs. Title: CO2 storage suitability, capacity, and emission-reduction implications of oil and gas reservoirs in the Shaanxi sector of the Ordos Basin, China
Abstract: Geological storage of CO2 offers a viable means of reducing large-scale carbon emissions, thereby contributing to the mitigation of global climate and environmental challenges associated with CO2 emissions. This study evaluates candidate oil and gas reservoirs in the Shaanxi sector of the Ordos Basin using an Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation framework and estimates CO2 storage capacity with the US-DOE volumetric method. The results show that Hengshan Oilfield has the highest overall suitability for CO2 sequestration, whereas Jinghe Oilfield has the largest effective storage capacity. The total effective storage capacity of the screened reservoirs is estimated at 1.02 × 109 t CO2, Meanwhile, total CO2 emissions in Shaanxi Province increased from 308.25 Mt in 2010 to 601.25 Mt in 2022, with fossil fuel combustion contributing more than 94% of total emissions and with higher emissions concentrated in northern Shaanxi and Guanzhong region. The CO2 injected into oil and gas reservoirs, if employed for enhanced oil recovery, is projected to produce 1.02∼6.12 × 108 t of crude oil, translating to economic returns of 50 billion USD. This study provides a reference for achieving carbon neutrality in Shaanxi Province and advancing low-carbon development in the Ordos Basin. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production utilizing offshore wind energy using the AHP method and the Weibull distribution approximation. A case of Sakhalin Island
Abstract: The study is devoted to assessing the suitability of the Sakhalin Island offshore zone for the development of a wind energy complex, with a focus on the potential production of green hydrogen. In the course of the research, the hierarchy analysis method was applied along with fuzzy logic. Criteria influencing the placement of wind farms were selected, experts in the field were interviewed to compile pairwise comparison matrices, after which the weights of these criteria were obtained. Using fuzzy logic functions, the absolute values of the parameters were unified. The territories where the construction of wind farms is undesirable were also taken into account. As a result, the final data set was obtained using the weighted linear combination method. As a result, it was possible to identify 4 zones with the best indicators of suitability for the construction of wind farms. The territories in the Gulf of Patience near the port of Poronaysk look the most promising. Based on the data collected, 8 promising locations within 4 zones have been identified. For each location, the potential amount of electricity and green hydrogen that can be produced has been calculated using the Weibull distribution model, with 6 different methods to parameter estimation. Six different turbine models have been used in the analysis. Additionally, LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy) and LCOH (Levelized Cost of Hydrogen) calculations were conducted. As a result, the minimum LCOE calculated was 0.087 $/kWh and the lowest LCOH recorded was 7.4 $/kg. The Vestas V236-15.0 MW wind turbine demonstrated optimal performance for the study area. If actively invested in this area, this area could become an important hub for hydrogen trading in the Asia-Pacific region. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Jiang Y.; Chen Z.; Sun X.; Li H.; Xie J.; Li Y.; Nie X.; Lan F.; Zhang Y.; Wen Q.
Title: Rheologically Engineered 3D-Printed Highly Loaded Magneto-Dielectric Absorbers for Device-Level Electromagnetic Compatibility
Abstract: Highly loaded magneto-dielectric composite systems are promising for achieving strong electromagnetic loss and structural design flexibility, yet their processability and geometric controllability remain extremely challenging. Herein, a rheologically engineered direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing strategy is developed. Graphene (Gr) is introduced to reconstruct the particle-loading network, which synergistically improves the ink’s yield behavior, shear-thinning property, structural recovery, and a magnetic–dielectric synergistic loss system is constructed with carbonyl iron powder (CIP). The critical CIP content (~ 84.06 wt%) is determined by the yield model, and a tunable Gr/CIP (GC) composite ink is obtained. The correlation among rheological response, geometric fidelity, and temporal stability is established, enabling high-fidelity 3D-printed gradient honeycomb structures. The rationally designed 3D-printed GC honeycomb (GCH) absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 18 GHz–4 THz, with an RLmin of − 84.30 dB at a thickness of 2.6 mm. When integrated into device-level terahertz reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), the GCH absorber contributes to a ~ 3.3 dBi main lobe gain enhancement, 1.9–3.3 dB sidelobe suppression, and a ~ 58% reduction in reflection beamwidth, showing excellent electromagnetic compatibility performance for communication, imaging, and radar. This work offers a practical strategy for the structural fabrication and device integration of high-load magneto-dielectric synergistic absorbers. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Wu J.; Yang Y.; Li T.; Zhang B.; Chen Z.; Li J.; Xiao Y.
Title: Genome-integrated engineering of Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 enables sustained gut-local biosynthesis of 5-hydroxytryptophan
Abstract: 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP) is a functional precursor of serotonin; however, achieving sustained 5-HTP production in vivo by engineered microbes remains challenging. To address this, we developed a genome-integrated engineered probiotic system enabling gut-local biosynthesis of 5-HTP. Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN), a clinically validated probiotic with an established safety profile for intestinal application, was selected as the chassis. Constitutive expression was employed to eliminate inducer dependence, while genomic integration was used to enhance genetic stability and avoid reliance on antibiotic selection for pathway maintenance. In addition, BH4 biosynthesis and regeneration modules were incorporated to address the limited endogenous BH4 availability in the gut environment. Different administration strategies were systematically evaluated to characterize in vivo performance. Notably, our results showed that the hTPH2 hydroxylation module, together with the BH4 biosynthesis and regeneration system, supported 5-HTP biosynthesis in EcN. The engineered EcN strain achieved a 5-HTP titer of 863.2 mg/L, the highest level reported in EcN-based systems. Under non-selective conditions, EcNPconst−5−HTP carrying the chromosomally integrated pathway maintained stable 5-HTP production in vitro and retained 5-HTP-producing capacity after intestinal passage, whereas plasmid loss in non-integrated constructs resulted in a pronounced decrease in production. In vivo analysis showed that single-dose administration induced a transient elevation in plasma 5-HTP, whereas repeated dosing generated reproducible, time-dependent fluctuations in fecal bacterial abundance and gut-local biosynthetic activity. Treatment with the engineered probiotic further improved behavioral phenotypes and modulated brain 5-HT-related metabolites in a reserpine-induced mouse model. Together, these findings provide a translational framework linking in vitro 5-HTP production by engineered probiotics to their in vivo functional performance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Tailoring strain delocalization in particle-reinforced metal matrix composites toward strength-ductility synergy through core-shell heterostructured metallic building blocks
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Particle-reinforced metal matrix composites (PRMMCs) suffer from severe strain localization stemming from the mechanical incompatibility between hard reinforcements and soft metallic matrices. To overcome this challenge, SiC-nanoparticle-decorated aluminum powder was subjected to low-energy ball milling to produce core-shell heterostructured building blocks composed of ultrafine-grained (UFG) shells surrounding coarse-grained (CG) cores. Upon consolidation with micro-SiC particles, these building blocks induce a bulk composite featuring a dual core-shell architecture of CG-UFG matrix and SiC-UFG particles. Mechanistically, the UFG shells served distinct and complementary functions: Those around the CG in the matrix provided a hetero-deformation-induced strengthening contribution of ∼68 MPa (∼14% of yield strength) via long-range back stresses arising from hetero-interfaces; concurrently, those around micro-SiC particles suppressed strain localization at particle-matrix interfaces and promoted macroscale uniform deformation. As a result, an exceptional tensile strength of ∼685 ± 26 MPa combined with > 8% elongation was achieved. Therefore, the featured dual core-shell architecture induced by CG-UFG metallic building blocks offers a robust design route for achieving strength-ductility synergy in PRMMCs. © 2026

Authors: Ma Y.; He A.; Long W.; Guo F.; Li X.; Fang P.; Wu J.; Jin L.; Xi Z.
Title: Unique polarization configuration and enhanced anhysteretic electrostrictive strain in PMN-PZN crystal via antiferroelectric PMW modification
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-precision actuators serve as critical components in precision measurement, control, and drive. Ferroelectric materials with large electrostrain are constrained from application in precision actuators due to their severe hysteresis. In this work, two relaxor systems, Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Zn1/3Nb2/3)O3 (PMN-PZN) and Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Zn1/3Nb2/3)O3-Pb(Mg1/2W1/2)O3 (PMN-PZN-PMW), were designed and grown into single crystals. The obtained PMN-PZN-PMW crystal demonstrated significant improvements in breakdown field and electrostrictive strain level compared with that of the PMN-PZN crystal: PMN-PZN gets an anhysteretic electrostrictive strain of 0.107% at 25 kV cm−1, while PMN-PZN-PMW achieves an anhysteretic electrostrictive strain of 0.17% at 50 kV cm−1. The enhancement in electrostrictive strain and the absence of hysteresis are attributed to the morphotropic relaxor boundary-like structure induced by the incorporation of antiferroelectric PMW. In this structure, multiple polar nanoregions coexist and are interconnected through continuously rotating polarization vectors. This unique polarization configuration not only suppresses leakage current but also lowers the energy barrier for polarization switching. This demonstrates an innovative approach to improving electrostrictive strain performance by constructing a multi-relaxor structure. The developed single crystals are highly suitable for precision actuators and hold broad application prospects. © 2026

Authors: Mao Y.; Wei G.; Zhao Q.; Lu Y.; Jin L.
Title: Prismatic <c>-type dislocation-induced nanoscale ordered phase boundary engineering enables static–dynamic property synergy in high-oxygen titanium alloys
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Achieving simultaneous static strength–ductility synergy and dynamic deformation stability remains a major challenge for multiphase structural alloys, largely because heterogeneous phase boundaries promote strain incompatibility and localization across loading regimes. Here, we develop chemically ordered phase boundary engineering (COPBE) to reconstruct α/β interfaces in a high-oxygen titanium alloy through dislocation-induced nanoscale oxygen ordering. Prismatic <c>-type dislocations generated at α/β interfaces are stabilized by ordered O configurations, forming a BCC/COPB/HCP interfacial architecture. Under quasi-static tension, COPBs redistribute interfacial stresses and promote coordinated dislocation transmission across α/β interfaces, sustaining work hardening and plastic accommodation while retaining ultrahigh strength. Under dynamic compression, oxygen redistribution from COPBs toward octahedral interstitial sites in the BCC phase provides an additional pathway for thermal and mechanical energy dissipation, thereby suppressing strain softening and delaying adiabatic shear localization. Consequently, Ti-5553-0.43O (wt.%) achieves a tensile strength of 1.9 GPa with 7.0% elongation, together with a dynamic compressive strength of ∼2.9 GPa and a fracture strain of 26.9%. These results demonstrate that COPBE couples interfacial chemical ordering, dislocation transport, and O configurational evolution to regulate deformation across strain rates, providing a general strategy for achieving static–dynamic mechanical synergy in multiphase metallic materials. © 2026

Authors: Song X.; Cheng R.; Hao J.; Zhang H.; Liang Y.; He Y.; Hu T.; Wang X.
Title: Defect dipole engineering induced by Cobalt(II) doping enables ultralow dielectric loss in Zn2SiO4 ceramics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Tunnel-structured zinc orthosilicate (Zn2SiO4) is a promising low-loss dielectric ceramic, yet further suppression of dielectric dissipation requires effective regulation of its local defect structure. Herein, pristine Zn2SiO4 and Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ singly doped ceramics are prepared from chemically homogeneous precursors obtained by solvent evaporation. This synthesis route promotes uniform transition-metal incorporation at Zn lattice sites and enables controlled perturbation of the tetrahedral framework. Although Ni, Co, and Mn substitution all induce lattice distortion and defect formation, their dielectric effects are markedly different. In contrast to Ni and Mn, which introduce additional relaxation loss, Co selectively lowers dielectric dissipation. The Co-doped ceramic exhibits an ultralow tanδ of 7.3 × 10−5 at 1 MHz with an εr of 9.2 at room temperature, nearly one order of magnitude lower than that of pristine Zn2SiO4. Electron paramagnetic resonance, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations suggest that tetrahedrally coordinated Co2+ may enhance localized electron trapping and stabilize oxygen-vacancy-related defect complexes. These localized defect centers may suppress long-range carrier migration and weaken Maxwell-Wagner interfacial polarization, thereby reducing dielectric loss while maintaining a relatively high dielectric constant. This work establishes dopant-stabilized defect localization as an effective strategy for designing ultralow-loss silicate dielectric ceramics. © 2026

Authors: Bai Y.; Chang L.; Nie S.; Gao W.; Zhu P.; Zhang L.; Cui K.; Yu J.
Title: Porphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks with tunable conductivity for intelligent multi-signal formaldehyde monitoring
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The development of intelligent multi-signal gas monitoring systems requires the synergistic integration of high-performance sensing materials and advanced signal-processing architectures. Herein, porphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dimension-regulated conductivity were developed as electroactive materials for room-temperature formaldehyde (HCHO) detection and integrated into a multi-signal monitoring platform for environmental surveillance. Specifically, three porphyrin-based COFs (3D-MnPor-COF, 2D-MnPor-COF, and 1D-MnPor-COF) with tunable conductivity and controllable dimensionality were synthesized through rational precursor engineering. Compared with the 1D and 2D counterparts, which mainly provide directional diffusion pathways and molecular selectivity, the 3D COF features an ordered isotropic network of interconnected cage-like nanochannels, thereby exposing more Mn−N4 sites. Consequently, when integrated with pencil-drawn paper-based interdigitated electrodes, three flexible gas sensors exhibited sensitive responses toward HCHO, featuring wide detection ranges (0.05−100 ppm), low detection limits (13, 28, and 22 ppb), and excellent mechanical flexibility. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental analyses clarified the relationship between framework dimensionality and sensing performance. Inspired by the human central nervous system, a homo-spatiotemporal multi-signal intelligent monitoring system integrated with “AND” molecular logic-gate operations was further developed to enable self-correction of sensing signals, as well as remote real-time HCHO monitoring and intelligent warning in household environments. This work not only provides an effective strategy for modulating COF conductivity through dimensional engineering, but also establishes a versatile platform for next-generation intelligent Internet of Things-based multi-signal monitoring systems. © 2026

Authors: Liu Z.; Liu S.; Wang Y.; Chen Y.; Deng H.; Tan Z.; Zhao X.; Chen Y.; Zhu M.
Title: Broad-spectrum chromaticity and high color fastness of polyimide fibers via intrinsic coloration
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Due to the exceptional thermal stability, radiation resistance, and mechanical properties, polyimide (PI) fibers are widely used in various extreme environments. However, the intrinsic monochromatic golden hue and chemically inert surface of PI fiber give rise to a natural barrier to dyeing and low color fastness. Herein, a facile and transformative intrinsic coloration strategy for the dyeing of PI fibers is proposed by directly incorporating a perylene-based chromophore monomer into the backbone of PI. By tuning the concentration and categories of perylene derivatives, various intrinsic colors of PI fibers are afforded, constructing a diverse chromatic PI fiber library with a broad color gamut (spanning from warm tones to slate-grey). Significantly, the strategy successfully overcomes the long-standing trade-off between dyeing and mechanical integrity. Moreover, the incorporation of perylene-based chromophores exhibits excellent structural compatibility with the PI backbone, acting as reinforced components rather than stress-concentrating defects. Consequently, the fibers exhibit simultaneous enhancements in mechanical properties and exceptional color fastness against harsh environments. This work establishes a cost-effective and scalable paradigm for the functionalization of PI fibers, contributing to the expanding application of PI fibers in high-end textiles and smart wearables. © 2026

Title: Oxygen vacancy-rich Ce-substituted LaCoO3 perovskites for high-efficiency plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis under ambient conditions
Abstract: Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions using non-thermal plasma provides a promising route for decentralized and renewable-driven production. However, the rational design of catalysts that can simultaneously regulate plasma activation and surface reaction pathways remains challenging. Herein, a series of Ce-substituted La1-xCexCoO3 perovskite catalysts were developed for plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis, and the role of A-site Ce engineering in modulating catalytic structures and plasma-catalyst interactions was systematically investigated. Moderate Ce incorporation reconstructed the surface Co-Ov interfacial sites through lattice distortion, oxygen vacancy generation, and electronic redistribution between Ce and Co species. The optimized Co-Ov sites exhibited enhanced electron-donating capability, promoting N2 adsorption and activation through electron transfer to the antibonding π* orbitals of N2. The increased weak acid sites facilitated NH3 desorption and suppressed plasma-induced NH3 decomposition. Excessive Ce substitution resulted in the segregation of CeO2 and Co3O4 phases, blocking accessible Co-Ov sites and deteriorating catalytic performance. Under an SEI of 40 kJ·L−1, the optimized La0.9Ce0.1 catalyst achieved an NH3 synthesis rate of 19.1 mmol·g−1·h−1 with an energy efficiency of 4.8 g-NH3·kWh−1, representing the most competitive performances reported for plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis. In-situ DRIFTS, OES, and plasma discharge simulations further revealed that Ce engineering simultaneously regulated surface nitrogen intermediates and plasma-generated reactive species. This work establishes Co-Ov interfacial site engineering as an effective strategy for designing efficient plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis catalysts. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation of yolk-shell metal sulfides toward tunable microwave absorption
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The regulation of heterogeneous nucleation is considered a promising strategy in constructing multiple hetero-interfaces and simultaneously promoting interfacial polarization. However, the precise control of heterogeneous nucleation during the growth of the crystal nucleus still remains a huge challenge. In this work, a kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation strategy via the change of gradient concentration has been proposed to realize the phase evolution for yolk-shell metal sulfides. The results indicate that excessive Zn2+/Co2+species regulate the sulfur liberation and facilitate the formation of multi-phased metal sulfides, thereby generating increased concentration of sulfur vacancies. As expected, benefiting from the cooperative merits of optimized impedance, introduced sulfur vacancies, multiple hetero-interfaces, and yolk-shell architectures, the yolk-shell ZnCo2S4/ZnS composites exhibit a maximum reflection loss of −55.9 dB, an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.6 GHz, and a greatest radar cross section reduction value of 23.9 dB m2. Meanwhile, the as-synthesized composites display superior specific reflection loss and specific effective absorption bandwidth than the vast majority of counterparts. Furthermore, this study inspires a new insight in regulating the phase evolution via a kinetics-driven heterogeneous nucleation strategy. © 2026

Title: Machine learning-driven electromagnetic wave absorbing: Prediction and its applications
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: With the rapid development of electronic information technology and increasingly complex electromagnetic environments, electromagnetic wave absorbing materials are essential for electromagnetic compatibility, stealth, packaging, and anti-interference applications. Modern absorbers require lightweight, thin, broadband, efficient, and multifunctional designs, yet their performance is governed by strongly nonlinear interactions among composition, phases, defects, interfaces, thickness, processing, dielectric/magnetic losses, impedance matching, interfacial polarization, and multiple scattering. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are inefficient for such high-dimensional design spaces, whereas machine learning provides data-driven tools for nonlinear modelling and multi-objective optimization. This review summarizes machin- learning applications in absorption performance prediction, structure-activity relationship mining, key variable identification, parameter optimization, high-throughput screening, and inverse design. Current challenges include limited and inconsistent data, insufficient feature representation, weak generalization and interpretability, and incomplete experimental validation. Future efforts should focus on high-quality databases, mechanism-constrained models, few-shot learning, multi-objective optimization, and automated closed-loop platforms to enable intelligent design and rapid engineering application of high-performance absorbing materials. © 2026

Title: Polymer-bitumen compositions for improving the energy efficiency of road construction; [Жол құрылысының энергия тиімділігін арттыруға арналған полимер-битум қоспалары]; [Полимер-битумные композиции для повышения энергоэффективности дорожного строительства]
Abstract: This article examines the effect of two types of polypropylene (H030 and H350) and petroleum residue on the bitumen modification process. Bitumen modification is one of the key methods for improving its physical and mechanical properties and enhancing the quality of road pavement. Currently, bitumen modification is widely used in road construction, playing a crucial role in improving its quality and energy efficiency. Studying the effect of polymers on the mechanical stability of bitumen is a relevant issue in increasing the durability of road surfaces. During the study, six different concentrations of polypropylene H030 and H350 were introduced into bitumen samples, and their main characteristics were compared. The obtained results demonstrated that polypropylene significantly alters the properties of bitumen, contributing to increased strength and durability of road pavements. Furthermore, the addition of petroleum residue enhances the rheological properties of the bitumen mixture, improving its adhesion. These studies provide essential data for improving bitumen used in road construction. The research results indicate that the use of polymer-modified bitumen increases the wear resistance of road surfaces, reduces crack formation, and enhances resistance to climatic factors. This, in turn, extends the service life of road pavements and reduces road maintenance costs. Long-lasting pavements help decrease energy consumption for bitumen production and road construction. The obtained data expand the possibilities for the effective use of polymer-modified bitumen mixtures in asphalt concrete production. Thus, the compatibility of bitumen and polypropylene has been studied, and their optimal compositions have been determined. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: In-situ nanowhiskers/cellular interpenetrating networks synergistic enhancing 2024 Al matrix composites achieving ultra-high thermal stability via additive manufacturing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Conventional high-strength aluminium alloys are generally susceptible to hot cracking during laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) and often suffer from grain coarsening and thermal instability of strengthening phases at elevated temperatures, which restricts their application in aerospace thermal-resistant components. To address these issues, an in-situ strategy combining nanowhiskers with three-dimensional cellular networks is proposed to develop a new 2024 Al alloy (AA2024)-based composite tailored for L-PBF. In-situ formation of nano-sized MgAlB4 whiskers and continuous Al3(Cu,Ni)2 cellular networks constructs an interpenetrating architecture, with whiskers inside cells or in walls, refining α-Al grains and blocking dislocation motion. These quasi-continuous MgAlB4 whiskers effectively mitigate performance degradation caused by the decomposition of Al3(Cu,Ni)2 cellular networks and grain coarsening at high temperatures, maintaining the synergistic enhancement effects of the interpenetrating architecture. Consequently, the as-built composite achieves a high ultimate tensile strength of ∼630 MPa at room temperature, ∼496 MPa at 200 °C, and ∼408 MPa (65% retention) after exposure at 300 °C for 1000 h. Title: Gluconic acid-driven thermodynamic and kinetic synergy for efficient alkaline seawater oxidation
Abstract: Interface engineering constitutes a promising strategy for enhancing catalytic performance. However, the synergistic kinetic-thermodynamic mechanisms induced by interface engineering are yet to be elucidated. Herein, a feasible ligand-modification strategy is proposed to tailor the catalyst-electrolyte interface, aiming to achieve cooperative kinetic and thermodynamic improvements in alkaline seawater oxidation. Thermodynamically, the intrinsic reducibility and the alkaline deprotonation of gluconic acid (GA) ligands render an electron-rich surface of the reconstructed NiFeGA-MoOx (R-NiFeGA-MoOx), elevating the Cl– adsorption barrier to suppress chlorine evolution reaction (ClER). Kinetically, GA destabilizes the hydrated K+ layer and reconstructs the H-bonds in the Helmholtz layer, facilitating the access of free OH– to the catalytic sites. The rapid OH– mass transport provides a kinetically driving force for the alkaline seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Besides, GA-induced hydrophilicity mitigates O2 bubble adhesion, further accelerating mass transfer of the whole reaction system. Based on the synergistic effects of kinetics and thermodynamics driven by GA, the R-NiFeGA-MoOx achieves a favorable OER performance with a low overpotential of 220 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline seawater. Title: Unlocking high work-hardening in multilayered bimodal ZnCu/ZnMg biodegradable composites for bone implants
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Zinc (Zn) and its alloys are considered promising biodegradable metallic implant materials due to their moderate degradation rate, excellent biocompatibility, and multiple biofunctional properties. The grains in the ZM layer grew up to 3.7 ± 1.9 µm, whereas the ZC layer retained fine grains (∼1 μm) in the annealed ZC/ZM composites. This multilayered bimodal structure, consisting of regions with distinct grain sizes and hardness, caused additional hetero-deformation-induced strengthening during tensile deformation, contributing ∼60% of the flow stress. Notably, the ZC1/ZM2 composite sample subjected to 4 ARB cycles after annealing showed a marked increase in uniform elongation from 6.5% ± 0.4% to 15.6% ± 0.3%, while the ZC2/ZM1 composite sample subjected to 8 ARB cycles after annealing achieved the highest yield stress of 343.5 ± 1.1 MPa. Title: Hardness convergence enables ductilization of flash-heated high-carbon martensitic steel via two-stage tempering
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Flash quench-tempering is an efficient route for producing ultrahigh-strength high-carbon martensitic steels by refining the martensitic framework and retaining a high defect density. However, further improving ductility without sacrificing ultrahigh strength remains challenging because non-equilibrium carbon distribution generates microscale mechanical heterogeneity and promotes strain localization. Here, we propose a two-stage tempering strategy to ductilize a flash-heated high-carbon low-alloy martensitic steel without sacrificing strength. Microstructural characterization revealed continued carbide evolution from η-Fe2C to θ-Fe3C, while the martensitic block size and dislocation density were both largely retained. Nanoindentation mapping demonstrated a clear convergence of local hardness after secondary tempering, as evidenced by the decrease in the fraction of high-hardness indents above 12 GPa from 19% to 3.5% and the reduction in hardness standard deviation from 3.1 to 1.8 GPa. High-resolution micro-digital image correlation (μ-DIC) further revealed reduced microscale strain heterogeneity after secondary tempering, indicating improved deformation compatibility. This enhanced ductility is attributed to hardness convergence and improved deformation compatibility rather than global martensite softening. These findings establish two-stage tempering as a practical strategy for ductilizing flash-heated ultrahigh-strength martensitic steels by tailoring local mechanical gradients. © 2026

Title: Wastewater heat recovery systems for sustainable building energy efficiency and decarbonization: A comprehensive review with practical insights
Abstract: Growing energy demand and carbon emissions pose a major challenge to the building environment, particularly in addressing heating and cooling needs sustainably. In this context, wastewater is recognized as an unconventional and largely untapped thermal energy resource due to its consistent supply and generally stable temperature. Wastewater heat recovery has the potential to significantly improve building energy efficiency and boost decarbonization efforts. This review provides a comprehensive and system-level assessment of wastewater heat recovery technologies for building- and district-scale applications, with particular emphasis on heat extraction locations, heat exchanger configurations, and wastewater source heat pump systems. Rather than treating individual components in isolation, the study integrates heat exchanger and heat pump technologies within a unified framework to support practical design and implementation decisions. State-of-the-art literature covering wastewater characteristics, recovery locations, heat exchanger technologies, and combined wastewater heat exchanger-heat pump systems is critically analyzed through comparative evaluation of performance indicators, benefits, and limitations. Key recovery locations, including building outlets, sewer networks, and wastewater treatment plants are examined in terms of thermal potential, operational constraints, and system compatibility. The review highlights that appropriately selected heat exchangers and wastewater source heat pump configurations can significantly improve energy recovery efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, practical recommendations are provided to guide the selection, installation, and integration of wastewater heat recovery systems, identifying fouling control, system optimization, and data-driven design as critical factors for advancing wastewater as a viable unconventional thermal energy resource in modern building energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Optimization of cultivated-wasteland ratio and crop irrigation quota in the Hetao Irrigation District based on long-term soil salinity simulation
Abstract: The Hetao Irrigation District serves as a vital grain production base in China. Utilizing long-term soil salinity simulations, various scenario schemes were established to optimize the cultivated-wasteland ratio and crop irrigation quotas in the area under investigation. The results indicate that over the next decade, soil salinity levels in wasteland, cultivated land, and the transition zone above the drain level are expected to decrease, whereas soil salinity in the transition zone below the drain level is projected to increase. Title: Transcriptomic biomarker analysis of micro- and nanoplastic induced cardiovascular toxicity reveals perturbations in mitochondrial and ribosomal networks

Abstract: Environmental pollutants are increasingly recognized as major threats to human health worldwide with micro and nanoplastics (MNPs) outstanding on top, yet their contribution to cardiovascular disease (CVD) at the molecular level remains underexplored. This dual molecular mark, mitochondrial transcriptional regulation alongside ribosomal suppression highlights a coordinated cellular stress mechanism that could contribute to inflammation, remodeling, and energy imbalance in cardiovascular tissues. By mapping these signatures against cardiovascular associated gene sets, we demonstrated the MNP exposure converges molecular pathways already implicated in atherogenesis, cardiac remodeling, and vascular dysfunction. Importantly, transcription factor enrichment suggested upstream regulation by stress responsive factors, providing new insights into how plastic exposure may alter cellular homeostasis. Collectively, this work presents an integrative analysis linking transcriptomic signatures of human MNP exposed lung and intestinal cell models to curated cardiovascular disease gene sets. Title: Beyond passive mixing: Geometric evolution and multifunctional applications of staggered herringbone microfluidic devices
Abstract: Staggered herringbone microfluidic chips are widely used passive systems for enhancing transport and interaction under laminar flow conditions, and have been extensively applied in chemical synthesis, biosensing, and cell-related studies. The performance of these systems is fundamentally governed by their geometric design, which determines mixing efficiency, mass transfer, and flow-induced stimulation. Despite their widespread adoption, the design logic connecting geometric parameters, fabrication constraints, and functional applications has not been systematically clarified. In this review, we summarize and organize the key geometric features of herringbone microstructures and their influence on fluid behavior, fabrication feasibility, and application performance. Representative design strategies are discussed across different application scenarios, ranging from homogeneous reactions and nanoparticle synthesis to surface-interaction enhancement and cell functional regulation. Authors: Liu H.; Zhang X.; Wu W.; Wang C.; Deng Y.; Han C.; Wang X.; Wang B.
Title: Self-driven bidirectional redistribution of Zr species constructing a dual oxidation barrier in SiC-ZrC ultrafine fibers
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) ultrafine fibers hold great promise for flexible thermal protection systems, yet their service temperature is severely limited by oxidative degradation above 1300 °C. Herein, SiC-ZrC ultrafine fibers (SZF) with linearly tunable Zr content are fabricated by electrospinning, electron-beam curing, and carbothermal pyrolysis. The optimal SZF-20 maintains structural integrity after oxidation at 1600 °C for 30 min and at 1300 °C for 30 h in air. Focused ion beam sectioning and transmission electron microscope reveal temperature-dependent spatial redistribution of Zr species across the oxide scale. During high-temperature oxidation, nonstoichiometric ZrOxCy intermediates redistribute inward along the advancing oxidation front and accumulate at the oxide-matrix interface, forming a linear, high-melting-point inner ZrO2 barrier. Meanwhile, some ZrO2 grains segregate outward as the SiO2 matrix crystallizes into cristobalite, pinning grain boundaries to create an outer passivation layer. This dual-barrier architecture synergistically suppresses oxygen ingress and microcrack formation, thereby enabling reliable short-term high-temperature oxidation tolerance up to 1600 °C. The assembled fiber aerogels demonstrate nearly full shape recovery with residual strain below 1% following 80% compression, good thermal shock stability over repeated rapid cycles between 1600 and 25 °C, and low thermal conductivity, highlighting their great potential as reusable high-temperature thermal protection materials. © 2026

Title: Interlaminar shear behaviour of additively manufactured continuous fibre-reinforced composites using MWCNT-coated filaments
Abstract: The unsatisfactory interlaminar performance in additively manufactured continuous fibre-reinforced composites (CFRCs) remains a major challenge inherent to the printing process. Incorporating multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) has improved interlaminar performance in traditionally manufactured laminates. However, the use of MWCNTs in additively manufactured CFRCs has received little attention to date. This study investigates the interlaminar shear behaviour of additively manufactured CFRCs enhanced via coating MWCNTs on the surface of continuous fibre filaments. An automatic layer-by-layer process was developed to coat two types of fibre filament materials: glass fibre filaments (GFF) and carbon fibre filaments (CFF). Multilayer MWCNTs were deposited onto the filaments by sequentially adsorbing positively charged polyethyleneimine (PEI) and negatively charged MWCNTs via an electrostatic self-assembly process. The automated process promoted relatively uniform MWCNT coating through precise control of the filament speed. The updated coating baths allowed the filament to pass over a thin layer of solution without contacting rollers, thereby avoiding mechanical damage associated with the previous roller-based system. MWCNTs were successfully deposited on both GFF and CFF. The contribution of MWCNTs to the interlaminar shear properties differed between CFF and GFF in terms of tangent modulus, maximum load and ultimately the interlaminar shear strength. With a single layer of MWCNTs, the maximum short beam shear load improved by 4% and 14% for CFF and GFF composites, respectively. The addition of 1–5 MWCNT layers enhanced the tangent modulus across all tested configurations, ranging 12–20% for CFF and 32–96% for GFF. The effects of MWCNTs on the stiffness were more pronounced for GFF samples than stiffer CFF samples. The integration of MWCNTs into additively manufactured CFRCs would facilitate the production of customised lightweight components with improved interlaminar performance. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Evaluating the Durability and Aesthetic Stability of Three Vaccumm-Formed Retainer Materials: An In Vitro Comparative Study
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: To evaluate and compare the mechanical properties and color stability of three types of commercially available thermoplastic retainer materials in a simulated oral environment. Material and Methods: Ten thermoformed samples of retainer materials from three manufacturers (Leone; Duran; Essix ACE) were selected. Samples were subjected to three different testing solutions: artificial saliva at room temperature; artificial saliva supplemented with hot tea at 55º C to 60º C temperature (15 minutes each day); artificial saliva augmented with a cold carbonated drink at 3.5º C to 5.5º C temperature (15 minutes each day), all for 2 weeks. The mechanical properties were characterized using a universal testing machine (MultiTest 10-i) and colour stability was evaluated using a Bio-Rad Smart Spec Analyser Statistical analysis comparing results between retainer groups and testing solutions was carried out using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by Dunn's post hoc test. Results: Samples tested in the Hot Tea group showed statistically significant (p<0.05) differences in modulus of elasticity, yield strength, and ultimate tensile strength compared with the other groups. Samples tested in the Hot Tea group and the Cold Carbonated drink group showed a statistically significant (p<0.05) colour change. Among the thermoplastic sample groups, Duran showed significantly better mechanical performance, and Leone showed the least colour change. Conclusion: Duran showed exceptional mechanical performance, whereas Leone showed greater stain resistance. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). All rights reserved.

Title: Validity and Reliability of the Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle Method for Determining Masticatory Preference in Children Before Premolar Transition
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: To evaluate the validity and reliability of Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle (PFMA) method with a modified device compared to the clinical method as the gold standard for determining masticatory preference side in children. Material and Methods: Validity and reliability study of diagnostic tests. The study included 102 children, aged 6 to 9 years, before the transition to premolars. The outcome measures were the validity and reliability of the PFMA method compared to the clinical method as the gold standard. To measure the PFMA, a device was designed; for the direct clinical observation method, it was performed with a portion of baguette bread over seven mastication cycles. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values were measured; and reliability through intra-and inter-observer agreements using simple Kappa. Results: Sensitivity and negative predictive values were the highest percentages, being 88% with a 95% confidence interval, providing good validity, ruling out the condition of unilateral mastication with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.15. The interobserver agreement (reproducibility) was ideal (p=1.000), and the intraobserver agreement (repeatability) was significant, with an agreement percentage of 30.95%. Conclusion: The Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle with a modified device proved to be a method with good validity and a useful tool as a screening test to identify the masticatory preference side.
