Authors: Wang A.; Liu E.; Li Z.; Wang B.; Wang Y.; Guan Y.
Title: Dual boron‑coordinated active sites steering an “activation‑migration‑desorption” relay pathway in S‑scheme SubPc/Ag‑ZnIn2S4 for H2O2 photosynthesis from wastewater
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) faces an intrinsic trade-off between activity and selectivity, primarily due to the lack of well-defined and functionally differentiated active sites. Herein, a SubPc/Ag–ZnIn2S4 (SubPc/Ag–ZIS) S-scheme heterojunction is constructed by coordinating subphthalocyanine (SubPc–Br) onto Ag cluster-decorated ZnIn2S4. Distinct from conventional dual-site catalysts, this work achieves atomic-precision site differentiation via boron coordination chemistry, where the electron-rich B–Ag site activates O2, and the B–S site lowers the H2O2 desorption barrier. More importantly, the interfacial potential difference drives directional migration of the activated ·O2− intermediate from B–Ag to B–S, establishing an unprecedented “activation–migration–desorption” relay pathway. Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) confirms that this dual-site synergy significantly prolongs the charge carrier lifetime, providing a favorable kinetic foundation. The optimal catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 1200 μmol g−1 h−1 with a 2e− ORR selectivity of 78%. In the presence of tetracycline (TC) wastewater, hole-driven TC degradation (reaching 93.5% within 60 min) further inhibits charge recombination and synergistically increases the hydrogen peroxide generation rate to 1579.8 μmol g−1 h−1. This work establishes a boron coordination chemistry-driven dual-site relay catalysis strategy, offering a new paradigm for integrating efficient H2O2 photosynthesis with pollutant degradation. © 2026

Authors: Simbolon D.; Siregar E.S.Y.; Wahju R.I.; Yulianto I.; Siregar V.P.; Pianto T.A.; Rosmasita; Sangadji M.S.; Andika F.; Mulyadi R.A.; Putra M.Y.U.; Rasidi
Title: Environmental modeling of yellowfin tuna fishing grounds integrating oceanographic and biological parameters using generalized additive model
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Marine environmental variability influences the distribution, productivity, and habitat suitability of yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares). However, fishing-ground assessment based primarily on environmental conditions or production may overlook the biological suitability of harvested fish. The study objectives were to develop an integrated generalized additive model framework for assessing yellowfin tuna fishing grounds. The framework combined oceanographic conditions and fishing operational factors with production potential and fish size through two complementary Generalized additive models. METHODS: The study was conducted in the waters of West Sumatra, eastern Indian Ocean, Indonesia. Fisheries and oceanographic data covered 2019–2024, while biological observations covered 2019, 2020, and 2024. Oceanographic predictors included sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a concentration, sea surface salinity, and sea surface height. Fisheries predictors included fishing year, month, gear, spatial location, and vessel capacity. A total of 8,771 yellowfin tuna fork-length measurements were analyzed. A fork length of 99 centimeters was used as the maturity-based threshold. Two complementary generalized additive models were developed. The Fishing Ground–Environment, Technology, and Production model used catch as the production response. The Fishing Ground–Environment, Technology, and Size model used fork length as the biological response. FINDINGS: Sea surface temperature ranged from 29.37–30.45 degrees Celsius. Chlorophyll-a concentration ranged from 0.21–0.43 milligrams per cubic meter. Sea surface salinity ranged from 33.29–33.87 practical salinity units. Sea surface height ranged from 0.46–0.59 meters. Overall, 94 percent of fish were harvest-suitable. The production model had an Akaike information criterion of 155,482.9 and cumulative deviance explained of 11.5 percent. The size model had an Akaike information criterion of 77,913.73 and cumulative deviance explained of 28.74 percent. Medium to high fishing-ground potential occurred more frequently around the Mentawai Islands. Temporal integration identified highly potential and potential fishing-period statuses based on relative production potential and the landing-based biological size indicator. CONCLUSION: The integrated generalized additive model framework links environmental conditions, fishing operations, production, and biological size. This approach provides a more selective basis for adaptive and sustainable management of yellowfin tuna fisheries. Title: Host-guest interaction and π–π stacking-directed construction of three-dimensional monolithic precursors for molecular-level N/O/S co-doped porous carbon in supercapacitors
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Heteroatom doping is an effective strategy for enhancing the electrochemical performance of porous carbon for supercapacitors. However, inhomogeneous dopant distribution within carbon frameworks presents challenges in enhancing specific capacitance. Herein, a molecular-level heteroatom doping strategy was proposed for constructing N/O/S co-doped porous carbon (DPC) through synergistic integration of chemically induced phase separation (CIPS), host-guest inclusion, and π–π stacking interactions. Monochlorotriazinyl-β-cyclodextrin was synthesized as a host molecule and oxygen source to encapsulate sulfur-containing guest molecules, and the aromaticity of triazine moieties and guest molecules further promoted π–π stacking-assisted assembly. Meanwhile, branched polyethylenimine (b-PEI) served as both nitrogen source and crosslinker to construct a three-dimensional interconnected monolithic precursor via CIPS. The resulting monolithic precursor enabled homogeneous heteroatom incorporation to enhance pseudocapacitance and facilitated the formation of hierarchically porous carbon with abundant accessible active sites after carbonization and activation. Benefiting from uniform N/O/S co-doping, high specific surface area, and hierarchical porosity, the obtained DPC delivered a high specific capacitance of 642 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and maintained 99% capacitance retention after 20,000 cycles in a three-electrode system. Furthermore, the assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieved an energy density of 19.78 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 299.95 W kg−1, with 96% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. Notably, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor delivered an energy density of 40.2 Wh kg−1. This work provides an effective strategy for achieving uniform heteroatom doping in porous carbon materials toward high-performance supercapacitors. © 2026

Title: Stability of new X-site MAX phases by high-throughput DFT simulations and machine learning with experimental assessment
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The MAX phases have attracted significant attention due to their structural diversity and potential applications. However, they were previously restricted to a very limited set of X-site elements, primarily B, C, and N. This work systematically investigates the synthetic potential of novel X-site MAX phases through first-principles calculations, machine-learning screening, and experimental validation. By selecting thermodynamically and intrinsically stable MAX phases, 206 stable phases (109 211-type and 97 312-type) were identified from a pool of 1980 candidate phases. The stability trends reveal that X-site elements with moderate atomic radii and electronegativity favor phase stability. Further, machine learning models, particularly an artificial neural network with eight key elemental descriptors, achieved an overall accuracy of 86.74%, with 83% accuracy for stable phases. Experimentally, Ti2SeP was obtained as the dominant phase via self-propagating high-temperature synthesis, with lattice parameters matching theoretical predictions, providing preliminary experimental support for its predicted accessibility. © 2026

Title: Structural evolution and mechanical properties of metallic disordered materials influenced by the Bragg effect of ion irradiation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Ion irradiation, an established radiation damage technique, exhibits the Bragg peak effect, resulting in uneven energy deposition along the incidence trajectory. This study evaluated proton irradiation on ZrCuNiAl(Nb) metallic glasses (MGs). A SRIM simulation demonstrated decreased displacement damage in the Nb-containing MG in the cascade region (CR). Atomic force microscopy revealed an anomalous increase in energy deposition (Edis) in the CR of the Nb-containing sample, in contrast to the reduced liquid-like character in the Nb-free sample. Combined with synchrotron radiation results, Nb promotes short-range ordered structures with high displacement threshold energy; its doping mainly alters the structural response inside the track region under electronic energy loss, forming a “loose yet stable” latent track structure with enhanced damage buffering capability. The structure can accommodate part of the cascade-induced defects and suppress their long-range migration, thereby maintaining stable hardness and modulus in ZrCuNiAlNb along the irradiation path, whereas ZrCuNiAl exhibits irradiation-induced hardening. These results yield fundamental insights into the role of electronic energy loss and provide important guidelines for elucidating defect-buffering mechanisms in MGs under ion radiation. © 2026

Title: Artificial gene clusters designed for simultaneous multi-gene expression enable reconstruction of metabolite biosynthesis pathways in Trichoderma reesei
Abstract: The filamentous fungus Trichoderma reesei represents a highly promising chassis cell for the efficient synthesis of both protein and non-protein metabolites. Despite the availability of diverse genetic manipulation tools for T. reesei , the engineering of chassis cells frequently requires coordinated regulation of multiple genes, a process that remains laborious and time-consuming with current methods. Here, we designed a modular and inducible artificial gene cluster (AGC) by repurposing functional DNA elements from the quinic acid (QA)-responsive gene cluster in T. reesei . This AGC is capable of expressing up to six functional genes for the assembly of genetic circuits. Under culture conditions utilizing a mixed carbon source of glycerol and QA, both robust cellular vegetative growth and activation of the gene cluster are compatible. Moreover, we identified qai1 as a gene encoding a putative transcriptional activator that governs the expression of the qai gene cluster. Notably, its overexpression alone is sufficient to bypass QA-sensing induction. Leveraging this insight, we engineered a QA-independent, constitutively expressed version of the AGC. As a proof of concept, we reconstructed the biosynthetic pathways for ilicicolin H and erythritol in T. reesei using the above QA-dependent and QA-independent AGCs, successfully achieving the synthesis of ilicicolin H and enhanced erythritol production in the T. reesei chassis cells. In summary, our study establishes novel genetic manipulation tools for engineering T. reesei chassis cells, allowing for rapid, multiplexed gene expression regulation to facilitate metabolite biosynthesis. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang J.-N.; Wang Y.-Q.; Zuo J.-D.; Wu K.; Zhang J.-Y.; Liu G.; Sun J.
Title: Interface engineering: Enhanced oxidation resistance of Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating exposed to 1000 °C steam
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: In this study, a crystalline/amorphous Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating with equal layer thickness of 50 nm, as well as the amorphous CrTaAl and pure Cr coatings, were deposited on zircaloy substrates via magnetron sputtering, subsequently exposed to 1000 °C steam to investigate their oxidation behavior and the structural evolution of oxide scales. The amorphous CrTaAl coating exhibited limited oxidation resistance comparable to that of the Cr coating, while its degradation was mainly driven by the extensive phase separation within the amorphous coating upon O penetration and the insufficient retardation of O diffusion by the thin Cr2O3 layer and adjacent Ta2O5 layer. In contrast, the heterogeneous interfaces and tailored elemental diffusion kinetics synergistically dominate the oxidation process in Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating, resulting in a gradually thickened Cr2O3 outer oxide layer with multilayered Al2O3 formed at the interfaces. This hierarchical oxide structure functions as an effective diffusion barrier for impeding O penetration and confers superior oxidation resistance on the Cr/CrTaAl multilayered coating than single layer coatings. Moreover, the detailed microstructure evolution during oxidation and the underlying failure mechanisms were unraveled. These findings provide critical insights into the microstructural design of advanced multilayered coatings for enhanced oxidation resistance in nuclear fuel cladding applications. © 2026

Title: Design and simulation of a renewable energy-based microgrid for Accra Technical University
Abstract: Rising electricity costs, coupled with the unreliability of the supply, are big challenges facing higher learning institutions in developing nations, where the use of fossil fuels in centralized power generation systems limits the efficiency of the systems in providing sustainable power services. In the case of Ghana, the challenges are more pronounced in urban-based institutions where the availability of electricity is essential in the conduct of learning, research, and administrative activities. This study outlines the design and techno-economic optimization of the microgrid system, powered by renewable energy, for Accra Technical University (ATU) in Ghana, with the aim of providing reliable energy services while minimizing the cost of energy production and its impact on the environment. Using HOMER PRO, the study developed the microgrid model, where the optimized microgrid is composed of a solar–battery microgrid, comprising 3400 solar panels, Schneider Core inverters, and lithium iron phosphate battery systems, where the simulation results indicate the ability of the microgrid system to generate energy that meets 100% of the energy demand, with the expected energy generated per annum being 3.35 GWh, while the autonomy of the battery is expected to be 68.5 h. Economically, the optimized design realizes a Net Present Cost of GHS 17.1 million and a Levelized Cost of Electricity of GHS 0.350/kWh, which reflects a significant reduction in electricity cost compared to traditional grid-connected supply. The optimized configuration supplies the full campus electricity demand primarily from solar-based generation supported by battery storage, thereby reducing dependence on conventional grid electricity and improving the environmental performance of the institution. Apart from the cost savings, the suggested microgrid design enhances the reliability of electricity supply, reduces the risk of power outages, and realizes a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, which aligns with the renewable energy goals of Ghana. The results prove that renewable energy-based microgrids for university campuses are technically viable and economically justifiable. This paper also presents a model that can be followed for developing reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective microgrids for universities in developing countries. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Tian J.; Chen H.; Dong Q.; Xu C.; Xu J.; Zhang L.; Liu D.; Wang W.
Title: Ultrasonically textured engineering of protein amyloid fibrils-tannic acid composite hydrogels for dysphagia management
Abstract: Dysphagia severely affects the quality of life in elderly and neurological patients. Conventional carbohydrate-based dysphagia-oriented foods, which have insufficient nutritional richness, tend to fragment during oral processing, increasing aspiration risk. Protein amyloid fibrils offer high protein supplement and robust mechanical properties, which can form stable hydrogels with polyphenols, suggesting potential for dysphagia-oriented foods. However, the effect of the protein amyloid fibril structure on related hydrogel properties and its International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative (IDDSI) classification remain unclear. In this case, we used ultrasonic pretreatment to modulate the β-lactoglobulin fibril structure, and then induced fibril-tannic acid (TA) interactions to form composite hydrogels. Transmission electron microscopy showed that ultrasound accelerated fibrillation kinetics and induced fibril shortening, and excessive treatment (U50-10, 4.80 W/mL, 10 min) resulted in predominantly short fibrillar species. Ultrasonic pretreatment significantly increased the surface hydrophobicity and free sulfhydryl content of the resulting fibrils. These morphological and physicochemical changes markedly enhanced hydrogel network stability, as confirmed by rheology and texture analysis. Among all groups, U50-6 (4.80 W/mL, 6 min) improved elasticity and creep recovery the most, while also showing the highest water-holding capacity and hardness, attributed to a denser crosslinked network formed by moderately shortened fibrils. Notably, hydrogels precisely covered IDDSI levels from 3 to 5, allowing tailored design for patients with varying swallowing abilities. This study establishes a structure-assembly-function relationship for protein fibril–polyphenol systems and offers a rational strategy for developing personalized dysphagia-oriented foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Cen M.; Xu F.; Zhu X.; Yang M.; Li K.; Zhou Q.; Li R.; Qin Y.; Chen J.; Balogun M.-S.; Huang Y.; Yang H.; Hu Y.
Title: Lattice tensile strain restructures interfacial hydrogen‑bond network for boosted alkaline hydrogen evolution
Abstract: The sluggish kinetics of alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), governed by water dissociation, remains a critical challenge for efficient hydrogen production. Here, we demonstrate that lattice tensile strain can regulate interfacial water structure and thereby accelerate HER kinetics. Density functional theory calculations identify an optimal tensile strain (~+2%) that maximizes p-d orbital hybridization and induces a favorable downshift of the D-band center, optimizing adsorption energetics. Meanwhile, the strain-enhanced built-in electric field promotes charge transfer to interfacial water, facilitating its activation. Guided by this principle, a Mo/W-CoP catalyst supported on etched NiCu1-x@Ni foam with a tensile strain of ~ + 1.9% is constructed. An operando Raman imaging approach is developed to spatially resolve lattice strain and interfacial water configurations, revealing that tensile-strain-rich domains serve as preferential sites for the enrichment of coordinated water, thereby reconstructing the hydrogen-bond network. Consequently, the catalyst delivers an overpotential of 133 mV at −50 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH. This work establishes a direct link between lattice strain and interfacial hydrogen-bond network, offering a general strategy for engineering electrocatalytic interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Huang L.; He X.; Jiang J.; Li X.; Zhou M.; Mia M.H.; Hong M.; He H.; Huo S.; Yu Z.
Title: Biomimetic Gradient Porous Core–Shell Fibers with Enhanced Gas Sensing for CO-Temperature Dual-Mode Early Fire Warning
Abstract: Early fire detection systems that are highly sensitive are essential for reducing the impact of fire disasters. However, their development still faces significant challenges due to the lack of capability for simultaneous monitoring of both temperature and gas. Herein, we propose a facile coaxial wet-spinning strategy to fabricate a dual-parameter fiber sensor capable of simultaneously detecting carbon monoxide (CO) and temperature for early combustion warning. The resulting core–sheath structured fiber consists of a CO sensing sheath made of SnO2/In2O3 heterojunction/aramid nanofiber (ANF)/silver nanowire composite with biomimetic gradient pores, an ANF isolation layer, and a temperature sensing core composed of MXene. The gradient porous sheath constructed by gradient-induced phase separation technology exhibits gradually decreasing pore sizes from outer (> 10 μm) to inner (< 3 μm) regions. This structure demonstrates a significant enhancement in the fiber sensor’s sensitivity to CO, achieving a 15% higher response compared to non-gradient porous structures (ΔR/R0 = 0.95%/ppm; detection limit of 10 ppm), with the response time reduced to 19.28 s, surpassing the response speed of most fire-warning fibers. Additionally, this fiber sensor can rapidly monitor abnormal temperature increases, enabling flame alarm functionality within 3 s. It also achieves precise real-time temperature detection within the range of 50–300 °C, exhibiting high sensitivity (20.6 μV K−1) and a strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.99). This work highlights the significant potential of gradient pore in enhancing CO sensing and offers a novel perspective for the design of ultrafast early fire-warning fiber sensors. Authors: Zhang X.; Niu J.; Fan Y.; Jia L.; Ma J.; Song T.
Title: Engineering hollow-strut lattices for low-density, high-strength metal mechanical metamaterials
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hollow-strut lattice metamaterials enable lightweight metallic materials by placing material away from the neutral axis, thereby enhancing bending stiffness and buckling resistance. Their design has been largely limited to circular hollow struts. Here, strut cross-sectional geometry is introduced as a new design lever for high-performance hollow-strut lattices. Hollow square-strut body-centered cubic lattices are designed, fabricated in Ti-6Al-4V by laser powder bed fusion, and rationalized using a geometry-dependent analytical model. The square hollow geometry provides a higher second moment of area than circular hollow strut, enabling stronger resistance to deformation. Consequently, Ti-6Al-4V hollow square-strut lattice designs with three densities in the range of 1.4–2.3 g/cm3 achieve yield strengths of 103–328 MPa, compressive strengths of 132–448 MPa, and elastic moduli of 5.0–7.5 GPa, outperforming circular counterparts across all densities. Their yield strength increases by up to 27%, accompanied by more uniform strain distribution, delayed strain localization, and improved deformation stability. At comparable densities, their absolute yield strength exceeds that of high-strength magnesium alloys while retaining the corrosion resistance, biocompatibility, and other intrinsic advantages of Ti-6Al-4V. This work establishes cross-sectional geometry as a powerful design dimension for lightweight, high-strength metallic mechanical metamaterials. © 2026

Title: Ce/La-induced formation of Al2RE/Al2Ca composite phases and enhancement of mechanical properties and ignition resistance in Mg-Al-Mn-Ca alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Mg-Al-Mn-Ca (AMX) alloys are promising candidates for next-generation lightweight structural materials owing to their attractive combination of mechanical properties and ignition resistance. In this study, the effects of Ce/La co-addition on the second-phase evolution, mechanical properties, and ignition resistance of an AMX402 alloy were systematically investigated. The results show that Ce/La co-addition induces the formation of micron-scale Al2 rare earth (RE)/Al2Ca composite phases, which is governed by preferential Al2RE precipitation, low lattice mismatch between Al2RE and Al2Ca, and favorable adsorption of Ca atoms at Ce-enriched sites. Meanwhile, the tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength increased from 270 ± 4 and 316 ± 5 to 293 ± 6 and 326 ± 6 MPa, respectively, mainly owing to precipitation strengthening by the rod-like Al2Ca phase, grain boundary strengthening, and residual dislocation strengthening. The ignition temperature also increased from 897 ± 15 to 971 ± 6 °C. This improvement is attributed to Ce/La-induced redistribution of Ca, which increases dissolved Ca in the α-Mg matrix and promotes the formation of a compact MgO-CaO protective oxide film. These findings provide insight into rare-earth-mediated second-phase regulation for developing high-strength ignition-resistant Mg alloys. © 2026

Authors: Zheng S.; Zhang L.; Bai W.; Ren L.; Wei L.; Feng D.; Wang S.; Zhang L.
Title: AIE-enhanced mesoporous nanozyme-based multimodal lateral flow assay for trimodal sensing of imidacloprid and Hg2+
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Multimodal lateral flow immunoassay (LFA) strategies have largely relied on the parallel combination of functionally homogeneous signals, leaving the effective dynamic range and gradient complementarity among detection modes unaddressed. Herein, we report a mesopore-confinement co-assembly strategy in which the AIE fluorophore BTPE and AuIr bimetallic nanozymes are simultaneously loaded into the radial channels of dendritic mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DMSNs), yielding a multifunctional nanotag DMSN-BTPE/AuIr with colorimetric, catalytic-enhanced colorimetric, and fluorescent outputs. Channel confinement enriches BTPE to activate AIE emission while sustaining AuIr catalytic loading; optimization of the BTPE-to-AuIr ratio balances the fluorescent and catalytic outputs within a single nanoparticle. The three signals provide complementary readouts across different concentration ranges, extending the effective dynamic range to six orders of magnitude. Applied to simultaneous dual-channel detection of imidacloprid (IMI) and Hg2+ in cucumber and river water, the fluorescent mode achieved LODs of 3.97 and 4.04 pg/mL with recoveries of 81.44%–115.87%, in close agreement with LC-MS/MS and ICP-MS reference methods. This work provides a design strategy for multifunctional nanotags and multimodal lateral flow detection over a wide concentration range. © 2026

Authors: Tan H.; Wang D.; Li Y.
Title: New pulse sequence for improving cardiac black-blood and PSIR MRI quality in cases of arrhythmia
Abstract: Most conventional cardiac MRI scans, which rely on electrocardiogram (ECG)-triggered segmented acquisition for k-space data, are highly sensitive to arrhythmia—a vulnerability that can induce severe motion artifacts, thereby degrading image quality and diagnostic accuracy. This study developed a novel pulse sequence: an MRI-independent thread continuously records and analyzes the subject's heart rhythm throughout the entire scan, calculates key temporal parameters in real time, feeds them back to update the sequence dynamically based on actual rhythm, thereby reducing k-space data misalignment and eliminating motion artifacts. Experimental results showed that the new pulse sequence effectively improved cardiac black-blood T2-weighted and phase-sensitive inversion recovery (PSIR) image quality in cases of arrhythmia, and with broad application prospects for cardiac MRI in arrhythmic subjects. This “prevention-first” approach (rather than “repair-after”) makes it highly clinically translatable, as it can be deployed on standard equipment without additional costs. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zheng H.; Chen W.; Liu Y.; Guo L.; Huang X.; Pan J.H.
Title: Proton-rich interfacial microenvironment engineering enables efficient and durable hydrogen evolution over Ru/metal (hydr)oxide catalysts
Abstract: The intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are largely associated with limited proton availability in alkaline media. To accelerate the Volmer kinetic step and alleviate pH dependence, we report a Ru3 + hydrolysis-driven impregnation strategy for constructing localized acidic and proton-enriched interfaces. Using Ru@Ni(OH)2 as a model catalyst, Ru species are anchored onto oxygen-vacancy-rich Ni(OH)2 nanosheets. Operando Raman spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that Ru sites promote water dissociation process and act as proton capture centers, thereby facilitating the formation of hydronium ions (H3O+) species. The resulting interfacial microenvironment balances hydrogen adsorption strength and accelerates HER kinetics. As a result, the Ru@Ni(OH)2 catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 50 mV at -10 mA cm-2 and 364 mV at -2800 mA cm-2, together with sustained operation over 1200 h at -100 mA cm-2. This synthesis approach can be readily applied to a wide range of transition-metal and rare-earth (hydro)oxide systems. This work establishes interfacial proton regulation as an effective strategy and provides a broadly applicable framework for designing high-performance electrocatalysts with accelerated reaction kinetics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Abstract: The article presents the results of a qualitative analysis of circuits of autonomous current and voltage inverters with cut-off valves. The influence of the charge on the switching capacitor in parallel and series equivalent circuits on the restoration of the switching properties of the thyristors in the inverter power circuit is studied. It is shown that, due to the energy periodically accumulated in the inductive elements of the load, the voltage across the switching capacitor in the cut-off state is higher than in a conventional parallel autonomous current inverter. This ensures increased switching stability of the inverter. Consequently, the circuit of an autonomous current inverter with cut-off valves remains operational in valve converters for variable-frequency electric drives and maintains performance during sudden load surges and short circuits, since the voltage on the switching capacitor does not depend on the load voltage. Thus, the charge on the switching capacitor is preserved even when the load voltage drops sharply between thyristor commutations. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Authors: Sardar Khan S.K.; Sabarees G.

Title: MXene-based biosensors for biomedical diagnostics: From molecular recognition to wearable systems
Source title: Advances in Biomarker Sciences and Technology
Abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) have emerged as a versatile class of electroactive nanomaterials for next-generation biomedical diagnostics. Their metallic conductivity, tunable surface terminations (–O, –OH, –F), hydrophilicity, and compatibility with nanocomposite engineering enable efficient biomolecule immobilization and high-fidelity signal transduction across electrochemical, plasmonic, wearable, and implantable platforms. This review critically examines recent advances in MXene-enabled biosensors for oncology diagnostics, metabolic monitoring, neurotransmitter detection, and continuous physiological analysis. In cancer diagnostics, MXene-based immunosensors have achieved ultralow detection limits, including 0.0036 pg mL−1 for squamous cell carcinoma antigen and 1 nU mL−1 for CA15-3 and CA-19-9, while exosome detection has reached sensitivities of 19 particles μL−1. In metabolic applications, MXene systems demonstrate nanomolar detection capability, rapid response times (as low as 2 s), and stable performance in whole blood and sweat matrices. Engineering strategies including noble metal hybridization, polymer stabilization, dendrimer functionalization, ratiometric sensing, and microfluidic integration are analyzed to elucidate structure–property–performance relationships. Wearable and implantable architectures further extend MXene functionality toward real-time health monitoring. Despite their promising analytical performance, important translational challenges remain, including oxidation susceptibility, biofouling, enzyme fragility, batch-to-batch reproducibility, large-scale manufacturing standardization, and limited long-term clinical validation. By integrating materials engineering with mechanistic insight, comparative analysis, and translational benchmarking, this review provides a strategic roadmap for advancing MXene biosensors from laboratory prototypes toward clinically viable and commercially translatable diagnostic technologies. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Buckling Analysis of Functionally Graded Beams under Combined Loadings
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This paper investigates the buckling behavior of axially functionally graded (FG) material beams subjected to combined loads with various boundary conditions. The classical beam theory is employed for the analysis, and material properties are described using power law equations. The governing equation for buckling of FG beams was derived using the energy method and solved by using the generalized differential quadrature (DQ) method. The current study explores the buckling problem of FG beam under combined loadings, focusing on the interplay of gradient index, parameter np and boundary conditions. The results demonstrate that the buckling resistance of functionally graded beams is enhanced with an increase in the gradient index. For functionally graded beams with a fixed parameter np, the critical buckling load exhibits a nonlinear increase with the gradient index. On the other hand, for functionally graded beams with a fixed material distribution, the critical buckling load decreases almost linearly with the parameter np, and the slope of this linear relationship is determined by the gradient index and the boundary conditions. This study provides valuable insights into the buckling behavior of functionally graded beams under combined loads, offering guidance for the design and optimization of such beams in engineering applications. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Authors: Yang H.-K.; Wang C.; Li J.-Z.; Song S.-L.; Jiang Y.-M.; Ning H.; Wang H.-Y.
Title: Multi-layered texture-heterogeneous architecture enabling strength-ductility synergy in Mg laminates
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys remains challenging because their inherent plastic anisotropy leads to a trade-off between texture-induced strengthening and strain accommodation. Here, we designed and fabricated texture-heterogeneous Mg laminates by accumulative roll bonding, comprising five alternating layers of Mg-Al-Zn with a strong basal texture (hard layer) and Mg-Al-Sn-Ca with a weaker basal texture (soft layer). Two texture-heterogeneous laminates with different stacking architectures have been constructed, i.e., hard-soft-hard-soft-hard (HSH-5L) and soft-hard-soft-hard-soft (SHS-5L). HSH-5L exhibits a yield strength of 192 MPa and fracture elongation of 22%, representing improvements of 8.1% and 27%, respectively, compared with SHS-5L. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, digital image correlation, and finite element simulation indicate that the improved mechanical response is associated with enhanced interfacial constraints and higher strain gradients in HSH-5L. These conditions facilitate <c+a> slip near interfaces and provide more nucleation sites for strain bands (SB). As deformation proceeds, dense SBs mainly dominated by basal <a> slip gradually intersect. The intersection regions induce local stress concentration and activate additional non-basal slip, which in turn restricts the further propagation of SBs and thereby contributes to sustained strain hardening in the HSH-5L sample. By contrast, in the SHS-5L sample, basal <a> slip initiates and propagates rapidly during deformation, forming long-range SBs that lead to local deformation instability and premature fracture. These findings provide insights for the design of heterogeneous Mg laminates with high strength and ductility. © 2026

Authors: Du J.; Yan X.; Zhang L.; Wu Z.; Liu B.; Li Y.; Jin Z.; Aurbach D.; Fornasiero P.
Title: Oxygen–vacancy-assisted S-scheme interface engineering toward efficient and stable solar hydrogen generation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Although the conduction band position of ZnCdS is thermodynamically favorable for proton reduction, its photocatalytic performance is limited by the rapid recombination of charge carriers and the low efficiency of charge separation. To address this issue, a ZnCdS/OV–CoCeOX heterojunction was constructed. The energy level difference between ZnCdS and CoCeOX drives the formation of an S-scheme heterojunction, promoting directional electron transfer and selective recombination of low-energy holes, and improving the efficiency of electron–hole separation. The oxygen vacancies in CoCeOX capture electrons by creating trap states, delaying recombination and providing unsaturated sites to promote the adsorption and activation of reactants. The synergistic effect of the S-scheme band alignment and the oxygen vacancies enables the effective accumulation of electrons at the active sites, promoting hydrogen production. DFT calculations and experiments confirmed that the redistribution of interface charges dominates the separation of charge carriers and the catalytic performance. After optimization, the composite material containing 20% OV–CoCeOX has an activity 5 times higher than that of a single component. This work reveals the synergistic enhancement mechanism of band matching in S-scheme heterojunctions and oxygen vacancy defects, providing new ideas for the design of efficient heterojunction catalysts. © 2026

Title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT. © 2027 The author(s). Title: An explainable quantum neural network framework for reservoir permeability prediction from conventional well logs
Abstract: Accurate prediction of reservoir permeability is essential for reservoir characterization, production forecasting, and hydrocarbon recovery optimization. Conventional empirical and machine learning approaches often struggle to capture the complex nonlinear relationships between petrophysical variables while providing limited model interpretability. This study presents an explainable permeability prediction framework based on a variational Quantum Neural Network (QNN) simulated on classical hardware using the PennyLane quantum machine learning platform. The proposed framework integrates Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to improve model transparency and facilitate geological interpretation of the learned relationships. A total of 3213 depth-matched samples acquired from three wells in the Mpyo Field, Albertine Graben, Uganda, were used to develop and evaluate the model using five conventional well-log measurements: thermal neutron porosity (TNPH), effective porosity (PHIE), formation density (RHOZ), spectral gamma ray (SGR), and shale volume (VSH). Hyperparameters of the QNN were optimized through systematic grid search and compared with a classical Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH), Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) models under identical experimental conditions. The simulated QNN achieved superior predictive accuracy, yielding training RMSE and MAE values of 0.019 and 0.0105, respectively, while demonstrating improved generalization on a blind test well compared with the benchmark model. SHAP analysis identified effective porosity as the dominant predictor of permeability, followed by thermal neutron porosity and spectral gamma ray, with feature contributions remaining consistent with established petrophysical principles. Bootstrap-based uncertainty analysis further demonstrated reliable prediction intervals across different reservoir intervals. Although implemented on a classical simulator rather than physical quantum hardware, the proposed framework illustrates the potential of quantum-inspired learning architectures for nonlinear permeability prediction while maintaining model interpretability for practical reservoir characterization. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wei L.; Xu X.; Yu Y.; Cheng G.; Fu X.; Liu P.; Chen H.
Title: Rapid globularization of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloy via ordered dislocation structures induced by pulsed current
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Transforming lamellar grains/phases to globular can improve the ductility of metallic materials. However, this process always relies on time-consuming, complex heat treatments (HTs) to regulate dislocations. This work introduces a current-driven strategy that “guides” dislocation motion to bypass this complexity, enabling rapid globularization. A prior electropulsing treatment (EPT) rapidly reorganizes the initially high-density dislocations into ordered intra-lamellar structures and promotes their accumulation near pre-existing twin boundaries under transient electro-thermal conditions. These preconditioned dislocation structures facilitate boundary splitting during a subsequent short HT, eliminating the need for cyclic or multistep processing. The resulting EPT+HT process achieves rapid globularization and a favorable strength–ductility balance. This work not only delivers an efficient strategy for microstructure regulation in additive manufacturing but also provides fundamental insights into defect dynamics under electro-thermal coupling. © 2026

Authors: Tang Y.; Yang Y.; Li J.; Cao F.; Gong Z.; Zhu H.; Li J.; Rao W.-F.; Bai Y.
Title: Simultaneous giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability in PNZST ceramics via antiferroelectric phase boundary regulation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramics are promising candidates for precision actuators, but the trade-off between giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability has severely limited their practical applications. Here, we propose a dual-pathway phase boundary regulation strategy in perovskite AFE systems to synergistically optimize electrostrain magnitude and temperature stability by designing the electric-field-induced AFE-ferroelectric (FE) transition sequence under coupled temperature-electric-field conditions. Using the prototype system of Pb0.99Nb0.02[(Zr0.75Sn0.25)xTi1−x]0.98O3 (PNZST-100xZS), our results show that PNZST-99ZS and PNZST-97ZS exhibit giant electrostrains of 0.98% and 0.77%, respectively. Remarkably, over a wide temperature range of 25–155 °C, they maintain low electrostrain fluctuations of only 16.12% and 9.21%, significantly better than previously reported materials. The excellent performance stems from the electric-field-induced orthorhombic AFE (AFEO)-rhombohedral FE (FER) transition at low temperatures and the tetragonal AFE (AFET)-FER transition at high temperatures. Between these two temperature regions, the diffuse AFEO-AFET transition bridges the two field-induced pathways, ensuring a smooth evolution of the electrostrain response across the entire operating temperature range. This work provides a new route to high-performance AFE actuator materials with both large electrostrain and wide-temperature stability. © 2026

Authors: Liu P.; Lu H.; Xu G.; Han C.; Shang M.; Song X.
Title: Synergistic enhancement of coercivity and saturation magnetization in Sm-Co alloys via multi-element doping
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Multi-element doping represents the most effective approach for enhancing the performance of permanent magnetic alloys. However, the complex interdependencies among diverse doping elements, broad concentration ranges, and intricate element-matrix interactions present significant challenges in establishing appropriate composition-property relationships, impeding efficient development of high-performance multicomponent alloys. To address this fundamental limitation, this study introduced a data-driven framework incorporating high-throughput identification of key elemental features governing magnetic properties. Principal component and feature sensitivity analyses quantified feature contributions to distinct magnetic characteristics and evaluated comprehensive weighting factors for multi-objective optimization. This integrated methodology enabled efficient and appropriate design of multi-element doped alloys targeting simultaneous enhancement of competing magnetic properties. Demonstrated by the Sm-Co-based systems, the framework concurrently enhanced both saturation magnetization and coercivity, which effectively resolved the trade-off between these properties through multi-element doping. Experimentally validated designs across multiple matrix types exhibited superior comprehensive magnetic properties, with quantitative confirmation of the model predictions. The present study provides a novel strategy that is in principle broadly applicable for designing multicomponent alloys that overcome inherent property trade-offs. © 2026

Authors: Wang J.; Ma Y.; Wang W.; Chen C.; Tang M.; Zhu S.-Y.; Zhang Y.-X.; Liang R.-Y.; Yuan F.-P.; Wu X.-L.
Title: Designing a heterogeneous dual-phase Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo alloy with enhanced strength-impact-toughness synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing high-strength titanium alloys with high toughness under varying strain rate loading has been a long-standing pursuit in the development of advanced structural materials. In this study, we report a hierarchical multiscale heterogeneous microstructure (HS) in the Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo (Ti80) alloy, comprising fine equiaxed α grains, discontinuous lamellar α phase, and transformed β (βt) phase with strong nanoscale α′ precipitates. The HS-Ti80 exhibits an unprecedented synergy of yield strength (860 MPa), uniform elongation (11.2%), and impact toughness (KV2, 104 J). The superior strain hardening capacity of the HS arises from the heterogeneous deformation induced by the coexistence of multiscale domains. The fine equiaxed α grains promote uniform stress distribution and delay strain localization, while the βt phase with nano‑α′ precipitates serves as a hard domain that accommodates strain compatibility with the α matrix. Consequently, multiple types of dislocations and deformation twins are activated, and their intricate interactions sustain plastic deformation over a wide strain range. Simultaneously, the discontinuous lamellar α grains act as effective crack buffers, deflecting propagating cracks, generating a high density of secondary cracks, and forcing a tortuous crack path, thereby substantially dissipating strain energy and enhancing impact resistance. These findings establish that architecting hierarchical HSs provides a promising strategy for developing high‑performance titanium alloys capable of withstanding both quasi‑static and impact loading. © 2026

Authors: Shahsavar A.
Title: Where does the exergy go? Risk-aware irreversibility mapping of a PCM-buffered solar photovoltaic-thermal/geothermal ventilation system
Abstract: This study answers a practical question in renewable ventilation design: where does the exergy go when solar–geothermal preconditioning is combined with latent thermal buffering? A hybrid ventilation system coupling an earth–air heat exchanger (EAHE) with an air-based photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) unit is investigated, where phase change material (PCM) is embedded around the buried duct to act as a thermal buffer. Rather than reporting only annual energy savings, the work provides a risk-aware irreversibility breakdown that tracks exergy destruction across preconditioning, mixing, humidity control, and final conditioning. Several scenario analyses are conducted using hourly meteorological records collected over the 2019–2024 period. A bi-level optimization strategy is employed to simultaneously refine the system configuration and time-dependent operating conditions, including ventilation intensity and fresh-air intake ratio. To reduce occupant discomfort under critical conditions, a conditional value-at-risk criterion is incorporated to account for extreme thermo-hygrometric situations. The results indicate that PCM integration lowers system irreversibility. This behavior is mainly attributed to decreased ventilation demand and lower fresh-air intake. As a result, exergy destruction caused by air mixing and dehumidification is reduced. Although CVaR slightly increases during limited hot periods, overall discomfort risk remains about 50–60% below the baseline. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Pérez-Lancellotti G.; Marín-Ocaranza L.
Title: Mitigation and adaptation strategies for mass removals in arid zones: A theoretical model based on urban architecture projects in Antofagasta; [Estrategias de mitigación y adaptación para remociones en masa en zonas áridas: Modelo teórico basado en proyectos de arquitectura urbana en Antofagasta]
Abstract: The Atacama Desert, particularly in the Antofagasta region, faces increasing risks of mass movement exacerbated by climate change. This article proposes a theoretical model that integrates mitigation and adaptation strategies within urban architecture projects at the neighbourhood scale, focusing on sloped desert areas. The methodological process includes an initial deductive classification stage followed by an inductive qualitative analysis. Within 13 academic projects from the School of Architecture at the Universidad Católica del Norte in the city of Antofagasta, two typologies are identified: one oriented toward mitigation through flood-control basins and retaining walls, and another mixed type that incorporates terrain adaptation, green barriers, floodable areas, ramps, and underground channelling. The model helps fill a gap in the literature on risk management in arid contexts, aligning with SDG 11 and SDG 13. It also offers a practical guide for architects and urban planners, promoting more resilient, sustainable, and safe urban policies and projects. © of the edition: Estoa, 2027.

Title: The Band Structure of In-Plane Elastic Cracked Phononic Crystals Based on the Local RBF Collocation Method
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: In this paper, the 2D cracked phononic crystals of in-plane elastic waves are studied based on the local radial basis function collocation method (LRBFCM). The direct method is used to solve the instability caused by the derivative calculation of the LRBFCM in the crack. The band structure of the cracked phononic crystals according to the wave vectors in the first Brillouin Zone are presented. The relationship between the band structure and the cracks with different lengths and positions are fully studied. Different acoustic impedance ratios, filling rates, and lattice forms are considered. The numerical results are validated by the band structures obtained from the FEM, which also show interesting phenomenon of the cracked phononic crystals. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Correlation study of vortices and pressure pulsations in multistage centrifugal pump as turbine
Abstract: Multistage centrifugal pumps operating as turbines (PATs) are important devices for hydraulic energy recovery. However, vortex-induced flow instabilities cause pressure pulsations and efficiency losses, especially in configurations with complex interstage interactions. In offshore oil and gas field systems—such as platform seawater systems, produced-water treatment systems, and subsea energy recovery—stable PAT operation is essential for reliability and continuous energy utilization. This study investigates the correlation between vortex evolution and pressure pulsation across different stages of a multistage PAT. Numerical simulations and Pearson correlation analysis reveal that in the first three stages, vorticity and pressure pulsation distributions exhibit strong spatial consistency. From the second to the last stage, both vorticity intensity and pressure pulsation amplitude increase markedly compared with the first stage. The first stage maintains a stable flow with weak dynamic–static effects, while downstream stages show less stability, dominated by dynamic interactions. In high-vorticity regions, vortex evolution is the primary cause of pressure fluctuation, and its correlation with pulsation intensity is strongest. In later stages, the vortex–pressure correlation weakens as complex interstage dynamics prevail. Overall, the results confirm a positive correlation between vorticity and pressure pulsation intensity at various locations within the multistage PAT. These findings provide theoretical insight and practical guidance for optimizing impeller–diffuser matching and stage configuration, enabling improved hydraulic stability and enhanced energy recovery efficiency, particularly under offshore and subsea operating conditions. © 2026 Author(s).

Authors: Feng X.; Su Q.; Zhou L.; Zhang J.; Chen D.; Zhu W.; Xi H.; Zhang C.; Zhang J.; Hao Y.
Title: Designing Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells with Self-Assembled Monolayer Hole Transport Layers
Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as highly versatile interfacial materials in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), offering tunable molecular structures, favorable energy-level alignment, high optical transparency, and minimized non-radiative recombination losses. With the rapid advancement of inverted (p-i-n) PSC architectures, SAM-based hole-selective contacts have demonstrated distinct advantages in achieving superior power conversion efficiency, cost-effective fabrication, and strong compatibility with scalable manufacturing processes. This review first summarizes the evolution of SAM applications, with a particular focus on SAM-based materials in p-i-n PSCs. Subsequently, the fundamental aspects of SAMs are systematically discussed. Further, common preparation methods of SAMs are reviewed, along with the key challenges encountered in achieving uniform SAM coating. Based on this, recent progress in SAM-based PSCs is comprehensively summarized, including their applications in high-efficiency single-junction devices, perovskite tandem solar cells, and large-area photovoltaic modules. The crucial roles of SAMs in energy-level modulation, interfacial modification, defect passivation, and charge transport are highlighted. Finally, the remaining challenges and future prospects of SAMs in inverted PSCs are discussed, with particular emphasis on interfacial stability and long-term operational reliability. This review aims at providing systematic insights and guidance for the further development of SAM-based inverted PSCs. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
Abstract: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries. Authors: Yudo S.; Martono D.N.; Sutjiningsih D.; Kurniawan B.
Title: Integration of the online river water quality monitoring management framework based on inclusive governance
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Online river water quality monitoring systems are increasingly used to support pollution control. Nonetheless, the efficacy of these systems remains constrained by key technical and organizational challenges, namely high data variability, sensor instability, restricted interoperability, and decentralized institutional governance. These challenges reduce the trustworthiness of online data for evidence-based pollution control policy and decision-making. The study objectives were to develop an integrated framework to improve data quality, system performance, and coordination in the governance of online river water quality monitoring river water quality monitoring in watersheds across Indonesia. METHODS: A transdisciplinary methodological approach was applied by combining 1) Integrated data quality management to assess data completeness, accuracy, validity span and stability; 2) Key performance indicators measured by the analytical hierarchy process to evaluate the performance of online river water quality monitoring systems; and 3) Soft systems methodology to build a governance-oriented conceptual model through rich descriptions, root definitions, conceptual models and evaluation of the 3Es (efficacy, efficiency and effectiveness). This study analyzed environmental data collected between 2023 and 2025 from four monitoring stations representing the upstream and downstream reaches of the Ciliwung and Cisadane Rivers. To complement these quantitative findings, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a broad range of stakeholders, including government agencies, vendors, academics, researchers, the media, community-based non-governmental organizations, and local communities residing near the four stations. FINDINGS: An analysis of data quality demonstrated robust completeness (99–100 percent), highly variable non-zero completeness across all stations, high validity across the range for dissolved oxygen, hydrogen potential, and temperature (greater than 95 percent), and large fluctuations in stability at stations affected by tidal and sediment dynamics. The system performance index was 61.18 percent. Synthesizing soft systems methodology highlighted key operational barriers, such as fragmented roles, low trust towards online data, and lack of community participation. Consequently, this study developed an online river water quality monitoring management framework designed to prioritize digital interoperability, transparency, accountability, and multi-stakeholder governance. CONCLUSION: The inclusive governance-based online river water quality monitoring framework provides an empirically informed conceptual framework for organizing data-quality, performance, and governance improvements, improved collaboration among government agencies. Subject to contextual adaptation and prospective validation, this framework offers valuable insights for management design in other watersheds, ultimately contributing to the advancement of digital environmental governance in developing nations. ©2026 The author(s). Title: Tailoring ferroelectric phase stability in zirconium-rich hafnia through atomic layer stack engineering
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: HfO2-based ferroelectric thin films are attractive for nonvolatile memories due to their scalability and CMOS compatibility. However, ferroelectricity in hafnia is typically constrained by a narrow compositional window, while Zr-rich films are prone to stabilize antiferroelectric tetragonal phases rather than the desired ferroelectric orthorhombic phase, thereby limiting both polarization robustness and device reliability. Here we show that an atomic layer stack strategy offers an effective handle to tailor the strain and further modulate phase evolution in Zr-rich HfO2-ZrO2 films. By constructing solid-solution, periodic multilayer, and bilayer HfO2-ZrO2 films under a comparable Zr-rich nominal design, we observe a clear evolution from antiferroelectricity to stable ferroelectricity with progressive relief of in-plane strain. Structural and electrical characterizations reveal that stack configuration favors the stabilization of the metastable orthorhombic phase in a Zr-rich regime conventionally unfavorable for ferroelectricity. Among the investigated architectures, the bilayer H20Z80 film exhibits a high 2Pr of 52.1 μC/cm2 together with endurance beyond 1011 cycles and a projected retention time of 10 years. These results reveal that ferroic phase evolution is extendable beyond conventional compositional constraints and can be accessed through atomic layer stacking engineering. This work provides a practical materials-design strategy for high-endurance hafnia-based ferroelectric memories. © 2026

Title: Cellular-reaction pretreatment enabled 950 °C rolling of TiAl alloy sheet: Achieving exceptional strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: In this work, we report a cellular-reaction-assisted strategy that enables successful rolling of a Ti-44Al-1.5Cr-0.5Re (at.%) alloy sheet at 950 °C while achieving an exceptional strength-ductility synergy. The cellular-reaction-derived pearlite-like microstructure contains discontinuously dispersed β0 phase, abundant phase interfaces, and pre-existing planar defects. During rolling, these microstructural features promote lamellar bending, interfacial separation, defect accumulation, and particle-stimulated nucleation-assisted recrystallization, leading to an ultrafine near-γ microstructure with an average γ grain size of 0.84 μm after 80% reduction. The rolled sheet exhibits a room-temperature tensile strength of 1378 MPa with 1.42% elongation, mainly owing to ultrafine-grain strengthening and deformation-induced stacking faults, twins, and 9R/long‑period stacking‑ordered-related structures. At 800 °C, the alloy shows a tensile strength of 476 MPa and an exceptional elongation of 283%. This superior high-temperature ductility originates from the cooperative deformation of the heterogeneous microstructure, where coarse γ grains provide strain hardening, fine γ grains accommodate deformation through grain-boundary-mediated processes, and boundary discontinuous dynamic recrystallization governs flow softening. These results highlight cellular reaction as an effective route to reconcile low-temperature rollability with strength-ductility synergy in TiAl alloy sheets. © 2026

Title: Interfacial layer-driven sliding ferroelectricity in MoS2
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Two-dimensional sliding ferroelectricity offers a promising route toward ultrathin nonvolatile memory devices by enabling polarization control via interlayer sliding. However, scalable integration of interface-engineered structures remains challenging due to complex stacking and fabrication limitations. Here, we develop a controllable thermal-gradient chemical vapor deposition strategy for the one-step synthesis of homo-structured ABB- and AAB-MoS2 with integrated interfacial and ferroelectric layers. Hybrid 2H/3R-stacked MoS2 exhibits pronounced out-of-plane ferroelectricity governed by interlayer symmetry breaking and interfacial charge redistribution. Notably, the ferroelectric response is dictated by the position of the interfacial layer. AAB-MoS2 enables nonlocal propagation of the interfacial electric field, giving rise to proximity ferroelectricity across the entire trilayer, whereas ABB-MoS2 results in a spatially confined interfacial field and layer-confined polarization. Vertical Au/MoS2/Co devices exhibit a switchable diode effect, in which interfacial layer positioning governs the Schottky barrier height via polarization switching. This work establishes stacking-engineered MoS2 as a platform for uncovering ferroelectric mechanisms and advancing ultrathin nonvolatile memory devices. © 2026

Title: Curvature-engineered dome-shaped TMD monolayers for tunable near-infrared photoluminescence
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Strain engineering has emerged as a powerful approach to modulate the electronic and optical properties of two-dimensional materials without altering their chemical composition. Among these materials, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted significant attention due to their strong light-matter interactions and highly tunable band structures. Various strain-induced morphologies, including domes, grooves, and roll-ups, have been widely explored to achieve localized carrier confinement and exciton modulation. In particular, dome-like geometries formed in nanopillar-based architectures provide a versatile platform for engineering strain distributions and position-dependent optical responses. However, the electronic and excitonic properties of dome structures with large height-to-radius ratios and flattened apex geometries remain poorly understood. To address this limitation, we investigate dome-shaped TMD monolayers using a geometry-controlled model based on a Woods-Saxon-type height profile. We show that curvature engineering induces a transition between distinct carrier confinement regimes, leading to strong modulation of electronic states and excitonic transitions. This enables continuous tuning of photoluminescence across the near-infrared (NIR) spectrum, extending into the long-wavelength NIR region that is difficult to access using conventional material or compositional approaches. Title: Inflow modeling strategies designed to enhance the ecological sustainability of hydroelectric reservoir operation planning
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid global expansion of water infrastructure alters major rivers, causes severe biodiversity declines, and destabilizes aquatic ecosystems. Amid intensifying eco-hydrological pressures, accurate prediction of reservoir inflow remains imperative to safeguard downstream aquatic ecosystems, yet data-sparse tropical environments chronically impair the generalizability of deep learning architectures due to pronounced overfitting. The study objectives were to evaluate three statistical inflow modeling frameworks, representative of design-era hydrological understanding, against the observed 1998–2023 flow regime to identify the most reliable forecasting approach for supporting environmental-flow-informed reservoir operation planning under monsoonal variability. METHODS: Using a multi-decadal hydro-meteorological dataset from 1998 to 2023 ( n = 312 monthly time steps) at Karian Reservoir in Banten Province, Indonesia, three primary modeling approaches were tested: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, Markov Chain, and Multiple Linear Regression. To rigorously assess model diagnostics and predictive performance across historical drought and wet regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient, Kling-Gupta efficiency, and operational trajectory metrics were integrated. FINDINGS: Deterministic multiple linear regression achieved the highest overall predictive accuracy with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.74, a Kling-Gupta efficiency of 0.64, and a superior operational trajectory guideline correlation of 0.85. The observed enhancement in model efficacy stems from the methodical integration of lagged streamflow predictors that effectively characterize catchment-scale moisture persistence. Conversely, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model exhibited the weakest diagnostic capability (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.62; Kling-Gupta efficiency = 0.60) due to systematic overestimation of dry-season baseflows, risking artificial inflation of safe water availability. Meanwhile, the stochastic Markov yielded a commensurate aggregate Kling-Gupta efficiency score of 0.66 and exhibited a superior proficiency in replicating long-term probability distributions. CONCLUSION: While Multiple Linear Regression shows the strongest performance for monthly operational scheduling, the Markov Chain model offers a complementary probabilistic framework for screening extended seasonal drought risk. Independent out-of-sample validation against a held-out 2019-2023 period revealed substantial performance degradation for both models (Multiple Linear Regression Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.61 to 0.02; Markov Chain Nash-sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.28 to -1.01), directly evidencing non-stationary rainfall-inflow relationships. Ultimately, these results establish that the evaluated models serve as an initial decision-support tool for raw water allocation planning, though their sustained operational reliability necessitates systematic recalibration. Title: Precipitation-assisted microstructural stabilization and twin-mediated strength-ductility synergy in EB-PBF TiAl alloys
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Inherent microstructural inhomogeneity and limited ductility remain major obstacles to achieving superior strength-ductility synergy in additively manufactured TiAl alloys. In this study, a TiAl-Si alloy was fabricated by electron beam powder bed fusion and tailored through a two-step heat treatment to control its microstructure and mechanical performance. The resulting alloy exhibits a hierarchical multiscale architecture. Atom probe tomography reveals that nanoscale Ti5Si3 precipitates partially dissolve while submicron particles are retained, stabilizing the lamellar structure through Zener pinning and diffusion inhibition, and effectively suppressing coarsening. Transmission electron microscope observations further identify three twin-twin interaction modes that activate defect-mediated mechanisms triggered by local stress concentrations, thereby accommodating strain and sustaining plastic flow. Consequently, the alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength of ∼1050 MPa and significantly enhanced elongation relative to the as-built state. This strength-ductility synergy arises from the decoupled yet complementary effects of precipitate-stabilized lamellae and twin-interaction-induced plasticity, establishing a mechanistic framework for designing additively manufactured TiAl alloys. © 2026

Title: Rational Design of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Electrocatalysis: Recent Advances and Mechanistic Insights

Abstract: This article describes a comprehensive analysis of the optimal evaporation method for an alkaline solution that is prepared using the aqueous extract of cotton stalk ash, along with the investigation of the chemical composition of the precipitation that appears during evaporation of the solution. In the presented research, the procedure for preparation of the alkaline solution was conducted under optimal conditions, when the mixture of ash and water with the weight ratio of 1:5 was boiled. Then, filtration and evaporation of the obtained suspension were performed. From the results obtained, the optimal evaporation regime was identified as 75%, as during this regime no precipitation occurs. Nevertheless, at an evaporation level of 80%, precipitation was observed in the solution due to the disturbance of the solubility equilibrium. The content of the precipitated components in relation to cations was estimated using flame photometry, and the phase composition was evaluated with FTIR spectroscopy. Thus, the precipitate was found to contain mainly carbonate-like compounds. It was proved that potassium ions prevailed in the solution, and their molar concentration is much greater than that of other cations. Moreover, when the concentration is high, a certain share of potassium ions is transferred from the solution into the precipitate phase. Title: ‘Rigid-flexible hybrid’ epoxy resin with superior curing performance, fire safety, and toughness
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The rapid advancement of aerospace, electronics, and electrical industries has imposed increasingly stringent requirements on the fire safety and mechanical properties of epoxy (EP) resins. However, traditional additive flame retardants suffer from low efficiency, and their excessive incorporation often leads to deterioration in the mechanical properties of EP. Therefore, the development of intrinsically flame-retardant EP has emerged as an important research direction. Herein, a flame-retardant co-curing agent, N-(2-(bis(2-aminoethyl)amino)ethyl)-P, P-diphenylphosphinic amide (BADP), was synthesized and introduced into the EP matrix to construct a ‘rigid-flexible hybrid’ crosslinking network. When the phosphorus content was only 0.6 wt.%, the resultant EP sample (EPBP4) achieved a vertical burning (UL-94) V-0 rating with a limiting oxygen index of 36.3%. Compared with pure EP, the peak heat release rate and total heat release of EPBP4 declined by 43.3% and 24.9%, respectively. These results demonstrate a significant enhancement in fire safety performance, which can be attributed to the char‑forming promotion effect of BADP. In addition, EPBP4 exhibited 113.0% and 34.7% improvements in impact strength and flexural strength, owing to the construction of a ‘rigid-flexible hybrid’ network. Overall, EPBP4 achieved an excellent balance between flame retardancy and mechanical properties, demonstrating strong potential for applications in electrical and electronic, aerospace, and other emerging advanced industries. © 2026

Title: High creep resistance in a dilute Mg-Al-Mn-Sm cast alloy at elevated temperature
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: This study achieved significant enhancement in creep resistance in a dilute Mg-Al-Mn-Sm alloy by forming a thermally stable eutectic network through optimizing the Al to Sm ratio. It was found that at 200 °C and 50 MPa, the steady-state creep rate of the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy was 1.10 × 10−9 s−1, nearly two orders of magnitude lower than that of the Sm-free alloy, and no fracture occurred after 500 h of creep testing. With the increase in Al content to 2.5%, despite the suppression of Mg17Al12 formation, the creep resistance deteriorated to 2.75 × 10−8 s−1. Microstructural observations showed that the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy contained a homogeneous distribution of Al2Sm-rich eutectic network throughout the matrix. They effectively pinned dislocations, suppressed twin growth and coalescence as a manifestation of enhanced microstructural stability, and reduced damage accumulation along grain boundaries during creep. In contrast, even with a higher alloy concentration, the fraction of eutectic particles was much lower. Solidification simulations revealed that a low Al/Sm ratio led to a wide Al2Sm formation window of approximately 84 °C and a final eutectic fraction of 7.5%, whereas a high Al/Sm ratio narrowed the window to approximately 20 °C and produced only discrete Al-Sm compounds with a final eutectic fraction of only 1.3%. Consequently, the effective creep driving force in the Mg-0.8Al-0.7Mn-0.9Sm alloy is only about 2% of that in the Mg-2.5Al-0.8Mn-0.9Sm alloy, leading to a much lower creep deformation. © 2026

Authors: Lu M.; Ding H.; Zhang H.; Xu J.; Meng R.; Li Y.; Zhang Z.; Zheng P.; Zhu Y.; Sun J.
Title: Strategies and applications for alleviating carbon catabolite repression
Abstract: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) is a widespread regulatory strategy across diverse microorganisms that prioritises the utilisation of preferred carbon sources. In industrial bioprocesses, however, CCR-mediated substrate hierarchy can delay the utilisation of secondary carbon sources in mixed feedstock, thereby extending fermentation time and limiting carbon conversion efficiency toward target products. Existing reviews have largely addressed CCR in a microorganism-specific manner, potentially obscuring conserved principles, limiting cross-species comparisons, and constraining generalisable engineering; computational modelling and engineering applications also remain underrepresented. This review therefore first summarises CCR mechanisms across diverse microorganisms through a common systems-level framework, in which transport-linked sensing converts carbon flux into intracellular signals, transcriptional regulators reprogramme genome-wide expression, RNA-based mechanisms fine-tune the timing and magnitude of responses, and protein stability shapes their persistence. Multi-omics approaches, particularly interactomics and single-cell omics, are then highlighted for revealing CCR as a dynamic and multilayered regulatory system by resolving interaction networks, temporal changes, and cell-to-cell heterogeneity beyond bulk measurements. Quantitative computational modelling is also discussed, with emphasis on kinetic and constraint-based frameworks that connect regulatory mechanisms to metabolic flux and predict system behaviour under changing carbon substrates. Engineering strategies, including adaptive laboratory evolution, transcription factor engineering, transporter and promoter engineering, and pathway rewiring, are further compared for the relief of CCR and improvement of substrate co-utilisation and production performance. Finally, these advances are presented within a Design-Build-Test-Learn framework, through which mechanistic discovery and omics-scale analysis are used to inform model development, and modelling and engineering are iteratively coupled to improve microbial performance. We propose that such an integrative paradigm is emerging as a unifying direction for CCR research, and provides a foundation for rational strain design and more efficient, sustainable biomanufacturing. © 2026 The Authors.
