Title: Marrying PDI with cyano-oxygen co-doped carbon nitride for efficient self-powered H2O2 photoelectrochemical cells

Abstract: A novel heterojunction photocatalyst is crafted by strategically marrying perylene diimide (PDI) with cyano-oxygen co-doped carbon nitride (COCN). This configuration demonstrates a 2.5-fold and 4.2-fold enhancement in power density over cells based on pristine PDI and graphitic carbon nitride, respectively. Moreover, the cell exhibits superior energy storage capability, retaining 58.9% of its specific capacitance after 12 h of operation in the dark. Title: Targeted Modulation of Zn Deposition Behavior toward High-Performance Stable Zn Anodes
Abstract: Dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions at the Zn metal anode remain critical obstacles to the commercialization of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Zn anode design regulates Zn deposition behavior from its thermodynamic and kinetic roots and is therefore recognized as a pivotal strategy to address the above bottlenecks. However, Zn deposition evolves through a complex multistage nucleation-growth process, and the structure–property relationship between the anode designs and practical Zn deposition behavior remains to be elucidated. This review focuses on Zn deposition substrate and functional interphase engineering, systematically elucidates the microscopic mechanisms and key regulatory targets of Zn deposition at each stage, and establishes a multidimensional regulation framework covering atomic tuning, interfacial modification, and spatial confinement. Based on this framework, we summarize three core design strategies, namely zincophilic regulation, lattice-matched effects, and three-dimensional structural engineering, and provide in-depth elucidation of the working mechanism and structure-property relationship of each strategy. By correlating these fundamental principles with the latest research advances in the field, we highlight the paradigm shift from empirical trial and error to rational material design. Finally, we outline the prevailing challenges and future research directions for Zn anode design, aiming to provide actionable insights for the development of advanced dendrite-free Zn anodes toward high-performance AZIBs. Title: Temperature-dependent interfacial degradation and premature oxide spallation of a Y-Hf co-doped AlCrFeNi multi-principal element alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The high-temperature oxidation resistance of multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) is influenced by the adhesion and stability of the oxide scale. In this study, the oxidation behavior and failure mechanism of the Y-Hf co-doped AlCrFeNi MPEA at 1100 and 1200 °C in static air are studied. After oxidation for 500 h at 1100 °C, a continuous, adherent α-Al2O3 scale consisting of inner columnar grains and outer equiaxed grains is formed. In contrast, severe spallation and interfacial rumpling are observed after oxidation for 50 h at 1200 °C, despite the formation of a similar α-Al2O3 scale. The premature spallation is attributed to the degradation of the oxide-scale/alloy interface. Accelerated Al consumption and phase-dependent Al/Ni mobility mismatch promote interfacial pore formation, reducing the effective contact area between the scale and substrate. The sulfur enrichment detected at the spalled interface suppresses pore healing and converts interfacial pores into effective decohesion sites. Furthermore, the reduced high-temperature strength of the alloy enhances oxide rumpling, facilitating stress localization and accelerating scale spallation. These results indicate that the beneficial Y-Hf reactive-element effect in stabilizing the oxide scale becomes insufficient at 1200 °C under severe interfacial degradation conditions, providing scientific guidance for developing MPEAs with enhanced oxidation resistance. © 2026

Title: CFD analysis of thermophysical characterization & performance optimization of a solar updraft tower utilising multi-composition gas mixtures
Abstract: The thermophysical behaviour of the solar working fluid plays an important role on the performance of the solar chimney. This work presents the results of a systematic Reynolds-averaged computational fluid dynamics (CFD) study, with turbulence closed by the shear-stress-transport (SST) k–ω model, of the buoyancy-driven flow in an axisymmetric solar chimney with six industrially relevant binary gas mixtures namely Air–CO, Air–CO2, CO–CO2, CO2–SO2, Air–SO2 and CO–SO2. Uniform wall heat flux of 1000 W/m2 is applied and mole fractions are taken between 0 and 1 with an interval of 0.1, and inlet temperatures are taken between 300K and 900K which results in a total of 462 simulations performed in ANSYS Fluent 2023 R1. The specific heat (Cp), density (ρ), thermal conductivity (k) and dynamic viscosity (μ) are obtained directly from the ANSYS Fluent property database and depend on the composition and temperature. Eight performance measures are reported: Pr, Nu, Re, Gr, Ra, draft pressure ΔP, mass flux G, and a conductivity-bias-corrected Thermal Performance Index TPI = Nu/Pr1/3. Two salient trends found in the data during analysis and retained unchanged in the results are worth noting: the non-physical decrease of Cp with inlet temperature for several pure-component points, and the molar-mass label anomaly in the CO2–SO2 sheet, which raises the value of Pr toward unity at 300 K. The highest centre-line velocity (60.1 m s−1 at 900 K) is reached for the air–CO mixtures while the SO2-rich mixtures produce up to 45 % higher ΔP at 300 K. This pressure gain is overcome at higher temperatures (≈650 K), where the effect of the greater temperature rise of Air–CO outweighs its lower density. The apparent Nu superiority of SO2 systems is shown to be a low-k normalisation artefact. The results are used for quantitative working fluid selection guidelines for industrial solar chimney, passive ventilation systems and flue gas stacks. © 2026 The Authors. Title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT

Abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Title: Kinetic modulation via trace cationic surfactant additive enabling dense Zn deposition for ultra-stable aqueous batteries
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Aqueous Zn metal batteries are promising for grid-scale energy storage but suffer from severe anode instability. METAC preferentially adsorbs on Zn via its quaternary ammonium center, forming a persistent protective layer that displaces water and suppresses corrosion. Title: Relaxation crossover under stress annealing governing non-monotonic coercivity evolution in Fe-based metallic glass
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: AI megasystems and 5G/6G technologies demand advanced soft magnetic materials for high-frequency, high-power-density conversion, for which Fe-based amorphous soft magnets are attractive owing to their low-coercivity potential. This potential can be fully realized only when rapid-quenching-induced frozen-in stresses are relieved, commonly by stress annealing. Yet how stress-coupled glassy relaxation modifies magnetic reversal remains unresolved. Here we address this issue using tensile stress relaxation in Fe82Si4B14 metallic-glass ribbons, where coercivity shows a non-monotonic time dependence that cannot be understood as simple stress relief. Time-resolved activation-energy analysis and strain recovery reveal a transition from reversible γ-like relaxation to cooperative β-related relaxation with irreversible strain accumulation. Magneto-optical Kerr imaging shows that this transition is accompanied by more uniform reversal at the coercivity minimum and renewed heterogeneous reversal after prolonged relaxation. Title: Fourier neural operators with least-squares readout refit for learning random obstacle-to-solution maps
Abstract: We study operator learning for random obstacle-to-solution maps arising from elliptic variational inequalities with finite-band self-affine random obstacle fields. Instead of introducing an explicit truncated stochastic parametrization of the random input, we learn the map directly from sampled obstacle realizations on a fixed grid. This problem is challenging because the solution is governed not only by the obstacle field itself, but also by the induced contact set and free-boundary geometry. We introduce a post-training least-squares readout refit for the Fourier neural operator (FNO). After the FNO is trained end-to-end, its nonlinear backbone is frozen and the final affine readout is recomputed by solving the induced linear least-squares problem over all training samples and grid points. We compare vanilla DeepONet, POD-DeepONet, a two-stage DeepONet baseline, FNO, and FNO with least-squares readout refit (FNO-LS) on two obstacle ensembles with different amplitude levels. Numerical results show that FNO-LS achieves the best average field accuracy and the strongest structure-sensitive performance among the tested models, particularly in the higher-amplitude regime. The least-squares refit further improves contact-set recovery and obstacle-violation metrics at low additional cost, especially when the FNO backbone is informative but not fully converged. Title: Polyvinyl alcohol/gelatin/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogels with improved mechanical strength and fatigue resistance for artificial heart valves
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hydrogels are promising materials for heart valve tissue engineering; however, their translation into medical devices remains limited by post-processing steps that can introduce defects and weaken mechanical performance. Title: Enhanced Antibiotics Sieving by Exfoliated TiS2 Membranes via Surface Functionalization and Passivation
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanolaminate membranes hold great promise for molecular sieving due to their two-dimensional capillary structures, which facilitate size-restricted diffusion. Title: Bioinspired Molecular Magnetic Field-Responsive Catalyst for On-Demand Switching of 2e− and 4e− Oxygen Reduction
Abstract: Achieving precise and on-demand steering of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) pathway between the efficient 4e− route to H2O and the valuable 2e− route to H2O2 remains a pivotal challenge in electrocatalysis. Herein, we address this challenge by designing a bioinspired molecular magnetic field-responsive catalyst (MMFR-C) via magnetic single-atom-anchored Salen-based covalent organic frameworks (MSA-Salen COFs) onto magnetic nanoparticles (single/multi-domain Fe3O4). Mimicking cytochrome c oxidase, the MMFR-C employs MSA-Salen COFs as an ordered proton-transfer channel and well-defined N2-M-O2 moieties as enzymatic O2 activation sites, with Fe3O4 providing a built-in magnetic field for remote regulation of the active-site electronic structure. The bioinspired MMFR-C exhibits switchable ORR pathways. Relative to the pristine Co-Salen COF (26% H2O2 selectivity, n = 3.48), the MMFR-C integrated with a single-domain Fe3O4 exhibits a remarkably enhanced H2O2 selectivity of 63.9% (n = 2.72), while that with a multi-domain Fe3O4 diverts the ORR pathway toward the 4e− route (n = 3.67). (i) We elucidate that the uniform magnetic field from the single-domain Fe3O4 in MMFR-C favors orbital hybridization between its active N2-M-O2 moieties and the *OOH intermediate, with moderate *OOH adsorption suppressing O–O scission and thus steering ORR selectivity toward H2O2. (ii) In contrast, the enhanced specific magnetism from its multi-domain Fe3O4 core optimizes the d-band center of MMFR-C’s active sites, stabilizes triplet O2 adsorption, and reduces spin-forbidden transition barriers, thereby facilitating O–O cleavage and diverting its ORR pathway to the 4e− route. Title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
Abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Title: Plasticized eutectic electrolytes for safe 4.7 V lithium-ion batteries
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Raising the charge cutoff voltage enhances the energy density of lithium-ion batteries but imposes stringent requirements on electrolyte stability and safety. Nonflammable eutectic electrolytes are promising candidates; however, strong hydrogen-bond (H-bond) networks and cation-solvent coordination often limit room-temperature ion transport and high-voltage interfacial stability. Although fluorinated ether additives can enhance ionic conductivity and oxidative stability, the underlying structure-property relationships remain unclear. Here, we investigate the effects of different fluorinated ether molecules in an amide-based eutectic electrolyte. Three solvation configurations are identified: non-bridging, micelle-like, and plasticized. Among them, the plasticized solvation structure provides the most effective regulation of both bulk transport and interfacial chemistry. Particularly, fluorinated ether molecules penetrate the H-bond network via multisite interactions, weakening intermolecular H-bonding and promoting cathode-electrolyte interfacial reconstruction. This behavior is analogous to plasticizers in polymer systems, which enhance segmental mobility by reducing intermolecular interactions. As a result, the plasticized eutectic electrolyte markedly improves rate capability and cycling stability in 4.7 V Graphite||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cells and enables the 1.6 Ah pouch cell to pass a nail penetration test without thermal runaway. Title: Temporal water-quality variability and its implications for environmental management of sand lobster aquaculture
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable management of sand lobster aquaculture is often limited by monitoring approaches that summarize environmental conditions using long-term averages, obscuring short-term extremes and spatial variation. The study objectives were to characterize spatial and temporal variations in water quality within a floating net cage aquaculture system, identify their underlying physical drivers, evaluate whether longitudinal growth is governed more by culture duration, initial size, and stocking density than by environmental exposure alone, and translate these empirical relationships into a transferable environmental monitoring framework. METHODS: The study collected longitudinal growth and environmental data from floating net cage culture in Indonesia. Monitoring covered temperature, salinity, oxygen concentration, potential of hydrogen, and nutrient concentrations across three water depths and multiple sampling times. Non-parametric statistical tests were employed to evaluate depth-dependent variations in dissolved oxygen, while correlation and regression analysis assessed the relationships between wind speed, water temperature, and dissolved oxygen levels. Multivariate statistical ordination summarized dominant environmental gradients, and mixed-effects statistical models, compared through an information-theoretic model selection approach, captured longitudinal growth. FINDINGS: Dissolved oxygen concentration differed significantly among depths (test statistic 29.27, probability below 0.001), declining by close to a fifth from the surface to three and ten meters. Monthly wind speed closely tracked the concurrent decline in temperature closely (correlation coefficient -0.988, probability below 0.002) but exhibited no statistically significant association with dissolved oxygen, consistent with a wind-driven transition observed during this production cycle. Culture duration, initial size class, and stocking density together explained total length best, with an additive model carrying more than seventy percent of the statistical weight among six candidate models. Growth rate exhibited its strongest association with low-oxygen exposure, followed by temperature and potential of hydrogen condition, an interpretation that warrants caution given the limited independent exposure intervals available. CONCLUSION: Successful sand lobster aquaculture requires an adaptive environmental monitoring architecture that accounts for depth-related oxygen stratification and wind-driven seasonal variability, alongside coordinated management of culture duration, initial seed size, and stocking density. Using single-crystalline non-polar SrTiO3 thin films as a model system, we spatially resolve vacancy-associated vertical transport at step edges using light-assisted conducting atomic force microscopy. At vacancy-enriched step edges, vertical transport is enhanced through a defect-mediated conduction mechanism distinct from direct tunneling. Our density functional theory calculations and diffusion-trapping modeling reveal that step edges are energetically favorable sites for oxygen vacancies, accounting for their accumulation during post-growth cooling. Title: Photonic Quantum Gates Using OAM and MPLC

Abstract: Quantum computing based on photonic platforms offers a promising route toward scalable quantum information processing due to its low decoherence and access to high-dimensional state spaces. A promising approach for realizing photonic quantum computation is to encode quantum information in the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) states of light, enabling the realization of high-dimensional quantum gates. Implementing such quantum gates requires programmable unitary transformations between selected computational basis states. The fabrication of integrated multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) structures could provide a pathway toward large-scale programmable quantum processors. In this work, we investigate the implementation of photonic NOT-gate transformations using OAM states and MPLC systems with a limited number of phase planes. Unlike conventional MPLC approaches that optimize phase masks for a fixed modal basis, the proposed framework treats the computational basis itself as the optimization variable. To identify suitable computational basis states, a photonic quantum-gate optimization algorithm was developed to systematically evaluate candidate LG mode pairs. The results show that conjugate-OAM mode pairs {LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p}^{-l}} and neighboring-radial mode pairs {LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p+1}^{l}} consistently achieve higher gate fidelity than structurally mismatched mode pairs under identical hardware constraints. Title: Bioinspired flexible materials with Lactuca indica leaf-mimicked structures for radar-infrared compatible stealth

Title: Carbon nitride enhanced with carbon dots in PDMS coatings: A synergistic approach for elevating corrosion resistance and photothermal self-healing activity

Title: Existence of variational solutions to the problem of contact of a beam with a DNC obstacle
Abstract: This work establishes the existence of weak solutions to a mathematical model for the vibrations of an Euler-Bernoulli beam that may come in contact with a reactive obstacle situated below it. Authors: Wang X.; Chen J.; Li X.; Xu J.; Zeng Q.
Title: Evaluating the safety impacts of three-dimensional alignments of mountainous freeways using an interpretable machine learning approach
Source title: International Journal of Transportation Science and Technology
Abstract: The safety of mountainous freeways remains a critical concern in road infrastructure planning, especially for routes characterized by intricate geometric alignments. The roadway is essentially a ribbon-shaped structure in three-dimensional (3D) space, and using 3D spatial parameters allows for a more accurate representation of its true geometric characteristics. However, quantifying the impact of 3D alignment features on crash occurrence remains challenging. To this end, this study investigates the nonlinear relationship between crash rate and 3D alignments using 4 neural network models: multilayer perceptron (MLP), Wide & Deep, residual network (ResNet), and graph neural network (GNN). The crash dataset was collected from two mountainous freeways in Guangdong Province, including crash records, traffic volumes, and road geometry over a 3-year period (2021–2023). According to model evaluation metrics, the Wide & Deep model achieved the best predictive performance. To enhance model interpretability, the SHapley additive exPlanations (SHAP) method and partial dependence plot (PDP) method were applied, enabling insights into the global importance of each feature and their interaction effects. SHAP results indicate that three geometric attributes, namely vertical curve length (VC_length), horizontal curve length (HC_length), and grade, have a significant influence on crash rate. Notably, 3D curvature-related features emerged as key predictors. As shown in the SHAP analysis, both excessively high and low curvature values, as well as a pronounced drop in curvature between consecutive segments, exhibit negative SHAP contributions, implying a mitigating influence on the predicted crash risk and underscoring the significance of curvature consistency. By contrast, torsion-related variables show limited impact. Additionally, key interaction effects were identified among several variable pairs, particularly between VC_length and HC_length, VC_length and back curvature difference, and HC_length and back curvature difference. These findings provide practical guidance for optimizing geometric design on mountainous freeways, supporting safer and more informed infrastructure planning. © 2026 Tongji University and Tongji University Press.

Title: Dislocation defects in 4H‑SiC crystals grown by physical vapor transport: Evolution, origins, and control strategies
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Silicon carbide (4H-SiC), a key wide-bandgap semiconductor material commonly grown by the physical vapor transport (PVT) method, holds great promise for high-power electronics, quantum photonics, and advanced optoelectronics. This review systematically outlines the evolution behavior and distribution characteristics of dislocations in PVT-grown 4H-SiC, and examines the underlying mechanisms driving dislocation multiplication across different growth stages. Key influencing factors-including seed crystal quality, source powder properties, growth interface morphology, and cooling protocols-are analyzed in detail. Effective strategies for suppressing dislocations, such as controlling carbon inclusions and eliminating edge polycrystals, are summarized. Title: Spatially encoded broadband all-optical thermoelectric synapses for in-sensor computing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: In-sensor computing integrates the separated sensing, memory, and computing functions of conventional artificial intelligence (AI) systems, enabling low-power and efficient intelligent systems. The excitatory and inhibitory behaviors of biological nervous systems can be emulated by a single Ag2Se device through the generation of continuously tunable spatially dependent positive and negative photo-thermoelectric responses. Under consecutive optical pulses, the device can exhibit typical short-term potentiation (STP) and inhibitory facilitation, demonstrating dynamic synaptic plasticity, with synaptic weight updates regulating the enhancement and attenuation of neural signal transmission. Title: Activation of the mineralized mass of Central Kyzylkum using acidic wastewater from the oil and fat industry: Freundlich-based adsorption kinetics for fluorine release; [Май-тоң май өнеркәсібінің қышқыл ағынды суларын пайдалана отырып Орталық Қызылқұмның минералданған массасын белсендіру: Фрейндлих моделіне негізделген фтордың бөлінуінің адсорбциялық кинетикасы]; [Активирование минерализованной массы Центрального Кызылкума с использованием кислых сточных вод масложировой промышленности: адсорбционная кинетика высвобождения фтора на основе модели Фрейндлиха]

Authors: Wang Z.; Tao W.; Sun S.
Title: Numerical Investigation of the Reverse Diffusion in Binary Hydrocarbon Systems at Equilibrium States
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: Molecular diffusion is a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature, where the diffusive flux typically aligns with the concentration gradient of species. However, this conventional relationship between diffusive flux and concentration gradient does not always hold, as seen in reverse diffusion, where the flux and concentration gradient are oriented in opposite directions. An important cause of reverse diffusion is the inverse relationship between species concentration and chemical potential, which can be attributed to the non-ideality of the species involved. This study investigates the conditions for reverse diffusion in binary hydrocarbon systems by calculating the derivatives of chemical potential with respect to molar concentration. The Peng-Robinson Equation of State (PR-EoS) is employed to describe the fluid thermodynamics. Additionally, the derivatives of chemical potential with respect to molar fraction, as well as the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Jacobian matrix of chemical potentials with respect to molar concentrations, are calculated. The complete results include binary normal alkane systems ranging from C1 to C10, and CO2-normal alkane systems at temperatures ranging from 200K to 600K, with molar concentrations between 0 and 20,000 mol/m3. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Ideal gases and ideal solutions exhibit no reverse diffusion theoretically; (2) Reverse diffusion is strongly temperaturedependent, with a higher likelihood at lower temperatures; (3) Binary mixtures with a near-zero molar concentration of one species are more prone to reverse diffusion than those where both species are present in appreciable molar concentrations; (4) The reverse diffusion phenomenon is most pronounced near phase interfaces. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: In situ observation and dynamic evolution of 9R structures enabled by Mg/Ag alloying for exceptional strength-conductivity synergy in a Cu alloy wire
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Achieving high strength while retaining high electrical conductivity remains a central challenge in precipitation-strengthened copper alloys. Here, a Cu-Ni-Co-Si-Mg-Ag alloy wire was developed through multi-step cold drawing and intermediate aging, and the strain-dependent role of localized 9R structures during plastic deformation was investigated. At a true strain of 3.79 after peak aging, the alloy exhibits an ultimate tensile strength of 1055 MPa, a yield strength of 955 MPa, an elongation of 5.9%, and an electrical conductivity of 48.2% IACS. Multiscale characterization and atomistic calculations reveal that Mg and Ag preferentially segregate at Cu/δ-(Ni, Co)2Si interfaces, thereby reducing interfacial energy and stacking fault energy, stabilizing nanoscale precipitates, and creating favorable conditions for localized 9R formation. Meanwhile, severe drawing develops a strong 〈111〉 fiber texture, which shifts the Schmid factor distribution toward lower values, thereby promoting localized partial-dislocation-mediated deformation. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction and in situ transmission electron microscope further reveal that the 9R structures are not only retained after cold drawing but also evolve dynamically during tensile deformation, with their local fraction initially increasing and subsequently decreasing before fracture. This dynamic evolution intensifies the interactions among 9R structures, precipitates, and dislocations, thereby enhancing dislocation storage and resistance to plastic flow. In parallel, solute depletion and limited electronic perturbation by Ag preserve the electrical conductivity. These findings establish a mechanistic link among Mg/Ag segregation, dynamic 9R evolution, hierarchical defect interactions, and the high strength-conductivity performance of highly drawn Cu alloy wires. © 2026

Title: Eliminating abnormal grain growth enabled by in-situ micro-alloying in friction stir welding of ultra-high Zn-containing Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys

Abstract: Abnormal grain growth (AGG) has long plagued Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys produced by friction stir welding (FSW), making them unsuitable for post-welding heat treatment. Title: Defect reconfiguration driven by transient vibration enables superior forging formability and cryogenic strength–ductility synergy in titanium
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hexagonal close-packed metals such as titanium (Ti) are widely regarded as promising materials for cryogenic applications, where concurrently achieving high strength and ductility is crucial for extreme-service reliability. Besides, the unique dislocation mechanism efficiently activated a high-density nanotwinned structure, facilitating the uniform distribution of dislocations. As a consequence, the nanotwinned Ti exhibited a high yield strength of 841 MPa and remarkable ductility of 24.1% at −183 °C after simple stress-relief annealing. This exceptional strength originates from the combined effect of nanotwin boundary strengthening and vibration-induced grain refinement. Further, the strain-hardening ability and ductility are improved by nanotwin-mediated heterogeneous deformation-induced stress, <c+a> dislocation activity, and secondary twinning. These findings reveal a novel deformation mechanism in Ti induced by transient vibration, offering a novel defect-level microstructural reconfiguration to design high-performance Ti and its alloys for cryogenic applications. © 2026

Title: Hierarchical polyimide-based composite with compatible radar/dynamic infrared stealth performance

Title: Role of deformation heterogeneity in the superplasticity of Ti6321 titanium alloy with a bimodal microstructure
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Superplastic forming offers a promising approach for producing critical ultra-thick titanium alloy components for marine applications. Near-α Ti6321 titanium alloy with a bimodal microstructure provides excellent mechanical performance and is therefore widely used in marine engineering. However, the influence of microstructural heterogeneity on its superplastic behavior and the underlying deformation mechanisms remains insufficiently understood. In this work, interrupted high-temperature tensile tests combined with systematic microstructural characterization were performed. The results reveal that deformation is accommodated by distinct yet coupled mechanisms in equiaxed α and lamellar α regions. In equiaxed α, plastic flow is predominantly governed by strong dynamic recovery and continuous dynamic recrystallization (DRX), with discontinuous DRX activated at intermediate strains. In contrast, lamellar α undergoes pronounced strain- and orientation-dependent dynamic globularization and more extensive DRX, particularly in Type II/III colonies. The co-activation of multiple slip variants gradually alters the local misorientation axes away from those established by preceding slip, thereby modifying local grain orientations through slip-induced lattice rotation and promoting increasingly dispersed slip activity. The synergistic interplay of heterogeneous slip and multiple DRX mechanisms promotes the transformation of hard-slip-dominated lamellar α into a fine-grained equiaxed microstructure. This microstructural homogenization facilitates multidirectional soft slip and grain boundary sliding, thereby underpinning the superior superplastic response of the alloy. © 2026

Title: A Mixed Finite Element Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Local Anisotropic Hybrid Meshes
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: We propose a mixed finite element method for solving second-order elliptic interface problems. The method is based on a fitted hybrid mesh, constructed by connecting the intersection points of the interface with an underlying unfitted triangulation. The resulting mesh consists of anisotropic triangles and quadrilaterals aligned with the interface. On this mesh, we define a pair of finite element spaces of type RT0–P0, designed to preserve the commutativity between the interpolation operator and the divergence operator. This structure ensures that the discrete inf-sup condition is satisfied without the need for additional stabilization. We establish optimal convergence rates in the L2-norm for both the velocity and pressure approximations. Title: Existence and necessary optimality conditions for nonlinear inverse problems governed by quasi-hemivariational inequalities with parameter-dependent constraints
Abstract: This paper investigates nonlinear inverse problems governed by a class of evolutionary quasi-hemivariational inequalities featuring constraints that depend simultaneously on parameters and unknowns. We begin by establishing the well-posedness of the parametric forward problem within the framework of evolution triples, providing existence, uniqueness, and a priori estimates for the state system. The associated inverse problem is subsequently formulated as a Tikhonov-regularized output-least-squares optimization problem, where the existence of at least one optimal parameter is proved utilizing the direct method of the calculus of variations. A primary analytical contribution of this work is the derivation of necessary optimality conditions in the presence of both nonsmoothness and state constraints with potentially empty interiors. To overcome these inherent challenges, we employ a rigorous double-approximation strategy combining smoothing and penalization techniques. This methodology leads to the derivation of an adjoint system and a first-order variational inequality associated with a singular Lagrange multiplier. Finally, to demonstrate the utility and applicability of our abstract theoretical framework, we apply our results to a nonlinear parabolic quasi-obstacle problem. Within this context, the abstract framework is verified in appropriate Sobolev spaces, and explicit optimality conditions are successfully derived. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: High-temperature degradation mechanisms of SiC whiskers reinforcement driven by thermo-mechanical coupling effects during sintering processes
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The sintering of SiC whiskers (SiCw)-reinforced ceramic matrix composites typically requires the combined application of high temperature and pressure to achieve densification. However, at elevated temperatures, the degradation of SiCw (i.e., a transition from rod-like to equiaxed morphology) prevents the anticipated reinforcing effect from being realized. How this thermo-mechanical coupling governs whisker degradation remains a critical gap in current understanding. To address this, this study investigates the degradation behaviors of SiCw under both pressure-assisted and pressureless conditions over a temperature range of 1700–1900 °C. The analysis covers SiCw as a reinforcement in two different ceramics: SiAlON (liquid-rich) and SiC (liquid-poor), along with a comparison of SiCw powders. The results demonstrate that the degradation of SiCw is primarily driven by the minimization of surface energy, proceeds in close conjunction with the annihilation of intrinsic stacking faults, and is significantly accelerated by the applied pressure and temperature. Under pressureless conditions, surface diffusion dominates mass transport, resulting in a bimodal microstructure consisting of residual rod-like whiskers and equiaxed grains. The application of pressure dramatically accelerates degradation kinetics by enhancing inter-whisker contact, inducing plastic deformation, and promoting grain-boundary diffusion, leading to complete conversion of SiCw into particles at 1800 °C. Further investigations using SiCw/SiC and SiCw/α-SiAlON composite systems revealed that the pressure-induced accelerating effect of whisker degradation is significantly suppressed in a liquid-rich sintering environment. This study provides a direct theoretical basis for tailoring the microstructure and optimizing the sintering process of SiCw-reinforced composites. © 2026

Title: Feedback-Free Photonic Reservoir Computing via Time-Concatenated Dimensional Expansion and Hybrid Pruning
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) offers an efficient framework for temporal processing by combining nonlinear mapping with short-term memory. However, conventional implementations are often hindered by the high hardware costs of spatial arrays or the speed and integration bottlenecks associated with feedback delay lines and input masking in time-delayed RC. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a single-node photonic reservoir computing system without physical delay lines and input masking operations. To enhance the representational capability of the single-node system, we introduce a time-concatenated dimensional expansion technique to construct a high-dimensional state space. Furthermore, a hybrid pruning strategy is employed to quantitatively optimize the trade-off between computational resources and forecasting performance. Our results demonstrate a feedback-free photonic reservoir computing framework that combines physical photonic feature generation with digital state construction and optimization for temporal processing tasks with diverse dynamical characteristics.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: Amino-vacancy dual-site engineering in Ru-incorporated nickel hydroxide for ampere-level alkaline hydrogen evolution
Abstract: The sluggish Volmer step of the Ru-based catalysts remains a persistent major kinetic bottleneck for ampere-level alkaline water electrolysis. To mitigate this limitation, we developed a strategy to regulate both the local electronic structure and the interfacial water microenvironment. A self-supported Ru-incorporated Fe-doped nickel hydroxide skeleton was successfully grown on the nickel foam substrate. NRNFOH/NF delivers 1000 mA cm−2 at an iR-corrected overpotential of 124 mV in 1.0 M KOH, maintaining outstanding catalytic stability for 500 h. Title: Heterointerface-grain boundary defect engineering enables high-performance and mechanically robust Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric nanocomposites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The simultaneous optimization of thermoelectric (TE) performance, mechanical robustness, and device-level applicability remains a long-standing challenge for the practical deployment of Bi2Te3-based TE materials in power generation and solid-state cooling. Herein, we report a high-performance TE nanocomposite, Bi0.3Sb1.7Te2.99S0.01 + 0.7 wt.% ZrO2, which concurrently exhibits enhanced TE properties and mechanical strength, enabling reliable device fabrication. By integrating heterogeneous interface engineering with deliberately constructed grain-boundary defect architectures—including twin boundaries, staggered lamellae, and antisite defect layers—a cooperative regulation of charge and phonon transport is achieved across multiple length scales. This defect-mediated transport modulation markedly enhances the Seebeck coefficient and power factor, while suppressing both electronic and lattice thermal conductivities, thereby effectively mitigating the intrinsic trade-off between TE efficiency and mechanical integrity. Consequently, the optimized nanocomposite delivers a peak zTmax of ∼1.46 at 350 K and an average zTave of ∼1.23 over 300–500 K, in addition to a Vickers hardness of 1.17 GPa and a compressive strength of 218 MPa. Importantly, a seven-pair TE device achieved a maximum conversion efficiency of ∼6.8% at a temperature difference of 200 K and a maximum cooling temperature difference of ∼63.4 K at 300 K. This study demonstrates that heterointerface–grain boundary defect engineering provides an effective and scalable strategy to simultaneously advance TE performance, mechanical reliability, and device-level functionality in Bi2Te3-based TE nanocomposites. © 2026

Title: Nonlinear Vibration Analysis of Fractional Viscoelastic Timoshenko Nanobeams Considering Nonlocal and Surface Effects
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This study proposes a non-classical Timoshenko beam model that incorporates von-Kármán geometric nonlinearity and a fractional Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic model, based on nonlocal strain gradient theory and surface elasticity theory. The model captures the effects of microstructure, surface energy, and nonlocality, with governing equations and boundary conditions derived using Hamilton’s principle to describe fractional viscoelastic nanobeams under transverse harmonic excitation. The Galerkin method and a predictor-corrector algorithm solve the resulting fractionalorder equations, revealing how key parameters influence nonlinear free and forced vibrations. Numerical simulations reveal that fractional order significantly modifies the nonlinear vibration characteristics of structures and enhances damping as the fractional order increases. Furthermore, due to the correlation between fractional order and excitation frequency, the effects of fractional order on nonlinear time responses differ between free and forced vibrations. These findings highlight the crucial role of fractional viscoelasticity in influencing the dynamic behavior of nanostructures, providing valuable insights for the design of advanced nanoscale systems. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Surfactant-Derived Nitrogen-Bridged MoS2/C Heterostructures for Robust Lithium-Ion Storage
Abstract: Structural stability, ionic transport, and electronic conductivity are the major challenges of layered transition-metal dichalcogenide/carbon nanocomposites (LTMD/C) for lithium-ion storage. As an anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), the optimized MoS2–N–C700 electrode delivers remarkable cycling stability (~ 100% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 0.5 A g−1) and excellent rate capability. Moreover, lithium-ion supercapacitors (LISCs) based on the as-prepared MoS2–N–C composite achieve an ultrahigh power density of 3500 W kg−1, and excellent cycling stability over 10,000 cycles. The cycling performance in both LIBs and LISCs surpasses that of most previously reported MoS2/C nanocomposites and conventional carbon-based anodes. Title: High-entropy ferrite with ultrafine heterostructured nanoclusters for broadband and intelligent switchable microwave absorption
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-entropy (HE) ferrites with multi-element substitution emerge as promising candidates for microwave absorption (MA) due to their adjustable structure and unique HE effects. However, the effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) and the absorption strength of conventional kinetically random-mixing single-phase HE ferrites are limited. Herein, we report the synthesis of HE ferrite with the formation of ultrafine nanoclusters within the matrix anchored on carbon aerogel (CA) through rapid microwave heating. Benefiting from the binary formation energy differences among the constituent elements (Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn, Ce, O), CeO2 nanoclusters are formed within the HE ferrite matrix. The CeO2/HE ferrite-decorated CA (CH/CA) exhibits polarization-enhanced electromagnetic attenuation, which substantially widens the EAB. At 4.0 mm thickness, CH/CA achieves a minimum reflection loss of −69.14 dB at 5.21 GHz, with EAB covering 92.9% of C-band. Notably, the EAB reaches 8.94 GHz at a thickness of 2.5 mm, covering 89.4% of the combined X- and Ku-bands. The integrated EAB of CH/CA at a thickness ranging from 1.5 to 5.0 mm reaches 14.82 GHz, which is comparable to the reported highest values. Furthermore, the CH/CA exhibits compressive strain-driven intelligent on/off switchable and frequency-tunable MA performance. This work proposes a phase-separated HE composite for broadband and smart MA applications. © 2026

Title: Prediction of shale brittleness index by genetic algorithm optimization random forest algorithm
Abstract: The brittleness index (BI) is a key parameter for determining whether shale is compressible. Accurately predicting BI during CO2 storage is beneficial for evaluating shale's reservoir and cap rock properties and selecting favorable CO2 geological reservoirs. This study uses six logging parameters, including acoustic log (AC), gamma ray log (GR), density log (DEN), neutron porosity (CNL), array induction resistivity (AT120), and potassium log (K), as input variables to develop a traditional multiple linear regressionmodel and four machine learning models for predicting BI. The machine learning models include backpropagation neural network (BP), random forest (RF), genetic algorithm optimized backpropagation neural network (GA-BP), and genetic algorithm optimized random forest (GA-RF). The interpretability of the model is analyzed with Shapley Additive explanations (SHAP). The results indicate that: (1) The coefficient of determination (R2) of the multiple linear regression model is 0.78. For the machine learning models, the R2 values between predicted and ture value are 0.83 (BP), 0.9336 (RF), 0.84 (GA-BP), and 0.96 (GA-RF). The GA-RF model exhibits the highest accuracy. In cross-basin validation, the GA-RF model achieves an R2 of 0.84. (2) In the GA-RF model, the parameter contributions in the importance voting are ranked in descending order as AC > K > CNL > AT120 > GR > DEN. The results indicate that mechanical and petrophysical properties, especially formation hardness, density, and shale-related indicators, are strongly correlated with BI, highlighting their key role in its prediction. (3) The SHAP analysis of the GA-RF model reveals that AC, K, CNL, and GR are strongly negatively correlated with their SHAP values, while AT120 exhibits a weak positive correlation. In contrast, DEN shows SHAP values concentrated around zero with limited variation. The SHAP results are consistent with the feature importance ranking. Accurate prediction of shale BI not only facilitates the identification of optimal fracturing pathways and development sweet spots, but also provides an important theoretical basis for CO2 sequestration site selection. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Bioinspired photothermal self-healing anti-fouling coating with continuously enhanced slipperiness through dynamic release of lubricant and antibacterial filler

Abstract: Marine bio-fouling severely threatens the safety and efficiency of marine equipment. Slippery liquid-infused porous surface (SLIPS) is a promising approach for solving bio-fouling. However, poor durability limits its application due to the loss of the lubricant. In addition, it was verified that there are three types of hydrogen bonds in polyurethane chain through experimental characterization and theoretical calculation, thereby enabling the coating with rapid photothermal self-healing performance (397 s). The degradable coating achieves continuously release of filler and BS, endowing the coating with enhanced slippery surface and antibacterial performance during degradation. The antibacterial rate of the coating after 120 days of degradation remained as high as 93.9% against Escherichia coli. Meanwhile, the coating exhibited an extremely low coverage of algae (0.165%). Title: Advancing urban solar integration: Performance and policy analysis of BIPV systems in India
Abstract: Sustainable urban energy generation is an attractive goal with a growing solution: building integrated photovoltaic system. By combining the functions of a building envelope with those of a photovoltaic system in a single construction, building integrated photovoltaic systems simultaneously serve as a building component and an energy generation system. India has a high potential for building integrated photovoltaic applications in massive scales due to the extensive urbanization and ambitious targets set by the Indian government for renewable energy. The novelty of this study is that it has an analytical framework is India-specific, and merges the aspects of architectural design, technical performance, operational challenges, policy analysis, and comparative evaluation of real-world case studies of building integrated photovoltaic systems. Title: High-Spatiotemporal and Multimodal Soft Tactile Interface with Layered Architecture for Simultaneous Structural and Thermal Perception
Abstract: Advanced robotic systems require tactile perception to interact reliably with objects in environments where visual information is limited by occlusion, illumination variations, and focusing issues. However, conventional tactile sensors are limited to single-stimulus recognition and face fundamental challenges in scalability and functionality, as miniaturizing sensor pixels reduces baseline signal levels and degrades the SNR. This study presents a high-spatiotemporal and multimodal soft tactile interface for simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles, fabricated through a layered architecture enabled by additive manufacturing. The proposed interface incorporates a 3D-stacked capacitive pressure sensor that combines buried interdigitated capacitors and a parallel-plate capacitor, and a reduced graphene oxide based temperature sensor within the same pixel area. The 3D-stacked electrode architecture enhances baseline capacitance within a miniaturized pixel footprint, and a via-free, interlayered interconnection scheme resolves wiring complexity in the temperature sensor array. Each sensing layer operates through independent transduction mechanisms, enabling the simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles with minimal cross-interference. The fabricated multimodal array can spatially resolve both contact geometry and localized thermal distributions with high-spatiotemporal resolution. Furthermore, by applying a tactile scanning strategy in robotic perception, the platform successfully identifies geometric features and surface thermal profiles of target objects even under vision-limited conditions. This study provides a scalable and robust foundation for multimodal tactile perception in advanced robotic manipulation and human–robot interaction. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A base-editing and auxotrophic selection platform for linking epigenetic regulators to silent biosynthetic gene clusters in Aspergillus nidulans

Title: Atomic engineering of stability-kinetics Ce-Fe dyads in Ni3S2 for efficient urea-assisted hydrogen production
Abstract: Replacing the energy-intensive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) presents a promising route for energy-saving hydrogen production coupled with wastewater remediation. However, developing electrocatalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we propose and validate a novel “kinetic-structural synergy” design principle by constructing atomic-scale Ce-Fe binary catalytic unit within Ni3S2 nanoarrays. Unlike random doping, this defined architecture enables a functional division of labor. The Fe site acts as a kinetic promoter to dramatically lower the potential for active NiOOH phase formation, while the adjacent Ce site functions as a structural and electronic stabilizer, securing the high-valent Ni intermediates. The resulting catalyst achieves an ultra-low UOR potential. When configured in a two-electrode urea electrolyzer, it requires only 1.37 V to deliver 100 mA·cm−2 current density and maintains remarkable stability for over 510 h. Title: Micropore confinement engineering of porous carbon for efficient two-electron oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide
Abstract: Two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR) for H2O2 synthesis offers a sustainable alternative to the traditional anthraquinone process. The structure-activity relationship between PC and ORR performance demonstrates that the micropore volume is positively correlated with the ORR onset potential. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the mean square displacement (MSD) of reactant molecules decreases with decreasing channel size, verifying the confinement effect of micropores. Abstract: Against the backdrop of depleted rich deposits and the increasing proportion of refractory gold-bearing ores, improving their processing methods has become an urgent task. This work presents the results of a comprehensive study of gold-bearing ores from the Pakrut deposit, located in Central Tajikistan's Zeravshan–Gissar zone. Mineralogical analysis established that the principal gold carriers are pyrite and arsenopyrite, with the metal predominantly localized as fine inclusions and fracture-related accumulations. A notable fraction of gold occurs as free particles (17.03%); however, the dominant share is fracture-bound (62.41%) and is predominantly associated with arsenopyrite. This distribution explains the limited efficiency of single-stage treatment and substantiates the need for combined unlocking and recovery routes. Physicochemical studies confirmed the ores' refractory nature, attributed to the fine dissemination of gold within the sulfide matrix, combined with high hardness and abrasiveness. At the laboratory scale, various beneficiation flowsheets were tested, including direct cyanidation; flotation combined with additional leaching of tailings; and variants incorporating gravity separation. Title: Characterization of two key cytochrome P450 enzymes in Isodon amethystoides and de novo production of 3α,15β-dihydroxy-ent-kaurene in yeast
Abstract: Glaucocalyxin A (GLA), a well-known ent- kaurene diterpenoid, has emerged as a high-value bioactive natural product in pharmaceutical research owing to its potent and broad-spectrum activities. Herein, we identified two enzymes, IamCYP71D761 and IamCYP706V18, in Isodon amethystoides , which specifically mediate the C3α- and C15β-hydroxylation of ent- kaurene with high stereoselectivity and regioselectivity, respectively, generating 3α,15β-dihydroxy- ent- kaurene ( 3 ), a key precursor in the biosynthesis of GLA. In addition, we established an efficient de novo biosynthesis platform for 3 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Briefly, high-efficiency isozyme screening, protein engineering, increased acetyl-CoA synthesis, and copy number enhancement were applied to the ent- kaurene biosynthesis module. Subsequently, promoter optimization, competitive pathway knockout, and electron transfer optimization were introduced, resulting in production of 3 to 24.0 ± 0.2 mg/L in shake flask. In summary, this work highlights the pivotal roles of IamCYP71D761 and IamCYP706V18 in the heterologous biosynthesis of 3 , offering valuable insights for the further pathway reconstruction and de novo production of GLA, GLB, and other ent- kaurene diterpenoids. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Plasmonic heterojunction on dental implant abutments for enhanced antibacterial activity and soft tissue integration
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Peri-implantitis, a leading cause of dental implant failure, is characterized by bacterial infection, immune dysregulation and inadequate soft tissue integration. To address those challenges, this study proposes a novel plasmonic heterojunction coating on titanium-based abutments. The introduction of tungsten doping and lattice defects significantly increases the free electron density, thereby inducing a strong LSPR effect in the titanium oxide matrix within the near-infrared region. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, the coating demonstrates good antibacterial activity through a dual-mode mechanism: it generates energetic “hot holes” that participate in the “electron hijacking” process, which disrupts bacterial energy metabolism and redox balance; concurrently, the non-radiative relaxation of surface plasmons produces a controlled and mild photothermal effect, which induces bacterial thermal stress and increases bacterial membrane permeability. In vivo experiments in rats and beagle dogs confirm its good antibacterial activity and biocompatibility, as well as its therapeutic potential in treating peri-implantitis. This work presents a promising potential of plasmonic heterojunction coatings in developing next-generation smart, multifunctional implants to improve long-term clinical success. © 2026

Title: Superior interface thermal conductance via chemical bonding between diamond and carbon nanotubes
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Facing growing thermal challenges in electronics, diamond/carbon nanotube (CNT) composites offer a breakthrough heat-dissipation solution, yet the phonon transport across covalently bonded diamond/CNT interfaces remains poorly understood at the atomic scale. Based on our experimental synthesis results, we build the interfacial bonding structure model of the diamond/CNT composite materials for the first time and demonstrate the effects of covalent bonding and atomic interfacial structure on interfacial thermal conductance (ITC). The interfacial chemical bonding can significantly enhance ITC (by 4 to 73 times compared to unbonded interfaces, depending on the temperature and the number of bonds per unit diameter), with the most pronounced enhancement observed at 700 K. Increasing the number of bonds further improves ITC by exciting more delocalized phonons to participate in transport. Structural analysis reveals that the combination of diamond with the (111) crystal plane and zigzag CNTs yields the optimal thermal conductance, while phonon analysis shows that delocalized phonons in CNTs contribute more prominently to thermal transport. We design several diamond/CNT array structures, including aligned and crossed arrangements, and achieve ITC on the order of ∼100 GW/(m2 K), which is the highest value reported in the literature. Title: Experimental comparison of dual-stage organic Rankine cycle and organic Rankine flash cycle for low-temperature geothermal power generation
Abstract: Organic Rankine cycle (ORC) has gained increasing attention in thermal power generation, but with a relatively low efficiency due to the irreversible loss of the evaporation process. Title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
Abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Mathematical Model of the Dynamics of the Armament of the Tricone Drill Bit; [Үш қашау тісті бұрғыларды жабдықтау динамикасының математикалық моделі]; [Математическая модель динамики вооружения трехшариковых долот]
Abstract: This study presents a mathematical model of the dynamics of tricone drill bits, which remain widely used in open-pit mining due to their reliability and versatility. Despite their extensive application, improving their efficiency and durability remains a relevant issue. The main operational challenges are identified, including insufficient knowledge of the stress–strain state of rocks in the contact zone and the effect of tooth geometry on kinematics and rock-breaking efficiency. Analytical dependencies are proposed to account for bit geometry, trajectory motion, transmission ratios, and tooth–rock interaction. Based on the principles of theoretical mechanics, performance criteria are formulated through specific contact and volumetric work of rock destruction, enabling an objective assessment of energy consumption. The model demonstrates the potential of analytical methods for optimizing drill bit design and kinematics, reducing energy consumption, increasing productivity, and extending tool life. The results can be applied in the design of next-generation drill bits and in engineering software for selecting rational drilling parameters under specific geological conditions. The proposed approach provides a foundation for further studies in mathematical modeling of rock destruction dynamics and the advancement of open-pit mining technologies. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: Innovative technologies for paraffin deposit removal in oil tubing to enhance oil recovery: a mechanical approach; [Мұнай өндіруді арттыру үшін мұнай құбырларын парафиндік шөгінділерден тазалаудың инновациялық технологиялары: механикалық әдіс]; [Инновационные технологии очистки нефтяных труб от парафиновых отложений для повышения нефтеотдачи: механический подход]
Abstract: Asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposits (ARPD) on the inner wall of production tubing shorten service intervals, elevate operating expenditures, and frequently induce downtime at mature fields. This paper presents the design and field performance of a rod-driven in-well scraper that provides continuous tubing cleaning during routine sucker-rod operation without chemical dosing or surface interventions. The scraper sub is inserted into the rod string and is compatible with Ø73-89 mm tubing and Ø19-22 mm rods. Performance was evaluated on a before/after basis using the inter-cleaning period (ICP), downtime, and annual cleaning costs, with extrapolation to multi-well programs. Field deployments of model CP TP ST 01KZ achieved an ICP of 144-280 days with zero cleaning-induced downtime (0 days yr⁻¹). Annual cleaning costs were ~0.265 million KZT per well (scheduled service only), which is ≈31× lower than hot-wash budgets on the same asset. The implied per-well saving is ≈7.94 million KZT yr⁻¹; for a 50-well program, this corresponds to ≥397 million KZT yr⁻¹ in avoided expenditure. Continuous in-well action of the reciprocating toothed head on each rod stroke disrupts the boundary wax layer and limits deposit regrowth between services, eliminating periodic thermal/chemical treatments and their logistics. The subassembly mass (≈30 kg) permits installation with standard handling; the pump string configuration is unchanged apart from the insertion of the scraper section. Compared with thermal, chemical, and batch mechanical methods, the technology extends service intervals, removes cleaning-related shut-ins, and compresses the cleaning budget to a predictable, low annual service cost. The results support routine use of rod-driven scraping for ARPD control in wax-prone wells and provide quantitative guidance for field-scale rollout and further optimization (wear resistance, centralization tolerances, and application in deviated completions). © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Authors: Lu J.; Hou L.; Xu X.; Su B.; Lin X.; Lu X.F.; Liu K.; Lan Z.-A.; Wang S.
Title: Interfacial charge redistribution in Au/TiN Schottky photocatalysts enabling efficient full-spectrum CO2 reduction with H2O
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction using H2O as the electron donor is limited by rapid charge-carrier recombination and insufficient CO2 adsorption and activation, resulting in low solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency. Herein, we demonstrate that Schottky interface engineering upon metallic photocatalysts offers an effective strategy to optimize charge-carrier dynamics and surface reaction kinetics concurrently. Au nanoparticle-decorated TiN (Au/TiN) photocatalysts were fabricated via a facile impregnation-reduction method, in which uniformly dispersed Au nanoparticles are anchored onto metallic TiN to construct well-defined Schottky heterointerfaces. Spectroscopic studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal spontaneous interfacial charge redistribution driven by the Fermi-level mismatch between Au and TiN, rendering the formation of a built-in electric field that promotes directional electron transfer from TiN to Au. Consequently, the Au-TiN Schottky junction effectively suppresses charge-carrier recombination and accelerates interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, the deposited Au nanoparticles also serve as active centers for CO2 adsorption and activation, facilitating the reduction reaction. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the optimized Au/TiN photocatalyst affords CO and H2 evolution rates of 23.04 and 27.69 μmol g−1 h−1, respectively, with the CO production rate being nearly three times that of pristine TiN. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy identifies a *COOH-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer pathway for CO2-to-CO conversion. This work establishes Schottky interface engineering as an effective approach for metallic photocatalysts to regulate charge-transfer behavior and catalytic reaction pathways, providing a reliable strategy for efficient solar-to-fuel conversion. © 2026

Title: Polar-Twisted Electron-Transport Layer Simultaneously Breaks Efficiency-Flexibility-Cost Limits in Organic Solar Cells
Abstract: Perylene diimide (PDI)-based electron-transport layers (ETLs) are fundamental in governing charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and the operational longevity of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet their molecular design still lacks transferable principles. Here we present a PDI-ETL molecular design framework that couples bay-position engineering with polar, bulky side-chain modulation to improve additive-free alcohol solubility, suppress over-crystallization, and mitigate oxidative degradation. With this framework, H75-DMA suppresses reactive-oxygen-driven chemical evolution and interfacial trap accumulation, thereby stabilizing interfacial energetics and electron transport. Binary OSCs based on H75-DMA achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) above 20% and exhibit improved mechanical toughness and bending durability in flexible devices. Its smooth, high-surface-energy interface also induces continuous growth of ultrathin metal cathodes, leading to increased light-utilization efficiency in flexible semitransparent OSCs. In addition, H75-DMA enables cathode substitution from Ag to Cu while retaining about 97% of the PCE of the Ag-based devices, thereby improving cost-effectiveness at the device level. Title: Heterogeneity, petro-fabric and petrophysical subdivision of the El Garia Formation (Ypresian, Tunisia): Implications for CO2 storage
Abstract: Assessing and evaluating each reservoir suitability for carbon dioxide storage (CCS) prior to injection is crucial to ensure safe and long-term geologic carbon storage. Rock physics is a key technique in determining the CO2 storage potential of rock formations. Each assessment should start by understanding the microstructural heterogeneity of each reservoir. Microstructural and petrophysical studies of El Garia nummulitic limestone reservoir were carried out in order to: a) understand the heterogeneity of this complex reservoir and b) subdivide this formation into petrophysical levels in order to define the suitable levels for CO2 storage and c) define factors controlling the heterogeneity of microstructural and petrophysical properties and determine its interrelation as a neecessary step to assess suitability of the formation to host CO2. Microstructural observations, made on 24 thin sections under optical and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), identifies seven deposit facies. Porosity has been measured on seven samples by the triple weight method and estimated from the optical microscopy and SEM observations using JMicrovision software. After microstructural and reservoir characterization studies focusing on sedimentology, diagenesis, types of cement and porosity values and types, a petro-fabric zonation of El Garia reservoir was carried out identifying around four distinct levels based on these cited parameters. In the light of these results, a rock physics study was established. Electrical conductivity, P wave velocities, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility have been measured in five samples corresponding to these different levels of El Garia reservoir in order to delves into the microstructural and petrophysical subdivision, to determine the factor controlling the formation heterogeneity and its interrelation. Four parameters have been determined when studying the electrical conductivity (surface conductivity, formation factor, tortuosity and cementation exponent). Petrographical characteristics and petrophysical properties of the sample plugs indicate a correlation between these parameters, showing a microstructural and petrophysical heterogeneity of this reservoir. The results obtained for these electrical parameters show heterogeneity in the pore connectivity and in the arrangement of mineral crystals, particles and pores from one facies to another. The acoustic measurement results show that the vertical evolution of the acoustic velocity varies as a function of the diagenetic evolution and the internal microstructure of each facies of the El Garia Formation. The anisotropy study allows the definition of four acoustic fabric levels into the formation. © 2026 The Authors. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Ltd. Title: Synergistic surface modification of β titanium alloy by friction stir processing and compressed plasma flow for enhanced osteogenesis and antibacterial performance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: To address the key technical challenges of insufficient bioactivity and poor coating adhesion on the surface of β-titanium alloy biomedical implants, this study employed a synergistic modification technology combining friction stir processing (FSP) and compressed plasma flow (CPF) to prepare a composite functional structure containing ZnO nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs). Utilizing the severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization effects generated during the FSP process, the alloy surface exhibits a fine-grained structure with reduced elastic modulus. The cross-section reveals a gradient grain structure, significantly improving the mechanical compatibility between the implant and bone tissue. Subsequent CPF treatment promotes the uniform dispersion of ZnO-NPs, which is associated with the formation of TiN phases. This treatment further optimized the surface morphology, creating a rough interface at the micron scale and a smooth interface at the nanoscale. In vitro experimental results demonstrate that these improvements significantly enhanced cell adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation, while also improving antibacterial properties by reducing bacterial adhesion and disrupting bacterial cell membranes. In vivo experimental results indicate that the implant significantly promoted the growth of bone tissue. The synergistic effect of FSP and CPF technologies provides an innovative strategy for the surface modification of biomedical titanium alloys. © 2026

Title: miRNA-mRNA multi-omics integration in breast cancer staging
Source title: Advances in Biomarker Sciences and Technology
Abstract: The tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) anatomic system is the current clinical standard for breast cancer staging, yet it inadequately captures the molecular heterogeneity that drives disease progression, motivating the development of expression-based biomarker classifiers. We integrated microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression profiles from 1081 primary TCGA-BRCA tumors (early-stage, Stages I–II, n = 822; late-stage, Stages III–IV, n = 259) and benchmarked nine machine learning algorithms using a stratified 70/15/15 train–validation–test split with class-imbalance weighting. On the held-out test set, XGBoost, selected after Bayesian hyperparameter optimization on the validation set, achieved AUC = 0.687 (95% CI: 0.622–0.748), accuracy = 79.8%, and good model calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.31), significantly outperforming mRNA-only (AUC = 0.654; p = 0.028) and miRNA-only (AUC = 0.612; p = 0.007) models. Differential expression analysis identified 15 significant miRNAs and 194 significant mRNAs (FDR <0.05), and regulatory network analysis revealed three co-expression modules governing epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metabolic reprogramming, and immune evasion, with 15 hub miRNAs regulating 97–516 predicted targets. Multi-omics integration captures progression-associated molecular signatures beyond anatomic staging and could, pending external validation, complement conventional TNM staging by providing a molecularly informed risk-stratification layer; the framework provides a reproducible basis for exploratory translational biomarker discovery. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Tehrani M.; Shahgholian-Ghahfarokhi G.H.
Title: Sustainable Dyeing of Cotton Fabrics with Papaver Rhoeas-Derived Anthocyanins: Impact of Mordant and Acid Types
Abstract: T his study explored the eco-friendly application of natural dyes extracted from Papaver rhoeas petals for cotton fabric coloration. Due to growing environmental concerns, natural dyes are being considered as alternatives to synthetic dyes; however, they often suffer from low color strength and poor fastness. To overcome these challenges, this study examined how different mordanting methods, including pre-, meta-, and post-mordanting, a range of metallic and plant-based mordants, and various acid types influence dyeing performance. The petals of Papaver rhoeas contain anthocyanins, especially cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, which provide bright red to purple shades. The results showed that the mordanting method, acid type, and mordant type significantly affected color strength, shade, and fastness properties. Among the tested acids, citric and oxalic acids provided the most favorable dyeing performance, while meta-mordanting was the most effective method overall. Furthermore, natural mordants such as pomegranate rind, oak bark, and Juglans regia performed as well as or better than traditional metal mordants such as tin and iron. Pomegranate rind produced the highest color strength, while these bio-mordants improved color depth and durability. Overall, the study demonstrates that when appropriate mordanting methods, mordant types, and acid types are selected, Papaver rhoeas can be used as an effective and sustainable natural dye for cotton fabrics. © Institute for Color Science and Technology.

Title: Predicting Copper Production Cycles in Hydrometallurgy with Interpretable Machine Learning; [Прогнозирование циклов производства меди в гидрометаллургии с помощью интерпретируемого машинного обучения]
Abstract: Accurate production forecasting in industrial hydrometallurgy is essential for process optimization yet is often hindered by the scarcity of extensive historical data. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of classical machine learning models as a data-efficient and interpretable alternative to complex deep learning methods for predicting total copper mass. We evaluated four models— Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Decision Tree, and Linear Regression—using a methodology centered on two key strategies: synthetically expanding a limited 150-day dataset into 10,000 simulated cycles (approximately 1.5 million data points) via data augmentation, and engineering 10-day lag features to provide the models with a temporal perspective for a 10-step-ahead forecasting task. The results revealed exceptional predictive accuracy, with ensemble techniques proving superior. The Random Forest model emerged as the top performer, achieving an R² of 0.974, an MAE of 0.088, and an RMSE of 0.111, closely followed by Gradient Boosting (R² of 0.971). All models successfully captured the distinct 150-day cyclical dynamics of the production process, showing a near-zero phase lag (0.00 ± ≤0.05 days). While performance on new, independent data requires further validation, this work establishes a robust and transparent framework for developing reliable forecasting tools in data-limited industrial environments. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC.
