Title: Effect of Y addition on microstructure, tensile properties, and corrosion behavior of high-speed-extruded Mg–5Bi–3Al alloy
Abstract: This study investigates the effect of Y addition on the microstructure, tensile properties, and corrosion behavior of high-speed-extruded Mg–5Bi–3Al (BA53) alloy. Y-free BA53 and Y-containing BAW53 x alloys ( x = 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 wt.%) are extruded at a die-exit speed of 67 m/min, and the role of Y is examined with emphasis on second-phase evolution and its influence on mechanical and corrosion behavior. Y addition progressively changes the second-phase characteristics from fine intragranular Mg3Bi2 particles to coarse BiY particles concentrated mainly along grain boundaries, while distinct grain refinement appears only at the highest Y content. The tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength decrease slightly with increasing Y content, whereas tensile elongation remains comparable and increases slightly at 0.2 wt.% Y. The strength reduction is mainly associated with the reduced strengthening contribution of fine Mg3Bi2 particles. Longitudinal-section observations near the fracture surface show that coarse BiY particles do not act as dominant crack-initiation sites; instead, fracture remains governed mainly by twin-related cracking, which accounts for the limited change in tensile ductility despite the marked change in second-phase characteristics. The corrosion behavior shows a strongly non-monotonic dependence on Y content. A minor addition of 0.2 wt.% Y markedly improves corrosion resistance, whereas larger additions lead to severe deterioration. The Volta potential difference between BiY and the α -Mg matrix is substantially larger than that between Mg3Bi2 and the α -Mg matrix, indicating a stronger local galvanic driving force. Early-stage and cross-sectional corrosion observations further show that BA53 is more susceptible to widespread Mg3Bi2-assisted corrosion initiation, whereas high-Y alloys increasingly develop BiY-assisted localized corrosion, corrosion-front propagation along grain-boundary regions, and corrosion-film instability. These results demonstrate that a minor addition of 0.2 wt.% Y provides a favorable combination of high-speed extrudability, strength–ductility balance, and enhanced corrosion resistance in the present BA53-based alloy system. Title: EXTENSION OF THE BERIT SUTURE ZONE TO EASTERNMOST TÜRKIYE (EAST OF LAKE VAN): EVIDENCE FROM AN UPPER CRETACEOUS INTRA-OCEANIC ARC, SUPRA-SUBDUCTION ZONE OPHIOLITES, AND PALAEOZOIC-CENOZOIC SEDIMENTARY SUCCESSIONS
Abstract: This paper discusses and interprets the important but little studied eastward extension of the regionally important Berit Suture Zone that extends across eastern Türkiye into Iran (>500km). Fragmentary Upper Cretaceous ophiolites, oceanic island arc units and accretionary melange, east of Lake Van, are keys to an understanding of the Berit Suture Zone in this area. Field and geochemical evidence suggest that a dismembered ophiolite (Mehmetalan ophiolite) in the study area, mainly depleted mantle harzburgite, dunite and cumulate gabbro, formed in an Upper Cretaceous fore-arc setting. Cross-cutting alkaline diabase dykes in one of the ophiolite fragments hints at plume involvement. The volcanic arc, part of the regional Yüksekova Complex, is dominated by variably evolved tholeiitic, calc-alkaline and alkaline volcanics that erupted in an open-ocean setting, together with minor granodioritic intrusives. Intercalated pelagic carbonates are dated here as Campanian-Maastrichtian (locally late Maastrichtian) based on planktic foraminifera. The arc-related volcanics display two geochemical trends: one is typical of variably evolved basic-felsic oceanic arc volcanism; the other is alkaline and could represent escape of relatively enriched upper mantle through a slab rupture or alternatively plume involvement in the SSZ magmatism. A dismembered Palaeozoic-Mesozoic platform succession in the area can be correlated with the Malatya-Keban (Tauride) platform >300 km to the west. The deposition and deformation of the sedimentary cover units, of Late Palaeocene-Middle Eocene and also of Oligocene-Early Miocene age, help to constrain the timing of deformation. Three main phases of southward-directed compression, thrusting and consequent subaerial erosion are recognised: latest Cretaceous, Late Eocene and Mid-Late Miocene. This was followed by plateau uplift, strike-slip/transpression and westward ‘tectonic escape’. The proposed tectonic model correlates the various units east of Lake Van with the development of the Berit Ocean between the Malatya-Keban platform to the north and the Pütürge and Bitlis metamorphic units generally to the south. Differences, however, include the absence of exposed Bitlis continental crust to the south, the lack of significant Eocene volcanism, thrust emplacement farther south, and a more complex and variable deformation history. © 2027, Edizioni ETS. Title: Diffusion kinetics and atomistic migration mechanisms of order transition driven by third-element dopants in L10-FePt alloys
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Third-element doping is an effective strategy for promoting low-temperature L10 ordering in FePt nanoparticles, but the underlying dopant-regulated diffusion kinetics and atomic migration mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experiments are combined to elucidate these processes. The calculations reveal distinct defect-mediated diffusion mechanisms. Fe preferentially migrates through nearest-neighbor vacancy jumping, whereas Pt favours a lower-energy antisite-assisted pathway. A five-step strategy integrating thermodynamic, structural, magnetic, and ordering-transition screening with DFT prediction and experimental verification is established to identify promising dopants. Large-radius dopants reduce migration barriers by more than 20% and enhance low-temperature diffusion coefficients by over three orders of magnitude. Atomic radius is identified as the dominant geometric descriptor of migration barriers, while electronegativity and valence electron number provide secondary electronic contributions. Experimental results further support the predicted trends. Large-radius elements, such as Bi and Pb, can promote L10 ordering at low temperatures and achieve a high ordering degree and coercivity. In contrast, Mn shows limited ordering, whereas Co-, Ni-, and Cu-doped systems retain the disordered fcc phase, which is broadly consistent with the calculated trends. This work provides a framework for dopant selection and low-temperature synthesis of ordered intermetallic nanoparticles. © 2026

Title: Processing-driven interplay of interfacial asymmetry and microstructure in spin-orbit effects of Pt/Co heterostructures
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Deposition conditions such as Ar pressure and power density are well-known to influence the surface and microstructure of sputtered thin films and multilayers, which in turn affect spin-orbit coupling-related magnetic properties such as interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) and spin-orbit torque (SOT) in nonmagnetic layer (NM)/ferromagnetic layer (FM) heterostructures. Nonetheless, a holistic approach to understanding how processing conditions influence magnetic properties has been understudied. This study investigates how deposition conditions affect the surface roughness and microstructure of the Pt layer, and how these factors impact DMI and SOT in Pt/Co heterostructures. The Pt surface roughness exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on Ar pressure from 1.5 to 20 mTorr, altering the interfacial asymmetry and, consequently, varying the DMI energy density from 0.93 to 1.19 mJ/m2. In contrast, power density shows a weak influence on roughness and DMI within the investigated range from 1.23 to 7.40 W/cm2. Post-deposition annealing promotes interdiffusion at the Pt/Co interface, reducing both the surface anisotropy (Ks) and the absolute value of the DMI (Deff). Increasing Ar pressure also modifies the Pt microstructure, reducing crystallite size from 5.02 to 2.92 nm and increasing microstrain from 0.022 to 0.037. These microstructural changes promote electron scattering and increase electrical resistivity from 27.8 to 92.8 µΩ cm, accompanied by an increase in the damping-like SOT efficiency (ξDL) up to 0.24. Title: A simulation-informed machine learning framework for integrated energy and thermal comfort assessment in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings under hot-arid climates
Abstract: Adaptive reuse of heritage courtyard buildings as boutique hotels creates a complex balance between energy performance, thermal comfort, and cultural conservation in hot-arid regions. However, existing studies commonly address energy performance and thermal comfort separately and often depend on computationally intensive simulation workflows. This study develops a simulation-informed machine-learning surrogate framework for simultaneous prediction of end-uses energy consumption and thermal comfort indicators in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings. A comprehensive hourly dataset was generated from full-year simulations of twelve heritage courtyard buildings modelled in DesignBuilder using representative meteorological data for the hot-arid climate of Kashan, Iran. Building-specific heat-transfer characteristics represented by overall heat-transfer coefficient values, geometric attributes, operational parameters, indoor environmental conditions and weather were used as predictors. Seven end-uses energy outputs, namely cooling electricity, heating gas, lighting, appliance energy, system fan energy, system pump energy, and auxiliary energy, were evaluated alongside three thermal comfort indicators: predicted mean vote, predicted percentage of dissatisfied, and comfort percentage. Twenty-eight machine-learning algorithms were attempted, of which 22 successfully converged and were assessed using a leave-one-building-out validation strategy to evaluate cross-building generalization. In addition, an independently simulated heritage building, excluded from all training and validation procedures, was used for external testing to further assess model transferability. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean squared error, and predictor importance was examined using a Shapley-value-based feature-importance analysis. Ensemble Bagged Trees achieved the highest predictive performance for eight of the ten evaluated outputs, while the two system-level end-uses, system fans and system pumps, were predicted less accurately (coefficients of determination of 0.397 and 0.839, respectively). Thermal comfort analysis revealed substantial seasonal discomfort, ranging from cold winter stress to severe summer overheating, while annual comfort levels remained below the adopted comfort benchmark. The Shapley-value-based analysis indicated that climatic variables (e.g., solar irradiation and outdoor temperature) and building-scale geometric/envelope variables (e.g., orientation, façade area, window-to-wall ratio, and envelope thermal properties) were among the most influential predictors across the evaluated outputs. Although courtyard-specific geometric parameters were not included as explicit inputs, building-scale variables partly reflect the influence of courtyard configuration. The independent test case further demonstrated the framework's ability to predict several energy and thermal comfort outputs for a previously unseen building, while indicating lower transferability for some system-level end-uses. Although the framework is based on simulation-generated rather than measured data, it provides a computationally efficient basis for preliminary retrofit assessment and scenario exploration. Overall, the framework enables integrated and interpretable assessment of energy performance and thermal comfort to support heritage-sensitive retrofit planning in hot-arid climates. © 2026 The Authors. Title: NPR-NLMMI hybrid mode-locked fiber laser with an SMF-PCF-GIMF-SMF saturable absorber

Title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. Title: Tuning nanomaterial facets with light: A laser-enabled strategy for surface control
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-index facets play an important role in regulating the surface reactivity of functional nanomaterials. Here, we present a femtosecond (fs) laser-enabled strategy for post-synthesis facet engineering by fabricating laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on CoFe2O4/Co3O4 (CFO/CO) epitaxial films. Authors: Chandran S.; Ramachandran T.; Sivakumar D.; Ambika A.
Title: The impact of environmental, economic, and social sustainability under intensive agriculture
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intensive agriculture has substantially increased agricultural productivity but is increasingly associated with environmental degradation, resource depletion, and socio-economic challenges. The study objectives were to evaluate the sustainability impacts of intensive agricultural practices across environmental, economic, and social dimensions in Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu, India, with particular emphasis on resource utilization, ecological stress, and the factors influencing sustainable agricultural development. METHODS: Primary data were collected during 2025 from 663 eligible farmers selected through multistage stratified random sampling across eight taluks of Namakkal District using a structured questionnaire. Farms were classified as traditional or intensive based on cultivation practices. Relationships among the study variables were examined using correlation analysis, analysis of variance, regression analysis, and non-parametric statistical tests. FINDINGS: The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between landholding size and family size (correlation coefficient = 0.7214), indicating close structural and demographic linkages within farming systems. Intensive agriculture was significantly associated with land expansion (correlation coefficient = 0.658), environmental pollution (correlation coefficient = 0.519), and declining health conditions among farming communities (correlation coefficient = 0.412). Approximately 63 percent of respondents reported land degradation, while 65 –78 percent reported salinity and nutrient depletion, reflecting perceived ecological stress. The regression model explained 7.1 percent of the variation in agricultural production (coefficient of determination = 0.071), indicating modest explanatory power. Questionnaire reliability was satisfactory (Cronbach's alpha = 0.824), supporting the internal consistency of the survey instrument. CONCLUSION: Intensive agriculture is associated with higher short-term agricultural productivity but is also associated with environmental degradation, increases health risks, and places greater pressure on natural resources. These findings may inform strategies to improve the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of agricultural sustainability through sustainable soil management, balanced agrochemical application, efficient irrigation, and policy support. While the study is limited to a single district and cross-sectional data, it provides empirical evidence to inform future longitudinal and multi-regional investigations. ©2026 The author(s). Title: Charge-Carrier Behavior and Molecular Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
Abstract: Molecular interface engineering has become increasingly important for improving the efficiency and stability of perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Although highly emissive perovskite materials have advanced rapidly, their translation into high-performance devices remains limited by interfacial losses, unbalanced charge injection, and instability under electrical operation. In this review, we first discuss charge-carrier behavior in perovskite materials and devices, with emphasis on radiative and non-radiative recombination, carrier accumulation under injection, and the device-level consequences of interfacial constraints. We then examine the development of interfacial molecular strategies in PeLEDs, including self-assembled monolayers and related interfacial molecules, and summarize how such molecular layers influence charge injection, interfacial recombination, local electronic structure, and film formation at both charge-injection interfaces. On this basis, we further consider the implications of these interfacial effects for molecular regulation in light-emitting devices, with particular attention to electronic regulation under bias, chemically persistent passivation, and structural compatibility with emissive-layer formation. By connecting carrier physics, interfacial function, and molecular regulation, this review aims to provide a clearer framework for understanding and developing molecular interfacial strategies for high-performance PeLEDs. Title: Error Analysis of the Stabilized Finite Volume Method for Time-Dependent Incompressible MHD Equations with Rotational Velocity Correction
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a fully decoupled numerical method for solving the time-dependent incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations. The method features a rotational velocity correction technique, which is combined with the finite volume method to ensure both the local conservation of physical quantities. Using the lowest equal-order mixed finite element pair (P1 −P1 −P1 ) to approximate the velocity, magnetic field, and pressure, we address the inf-sup condition through pressure projection stabilization. A semi-implicit method is used to handle the nonlinear terms, and the rotational velocity correction method decouples the MHD system into three subsystems, thereby simplifying the computation and solution process. By selecting appropriate test functions and applying the Gronwall inequality, the stability of the numerical solution and optimal error estimates for velocity, magnetic field, and pressure are established. Finally, numerical results are presented to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Water-Cooled Photovoltaic Modules Using a Helical Pipe Network with Twisted Tape Inserts
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape inserts as separate solutions, there's a noticeable absence of studies that combine these approaches. Specifically, there is a lack of investigation into optimizing the arrangement of cooling pipes before incorporating internal flow enhancements. Moreover, experimental evidence is essential to confirm if such a dual strategy can genuinely improve the performance without imposing significant hydraulic disadvantages. This research directly tackles these issues by introducing and validating a two-step optimization strategy for water-cooled PV/T modules. Our work commenced with a computational assessment of four different helical pipe arrangements (100 × 150, 100 × 100, 100 × 50, and 80 × 80 mm). After this initial evaluation, the most promising configuration was further refined by adding either four or ten twisted-tape inserts. The best-performing layout was then enhanced using four and ten twisted-tape inserts. Simulations in three dimensions, investigating conjugate heat transfer, were performed using ANSYS Fluent. These simulations were carried out under a heat flux load of 800 W/m², with incoming water at a temperature of 25 °C, and across a range of Reynolds numbers from 5,000 to 11,000. The configuration featuring an 80 × 80 mm layout emerged as the optimal baseline. This setup successfully lowered the average temperature of the PV surface to 45.62 °C when the Reynolds number was 11,000. Concurrently, it achieved an electrical efficiency of 16.05% and an electrical power output of 205.49 W. The subsequent introduction of ten twisted-tape inserts led to a further reduction in temperature, bringing it down to 42.30 °C. This enhancement also boosted the electrical efficiency to 16.44% and the power output to 210.48 W. To confirm these findings, experimental validation was conducted. The results from these experiments showed mean absolute percentage errors of 1.46% for the baseline setup and a slightly lower 1.23% for the configuration enhanced with inserts. An important consideration, the pumping power required for these systems remained below 3 W across all tested conditions. The distinct contribution of this research lies in its comprehensive approach, which unifies several key aspects within a single design framework. This includes optimizing the helical pipe layout, harnessing the flow enhancement provided by twisted tapes, evaluating the uniformity of temperature, and undertaking experimental validation of the thermohydraulic performance. This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Engineering asymmetric energy pathways using Janus gel heteroarchitectures for electromagnetic radiation absorption and directional radiative‑evaporative thermal management

Title: Top-down systems engineering of manganese-based lithium-ion batteries for practical deployment

Abstract: Uniting economic viability, environmental benignity, highly tunable electrochemical attributes, and paramount safety, manganese (Mn)-based batteries stand as the most formidable contenders to define the state-of-the-art in the upcoming next-generation energy landscape. However, their intrinsic structural and interfacial instabilities are aggressively exacerbated by scenario-specific operational stressors, cascading across multiple engineering echelons in Mn-based batteries. Adopting a forward-looking, Mn-centric perspective, this review uniquely and systematically deconstructs the distinct challenges of Mn-based batteries across three echelons—material, device, and scenario—thereby exposing their cross-layer mismatches and subsequently mapping out targeted technological trajectories. Addressing these intertwined, dynamic multi-scale impediments, we delineate a scenario-driven, cross-layer co-design paradigm for the broader Mn-based battery ecosystem, championing the integration of frontier characterization and digital intelligence as the twin engines to catalyze the journey of Mn-based technologies from laboratory curiosity to industrial and commercial maturity. © 2026

Title: Laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers with different doping types: Multiscale mechanism investigation and deep learning-based processing strategy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) is the core substrate material for next-generation high-voltage power devices and high-frequency radio-frequency electronics, while wafer slicing remains a critical bottleneck constraining its low-cost, high-yield manufacturing. Conventional diamond wire sawing suffers from severe kerf loss and serious subsurface damage; ultrafast laser slicing technology represents a revolutionary alternative to traditional wire sawing, yet the pivotal regulatory effect of doping type on optical absorption and energy deposition remains unrevealed. This study comprehensively employs experimental characterization, first-principles calculations, and the two-temperature model to systematically investigate the multiscale mechanisms of ultrafast laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers with different doping types, elucidating the regulatory laws of dopant elements on laser energy absorption, free-carrier excitation, carrier-lattice coupling, and crack propagation behavior. A deep learning-based process optimization framework is proposed, and a conditional neural network model based on feature-wise linear modulation is constructed, taking material resistivity, focal depth, and doping type as inputs to accurately predict critical process parameters including laser power, scanning speed, and hatch spacing. With model-optimized parameters, the exfoliated surface roughness of samples is significantly reduced to below 0.4 μm. The coefficient of determination (R2) on the test set exceeds 0.97, achieving adaptive optimization of process parameters for wafers with different doping types. This study provides systematic theoretical interpretation and intelligent process solutions for low-damage, high-precision laser slicing of 4H-SiC wafers. © 2026

Title: A pseudo-labeling approach for automated assignment of unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues
Abstract: In the era of AI-driven protein structure prediction, there is an urgent demand for rapid, accessible experimental approaches to validate computationally predicted structural models or to improve the accuracy of AI-based structure determination. As a key experimental technique for determining protein structures in solution, conventional biomolecular NMR spectroscopy relies heavily on proteins labeled with 13C and 15N isotopes, a requirement that entails high experimental costs, lengthy sample preparation times, and steep technical barriers, thereby limiting its broader application. Building on our previous work, we have developed a pseudo-labeling strategy for the automated resonance assignment of unlabeled proteins. Using high-field NMR spectrometers equipped with cryoprobes, we acquired natural-abundance 1H–13C and 1H–15N heteronuclear correlation spectra directly from unlabeled samples. By integrating predicted chemical shifts of HN, Hα, 13Cα, and 15N from three complementary AI tools into an iterative simulated annealing framework with an alternating scoring scheme, our method effectively resolves severe cross-peak overlap during the automated assignment process by introducing heteronuclear dimensional constraints. This approach enables reliable automated backbone resonance assignment for unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues. We anticipate that this labeling-free strategy will lower the technical barrier to biomolecular NMR, enabling researchers without specialized NMR expertise to employ NMR spectroscopy in fundamental life science research and drug development. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Bolstered Interfacial Field Chemistry for Deep Fast-Charging Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
Abstract: Deep fast-charging capability has become the core pursuit for practical applications of aqueous zinc metal batteries, yet it is critically impeded by unfavorable interfacial field evolution at the electrode/electrolyte interface under high-current–density conditions. The coexistence of sluggish Zn2+ desolvation, competitive H2O reduction corrosion, uneven electric field, and concentration field collectively leads to poor rate performance. To tackle these issues, a bolstered interfacial field chemistry strategy was developed via sulfosuccinic acid to precisely regulate the physicochemical and electrochemical properties within the inner Helmholtz plane. The tuned interfacial field comprises a homogeneous distribution of interfacial ions and electric fields, promoting fast desolvation and interfacial electron transfer. Consequently, the modified Zn||Cu asymmetric cells deliver an outstanding average Coulombic efficiency of 99.48% over 1600 cycles at 2 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, the modified Zn||Zn symmetric cells demonstrate exceptional stability under challenging conditions of 5 mA cm−2, 2 mAh cm−2 (over 1600 h), and 10 mA cm−2, 10 mAh cm−2 (over 675 h, depth of discharge = 17.08%). Impressively, a substantial cumulative capacity of 3500 mAh cm−2 is attained at 10 mAh cm−2 and a 56.93% Zn utilization rate. Besides, the enhanced Zn (10 µm) ||I2 (10.87 mg cm−2) full cell sustains over 1490 cycles at 1 A g−1 with 77.13% capacity retention and a harsh N/P ratio of 2.31. Remarkably, the Zn (10 µm) ||I2 pouch cell achieves over 680 cycles with an ultralow N/P ratio of 2.04. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Geometry-agnostic reinforcement learning for toolpath-dependent residual stress mitigation in metallic component manufacturing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Residual stress (RS) remains a critical bottleneck in toolpath-dependent metal fabrication processes such as additive manufacturing, machining, and welding, because toolpath‑induced thermal non-uniformity drives distortion, cracking, and premature failure. Existing RS optimization methods necessitate either computationally intensive, geometry-specific simulation searches or extensive data requirements for machine learning models that require retraining upon changes in part geometry. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel reinforcement learning (RL) framework that facilitates geometry-aware, layer-wise toolpath planning for unseen 3D geometries within the trained computational domain without the need for part-specific retraining. The target 3D geometry is voxelized, and the RL state integrates the current layer design with the accumulated 3D temperature field predicted by a finite difference method simulation that incorporates the heat source, heat transfer, and dwell time. The RL agent learns to select from 30 distinct toolpath patterns per layer to maximize thermal uniformity and mitigate RS. Consequently, the model reduces per-part optimization time by approximately three orders of magnitude compared with the evaluated search-based optimization baselines, demonstrating superior computational efficiency. Experimental validation demonstrates that the optimized toolpaths reduce warpage by up to 27.5% and mitigate the average RS within critical high-stress regions by up to 25.5%, while microstructural analysis reveals more uniform thermal histories. By integrating physics-based thermal modeling with RL, this framework demonstrates potential for extensibility to various manufacturing processes where the toolpath governs thermal quality. © 2026

Title: Advanced optimization problems and solution methods for renewable energy integration - A bibliometric review
Abstract: The worldwide shift to sustainable energy supply has led to extensive incorporation of renewable energy sources into modern power systems incorporating specifically with wind-turbine and solar-photovoltaic systems. The stochastic and intermittent nature of such renewable energy sources, however, poses significant challenges in their operation and planning, especially regarding optimization and system coordination. This paper provides a detailed overview of various advanced optimization problems and solution methods for the integration of renewable energy in today's power systems. The study divides important optimization problems into three categories: active and reactive power management, uncertainty modelling and real-time stochastic operation of power systems. Coordination of active and reactive power resources is a critical issue that needs to be addressed to ensure voltage stability and reliability of the grid with high penetrations of renewables. The review also explores the concept of stochastic energy and reactive power markets, which entails optimizing ancillary services like voltage support and reactive power dispatch together, considering interactions between transmission system operators and distribution system operators. Moreover, the traditional optimization techniques such as linear programming, nonlinear programming and mixed-integer programming are compared with the new ones such as the intelligent and hybrid techniques. The current review is a structured reference which combines technical analysis with bibliometric analysis and indicates future research directions to develop resilient, intelligent and market-oriented power system optimization frameworks. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Ionizing irradiation induced non-equilibrium cation vacancies switching peroxymonosulfate activation pathways
Abstract: Ionizing irradiation was investigated as a non-equilibrium defect-engineering strategy to generate Fe-vacancy-associated environments in spinel ferrites and thereby regulate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation pathways. Using CoFe2O4 as a model catalyst, irradiation conditions were tuned to control Fe deficiency, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy, in situ Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical analyses, reactive-species quantification, and density functional theory calculations were integrated to resolve the resulting structure–activity relationship. The optimized catalyst exhibited a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.285 min−1 for sulfamethoxazole degradation and 99.7% PMS utilization, with •OH and SO4•- accounting for 83.4% of degradation; Fe-vacancy-associated environments promoted cooperative Fe–Co electronic coupling, PMS adsorption, and O–O bond cleavage, while maintaining efficient oxidation across pH 5–9 and for diverse contaminants. These results establish that irradiation-induced Fe deficiency redirects PMS activation toward radical-dominated oxidation through local coordination and electronic-structure regulation. The extension to NiFe2O4 and MnFe2O4 and stable 168-h continuous-flow wastewater treatment further demonstrate the potential of non-equilibrium irradiation engineering as a general route for tuning reactive-species pathways in Fenton-like catalysis. © 2026

Title: Water as a dual-function modulator: From defect passivation to energy-transfer control for color-tunable lead-free perovskite white LEDs
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: This work demonstrates a humidity-responsive, single-component white-light-emitting device based on Cs3CeCl6:Sb3+ nanocrystals. Under controlled humid conditions, the device exhibits continuously tunable white-light emission, with the correlated color temperature varying from 4400 to 5600 K while maintaining a color rendering index above 95%. Controlled H2O adsorption not only passivates surface defects in Cs3CeCl6 nanocrystals, increasing the photoluminescence quantum yield from 75% to 98%, but also regulates the Ce3+ → Sb3+ energy-transfer process in the Sb3+-doped system. Spectroscopic analysis, carrier-dynamics measurements, and surface-slab calculations show that adsorbed H2O interacts with the Cs3CeCl6 surface and perturbs the local electronic environment of Ce3+ sites near the nanocrystal surface, leading to a blue shift of the Ce3+ 5d-related energy levels and reduced spectral overlap with the Sb3+ absorption band. This suppresses the Ce3+ → Sb3+ Förster resonance energy-transfer process and enables dynamic tuning of the emission color and color temperature. These results reveal the dual role of surface-adsorbed H2O in defect passivation and energy-transfer regulation, providing a new strategy for developing efficient, color-tunable, lead-free metal-halide luminescent materials. © 2026

Title: Cooling-controlled microstructure engineering for mechanical–magnetic synergy in high-strength non-oriented silicon steel
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing non-oriented silicon steels with both high mechanical strength and low iron loss is critical for high-speed drive motors, yet remains challenging because conventional strengthening strategies often deteriorate magnetic performance. Herein, post-annealing cooling is employed as a kinetic control parameter to regulate the retained Cu precipitation state and magnetic domain structure without introducing a separate aging treatment. Rapid cooling retained a high density of fine, coherent B2-type Cu-rich clusters and BCC Cu nanoprecipitates by suppressing diffusion-mediated coarsening and structural transformation, whereas slower cooling promoted precipitate growth and evolution toward coarse incoherent 9R Cu precipitates. Combined density functional theory calculations and three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations indicate that fine coherent Cu-rich precipitates provide effective precipitation strengthening while causing relatively weak perturbation of local magnetization. Meanwhile, rapid cooling refined the magnetic domain width and reduced iron loss by approximately 24%, although a slight decrease in magnetic induction occurred because of the intensified γ-fiber texture. These results demonstrate that post-annealing cooling provides an effective kinetic pathway for coordinating precipitation strengthening, magnetic domain refinement, and texture evolution in high-strength non-oriented silicon steels. © 2026

Title: Co-condensation engineering of hydrophobic and mechanically robust alumina aerogels for thermal protection under extreme conditions
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Alumina aerogels have emerged as promising candidates for high-temperature thermal protection but suffer from mechanical fragility and hydrophilicity. Herein, we report a co-condensation strategy involving an inorganic aluminum precursor, methyltriethoxysilane (MTES), and polyvinyltrimethoxysilane (PVTMS) to fabricate alumina-based aerogels with a network of hydrocarbon chains and methyl-functionalized aluminosiloxanes. PVTMS provides multiple hydrolyzable silane sites and a polymeric backbone that enhance skeleton connectivity and stress redistribution, while MTES-derived methyl groups reduce surface polarity. At an intermediate PVTMS content, Al-SiMPV0.25 achieves the best balance of compressive robustness, thermal stability, and superhydrophobicity. Under hygrothermal exposure, its reinforced skeleton resists structural degradation, while the low-polarity surface limits moisture uptake and water-assisted thermal coupling, thereby preserving structural integrity and low thermal conductivity. The retained nanoporous framework suppresses gas-phase and solid-phase heat transport, while the aluminosilicate network attenuates radiative penetration through infrared extinction at elevated temperatures. Ultimately, under one-sided heating, Al-SiMPV0.25 maintains an approximately 731 °C temperature difference between the hot (∼980 °C) and cold (∼249 °C) faces. This work provides a route to durable oxide aerogels for humid and high-temperature environments. © 2026

Title: Diverse oxidosqualene cyclases for triterpenoid biosynthesis
Abstract: Triterpenoids, a significant group of secondary metabolites, possess diverse skeletons and excellent pharmacological activities and are widely applied in cosmetics, medicine, and biopesticides. Traditional plant extraction and chemical synthesis cannot meet the needs of commercial production, and heterologous biosynthesis of triterpenoids has become a promising strategy. Oxidosqualene cyclases (OSCs) are the key enzymes that determine triterpenoid biosynthesis. However, most OSCs exhibit low heterologous expression, low catalytic activity, and promiscuous catalytic products, which impedes the heterologous biosynthesis of triterpenoids. In this study, we constructed a dataset of 348 OSCs with known functions, which is the largest centralized resource of characterized OSCs to date. The 88 triterpenoid skeletons produced by these OSCs are classified based on their structural features, 49 of which have been experimentally characterized as the main products of OSCs, and the formation mechanisms of the common skeletons are summarized. Phylogenetic analysis and motif analysis elucidated the relationships among the sequences, structures, and products of plant-derived OSCs. Phylogenetic analysis showed that plant-derived OSCs were divided into two major clades, which corresponded to the biosynthetic mechanisms of the "protosteryl/dammarenyl" dichotomy. Motif analysis showed that 5 motifs are present in plant-derived OSCs, including 3 related to the catalytic activity of the OSCs and 2 related to product specificity. Finally, we summarized the common strategies for mining OSCs to provide directions for the discovery of novel OSCs and new triterpenoid skeletons. Our study will help discover or design OSCs with specific product profiles as functional elements for applications in synthetic biology. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Cyclic melting of Ni-Nb-Y alloy under space and ground conditions: A comparative study of phase separation and solidification behavior

Title: Melt-spinning-enabled microstructure engineering toward high thermoelectric and mechanical properties in Ag2Se-based composites

Abstract: Tailoring the microstructures is essential for simultaneously enhancing the thermoelectric and mechanical properties of Ag2Se‑based materials, while effective processing strategies for realising such rational microstructural design are still required. Title: Interfacial charge-driven hydrogel enables self-sustained Fe redox cycling for synergistic therapy of infected wounds
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Chronic wound infections by drug-resistant bacteria remain challenging due to biofilms, oxidative stress, and impaired immunity. Here, we report an interfacial charge-driven hydrogel that enables a light-assisted self-sustained redox cycling for the efficient therapy of infected wounds. By integrating MXene/FeCu-MOFs heterojunctions into the sulfonated chitosan hydrogel (M/M-SCS@Gel), a built-in electric field induces directional charge redistribution and continuous interfacial electron transport across the heterojunction. This process continuously regenerates catalytically active Fe2+ from Fe3+, thereby overcoming the kinetic limitations of Fe2+ depletion and sustaining Fenton-like reactions for persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Notably, MXene-mediated photothermal conversion accelerates electron transfer and redox kinetics, amplifying ROS under NIR irradiation. This synergistic effect enables efficient eradication of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) through ROS generation and Fe2+-mediated catalytic effects, while simultaneously promoting M2 macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and collagen deposition. These findings demonstrate that the antibacterial mechanism of M/M-SCS@Gel is associated with transcriptomic signatures of translational stress and proteostasis imbalance, including inhibition of ribosome assembly and disruption of translation initiation, which ultimately leads to a translational-metabolic imbalance between amino acid biosynthesis and protein synthesis. This work establishes an interfacial charge-driven therapeutic strategy that integrates self-sustained redox catalysis with immune modulation, providing a broadly applicable strategy for treating pathogen-infected wounds. © 2026

Title: Grain boundary segregation engineering via in-situ TiB2 formation for enhanced mechanical properties in additively manufactured AA2024 alloys
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The non-equilibrium solidification that occurs during additive manufacturing (AM) of Al-Cu-Mg alloys typically results in hot cracking and compromised mechanical properties due to their wide solidification range. Here, a grain boundary segregation engineering (GBSE) strategy is developed through the in-situ formation of TiB2 nanoparticles during laser-powder bed fusion, effectively enhancing both printability and mechanical performance of AA2024. The in-situ TiB2 nanoparticles not only promote the formation of a refined equiaxed grain structure with a high density of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs), but also induce a semi-coherent interface between TiB2 particles and the Al matrix. These microstructural evolutions facilitate segregation of Cu and Mg atoms towards grain boundaries (GBs), which contribute to the development of a continuous intermetallic network composed primarily of θ-Al2Cu and S-Al2CuMg phases. Such a network strengthens GB cohesion and suppresses the formation of intergranular liquid films, thereby mitigating hot cracking. Additionally, it serves as a barrier to GB sliding and dislocation propagation, enhancing microstructural stability and deformation compatibility. Consequently, the as-built TiB2/AA2024 composite achieves an ultimate tensile strength of ∼502 MPa and fracture elongation of ∼9.9%. This work offers new insights into microstructure engineering in AM, demonstrating the synergistic effects of in-situ nanoparticle formation and GBSE in achieving high-performance Al alloys. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Title: Scalable microfluidic blow spinning for in situ synthesis of A-site engineered perovskite nanocrystals in nanofibers with enhanced stability and outdoor functionality
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Scalable fabrication of perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) with both exceptional fluorescence stability and tunable blue-to-red emission remains a key challenge in perovskite research. In this study, we develop a room-temperature microfluidic blow spinning (MBS) strategy that enables in situ growth and encapsulation of PNCs within polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers, together with simultaneous modulation via A-site and ligand engineering. Starting from a green-emitting γ-phase Rb0.5Cs0.5PbBr3/PAN nanofiber film, achieved through partial substitution of Cs with Rb at the A-site, a series of γ-phase Rb0.5Cs0.5PbX3/PAN (X=Br, I) nanofiber films are fabricated at scale. By tuning the halide composition and the type and concentration of ligands, including oleylamine (OAm) and octylamine (OTAm), blue-to-red emission spanning 476‒600 nm is achieved. The resulting nanofiber films exhibit excellent stability under harsh conditions, including long-term storage, thermal cycling, water immersion, and ultraviolet irradiation. Furthermore, the Rb0.5Cs0.5PbX3/PAN nanofiber films demonstrate multifunctional performance, enabling fluorescent patterning for wearable devices and efficient photocatalytic CO2-to-CO conversion under natural sunlight, with a maximum production rate of 83.6 μmol g−1 h−1. This work provides a scalable approach for fabricating high-performance PNCs and offers new insights into their practical application. © 2026

Authors: Liu Y.; Zhu Z.; Zhu Z.
Title: Calculation of the local ground-level total electric field near a tower in a multi-circuit AC-to-DC conversion project based on an improved upwind finite element method
Abstract: To address the problems of complex ion-flow space-charge distribution in AC-to-DC converted transmission lines under wind action, and the tendency of the conventional upwind finite element method to suffer from iterative oscillations and convergence difficulties, this paper proposes an improved upwind finite element method that enhances the stability of ground-level total electric field calculation under complex wind conditions. Taking a typical multi-circuit project where 750-kV AC cup-shaped towers are converted for 500-kV DC transmission as the engineering background, the local ground-level total electric field near one converted tower is investigated under different wind speeds and three-conductor polarity arrangements. The results show that the proposed method exhibits better convergence performance than the conventional upwind finite element method. An increase in wind speed promotes the wind-driven transport and redistribution of space charge, thereby affecting the peak magnitude and location of the local ground-level total electric field. The conductor polarity arrangement significantly influences the local field distribution, with the positive-positive-negative arrangement yielding a higher field magnitude among the investigated local configurations. The findings can provide a reference for local electromagnetic-environment assessment near towers in similar AC-to-DC conversion projects. © 2026

Title: Synergistic strength-ductility in wire arc additive manufacturing of Al-Cu-Mg alloys via Sc microalloying and in-situ multi-scale precipitation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) of high-strength 2xxx series Al-Cu-Mg alloys is severely restricted by the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off, severe mechanical anisotropy, and inadequate microstructure control under non-equilibrium solidification. This work addressed these challenges by developing a novel Sc microalloyed 2024 Al alloy wire and systematically investigating its microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in both as-deposited (AD) and T6-treated conditions. The results indicated that the non-equilibrium solidification during WAAM induced the in-situ transformation of primary Al3Sc into the highly stable Al8Cu4Sc (W-phase) at grain boundaries. The introduction of Sc and Mn synergistically mitigated the conventional bimodal grain structure by inhibiting interlayer recrystallization, reducing the microstructural anisotropy to 9.1%. Following T6 treatment, the intergranular T-phase (Al20Cu2Mn3) networks were largely dissolved and reprecipitated as nanoscale rod-like intragranular T-phase, while the coarse W-phase remained thermally stable at the boundaries. This cross-scale hierarchical microstructure enables a remarkable synergy of strength and ductility. The ultimate tensile strength and yield strength reached 453.0 and 313.9 MPa, respectively, with an extraordinary elongation of 10.1% (a 115% increase compared to the AD conditions). Quantitative calculation indicated that Orowan strengthening from nano-scale T- and W-phases dominated the yield strength (108.2 MPa), while uniform distribution of non-shearable precipitates promoted homogeneous dislocation slip and delayed strain localization, accounting for the improved ductility. This work provides fundamental insight into Sc microalloying in high-Cu Al alloys for WAAM, and offers a facile strategy for developing high-performance additively manufactured aluminum alloys. © 2026

Title: Strategies of Designing High-Efficiency Electrolyte Additives for Aqueous Magnesium Batteries: A Review
Abstract: With the development of next-generation energy storage systems focusing on green, safe, and sustainable devices, aqueous magnesium (Mg)–air batteries have emerged as promising candidates owing to the intrinsic merits of the Mg metal anode, including low cost, large volumetric capacity, a highly negative electrode potential, and excellent safety. However, the high self-discharge rate and formed discharge products substantially impair the practical discharge performance of Mg anodes with poor anode utilization efficiency and low cell voltage. While anode alloying and electrolyte additive strategies can help mitigate this issue, designing highly efficient electrolyte additives that are compatible with the established anode remains a challenge. This review summarizes recent progress toward understanding the role of electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries, provides insights into the discharge mechanism of Mg-based anode materials in different types of additive-containing electrolytes, and offers strategies for designing high-efficiency mixtures of electrolyte additives. Moreover, a highly promising direction of AI-supported and robotic workflows for the future fast design of advanced electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries is discussed. Authors: Wu G.; Li W.; Duan D.; Yue D.; Luca C.; Li W.; Rong C.; Wang W.; Liu B.; Jing C.
Title: Sedimentary facies modeling driven by morphodynamic sedimentary simulation under sparse-well conditions
Abstract: Offshore oil and gas fields have become an increasingly important domain for reserve additions and production growth. However, sparse well control and limited-quality seismic data impose significant challenges to constructing high-resolution, depositionally consistent 3D geological models. Multiple-point geostatistics (MPS) can preserve complex spatial structures through training images and maintain geological realism under sparse constraints, yet the construction of representative training images is often difficult and subject to analog-based uncertainties. To address this issue, we propose a sedimentary facies modeling workflow tailored for sparse-well offshore settings. This method employs morphodynamic sedimentary modeling, in which paleo-geomorphic and hydrodynamic conditions are explicitly constrained to generate simulation outputs that honor the geological context of the target system. Based on these simulation results, more objective training images that better reflect depositional dynamics and sedimentary patterns are constructed to constrain facies modeling. By reproducing depositional mechanisms and providing geologically consistent spatial patterns, the approach significantly enhances facies prediction under limited well control and offers a new pathway for fine-scale reservoir modeling in offshore fields. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Peng Z.; Chen Z.; Li X.
Title: Elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo-Levi space
Abstract: In this paper, we study elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo–Levi space D1,p(RN), where both the constraint set and the associated energy functional depend on the unknown solution. Owing to the lack of compactness of the embedding of D1,p(RN) into the standard Lebesgue spaces, we work within an appropriate weighted Lebesgue space framework. To overcome the difficulties arising from the solution-dependent constraints, we introduce an auxiliary penalized problem, whose solvability is established by combining a surjectivity theorem, Minty’s lemma, and Kluge’s fixed-point theorem. Finally, we establish the convergence of penalized solutions and recover a solution of the original quasivariational-hemivariational inequality. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Redistribution of rock pressure and deformation of the rock mass in the Karaganda coal basin; [Қарағанды көмір бассейніндегі тау жыныстары қысымының және тау жыныстарының сілемінің деформациясының қайта таралуы]
Abstract: The study examines the redistribution of rock pressure and associated deformation processes in the Karaganda Coal Basin. It focuses on the geometry and parameters of the abutment, unloading, and disintegration zones around underground workings, and on their influence on gas-dynamic phenomena. The methodological basis combines a critical review of current geomechanical models, calculation–graphic nomograms for estimating zone width as a function of mining depth and seam thickness, and schematic construction of high-stress regions from the boundaries of the goaf at limiting angles of 75–90°. It is shown that, with increasing depth up to about 500 m, the zone configuration becomes wedge-shaped with a tendency to narrow downward, while increasing seam thickness expands the affected areas. Lithology controls the localization of hazardous zones: weakly bedded argillites and siltstones accelerate loosening and loss of stiffness, whereas stronger sandstones form dome-like stress concentrations with elevated likelihood of sudden outbursts and rockbursts. As a verification case, an episode of a sudden coal-and-gas outburst was analyzed. The observed failure boundaries are consistent with the calculated wedgeshaped high-stress zone, supporting the validity of the chosen approach within the stated assumptions. The practical significance lies in refining threshold conditions that trigger mandatory comprehensive forecasting at depths exceeding ~400 m, justifying regular instrumental monitoring to validate calculations, and adjusting barrier-pillar parameters about seam thickness and depth. The findings can be applied to the planning and safe execution of longwall and development operations under outburst-prone conditions. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: Engineering rare-earth and amorphous/crystalline interfaces for efficient H2O2 photosynthesis
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Photocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production is an environmentally friendly and safe method. However, its widespread application is hindered by challenges such as a high recombination rate of photogenerated charge carriers. In this study, we propose a strategy that combines crystalline-amorphous interface engineering with rare earth atom doping to accelerate carrier dynamics, thereby significantly enhancing ORR performance. By strategically doping Er atoms into the CdIn2S4 lattice and subsequently loading amorphous CoS onto the prepared catalyst, the resulting catalyst exhibits a significant increase in photocatalytic H2O2 activity in pure water, approximately 9.8 times higher than that of undoped CdIn2S4. The in-situ photo-Fenton effect of CS/Er-CIS achieved a degradation efficiency of up to 85%. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that the Er atom acts as act as centers for electron capture, facilitating rapid electron transfer from the bulk to the surface. Meanwhile, the crystalline-amorphous interface formed by hybridizing with amorphous CoS creates a strong built-in electric field, enhances electron conductivity, and significantly improves the adsorption/desorption kinetics of reaction intermediates. This study presents a novel strategy for improving charge carrier kinetics and highlights the promising potential of metal sulfides for future development through rational electronic structure engineering. © 2026

Authors: Masethe R.
Title: Evaluating structural controls as seismic hazard potential through joint mapping and kinematic analysis: West Rand Gold Mine, South Africa
Abstract: This study investigates the structural characteristics of joint sets and their potential influence on seismic hazard at the West Rand Gold Mine, South Africa. A total of 144 systematic 2 m × 2 m window-mapping stations were established across the Eastern and Western sections of the mine to provide representative coverage of recognised geotechnical domains. Joint orientation, persistence, and infill characteristics were recorded and analysed using stereographic projection techniques to identify dominant joint sets and assess their potential influence on shear behaviour. The results identified three major joint sets that are persistent throughout the mine, with Joint Set 1 being the most prominent overall, while Joint Set 3 is more dominant in the Western section. Approximately 45% of the mapped discontinuities were classified as random joints and were predominantly steeply dipping. Calcite was identified as the dominant infill material, indicating reduced joint shear strength and an increased susceptibility to slip. Analysis of joint orientations relative to mining face configurations suggests that mining advances parallel or semi-parallel to persistent, weakly infilled discontinuities may increase the potential for shear reactivation and mining-induced seismicity. The findings demonstrate the importance of detailed structural characterization in seismic hazard assessment, mine planning, and ground control in deep-level gold mining operations. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health
Abstract: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

Title: A Buried Sulfonate Molecular Bridge for Synchronous Charge Transport and Defect Passivation in High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
Abstract: The quality of the buried interface between the self-assembled molecules (SAM) and the perovskite layer directly governs the processes of charge carrier transport and non-radiative recombination, which ultimately dictates the efficiency and stability of the inverted perovskite solar cells. However, the simultaneous mitigation of poor SAM layer adhesion and perovskite substrate interface defects remains a significant challenge. Herein, low-cost and readily available 2‑formylbenzenesulfonic acid sodium salt (2‑FAS) is employed as a bifunctional interlayer to molecularly bridge the SAM and perovskite. The benzene ring of 2‑FAS interacts via π–π stacking with the SAM, strengthening adhesion and promoting hole transfer, while its sulfonate group (-SO3−) coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and passivate surface defects. As a result, the 2-FAS-modified devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.21%, with a significant fill factor of 86.15%. Furthermore, Na+ from 2‑FAS occupies A‑site vacancies in the perovskite lattice, which effectively suppresses ion migration and phase transition, thereby enhancing structural integrity. Benefiting from these combined effects, unencapsulated devices retain over 90% of their initial PCE after 4500 h of storage in a nitrogen atmosphere, demonstrating exceptional long-term stability. Authors: Maticka M.J.
Title: Wholesale electricity market pricing model design: Layering the transparency
Abstract: The energy transition is challenging traditional wholesale electricity market pricing models. Divergences in modelling outcomes hinder comparisons across regional studies, often attributed to variations in model designs and data availability. This is further complicated by theoretical model designs that are insufficiently aligned with real-world constraints, such as limited access to market data, confidential information, or high-quality datasets.Rather than building a market model and then rummaging for suitable datasets, this study inverts the approach and layers data into the model design.The framework was applied in a longitudinal study across three study regions, Alberta (AESO), California (CAISO), and Western Australia (WEM), which have experienced high growth in renewable generation. The technical implementation employed a broad range of established machine learning methods (OLS, MARS, ANN, GAMLSS, XGBoost) alongside a structured probabilistic approach (Bayesian Belief Networks). The approach was found to be feasible as several models consistently provided the optimal design across regions and configurations implemented, as such supporting the assertion that models could be designed, configured and compared using this layered approach.Matching model complexity to all available data should serve as a guide, since higher-performing models do not necessarily require access to extensive datasets. Finally, cross-market comparisons showed that different market characteristics had a greater influence on model accuracy, illustrating that real-world data constraints need to guide model development. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A framework for transmission line ice thickness prediction integrating physics-informed feature engineering, attention networks, and causal inference
Abstract: Accurate prediction of ice thickness on transmission lines is essential for effective anti-icing and de-icing strategies. Existing methods predominantly rely on "black-box" models lacking physical interpretability, and correlation analysis alone cannot distinguish direct causal effects from mediated transmission among meteorological factors. This paper proposes a three-layer progressive analytical framework for high-altitude heavy-icing sites that integrates physics-informed feature engineering, an attention-based prediction network, and causal inference, progressively addressing prediction accuracy, feature-level interpretability, and causal mechanism discovery. A key finding is the synergistic effect between physics-informed feature engineering and the attention mechanism—neither component alone improves prediction accuracy, yet their combination yields a significant performance gain, with the proposed model achieving competitive performance among deep learning methods. Computational analysis further shows that the proposed model achieves a compact parameter count (12,321) and 40× faster inference than Random Forest, while providing interpretability. SHAP cross-model consistency analysis identifies humidity-related features as the dominant predictors across architecturally distinct models, a conclusion driven by data patterns rather than model bias. Causal inference further reveals that humidity exhibits a nonlinear inverted-U effect on ice thickness (peak at ∼82% RH), temperature serves as a necessary threshold condition, and wind speed exerts a modest direct effect (+0.21 mm/(m/s)) that is not mediated by temperature or humidity. These findings provide a scientific basis for a three-tier icing early-warning framework—temperature gating, humidity severity assessment, and wind intensification—rather than relying on temperature alone. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li W.; Zhao Z.; He Y.; Wang W.; Zhang Y.; Yang X.; Zheng Y.; Gao J.; Li S.
Title: A geology-guided GBDT–BiSSM framework for carbonate reservoir classification from well logs
Abstract: Accurate reservoir classification is essential for the efficient development of carbonate hydrocarbon reservoirs. Strong heterogeneity, complex diagenetic alteration, and overlapping well-log responses make this task difficult in the low-porosity and low-permeability Jialingjiang Formation of the central Sichuan Basin. To address this challenge, a GBDT-BiSSM fusion framework is proposed by integrating gradient boosting decision trees with a multiscale bidirectional state-space model. GBDT extracts static discriminative information from multivariate logging responses, whereas BiSSM learns depth-dependent contextual representations from ordered well-log sequences to characterize vertical variations and boundary-related transitions. Geological information is not embedded as an explicit constraint in the model-training process; instead, the fused predictions are refined during inference using geological-consistency decoding based on reservoir thickness, evaporite-related responses, and vertical reservoir continuity. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an overall classification accuracy of 92.9% and effectively reduces isolated label fluctuations and the misclassification of thin reservoirs. The method provides an effective approach for the detailed delineation of low-porosity and low-permeability carbonate reservoirs and the prediction of high-quality reservoir intervals. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Chen H.; Yuan C.; Wang K.; Yang L.; Feng T.; Tian Z.; Li Y.; Fan X.; Tang J.; Dai Y.; Guo X.; Cui R.
Title: Localized-state sensitization and coordination-environment modulation enhance Tm3+ near-infrared luminescence in a rare-earth double perovskite: Imaging and hierarchical optical encryption
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites combine low toxicity, structural tunability, and good dopant compatibility, making them important host materials for rare-earth near-infrared luminescence. However, the weak 4f–4f absorption of rare-earth ions limits near-infrared output under near-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we report a multiband Cs2NaGdCl6 phosphor co-doped with Sb3+ and Tm3+. Under near-ultraviolet excitation, the material simultaneously produces self-trapped exciton emission at 463 nm and characteristic Tm3+ emissions at 808, 1222, and 1432 nm, with the near-infrared internal quantum efficiency reaching 47.41%. Sb3+ increases the internal quantum efficiency of the host from 0.72% to 90.91%. The 1G4 level of Tm3+ serves as an energy bridge, enabling a maximum Sb3+→Tm3+ energy-transfer efficiency of 62.64%. Density functional theory calculations show that Tm3+ doping barely alters the band-edge structure of Cs2NaGdCl6, whereas Sb 5s/5p–Cl 3p hybridization creates localized states within the band gap that account for the enhanced near-ultraviolet absorption. Sb3+ also induces local charge rearrangement and octahedral distortion, reducing the local symmetry of [TmCl6]3− and thereby favoring a higher radiative probability for Tm3+ 4f–4f transitions. The packaged near-infrared phosphor-converted light-emitting diode enables clear night-vision and transmission imaging. By exploiting the similar visible luminescence of the series of samples and their differing responses to excitation wavelength and detection window, we also constructed a dual-gated platform for hierarchical dynamic optical information encryption. These results reveal the dual role of Sb3+ in near-ultraviolet photosensitization and regulation of the local coordination environment of Tm3+, and demonstrate the use of emission spanning the visible, near-infrared-I, and near-infrared-II regions in multi-scenario imaging and hierarchical optical information encryption. © 2026

Authors: Chang S.C.; Fendy N.A.; Shoparwe N.F.; Yusoff A.H.
Title: Geochemical Partitioning and Correlation of Rare Earth Elements, Thorium, and Uranium in Ion-Adsorption Clays from the Gemang Area, West Kelantan, Malaysia; [Геманг аймағы, Батыс Келантан, Малайзиядағы ион-адсорбциялық саздардағы сирек жер элементтерінің, торий мен уранның геохимиялық бөлінуі және корреляциясы]; [Геохимическое распределение и корреляция редкоземельных элементов, тория и урана в ионно-адсорбционных глинах района Геманг, Западный Келантан, Малайзия]
Abstract: This study aimed to determine the geochemical partitioning of total rare earth elements (ΣREE), thorium (Th), and uranium (U) in ion-adsorption clays (IACs) from the Gemang area, West Kelantan, Malaysia, and to evaluate how this partitioning may influence selective REE recovery with limited radionuclide mobilisation. An eight-step sequential extraction procedure was applied to representative saprolitic IAC samples, and the extracted fractions were analysed by ICP-OES. Pearson correlation analysis and principal component analysis (PCA) were further used to examine associations among ΣREE, Th, U, and selected major elements. The sequential extraction results showed that ΣREE were concentrated mainly in the ion-exchangeable fraction (average 22.0%), with additional contributions from the residual fraction (15.3%) and a notably high proportion in the primary sulphide step (53.4%). In contrast, Th and U were concentrated mainly in the primary sulphide fraction (54.4% and 41.3%, respectively) and the residual fraction (26.2% and 45.0%, respectively). Major elements such as Al, Fe, Mn, Ca, and Na showed distributions consistent with clay, oxide, and refractory mineral hosts. Statistical analysis indicated a positive association between ΣREE and Ca-Na, whereas Th and U were more closely associated with Fe-Mn-bearing fractions, indicating different host controls and different mobilisation behaviour. These results suggest that a recoverable REE pool is present in the exchangeable fraction, while most Th and U remain in less labile phases under the tested operational scheme. The study therefore provides geochemical evidence that mild ammonium-salt leaching may favour selective REE recovery from Gemang IACs while limiting the release of naturally occurring radioactive materials, although further mineralogical validation and dynamic leaching tests are still required. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Authors: Cui J.; Zhou C.; Lu X.; Lei S.; Wang P.; Tian D.; Sun R.; Hu Y.
Title: Surface-metallized microvia arrays empower omnidirectional conductive films with exceptional electromagnetic interference shielding and heat dissipation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Against the ongoing trend toward lightweight electronic packaging, conventional electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials, typically based on bulk metals or highly filled composites, struggle to simultaneously achieve low density, mechanical compliance, and structural resilience. Here, we develop a microvia-engineered metallization strategy to enable efficient EMI shielding at low metal loading. Specifically, a styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS) film is patterned with a controlled array of microvias, followed by in situ silver deposition on both the surface and microvia walls to construct a continuous 3D conductive network (denoted as TSV-Ag). Notably, the metallized microvia array does not deteriorate shielding in the X-band; instead, it produces a net increase in EMI shielding performance, delivering a shielding effectiveness of 66.35 dB in the X-band at an Ag volume fraction of only 0.58 vol.%. Moreover, the flexible SBS matrix suggests potential utility for gasket applications, and the microvia structure also provides additional pathways for heat transfer across the film thickness. These results indicate that microvia-enabled 3D conductive networks provide a viable route to decouple metal loading from shielding performance, offering a scalable design strategy for mechanically adaptive and thermally functional EMI shielding materials. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Authors: Zhou F.; Ma Y.; Zhao W.; Zhang L.; Chen Y.; Sheng X.
Title: Layer-by-layer assembled flexible phase-change/photothermal composite films for dual-mode thermal management
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing phase change composite films with high thermal conductivity and robust mechanical flexibility is crucial for preventing thermal failure in electronic devices. Herein, we prepared a flexible multilayer phase change composite film (APM) with a layer-by-layer (LBL) structure to create an anisotropically thermally conductive dual-mode thermal management system by integrating reversible phase transitions with sustainable solar heating. Firstly, the microencapsulated phase change material (MPCM) and Ag-modified MPCM (Ag@MPCM) were prepared by in-situ polymerization and modification. Subsequently, the APM composite materials were fabricated via the LBL assembly technique, comprising alternating layers of MXene-poly(vinyl alcohol) (denoted as the P layer) and Ag@MPCM-MXene-sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (denoted as the N layer). Specifically, the continuous P layers govern ultra-fast in-plane thermal conduction (1.7447 W m−1 K−1) to rapidly eliminate localized hotspots, while the N layers achieve remarkable heat storage ability (104.91 J g−1). This unique decoupled synergy empowers the APM to effectively manage and buffer transient thermal shocks in electronic devices. The resulting APM exhibited excellent thermal durability, remarkable tensile strength (10.82 MPa), and achieved a favorable photothermal conversion efficiency (96%). Overall, the developed APM demonstrated considerable potential for highly efficient solar energy utilization and advanced electronic thermal management. © 2026
