Authors: Lv J.; Li W.; Li Z.; Guo L.; Zhao J.; Li Y.; Li J.; Li T.; Fu Y.; Zhang J.; Zhang Y.; Li H.
Title: Phase-stability engineering of oxide scales in multicomponent (Hf,Zr,Sc)B2 coatings for durable cyclic ablation resistance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The growing demand for reusable thermal protection systems calls for ceramic coatings that can retain protective oxide scales under repeated ultra-high-temperature ablation. However, conventional ultra-high-temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings often fail under thermal cycling because their HfO2/ZrO2-dominated oxide scales suffer phase-transformation-induced cracking and delamination. Here, we address this limitation by incorporating Sc into multicomponent (Hf,Zr,Sc)B2 solid-solution coatings to engineer oxide-scale phase stability. The optimized coating containing 10 mol% Sc maintains scale integrity after 6 × 120 s exposures at temperatures above 2300 °C and exhibits a negative linear recession rate of −0.11 μm s−1. Multiscale characterization of the resulting oxide scale reveals partial tetragonal-to-monoclinic martensitic transformation within parent tetragonal grains, producing monoclinic laths while retaining Sc-stabilized metastable tetragonal domains and thereby limiting the overall transformation-induced volumetric strain. These tetragonal domains are preferentially retained at grain boundaries and triple junctions along intergranular crack paths, a spatial distribution consistent with transformation-associated crack tolerance. These findings establish phase-stability engineering of oxide scales as an effective strategy for maintaining scale integrity and protecting high-temperature structural materials under repeated extreme thermal exposure. © 2026

Title: Integrated probabilistic framework for long-term solar resource reliability assessment for photovoltaic planning at provincial capitals in Sumatra
Abstract: Reliable solar resource assessment requires consideration of both expected performance and associated uncertainty, particularly under heterogeneous climatic conditions. This study develops an integrated probabilistic framework for evaluating long-term solar resource reliability at ten provincial-capital reference locations across Sumatra, Indonesia. Satellite-derived hourly global horizontal irradiance data from 2015 to 2024 were temporally integrated to obtain daily global horizontal irradiation and analysed through climatological characterisation, probabilistic photovoltaic yield estimation, composite reliability assessment, multidimensional pattern recognition, and Bayesian hierarchical inference. Because the hourly observations were integrated into daily totals, the analysis characterises variability among daily irradiation values over the 2015–2024 period and does not resolve intraday fluctuations. Mean daily irradiation varied only moderately among the analysed locations, whereas temporal variability and photovoltaic yield uncertainty differed substantially. Median annual photovoltaic yield ranged from approximately 1330 to 1474 kWh/kWp/year, showing that locations with similar mean irradiation can exhibit markedly different long-term reliability characteristics. A composite reliability index combining normalised scores derived from temporal variability, annual photovoltaic yield spread, and resource magnitude ranged from approximately 0.15 to 0.80. The Bengkulu and Lampung reference locations obtained the two highest index values, whereas the Riau Islands reference location obtained the lowest. Bayesian hierarchical modelling quantified uncertainty in the location-level reliability estimates and generated partially pooled posterior estimates, thereby supporting more cautious interpretation of extreme deterministic scores. The framework provides a transparent and reproducible basis for preliminary comparative screening and for prioritising locations for detailed ground measurements and techno-economic assessment. The empirical findings are specific to the analysed locations in Sumatra; application to other tropical regions requires independent validation using locally representative and spatially distributed data. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Numerical and Experimental investigation on a new tube design featuring micro-finned tubes with broken double V-cut twisted tapes
Abstract: Achieving high thermal efficiency remains a key challenge in the design of absorber tubes. As a result, the thermohydraulic performance of a newly proposed absorber tube, featuring finned tubes with broken double-V-cut twisted tapes, was investigated using Thermohydraulic performance factor analysis. The numerical and experimental study evaluated five key parameters: the number of V-cuts (2, 4, 6), the number of twisted tapes (2, 5, 8), the thickness of twisted tapes (0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5 mm), the width of the twisted tape (6, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8 mm), and the twist ratio in the twisted tapes (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1). Authors: Li B.; Yan T.; Yuan X.; Cui S.; Liang H.; Zhang L.; Chen M.; Cheng X.
Title: Lightweight Ti-matrix composites reinforced by graphene-derived TiCx showing superior strain-hardening capacity and strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Lightweight Ti-matrix composites (Ti-MCs) have long exhibited strain softening and low ductility due to localized deformation, which has limited their application in the aerospace industry. In this study, a graphene-derived TiCx-mediated microstructural design strategy is developed for Ti-6Al-4V matrix composites. During processing, graphene is converted in-situ into uniformly dispersed and fragmentable TiCx. Hot rolling induces nanoscale amorphous bands at fragmented TiCx contacts, while subsequent water quenching promotes a refined hierarchical α′-Ti martensitic network. During deformation, TiCx can effectively transfer load and, as a strong obstacle phase, promotes the activation of multiple slip systems in the matrix. Meanwhile, the hierarchical α′-Ti evolves from a dislocation source into an effective barrier, markedly enhancing the deformation resistance of the Ti-MCs. In addition, the amorphous bands mitigate stress concentration, and the widespread activation of <c+a> dislocations delays strain localization, which is beneficial for plastic deformation of the Ti-MCs. The proposed processing route and synergistic deformation mechanism provide practical pathways for designing damage-tolerant, lightweight Ti-MCs. © 2026

Authors: Tai H.; Chen X.; Yu Y.; Sun Z.; Zhu P.; Cao P.; Wang F.; Li Q.
Title: Toughening strategies for additively manufactured ceramics: A multiscale review of mechanisms and process-structure-property relationships
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the fabrication of complex ceramic components unachievable by traditional methods. However, AM process-induced defects aggravate ceramic brittleness, the core bottleneck restricting its industrial application. Existing reviews on AM ceramic toughening have three critical unaddressed gaps, including no quantitative criterion to distinguish synergistic toughening from linear additive effects, no clear mapping between AM process constraints and multi-mechanism synergy compatibility, and no systematic summary of synergy failure mechanisms, negative cases, and research pitfalls. To fill these gaps, this review establishes a unified academic definition and quantitative evaluation system for multiscale synergistic toughening of AM ceramics, assesses the compatibility between toughening mechanisms and mainstream AM processes, dissects core synergy coupling mechanisms and quantifies their efficiency, analyzes synergy failure boundaries and industrialization bottlenecks, and proposes a phased, industry-aligned technical roadmap with quantifiable milestones to guide full-cycle engineering application of high-toughness AM ceramics. © 2026

Title: Systems metabolic engineering of a plasmid-free Escherichia coli cell factory for high-level cytidine production
Abstract: Cytidine is an important precursor for nucleoside pharmaceuticals, but its fermentative production is constrained by competing degradation, poor selectivity of pyrimidine flux, insufficient precursor supply, and energy-redox imbalance. In this study, a plasmid-free E. coli cell factory was constructed through systems metabolic engineering. Sequential deletion of cytidine degradation, salvage, and precursor-consuming pathways enabled initial cytidine accumulation. The conversion from UMP to CMP was strengthened by introducing feedback-deregulated pyrH D93A and pyrG D160E, E162A, E168Kcgl mutants and nudG , while the heterologous expression of PHM8 sce improved CMP-to-cytidine conversion selectivity. Scaffold-based assembly of PyrF, PyrHD93A, NudG, and PHM8sce using CipA/CipB further improved local pathway channeling and reduced uridine formation by 98.70%. To reinforce upstream flux, de novo UMP biosynthesis was reconstructed with the B. subtilis pyr operon, PRPP synthesis was enhanced, and nitrogen-donor and pyrimidine-ring precursor supply was improved through glnA , ppc , and aspC expression. Finally, an ATP-responsive ydaO motif regulatory module was used to dynamically control respiratory-chain and oxygen-utilization modules, coordinating ATP supply with NAD+ regeneration. The final strain cyt 23 produced 96.20 g/L cytidine in 50 h in a 5 L fed-batch bioreactor, with a glucose conversion yield of 0.38 g/g and productivity of 1.92 g/(L·h), representing the highest reported titer, yield and productivity for microbial cytidine production to date. This work provides an integrated strategy for high-level microbial cytidine production and nucleoside cell-factory development. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Peng C.; Li H.; Zhang Y.; Bo K.; Qiao G.
Title: Prediction and optimization of drill string torque and drag in horizontal wells based on dynamic friction coefficient testing
Abstract: With the large-scale development of unconventional oil and gas resources, extended-reach horizontal wells have been increasingly utilized in shale reservoirs. However, excessive torque and drag caused by drillstring–wellbore contact can reduce weight-on-bit transfer efficiency, limit horizontal-section extension, and increase the risk of drilling complications. A major source of uncertainty in conventional torque-and-drag prediction is the use of a constant friction coefficient, which cannot adequately represent the dynamic friction behavior under different drilling modes and water-based drilling fluid lubrication. In this study, dynamic friction coefficient tests were conducted for steel–shale, steel–sandstone, and steel–steel contact pairs under water-based drilling fluid lubrication. The effects of lithology, sliding velocity, rotational speed, and normal load on the friction coefficient were investigated. Based on the experimental results, a velocity-dependent dynamic friction coefficient model was established and incorporated into a three-dimensional stiff-string torque-and-drag prediction model. The additional contact force induced by drillstring buckling was also considered to improve the calculation of normal contact force in highly deviated and horizontal sections. Field verification was performed using the J-H1 Well in the Ordos Basin and ZH-5 Well in the Sichuan Basin. For the J-H1 Well, the proposed model reduced the hook-load prediction error to 6.5% under sliding drilling and 5.9% under composite drilling, and reduced the wellhead torque prediction error to 8.5%. For the ZH-5 Well, the relative errors of hook-load and wellhead torque prediction were 5.0% and 8.2%, respectively, which were significantly lower than those obtained using the conventional constant-friction-coefficient model. The model was further applied to the J-H2 Well to evaluate the effects of trajectory control tools, weight on bit, rotational speed, lubricants, and drilling modes on torque and drag, drillstring buckling, and horizontal-section extension capability. The results show that the proposed dynamic-friction-coefficient model provides more reliable friction inputs for torque-and-drag prediction under water-based drilling fluid lubrication and can support drilling-parameter optimization in extended-reach horizontal wells. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Continelli E.; Haskovec J.; Pignotti C.
Title: Consensus and flocking with transmission and reaction delays
Abstract: We investigate consensus formation and flocking behavior in multi-agent systems subject to two distinct types of delay: a transmission delay accounting for information exchange between agents, and a reaction delay representing the processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simplified linear two-agent system, we analyze how these delays affect asymptotic stability. We then derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi-agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. These conditions require the delays to be sufficiently small relative to the initial data and the decay rate of the influence function. The analysis is based on a Lyapunov functional approach combined with a Grönwall–Halanay-type inequality. Our results establish rigorous sufficient conditions under which collective behavior emerges in delayed multi-agent systems where both communication and reaction lags are non-negligible, with applications to biological, social, and engineered systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Electric current generation in bacterial isolates from river sediments using microbial fuel cell
Source title: Advances in Biomarker Sciences and Technology
Abstract: Microbial fuel cell (MFC) represents a total approach to converting organic matter to sustainable and clean energy. This study investigated the electricity production potentials of bacteria isolated from the sediment of some Rivers at various depths using microbial fuel cells. Samples were taken from River Ala, Ogbese, and Owena at surface water, sediment surface, 50 cm, 100 cm, and 150 cm (depths) using a soil auger. Bacterial population, isolation, and identification of sediments at various depths were determined using microbiological techniques. Pure cultured, Co-cultured, and mixed bacterial isolates of some bacteria isolated from the sediment were used in the current generation. A double-chamber microbial fuel cell was constructed for these bacterial isolates and current, voltage, and resistance readings were taken for 12 days. The current and voltage generated increased in the earlier days of the experiment and decreased in the latter days while the resistance readings were high throughout the experiment. Bacillus pumilus generated the highest current of 0.47 mA and Pseudomonas aeruginosa generated the highest voltage of 1.85V for the pure cultured MFC chamber. In the co-isolated and mixed cultured MFC chamber, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Bacillus pumilus generated the highest current of 1.18 mA and the highest voltage of 1.16 V. Therefore, it is shown that bacteria isolate from river can be used to generate microbial fuel cell which could be a promising technologies to generate electric power in a large scale electric power generation. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Assessing salinity intrusion risk from coastal flooding through a spatial multi-criteria approach in Satkhira district of Bangladesh
Abstract: Bangladesh's coastal zones face compounding threats from climate change, sea-level rise, and the resulting intensification of salinity intrusion, critically jeopardizing freshwater security, agriculture, and local livelihoods. This study presents a spatial multi-criteria analysis using a Geographic Information System (GIS) integrated with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to systematically assess and map the hazard, vulnerability, and exposure dimensions driving flood-induced salinity intrusion risk in Satkhira District. The comprehensive assessment utilized 17 thematic criteria, revealing distinct spatial patterns of susceptibility. The Hazard analysis demonstrated that 35.21% of the total area is classified under the combined High and Very High zones, predominantly concentrated in the south-western and south-eastern coastal areas. The biophysical vulnerability assessment indicated a high degree of intrinsic sensitivity, with 36.59% of the district categorized as very highly vulnerable. Conversely, the Exposure analysis identified a substantial 28.19% of the land as highly and very highly exposed, reflecting the high density of valuable assets even in inland Upazilas. The final composite risk map reveals that 27.95% of the study area is subjected to either high or very high salinity intrusion risk, with the highest risk observed in Satkhira sadar. These empirically derived risk maps and quantitative findings offer crucial, evidence-based insights for policymakers, providing a foundational tool for the design and implementation of targeted adaptation strategies, sustainable land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction programs in vulnerable deltaic environments globally. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Rastvorova I.I.; Dvoynikov V.M.
Title: Dynamic Load Recovery in Hydraulic Force Sensors via Frequency-Domain Signal Separation and Inertia-Damping Correction
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This study presents an analysis of existing solutions for measuring dynamic loads and introduces an approach for reconstructing dynamic loads from hydraulic force sensor data, that accounts for the sensor's physical and structural characteristics. A mathematical model is proposed that relates the applied force to the measured fluid pressure while incorporating damping and inertia effects. It is demonstrated that parasitic high-frequency waves caused by resonant processes in the fluid column and forced oscillations of the piston and fluid can be separated from the desired signal through spectral analysis. To isolate the mechanical component of pressure, frequency-domain harmonic selection is employed, followed by signal decomposition into Gaussian functions and envelope-based correction, accounting for inertia and damping. The validity of the approach is confirmed by numerical simulation of wave processes in the sensor chamber and laboratory experiments involving impact loads generated by a conical striker in free fall from various heights. A comparison of the reconstructed signals with reference signals obtained using a grapho-analytical method shows excellent agreement. Pearson's correlation coefficient was 0.951 and mean squared error was 0.0107. The relative deviation of the total transmitted impulse from the theoretical value is less than 0.02%. © 2027 The author(s). Title: The impact of ideality assumption on biomethane upgrading model
Abstract: While most research rely on ideal-gas assumptions without ensuring their accuracy, simulation of adsorption-based biomethane upgrading can lower experimental costs and enhance process analysis. In the current age of decarbonization and clean energy, biomethane has gained attention as a promising renewable energy source. Biomethane is a reliable and sustainable fuel source. This work focuses on biomethane upgrading by the adsorption process. Effect of pressure, temperature on adsorbent breakthrough and saturation time were examined. Four different adsorbents silica gel, activated carbon, carbon molecular sieve, and 13X zeolite were investigated. The effects of model assumptions in regard to adsorbate ideality was also investigated. The results show that adsorption pressure is the main factor influencing the responses coinciding with the process being pressure dominated. Breakthrough time increased by up to 58% when pressure was increased from 2 to 15 bar, but it fell by around 10% when temperature was raised from 25 to 45 °C. The design models for breakthrough and saturation time obtained R2 values of 0.986 to 1, and simulated breakthrough curves corresponded with data from the literature, with R2 values ranging from 0.95 to 0.99. The ideal equation of state assumptions were reliable up to 20 bars. Beyond this point the model is more sensitive to assumptions as the adsorbate reacts non-ideally. This research helps shed light on underreported aspects of biomethane modelling and help provides more reliable frameworks for process assumptions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Technological Assurance of the Quality of Slide Bearing Shells Based on Two-Stage Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: The article describes the methodology of a two-stage finishing process for slide bearing shells made of bronze. The goal of the first finishing stage was to form a base roughness profile with uniform values of the controlled parameters. Based on the results of the first stage, regression equations were derived. These equations make it possible to evaluate the effectiveness of the influence of the process variable factors (tool rotational speed, feed rate, processing time, and workpiece diameter values) of magnetic abrasive finishing on the value of the controlled parameters. The results showed that the parameters of tool rotational speed and processing time have the greatest influence. In the second stage of the experimental research, a two-factor experiment (varying the time and abrasive grain sizes) was conducted. The aim of this stage was to test the possibility of applying oil-retaining grooves onto the formed profile. The results showed that the most noticeable grooves are formed at a processing time of 6 minutes and an abrasive grain size of 350 µm. The roughness parameters did not increase significantly compared to the values after the first processing stage. The need for further research to evaluate the operational characteristics of the machined workpieces during wear testing is established. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: Xie S.; Zeng Z.; Xu J.; Pan Y.; Li R.; Yuan T.
Title: Constitutive modeling of the BCC-FCC transformation-affected powder densification controlled by diffusion and creep of the Al0.7CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys during spark plasma sintering
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The precise construction of the densification model of spark plasma sintering (SPS) is the theoretical basis for the preparation of high-performance materials and guidance of process parameters. Diffusion and creep are the two dominant mechanisms responsible for powder densification during SPS. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) prefer sintering temperatures in the ranges accompanying the beneficial phase transformation to obtain satisfying structural properties. However, it brings difficulty in the study of densification kinetics as none of the current models consider the phase transformation and, as a result, reduces the accuracy in describing both diffusion- and creep-dominant densification of HEAs in SPS. Thus, a new constitutive model considering the effect of phase transformation on densification is proposed in this study. The transformed phase volume fraction is determined according to the nucleation and growth model, and Taylor expansion is introduced in the calculation of the convolution integral in the model during the heating period. After the transformed fraction is obtained, the chemical compositions in the retained parent phase are computed based on the conservation of matter. Subsequently, the contribution of atomic diffusion to densification as a function of the transformed fraction under the electromigration effect is obtained. Furthermore, the grain size of the parent and daughter phases as a function of the transformed fraction is determined utilizing the grain growth model. The final model is obtained by substituting the functional relations between atomic diffusion, grain growth, and phase transformation into the densification model framework consisting of diffusion and creep. © 2026

Title: Designing a Data-Driven E-Learning Module for Teaching English to Young Learners: Integrating Needs Analysis and the ISAV Learning Model
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study designed a data-driven e-learning module for Teaching English to Young Learners by integrating needs analysis with the Interactive, Somatic, Auditory, and Visual learning model. Using a design-based research approach, the study focused on the analysis and design phases. Data were collected from elementary school English teachers and pre-service English teachers through a structured questionnaire addressing necessities, lacks, and wants. The findings identified vocabulary, reading, and oral communication as key learning necessities, alongside difficulties in sentence structure and broader instructional constraints. Respondents also preferred interactive and multimodal learning activities. These findings informed an ISAV-based e-learning module prototype integrating interactive, somatic, auditory, and visual features to support learner-centered, multimodal, and contextually responsive English instruction for young learners in digital environments. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Authors: Yan Z.; Zhang B.; Li X.
Title: Effect of grain size and thermal annealing on the mechanical and superconducting properties of nanograined Nb-47wt.%Ti alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: To investigate the effects of grain refinement on the superconducting properties (critical temperature (Tc), critical current density (Jc), and upper critical field (Hc2)) and mechanical properties of Nb-47wt.%Ti superconducting alloys, bulk samples with grain sizes from micrometers down to 19 nm were fabricated via high-pressure torsion. Microstructural refinement led to a continuous increase in hardness, while the superconducting properties exhibited a non-monotonic dependence on grain size. An optimal grain size of ∼55 nm exhibited a high Jc of ∼30.9 kA/cm2 (4.2 K, 5 T), a hardness of 2.9 GPa, and a well-retained Tc of 8.63 K. For the 55-nm-grained sample, subsequent annealing at 400 °C resulted in slight grain coarsening to ∼85 nm and simultaneous precipitation of nano-sized α-Ti precipitates. This composite structure endows the samples with better matching of strength and superconducting properties: a hardness of 3 GPa, a Tc of 9.19 K, and a Jc of ∼32 kA/cm2 (4.2 K, 5 T). This work provides insights into designing high-strength superconducting metallic materials. © 2026

Authors: Zhao Y.; Li Q.; Lv Y.; Zhang S.; Jiang K.; Xu M.; Muhammad M.; Wang Y.; Ren Y.; Zhao Y.; Sun X.
Title: Atomic High-Spin Cobalt Unlocks Reversible Multi-Electron Transfer Chemistry for Superb Aqueous Zn-Mn Batteries
Abstract: To settle inherent irreversible phase transition and motivate re-dissolution of deposited “dead” MnO2 without acid and redox mediator addition, we introduced atomic-dispersed Co atoms with high-spin state into layered MnO2, denoted as Co–MnO2, via an in situ topological phase transformation strategy, thereby unlocking reversible multi-electron transfer chemistry for superb Zn–Mn batteries. Specifically, atomic-distributed Co atoms within Co–MnO2 effectively modulate [MnO6] octahedral symmetry and reduce Co–O bond covalency along with enhanced lattice oxygen activity. Based on this, high-spin Co (t2g4eg2) greatly mitigates the Jahn–Teller distortion as well as promotes electrolytic MnO2 deposited onto the cathode surface completely converted from adsorbed Mn2+ for inhibited “Mn dendrites”, achieving reversible MnO2/Mn3+ and electrolytic MnO2/Mn2+ reactions with highly thermodynamical favorability. Benefiting from the “two-step, three-electron” mechanism triggered by high-spin Co, Zn//Co–MnO2 battery delivers an outstanding capacity of 658 mAh g–1 and ultra-long lifespan over 15,000 cycles. This work reveals the critical role of transition-metal spin state modulation for energy-dense and durable Zn-MnO2 batteries with reversible multi-electron storage mechanisms. Title: A real time simulation of rule-based energy management system for PV array and battery bank using OPAL-RT with ARTEMIS technique
Abstract: A nano-grid is a power distribution system comprising several energy sources. However, the intermittent nature of photovoltaic energy sources and the uncertainty of load demands are major challenges in efficient and reliable nano-grid operations. As such, this study addresses gaps in real-time energy management for nano-grid system based on short-term dynamic validation by proposing a rule-based energy management system for real-time power flow control to maintain the stability and power balance of nano-grid system. Real-time simulations, via the OPAL-RT platform, specifically the OP5700 test bench, was used to validate the performance of the proposed rule-based energy management system. Furthermore, the researchers used the ARTEMiS optimization technique to carry out real-time activities in a multi-converter framework. This technique categorises the nano-grid system into four independent subsystems and pre-calculates the state-space matrices for the different switching topologies, thereby eliminating the computationally expensive matrix processes, which lead to execution overruns. The proposed rule-based energy management system was utilized to manage local controllers, namely, converters and inverters. The rule-based energy management system was responsible for making critical decisions regarding real-time power distribution, load balancing, and system stability, while the local controllers implemented the directives. This technique was used for testing the four operating scenarios, which included dynamic load requirements, variable photovoltaic generation, and grid interaction modes. The results of all the experiments indicated that the rule-based energy management system displayed a zero computational overrun, with a primary computation time of 8.84 μs, 48.48% CPU utilization, and communication latency less than 1 s. This study has addressed the crucial gap between theoretical energy management system designs and fully operational control systems by conducting a real-time validation of a rule-based energy management system technique specifically designed for nano-grid system based on the OPAL-RT platform with ARTEMiS optimization. The results provide reference real-time performance benchmarks relevant to short-term feasibility evaluation of energy management strategies for small-scale renewable energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Anomalous strength inversion in multiphase ceramic joining: When the joint outperforms the base ceramic
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: In the field of ceramic/metal brazing, the joint strength is conventionally regarded as limited by the strength of the ceramic base material. However, an anomalous phenomenon challenging this perception was observed in the brazing of Y2O3−MgO multiphase ceramic to TC4 alloy. After undergoing the same heat treatment, the strength of the Y2O3−MgO ceramic was found to be lower than that of the Y2O3−MgO/TC4 brazed joint within a certain temperature range. This study investigated the joining of Y2O3−MgO/TC4 using various fillers and elucidated the intrinsic mechanism of this phenomenon through systematic microstructural characterization. Results show that this “strength inversion” phenomenon is attributed to the Ag-based plastic phase induced by the substitutional solid solution of In at the brazing interface. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) and transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) confirm that the rigid constraints of MgO within the ceramic trigger significant stress concentration, while the Ag plastic phase at the interface can alleviate residual stress through plastic deformation, thereby enhancing the joint strength. Consequently, this work reveals the anomalous mechanism where the base material strength is not the upper limit in multiphase ceramic brazing, providing novel strategies and insights for breaking through the strength limits of multiphase ceramic joints. © 2026

Title: Photothermal Superhydrophobic Textiles: An Emerging Paradigm from Passive Water Repellency to Active Thermal Management
Abstract: Photothermal superhydrophobic textiles represent an emerging paradigm integrating active light-driven functionality with passive liquid repellency. While previous reviews treated superhydrophobicity and photothermal effects in isolation, this work pioneers a systematic analysis of their synergistic interplay—a critical, underexplored mechanism where superhydrophobicity preserves photothermal efficiency by minimizing water-induced heat loss, while photothermal activity prevents surface fouling that compromises non-wetting performance. Through detailed case studies of advanced material systems, this review highlights how this synergy supports significant advancements in adaptive wearable technology, energy-efficient infrastructure, and eco-friendly water treatment. This review presents an original “lab-to-life” roadmap that structurally links material design to durability assessment, environmental impact evaluation, and scalable manufacturing strategies—a holistic framework absent in existing literature. The review emphasizes urgent sustainability priorities including green material substitutions, non-toxic solvent processing methodologies, and circular design principles aligned with global environmental regulations. By connecting fundamental mechanisms to real-world deployment scenarios while outlining transformative future directions such as AI-accelerated material discovery, stimulus-responsive systems, and intelligent manufacturing protocols, this work provides a timely and actionable reference for advancing next-generation textiles toward technological sophistication and practical viability in sustainable development. Title: Flowsheet Design and Modelling for High Purity Praseodymium and Neodymium by Solvent Extraction; [Еріткішпен экстракциялау арқылы жоғары тазалықтағы празеодим мен неодимді алудың технологиялық схемасын әзірлеу және модельдеу]; [Разработка и моделирование технологической схемы получения высокочистого празеодима и неодима методом экстракции растворителем]
Abstract: Purifying rare earth elements (REEs) from ion-adsorbed clay (IAC) deposits demands complex solvent extraction (SX) setups to achieve commercial-grade purity. This study presents the design and validation of a four-train counter-current SX flowsheet for processing a pre-treated REE chloride liquor sourced from Malaysia’s Jeli deposit. Using an iterative steady-state mass-balance simulation in Microsoft Excel, the research determines the operational parameters needed to achieve a 4N (99.99%) terminal purity target for each REE stream. The methodology involved pinpointing critical A/B separation cuts and optimising the organic-to-aqueous (O/A) ratios across the cascade. The results show that the flowsheet effectively fractionates the feedstock, starting with a bulk LREE/HREE separation (Train 1) and culminating in the challenging separation of praseodymium (Pr) and neodymium (Nd) (Train 4). The simulation identified Pr/Nd separation as the primary technical bottleneck, requiring 62 equilibrium stages (NE) due to a low separation factor (β) of 1.70. In contrast, simpler bulk splits needed as few as 16 stages. These findings confirm the theoretical minimum stage requirements (Nmin) and provide a detailed stage-wise concentration profile for each train. The study concludes that the Pr/Nd circuit dictates the overall plant footprint and capital intensity. The developed flowsheet offers a solid technical blueprint for commercialising Malaysian IAC resources, ensuring high-purity REE recovery through optimised metallurgical design. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: Thermo-energetic parametric assessment of PV/T cooling technologies: Implications for energy yield, economic savings and CO2 reduction
Abstract: Growing societal energy demand has increased the consumption of non-renewable resources, causing resource depletion as well as environmental, economic, and human health concerns. In this context, the transition to renewable energy systems has become essential. Photovoltaic panels integrated with electrical energy storage are among the most promising alternatives to fossil-fuel-based power generation. However, the rise in the photovoltaic panel temperature significantly reduces their efficiency, which remains a major limitation. This study addresses this issue through a theoretical parametric analysis of four photovoltaic-thermal cooling methods: water-based photovoltaic-thermal system, nanofluid-based photovoltaic-thermal system, phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system, and nano-phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system. Minimum and maximum interval boundaries of relative efficiency enhancement values collected from the literature were used to estimate the potential energy gains, economic savings, and carbon dioxide emission reductions under the climatic conditions of Tyre and Baalbek, Lebanon. The results revealed a strong influence of climate, with Baalbek consistently outperforming coastal Tyre because of its higher solar irradiation. Among all systems, nano-phase change material photovoltaic-thermal system achieved the best energetic, economic, and environmental performance. In July, under Baalbek conditions, it reached 100.06 kWh/m2 energy enhancement, 43.86 USD/m2 savings, and 55.61 kg/m2 carbon dioxide reduction. Normalizing the results per unit photovoltaic panel area also provided a scalable assessment tool for stakeholders. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Song X.; Sun L.; Gao P.; Cui R.; Tang Z.
Title: Engineering regulation of free radicals by Cu-Ni bimetallic synergistic effect for low-temperature catalytic hydrolysis of carbonyl sulfide
Abstract: Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is a stubborn organic sulfur contaminant hindering natural gas deep desulfurization. Traditional hydrolysis catalysts face short service life and severe overoxidation of byproduct H2S. Herein, Cu-Ni bimetallic modified CeAlOx composite oxide was synthesized via ammonia precipitation for low-temperature COS catalytic hydrolysis. Multiple material characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were adopted to uncover bimetallic synergistic regulation on oxygen vacancies and reactive free radicals. The Cu-Ni co-modified CeAlOx catalyst exhibited optimal desulfurization performance, prominent anti-interference ability against H2O and CH4. Cu-Ni/CeAlOx maintained full COS removal for 570 min and achieved 209 h long-term stable operation. Cu promoted water dissociation and superoxide radical (·O2-) generation to accelerate COS hydrolysis, while Ni suppressed excessive ·O2- production to avoid deep oxidation of H2S. Oxygen vacancies and triply bridged hydroxyl groups acted as core active sites. Atomic-scale DFT confirmed CuO oxygen vacancies dominated COS hydrolysis, and NiO oxygen vacancies realized selective oxidation of H2S to elemental sulfur. The formation and the decomposition of HSCO2- are the rate-determining step for COS hydrolysis. This work provides theoretical guidance for developing high-efficiency desulfurization catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Physicochemical and commercial properties of a microelement-containing nitrogen fertilizer based on ammonium nitrate and spent lithium-ion batteries; [Аммоний нитраты мен пайдаланылған литий-ионды батареялар негізіндегі микроэлементтермен байытылған азотты тыңайтқыштың физика-химиялық және тауарлық қасиеттері]; [Физико-химические и товарные свойства микроэлементсодержащего азотного удобрения на основе нитрата аммония и отработанных литий-ионных батарей]
Abstract: The results of a comprehensive study of the physicochemical and commercial properties (hygroscopic point, sorption kinetics, sorption moisture capacity) of trace-containing nitrogen fertilizers based on ammonium nitrate (AN) melt and cathode powder from used lithium-ion batteries are presented. The use of cathode powder as a polymicroelement additive (PMА) is shown, and they were introduced into the saltpeter melt at various mass ratios of NА: PMА from 100 (0.5-3.0). The prepared samples of fertilizers with a granule size of 2-3 mm were tested to determine the hygroscopic point, sorption kinetics, and sorption moisture capacity at relative air humidity of 60, 70, 85, and 100%. The samples of fertilizers were studied at a relative humidity of 60%, and it was proved that at such a relative humidity, the samples do not get moistened, but rather dry out. The results of the study of samples with a 4-hour exposure are given and it is found that fertilizer granules have a low hygroscopic point from 50 to 60% and a high moisture absorption rate in the order of 1.860; 5.920 and 6.710; 2.052; 6.790 and 9.451, as well as 3.481; 6.954 and 9.906 mg/(g min) at relative air humidity of 70, 85 and 100%, respectively. Due to the fact that the process of sorption of the investigated granules of products lasts up to 30 days (or 720 hours), they have a hygroscopic point of 60 to 70%, related to hygroscopic substances. Appropriate conclusions are drawn due to the properties of the studied fertilizers: they have a low moisture capacity, and their physical properties begin to deteriorate sharply only at a moisture content of about 2%. The resulting fertilizers are not inferior to known fertilizers in their characteristics. Title: The complex Ginzburg-Landau equation on a finite interval and chaos suppression via a finite-dimensional boundary feedback stabilizer
Abstract: In this paper, we study the well-posedness and boundary stabilization of the initial-boundary value problem for the complex Ginzburg-Landau (CGL) equation on a finite interval. First, we establish a local well-posedness theory for the open-loop model in L 2-based fractional Sobolev spaces in the case of Dirichlet-Neumann type inhomogeneous mixed boundary conditions. This local well-posedness result is based on linear estimates derived by using the weak solution formula obtained via the unified transform (also known as the Fokas method). Next, we study the global well-posedness properties of the open-loop model in presence of inhomogeneous boundary conditions. Then, we turn our attention to the rapid boundary feedback stabilization problem and design a nonlocal controller which uses a finite number of Fourier modes of the state of solution. This design relies on the fact that solutions of the CGL equation can be separated into a slow, finite-dimensional component and a rapidly decaying tail, with the former primarily governing long-term behavior. We determine the necessary number of modes required to stabilize the system at a specified rate. Additionally, we identify the minimum number of modes that ensure stabilization at an unspecified decay rate. These theoretical results are validated by numerical simulations. The spatiotemporal estimates established in the first part of the paper are also employed to obtain local solutions of the controlled system. The existence of global energy solutions follows from stabilization estimates, while uniqueness follows from the uniqueness of an associated initial-boundary value problem with homogeneous boundary conditions whose solutions are in correspondence with the solutions of the original system through a bounded invertible Volterra-type integral transform on Sobolev spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Fu T.; Xu L.; Wang W.; Zhao D.; Xin Y.; Zhang B.
Title: Regulating Fe3O4-to-FeO ratio by Co3O4 pre-deposition to enhance oxidation resistance of pure iron
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Oxidation of iron-based alloys above 600 °C produces a Fe2O3/Fe3O4/FeO trilayer scale, in which the porous, rapidly growing FeO layer is detrimental, whereas Fe3O4 is desirable owing to its high compactness and lower growth rate. Yet the vastly different growth kinetics of the two oxides make FeO suppression challenging. Here, we demonstrate that pre-depositing a layer of Co3O4 nanoparticles on pure iron can effectively regulate the growth kinetics and structure of the oxide scale at 700 °C, reducing the oxidation rate constant by one order of magnitude and increasing the Fe3O4/FeO thickness ratio from 0.06 to 1.36. Density functional theory calculations reveal that these changes originate from Co2+ doping, which increases the diffusion barrier for cation vacancies while lowering that for anion vacancies in both Fe3O4 and FeO. As a result, FeO growth is strongly suppressed, and Fe3O4 growth shifts toward inward O2− diffusion, promoting competitive growth at the Fe3O4/FeO interface and further hindering FeO thickening. This work provides theoretical guidance for rational regulation of oxide-scale phase structure and oxidation-protection strategies in iron. © 2026

Authors: Zhang Y.; Cao L.; Yang X.; Su H.; Zhang L.; Feng Y.; Zhang J.; Ma R.; Liu B.; Li X.
Title: Balancing the mechanical-corrosion performance via the in-situ alloying effects of commercial Al-Mg and Al-Zn powders during additive manufacturing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Corrosion-mechanical performance trade-off is a key issue for engineering application of Al-Mg alloy. The main restriction is the contradicted performance variation and sensitization phenomenon. Current research has achieved prominent progress in performance optimization of casting Al-Mg alloy, by in-situ alloying, post treatment, etc. Whereas, the performance evolution in hot-spot additive manufacturing still needs systematic study. More importantly, the performance is vitally sensitive to microstructure variation, and their intrinsic mechanism still needs clearer elucidation. This work attempts to testify the influence of microstructure evolution on the strengthening-corrosion behaviors. Herein, an economic and efficient alloying approach is adopted by coupling commercial Al-Zn/Al-Mg system. The cooperation of Al3(Sc,Zr) and low-brittleness T-Mg32(Al,Zn,Cu)49 suppresses the sensitization effects and harmonizes the strengthen-deformation behaviors. Therefore, the novel Al-Mg-Zn-Cu alloy achieves a yield strength of 420.4 MPa and an elongation of 11.4%, and they retain 310.9 MPa and 29.4% at 200 °C, respectively. Moreover, the microstructure can restrain intergranular corrosion and promote pitting homogeneity. Zn addition promotes the passive film densifying, and T-phase shows a standard potential close to matrix, thus lowering the corrosion tendency. By regulating the plastic deformation-corrosion behaviors, the comprehensive performance is improved. The findings can provide a supplement for the performance regulation theory of Al-Mg alloy. © 2026

Authors: Zhou W.; Zhang J.; Fu J.; Sun Y.; Zhan Y.; Peng C.
Title: Numerical investigation on percussive cutting of Hubei hot dry rock using conical cutter under varying impact parameters
Abstract: As the development of geothermal resources in medium to deep dry hot rock formations progresses, traditional drilling technologies face numerous challenges posed by high-strength hard rocks. These challenges, including inadequate bit penetration capacity and low rotational cutting efficiency, severely constrain drilling performance. In this context, hydraulic impact hammer drilling technology has demonstrated significant advantages in enhancing drilling speed. To investigate the rock-breaking mechanisms under the coupled effects of impact load magnitude and frequency, deep granite was selected as the research object. Based on dynamic mechanical experimental data obtained under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions (200 °C, 40 MPa), a two-dimensional dynamic numerical model for cone-shaped tooth impact cutting of dry hot rock has been developed by incorporating cohesive elements. This model systematically analyzes the effects of varying impact loads (9 to 12 kN) and impact frequencies (30 to 60 Hz) on rock fragmentation patterns, dynamic response characteristics, and impact energy. The results indicate that the cone-shaped tooth impact cutting exhibits a pronounced “dynamic crushing-shear coupling” feature, with the rock-breaking process undergoing dynamic evolution from local crushing initiation to volume fracturing, eventually leading to shear-mixed destruction. An increase in impact load significantly enhances the system's dynamic response amplitude, leading to a transition in the rock-breaking mode from shallow local crushing to extensive shear-mixed failure, accompanied by a notable increase in the fractured area. Additionally, increasing the impact frequency reinforces the superposition effect of stress waves within the rock and ensures continuous energy input, resulting in a denser dynamic response and further expanding the wedge-shaped fracture zone in front of the tooth tip. Moreover, as both load and frequency increase, the impact damaged area and energy increases significantly, allowing the system's energy to be more efficiently converted into rock damage and fracture energy. This study reveals the mechanisms by which high-frequency and high-energy parameters influence the efficiency of impact rock breaking, providing important theoretical support for the optimization of hydraulic impact hammers and the design of drill bit structures. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Mirzahosseini M.; Biglari M.
Title: A Review of Constitutive Modeling of Unsaturated Soils
Abstract: The mechanics of unsaturated soils are integral to understanding and predicting the behavior of diverse geotechnical and geo-environmental systems, including natural slopes, engineered embankments, landfill covers, and agricultural fields. Unlike saturated soils, unsaturated soils exhibit a complex interplay among air, water, and solid phases, in which suction and partial saturation are pivotal in governing stress-strain responses, volume changes, and fluid flow processes. Over the past several decades, extensive theoretical, experimental, and computational efforts have culminated in sophisticated constitutive models, reflecting the need to include moisture content and suction as additional state variables. This article comprehensively reviews these modeling endeavors, tracing historical developments from empirical extensions of saturated soil models to contemporary elastoplastic, multi-scale, and data-driven frameworks. Emphasis is placed on the evolution of stress state variables, the role of hydraulic hysteresis, and the bidirectional coupling between mechanical and water retention behavior. Special attention is given to recent models that incorporate bound water structure and dehydration mechanisms in expansive clays, highlighting their influence on retention properties, suction, and thermomechanical responses. The paper also explores advances in small-strain stiffness modeling (which is crucial for predicting seismic behavior of unsaturated soils), machine learning integration, and coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes. Practical challenges, including parameter calibration, are examined. The paper also offers examples of prominent constitutive models, detailing their mathematical formulations and underlying assumptions. Current trends, including the integration of machine learning, are evaluated, and future research directions are proposed, underscoring the importance of interdisciplinary collaborations and long-term monitoring to refine and validate constitutive models for unsaturated soils. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. Authors: Kong K.; Wang D.; Li H.; Wang Z.; Liu G.; Yuan D.; Wang R.; Hu N.
Title: Hierarchically woven covalent organic framework hydrogels with programmable hydrogen-binding domains for adaptive human–machine interfaces
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hydrogels are among the most promising materials for wearable sensors in human–machine interaction, but the pursuit of high mechanical strength and resilience in hydrogels often leads to a trade-off with conductivity, which significantly limits their practical applications; thereby, balancing energy dissipation and ion transport in hydrogels remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop molecularly woven hydrogels by non-covalently threading linear polymers into thiadiazole-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs), in which the thiadiazole dihydrazide units in the COFs function as hydrogen-binding domains, fostering multiple non-covalent interactions between the COFs and linear polymers. This unique configuration facilitates energy dissipation while simultaneously enhancing ion transport. The resulting hydrogels exhibit a tensile strength of 0.41 MPa, resilience of 99%, an ionic conductivity of 1.27 ± 0.18 S m−1, and limited crack propagation, ranking among the highest values reported for hydrogel materials. Furthermore, the hydrogel-based sensor demonstrates a rapid strain response of 12.5 ms, excellent cyclic stability, and superior environmental weatherability, enabling accurate monitoring of human activities and gesture recognition for dexterous robotic manipulation. This work holds great promise for developing intelligent human-machine interfaces to perform dangerous and high-precision tasks. © 2026

Authors: Li J.; Ma H.; Qu R.; Guo S.; Liu F.
Title: Competition and interaction between shear-banding and cleavage-cracking in an Fe-based metallic glass
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-strength Fe-based metallic glasses (Fe-MGs) are prone to catastrophic fracture under external loading, and clarifying their ductile-to-brittle transition (DBT) mechanism and realizing brittleness modulation is of significance. The competition between shear-band-dominated plastic deformation and cleavage-crack-dominated fracture is the key to determining the failure mode transition of Fe-MGs. However, the interaction mechanism between shear-banding and cleavage-cracking remains unclear. In this work, we performed a systematic investigation on a high-strength and relatively tough Fe-MG using two different sample sizes and quasi-in situ compression tests to vividly show the size-dependent failure behavior, damage evolution, competition and interaction between shear bands and cleavage cracks. We found that the stress concentrators due to the pre-existing external defects and the interaction of shear bands promote the initiation of cleavage-cracking, while the stable crack propagation depends on sample size. This study deepens the current understanding of the failure mechanisms in high-strength MGs and also provides a new insight into the sample size effect in brittle MGs. The fact that the smaller MG sample deforms more plastically rather than brittle fracture is not only because it contains smaller and fewer external defects but also due to the more stable crack propagation. © 2026

Title: Evolving the DarTwin evolution language
Source title: Innovations in Systems and Software Engineering
Abstract: DarTwin is a notation for describing and planning evolution of digital twin systems. Originally conceived as a graphical notation, DarTwin has evolved into a domain-specific language formally defined in SysML v2. This evolution exposed challenges related to graphical notation support, tooling interoperability, and co-evolution between notation, language definition, and modelling environments. We experienced that SysML v2 tooling was not adequate to provide our DarTwin graphical notation even with some post-processing. The SysML v2 definition of DarTwin did, however, motivate improvements of the DarTwin DSL. To provide fruitful DarTwin graphical notation and still maintain the formal definition in SysML v2 we demonstrate how domain-specific tooling (MetaEdit+) helps improving the graphic editing and rendering support and thus achieve a more effective and intuitive use of DarTwin. By generating SysML v2 from MetaEdit+ we preserve the connection between the adequate graphical notation and the precision and formality of DarTwin. The combined DarTwin tooling made the methodology to apply general evolution transition patterns (DarTrans) more formal and precise while still intuitive through graphic notation using colour and dashes. This in turn motivated enhancing the DarTwin language by adding concepts related to the evolution transitions to facilitate discovering and documenting the transitions. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Long X.; Xi G.; Ou J.; Mei M.; Xiao R.; Ma Y.; Shi J.; Ma Y.; Sun W.; Guan D.
Title: Effects of dislocation-twin interactions on twin evolution and dislocation transformation in AZ31 magnesium alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The interaction between dislocations and deformation twins strongly influences microstructural evolution and deformation behavior in Mg alloys. In this work, the effects of dislocation-twin interactions on twinning and slip behavior in AZ31 magnesium (Mg) alloy were investigated using a two-step quasi-in-situ compression approach. The results show that during the initial deformation stage, basal-prismatic/prismatic-basal (BP/PB) interfaces generated by dislocation-twin interactions suppress twin growth while promoting new twin nucleation and non-basal dislocation transformation, with the strongest pinning effect occurring at an intermediate interface density. During subsequent deformation, twin growth continues, while dislocation slip gradually becomes the predominant deformation mode. Basal ⟨a⟩ dislocations transform into non-basal dislocation types through distinct pathways governed by geometric compatibility. Direct transformation is favored at high geometric compatibility factor (m′), whereas indirect transformation predominates at low m′ values. These findings reveal how BP/PB interfaces influence twin evolution and dislocation transformation in Mg alloys. © 2026

Title: Atomic and Molecular Structure Regulated In Situ Cross-Linked Polyurethane Gel Electrolyte for High-Performance Lithium Metal Batteries
Abstract: The incompatibility of conventional electrolytes with high-voltage cathodes and lithium metal anodes limits the performance of lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Here, an in situ cross-linked polyurethane gel electrolyte (G-P3 AR) is designed through atomic and molecular structure regulation. The polyester segments widen the highest occupied molecular orbital–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital gap, extending the electrochemical stability window to 4.97 V for compatibility with NCM811 cathodes. Polyether segments exhibit a lower Li+ binding energy, reducing the desolvation barrier and enhancing anode stability. At the atomic level, sp2-hybridized boron in the chain extender immobilizes anions (TFSI− and DFOB−) through Lewis acid–base interactions, raising the Li+ transference number to 0.78 and enabling exceptional rate capability (157.7 mAh g−1 at 2 C in the Li||NCM811 cell). Hydrogen bonding between the polymer and solvent restructures the solvation sheath, promoting inorganic-rich interphases. The Li|G-P3 AR|NCM811 cell retains 81.7% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C charge/1 C discharge, demonstrating a rational electrolyte design strategy for high-performance LMBs. Title: Ribosome engineering enhances genetic code expansion in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Abstract: Genetic code expansion enables the site-specific installation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) into proteins, but its limited efficiency in eukaryotes remains a major barrier to broader application. Here we establish a visual, plug-and-play screening platform to evolve 18S ribosomal DNA in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and identify ribosomal variants that improve ncAA incorporation. The best-performing strain, designated ribo-hyper, increased ncAA-dependent GFP production by 2.9-fold relative to the wild-type rDNA strain and enhanced incorporation across distinct orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. Proteomic analysis further revealed changes in amino acid biosynthesis, translation-related proteins and stress-response pathways, indicating that the engineered ribosome reshapes cellular translation homeostasis. Perturbation of translation quality-control pathways, including the ribosome-rescue factors Dom34 and Hbs1 and the core mRNA exosome component Ski6, reduced ncAA-containing protein output, whereas disruption of ribosome quality-control factor Rqc2 had little effect. These findings support a role for ribosome rescue and associated mRNA turnover in efficient ncAA incorporation in the ribo-hyper strain. Together, our results establish eukaryotic ribosome engineering as a viable strategy for improving genetic code expansion in yeast. Copyright © 2026. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Kuto K.; Wu Y.
Title: The existence and instability of blowing-up steady states for the Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto competition model with cross-diffusion
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence and stability of a type of blowing-up positive steady states for a shadow system of the Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto (SKT) two-species competition model and for the perturbed SKT system with a sufficiently large cross-diffusion parameter and bounded random diffusion parameters. The asymptotic behavior of coexistence steady states of the SKT model as one of the cross-diffusion parameters tends to infinity was studied by Lou and Ni [1], who showed that almost all coexistence states can be characterized by one of three shadow systems. In [2], the first author of the present paper studied one of these shadow systems with one cross-diffusion term in one space dimension and proved that one component along a bifurcation branch blows up as the bifurcation parameter approaches the least positive eigenvalue of −Δ under the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. Using a different approach from that in [2] , based on suitable transformations and the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, we establish the existence and detailed asymptotic structure of several branches of positive steady states near the blow-up points for shadow systems with one or two cross-diffusion terms in one- and multi-dimensional domains. We further prove that all the large steady states obtained near the blow-up points are spectrally unstable. Finally, by perturbation arguments, we establish the existence and instability of corresponding branches of positive steady states for the original SKT system when one of the cross-diffusion parameters is sufficiently large. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Sustainability assessment for multi-activity coastal areas using an integrated hierarchical decision-making framework
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainability assessments of multi-activity coastal areas generally evaluate each utilization activity independently, leaving interdependencies unaccommodated and risking biased contribution estimates under conventional hierarchical weighting. This constraint carries profound implications for settings where anthropogenic activities vie for finite ecological space, most notably within tropical coastal socio-ecological systems in developing countries. The study objectives were to develop an activity-based sustainability assessment framework integrating hierarchical and network-based multi-criteria weighting to estimate the relative contribution of three activities: small-scale capture fisheries, vannamei shrimp ponds, and coastal tourism, in the coastal area of Pariaman City, Indonesia. METHODS: Assessments covered 36 indicators across four sustainability dimensions: ecological, social, economic, and governance, with a 17-node interdependence network built from 14 indicators showing cross-activity dependencies through shared resources and identified causal pathways. Hierarchical weights for individual activities were derived independently by fifteen experts across three sectoral panels. Additionally, network-based weighting to account for inter-activity interactions was performed by a subset of five cross-sectoral experts. All pairwise comparison matrices satisfied the predetermined consistency threshold. The resilience of the regional index to weighting uncertainty was tested through sensitivity analysis. FINDINGS: Network-based weights ranked vannamei shrimp ponds above small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism, but far less dominantly than under hierarchical weighting, which treated ponds as an extreme outlier by ignoring their negative influence on shared water quality and spatial resources. With a near-uniform contribution value of 0.554 across all three activities, the regional index underscores that intervention prioritization requires integrating interdependent cross-activity contributions rather than relying exclusively on standalone activity assessments. The moderately sustainable category held consistently across sensitivity scenarios, although activity contribution order proved more sensitive to weighting uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Accounting for interdependence corrects the hierarchical approach's over-estimation of vannamei shrimp ponds and reveals a greater contribution from small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism than independent estimates suggest. The sustainability contribution of a given activity cannot be reliably determined in isolation from cross-sectoral interdependencies, highlighting the primary utility of this framework as a decision-support mechanism for coastal management. Title: Self-adaptive phase transition precipitates enabled superior strength of additively manufactured (Nb15Ta10W75)98.5C1.5 refractory multi-principal element alloys at ultra-high temperatures
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Refractory multi-principal element alloys (RMPEAs), particularly those of the Nb-Ta-W system, are promising candidates for structural applications under ultra-high temperature (UHT) conditions of ≥ 1500 °C. However, their softening temperatures (Tc ≈ 1600–2000 °C) coincide with the operational range required for the heat-resistant components in aerospace and energy systems, leading to severe strength degradation. Here, we propose an in-situ nano-precipitation strategy mediated by adaptive phase transformations to overcome this limitation. The required C content of 1.5 at.% was estimated using Thermo-Calc software. We designed a novel (Nb15Ta10W75)98.5C1.5 (NTWC) RMPEA that enables in-situ (Nb,Ta)C precipitation during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). Isothermal kinetic calculations show that the in-situ precipitates have excellent thermal stability. These nano-precipitates undergo a three-stage evolution successively from metastable (Nb,Ta)C to equilibrium TaC at 1600, 1800 and 2000 °C, enabling NTWC to achieve yield strengths of 634, 328 and 126 MPa respectively, surpassing most LPBF-fabricated refractory alloys. The effect of microstructure characteristics and phase transition behavior of nano-precipitates on the UHT strength was evaluated in detail. Beyond demonstrating a pathway for unprecedented UHT strength retention, this work establishes a general principle of coupling thermodynamic stability and kinetic adaptability for precipitates in complex concentrated systems via molecular dynamics. © 2026

Abstract: Open-pit slope stability is one of the key factors determining the safety and efficiency of open-pit mining operations. With increasing pit depth, growing complexity of rock mass structure, and intensification of mining activities, the need for advanced methods for studying slope stability based on digital technologies is steadily increasing. The aim of this study is to systematize and comparatively analyze modern methods for investigating open-pit slope stability, taking into account their capabilities and limitations under mining conditions. The paper presents an analytical review of computational geomechanical approaches, geodetic instrumental methods, terrestrial laser scanning, UAV-based photogrammetry, and satellite radar interferometry (InSAR). A comparative analysis of these methods is performed based on key parameters, including data type, spatial coverage, and capabilities for deformation analysis. The results show that each method has specific advantages and limitations related to data characteristics, observation conditions, and analytical potential. It is established that none of the methods, when used individually, provides a complete and reliable description of slope stability. The highest level of informativeness is achieved through the integration of different methods within comprehensive analytical approaches. Title: Impact of temperature-dependent viscosity and permeable boundaries on thermal instability in a Darcy–Brinkman ferrofluid layer
Abstract: This study investigates the onset of thermal instability in a horizontal Darcy–Brinkman ferrofluid layer with temperature-dependent viscosity, bounded by permeable horizontal surfaces. The variation of viscosity with temperature is described using linear, exponential, and inverse-linear relations. The governing equations are nondimensionalized and reduced to an eigenvalue problem, which is solved using the single-term Galerkin method to determine the critical Rayleigh number for the onset of stationary convection. The incorporation of permeable boundaries, together with different viscosity relations in a ferrofluid-saturated Brinkman porous medium, provides a novel extension of the classical framework and broadens its applicability in various scientific and engineering contexts. The results reveal that the viscosity variation parameter stabilizes the system under linear and exponential laws, but has a destabilizing effect in the inverse-linear case across all boundary conditions. A transition in permeable boundaries from free to rigid enhances the stability of the system by delaying the onset of convection. Additionally, the magnetization parameters M 1 and M 3 both promote instability; however, their effects on convection cell size differ: M 1 favors smaller convection cells, while M 3 promotes larger ones. The permeability of the porous medium also supports the development of larger cells and reduces the critical Rayleigh number. Previous results are consistently recovered as limiting cases, confirming the validity of the present analysis. The study provides deeper insight into ferrofluid convection with relevance to aerospace, porous thermal management, and magnetically driven heat transfer applications. © 2026 Author(s).

Authors: Song W.; Zhang Y.; Huang M.; Feng D.; Zhang D.; Fu L.
Title: Constructing a cross-scale structure via self-doping for high-performance n-type PbTe thermoelectrics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Decoupling electron and phonon transport is a central challenge in thermoelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that self-doping in PbTe enables a cross-scale structural strategy to achieve this goal and enhance thermoelectric performance. The introduction of excess Pb into Pb0.993Bi0.007Te triggers the formation of Pb interstitials, which promotes carrier density by donating electrons into the conduction band and provides impurity levels near the conduction band minimum to enlarge effective mass. Meanwhile, a nanoscale porous structure at grain boundaries is generated during cooling of the sintering process by the thermal expansion mismatch between the PbTe matrix and Pb-rich precipitate phases. The cross-scale structure, comprising interstitial defects and nanopores, significantly enhances phonon scattering. Therefore, a high peak ZT of about 1.7 at 773 K is achieved by adding 1% Pb excess to Pb0.993Bi0.007Te, contributing to an experimental conversion efficiency of 3.3% under a small temperature difference of 370 K in the single-leg module. This work highlights that constructing a cross-scale structure by simple self-doping is an effective pathway for high-performance thermoelectrics. © 2026

Authors: Wang B.; Sun J.; Ding C.; Zhang Y.; Zhu Q.; Zhang T.; Wang F.
Title: Construction of a corrosion signal network based on ultra-sensitive near-infrared fillers for rapid diagnosis of early corrosion of magnesium alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Magnesium alloys, possessing excellent mechanical properties and low density, have attracted considerable interest in engineering applications. However, they possess poor corrosion resistance, limiting their implementation. The early detection and imaging of corrosion in coated magnesium alloys, as well as the construction of an integrated early-corrosion signal network, are highly sought after but remain challenging in practice. Herein, we report the synthesis of a novel core-shell near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent filler by coating ZnGa2O4:Cr3+ (ZGOC, NIR signal source) with H3PW12O40 (HPW, ultraviolet-shielding shell). The NIR emission and afterglow of ZGOC are completely quenched upon HPW coating. However, the alkaline environment (pH ≈ 8) generated during early-stage corrosion of magnesium alloys can dissolve the HPW shell, thereby restoring the NIR afterglow of ZGOC. This recovery enables precise localization of corrosion sites and reliable quantitative evaluation of corrosion severity. The corrosion indication capability was evaluated using laser confocal microscope (LCM) and scanning electron microscope (SEM). The results show that after 50 days of salt spray testing, the optical imaging system detects fluorescence signals at the corrosion sites, and the afterglow intensity increases by 3.3 times compared to that at the initial stage, which is consistent with the SEM and LCM results. This work enables detection of corrosion, precise localization of corroded sites, and visualization of corrosion severity, thus enabling the construction of a spatial corrosion signal distribution network and achieving ultra-sensitive detection of early-stage corrosion in magnesium alloys. © 2026

Authors: Xu J.; Huo S.; Tian Q.; Wang Y.; Wang Z.; Song Z.; Xie Y.; Hu X.; Wu E.
Title: Atomristors: A new memristive paradigm enabled by atomic-scale switching
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Atomristors represent the ultimate thickness limit of memristors by employing monolayer two-dimensional materials as atomically thin switching media. Reducing the switching layer to a single atomic plane fundamentally transforms resistive switching (RS) from the evolution of extended conductive filaments into atomically confined processes governed by point defects, electrode-derived metal species, and van der Waals interfaces. This Review summarizes atomristors from switching mechanisms, device engineering, and emerging applications. We first present the dissociation-diffusion-adsorption mechanism as a conceptual framework for understanding how metal species migrate across monolayer interfaces and are immobilized at atomic defects to generate conductive spots. We then summarize how defect, electrode, and interface engineering govern device performance and reliability. Benefiting from atomic-scale confinement, representative atomristors have demonstrated fA-level leakage currents, switching ratios exceeding 1011, sub-volt operation, and ps-level switching speeds. Finally, we highlight recent advances in nonvolatile in-memory computing, volatile threshold selectors, radio-frequency switches, and stochastic sources. We then discuss the remaining challenges in clarifying atomic-scale switching mechanisms, reducing cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability, and achieving wafer-scale integration. By linking atomically confined switching physics with materials and device engineering, atomristors offer a platform for understanding RS at the atomic limit and for developing scalable atomic-scale information hardware. © 2026

Abstract: Silica fouling reduces the effectiveness and durability of membrane-based treatment systems, and silicon contamination in industrial water streams poses ongoing operational issues. With an emphasis on their processes, drawbacks, and applicability for various silica species, this article provides a comparative examination of the main silica removal technologies: ion exchange, reverse osmosis (RO), ultrafiltration (UF), electrocoagulation (EC), adsorption, and lime softening. Although they need a significant amount of chemical input and pH control, lime softening and ion exchange are efficient for dissolved silica. RO requires thorough preparation and offers broad-spectrum separation, although it is susceptible to silica scaling. While UF works well with colloidal and particulate silica, it is unsuccessful with monomeric forms. EC achieves excellent removal rates with less sludge by combining electrochemical destabilisation and crystallisation. Adsorption provides variable selectivity, low energy consumption, and compatibility with membrane systems, especially when employing tailored materials like activated alumina, iron oxide-coated media, and functionalised hybrids. Title: Enhanced loss of circulation prediction using Sea Lion-optimized machine learning models
Abstract: Lost circulation is a major drilling challenge that increases cost and non-productive time and is influenced by different parameters. This study develops and evaluates machine learning models for predicting lost circulation severity during drilling operations. Three machine learning algorithms, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN), and Random Forest, were optimized using the Sea Lion Optimization algorithm to enhance prediction accuracy. Feature importance analysis identified azimuth as the most significant predictor, followed by measure depth, average bit RPM, hook load, and torque, indicating that directional and mechanical drilling parameters outweigh mud properties and formation data in predicting fluid loss. Correlation analysis further confirmed strong relationships among these key parameters. The results indicate that azimuth and depth have a stronger correlation with the target parameters. All optimized models demonstrated good performance in classifying fluid loss severity. The Random Forest model achieved the best performance among the evaluated models. The K-NN and Decision Tree models also showed strong performance. Confusion matrix analysis validated all models' capability to reliably distinguish between different fluid loss severity categories (Seepage, Partial, Severe, and Total Loss) on both training and testing datasets. The findings of this study can help to provide an effective approach for predicting lost circulation severity, offering potential for reducing non-productive time, cost, and improving drilling safety. © 2026 The Authors.
