Authors: Prasetyo S.D.; Arifin Z.
Title: Unveiling the thermodynamic performance of nano-enhanced bio-PCM for improved efficiency in solar cooling systems
Abstract: Nano-enhanced bio-based phase change materials have emerged as promising thermal management materials for solar cooling applications because of their ability to improve heat transfer and thermal energy storage performance. This study presents a systematic review and quantitative synthesis of 50 peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2025, focusing on thermodynamic mechanisms, thermophysical characterization, and cooling applications in photovoltaic and photovoltaic/thermal systems. The results demonstrate that nanoparticle incorporation significantly enhances thermal conductivity by approximately 15–400%, particularly with carbon-based nanofillers such as graphene and multi-walled carbon nanotubes, whereas latent heat retention generally decreases by 5–15% due to nanoparticle volume displacement and molecular interactions. The synthesized datasets indicate that an optimal nanoparticle loading of 2–4 weight percent provides a balanced enhancement of thermal conductivity and latent heat storage capacity. The correlation analysis reveals a minimal linear relationship between dispersion quality and latent heat retention, with a coefficient of r = 0.0935. This indicates that dispersion quality alone does not adequately account for the variations in latent heat retention observed across the reviewed studies. Instead, it suggests that factors such as nanoparticle morphology and interfacial compatibility are likely to have a more significant impact on thermodynamic behavior. The synthesis further shows that photovoltaic operating temperature can be reduced by up to 11°C under peak solar irradiance, resulting in an approximately 7.2% improvement in electrical efficiency. Exergy evaluation indicates that the latent phase contributes the highest useful exergy, approximately 42%, while demonstrating lower thermal irreversibility. Despite substantial material-level improvements, the aggregated system-level performance remains constrained by thermal resistance, methodological inconsistencies, and integration challenges in practical PV and PV/T configurations. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Ma C.; Yu Z.; Yang Z.; Zhang W.; He B.; Shi S.; Liu Y.
Title: A composition generation framework embedded with domain knowledge for chemically disordered inorganic compounds
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Generative models are increasingly attracting attention due to their ability to navigate the chemical space for inverse design of materials. However, generating valid compositions for chemically disordered crystals remains challenging, as inherent model noise makes it difficult to map continuous outputs onto precise, discrete stoichiometric coefficients. Here, we propose Tri-Control-MatVAE, a domain knowledge-embedded Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for triple-objective controllable generation over element selection, target properties, and ordered/disordered regimes. By decoupling the integer and fractional states of elements through autoregressive prediction, the framework captures the hybrid stoichiometric distribution of chemically disordered compositions. We further propose a reliability metric termed Stoichiometric Fidelity to quantify the alignment between authentic and generated compositions, under which our framework achieves an improvement from 59.55% to 97.87% compared to conventional generative models. Such fidelity and controllability enable the direct exploration of complex chemical spaces without requiring model retraining. By steering the generation toward targeted lithium-containing compositional regimes, it generates 1229 candidate compositions, including 349 stoichiometric variants of established database entries, providing a narrowed compositional starting point for downstream structural validation. Our work establishes a domain knowledge-embedded framework that extends controllable compositional inverse design to chemically disordered materials. © 2026

Title: The environmental efficiency of the combined combustion of low-grade Ekibastuz coal and plant biomass; [Төмен сұрыпты Екібастұз көмірі мен өсімдік биомассасының аралас жануының экологиялық тиімділігі]; [Экологическая эффективность совместного сжигания низкосортного Экибастузского угля и растительной биомассы]
Abstract: This article presents the results of a study on the layered combustion of low-grade Ekibastuz coal blended with biomass additives aimed at improving the energy efficiency and environmental sustainability of small-and medium-scale energy systems. Corn waste, which is a by-product of agro-industrial production, was used as a bio-additive. Comprehensive physico-chemical analysis of the original components was carried out, including determination of their calorific value. Based on the obtained data, fuel mixtures with different biomass contents were prepared, which allowed an in-depth analysis of co-combustion processes and the relationship between the proportion of biomass, the calorific value of the mixture, the combustion efficiency, and the level of pollutant emissions to be determined. The results showed that the most optimal composition is a fuel mixture with a biomass content in the range of 20-30% and coal in the range of 70-80%, providing the best combination of energy and environmental performance. Calculations and experimental studies of layered combustion parameters in installations with a fixed layer have been performed. It was demonstrated that the addition of 20–30% biomass intensifies the combustion process, increases the overall calorific value of the fuel blend, and reduces the concentration of harmful substances in flue gases compared to the combustion of pure coal. Rational process conditions have been defined, including the optimal height of the fuel layer, temperature regimes, and combustion duration. Abstract: Controlled and sustained drug delivery has emerged as a transformative strategy for overcoming the limitations of conventional pharmaceutical formulations, including poor bioavailability, rapid drug clearance, systemic toxicity, and non-specific distribution. Title: A perfluorooctanol functionalization strategy boosting CO2 electroreduction to ethylene
Abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene represents an environmentally friendly and promising technological pathway for achieving a carbon-negative cycle. However, sustaining efficient CO2-to-ethylene conversion under industrially relevant current densities remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a perfluorooctanol functionalization strategy that effectively boosts the performance of electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene. The functionalized copper-based catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 50% for ethylene and exhibits robust stability spanning over 100 h at a current density of 0.6 A cm−2. The incorporation of perfluorooctanol significantly alters the surface microenvironment and modulates the electronic structure of the Cu active sites. In situ spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations demonstrate that this molecular modulation effectively lowers the energy barriers for key intermediate formation and facilitates asymmetric C–C coupling, thereby promoting ethylene generation. This work presents a promising molecular interface engineering approach to realize efficient CO2-to-ethylene conversion at industrially viable current densities. © 2026

Authors: Jinadu A.; Monagan M.
Title: A new Dixon resultant algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems using sparse multivariate rational function interpolation
Abstract: Elimination methods such as Gröbner bases and triangular sets have been employed to address the growing demand for solving parametric polynomial systems in practice. However, experiments have shown that when used in Computer Algebra Systems such as Maple and Magma they often struggle with systems that have many parameters. To address this problem, we present a new interpolation algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems over Q using the Dixon resultant. The Dixon resultant is a multiple of the unique generator of an elimination ideal of a polynomial system. It can be expressed as the determinant of a matrix of polynomial entries called the Dixon matrix.In practice, the Dixon resultant R often has many repeated factors and a large polynomial content. To avoid computing these unwanted factors of R, our new algorithm interpolates the rational function coefficients in the parameters of the monic square-free factors of R from monic univariate images of R. It does this using our newly developed sparse multivariate rational function interpolation method. By not computing R in expanded form, our approach often dramatically reduces the number of images needed to interpolate the monic square-free factors of R over Q[jls-end-space/].We have implemented our new Dixon resultant algorithm in Maple with many parts of the algorithm coded in C for increased efficiency. Our benchmarks show that our new Dixon resultant algorithm can solve many parametric polynomial systems that other algorithms for computing R are unable to solve. Our new algorithm is probabilistic; it may fail to produce an answer, and even when successful, it may return an incorrect answer, but with provably low probability. In this work we identify and classify all the causes of failure in our new algorithm, and we give a detailed failure probability analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Covalent Organic Framework-Anchored Carbon Nanotubes Enabling Ultra-Thin Robust Polyimide Films for High-Specific-Power Flexible GaAs Solar Cells
Abstract: Free-standing polymer films that are ultra-thin, lightweight, and robust hold significant promise for applications in flexible electronics. However, their performance has been constrained by the challenge of simultaneously enhancing mechanical strength and reducing density. Herein, an ultra-thin and robust polyimide (PI)-based covalent organic framework-modified multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT-COF) film is demonstrated for high-specific-power flexible GaAs solar cells. The film exhibits a high Young’s modulus of 1.53 GPa, a tensile strength exceeding 97.53 MPa, and a low density of 0.73 g cm−3, representing a 45.1% reduction in density. The incorporation of 3D interconnected layered and porous MWCNT-COF significantly enhances the film’s mechanical properties while reducing its density. The synergistic effects of robust MWCNTs and covalently bonded COF layers, combined with the thermally stable PI molecular structure, impart exceptional strength and lightness to the film. Computational studies further confirm that COF-grafted MWCNTs effectively modify the polyamide acid matrix, substantially improving the mechanical properties of the PI films. Moreover, flexible dual-junction and triple-junction GaAs solar cells were successfully fabricated using 6 µm-thick MWCNT-COF/PI composite films, delivering outstanding specific powers of 8998 and 7749 W kg−1, along with efficiencies of 26.6% and 31.5% (AM0), respectively. These results underscore the potential for high-performance applications in space and energy systems. This work offers valuable insights into the development of high-performance flexible GaAs solar cells based on ultra-thin and robust PI films for a wide range of applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Efficient IP Lookup Using a B-Tree on Expanded Trie
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: As routing tables continue to increase in size, IP address lookup has become a critical performance bottleneck in packet forwarding. A fundamental challenge arises from the variable-length nature of IP prefixes, which requires longest prefix matching (LPM) to identify the appropriate next-hop router. This paper presents BTET (B-tree on Expanded Trie), an efficient data structure designed to support high-performance IP address lookup. BTET combines the hierarchical organization of B-trees with the Controlled Prefix Expansion (CPE) technique to achieve efficient lookup and update operations. The core of the proposed structure consists of a collection of B-trees, where each expanded prefix is partitioned into multiple segments, and each segment is stored in the B-tree corresponding to its expansion level. Title: Strong electron coupling effect of Cd0.5Zn0.5S nanoparticles anchored on NiCo2S4 nanoflowers: Ohmic junction formation for boosted photocatalytic hydrogen production

Abstract: Optimized interfacial charge transport and reinforced interfacial bonding are indispensable for achieving efficient carrier separation and constructing advanced heterogeneous systems toward photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. The synthetic strategy ensures the uniform dispersion of CZS nanoparticles on NCS nanoflowers with intimate interfacial contact. The introduction of NCS nanoflowers significantly enhances the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance of CZS. Impressively, the optimized NCS-0.04/CZS heterojunction reaches an optimal hydrogen production activity of 92.62 mmol h−1 g−1, showing a 20-fold enhancement relative to pure CZS. Efficient charge separation triggered by the intrinsic electric field formed at the NCS/CZS Ohmic junction interface accounts for the remarkable improvement in photocatalytic performance. Specifically, the Ohmic junction efficiently facilitates the directional migration of photogenerated electrons from CZS to NCS and effectively suppresses their backflow. Through a combination of experimental studies and theoretical simulations, the fundamental mechanism underlying photocatalytic hydrogen evolution was elucidated. This research is expected to provide a novel perspective and pathway for the design and fabrication of high-performance photocatalysts. © 2026

Abstract: This study explores the prospects of extracting phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) from the mineralized mass of the Central Kyzylkum region using acidic wastewater (AWW) derived from cottonseed soapstock processing. Experiments were conducted at 333 K under varying AWW-to-mineralized mass (AWW:MM) ratios ranging from 100:10 to 100:40. The concentration of P2O5 was determined using a photometric method at a wavelength of 440 nm. The research was based exclusively on the analysis of the solid phase, where the extent of the reaction was assessed through the quantity of precipitate formed. It was demonstrated that an increase in pH had a direct effect on P2O5 extraction. The reduction in CaO content followed an exponential trend, while the P2O5 release exhibited a logarithmic relationship with pH. Title: Facet-directed multiphase TiO2–BiVO4 heterojunction for directional charge transport and photoelectrochemical cathodic protection
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Regulating charge transport across semiconductor heterojunctions is critical for photoelectrochemical (PEC) energy conversion and photoelectrochemical cathodic protection (PECP). Herein, we report a facet-directed multiphase and defect-regulated strategy to tailor interfacial energetics and carrier dynamics in TiO2–BiVO4 heterostructured photoanodes. By introducing Bi-containing domains onto TiO2 nanosheets with co-exposed {001}/{101} facets, the optimized TiO2–BiVO4-T forms a spatially heterogeneous multiphase architecture consisting of residual α-Bi2O3, tetragonal BiVO4, and monoclinic BiVO4. TiO2 facet configuration, multiphase BiVO4 domains, and defect-associated electronic modulation are proposed to regulate local band alignment, facilitate charge separation, and favor electron extraction. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analysis, density functional theory calculations, and light-assisted Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) show modified interfacial energetics, photoinduced surface-potential response, and improved carrier-transfer behavior. Accordingly, TiO2–BiVO4-T exhibits higher charge-separation efficiency, stronger PEC activity, and stable solar-driven cathodic protection for stainless steel and copper. The relationship between structure, electronic modulation, and PECP response identifies facet-selective formation of multiphase domains as a practical route for photoelectrodes used in corrosion protection and solar-energy conversion. © 2026

Title: Genetic engineering of cyanophages for harmful cyanobacterial bloom treatment—A mini review
Abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) are a prominent worldwide environmental concern. Proliferation of HCBs outpaces the development of mitigation and management technologies. Recently, cyanophages began to emerge as a potential abundant resource that can be harnessed for target-specific HCB treatment. However, there exist two major technical barriers in applying cyanophage-based treatment to HCB mitigation: host specificity and lysogenic life cycle. This minireview attempts to parse documented studies that developed or applied genetic engineering approaches or technologies to tackle the barriers through expanding host range and bypassing or abolishing the lysogenic life stage. We summarized representative technical approaches that may be extrapolated from bacteriophage to cyanophage, discussed genes and pathways that regulate host binding and infection or determine the switch between lytic and lysogenic lifecycles, identified existing knowledge and technological gaps and challenges, and proposed some attainable solutions and future perspectives for this fast-growing field of engineered cyanophage-mediated HCB remediation. © 2026 .

Title: 3D modeling of electro-facies using a geostatistical algorithm
Abstract: Facies analysis is a critical component of reservoir characterization studies. This study employs several clustering methods to generate reservoir electro-facies (EFs) from well logs. Title: Stress interference and propagation uniformity in multi cluster hydraulic fracturing using a coupled XFEM based CZM model
Abstract: The uniform propagation of multiple hydraulic fractures is crucial to maximize the volume of stimulated reservoirs and improve the recovery of hydrocarbons in unconventional reservoirs. However, simultaneous fluid injections often result in non-uniform fracture growth due to strong stress interference between adjacent clusters. The unresolved issue is a quantitative ranking of how the spacing of the clusters, the count of the clusters, the injection rate and the viscosity of the fluid control the uniformity of propagation under matched geomechanical conditions. This study addresses that gap using a two-dimensional plane strain coupled XFEM based CZM model for simultaneous multi-cluster fracture propagation from a horizontal wellbore in a tight and low-permeability reservoir. The model is verified against the analytical solution dominated by toughness of KGD and applied to fourteen parametric cases covering cluster spacing of 20 to 35 m, injection rate of 0.001 to 0.005 m3/s per cluster, fluid viscosity of 10−3 to 10−1 Pa s, and two to five clusters. Results show that coalescence of individual stress shadows into a continuous compressive stress umbrella is the main cause of non-uniform growth, with interior clusters confined while exterior fractures propagate more freely. Fracture spacing is the dominant control and increasing spacing from 20 to 30 m raises the uniformity index from 0.42 to 0.94 and supports uniform growth to 88 to 95 m. Cluster count is the second strongest control, injection rate has a secondary non-monotonic effect, and fluid viscosity has negligible influence on uniformity. Title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder

Abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. Title: Thermodynamic-guided design of cost-effective ultrahigh-strength carbide-free bainitic steel
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Carbide-free bainitic (CFB) steels offer an attractive combination of strength, ductility, and toughness but generally rely on complex alloy chemistries and prolonged isothermal treatments to achieve bainite formation and retained-austenite stabilisation. Here, a new air-cooled CFB steel with simplified chemistry was developed using a thermodynamics-guided alloy design framework. By analysing the effects of common alloying elements on the bainite start temperature, T0′ locus, and bainite hardenability, the carbon partitioning window is introduced as a thermodynamic descriptor to assess the compatibility of bainite formation under continuous cooling. Using this framework, it is shown that combined additions of cost-effective Mn, Al, and Si are sufficient to promote carbide-free bainite without relying on conventional heavy alloying with Ni, Cr, or Mo. Based on this design strategy, a Fe-0.4C-3.5Mn-2Si-0.5Al steel was selected and experimentally validated. The alloy formed a fully CFB microstructure directly after forging and air cooling, eliminating the need for prolonged isothermal treatment. The as-forged steel exhibits a yield strength of ∼1650 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 2300 MPa, an elongation greater than 8%, and a Charpy impact toughness of 14 J. These properties are comparable to those of heavily alloyed CFB and martensitic steels while requiring substantially simpler chemistry and processing. The proposed design framework provides a practical pathway for developing cost-effective, sustainable ultrahigh-strength bainitic steels. © 2026

Authors: Geng J.; Zhang H.; Mao Y.; Chen Y.; Wang N.; Zhao Q.; Kang Y.; Hou Z.; Zhu L.
Title: Dislocation network-induced multiple deformation mechanisms enabling a near-α titanium alloy with high strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Overcoming the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off remains a central challenge in developing advanced titanium (Ti) alloys, as conventional strengthening strategies invariably sacrifice ductility. Here, we propose a dislocation engineering strategy that deliberately constructs ordered dislocation networks in the TA18 alloy, achieving exceptional strength-ductility synergy. These ordered geometric architectures are robustly stabilized by sessile jogs originating from specific crystallographic interactions between <a> and <c+a> dislocations. During early deformation, the networks subdivide grains into fine deformable units, providing massive initial strain hardening by impeding mobile dislocations via the dislocation jog dragging effect. With progressive strain, inhomogeneous local stresses drive the sweeping out of jogs, dynamically transforming the static networks into glissile dislocation arrays and dense dislocation walls. This critical structural evolution triggers a fundamental transition to a “transport-dominated” plasticity regime, activating potent hetero-deformation-induced strengthening and indirect slip transfer. These findings establish a scalable paradigm for designing high-performance Ti alloys via dislocation architecture control. © 2026

Title: Environmental risks of pest management practices in smallholder coconut plantations
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: Oryctes rhinoceros, the coconut rhinoceros beetle, remains one of the most damaging pests of coconut (Cocos nucifera) across South and Southeast Asia, the Pacific, and increasingly, new invasion fronts in the Americas. Although climatic alterations may redistribute the geographic footprint of the hazard, predictive assessments underscore non-linear and variable outcomes. Regional expansions in vulnerable or suitable extents are largely contingent upon the analytical scenario and structural parameters of the model utilized. This reinforces the case for treating its management as an environmental, not solely agronomic, concern. The study objectives were to characterize how smallholder-level management choices translate into differentiated environmental and health risk. Smallholder coconut plantations, which supply most world coconut production, are disproportionately exposed because of fragmented land holdings, limited capital, and constrained extension access. This review evaluates the translation of management interventions into distinct environmental and health hazards by systematically reviewing evidence on coconut rhinoceros beetle biology, intervention efficacy, smallholder socioeconomic dynamics, and insecticide risk literature through a standardized four-tier risk framework. Smallholders commonly rely on chemical control options such as organophosphates and pyrethroids. These options carry documented risks: non-target toxicity, soil and water contamination, and occupational exposure. In the absence of beetle-specific metrics, elevated occupational exposure risks are inferred from prevailing normative practices in smallholder agriculture concerning the omission of protective equipment. Biological and cultural alternatives include O. rhinoceros nudivirus, Metarhizium anisopliae, Bacillus thuringiensis, botanical larvicides, and pheromone-based trapping. These present a substantially lower environmental risk profile: laboratory bioassays report 90 to 100 percent larval mortality for Metarhizium isolates from East Java, comparable to the up to 98 percent larval and 90 percent adult mortality reported for a granular carbamate alternative, indicating technical efficacy is not the limiting factor, with field-deployed monitoring documented in Jepara and Bengkulu. Uptake of these lower-risk options is nonetheless constrained less by technical efficacy than by production economics, extension access, and the fragmented governance of smallholder replanting and pest-management programs. The evidence suggests that attenuating this risk burden is predominantly constrained by the disparity between existing lower-risk technological interventions and their operational uptake, among other compounding determinants. Risk-management strategies must therefore be designed around smallholder economic and institutional realities rather than efficacy data alone. Authors: Hu H.; Zhao F.; Wang Z.; Zhang Z.; Wu D.; Wang Z.; Xie J.
Title: Digital modeling for rapid prediction and multi-objective optimization of the entire microstructure and property fields of complex components in die forging
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Die forging components used in high-end manufacturing have complex geometries and many interacting process variables, complicating accurate prediction and control of the entire microstructure and properties. This work proposes a method integrating finite element simulations, a limited number of forging experiments, and machine learning to enable rapid and precise prediction and optimization of die forging component's entire microstructure and property. First, finite element simulations were conducted under 114 different sets of process parameters. The deformation physical quantities (mean deformation temperature, mean strain rate, mean equivalent stress, and equivalent strain throughout the forging process) were obtained at 100 feature points on the forgings. Using forging process parameters and feature point coordinates as inputs, deformation physical quantity prediction models (DPQ models) were established employing the gradient boosting algorithm. Next, forging experiments were conducted under 16 different sets of process parameters. The microstructure and properties were measured at six sampling points in forging samples, including grain size, recrystallization volume fraction, grain aspect ratio, and hardness. Using deformation physical quantities as inputs, microstructure and property prediction models (MP models) were developed employing the random forest algorithm. The DPQ and MP models were then connected in series and combined with thin plate spline interpolation to enable rapid prediction of forging's entire microstructure and property fields. Prediction time is on the order of seconds, with errors below 10%. For forging process parameters optimization, a multi-objective optimization method based on a genetic algorithm was developed to achieve grain refinement, hardness improvement, and homogenization of grain size and hardness. This work offers valuable insights and methodological references for real-time prediction and intelligent control of the microstructure and properties of die forgings. © 2026

Title: Characterization of shale gas adsorption behavior based on the gravimetric method
Abstract: Based on gravimetric isothermal adsorption experiments, methane adsorption isotherms were obtained under different temperature and pressure conditions. High-pressure adsorption models were used to investigate methane adsorption behavior and its controlling factors in shale, and machine-learning methods were further introduced to predict adsorption capacity and quantify the influence of different parameters. The dual-site Langmuir model, supercritical Dubinin-Radushkevich model, and Ono-Kondo lattice model were employed to fit and compare high-pressure adsorption behavior over the full pressure range. For machine-learning prediction, temperature, pressure, total organic carbon, and vitrinite reflectance were selected as input variables, and excess adsorption capacity was used as the output variable. The results show that the absolute methane adsorption capacity of shale generally increases rapidly with pressure at the initial stage and then gradually approaches a plateau, while it decreases significantly with increasing temperature. The Ono-Kondo lattice model exhibits the best fitting stability and physical interpretability across different pressure ranges, effectively characterizing adsorption behavior under supercritical conditions. Factor analysis indicates that total organic carbon is positively correlated with methane adsorption capacity, whereas temperature shows a negative correlation. Thermal maturity, as represented by vitrinite reflectance, also affects methane adsorption capacity; however, its apparent influence is nonlinear and coupled with total organic carbon content. Among the machine-learning models, CatBoost achieves the highest prediction accuracy, with a coefficient of determination of 0.9528, indicating strong nonlinear fitting capability. SHAP-based interpretability analysis shows that the importance of different parameters controlling methane adsorption capacity follows the order: pressure > total organic carbon > temperature > vitrinite reflectance. This study provides experimental evidence and methodological support for understanding high-pressure shale gas adsorption mechanisms, accurately characterizing adsorption capacity, and evaluating geological gas-in-place in the Xujiahe Formation of the Sichuan Basin. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Interface-stabilized MXene/nanofiber film for integrated thermoelectric sensing and electromagnetic interference shielding
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of wearable electronics demands materials that enable simultaneous physiological monitoring and protection against electromagnetic interference (EMI), yet these functions are typically decoupled into separate components. Here, we report an interface-stabilized thermoplastic polyurethane/pluronic F127/MXene/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) nanofiber film treated with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), denoted TFMPD, for thermoelectric sensing, EMI shielding, and shielding-state feedback. F127-mediated surface hydrophilization and polyethyleneimine activation promote MXene deposition on the nanofiber film, while DMSO treatment reorganizes PEDOT:PSS and consolidates the conductive coating through solvent-assisted fiber welding. The film shows thermoelectric voltage responses to small temperature differences, with a temperature resolution of 0.07 K and a response time of ∼410 ms, enabling self-powered respiration and body-temperature monitoring. The same conductive network achieves an X-band EMI shielding effectiveness of ∼44 dB with reflection-dominated attenuation and retains stable shielding performance after 5000 bending cycles and three months of ambient exposure. By correlating sheet resistance with EMI shielding degradation, the film further enables resistance-based evaluation of healthy, warning, and failure-risk states. This work provides a flexible conductive-interface strategy for wearable systems requiring thermal-signal monitoring, EMI protection, and service-state feedback. © 2026

Title: Microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia shrinkage and their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios
Abstract: Lake Urmia, one of the world's largest hypersaline lakes, has experienced dramatic shrinkage over recent decades, raising concerns regarding its impacts on regional climate, urban thermal environments, and energy sustainability. This study investigates microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia desiccation and evaluates their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios. An integrated framework combining multi-temporal remote sensing observations, climate data, urban thermal indicators, and energy-emission modeling was employed to quantify relationships among lake shrinkage, land surface temperature, urban heat island intensity, cooling demand, and carbon emissions. Results show that Lake Urmia's surface area declined from 5420 km2 in 1990 to 610 km2 in 2025, representing an 88.7% reduction. This hydrological decline was accompanied by substantial thermal amplification, with mean Land Surface Temperature increasing from 28.4°C to 36.4°C and maximum Land Surface Temperature rising from 34.8°C to 47.1°C. Vegetation degradation was also pronounced, with the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index decreasing from 0.46 to 0.23. Concurrent urban expansion intensified thermal stress, increasing surface urban heat island intensity from 1.8°C to 4.7°C in Urmia and from 2.1°C to 5.2°C in Tabriz. Correlation analysis revealed strong relationships between lake area and LST (R = −0.87), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Land Surface Temperature (R = −0.81), Land Surface Temperature and Urban Heat Island intensity (R = 0.79), and LST and cooling demand (R = 0.84). Future climate projections indicate temperature increases of 1.4°C, 2.6°C, and 4.1°C by 2050 under the SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, respectively, resulting in projected increases in cooling demand of 18–36%. Given Iran's electricity sector's fossil-fuel dependence, rising cooling demand is expected to increase carbon emissions. These findings highlight Lake Urmia desiccation as a coupled hydro-climatic–urban-energy challenge requiring integrated restoration, climate adaptation, and sustainable energy strategies. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Zr-regulated discontinuous precipitation suppressing intermediate-temperature embrittlement in L12-strengthened HEAs
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Intermediate-temperature embrittlement (ITE) limits the structural reliability of L12-strengthened high-entropy alloys (HEAs). However, the microstructural origin of preferential grain-boundary damage during ITE, particularly the role of discontinuous precipitation (DP), remains unclear. In the heat-treated Al0.5Cr0.9FeNi2.5V0.2 HEA, ITE is closely associated with preferential damage along DP-affected grain boundaries. Here, we reveal that trace Zr microalloying mitigates ITE by regulating this damage process. Zr addition increases the elongation at 700 °C from ∼2.5% to ∼23.4% while retaining comparable strength. Multiscale characterization reveals that Zr substantially reduces the DP area fraction, refines DP colonies, and modifies the body-centered cubic morphology within the DP regions by decreasing the proportion of lamellar constituents. The refined DP structure disrupts continuous brittle damage pathways and delays grain-boundary crack initiation. In addition, serrated grain boundaries may further impede crack propagation. Consequently, the dominant failure mode shifts from intergranular fracture to ductile fracture. These findings indicate that Zr-induced DP refinement mitigates grain-boundary damage and improves ductility in the studied alloy at 700 °C, suggesting a potential microstructural design route for alleviating ITE in L12-strengthened HEAs. © 2026

Title: Comparative optimization of biohydrogen production and purification using pressure swing adsorption
Abstract: Biohydrogen production has emerged as a promising alternative for the development of sustainable energy systems due to its high calorific value and potential to reduce polluting emissions. Among the most efficient purification technologies, pressure swing adsorption stands out for its ability to increase hydrogen purity through selective separation processes. The objective of this article is to perform a sensitivity analysis and parametric study, which allows for the identification of the most influential operating variables on the performance of the rigorous pressure swing adsorption process. Therefore, the evaluation of a two-bed pressure swing adsorption plant is fundamental to optimizing key indicators such as energy efficiency, productivity, and biohydrogen recovery. Significant results were achieved, as the sensitivity analysis showed that the best breakthrough curve was obtained by using the temperature variable, which adsorbed a greater amount of the compounds CO2, CO, and CH4 in a shorter time (300 s[jls-end-space/]) compared to the other variables. The results obtained from the parametric study after achieving a biohydrogen purity of 99.9% were outstanding, as it was determined that the composition variable resulted in a greater retention of CO2 along the column. However, with the temperature variable, the purity of the biohydrogen was 99.1% compared to the other purities obtained (production and purge pressure variables). A recovery of 60.24% was achieved, with a productivity of 0.0021 (Formula presented) and an energy efficiency that ranged between 0.89% and 2.10%. © 2026 The Authors. Title: IrMn-Cluster-Based Artificial Metalloenzymes with Radiosensitized Systemic Antitumor Responses to Prevent Malignant Tumor Metastasis and Recurrence
Abstract: Developing radiosensitizing agents to amplify tumor-eradicating effects on primary, regional recurrence, and distant metastases plays a transformative role in modern cancer care. Here, we report the de novo design of biocatalytic artificial metalloenzymes with an IrMn-cluster-based redox center (IMM) to achieve radiosensitized systemic antitumor responses for preventing malignant tumor metastasis and recurrence. Notably, our findings indicate that Mn-organic ligands substantially enrich the electron density of Ir clusters, thereby optimizing their interaction with oxygen species and markedly enhancing the production of both reactive oxygen species and molecular oxygen. When combined with radiotherapy, the IMM effectively amplifies DNA damage and induces pronounced apoptosis by alleviating intratumoral hypoxia. This shift reprograms the tumor microenvironment, enhancing radiosensitivity and facilitating the infiltration and activation of intratumoral CD8⁺ T cells and dendritic cells. Moreover, when integrated with anti-PD-1 therapy, this coordinated therapeutic regimen elicits potent systemic immune responses and durable antitumor memory, effectively suppressing tumor recurrence and metastasis while markedly improving therapeutic efficacy and long-term survival. Title: Orientation-geometry correction for quantitative radial Raman analysis of carbon fiber based on the G-band tensor
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Radial Raman spectroscopy is widely utilized to probe the skin-core architecture of carbon fibers. However, the continuous variation in spatial orientation of graphitic crystallites across the cross-section heavily modulates the Raman scattering intensity under a fixed polarized laser. Consequently, the conventionally measured Raman intensity ratio (AD1/AG) manifests as a convoluted apparent signal, where intrinsic microstructural gradients are severely distorted by geometric optical artifacts. To address this fundamental challenge, we established a rigorous orientation-geometry decoupling framework grounded in Raman tensor physics. Utilizing highly oriented pyrolytic graphite as a macroscopic, structurally uniform model, the exact E2g G-band tensor response was experimentally isolated to purely formulate the geometric modulation mechanism. To systematically evaluate this methodology, this framework was applied to a comprehensive library of polyacrylonitrile-based carbon fibers with customized structural states. By correlating the recovered intrinsic Raman responses (R′) with the reciprocal in-plane crystallite size of graphene (1/La) independently derived from micro-beam wide-angle X-ray scattering—a bulk technique fundamentally immune to optical polarization interferences—we confirm the accuracy and reliability of the proposed decoupling process. The tensor-based decoupling effectively strips away optical measurement artifacts and substantially strengthens the linear correlation between R′ and 1/La. More importantly, the post-decoupling slopes move closer to the theoretical expectation of the Tuinstra-Koenig relation. This work provides a universal physical paradigm for the authentic quantitative profiling of highly anisotropic carbon materials. © 2026

Title: Consumer awareness, participation, and accessibility in sustainable electronic waste management
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid increase in electronic waste has created increasingly complex environmental and health challenges, especially in developing countries like Indonesia. The study objectives were to examine how household awareness and accessibility of electronic-waste management facilities are associated with consumer participation, controlling for socioeconomic factors, demographics, and the region's spatial characteristics. METHODS: This study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine household consumers living near electronic waste management facilities in Indonesia. To analyze the data, Spearman's rank correlation was employed to evaluate variable relationships, ordinary least squares regression to estimate the associations of awareness and accessibility with participation levels, Kruskal-Wallis test to examine group differences, and Geographic Information System-based spatial analysis to describe the spatial patterns of facility distance, accessibility, and electronic waste management participation. FINDINGS: Consumer awareness of the consequences of electronic waste showed a significant positive correlation with the intention to manage electronic waste, with a correlation coefficient of 0.340, but showed no significant correlation with actual behavior, with a correlation coefficient of only 0.067. Accessibility showed a significant positive correlation with both intention and actual behavior, with correlation coefficients of 0.197 and 0.416, respectively. Accessibility had the largest reported regression coefficient for actual behavior ( β = 0.449 ), followed by awareness of consequences ( β = 0.182 ). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed significant differences in intention and actual behavior across accessibility levels, with chi-square values of 11.67 and 35.91, respectively. Spatial analysis using the nearest neighbor method produced a nearest neighbor ratio of 0.60 with a z score of -10.01. Spatial analysis revealed that highly aware and active residents are significantly clustered rather than randomly dispersed, with the vast majority residing within a functional catchment area defined by 10 to 30 kilometer distances or 10 to 30 minute travel times from e-waste facilities. CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for electronic waste management policies that prioritise facility accessibility and spatially based approaches to strengthen community participation within a circular economy framework. Authors: Liu S.; Hong X.; Wang Z.
Title: Liquid-Core Long Period Grating Temperature Sensor Fabricated by Femtosecond Laser Line Scanning
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: We propose a novel liquid-core long-period fiber grating (LPFG) based on a hollow-core fiber (HCF). The grating is fabricated using a femtosecond laser line-scanning technique to periodically induce refractive index modulation in the silica region adjacent to the air core. By infiltrating a high-refractive-index liquid into the HCF, a liquid-core waveguide is formed, enabling resonant coupling between the fundamental core mode and cladding modes, which gives rise to distinct resonant dips. The dispersion characteristics of the liquid-filled fiber can be tailored through the refractive index of the infiltrated liquid. By optimizing this parameter, enhanced temperature sensitivity is achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that the temperature response of the LPFG strongly depends on the refractive index of the filling liquid. In particular, when a liquid with a refractive index of 1.476 is used, a high temperature sensitivity of approximately −3.34 nm/°C is obtained over the range of 25–40 °C. The proposed device provides a proof-of-concept platform for high-sensitivity liquid-core LPFG temperature sensing. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Liu Y.; Tang B.; Li J.; Ai F.; Dong A.
Title: Strain partitioning and recrystallization suppression via intralamellar β0 precipitates in a β-solidified γ-TiAl alloy during hot deformation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The β0 phase is an important phase in TiAl alloys, and its influence on the hot deformation behavior warrants in-depth investigation. In this study, the hot deformation behavior of a heat-treated (HT) specimen, in which β0 precipitates are formed within the (α2/γ) lamellae, is compared with that of an as-cast specimen free of such intralamellar precipitates. The results show that the HT specimens exhibit a lower peak stress and a slightly decreased work-hardening rate compared to the as-cast specimens, indicating that the intralamellar β0 (IL-β0) precipitates can moderately improve the hot workability of the TiAl alloy. After deformation, a high density of γ twins is formed in the lamellar colonies of both specimens; however, the twin density within the lamellae of HT specimens is distinctly lower than that of the as-cast microstructure. Furthermore, twin pairs are clearly identified in the HT specimen, whose formation arises from the propagation and traversal of twins across γ/γ interfaces generated via the α2 → γ phase transformation. Such effects are proposed to stem from the fact that the IL-β0 precipitates in the HT specimens undergo intrinsic plastic deformation and effectively mediate strain partitioning between adjacent α2 and γ lamellae. This interphase coordination is considered to be responsible for: (i) reduced twin density in the γ lamellae, (ii) the alleviated stress concentration within the α2/γ colonies, and (iii) the delayed recrystallization of the γ lamellae. Collectively, elucidating the role of IL‑β0 precipitates in modulating hot‑deformation behavior and lamellar recrystallization provides valuable insights for the rational optimization of thermomechanical processing of TiAl alloys. © 2026

Title: Analytic hierarchy process-based criterion weighting for water resources management projects
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Prioritizing water resources projects requires decision-makers to balance hydrological performance, engineering feasibility, environmental and social sustainability, and economic value under limited budgets and implementation resources. Conventional evaluation frameworks are frequently bound to specific project typologies or geographical contexts, thereby constraining their direct applicability across heterogeneous project portfolios. The study objectives were to develop an analytic hierarchy process-based multi-criteria decision-making framework for deriving criterion weights for water resources management project assessment, using Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as the empirical context. METHODS: The framework was developed by synthesizing water resources management principles, practical project-assessment considerations, and relevant multi-criteria decision-making literature. The evaluation model comprised four principal dimensions and 18 operational sub-criteria. The Analytical hierarchy process framework was employed to analyze expert judgments elicited from six senior water resources and irrigation specialists, each possessing a minimum of 20 years of professional experience. Individual judgments were subsequently evaluated for consistency and aggregated using the geometric mean. Local weights were calculated using the eigenvector method and combined with the corresponding main-dimension weights to obtain global priorities. FINDINGS: Engineering and Implementation Feasibility received the highest main-dimension weight (32.58 percent), followed by Economic performance (25.84 percent), Environmental and Social Sustainability (21.87 percent), and Water Resource and Hydrological Performance (19.71 percent). At the global level, cost effectiveness ranked first (13.99 percent), followed by Structural Scale (11.58 percent), Foundation Suitability (10.60 percent), and Storage and Hydrological Adequacy (8.93 percent). These four sub-criteria accounted for 45.10 percent of the total weight. Accounting for 81.88 percent of the total weight and encompassing elements across all four dimensions, the top 11 sub-criteria demonstrate that comprehensive assessment necessitates an integrated approach spanning technical, economic, hydrological, environmental, and social dimensions. CONCLUSION: By establishing a transparent architecture for criterion organization and context-specific priority derivation, the framework facilitates water resources project evaluation. Integrated with empirical performance data and explicit scoring protocols, it underpins the formulation of robust project screening, portfolio comparative analysis, and budgetary prioritization procedures. The reported weights represent the judgments of the study panel and should be recalibrated for other locations, project types, and stakeholder groups. Subsequent applications of this framework should formulate a structured operational scoring rubric while comprehensively evaluating parameter sensitivity, model robustness, and project-ranking stability. Authors: Zhou C.; Chen J.; Zhu D.; Hui S.; Zhan L.
Title: Electric pulse-induced inversion of asymmetric tension-compression creep in an Al-Cu-Li alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Experiments confirm that incorporating electroplasticity into creep aging facilitates dislocation motion and accelerates creep deformation. While tension-compression creep asymmetry is well-documented under normal thermo-mechanical coupling, its electro-thermo-mechanical counterpart remains rarely investigated. Herein, we studied the asymmetric creep response of an Al-Cu-Li alloy under tensile and compressive stress during electro-assisted creep. We found that electric pulses reverse the conventional tension-compression creep asymmetry. Contrary to the ordinary pattern where tensile creep rate exceeds compressive creep rate, the electroplastic compressive creep rate surpasses its tensile counterpart. Microstructural data show that at the creep onset, the dislocation loop density in compressive specimens is nearly three times that in tensile counterparts. Further analyses indicate that electric pulses promote the evolution of those extra dislocation loops into short dislocation lines, thereby increasing the number density of mobile dislocations and compressive creep rate. In short, electric pulses transform creep-restricting extra dislocation loops into highly mobile short dislocation lines within compressive specimens, resulting in a higher electroplastic compressive creep rate. This work advances the understanding of tension-compression asymmetric creep of aluminum alloys under electro-thermo-mechanical coupling. © 2026

Authors: Li C.; Wu Y.; Zheng B.; Zhang X.; Hui X.; Li S.; Wang Y.
Title: Coupling composition design with defect engineering: An oxygen-doped Ti-Zr-Nb strain glass alloy with enhanced high-temperature shape memory effect
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-temperature shape memory alloys (HTSMAs) are critical for temperature-sensitive applications, yet the trade-off between high transformation temperatures and large recoverable strains remains a long-standing challenge. This study addresses this limitation by deploying a composition control and defect engineering strategy to regulate the martensitic transformation in HTSMAs via a strain glass while preserving elevated transformation temperatures. By introducing 1 at.% oxygen as point defects, a Ti47Zr47Nb5O1 strain glass alloy with a freezing temperature of about 462 K was fabricated. The microstructure consists of a strain‑glass‑dominated β matrix with minor residual α″ martensite. The low Nb content destabilizes the β phase, enabling the alloy to retain a high transformation temperature of about 745 K. Enabled by the strain glass state and the remarkable theoretical transformation strain derived from the addition of high-content Zr with large atomic radius, this alloy exhibits nearly full recoverability for pre‑strains up to about 5%, and achieves a shape memory recovery strain of ∼5.7% at a pre‑strain of 10%, outperforming most reported HTSMAs. The underlying deformation mechanism is attributed to the stress-induced reversible β → α″ martensitic transformation together with martensitic variant reorientation, which cooperatively accommodate local strains within nanoscale domains. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Title: Strategic deployment of seasonal thermal energy storage for decarbonizing remote northern communities in Canada: A multidimensional evaluation framework
Abstract: Remote northern communities face major energy-transition challenges due to extreme climates, prolonged heating seasons, geographic isolation, dependence on imported fossil fuels, and limited energy infrastructure. Seasonal Thermal Energy Storage (STES) can address the mismatch between renewable heat availability and winter heating demand, but technology selection must account for environmental, geological, logistical, economic, and socio-technical constraints alongside conventional engineering performance. This review evaluates seven STES technologies using a northern-specific multidimensional framework integrating thermodynamic performance, technical maturity, economic performance, constructability and logistics, permafrost compatibility, and community implementation capacity. The framework operationalizes this assessment through non-compensable feasibility screening and TOPSIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis using a literature-informed technology-performance matrix, an equal-weight reference, two contrasting northern deployment archetypes, and weight- and score-sensitivity analyses. Results show that suitability depends on the interaction between technology characteristics and deployment context rather than engineering performance alone. Tank Thermal Energy Storage (TTES) exhibits the most robustly favourable profile across the evaluated scenarios and sensitivity analyses, whereas Pit Thermal Energy Storage (PTES), Borehole Thermal Energy Storage (BTES), and Rock Thermal Energy Storage (RTES) are more context dependent. Phase Change Material (PCM) and Thermochemical Energy Storage (TCES) offer high theoretical storage potential but remain limited by large-scale operational validation, while Aquifer Thermal Energy Storage (ATES) is conditional on suitable hydrogeological conditions. The proposed framework shifts STES selection from performance-based ranking toward context-driven decision support, providing developers, utilities, engineering practitioners, and community decision-makers with a transparent and reproducible methodology for identifying robust candidates, context-sensitive alternatives, and critical deployment constraints before detailed site-specific assessment in northern Canada and other circumpolar regions. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Sarkar R.; M Y.H.; Sahoo R.N.; Chatterjee P.; Singh C.; Rajna S.
Title: EVALUATION OF UAV-ADMINISTERED INSECTICIDES AT DIFFERENT DOSES AGAINST BROWN PLANTHOPPER NILAPARVATA LUGENS (STAL)
Abstract: The study aimed to evaluate the bioefficacy of triflumezopyrim 10 SC and pymetrozine 50 WG applied through an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for managing brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens) in rice, and to assess their effect on its key predator, the mirid bug (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis). A field experiment was conducted during kharif 2024 at ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, using rice variety Pusa Basmati 1885 under natural pest infestation. Each insecticide was applied at different rates, i.e., 0.75x, 1x and 1.5x concentrations of the recommended dose using a calibrated Marut 365S multi-rotor UAV. Population counts of BPH and mirid bugs were recorded on tagged hills before spraying and at 5 and 10 days after spraying (DAS). Both insecticides significantly reduced BPH populations at 10 DAS compared to the untreated control, with hopper counts declining to below two insects/ hill across all treated plots. No statistically significant differences were observed among the three dose levels of either insecticide, indicating that even the reduced dose (0.75x) was equally effective under UAV application. Mirid bug populations showed a moderate decline in treated plots but remained comparatively higher in reduced-dose treatments, suggesting lower non-target impact. The findings demonstrate that UAV-based application of triflumezopyrim and pymetrozine is effective for BPH suppression even at reduced doses, while causing comparatively less disruption to the predator community. Reduced-dose UAV application therefore offers potential advantages for resistance management, environmental safety, and integration within rice IPM programs, while reducing pesticide input and application costs. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. Title: Enhanced prediction of reservoir porosity and permeability via a Second Spectrum-inspired hybrid framework integrating LSTM, Random Forest, and SHAP
Abstract: Accurate prediction of reservoir porosity and permeability from wireline well logs remain a central challenge in subsurface characterization, owing to the nonlinear, non-stationary, and spatially autocorrelated nature of petrophysical data. This study presents the Second Spectrum Dual-Pathway Framework, a novel hybrid machine learning architecture conceptually adapted from the NBA Second Spectrum spatiotemporal player-tracking system, which separates macro-level spatial patterns from micro-level sequential dynamics. Applied to 12,101 well-log samples from the Southeastern Sichuan Basin (8 input features: GR, AC, CAL, CNL, DEN, SP, RXO, PE), the framework integrates two complementary learning pathways: Pathway 1 deploys a Random Forest (RF) regressor (n = 200 trees, max_features = √p, min_samples_leaf = 4) as a macro-level, point-wise nonlinear mapper, achieving R2 = 0.8619, MAE = 0.1772, and RMSE = 0.3003 for porosity, and R2 = 0.8357, MAE = 0.0728 (log10 scale) for permeability. Pathway 2 employs a two-layer Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM; 64 and 32 units, dropout = 0.25, L2 = 10−4, Layer Normalization) trained on RF residuals to model depth-axis sequential autocorrelation — a mechanism physically justified by Durbin–Watson statistics < 1.5 across all logs, confirming strong positive stratigraphic continuity. The hybrid combination (ŷ_hybrid = ŷ_RF + ε_BiLSTM) yields R2 = 0.8620, MAE = 0.1773, and RMSE = 0.3002 for porosity, demonstrating that the BiLSTM residual pathway captures depth-trending prediction errors unresolved by the spatial model alone. Five-fold cross-validation confirms stable generalization across geological intervals (porosity: mean R2 = 0.8696 ± 0.0116; permeability: mean R2 = 0.8440 ± 0.0246). Ensemble-based prediction intervals (RF tree variance) achieve a 90 % PI empirical coverage of 98.97 %, with higher predictive uncertainty localized in high-permeability zones (mean σ = 0.1103 log10 mD) relative to tight matrix intervals (mean σ = 0.1857 log10 mD), consistent with heterogeneous pore network structures beyond wireline log resolution. Explainability is provided via Tree SHAP (RF) and GradientSHAP (BiLSTM): for porosity, the acoustic log (AC; mean |SHAP| = 0.1979) ranks first, followed by GR (0.0985), SP (0.0919), and DEN (0.0909), consistent with established density-porosity and sonic transit time transforms. For permeability, DEN and CNL retain dominance while RXO gains relative importance, reflecting pore connectivity encoded in flushed-zone invasion. Critically, the BiLSTM SHAP profile diverges from the RF profile depth-sensitive logs gain relative attribution in the sequential pathway confirming that the two pathways model complementary and physically distinct geological signals. The total training pipeline executes in approximately 149 s (RF: 18 s; BiLSTM: 131 s), with sub-second inference at deployment. The framework is directly integratable into petrophysical evaluation platforms (Techlog, Interactive Petrophysics) and supports uncertainty-aware population of 3D geomodels via P10–P90 permeability realizations. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhancing Na-ion conduction in Na3Zr2Si2PO12 electrolyte for solid-state sodium batteries via Na/Si/P ratio regulation strategy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: NASICON-type Na3Zr2Si2PO12 (NZSP) has received extensive attention as an electrolyte for solid-state sodium batteries (SSSBs) owing to its good air stability and chemical durability. However, low ionic conductivity and poor interfacial contact are major challenges for the application of NZSP electrolyte in SSSBs. Herein, an intrinsic Na/Si/P ratio regulation strategy is adopted to optimize the crystal structure and Na-ion transport behavior of the NZSP electrolyte, enhancing its ionic conductivity and electrochemical performance. A series of Na3+xZr2Si2+xP1−xO12 (x = 0–0.3) electrolytes are synthesized by a sol-gel method, and the influence of intrinsic Na/Si/P ratio variation on the crystal structure, microstructure, ionic conductivity, and electrochemical performance is systematically investigated. The optimized Na3.1Zr2Si2.1P0.9O12 (NZSP0.1) exhibits effective enhancement of electrical and electrochemical performance, achieving an improved ionic conductivity of 0.26 mS cm−1, which is approximately three times higher than that of NZSP. A Na/NZSP0.1/Na symmetric battery demonstrates reduced interfacial resistance and an elevated critical current density of about 0.42 mA cm−2, enabling stable sodium plating and stripping for 400 h at 0.05 mA cm−2. Moreover, a Na3V2(PO4)3/NZSP0.1/Na full battery delivers favorable rate capability and cycling stability. This work presents a simple and effective strategy to prepare advanced NZSP-based electrolytes for application in SSSBs. © 2026

Title: Enhancing accounting students’ writing performance through problem-based learning: Evidence from a vocational higher education context
Abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) has gained momentum in English for specific purpose (ESP) education, yet little is known about how PBL functions in vocational higher education settings for accounting for students' writing. This study investigated the effectiveness, benefits, and challenges associated with accounting students' writing performance. This study employs a mixed-methods design involving 60 students from one of the state polytechnics in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. The experimental group (N=30) experienced PBL, and the control group (N=30) received conventional learning. Data were collected through writing tests to investigate students' improvement in their writing performance, and interviews to explore students' perceptions of benefits and challenges. The results of the writing test were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics via SPSS, and the interview results were analyzed using thematic analysis. The quantitative results reveal that there is a significant difference in the writing performance of accounting students who were taught by using PBL and those who were taught by using conventional learning, with PBL being better than conventional learning. It can be concluded that PBL is effective at enhancing accounting students' writing performance. The qualitative results of the interviews revealed that the accounting students mentioned the benefits of PBL, including improvement in students' writing skills, development of students' problem-solving skills, development of students' critical thinking, team collaboration, and real accounting problem connections. However, they listed the challenges of PBL, which include difficulty relating to the varied ideas and a lack of experience with the problems. Future research is recommended to extend the study duration to better capture the lasting impacts of PBL, offering a more comprehensive understanding of this approach. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Ultramicropore-Confined Solvation and Interphase Regulation Unlock High-Performance Hard Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
Abstract: Hard carbon (HC) anodes are promising for sodium-ion batteries, yet achieving high initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), large plateau contribution, and fast charge-transfer kinetics remains challenging due to insufficient control of micro–nanostructure and interphase chemistry. Here, we present a precursor-level molecular engineering strategy that simultaneously regulates sodium desolvation and interphase chemistry in HC. An iodine-mediated oxidative cross-linking process converts starch into spherical HC with uniformly distributed ultramicropores and carbonyl-rich surfaces. These nanoconfined pores are proposed to act as molecular sieves, preferentially excluding bulky solvent molecules while allowing PF6−-coordinated Na+ access, thereby favoring anion-enriched electrolyte structures under confinement. Surface carbonyls exhibit strong PF6− affinity, which may promote fluorine-rich inorganic interphases on pore surfaces. The synergistic effects of anion-selective adsorption and confined desolvation are suggested to favor thin and robust NaF-rich interphases at external surfaces and within nanoconfined pore regions, contributing to reversible interfacial reactions and rapid Na+ storage kinetics. Consequently, the HC delivers an ICE of 88.4%, a reversible capacity of 352.9 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, excellent rate capability (288.9 mAh g−1 at 5C), and 95.6% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This work offers a molecular-level design paradigm integrating efficiency, capacity, and kinetics in HC anodes. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Effect of ECAP on the microstructure and mechanical properties of titanium fabricated by thermomechanical particle consolidation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: In this work, fully dense titanium fabricated by thermomechanical consolidation of titanium sponge particles was processed by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP) to refine its microstructure and improve its mechanical properties. It was found that 4 passes of ECAP carried out at 400 °C with a channel angle of 120° caused a significant change in the microstructure and mechanical properties of the titanium: an ultrafine-grained structure consisting of equiaxed grains in the range of 0.2–20 µm and with a high density of dislocations (4.36 × 1013 m−2) was formed, the yield strength increased from 186 to 380 MPa, the ultimate tensile strength increased from 293 to 418 MPa, but the elongation to fracture decreased from 45% to 22% which shows that the ECAP processed titanium still exhibits an excellent ductility. The strength increase can be attributed to the combined effect of grain refinement (Hall–Petch strengthening) and dislocation hardening (Taylor strengthening), while the ductility decrease is associated with the drastic flow stress increase and the decrease of the strain hardening rate resulting from strain hardening. Title: Numerical Investigation of Flow Control Around Three Cylinders using a Passive Method
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This study investigates the flow behavior around three cylinders with attached splitter plates arranged in an equilateral triangular configuration using the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) at low Reynolds numbers (Re). Although previous research has focused on flow around bluff bodies without splitter plates, this study examines the effects of splitter plates on flow control. The primary objective is to explore passive flow control methods-those requiring no external energy-around the cylinders. Key parameters analyzed include Reynolds number (Re), gap ratio (g∗ ), and splitter plate length (L∗). The investigation considers three different Re values, five g∗ values, and five L∗ values for each g∗ . Drag coefficients (CD), lift coefficients (CL ), and Strouhal numbers (St ) are computed to elucidate the relationships between vortex shedding characteristics, g∗, L∗, and Re. The results demonstrate that wake flow patterns, flow characteristics, and force coefficients are strongly influenced by g∗, L∗ and Re. Distinct flow regimes emerge: at low g∗ and L∗, the three cylinders behave as a single bluff body (SBB), whereas at large g∗ and L∗, the flow transitions to a continuous pattern, diminishing the interaction effects among the cylinders. For small L∗, vortices form near the cylinders, while larger L∗ results in streamlined flow. Additionally, at low Re, vortex shedding remains consistent, but as Re increases, the vortices become irregular. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Abstract: This paper presents the results of a study aimed at improving the reliability of predicting hidden fracturing in the near-contour rock mass adjacent to underground mine workings at a polymetallic mine. The study included analysis of the mining and geological conditions of the deposit, laser scanning of mine working sections, spatial fracture analysis in ShapeMetriX, numerical modeling in RocTunnel3, and GPR profiling using the GROT 12N system. It was established that the highest reliability of hidden fracturing prediction is achieved through the sequential integration of 3D survey data, spatial fracture analysis, and GPR investigation. Title: Polyhydroxy Molecular Regulator Enabled Interfacial Microenvironment Programming for Alkaline Zinc–Iron Flow Batteries
Abstract: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (ZIFBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost, intrinsic safety, and scalable architecture, yet their practical deployment remains hindered by hydrogen evolution and uncontrolled Zn deposition in three-dimensional porous electrodes. Here, we report that isomalt acts as a polyhydroxy molecular regulator that reconfigures the interfacial microenvironment of porous carbon felt, thereby endowing the porous electrode with a more deposition-directing function for reversible Zn plating/stripping. In the bulk electrolyte, isomalt reconstructs the local hydrogen-bond network, lowers water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. At the carbon/electrolyte interface, its preferential lateral adsorption establishes a hydroxyl-rich interphase that homogenizes zincate transport and directs Zn growth toward a preferred (002) orientation, thus promoting compact and reversible deposition. This interfacial microenvironment programming markedly reduces the charge-transfer resistance and activation barrier of the Zn anode, enabling stable cycling for over 500 cycles at 20 mA cm−2. In full-cell tests, the optimized ZIFB delivers a high energy efficiency of 87.5%, substantially outperforming the pristine electrolyte. Beyond identifying a low-cost green additive, this work establishes polyhydroxy molecules as interfacial programming units for three-dimensional porous electrodes, offering a new design concept for directional metal deposition in aqueous flow-battery systems. Title: Morphology-tunable ZrO2@SiC@NiCo2O4/NiO composite fibers for integrated high-temperature electromagnetic wave absorption and multifunctional performance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption materials with high-temperature tolerance is urgently required for applications in extreme environments, including stealth aircraft and aeroengine heating components. Traditional EMW absorption materials primarily exhibit outstanding EMW absorption performance at room temperature. However, maintaining long-term performance in extreme environments remains challenging. To address this challenge, morphology-tunable ZrO2@ silicon carbide (SiC)@NiCo2O4/NiO composite fibers were constructed through electrospinning and hydrothermal reactions to integrate room-temperature and high-temperature EMW absorption. SiC fibers, renowned for their high-temperature stability and oxidation resistance, served as thermally robust frameworks for the controlled growth and spatial dispersion of NiCo2O4/NiO nanostructures. The results show that the sheet-like NiCo2O4/NiO-decorated ZrO2@SiC fibers achieve an effective absorption bandwidth of 7.4 GHz and maintain 7.3 GHz after heat treatment at 450 °C. Interfacial polarization at the heterogeneous interfaces between components significantly enhances EMW absorption. Furthermore, the fibers exhibit outstanding thermal insulation, flame retardancy, and infrared stealth properties. This material is a promising candidate for structural-functional integration in extreme environments and is suitable for demanding aerospace and military applications. © 2026

Authors: Di J.; Lv Y.; Li Z.; Sun Y.; Wang N.; Bo L.; Cheng Z.; Wang Y.; Su S.; Ning Z.; Sun J.; Pu J.; Huang Y.
Title: Effect of laser shock peening on the corrosion resistance of additively manufactured AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Here, laser shock peening (LSP) was employed to tailor the near-surface microstructure and corrosion behavior of laser-directed energy-deposited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) in 0.6 M NaCl solution. The LSP process preserved the face-centered cubic (FCC)/body-centered cubic (BCC) dual-phase constitution, and markedly modified the deformation microstructure. Within the FCC phase, the deformation microstructure evolved progressively with increasing laser impacts from dislocations to stacking faults, Lomer-Cottrell locks, nanotwins, and ultimately a 9R structure. However, the BCC phase primarily accommodated dislocation tangling, localized stacking faults, and heterogeneous lattice strain. All LSP-treated samples showed improved passivation relative to the as-built sample. Among the investigated conditions, twice LSP impacts (LSP-2) showed the most favorable overall passivation response, with the widest passive range (565.27 mV), the lowest passive current density (5.52 × 10−7 A cm−2), and the highest polarization resistance (24.24 × 105 Ω cm2). However, four LSP impacts (LSP-4) led to a deterioration in corrosion resistance relative to LSP-2 despite producing the highest compressive residual stress. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, Mott-Schottky, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses consistently revealed that the improved corrosion resistance was governed by passive film quality rather than film thickness. Specifically, LSP-2 exhibited the largest model-derived effective thickness of the highly resistive inner region (δi, PLM = 0.85 nm), the lowest apparent donor and acceptor densities, and the most favorable oxide/hydroxide ratios. By contrast, the deterioration in LSP-4 coincided with increased surface roughness, greater deformation complexity, and enhanced interphase electrochemical heterogeneity. These results demonstrate that LSP can optimize the corrosion resistance of additively manufactured EHEAs by regulating defect-mediated passivation mechanisms. © 2026

Title: Critical review of tools and techniques for predicting microplastics pollution in watershed runoff
Abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution, especially, stormwater runoff from non-point sources is a major source of MPs into surrounding soils and aquatic environment. Numerous studies have investigated MPs occurrence, distribution, sources, morphology, environmental impact, and fate and transport (F&T) modeling, particularly in marine and freshwater ecosystems. However, models for MPs F&T, especially in the surface runoff context, are limited in scope or underexplored. This critical evaluation of hydrodynamic, process-based, mass-balance based, statistical, artificial intelligence (AI) based and hybrid approaches, alongside dedicated watershed hydrological models, including their input data requirements, spatial and temporal resolution, land-use classification, MPs typology, and software accessibility, to underscore influence on the model predictive reliability. Key findings reveal that existing models lack the representation of MPs as a discrete pollutant entity with density-dependent, and morphology-driven transport behavior. Hydrodynamic models excel in mechanistic fidelity but limit their scope with urban watershed runoff, while hydrological models provide an appropriate framework for watershed dynamics but lack MPs specific parameterization. AI and hybrid models show promising options for MPs predictive modeling but require robust calibration and validation datasets. Interconnected components of conceptual, structural, and empirical models are linked but constrained by barriers, hence it continues to limit MPs F&T model development and application. Addressing these challenges require standardized protocols, benchmark datasets, and integrated modeling frameworks. The synthesized information presented in this paper will not only assist in developing future MPs F&T models but also guide urban planners, environmental scientists, and water resource managers in selecting appropriate predictive tools for managing watershed MPs pollution. © 2026 The Author(s)
