Title: Satellite-based assessment of high Andean wetlands and carbon sequestration under the influence of climate change
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: High-Andean wetlands play an important role in providing ecosystem services, particularly carbon sequestration. Yet, anthropogenic climate change threatens to restrict their spatial footprint and curtail their overall efficacy as atmospheric carbon sinks. Therefore, the study objectives were to estimate carbon uptake in High-Andean wetlands using satellite imagery and to evaluate its relationship with climatic variables in the Huancané Basin, Peru. METHODS: Google Earth Engine and RStudio integrated development environment (v4.3.1) were used with JavaScript and R programming languages. Wetland extents were delineated across seasonal wet and dry phases via Linear Spectral Unmixing applied to Landsat 5–8 imagery. Subsequent to the conversion of digital numbers to surface reflectance, the wetland index was implemented to estimate carbon uptake using moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer gross primary productivity and net primary productivity datasets. Climate data were obtained from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration power platform, and the relationships between wetland extent, carbon dioxide sequestration, and climatic variables were analyzed. FINDINGS: Wetland coverage declined across both seasons over the study duration, experiencing contractions of 109.43 square kilometers during the wet season and 85.60 square kilometers during the dry season between 2010 and 2022. Carbon uptake also showed a decreasing trend during both seasons. Values ranged from 9.985 to 28.234 kilograms of carbon per square meter during the wet season and from 7.091 to 19.103 kilograms of carbon per square meter during the dry season. Significant relationships were found between wetland extent, carbon uptake, and climatic variables (p<0.05). Arid climatic trends, characterized by diminished precipitation, elevated temperature ranges, lower relative humidity, and increased wind speeds, corresponded closely with contractions in wetland extent and reduced carbon uptake. CONCLUSION: The results indicate that recent climatic changes have contributed to the degradation of high-Andean wetlands and to a reduction in their carbon uptake capacity in the Huancané Basin. These results provide vital baselines for tracking wetland trajectories, informing climate change mitigation and conservation frameworks to guide future ecosystem management and sustainable planning in fragile mountain regions worldwide. Title: Surrogate-model-assisted optimization of centrifugal pump-as-turbine impellers: A systematic review and structured evidence synthesis
Abstract: Impeller redesign can improve the turbine-mode performance of centrifugal pumps, but direct optimization with high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics is expensive. This review critically evaluates the evidence for surrogate-model-assisted optimization of centrifugal pump-as-turbine impellers. The revision followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for literature searches in systematic reviews reporting principles and used Synthesis Without Meta-analysis because the available studies did not report commensurate study-level uncertainty estimates. A reproducibility audit verified nine eligible studies published from 2015 to 2024. Artificial neural network families were most common; single studies used Kriging and support vector machine high-dimensional model representation, and one study used response surface methodology. Reported efficiency improvements from baseline to optimized designs were generally specific to the operating point. Directly comparable principal-point gains were generally about 2–6%, including 2.28–2.91% for genetic algorithm–backpropagation neural-network workflows, 3.8% for Kriging at the best-efficiency flow, 5.74% for a radial basis function neural-network and nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II workflow, and a 3.4% experimentally measured gain for support vector machine high-dimensional model representation; one multi-condition artificial neural network study reported larger point-specific gains of 8.67–13.1%. These results support a typical design-point improvement on the order of 4%, but they do not support a universal pooled effect or a model ranking. Computational savings were consistently attributed to replacing repeated computational fluid dynamics calls with surrogate evaluations, yet the reporting was insufficient to justify the previously claimed 45:1 ratio or a universal cost reduction. The evidence, therefore, supports surrogate assistance as a sample-efficient design strategy, while model choice should be based on dimensionality, data volume, validation rigor, and the need for uncertainty quantification. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Temperature-dependent island size-morphology correlation in Smoluchowski ripening from machine-learning molecular dynamics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Precise fabrication of nanostructures on surfaces requires an atomic-level understanding of surface ripening. Although Smoluchowski ripening (SR) describes the phenomenon where nanostructures migrate, collide, and coalesce, resolving the coupled temperature-dependent evolution of island size and morphology in a many-island ensemble remains challenging. Here, we develop a high-accuracy machine-learning potential (MLP) combined with large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine nanosecond-scale, early-stage nonequilibrium SR-like coarsening of Zn adatoms on the Zn(0001) basal surface over 100–500 K at 12.5% coverage, using three independent 4 ns trajectories at each temperature. We identify a reproducible three-stage evolution: initial clustering and early aggregation, active coalescence, and quasi-steady ripening. Temperature strongly regulates island size and morphology, with higher temperatures yielding larger, less morphologically anisotropic islands. Crucially, we uncover a consistent temperature-dependent island size-morphology correlation and trace it to the coupling between size-dependent thermodynamic preference for higher-coordination compact structures and temperature-enhanced kinetic relaxation through edge diffusion and post-coalescence rearrangement. These results demonstrate the capability of MLP-MD and provide an atomistic framework for understanding the coupled evolution of island size and morphology during early-stage surface coarsening, with significant implications for fields such as catalysis and electronic devices. © 2026

Title: Thickness-tailored FeB/Fe2B diffusion barriers on Q345R steel for long-term corrosion protection in molten solar salt

Abstract: Q345R steel is an economically attractive structural material for molten-nitrate thermal-storage systems, but its corrosion resistance in molten solar salt is limited. In this study, FeB/Fe2B diffusion layers were produced on Q345R steel by pack boriding at 850 and 900 °C for 2 h, and their corrosion behavior was evaluated in molten solar salt at 450 °C for 500 and 1000 h. Cross-sectional SEM observations showed that the boride-layer thickness increased from approximately 10 μm for B-850 to approximately 20 μm for B-900. Among all the conditions investigated, the B-900 specimen exhibited the most pronounced protective effect, achieving the lowest values in both mass loss and annualized corrosion rate. Title: Data-driven design of high-performance Ti-Fe-O alloys via iron oxide doping into titanium
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Conventional biomedical Ti alloys suffer from toxic elements, high cost, and the inability to quantify the nonlinear composition–microstructure–property correlation. Herein, a machine learning-driven strategy was proposed to establish high-precision property prediction models for Ti-Fe-O alloys, and four algorithms were compared to identify the optimal framework. Among them, the coefficient of determination (R2) of the optimal Random Forest (RF) model reached 0.98. Combined with the simulated annealing algorithm, inverse design was performed toward strength–ductility synergy, and the optimal Ti-1.28 wt.% Fe2O3 alloy was successfully developed. This alloy exhibits a thermally stable α+β duplex microstructure, and annealing induces significant coarsening and morphological transformation of secondary α (αs) from acicular to globular, which converts the hard, barely deformable β phase into a plastically deformable domain. O shows a gradient-type heterogeneous distribution across primary α and β phases. The as-annealed alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 888 MPa and an excellent elongation (El.) of 25.7%, demonstrating exceptional strength–ductility synergy. The results suggest that O redistribution and preferential accommodation in the αs/β regions, together with O-assisted dislocation pinning, contribute to mitigating local O-induced embrittlement and promoting coordinated plastic deformation. Meanwhile, O-assisted dislocation pinning activates massive 〈c + a〉 dislocations, and deformation twinning together with stacking faults further enhances the strain-hardening capacity. This work provides a reliable data-driven route for the design and engineering application of high-O biomedical Ti alloys. © 2026

Title: Mg single crystal microscopic fracture mechanism governed by twin-mediated synergistic non-basal slip
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The activation of non-basal slip can retard crack propagation during the fracture process of Mg. As a vital deformation mechanism, twinning reorients crystal lattices into favourable orientations for activating various non-basal slip systems, thereby accommodating abundant c-axis strain. In this work, pre-twins were introduced into pure Mg single crystals via compression perpendicular to the c-axis. Both untwinned and pre-twinned specimens were subjected to uniaxial c-axis compression until fracture, aiming to uncover the microscale fracture mechanism governed by twin-mediated synergistic multi-slip activity. The experimental results reveal that pre-twinning reduces the critical resolved shear stress ratio of non-basal slip to basal slip, simultaneously improving the formability of Mg single crystals. Three dominant slip modes give rise to distinct microstructural morphologies and fracture characteristics: Prismatic 〈a〉 slip generates sparse discrete dislocations and isolated dislocation loops, resulting in severe lattice distortion and localised stress concentration, with only discontinuous dynamic recrystallisation (DDRX) formed near fracture sites. Pyramidal 〈a〉 slip triggers extensive dislocation dissociation and abundant stacking faults, leading to the coexistence of continuous dynamic recrystallisation and DDRX within fractured regions. For pyramidal 〈c+a〉 cross-slip activated concurrently with detwinning, mutual dislocation annihilation eliminates lattice distortion and localised stress peaks, transforming the fracture mode from brittle failure to ductile fracture dominated by uniform equiaxed dimples. Title: Ultra-strong carbon fibers via atomic layer deposition-induced dual-scale defect regulation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Carbon fibers (CFs) with high tensile strength are highly desirable as reinforcement materials in advanced composites. Conformal Al2O3 layers reduced surface irregularities and stress concentration sites, while infiltrated Al-containing species promoted interfacial bonding and cross-linking within the carbon microstructure. Consequently, the tensile strength of commercial CFs was significantly enhanced after ALD treatment, with T1000G fibers exhibiting a ∼41% increase in tensile strength and reaching 8.45 ± 1.35 GPa. Structural analyses using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, field‑emission transmission electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping revealed reduced microvoid dimensions without significant alteration of the graphitic microstructure. Title: Engineering dual asymmetry: Directed magnetic and random conductive bilayer aerogels for absorption‑dominated EMI shielding
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The rapid advancement of 5G communications and wearable electronics has intensified the demand for high-performance electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials with low-reflection characteristics. Herein, we propose a dual-asymmetric design strategy that synergistically integrates compositional asymmetry (magnetic/conductive) and structural asymmetry (directed/random pores) within a bilayer aerogel architecture. Specifically, a magnetic/conductive bilayer aerogel (MCBA) comprising a directed magnetic top layer (ML) and a random conductive bottom layer (CL) was fabricated using a blended matrix of waterborne polyurethane (WPU) and bacterial cellulose (BC). The ML incorporates MXene@hollow Fe3O4 (MXene@HFO) heterostructures and directionally freeze-cast vertically aligned microchannels that facilitate maximal entry of incident electromagnetic waves (EMWs); the CL employs MXene nanosheets bridged by carbon nanotubes (CNTs) within a randomly freeze-cast, isotropic three‑dimensional (3D) conductive network that ensures highly efficient EMW attenuation. The HFO loading was systematically tuned to optimize the electromagnetic parameters and impedance matching of the MXene@HFO fillers, while the filler contents, pore orientations, and layer thicknesses of both layers were co‑designed to maximize absorption‑dominated shielding performance. This spatial decoupling of wave entry and energy dissipation enables a synergistic “absorption–reflection–reabsorption” pathway, yielding an outstanding EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 83.02 dB and an exceptionally low reflection coefficient (R) of 0.151. Furthermore, the MCBA delivers a low density (∼0.269 g cm−3), robust compressive resilience, low through‑plane thermal conductivity (∼0.149 W m−1 K−1), and favorable infrared camouflage. This work presents an ingenious dual‑asymmetric design strategy for developing lightweight, resilient, absorption‑dominated, and multifunctional EMI shielding materials tailored for complex operational environments. © 2026

Title: Capacity Degradation Mechanisms, Recovery Strategies, and Challenges of Flow Batteries
Abstract: Redox flow batteries, by virtue of their advantages in power/capacity decoupling, high safety, and long cycle life, have become a strategic support for long-duration energy storage systems; however, capacity degradation remains a bottleneck for their commercialization. This review systematically identifies the multi-dimensional mechanisms of capacity degradation: including volume imbalance caused by transmembrane migration, inactivation and decomposition of active species, electrode degradation, and valence imbalance induced by side reactions. Targeting these challenges, the review deeply explores recovery strategies from physical repair to intelligent scheduling: covering the research and development of high-selectivity membranes, precise regulation of valence states, functionalized repair of electrodes, and model-driven predictive pathways integrating digital twins. Finally, current challenges such as characterization limitations and incomplete recovery rates are summarized, and future development directions for capacity recovery are envisioned. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for extending the system cycle life of flow batteries and improving capacity recovery efficiency. Title: Interfacial engineering of MOF-on-MOF heterostructure for efficient charge separation and photoelectrochemical water splitting

Abstract: Hematite (α-Fe2O3) is a promising photoelectrode material for photoelectrochemical water splitting (PEC-WS). In this study, a dual metal-organic framework (MOF) heterostructure is constructed by introducing MIL-125(NH2) and UiO-66 onto the surface of an α-Fe2O3 photoanode to enhance carrier separation and transport. Dual-MOF modification lowers the work function of α-Fe2O3 and establishes favorable band alignment, generating an enhanced built-in electric field that drives photogenerated holes toward the MIL-125(NH2)/UiO-66 cocatalyst and accelerates water oxidation kinetics. The dual-MOF heterojunction further prolongs the photogenerated hole lifetime, increasing charge transfer efficiency. These synergistic effects enrich surface active sites, suppress charge recombination, and promote carrier separation and transport, resulting in improved PEC-WS performance of the α-Fe2O3 photoanode. © 2026

Title: A functionally synergistic sequential-response bilayer coating strategy for enhanced thermal protection of epoxy-based carbon fiber composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced epoxy composites (CFEP) possess excellent lightweight and high-strength properties; however, their resin matrix is flammable and lacks sufficient fire protection capabilities. To improve the fire safety and post-combustion structural integrity of CFEP, a bilayer protective system consisting of an intumescent flame-retardant coating (IFC) and a ceramicizable thermal-insulation coating (CTIC) was constructed in this work. Compared to single-layer coatings, the Bi-IFC/CTIC system exhibits superior comprehensive flame-retardant performance, with its LOI increased to 32.4% and achieving UL-94 V-0 rating. The bilayer coating also effectively reduces the CFEP's PHRR (69.4%), THR (47.4%), and TSR (20.7%), demonstrating optimal flame-retardant and smoke-suppressing effects. Direct flame impact tests indicate that the bilayer coating's char layer can stably support an applied weight, demonstrating greater char layer strength. Furthermore, Bi-IFC/CTIC can control the back-surface temperature of the CFEP at 201 °C and maintain a post-combustion flexural strength retention rate of 88.7%. Title: Unlocking high-performance manganese-based layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), characterized by energy-storage mechanisms similar to those of lithium-ion batteries and offering substantial resource and cost advantages, are regarded as highly promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems. Given that cathode materials are crucial in determining electrochemical performance, their rational design and optimization are essential for accelerating the commercialization of SIBs. Among various cathode candidates, manganese (Mn)-based layered oxide materials have attracted particular interest owing to their low cost, high specific capacity, and environmental benignity. However, their practical application is hindered by the intrinsic Jahn-Teller effect and complex phase transitions, which lead to structural and electrochemical degradation during cycling. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the key challenges encountered by Mn-based layered oxides during charge/discharge processes and delve into the fundamental mechanisms governing their electrochemical performance. We further discuss representative modification strategies designed to enhance cycling stability and rate capability, mainly including local-environment regulation, phase-structure tailoring, morphology engineering, and surface customization. These approaches can effectively suppress lattice distortion and parasitic side reactions, stabilize the structural framework, and thereby enhance the electrochemical performance. Finally, we outline the remaining challenges and future prospects for Mn-based layered oxide cathodes, with the goal of facilitating their practical application in SIBs. © 2026

Title: Sustained thermal stability over 1000 h in Cu–15Ni–8Sn alloy by Ti-guided exclusive L12 precipitation

Title: Heterolayered gradient photonic textile harmonizing scattering coloration and continuous microclimate comfort

Title: Multicomponent Nitride/High-Entropy Alloy Heterostructures as Highly Active and Stable Electrocatalysts for Ampere-Level Water Oxidation
Abstract: Developing highly active and stable oxygen evolution reaction catalysts is paramount for cost-effective large-scale green hydrogen production via water electrolysis. Here we report nonprecious metal-based multicomponent nitride/high-entropy alloy heterostructures as cost-effective electrocatalysts to efficiently mediate alkaline water oxidation by in-situ configurating cooperative Brønsted basic oxyanion-solid interfaces during phase transformation of multicomponent nitride into amorphous N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH along with partial dissolution of high-value metals of Mo and Cr to form molecular MoO42− and CrO42− species. The protonation of Brønsted basic oxyanions facilitates the critical *OOH intermediate formation on N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH with near-optimal adsorption energy, substantially accelerating the oxygen evolution reaction kinetics. Consequently, the heterostructure electrode exhibits superior oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysis in 1 M KOH solution, delivering ultrahigh current density of ~ 2.5 A cm−2 at low overpotential of 300 mV. Its alkaline water electrolyzer operates stably at ampere-level current density for > 1700 h. Our findings reveal an unconventional molecule-assisted multi-site mechanism of multicomponent catalysts to accelerate multiple-intermediate reaction. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Liu D.; Zhang F.; Shen Y.; Cheng Y.; Xu J.; Zhang Y.
Title: Theoretical Analysis of Liquid Lens Evaporation on Immiscible Liquid Surface
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: The evaporation of liquid lens widely occurs in various scientific and industrial applications. In this study, a theoretical model is set up for liquid lens evaporation under the axisymmetric toroidal coordinate, with coupled internal heat conduction and external vapor diffusion. The effect of evaporative cooling number, liquid lens shape and volume on evaporation performance is quantitatively analyzed. It is found that overall evaporation rate is determined by the competing effect of evaporation flux and area of upper surface. With the increasing ratios of upper and lower tangential angles, at high evaporative cooling numbers or large liquid volumes, overall evaporation rates decrease firstly, after reaching the minimum value, they start to increase until the asymptotic value. The ”2/3 power law” holds for transient volume variation of liquid lens over time, independent of evaporative cooling and liquid lens shape. These findings may help get insight into the liquid lens evaporation on immiscible liquid. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Authors: Wang Z.; Wang Q.; Wang T.; Yang R.
Title: Rotational twinning endows B2 multi-principal element intermetallic alloys with excellent strength and ductility
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The synergistic enhancement of strength and ductility remains a critical challenge for B2 intermetallic alloys due to their intrinsic room-temperature brittleness. Herein, using the Ni–Ti system with its highly tunable composition and sensitive phase stability as an ideal model, we designed Ni50Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 and Ni25Co25Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 alloys via a multi-principal element approach. Multiscale characterization and first-principles calculations show that the Co-free alloy adopts a brittle B19′ martensitic structure at room temperature, with a fracture strain of ∼13%. In contrast, Co-doping induces changes in the structural ground state, which facilitates the stabilization of the monolithic B2 phase. The Ni25Co25Ti16.7Zr16.7Hf16.6 alloy shows an exceptional combination of strength and ductility, with a yield strength of 1527 MPa, an ultimate compressive strength of 3099 MPa, and a compressive strain of ∼40%. This distinctive feature stems from a deformation mechanism in which <110>-oriented rotational twinning mediates strain accommodation, maintains long-range structural order, and facilitates screw dislocations cross-slip. This twinning-induced plasticity within ordered structures provides a generalizable pathway for designing high-performance B2 intermetallic alloys. © 2026

In contrast to the traditional molecular dynamic methods, this study used information technology to obtain the characteristics of the flow field in technological equipment. The novelty lies in: integration of thermomechanical modeling with an optimization algorithm; introduction of a criterion minimizing mechanical property variation; consideration of reduction and redistribution effects on roll wear; possibility of adaptive real-time control. An information analysis of the profiles of copper melt flow velocities in a wide range of temperatures in the Copper Rod Production Plant Kazkat is presented. Information Technology fulfils the need to address the problem of determining the optimal values of temperature, rolling speed, and other parameters to achieve the best quality and productivity of copper rod production processes. Title: Termination-dependent interfacial interactions of ionic-liquid-modified Ti3C2Tx for boundary lubrication
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The effectiveness of two-dimensional additives in boundary lubrication is often limited by poor dispersion stability and unstable low-shear interfaces in polar lubricants. Here, we report an ionic liquid (IL)-enabled interfacial-engineering strategy that couples surface anchoring with shear regulation at Ti3C2Tx MXene interfaces. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that the imidazolium cation acts as the primary anchoring motif, showing strong, termination-sensitive binding to Ti3C2Tx surface terminations, while the alkyl chain extends toward the counterface and may provide a molecular basis for an organic shear-accommodating overlayer. First-principles calculations further indicate a termination-dependent interfacial interaction trend, in which the calculated stability of the composite layer on steel is more closely associated with Ti3C2Tx-Fe electronic coupling than with cation-Ti3C2Tx anchoring. This trend provides a possible mechanistic basis for reconciling interfacial persistence with low shear resistance. Accordingly, IL-modified Ti3C2Tx reduces wear by up to 61% at an ultralow concentration of 0.05wt.%. Tribochemical and cross-sectional TEM analyses support the formation of an 8.5 nm continuous composite tribofilm enriched with IL- and Ti3C2Tx-derived species, consistent with reduced direct steel exposure during sliding. These findings offer design concepts for two-dimensional additives in polar lubricants. © 2026

Title: Damage-tolerant Cu/Cu2TiAl heterostructure enabled by Al-modified interlayer design for Ti6Al4V/CoCrFeNi dissimilar metals
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Additive manufacturing of Ti6Al4V/CoCrFeNi dissimilar metals is fundamentally limited by the strong chemical affinity of Ti with Fe, Co, and Ni, which causes brittle intermetallic compounds and severe interfacial cracking. Although ductile Cu interlayers with favorable metallurgical compatibility improve interfacial bonding, the formation of continuous Cu-Ti intermetallic compounds may still degrade interfacial integrity and trigger premature failure. An Al-modified Cu interlayer strategy is developed to regulate interfacial reactions during laser-directed energy deposition. The addition of Al redirects interfacial phase evolution from multiple continuous Cu-Ti binary compounds to a Cu/Cu2TiAl networked heterostructure, reducing lattice mismatch and improving metallurgical bonding with suppressed interfacial cracking. Unexpectedly, the continuous Cu-rich network promotes plastic accommodation and suppresses local stress concentration. Consequently, the interfacial shear strength of the interlayer/CoCrFeNi interface increases from 185.1 to 321.7 MPa, representing a 73.8% improvement. This work establishes a composition-mediated pathway for interfacial compound formation to convert deleterious intermetallic formation into mechanically compatible heterostructures, offering insights into interlayer design for additive joining of Ti-based dissimilar metals with severe metallurgical incompatibility. © 2026

Title: Architectural control of high-temperature creep and failure in additively manufactured superalloy metamaterials
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Additively manufactured superalloy-based metamaterials offer a promising route toward lightweight structural components for extreme high-temperature applications, yet the mechanisms governing their creep deformation and failure remain largely unexplored. Traditionally, creep is viewed as an intrinsic material limitation governed by microstructural degradation. Here, we show that creep resistance in superalloy metamaterials is highly governed by architectural topology. By systematically comparing strut-based, plate-based, and TPMS architectures, we reveal pronounced architecture-dependent creep behavior under compressive loading at 650 °C. The plate-based lattice demonstrates the best creep resistance, exhibiting the lowest steady-state rate under identical applied stresses. While all architectures fail by macroscopic shear bands, high-resolution 3D tomography and atom-probe analysis reveal a cross-scale transition where failure initiates at stress-concentrated nodes and propagates via oxygen-assisted intergranular damage, even as the core (γ′/γ″) remains remarkably stable. This work highlights architectural control as an effective design principle for tailoring creep resistance in metallic metamaterials, providing a foundation for designing lightweight and reliable metallic components for high-temperature applications. © 2026

Authors: Yan Y.; Liu H.; Zhu M.; Zhang W.; Chen R.; Chen Z.; Guo E.; Zhang S.; Kang H.; Wang T.
Title: Multifunctional cation-site doping unlocks high-performance Mg3Bi1.4Sb0.6-based thermoelectrics
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Thermoelectric (TE) materials require both high performance to maximize energy conversion efficiency and favorable mechanical properties to ensure processability and reliable operation. Herein, we propose a synergistic band engineering and defect engineering strategy to simultaneously optimize the TE performance and mechanical strength for Mg3.2−x(EryCu1−y)x(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01. Er-Cu co-doping effectively modulates the band structure, shifting the Fermi level deep into the conduction band and inducing band flattening, thereby maintaining a significant Seebeck coefficient at high carrier concentrations. Consequently, a remarkable power factor of ∼23.86 μW cm−1 K−2 is attained for Mg3.18(Er0.50Cu0.50)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01 at 323 K. Meanwhile, the integration of multi-scale defects, encompassing grain boundaries, precipitates, dislocations, nanoclusters, and interstitial atoms, synergistically enhances phonon scattering and significantly reduces lattice thermal conductivity. Ultimately, the Mg3.18(Er0.75Cu0.25)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01 exhibits an excellent zT of ∼1.30 at 573 K and a superior average zT of ∼1.14 from 323 to 573 K. Furthermore, Er-Cu co-doping introduces multiple strengthening mechanisms, resulting in a Vickers hardness of ∼1.63 GPa and compressive strength of ∼422.1 MPa for Mg3.18(Er0.75Cu0.25)0.02(Bi0.7Sb0.3)1.99Te0.01. This work demonstrates that band engineering and defect engineering through Er-Cu co-doping can simultaneously enhance TE and mechanical properties, providing a general paradigm for designing high-performance Mg3Bi2-based alloys. © 2026

Authors: Li J.; Li Z.; Zhao J.; Zhang Y.; Zhang L.
Title: High-Precision Calculation of Wave-Current Forces on Offshore Wind Turbines Based on the Regularized Singular Boundary Method
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: The main purpose of this article is to develop a regularized singular boundary method for high-precision simulation of wave-current forces on offshore wind turbines. The engineering bottlenecks encountered in the construction of offshore wind turbines are discussed, i.e., how to effectively deal with the singularity of the Green’s function at the origin, and how to accurately calculate wave forces on offshore wind turbines. An origin intensity factor technique for marine dynamic environment simulation is proposed. Based on the origin intensity factor and the Green’s function, a regularized singular boundary method is constructed, which only requires placing source points on the wet surface of offshore wind turbines. Wave load is calculated by substituting wave parameters affected by wave-current interaction into the linear diffraction model. The wave-current force on offshore wind turbines is finally obtained by superimposing the current load and the wave load. Numerical experiments show that the regularized singular boundary method can accurately analyze the Bragg resonance of offshore wind turbines caused by wave-current force. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Uncertainty estimation in earthquake magnitude determination using high-rate GPS data with Bootstrap method
Abstract: Accurate analysis of earthquake magnitude and evaluation of its associated uncertainty are fundamental topics in seismology and disaster management. In this study, the earthquake magnitudes were estimated using high-rate GPS data for three major events: the 2011 Tohoku earthquake (Mw 9.1), the 2021 Chignik earthquake (Mw 8.2), and the 2018 Anchorage earthquake (Mw 7.1). The final estimated magnitudes using the proposed method were approximately Mw 9.25 for Tohoku, Mw 8.27 for Chignik, and Mw 7.08 for Anchorage, closely aligning with official reports. High-rate GPS data, due to their ability to precisely capture real-time crustal displacements, were utilized as the primary data source. These data provided valuable information on maximum displacement, dominant period, and epicentral distance, and were employed for estimating earthquake magnitude and analyzing uncertainty. To analyze the data, combinations of different GPS stations were used to minimize the impact of noisy data and achieve more stable results. The application of the Bootstrap statistical method reduced uncertainty values significantly from approximately 0.0039 to 0.0011 for Tohoku, 0.0031 to 0.0019 for Chignik, and 0.004 to 0.0015 for Anchorage. These results demonstrate the statistical robustness and effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared to conventional seismic methods, which suffer from data clipping and saturation for large magnitudes, the high-rate GPS method provided stable and unbiased magnitude estimates without signal saturation issues. The findings underscore the importance of expanding GPS networks in tectonically active regions, integrating seismic and GPS data, and employing advanced algorithms for data processing. Furthermore, the research emphasizes the role of comprehensive data analysis in improving early earthquake warning systems. By incorporating high-rate GPS data with traditional seismic data, the precision and reliability of early warning systems can be significantly enhanced, ultimately reducing the potential for loss of life and property. Additionally, this study highlights the necessity of strengthening infrastructure resilience and investing in advanced monitoring technologies. In conclusion, this research successfully demonstrates that high-rate GPS data, combined with the Bootstrap method, can accurately estimate earthquake magnitudes, reduce uncertainty, and enhance the reliability of seismic assessments. These findings contribute to the development of more effective earthquake early warning systems and risk mitigation strategies. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. All rights reserved.

Authors: Pi B.; Bao M.; Yang J.; Zhang Q.; Cheng H.; Cui P.; Yu C.; Zhang W.
Title: Cr/Eu dual doping synergistically promotes reconstruction: Polymetallic MOFs-derived highly active oxyhydroxide for efficient oxygen evolution reaction
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Exploring the design and synthesis strategies of high‑performance MOF catalysts is of great significance for energy conversion technologies. Herein, bimetallic to pentametallic MOF arrays grown on iron foam were synthesized at room temperature using 1,3,5‑benzenetricarboxylic acid as the ligand via a sacrificial pre‑programmed template method. The optimized pentametallic CoNiFeCrEu‑MOF exhibits a low overpotential of 197 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2, along with stability exceeding 240 h at 100 mA cm−2. Through a combination of multiple characterizations and theoretical calculations, we reveal that Cr doping, together with its vigorous dissolution during activation, promotes the conversion of Co(II) in the MOFs to Co(III), whereas Eu accelerates the oxidation of Ni(II) and Fe(II) by facilitating electron transfer from Fe and Ni to Co. The dual‑doping engineering significantly promotes the formation of amorphous M(III)OOH, while optimizing the adsorption energies of *OH and *OOH intermediates, thereby accounting for the enhanced OER performance. These findings provide insights into the formation of active oxyhydroxide phases and the synergistic effects of multi‑metal components in MOFs during the OER, offering a viable strategy to enhance water splitting efficiency. © 2026

Title: Interface Contact Optimization via Phosphomolybdic Acid Enables 24.9% Efficiency in MoOX-Based Silicon Solar Cells
Abstract: The development of cost-effective carrier-selective passivating contacts is critical for enhancing the commercial feasibility of silicon compound solar cells. Molybdenum oxide (MoOX) has garnered considerable interest as a promising hole transport layer (HTLs). A key advantage of MoOX is high work function, in addition to the low-cost processability. However, in silicon photovoltaics, MoOX-based p-type contacts face fundamental limitations at hydrogenated amorphous silicon (i-a-Si:H)/MoOX interface, where oxygen vacancy defects lower work function, as well as, weak van der Waals-dominated interactions impair charge carry transport. To address these challenges, we introduced an ultrathin phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) interlayer at the i-a-Si:H/MoOX interface. PMA passivated oxygen vacancy defects, resulting in a notable improvement in open-circuit voltage from 713 to 730 mV, and 0.11 eV work function elevation via dipole formation; meanwhile, PMA strengthened the interfacial bonding energy, reducing saturation current density and contact resistance by 63% and 24%, respectively, contributing to a fill factor enhancement from 83.7% to 84.9%. In the end, we demonstrated a record efficiency of 24.9% for MoOX-based silicon solar cells, which provides valuable insights for developing high-performance MoOX HTL devices for dopant-free p-type contact technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Vincy M.V.; Anupama, V.; Brilliant R.
Title: Short-term variability in sediment carbon sequestration in tropical Indian Wetlands: Physicochemical controls and policy relevance
Abstract: Wetlands are critical components of the global carbon cycle, functioning as both carbon sinks and sources depending on environmental conditions. This study assessed short-term variability in sediment carbon storage and its physicochemical controls across five tropical wetlands in southern India. Sediment samples collected in March 2024 and March 2025 were analyzed for pH, macronutrients (N, P, K), bulk density (BD), organic carbon (OC), total organic carbon (TOC), and derived carbon indices, including carbon mass (CM), total mass carbon (TMC), and carbon density (CD). Results indicated consistent increases in OC (0.6–2.4% to 0.7–2.65%) and TOC (1.2–6.2% to 1.5–7.1%), accompanied by increases in CD (1.71–10.69–2.18–12.57 kgm⁻²), suggesting enhanced short-term carbon accumulation. Correlation and principal component analyses revealed strong associations among carbon-related variables, while BD and pH contributed to secondary gradients. However, these relationships partly reflect mathematical dependencies among derived indices and should be interpreted with caution. Effect size analysis (Cohen's d) indicated substantial short-term differences for carbon-related variables (d = 2.04–2.46), along with strong effects for OC and BD, reflecting consistent directional changes across sites. Nitrogen showed a supportive role in organic matter accumulation, whereas phosphorus exhibited limited short-term influence. Slightly acidic conditions (pH 4.2–6.0) were associated with reduced decomposition and enhanced carbon preservation. Despite these findings, the study is constrained by its short temporal scope and the absence of key biogeochemical parameters such as redox potential and greenhouse gas fluxes. Overall, the results provide baseline insights into sediment carbon dynamics and inform future wetland carbon monitoring and management strategies. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Envelope-like structured TiAl alloy with deformation-induced γ nano-grids for high-temperature strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Coarse lamellae are unable to generate sufficient dislocations and nanotwins, leading to reduced strength and ductility. In this study, a novel multiphase envelope-like microstructure, consisting of γE phases surrounding fine lamellar colonies, was obtained through heat treatment, providing favorable multiphase interfaces for dynamic nano-defect formation. The high-temperature deformation mechanisms of the TiAl alloy were investigated by in-situ experiments. Results show that γ shear bands form through Al/Ti interdiffusion-assisted multicomponent redistribution, while γ nanotwins nucleate and propagate via (1¯11)<11¯2] twinning dislocations slipping. First-principles calculations reveal that coherent twin boundaries correspond to a local energy minimum on the γ-surface, confirming twinning as a stable deformation mode. The dynamically formed γ nano-grids effectively hinder crack propagation, whereas the 60° interlocking dislocation structure within the γE phase promotes coordinated plastic deformation. Owing to the synergistic effects of γ nano-grids, dislocation activity, and lamellar interfaces, the alloy exhibits excellent high-temperature mechanical properties, with tensile strength increasing to 624 MPa at 850 °C and maintaining 527 MPa at 900 °C, and elongation improving from 2.13% to 12.54%. © 2026

Title: Strength-ductility synergy of hierarchical porous copper prepared by one-step dealloying of Cu-Mn-Fe alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The practical deployment of dealloyed porous copper for functional applications remains hampered by its inadequate mechanical strength and macroscopic brittleness. A critical challenge in this field lies in fabricating bulk structures with superior mechanical performance via facile synthetic routes. In this work, we prepared hierarchical porous copper with strength-ductility synergy through one-step dealloying of the Cu40Mn50Fe10 alloy. The resulting material exhibits remarkable mechanical properties, achieving an initial peak compressive stress of 58.22 ± 7.08 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 17.12 ± 1.32 MPa, and a fracture strain of 5.07% ± 0.44%. Such excellent mechanical performance originates from effective stress redistribution and crack deflection across the microscale ligament network, coupled with intrinsic strain accommodation and dislocation accumulation within the nanoporous structure. Moreover, the deformation resistance provided by retained twin structures inherited from the master alloy also plays a vital role. Furthermore, we anticipate that the tension-compression asymmetry in the mechanical response of the present material will provide new insights into the structural optimization and performance enhancement of hierarchical porous copper. © 2026

Title: Localization challenges and technological gaps in cleaning robots for fixed-tilt coplanar photovoltaic arrays: A review and perspective
Abstract: Accurate and reliable localization is crucial for autonomous mobile robots performing cleaning operations on coplanar photovoltaic arrays at fixed tilt angles, where smooth glass surfaces, repetitive textures, and narrow passageways frequently degrade localization accuracy. This paper provides a structured review of localization strategies relevant to photovoltaic panel cleaning. It establishes the fundamentals of ground robot localization and reviews both conventional and AI-enhanced techniques, from odometry and global positioning to deep visual perception and learning-based state estimation. The operational, environmental, perceptual, and computational constraints specific to coplanar photovoltaic arrays are analysed, together with the localization strategies adopted in existing photovoltaic cleaning robots. The review finds that current systems rely almost exclusively on short-range relative localization and lack mechanisms for globally consistent positioning across multi-row cleaning runs. Closing this gap will require localization architectures that bound drift through external geometric references and adapt to slip and illumination variation through learning-based estimation, with active tracking of passive landmarks via pan–tilt–zoom cameras combined with AI-enhanced sensor fusion offering one promising direction. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Yuan X.; Zhao B.; Li W.; Wu H.; Wang X.; Yuan Y.; Tian M.; Zhu Y.; Zhang F.; Wang H.; Zhang R.; Zhang Y.; Li H.; Fan B.
Title: Ultrabroadband microwave absorption via Co2+ site-occupancy-driven ligand-field reconstruction and spin-orbit coupling synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Despite its promise, ZnFe2O4 spinel is fundamentally limited by weak magnetic anisotropy and poor dielectric loss. Here, we overcome these barriers via a site-occupancy-driven ligand-field reconstruction and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) synergy strategy. By engineering the Co2+ distribution between tetrahedral and octahedral sites, we concurrently achieve two complementary functions: (i) the unquenched orbital angular momentum of high-spin Co2+ in the reconstructed crystal field intensifies SOC, significantly enhancing magnetic anisotropy and low-frequency magnetic loss; and (ii) the charge compensation triggered by Co2+ substitution generates oxygen vacancies and mixed-valence Fe3+/Fe2+ pairs, boosting dielectric loss via defect-induced polarization relaxation. Consequently, the optimized absorber delivers a 9.1 GHz effective bandwidth at 1.9 mm thickness and a −57.8 dB minimum reflection loss at 5.0 GHz. Title: Regionalization, temporal-spatial characteristics, and trend of changes in precipitation and drought in Iran
Abstract: This study regionalizes Iran's precipitation and analyzes the temporal-spatial behavior of precipitation and drought in Iran. It used two sets of precipitation data. The first data set is the monthly precipitation data of 63 synoptic stations and the second data set is the Gridded precipitation data of three databases: Global Precipitation Climatology Center (GPCC), Climatic Research Unit (CRU) of the University of East Anglia (UEA) of England and University of Delaware (UDel) of the United States. As the results showed, the GPCC Gridded precipitation data set with a very high correlation (R^2 = 0.97) with Iranian station data was recognized as the most suitable Gridded precipitation data set for Iran. Cluster analysis on this precipitation dataset showed Iran can fall under seven different precipitation regions. Various characteristics of droughts, such as intensity, duration, and frequency of each precipitation region, were extracted and analyzed through four standardized precipitation indices (SPI), percentage of normal precipitation (PNPI), precipitation variability (RVI), and deciles (DI). The results disclosed that the three precipitation regions of Southwest (SW), Central Iran (CI), and Northwest-Northeast (NW-NE), among the seven precipitation regions of Iran, are the most vulnerable precipitation regions to drought. © 2026, Iranian Geophyisical Society. Title: System-level assessment of operational transients in PV-integrated distribution networks
Abstract: The large-scale integration of photovoltaic generation introduces new electromagnetic transient challenges to distribution networks. This paper focuses on capacitor energization as a representative operational transient scenario in PV-integrated distribution networks and investigates its formation mechanism, system response, and assessment method. First, a dynamic equivalent model of capacitive operational transients is developed, revealing a dominant high-frequency damped oscillatory mode jointly determined by the grid equivalent impedance and the capacitor operating conditions. Then, based on a detailed electromagnetic transient model, the transient responses of key nodes on both the distribution network side and within the PV system are analyzed. To distinguish these transients from conventional fault ride-through scenarios, the engineering requirement of operational transient ride-through (OTRT) is introduced, and a minimal yet complete set of system-level assessment indices is established to quantitatively characterize the instantaneous electrical stress imposed by operational transients. The results provide a quantitative basis for transient safety assessment and engineering design of PV-integrated distribution networks under routine operational transients. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang P.; Xu S.; Wang S.; Cui X.; Bai J.; Sun Y.; Zhu X.; Zhao B.; Chou S.; Wu X.
Title: Anionic Bottom-Up Flux Orchestrated via Hard Carbon Surface Chemistry for Stable Sodium-Ion Batteries
Abstract: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries suffer from unstable solid-electrolyte interphase formation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and poor cycle stability. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface. By engineering a synergistic pair of pyridinic-N and carbonyl groups on the carbon surface, we create a functional-differentiation microenvironment where pyridinic-N selectively anchors PF6− anions, while the cooperative carbonyl repels solvent molecules. This dual functionality establishes a sustained concentration gradient that drives a continuous reverse flux of anions toward the interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition pathway from solvent-dominated to anion-preferential. The tailored surface lowers the PF6− decomposition barrier by over 70%, yielding a thin, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase dominated by NaF and Na2O. The optimized anode achieves 91.9% Coulombic efficiency with high reversible capacity of 368.2 mAh g−1, and 96.5% capacity retention after 5,000 cycles. A pouch cell assembled with NFPP cathode achieves an energy density of 239.1 Wh kg−1 and stable operation over 500 cycles, demonstrating strong practical potential. This work establishes active surface-guided anionic transport as a powerful strategy for interphase engineering in advanced sodium-ion batteries. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Around-the-clock intelligent sensing transportation systems based on vdWs n-p-n heterostructure memristive arrays
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The detection of near-infrared light is of great importance in fields such as traffic monitoring, medical imaging, and security monitoring. However, conventional sensing systems based on the von Neumann architecture face fundamental challenges in terms of integration and performance due to their sensing-computing separation model. In this study, we present a van der Waals n-p-n Bi2Te3/SnSe/Nb:SrTiO3 hetero-memristor. This device combines the advantages of two-dimensional (2D) topological insulators and 2D ferroelectric materials. Modulating the ferroelectric polarization effectively adjusts the device performance, achieving a 75% yield, an optical on/off ratio of approximately 104, and a pulse cycle lifetime of over 108 cycles. Furthermore, the device exhibits stable 32 resistance states and a pronounced wavelength-dependent optical response, demonstrating exceptional stability over 31,000 optical switching cycles under 808 nm illumination. By integrating optical measurement precision with infrared spectral robustness, a near-infrared sensing system based on memristor sensing arrays has been realized. Incorporating the memristive sensing characteristics into the YOLOv11-based recognition framework, the proposed system achieves accuracy rates of 83% and 93% for pedestrian and vehicle recognition, respectively. Title: Elucidating the Respective Roles of Photochemical and Photothermal Effects in Photocatalytic Methanol Decomposition
Abstract: Photocatalytic reactions can be driven by both photochemical and photothermal processes. However, their individual contributions and synergistic effect remain to be clarified. Herein, we investigated the respective roles of these effects using a Cu–TiO2/Ti model catalyst that integrated photochemical and photothermal functionalities within a single photocatalytic system. Employing photocatalytic methanol decomposition as a model reaction, the Cu–TiO2/Ti catalyst achieved a high H2 yield rate of 0.511 mmol h−1 with selectivity of 96.6% toward HCHO among oxidation products, attributed to the cooperative action of photochemical and photothermal processes. In situ resonant Auger electron spectroscopy (RAS), together with in situ Cu K-edge X-ray absorption fine structure and excited-state density functional theory calculations, revealed the accumulation of photogenerated electrons at Cu sites from TiO2, suggests the possible formation of an electron transfer pathway from TiO2 to Cu, which promotes stepwise methanol dehydrogenation to HCHO and H2. Simultaneously, the photothermal contribution from Ti enhanced catalytic activity by accelerating reaction kinetics and promoting the desorption of HCHO, thereby suppressing its overoxidation to CO. Authors: Fauziah L.; Nuraini Y.; Soemarno; Lestari N.D.; Djajadi; Aini N.
Title: Ecological diversity in soil properties and bacterial communities in tropical coastal areas with contrasting electrical conductivity
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Coastal soil salinization is an environmental constraint that alters soil physicochemical conditions and may restructure microbial communities, while field patterns may also reflect land use and co-varying soil properties. The study objectives were to characterize soil physicochemical conditions together with bacterial diversity, composition, community dissimilarity, and predicted ecological functions at three tropical coastal sites in Palang, Tuban, East Java, with contrasting electrical conductivity. METHODS: Electrical conductivity at sampling sites PA8, PA9, and PA10 was 13.68, 3.74, and 0.50 decidiemens per meter, respectively. A single composite soil sample was collected and analyzed from each site and subjected to near full-length bacterial small-subunit ribosomal ribonucleic acid gene amplicon sequencing. Following quality filtering and denoising, amplicon sequence variants were resolved, and taxonomic assignments were performed against a curated ribosomal reference database. Observed richness, Shannon and Gini-Simpson indices, Bray-Curtis and Weighted UniFrac principal coordinate analyses, taxonomic relative abundance, and taxonomy-based predicted functions were summarized descriptively. Site-to-site variations in exchangeable sodium, organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, phosphorus availability, soil texture, and culturable bacterial abundance were also compared among sites. Due to the confounding of site identity, electrical conductivity, land use, and other edaphic properties, replicated inference of salinity effects was not feasible. FINDINGS: PA8 had 2,052 observed sequence variants and a Shannon index of 9.61; PA9 had 5,205 variants and a Shannon index of 11.39; and PA10 had 3,145 variants and a Shannon index of 11.03. Taxonomic profiles differed among sites. PA8 was characterized by Bacillota, Bacillales, and Incertae_Sedis_14; PA9 by Bacillota/Pseudomonadota, Bacillales, and Neobacillus; and PA10 by Chloroflexota, Anaerolineales, and UTCFX1. Weighted UniFrac distances were 0.3266 for PA9-PA10, 0.4850 for PA8-PA9, and 0.5226 for PA8-PA10. Predicted chemoheterotrophy accounted for 20.46 percent, 16.97 percent, and 23.88 percent of post-filter reads at sites PA8, PA9, and PA10, respectively. PA8 also had the highest exchangeable sodium, whereas PA10 had the highest organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, Olsen-available phosphorus, and culturable bacterial abundance. CONCLUSION: While intra-site analyses revealed marked heterogeneity in physicochemical parameters and bacterial community structures, the observational framework of this study limits direct causal attribution to salinity gradients and restricts the extrapolation of findings to wider salinity categories. The findings provide a site-specific environmental baseline and hypotheses for future replicated studies. Title: AI-enabled multi-class visual fault diagnosis for large-scale solar photovoltaic systems supporting energy transition and net-zero operations
Abstract: Large-scale solar photovoltaic installations are required to have reliable inspection methodologies in order to detect surface conditions or degradation states which could negatively affect their operational efficiencies. In this paper, we develop a visual condition classification system for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) modules based on an AI technique capable of identifying six PV module surface conditions classified into six different classes: physically damaged, visually apparent electrical degraded, dirty/dusty, snow-covered, bird-drop impacted, and clean. Using transfer learning techniques, four different architectures were tested as classifiers under the same balanced classification protocol. EfficientNet-B0 produced the highest average results among all tested architectures with an average overall classification accuracy score of 94.3% for all tests. Additionally, the average Macro-Precision, Macro-Recall and Macro F1 scores for EfficientNet-B0 were 93.2%, 92.8%, and 93.0%. Furthermore, EfficientNet-B0 exhibited a variability in its Macro-Precision and Macro F1 scores of no greater than 1.6% between the best and worst test result of any individual run, thus demonstrating consistent performance across multiple runs. Lastly, the maximum processing time (inference time) for EfficientNet-B0 was less than 18 ms per image in the current reporting. The results demonstrated herein represent a proof-of-concept for a scalable methodology for visually inspecting PV surfaces, but additional testing at multiple sites along with the collection of additional data regarding operational status will be necessary before validation can be conducted. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Tunable oxygen vacancy engineering via electron beam irradiation in TiO2/MXene: A combined experimental and DFT study on photocatalytic performance and hydrogen adsorption energetics
Abstract: Defect engineering is a powerful strategy for enhancing catalytic activity, charge-carrier mobility, and structural stability through the controlled introduction of defects such as oxygen vacancies (Ov). Electron beam (EB) irradiation offers a precise route for generating vacancies and lattice disorders, enabling tailored modulation of electronic and surface states for photocatalytic applications. In this work, a 1D/2D TiO2/MXene (TMX) was synthesized via electrostatic self-assembly method, where TiO2 serves as the primary light-absorbing semiconductor and MXene acts as a co-catalyst to promote charge separation and surface redox reactions. High-energy EB irradiation was employed to induce Ov and Ti3+ species within TiO2, markedly improving the photocatalytic hydrogen production of TMX. The optimally irradiated sample (TMX3–500) achieved a hydrogen evolution rate of 691 ± 9.54 μmol g−1 h−1, 5.25 times higher compared to sample before irradiation. Such enhancement was ascribed to improved light absorption, efficient charge carrier separation by the generation of Ov, confirmed by different spectroscopic characterizations. DFT calculations further showed that Ov generate defect states within TiO2 bandgap that interact with adsorbed hydrogen, while interfacial charge transfer from TiO2 to MXene optimizes ΔGH* towards thermoneutrality. The findings highlight the role of EB-induced defect engineering in designing efficient photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen production. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Electrohydrodynamic inkjet printing of porous perovskite color-conversion layers via evaporation-induced phase separation for high-efficiency micro-LED displays
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Perovskite nanocrystal color-conversion layers (PeNC-CCLs) are highly promising for full-color micro-sized light-emitting diode (micro-LED) displays; however, inefficient photon harvesting and emission extraction in printed thin films remain major barriers to achieving high color-conversion efficiency. Herein, we develop a porous-structure engineering strategy for PeNC-CCLs based on evaporation-induced phase separation in a ternary ink system composed of polymethyl methacrylate, polyethylene glycol, and xylene. During solvent evaporation, the polymer blend undergoes phase separation to form a porous framework containing micro-/nanoscale scattering centers. These embedded pores extend the optical path of excitation photons and mitigate waveguided emission losses, thereby substantially improving photon utilization within the CCLs. To suppress nonradiative recombination and preserve the structural integrity of PeNCs during polymer incorporation, the nanocrystal surfaces are pre-stabilized through sequential ligand exchange using a quaternary ammonium bromide and a sulfonic-acid-based zwitterionic ligand. The resulting CsPbBr3 porous films achieve a photoluminescence quantum yield of 89.54%, placing them among the highest-performing polymer-encapsulated PeNC films reported to date. The strategy is fully compatible with electrohydrodynamic inkjet printing, enabling porous fluorescent arrays with a twofold enhancement in photoluminescence intensity and subpixels as small as 10 μm (1270 ppi). Printed dual-color PeNC-CCLs integrated with a blue micro-LED array further yield a full-color display prototype with a resolution of 520 ppi and a color gamut of 143% NTSC. These results establish porous-structure engineering as a scalable and effective route toward high-efficiency, stable, and high-resolution PeNC-based micro-LED displays. © 2026

Abstract: This study focuses on the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker using local raw materials found in the Aral Sea region of the Republic of Uzbekistan and on its properties. The obtained results highlight the technological, economic, and environmental advantages. The raw material mixtures consisted of limestone, barren sand, kaolin, and iron-containing industrial waste, resulting in a clinker with an optimized oxide composition (LSF = 0.82, SR = 2.15, AP = 0.94). Title: Screen-Printed Li Arrays with Reinforced Interphase as Ultrathin Anodes for High-Energy–Density Liquid- and Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: High-energy–density lithium metal batteries, either liquid or solid state, require ultrathin Li anodes, but their implementation is hindered by poor Li processability in fabrication and inhomogeneous Li plating behaviours upon cycling. This work addresses these challenges through a mask-patterned discrete array using a molten salt-derived Li nanocomposite. The screen-printing strategy circumvents the poor wettability of molten Li on copper that causes high Li|Cu contact angle and non-uniform Li spreading, thus fabricating ultrathin Li foils with equivalent thicknesses below 30 μm. Concurrently, the molten salt-derived inorganic nanoparticles in Li favour homogeneous Li deposition and induce inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase to jointly suppress active Li consumption. The resulting Li array (10–28 μm) anodes demonstrate remarkable performance in both liquid- and solid-state systems, achieving high energy densities up to 504 Wh kg−1/1071 Wh L−1 and stable cycling over 260 cycles with high-loading cathodes. This integrated approach resolves both fabrication and cycling challenges of ultrathin Li anodes and offers an alternative solution for high-performance liquid-/solid-state batteries. Title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Quantification to Symmetry-Breaking of Rotation Invariance for Attractors in Perturbed Lorenz System
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: For the existence of the external perturbation on the atmospheric system, the idealized Lorenz system cannot be used to describe the local characteristics of the atmospheric system accurately. From the opinion of mathematical physics, the failure of the description for local characteristics of the perturbed atmospheric system by the idealized Lorenz system is resulted from the symmetry-breaking effects on the local structure the solutions for the system, including the Lorenz attractor. This study aims to precisely quantify the symmetry-breaking degree of the rotation invariant law for the attractors in a perturbed Lorenz system to permit the reproduction on its local characteristics accurately. The attractors of the perturbed Lorenz system are reproduced employing the second-level fourth-order symplectic Runge-Kutta scheme firstly. The structure-preserving properties of the scheme are illustrated by the tiny relative energy error in the conservative field of the Lorenz system, which verifies the validity of the simulation results indirectly. The symmetry-breaking degree for the rotation invariant law of the attractors in the system is characterized by the quantized error defined as the Euclidean distance between the points on the trajectories of the rotated part and of the unrotated part at the same moment. The symmetry-breaking phenomenon characterized by the quantized error goes through three stages in sequence, including the slow growth stage, the quick growth stage, and the oscillation stage. In addition, a pair of Lorenz attractors with the approximate rotation invariant property are observed when the quantized error is in the slow growth stage or in the quick growth stage. From the numerical results, it can be found that, the perturbation may cause the periodic step increase (the amplitudes of steps are doubling increase approximately) of the error with the time elapse even if the perturbation is tiny, which leads to more serious damage to the stability of the system. The main contribution of this work is providing an approach to predict the local stability of the Lorenz system, which may benefit for the accuracy of meteorological forecast or the simulation of specific atmospheric phenomena. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Cooperative elemental variations: A novel composition control strategy based on the cluster formula approach

Abstract: Composition control is primary for alloy production. Title: From industrial electrowinning to reversible aqueous manganese metal batteries
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Aqueous manganese metal batteries (MnMBs) hold great promise for grid‑scale energy storage, owing to their low redox potential (–1.18 V vs. SHE), high volumetric capacity (7250 mAh cm–3), and vast crustal abundance. However, the severe thermodynamic mismatch between Mn and water induces concurrent hydrogen evolution, spontaneous corrosion, and interfacial passivation, which critically undermine Coulombic efficiency and cycle life. This review bridges the century‑old empirical knowledge of industrial electrolytic manganese metal (EMM) production with modern battery science. It shows that interfacial kinetic shielding, historically achieved by additives such as SeO2, provides a translatable blueprint for stabilizing Mn anodes. We systematically deconvolute the coupled failure mechanisms and assess state‑of‑the‑art modification strategies for the anode, electrolyte, and cathode. More importantly, we emphasize the need to translate macroscopic metallurgical principles into nanoscale reversible electrochemical loops and outline a holistic roadmap toward practical MnMBs. Key future directions are identified, including operando interfacial characterization, decoupling of competitive reaction pathways, development of low‑toxicity additives, pH mismatch management, self‑discharge mitigation, and impurity‑tolerance guidelines. By integrating fundamental chemistry and industrial metallurgical wisdom, this review aims to accelerate the development of highly reversible and cost‑effective aqueous MnMBs for next‑generation storage. © 2026

Title: A review of Nb-Si-based ultra-high temperature alloys on oxidation resistance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Nb-Si-based ultra-high-temperature alloys are promising candidate materials for next-generation aerospace engine blades, recognized for their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and low density. Research on these alloys primarily focuses on fracture resistance and oxidation resistance. Through compositional and processing optimizations, the room temperature fracture toughness of these alloys has reached levels suitable for engineering applications. However, significant breakthroughs in oxidation resistance remain elusive. This article reviews recent progress in the oxidation resistance of Nb-Si-based alloys, with a specific focus on three key aspects: alloying, processing routes, and coating technologies. It summarizes studies on the effects of various alloying elements on oxidation behavior, examines the oxidation performance of alloys produced by different processing methods, and compares the protective efficacy of various coating systems fabricated through different techniques. Title: Main characteristics of quartz-feldspar sands from the Khiva deposit, and the physico-chemical and technological fundamentals of obtaining an enriched concentrate
Abstract: This research presents studies on the beneficiation and application of quartz-feldspar sands from the “Khiva deposit” located in the Khorezm region of the Republic of Uzbekistan for the silicate industry. The composition of raw material samples was analysed using modern X-ray diffraction and IR spectroscopic methods. Based on the results, the quantitative mineralogical composition of the samples was determined using the BGMN/Profex Rietveld software package. According to the obtained data, the average chemical composition of the raw material (in wt.%) was determined as follows: SiO₂ – 86.06; Al₂O₃ – 2.64; Fe₂O₃ – 1.37; CaO – 1.37; MgO – 0.22; K₂O – 1.30; Na₂O – 1.85; TiO₂ – 0.04; SO₃ – 0.4, with a loss on ignition of 4.93. Based on the specific characteristics of the composition, it was found appropriate in subsequent studies to apply combinations of beneficiation methods such as washing, gravity separation, classification, attrition scrubbing, electromagnetic separation, and flotation. As a result, it was determined that the SiO₂ content in the beneficiated concentrate increased from 86.06% to 97.07%, while Al₂O₃ decreased from 2.64% to 1.06%, and Fe₂O₃ from 1.37% to 0.05%. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Abstract: The article is devoted to the generalization of data on the entire geological and genetic range of placers in Eastern and Northern Kazakhstan: from the weathering of the kaolin profile at the root sources of ore minerals Au, Ni, Co, RM, Ti, Zr, Nb, TR, through polyfacial and alluvial placers of the near demolition of the Zaisan depression to coastal-marine titanium-zirconium placers Northern Kazakhstan and Pavlodar Irtysh region. Title: Mechanistic study on self-healing coating with superior corrosion fatigue performance for Mg alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Although pre-corrosion-induced fatigue crack initiation is a limitation for the engineering application of Mg alloys, the development of protective coatings to address this issue remains unexplored. A self-healing electrophoretic paint (E-paint) coating on Mg-Al-Ca alloy was developed in this study by encapsulating a corrosion inhibitor (barbituric acid, BA) into halloysite nanocontainers (HNT) to fabricate pH-responsive nanocontainers, which were subsequently incorporated into the coating system. The mechanism of the coating on fatigue crack initiation under pre-corrosion conditions was systematically investigated. Results show that after 7 and 14 days of pre-corrosion, the E-paint-HNT-BA specimen achieved fatigue strengths of 112 and 98 MPa at 1 × 106 cycles, representing improvements of 60% and 133%, respectively, compared to the uncoated alloy. Further evidence demonstrates that when the coating is damaged and the Mg substrate begins to corrode, BA is rapidly released from the HNT in response to the local pH increase caused by corrosion, thereby achieving highly efficient self-healing. This mechanism retards corrosion fatigue crack initiation and enhances the fatigue performance of the Mg-Al-Ca alloy, effectively preventing the progression of localized corrosion attack toward fatigue cracking and thereby addressing the critical challenge of pre-corrosion-induced fatigue failure in service components. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Title: Protonated COF/g-C3N4 S-scheme heterojunction for photocatalytic H2O2 production
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Regulating the electronic structure and interfacial charge transfer of metal-free photocatalysts is essential for efficient solar-driven hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Herein, an all-organic S-scheme heterostructure (HCOF-CN) was fabricated by in-situ growth of an imine-linked covalent organic framework (COF) on graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4), followed by mild sulfuric acid protonation. Protonation converted neutral CdbndN groups into positively charged CdbndNH+ sites, thereby extending visible-light absorption, promoting charge separation, and lowering the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) barrier. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and in-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) confirmed that H2O2 was mainly produced through an indirect two-electron ORR pathway. Protonation further reduced the formation energy of the key *OOH intermediate from 1.61 to 0.97 eV. This work provides a simple protonation-assisted heterojunction strategy for designing efficient metal-free photocatalysts for sustainable H2O2 production. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Title: Beyond a sintering aid: Dual-function Li2CO3 enabling low-temperature co-firing and ultrahigh piezoelectricity in PNN-PZT- LiNbO3 relaxor ferroelectrics

Abstract: Reconciling low-temperature co-firing compatibility with ultrahigh piezoelectricity remains a longstanding challenge for advanced multilayer piezoelectric devices.
