Title: Design principles of metallophthalocyanine-based ORR catalysts: Coordination environment and spin-state engineering
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Metallophthalocyanine (MPc) complexes with well-defined M-N4 coordination sites are promising non‑precious metal catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rational design is limited by incomplete mechanistic understanding and computational challenges. This review establishes actionable design principles by examining how coordination geometry, ligand substitution, and spin configuration collectively govern O2 adsorption, O–O bond activation, and reaction pathway selectivity. Spin state is highlighted as a tunable catalytic degree of freedom, particularly for modulating intermediate binding and 4e−/2e− selectivity. We discuss the electronic origins of activity trends across 3d transition metal MPcs, the modulating effects of electron‑donating and electron‑withdrawing substituents, and the synergistic roles of carbon supports in enhancing conductivity and active‑site utilization. Current limitations in density functional theory calculations, including functional dependence, van der Waals interactions, and spin‑crossover modeling, are comprehensively assessed alongside the persistent theory‑experiment gap. Title: Localized corrosion and oxidation-assisted crack filling and bridging in cracked Cr coatings on Zr alloy cladding
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Through-thickness cracking can compromise the barrier function of Cr coatings on Zr-alloy fuel cladding, yet the defect response depends strongly on environment and crack geometry. Here, 15 ± 2 μm Cr coatings containing narrow cracks generated by 2% tensile strain and wide cracks generated by 20% strain were exposed, respectively, to low-dissolved-oxygen water at 360 °C and 20 MPa for 6000 and 10,000 h and to steam at 1100 °C for 600–3000 s. In pressurized water, coolant reached the substrate through the narrow cracks and produced isolated ZrO2 pockets whose depths increased from approximately 2.1 to 3.6 μm. The surrounding Cr remained adherent, and no continuous interfacial oxide or underfilm propagation was detected, in contrast to the continuous 4.4–5.5 μm oxide on the uncoated inner surface. In steam, the initially 4.7 ± 1.3 μm-wide cracks progressively narrowed and became bridged by 3000 s. Multiscale characterization resolved sequential sidewall Cr2O3 growth, Cr–Zr interdiffusion, ZrCr2 formation, and grain-boundary transport of Zr; the observed phase distributions were also consistent with a possible local reduction of Cr2O3 by transported Zr. These coupled processes generated a multiphase Cr2O3/Cr/ZrO2/ZrCr2 filling zone. The two investigated defect–environment combinations exhibited distinct condition-specific responses: Transport-limited localized corrosion around narrow cracks in hydrogenated water and oxidation-assisted crack filling and bridging of wide cracks in high-temperature steam. The latter produced geometric bridging in the examined sections but did not establish complete three-dimensional closure, recovered mechanical integrity, or gas tightness. © 2026

Title: Fault diagnosis of high-voltage transmission lines based on sequence components and multi-scale spatiotemporal awareness
Abstract: The transient signals of faults in high-voltage transmission lines usually exhibit strong nonlinearity and inter-phase coupling characteristics. Traditional protection algorithms are prone to false actions or false alarms in conditions with weak characteristics such as high-resistance grounding. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method that integrates physical machine decoupling and multi-scale spatiotemporal perception networks. Firstly, by combining the sliding Fourier transform and the symmetrical component method, independent time-series component features are constructed to eliminate inter-phase electromagnetic coupling. Secondly, a multi-scale one-dimensional CNN network is used to extract transient broadband features, and a BiGRU network with a sliding time-series window is utilized to track the sequence evolution process. The weighted attention mechanism is combined to dynamically focus on the key fault wavefronts. Additionally, the Bayesian algorithm is introduced to achieve global optimization of model hyperparameters. Experimental results based on the 220kV high-voltage three-phase transmission line simulation system show that the model exhibits excellent recognition accuracy in six typical scenarios: no fault, single-phase grounding short circuit, two-phase grounding short circuit, two-phase short circuit, three-phase short circuit, and three-phase grounding short circuit. The model has excellent resistance-to-high-resistance capability and has broad application prospects in smart grid engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: FDDNet: Frequency decomposition and dynamic deformable attention for insulator defect detection in complex backgrounds
Abstract: Insulator defect detection is a critical task in power system inspection, as it ensures the safe and reliable operation of electrical equipment. However, in real-world inspection scenarios, insulator defects typically appear as small-scale targets with irregular geometries, often amid complex background interference such as vegetation occlusion and illumination variations. Existing object detection methods based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) rely on feature modeling with fixed receptive fields, which can cause entanglement of redundant information within the feature extraction network. This limitation reduces feature discriminability and leads to suboptimal detection performance. To address these challenges, we propose FDDNet, an improved Frequency Decomposition Dynamic Network based on YOLO11. Specifically, we introduce a C3k2_WT module that enhances feature representation via multi-frequency decomposition, effectively suppressing background interference. In addition, we redesign the C2PSA_DLKA module with deformable large-kernel attention, which dynamically adjusts the receptive field. This design effectively overcomes the constraints of fixed receptive fields in traditional CNNs, mitigates feature redundancy, and improves the attention mechanism's ability to capture irregular edge contours. On the IDID dataset, FDDNet achieves 94.7% precision, outperforming the baseline by 4.0%, while requiring only 6.9 GFLOPs. On the CPLID dataset, FDDNet achieves 96.6% precision and 97.9% mAP@50, confirming its generalization capability. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, FDDNet achieves competitive detection performance with substantially lower computational complexity, demonstrating its potential for lightweight deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimentally validated ANN-based sustainable fault diagnosis framework for solar PV systems
Abstract: Faults in solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays significantly degrade energy yield, reliability, and operational safety, particularly on the DC side where continuous energization increases fault severity. This paper presents an integrated Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-based framework for fault detection, classification, and location (FDCL) in grid-connected solar PV systems. An ANN model is trained using irradiance and ambient temperature to predict the expected array current and voltage under normal operating conditions. Fault detection is achieved by comparing ANN-predicted and measured power, enabling robust identification of abnormal operating states under varying environmental conditions. Following detection, a rule-based classification algorithm distinguishes among major DC-side faults, including open-circuit, short-circuit, degradation, and partial shading faults, using normalized electrical indices and adaptive threshold parameters. A low-complexity voltage-sensor-based fault localization strategy is further developed to accurately identify the faulty module or string with minimal sensing requirements. The proposed FDCL framework is validated through detailed MATLAB/Simulink simulations and extensive experimental testing on a real grid-connected solar PV plant under field operating conditions. Experimental results confirm high fault detection accuracy, reliable fault classification, and precise fault localization, demonstrating the practical applicability of the proposed approach for real-time monitoring and maintenance of solar PV systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Dynamic Analysis of Functionally Graded Nanobeams Using Various Shear Deformation Theories Based on Doublet Mechanics
Abstract: This study investigates the vibrational behavior of a functionally graded beam using the doublet mechanics theory. This theory accounts for interactions between constituent atoms within a structure, enabling consideration of atomic-scale structure and orientation relative to the beam axis. While classical Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko beam theories are commonly used within the framework of doublet mechanics, they typically neglect key terms associated with shear deformation effects. To overcome this limitation, the present research introduces the novel application of higher-order shear deformation theories (HSDTs) within the doublet mechanics framework. This approach, not previously explored in the literature, provides more accurate predictions of vibrational characteristics. The results reveal that employing doublet mechanics can significantly influence natural frequencies, with deviations of up to 5%. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Effects of Balangu seed mucilage and plant proteins on the rheological and structural properties of gluten-free bread: A mixture design approach
Abstract: The absence of gluten weakens the structure of gluten-free bread systems, resulting in poor batter stability, limited gas retention, and reduced crumb porosity. To overcome these limitations, plant proteins and hydrocolloids are commonly incorporated to restore viscoelastic properties. In this regard, batter rheology plays a critical role in regulating gas-cell stability during fermentation and baking, thereby determining the final crumb structure and bread quality. This study used a mixture design to evaluate the effects of two protein isolates (soy protein isolate, SPI; faba bean protein isolate, FPI) and two hydrocolloids (carboxymethyl cellulose, CMC; Balangu seed mucilage, BSM) on the rheological properties of gluten-free batters and bread quality. The aim was to compare SPI and FPI and assess the performance of BSM relative to CMC, considering both individual and interactive effects. Results showed that batter viscoelastic behavior was strongly affected by both protein source and hydrocolloid type. BSM enhanced structural strength and stability more effectively than CMC, indicating a greater ability to promote network formation in the batter matrix. Appropriate protein–hydrocolloid combinations improved gas-cell stability and crumb porosity, whereas excessive hydrocolloid levels produced overly rigid matrices that restricted expansion. Optimization using a desirability function identified an optimal formulation (SPI 0.897%, FPI 3.60%, CMC 0.00%, BSM 0.498%), yielding bread with a specific volume of 4.37 mL/g and porosity of 31.5%. Overall, the results highlight the potential of BSM as a bio-based alternative to CMC and demonstrate the importance of optimizing protein–hydrocolloid ratios to improve gluten-free bread structure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. In the 90° case, VG orientation achieved the highest electrical efficiency at (Re = 11000), achieving an electrical efficiency of 16.9% and maximum achievable electrical power output of approximately 88 W, after accounting for DC fan power consumption, with the 90° VG configuration still showing the highest system electrical power. The 30° scenario, by contrast, resulted in the best thermal efficiency—nearly 80% and the greatest thermal power—over 420 W demonstrating practical merit in providing guidance for selecting PV cooling configurations based on specific electrical-output or thermal-recovery priorities. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Li H.; Li G.; Sun S.; Fu D.
Title: Electromagnetic state prediction in large PMSGs using a physics-informed KAN surrogate model
Abstract: To address the challenge of rapid and accurate electromagnetic state prediction for large-scale permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs), this paper proposes a multi-task learning (MTL) surrogate model integrating principal component analysis (PCA), physics-informed constraints, and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs). The model accepts rotor speed, rotor position, and three-phase currents as inputs. It employs PCA for dimensionality reduction of the spatial magnetic flux density and utilizes a KAN-based multi-task prediction framework to simultaneously output both the magnetic field distribution and scalar quantities, including electromagnetic torque magnitude, iron loss, and eddy current loss. To enhance physical consistency, boundary conditions, divergence constraints, and torque calculation constraints are explicitly embedded into the loss function. Validation using finite element simulation data demonstrates that the model achieves a mean absolute error below 0.01 T for magnetic field reconstruction and a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.99 for electromagnetic torque magnitude prediction. A single inference requires approximately 0.3 seconds, representing a computational speedup exceeding 540 times compared to the finite element method. This work provides a methodological basis for digital twin applications of large-scale PMSGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Han R.; Wei Z.; Zou B.; Zhang Y.; Hu Q.; Ma G.
Title: Co-optimization of production scheduling and demand response for hydrogen-based steel plants considering hydrogen buffering and liquid-steel thermal constraints
Abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduced iron and electric arc furnace (H2DRI-EAF) technology can support deep decarbonization of steel production and provide demand-response (DR) flexibility to power systems. Realizing this flexibility requires coordination of electrolysis, hydrogen storage, and sequential steelmaking operations. Existing studies rarely represent upstream hydrogen management together with downstream liquid-steel production requirements. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework for day-ahead co-optimization of hydrogen production, hydrogen storage, and heat-by-heat steelmaking schedules. Maximum waiting time limits preserve temporal coordination between consecutive liquid steel stages. A linear cooling relation verifies thermal feasibility for the final transfer from AOD to CC, while hydrogen storage decouples electrolyzer operation from shaft furnace hydrogen demand. Under matched conditions, coordinated scheduling reduces specific operating-energy cost by 31.14% and increases the DR flexibility index, quantified here as the off-peak electricity-share index, by 14.55 percentage points relative to the controlled baseline. All 27 joint stress-test scenarios combining variations in PV availability, electricity-price profiles, and shaft-furnace hydrogen consumption remained feasible. Relative to the nominal case within this assessment, the change in total operating-energy cost ranged from −6.67% to 16.73%. The off-peak electricity-share index changed by −1.04 to 1.25 percentage points. Sensitivity analysis identifies electrolyzer capacity as a key determinant of this index under the evaluated conditions. © 2026

Title: Effect of sintering aids on densification and microstructure of pressureless-sintered tantalum carbide coatings
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: Tantalum carbide coatings protect graphite during SiC crystal growth, but pressureless sintering often gives poor densification and residual impurities. This work compares cobalt, silicon, and tantalum sintering aids. Cobalt aids enable liquid‑phase sintering but leave Co residues (~350 ppm), yielding moderate hardness and corrosion resistance. Silicon aids form a liquid but react with TaC or carbon, generating carbides or gases that create pores. Among tantalum aids, Ta metal shows limited solid‑state effect, while Ta₂O₅ melts above 1850°C. Via coupled carbothermal reduction‑liquid spreading, pressureless sintering at 2000°C produces a fully dense, pore‑free, coarse‑grained (~22.15 μm) high‑purity TaC coating. Hardness is 10.4 GPa, better acid corrosion resistance than CVD or Co‑aided coatings, no foreign impurities. These results show a liquid phase is necessary but insufficient; dissolution‑precipitation of TaC in the liquid aid is key. This work provides a theoretical basis for preparing dense high‑purity TaC coatings via a simple pressureless route. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cheng Z.; Li X.; Zhang T.; Zhou Z.
Title: An efficient cooperative optimization reconfiguration scheme using joint integer coding and hybrid sparrow search algorithm for active distribution networks
Abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed generations (DGs) brings both opportunities and challenges to the operation of active distribution networks (ADNs). Conventional distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) approaches often struggle to achieve global optimality and maintain stable operation under DGs-rich conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid sparrow search algorithm (HSSA) based on an integer coding method for the multi-objective reconfiguration of ADNs. The DNR problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization model that simultaneously minimizes power loss, voltage deviation index (VDI), and load balancing index (LBI), while satisfying radial network topology and operational constraints. To effectively eliminate infeasible solutions and reduce the search space, the ordered loop matrix is constructed based on evaluating a specific electrical metric. To obtain reconfiguration schemes, the HSSA is employed, incorporating the particle swarm optimization (PSO) search strategy and the Metropolis criterion to maintain a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation. Numerical simulations on IEEE 33-bus and 118-bus distribution networks validate the effectiveness of the proposed HSSA, demonstrating its superiority over existing algorithms in terms of convergence rate and accuracy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang J.; Li X.; Wang X.
Title: Hierarchical and regional coordination strategy for optimal operation of shore power systems based on energy routers
Abstract: Energy routers act as the energy transmission hubs of shore power system and play a crucial role in achieving the reliable and efficient utilization of renewable energy. To improve the safe and economical operation of shore power systems, this paper proposes a hierarchical and regional coordination strategy for energy-router-based shore power systems. Firstly, a shore power network incorporating energy routers is introduced and divided into a regional layer and a global layer. Secondly, power allocation and loss optimization are implemented separately at the regional and global layers, enabling the shore power system to prioritize renewable energy consumption and minimize the system's active power loss under normal operating conditions. Case studies are conducted on a three-substation shore power system under both normal and faulty operating conditions. When the power supply of a substation is disconnected from operation due to a fault, the optimal fault transfer power supply scheme is determined by analyzing and comparing the hierarchical and regional optimal operation results under various fault transfer alternatives. Case study results indicate that the proposed strategy can minimize the active power loss of the shore power system under various operating conditions, thereby enhancing the safety and economy of the shore power system. © 2026

Authors: Wang H.; Yuan Z.; Chen J.; Lu F.
Title: A post-fault island partitioning method for distribution networks considering overall frequency security and spatial nodal RoCoF constraints
Abstract: For distribution networks with distributed generators, post-fault island partitioning can restore local power supply, whereas limited island inertia and frequency support may cause frequency security violations during load restoration. To address the limitations of conventional methods in simultaneously capturing the center-of-inertia frequency response and the spatial heterogeneity of nodal rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), this paper proposes a post-fault island partitioning method considering overall frequency security and spatial nodal RoCoF constraints. An island-level frequency response model is first established, in which the center-of-inertia RoCoF, frequency nadir, and quasi-steady-state frequency deviation are embedded into the stepwise load restoration process. A spatial nodal RoCoF model is then developed to identify local dynamic security risks that may be overlooked by center-of-inertia frequency indicators. Furthermore, nodal RoCoF checking is incorporated into the feasibility assessment of load restoration, and load blocks associated with RoCoF violations are adjusted to determine load block energization, partial load restoration, and final island partitioning results. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems show that a restoration scheme satisfying center-of-inertia frequency constraints may still experience local nodal RoCoF violations. The proposed method can eliminate such local violations by adjusting selected load blocks, thereby improving the dynamic security of post-fault island partitioning schemes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Mao S.; Li M.; Wang W.; Han P.; Li H.; Zhang T.; Lu C.
Title: Carrageenan based hydrogel systems with artificial compartment for probiotics microcapsules and tannic acid to preserve perishable food
Abstract: In this study, microcapsules of Lactococcus lactis in whey protein isolated/sodium alginate was co-encapsulated with tannic acid in the carrageenan hydrogel. This design created compartments via the microcapsules and prevented the activity loss with direct contact of the components. The structural analysis results indicated that tannic acid and microcapsules strengthened the network structure through hydrogen bonding. The incorporation of microcapsules into the hydrogel provided physical support, improving the mechanical properties of the carrageenan-based composite hydrogel by 36.5%. Furthermore, the acidic microenvironment created by Lactococcus lactis and the protective network formed by tannic acid mutually enhanced stability and demonstrated synergistic effects. The composite hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant activity with scavenging rates exceeding 80% for ABTS, DPPH and superoxide anion radicals. Meanwhile, it significantly inhibited the growth of bacteria and fungi, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Salmonella enteritidis, Aspergillus niger and Botrytis cinerea. Biocompatibility assessment showed that the composite hydrogel exhibited virtually no cytotoxicity or hemolytic activity, and could promote plant growth after degradation in water. Practical storage tests confirmed that composite hydrogel significantly delayed browning of fresh-cut apples and potatoes, maintaining acceptability after 1 and 8 h storage. Besides, it slowed the accumulation of total volatile basic nitrogen and deterioration of sensory quality in refrigerated chicken, extending shelf life by 2 days. In summary, the composite hydrogel possessed outstanding functionality and practicality, providing a promising strategy for the design of highly efficient and safe active food packaging. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Ren W.; Liu H.; Li L.; Li C.
Title: Research on online multi-step short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on selective representation-driven concept drift adaptation
Abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the secure operation and optimal scheduling of power systems. However, PV power data are highly non-stationary due to weather fluctuations, seasonal transitions, and changing operating conditions, which often cause concept drift in real-world scenarios. Most existing methods are developed in offline settings and lack the ability to adapt continuously to evolving data streams. To address this issue, this study proposes an online learning framework for multi-step short-term PV power forecasting. Specifically, a shared-parameter dual-branch Informer concept encoder is designed to capture concept discrepancies between historical and incoming data, while a mixture-of-experts adaptive parameter generator is introduced to produce targeted update parameters for different drift patterns. In addition, a selective segmentation mechanism is incorporated into the TimeBridge backbone to improve the modeling of critical temporal blocks. Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for drift-aware online PV forecasting and offers practical support for enhancing the reliability, stability, and dispatch efficiency of power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Crystallization of lithium aluminosilicate glass into low thermal expansion glass-ceramics by Ultrafast High-temperature Treatment

Abstract: We employed an Ultrafast High-temperature Treatment (UHT) to crystallize monolithic lithium aluminosilicate (LAS) glass pieces with variable holding time and electric power level under controlled power ramp. Title: Unveiling the impact of mixed-strain solid-state fermentation on wheat bran dietary fiber: gluten protein structure evolution, dough rheological modulation and steamed bread quality enhancement
Abstract: Wheat bran dietary fiber (WBDF) helps enhance the nutrition of dough products, but its direct incorporation triggers quality deterioration. In this study, a mixed-strain solid-state fermentation strategy involving Basidiomycetes, Candida utilis, and Lactobacillus plantarum was employed to modify WBDF. The underlying mechanisms by which modified WBDF affects dough and steamed bread quality were systematically investigated across a range of addition levels (0, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 %). Results showed that unfermented WBDF (UWBDF) disrupted the gluten network, reducing dough and steamed bread quality. In contrast, fermented WBDF (FWBDF) effectively mitigated these adverse effects. At the gluten protein level, FWBDF promoted disulfide bond cross-linking (free sulfhydryl groups content decreased from 8.16 to 7.36 μmol/g), and increased the glutenin macropolymer content from 0.47 to 1.92 g/100 g. Besides, FWBDF optimized water distribution within the dough, improving water availability for starch and gluten proteins. These changes enhanced the pasting, extension, and dynamic rheological properties of dough, ultimately improving steamed bread quality-characterized by increased specific volume (from 1.71 to 2.30 mL/g), texture (hardness from 3209 to 2670 g; springiness from 0.81 to 0.84), and antioxidant capacity. Notably, the beneficial effects of FWBDF were closely dependent on its addition level. At 3-6 % addition, the modifying advantages of WBDF were fully realized; however, at 12-15 %, excessive FWBDF exacerbated gluten network disruption, leading to quality deterioration of dough and steamed bread. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the fermentation modification of WBDF and its application in steamed bread production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Grid-connected performance optimization control strategy of DFIG with coaxial high-inertia flywheel system
Abstract: The high penetration of grid-connected renewable energy has significantly reduced power system inertia, bringing critical challenges to frequency stability and voltage support. To improve the operation resilience of low-inertia systems, this paper presents a grid-connected performance optimization control strategy for the combined topology of a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) and a coaxial high-inertia flywheel. The DFIG stator is directly connected to the grid, and the flywheel provides fast kinetic energy support through mechanical coupling. The grid-side converter maintains stable DC voltage and unity power factor, while the rotor-side converter realizes decoupled control of stator active and reactive power. To enhance frequency stability, a system frequency response model is established, and real-time active power compensation is generated via droop and inertia control. A variable-parameter optimization strategy is further proposed to adjust droop and inertia coefficients dynamically. For grid voltage sag conditions, an optimized feed-forward transient current control scheme is adopted to enhance low-voltage ride-through capability. Both theoretical analysis and results verify that the proposed topology and control strategy can effectively improve the frequency and voltage stability of low-inertia power systems, providing technical support for the reliable operation of high-renewable power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Simultaneous enhancement of hardness and corrosion resistance in liquid-metal-dealloyed Mg–Ti composites via short-time Al-melt treatment
Abstract: This study presents a short-time reactive Al-melt treatment that simultaneously enhances hardness and corrosion resistance in liquid-metal-dealloyed Mg–Ti composites. A three-dimensional bicontinuous Mg–Ti composite is first fabricated by immersing a Ti30Cu70 precursor in a pure Mg melt, followed by immersion in a pure Al melt at 750 °C for 10 s. TiAl3 forms along the residual α -Ti ligaments, whereas the original Mg-rich regions transform into Al3Mg2. The average effective grain size of the residual α -Ti decreases from 3.7 to 0.8 µm, accompanied by increased local misorientation and a higher density of {11–22} compression twin boundaries. As a result, the surface hardness increases from 106 to 378 HV, while remaining above 260 HV at a depth of 260 µm. The Al-treated Mg–Ti composite also exhibits a markedly reduced corrosion rate in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, decreasing from 13.2 to 0.5 mm/year based on hydrogen evolution measurements and from 17.2 to 0.7 mm/year based on weight-loss measurements. Scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals that the initial direct α -Mg/ α -Ti interface, with a Volta potential difference of approximately 635 mV, is replaced by α -Ti/TiAl3 and TiAl3/Al3Mg2 interfaces with lower potential differences of approximately 271 and 285 mV, respectively. Overall, the short-time Al-melt treatment enables simultaneous hardness increase and corrosion mitigation through rapid interfacial reconstruction and phase transformation while preserving the bicontinuous structure. Authors: Deng Y.; Li W.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.; Xin Q.; Hou X.
Title: Closed-loop robotic polishing cell with toolpath orchestration for mid-spatial frequency error suppression
Abstract: Mid-spatial-frequency (MSF) errors induced by repetitive toolpaths remain a major limitation in robotic polishing of precision optical surfaces. This study proposes a closed-loop robotic polishing cell with toolpath orchestration that integrates surface metrology, removal-function management, a parameterized toolpath library, path-based material-removal prediction, and multistage robotic execution. The proposed approach replaces isolated single-path optimization with stage-specific coordination of complementary trajectories. A NURBS-interpolated Gosper path is incorporated as a functional toolpath within the proposed framework, where the space-filling characteristics of the Gosper curve provide multidirectional coverage and NURBS interpolation improves trajectory continuity for MSF-error suppression. Numerical verification and two sets of polishing experiments were conducted on aspheric optical components. In the representative Hilbert–NURBS-interpolated Gosper strategy, the Hilbert path provided efficient baseline correction, whereas the proposed path further suppressed residual periodic textures. Numerical results reduced PV/RMS from 403.216/70.968 nm to 146.891/18.255 nm, corresponding to reductions of 63.6% and 74.3%, respectively. Experimental PSD analysis showed that this coordinated strategy produced the lowest final PSD value among the three tested configurations, with an overall convergence rate of 86.849% at the characteristic MSF wavelength. Additional experiments comparing spiral–NURBS-interpolated Gosper and NURBS-interpolated Gosper–pseudo-random sequences provided further experimental evidence for the effectiveness of toolpath coordination under the tested conditions. The former achieved PSD convergence rates of 99.99%, 99.96%, and 99.02% at characteristic wavelengths of 4, 2.5, and 1.28 mm, respectively, and produced the lowest final spectral levels. These results demonstrate that coordinated use of complementary paths can simultaneously improve form convergence, suppress characteristic MSF peaks, and enhance residual-surface uniformity, providing a framework for integrating metrology, toolpath planning, and robotic precision finishing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Comparative evaluation of SRF-PLL and instantaneous-power LVRT control for a three-wire grid-connected PV system under ground faults
Abstract: The performance of low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control depends on the voltage information used for synchronisation and current-reference generation, as well as the physical current paths of the converter. In this paper, four synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) and instantaneous power theory (IPT) implementations are compared on a common 1.504 MW photovoltaic simulation model under single line-to-ground and double line-to-ground faults. The three-wire converter is connected through a delta–grounded-wye transformer. Consequently, its zero-sequence line current is constrained to zero, although ground-fault current is present on the grounded transformer side. The current-control action is therefore confined to the two independent converter axes. The comparison uses conventional and positive-sequence-conditioned SRF and IPT implementations with a shared reactive-current-priority LVRT law, DC-voltage regulation and current-reference limits. For the double line-to-ground case, positive-sequence IPT provides 730.6 kvar at the low-voltage measurement point, compared with 376.1 kvar for instantaneous-voltage IPT, while its nonfundamental current residual decreases from 22.06% to 0.037%. However, the latter controller has a smaller 100 Hz active-power component, demonstrating a trade-off between power oscillation and current quality. Actual transient current reaches 1.234 pu despite a 1.2 pu reference ceiling. Sequence-extraction diagnostics against established DSOGI and DSC methods, together with transformer-side measurements, explain these outcomes. Hardware-in-loop captures document laboratory-platform observations; all quantitative controller comparisons are based on simulations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tang Y.; Jia J.; Ye H.; Chen J.; Zeng H.; Rui Z.
Title: Accelerated reaction dynamics in engineered multifunctional nanodomains for efficient photothermal ammonia synthesis
Abstract: Prospects for a sustainable economic and ecological growth identify the ammonia economy as a pivotal facilitator for future energy transition. Herein, we demonstrate that FeCo co-doped N,S-modified Ti3C2 MXene with in-situ derived TiO2-x nanoparticles (or FeCo-CNS-TM) achieves efficient photothermal catalytic ammonia synthesis from nitrogen and water vapor (100 mW cm–2, 350 °C), yielding a production rate of 1769.8 μmol g–1 h–1. In this catalyst, FeCo bimetallic nanoclusters enrich energetic photoelectrons from both TiO2-x and Ti3C2 MXene, and then bimetallic synergy promotes N2 side-on adsorption and electron donation, enabling effective N2 activation and reduction. Meanwhile, TiO2-x and hydrophilic groups on MXene preferentially interact with water molecules and produce protons, preventing the competitive water adsorption and poisoning of FeCo active sites, thereby ensuring high efficiency and selectivity of ammonia synthesis reaction. Such multifunctional nanodomains provide a viable approach for designing highly active and stable photothermal catalysts for green NH3 synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tian X.; Du Z.; Xu Y.; Tang Z.; Zhang C.; Li D.
Title: Fault recovery analysis and damping control for global stability of grid-forming energy storage based on Lyapunov's direct method
Abstract: With the continuous integration of large-scale new energy into the power system, grid-forming energy storage plays a crucial role in maintaining system stability. However, the current research on the transient stability of grid-forming energy storage is still not comprehensive. The energy function method, as an important tool for power system stability analysis, still does not fully describe the voltage dynamic response of grid-forming energy storage when constructing the energy function. To address these issues, this paper comprehensively considers the dynamic characteristics of the reactive power control loop of grid-forming energy storage, derives an improved Lyapunov energy function considering voltage dynamic changes, thereby improving the accuracy of transient stability judgment. Meanwhile, a global stability damping control strategy based on the second stable equilibrium point is proposed.By analyzing the correlation between the upper limit of frequency variation and virtual damping, it is pointed out that there exists a minimum damping such that the phase trajectory does not exceed the second unstable equilibrium point.This control strategy enables the system to recover stability within the region of attraction corresponding to the second stable equilibrium point under severe post-fault conditions, and improves the transient stability margin of the power grid under large disturbances. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li J.; Hou D.; Lin X.; Li X.
Title: Research on the integration method of power transfer and data communication based on LCL resonant topology
Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional Power Line Carrier (PLC) communication, which can only transmit weak signals and struggles to balance high-power supply in strong interference environments, this paper proposes a power and signal integration method based on an LCL resonant topology. Unlike conventional PLC that superimposes communication signals onto the power-frequency grid, this scheme utilizes the LCL resonant network to construct a physical channel characterized by "isolation at power frequency and conduction at high frequency." This enables efficient transmission of hundred-watt-level high-frequency power while simultaneously performing narrowband data communication. By establishing a fundamental equivalent model of the system, the dual mechanisms of impedance matching and bandpass filtering of the LCL topology near the resonant frequency are revealed. This demonstrates its feasibility in ensuring power transfer efficiency while naturally suppressing power-frequency and broadband noise through frequency selectivity. Simulation and experimental results show that the system can stably deliver hundred-watt-level power at a resonant frequency of 20 kHz. It exhibits excellent robustness in noisy environments, achieving a Bit Error Rate (BER) of 0.0649 even with a Gaussian white noise Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) as low as 5 dB. This research achieves the integrated "power supply and communication" functionality over power lines, offering a highly reliable and high-power-density transmission solution for local energy internet applications in complex electromagnetic environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhao Y.; Chi L.; Yang K.; Yan W.; Liu S.
Title: Gradient nanostructure promoting protective oxidation and suppressing dissolution corrosion of 9Cr ODS steel in oxygen-saturated LBE
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) steels are promising structural materials for lead-cooled fast reactors, but their corrosion resistance in liquid lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) is governed by the competition between protective oxide-scale formation and metal dissolution. Here, a gradient nanostructure (GNS) surface layer was introduced on 9Cr ODS steel by ultrasonic surface rolling processing (USRP) to regulate this competition. Corrosion tests were conducted in oxygen-saturated LBE at 650 °C for up to 500 h. The GNS layer, characterized by gradients in grain-boundary density and geometrically necessary dislocation density, facilitated the rapid formation of a protective oxide layer at the early stage of corrosion, with a formation rate markedly higher than that of the untreated sample. After 500 h, the USRP-treated sample developed a compact multilayer scale consisting of Fe3O4, Fe3−xCrxO4, and Cr2O3, with a dispersed Si-O-rich amorphous phase, with a total thickness of 8.90 ± 1.23 μm. By contrast, the untreated sample exhibited pronounced dissolution attack, with a Cr-depleted zone of 9.80 ± 1.40 μm. The enhanced corrosion resistance is attributed to the defect-assisted short-circuit diffusion of Cr and Si in the GNS layer, which promotes rapid oxide nucleation and the formation of a Si-O-rich amorphous phase/Cr2O3 composite barrier at the oxide/substrate interface. This barrier may contribute to the integrity of the inner oxide scale and the stability of the oxide/substrate interface, thereby shifting the corrosion mode from dissolution-dominated degradation to protective oxidation. These results demonstrate that GNS provides an effective surface-design strategy for improving the LBE corrosion resistance of ODS steels. © 2026

Title: Prediction of lightning flashover on overhead distribution lines from preliminary breakdown voltages based on deep learning
Abstract: Lightning strikes represent a major source of risk for power systems, particularly for overhead distribution lines, where indirect events can induce dangerous overvoltages through electromagnetic coupling. This work represents a first step towards the development of a predictive lightning protection system based on the detection of Preliminary Breakdown (PB) pulses, i.e., sequences of lower-intensity atmospheric discharges typically preceding the Return Stroke (RS) by several tens of milliseconds. Synthetic PB- and RS-induced voltage waveforms are generated using a dedicated simulation tool. Time-domain samples of PB-induced voltages from two sensors are used to train a Deep Learning (DL) model to predict the maximum RS-induced voltage and assess whether it may lead to a flashover event. The line Critical FlashOver Voltage (CFO), increased by 50%, is used as a threshold for classification between safe and dangerous conditions. The proposed model achieves promising performance, paving the way for further development of a preventive lightning protection system (to be combined with state-of-the-art methods) exploiting PB-induced voltage measurements. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Interlaminar Shear Failure Monitoring in GFRPs Using Graphene Nanoplatelets
Abstract: Components made of glass fiber reinforced polymers often fail under interlaminar shear loading conditions, which can significantly compromise their structural performance. To solve this problem, the piezoresistive effect of graphene nanoplatelets integrated into the glass fiber reinforced polymers is proposed as a technique to monitor and detect interlaminar shear failure. For that, short beam shear specimens were prepared from glass fiber reinforced polymers modified with graphene nanoplatelets, and changes in electrical resistance caused by quasi-static bending forces were recorded to monitor the electromechanical behavior and failure mode. The interlaminar shear strength was obtained at around 30 MPa for both composites (0.75 and 1 wt.% graphene nanoplatelets). Results indicate that the incorporation of graphene nanoplatelets has a minimal effect on the electromechanical behavior curves, and both concentrations (0.75 and 1 wt.%) provide good electrical sensing capability for interlaminar shear failure in glass fiber reinforced polymers, which can be used as an active tool for health monitoring applications across a wide variety of industrial applications, especially where this failure mode may occur. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Synergistic modification of okara insoluble dietary fiber by hydrothermal alkaline treatment and ball milling reinforces casein gel properties
Abstract: This study investigated how hydrothermal alkaline treatment, ball milling, and their combination modified the structural and physicochemical properties of okara insoluble dietary fiber (OIDF) and influenced the properties of acid-induced casein gels. Hydrothermal alkaline treatment (105 or 121 °C, pH 11.0) loosened the compact fiber structure, generated a porous network, and shifted the hydrogen-bonding pattern from intra- to intermolecular associations. These changes markedly enhanced water-holding capacity (WHC) and elasticity, supporting the formation of a gel-like fiber network. Ball milling (300 rpm, 1 or 3 h) preferentially disrupted amorphous regions, reduced particle size, and increased specific surface area and pore volume by 10- and 22-fold, respectively. In casein gels, the increased negative surface charge and altered hydrogen bonding may facilitate OIDF-casein interactions, while fiber structure further influenced its incorporation into the gel network. Hydrothermally alkali-treated OIDF may contribute to gel reinforcement through its network-like structure, whereas ball-milled OIDF primarily favored filling and surface interactions. The combined treatment, particularly hydrothermal alkaline treatment followed by 1 h of ball milling (105-BM-1 or 121-BM-1), combined the complementary effects of the two treatments, resulting in a link density of 90.0%, a WHC of 795 g/kg, and a storage modulus of 900 Pa. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Chen J.; Wu C.; Xu M.; Zhang Y.; Chang W.; Liu F.; Luan G.
Title: Soybean protein-stabilized O/W emulsion coagulant for controlled Mg2+ release: A novel green strategy for high-quality tofu production
Abstract: Conventional brine coagulant, mainly Magnesium chloride (MgCl2), tends to cause rapid solidification and result in uneven gel structure in tofu. The development and application of controlled release coagulants provide an effective solution to this problem. In this study, soybean protein was used as the natural emulsifier to construct oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion coagulants to achieve effective loading and controlled release of Mg2+. The preparation process, physical properties, Mg2+release of the emulsions, and the effect of temperatures on the quality of the tofu were investigated. The emulsion prepared under optimized conditions achieved a loading rate of MgCl2 to 57.39%, with an average particle size of 47.73 μm, exhibiting excellent physical stability, rheological property and long-term storage stability. Simulated release tests showed that the initial and equilibrium conductivity of Mg2+ in the emulsion coagulants was lower than that of the brine control, indicating that the emulsion had a good controlled release performance for Mg2+. This is mainly attributed to the high viscosity and the tight droplet network structure of the emulsion. Compared with traditional brine tofu, the moisture content of the emulsion coagulated tofu decreased lightly, but the water holding capacity increased significantly. Scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed that a uniform and dense protein network was formed inside the emulsion coagulated tofu, and there were numerous microporous structures, which could effectively capture and bind more water molecules. The color and texture analysis of the tofu revealed that the introduction of oil phase markedly enhanced the brightness of tofu. The color parameters of the tofu prepared at high temperature were very similar to those of traditional brine tofu. The texture analysis showed that the hardness of the tofu was significantly reduced, while its springiness and cohesiveness were greatly improved, resulting in a softer texture and enhanced resistance to deformation. The emulsion coagulants developed in this study based on the natural components of soybean seed without any chemical emulsifier, providing a novel approach to produce green or organic tofu. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li S.; Yu Z.; Song B.; Zhang D.; Wei D.
Title: Prescribed-Time voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing for multi-agent AC microgrids with time-varying cooperative gains
Abstract: Although voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing in AC microgrids have been extensively investigated, nonlinear Q-V coupling and mismatched feeder impedances can still induce power sharing imbalances. Fixed-gain droop control exhibits difficulties in simultaneously balancing transient response and steady-state accuracy, whereas conventional finite-time control may be sensitive to initial voltage deviations. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-agent prescribed-time control strategy for voltage synchronization and reactive power sharing in AC microgrids, incorporating nonlinear coupling and time-varying cooperative characteristics. Firstly, a DG state-space model is transformed into a linear canonical form via feedback linearization, which provides a tractable basis for coordinated voltage regulation under nonlinear Q-V coupling. A capacity weighted virtual impedance compensation is incorporated into the voltage consensus variable to enhance capacity based reactive power sharing under nonidentical feeder impedances. Meanwhile, a piecewise-smooth time-varying cooperative gain is designed to improve the initial disturbance response while moderating the control effort. Secondly, a time scale transformation converts the prescribed-time convergence objective into an asymptotic stabilization problem, and Lyapunov analysis is used to establish prescribed-time convergence under the stated assumptions. Finally, MATLAB/Simulink simulations are conducted under load disturbances, reactive load steps, DG plug-and-play events, unequal capacity conditions, practical parameter perturbations, measurement noise, and fixed communication delays. Comparative and sensitivity results with conventional droop control, fixed-gain consensus control, and fixed-time secondary control indicate improved voltage recovery, reduced reactive power sharing error, and finite virtual-input magnitude within the tested operating range. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Shi W.; Zhao H.
Title: MDG-Mamba: Evolution-aware selective state-space modeling with macro-micro decoupling for non-stationary photovoltaic power forecasting
Abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for the reliable integration of solar energy into modern power grids. However, the strong non-stationarity and rapid fluctuations of PV outputs caused by changing weather conditions make it challenging for existing methods to capture abrupt power transitions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes MDG-Mamba, a gradient-enhanced macro-micro decoupled framework built upon the Mamba architecture. The model incorporates gradient-based temporal evolution enhancement to characterize first-order variations in PV generation and employs macro-micro temporal decoupling to separate long-term trends from high-frequency fluctuations. A multi-frequency refinement mechanism is further introduced to preserve local fluctuation characteristics while enabling efficient long-range dependency modeling. Experiments on four heterogeneous real-world PV datasets show that MDG-Mamba consistently outperforms competitive baselines, with an average MAE reduction of approximately 8.5%. In ramp-event evaluations on the LSP-PV dataset, MDG-Mamba achieves an MAE of 0.241 under ramp-only conditions, outperforming representative baselines and demonstrating superior capability in tracking abrupt PV power transitions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li R.; Wang Y.; Zhu Z.; Xiao C.; Yang Y.; Qi J.; Zhou Y.; Li J.
Title: Engineered pyridinic-N-rich COFs drive an adsorption–reduction cascade for macroscopic gold recovery from e-waste leachates
Abstract: Gold recovery from electronic waste (e-waste) offers a sustainable solution to resource scarcity. However, integrating selective Au(III) capture, interfacial reduction, and efficient product recovery within a single functional platform remains challenging. Herein, we report a pyridinic-N-rich covalent organic framework (BTTPA-Bpy-COF) for selective gold recovery from e-waste leachates through an adsorption–reduction cascade. The integrated bipyridine/pyridine–imine motifs enable rapid [AuCl4]− capture through cooperative electrostatic and coordination interactions. Concurrently, the electron-rich π-conjugated COF framework promotes electron transfer to the coordinated Au species, facilitating the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). The resultant BTTPA-Bpy-COF exhibits rapid Au(III) adsorption kinetics and a maximum experimentally measured extraction capacity of 4655.95 mg g−1 under optimized conditions (1000 mg L−1 Au(III), pH 4, and 65 °C). Under mild thermal and mechanical stimulation, the in situ generated Au nanoparticles undergo aggregation and subsequent liberation from the COF scaffold, enabling physical isolation of an Au-rich fraction, followed by thermal purification to obtain metallic gold. Processing BTTPA-Bpy-COF into membrane and aerogel architectures further improves its processability and recoverability by enabling easier separation and reuse of the material compared with its powder form. This work offers a new strategy for integrating gold capture and recovery in COF platforms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enabling metal-free photocatalytic self-Fenton mineralization of refractory pollutants via a quinone/hydroquinone redox cycle
Abstract: Photocatalytic self-Fenton catalysts synergistically remove organic pollutants by coupling photosynthesis of H2O2 with the Fenton reaction. However, metal-based self-Fenton systems inevitably generate secondary pollution associated with transition metal sludge disposal. Here, we rationally designed a metal-free graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) catalyst covalently grafted with tetrahydroxy-1,4-benzoquinone (THQ) to construct an efficient, sustainable photocatalytic self-Fenton system. The integrated THQ not only enhances the visible-light harvesting and directional separation of photogenerated carriers of g-C3N4, but also serves as a dual-functional active center. Specifically, THQ is proposed to facilitate the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR) for in-situ H2O2 generation and subsequently promote the activation of the generated H2O2 into highly reactive hydroxyl radicals (•OH) through its quinone/hydroquinone (Q/QH2) redox cycle. Consequently, the THQ/g-C3N4 composite exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a 4.98-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant of ciprofloxacin (CIP) within 2 h compared to pristine g-C3N4. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrates remarkable practical applicability, achieving a 50 % total organic carbon (TOC) removal efficiency in Chinese Baijiu distillery wastewater within 5 h. This study establishes metal-free, photocatalytic self-Fenton catalysis as a promising strategy for sustainable environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Quantifying hydrophobicity migration threshold time of composite insulators based on dynamic contact angles under coupled temperature and humidity
Abstract: In this paper, a novel hydrophobicity migration threshold time characterization method is proposed on the basis of dynamic contact angle time series analysis, which aims to evaluate the performance of composite insulators after contamination and moisture absorption. Corresponding tests under six combined temperature-humidity environments were performed on artificially contaminated specimens, and a double-exponential empirical model was adopted for quantitative kinetic fitting. Coupled with molecular dynamics (MD) simulation results, the microscopic action mechanisms underlying temperature and humidity influences on hydrophobicity migration through contamination layers were systematically revealed. Furthermore, a continuous threshold time prediction model was constructed, which lays a reliable quantitative foundation for scientific decision-making in power system operation and maintenance in heavily polluted areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enhanced dynamic control of multi-area interconnected microgrids using virtual inertia and improved gazelle-optimized TPIDD2 controller
Abstract: Low system inertia in renewable-rich microgrids (μGs) makes frequency and voltage stability highly vulnerable to disturbances and non-nominal operating conditions. To address this challenge, this work proposes an enhanced control strategy for two-area interconnected μGs using an improved Gazelle optimization algorithm (IGOA) tuned tilt-proportional-integral-derivative second-order derivative (TPIDD2) controller integrated with virtual inertia control (VIC). The approach simultaneously targets improvements across load frequency control (LFC) and automatic voltage regulation (AVR). Its robustness is evaluated against variations in load demand, renewable generation uncertainty, changes in inertia levels, and communication time delays (CTDs). Performance is benchmarked against controllers optimized with grey wolf, whale, and arithmetic optimization algorithms, as well as a conventional PID controller. Sensitivity analysis is included to ensure reliability under diverse operating scenarios, and practical validation is demonstrated using a real-time experimental OPAL-RT platform. The results confirm that the offered approach substantially enhances the dynamic performance and resilience of interconnected μGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Deng J.; Li X.; Liu J.
Title: Zonal allocation and pricing of power system inertia considering frequency spatio-temporal characteristics
Abstract: In high‑ratio power electronic systems, the uneven distribution and diversity of generation sources lead to significant spatio-temporal characteristics in frequency response, complicating inertia configuration. Most power markets with frequency security constraints clear at the system level, which cannot capture the dynamic process. This paper aims to address the issue of improper inertia allocation in power systems with a high penetration of renewable energy. It proposes a zoning method that accounts for system topology and congestion risks to allocate inertia and establish zonal inertia prices, thereby implementing a zone-based framework for inertia dispatch and pricing. Firstly, the system topology and the line congestion characteristics under uncertain scenarios are analyzed, and the real-time zoning results under different scenarios are obtained by combining the cosine similarity and clustering algorithm. Secondly, the inertia market clearing model is constructed, and a continuous security constrained unit commitment (SCUC) model is proposed to accurately quantify the price of inertia in each zone. The final case study shows that, compared with overall dispatching, zonal dispatching of inertia effectively alleviates the inertia deficit in certain areas, leading to more accurate allocation and a 20% reduction in total cost, making this approach more economical. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Abbasi S.; Jalilian A.
Title: A robust energy management model for unbalanced microgrids under electricity price uncertainty considering central inverters and demand response for voltage unbalance mitigation
Abstract: The increasing penetration of unbalanced loads, such as single-phase electric vehicles, in microgrids (MGs) can lead to significant Power Quality (PQ) issues, requiring demand response and ancillary services for mitigation. In this regard, an energy management model for renewable energy resources (RES) and energy storage (ES)-based buses is proposed, in which central inverters are used to support PQ and coordinate energy trading. An unbalanced IEEE 13-bus test system is used to evaluate the proposed framework, with particular emphasis on voltage unbalance mitigation and energy management. The results show that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage unbalance Indicator (VUI) from approximately 4% to below the 2%, with only a 0.35% increase in operating cost. In addition, a robust optimization approach is employed to address electricity price uncertainty, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework under uncertain operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enhancing wind energy forecasting under constrained data conditions: a CRISP-DM-based deep neural network approach
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of wind energy production plays a crucial role in the efficient operation of energy markets. However, many advanced models depend on extensive datasets and detailed meteorological information that are rarely available in industrial environments. This work investigates short-term wind power forecasting under constrained industrial conditions, including limited data availability, incomplete high-resolution meteorological information, and noisy operational measurements. A Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM)-based workflow is adopted to support data preprocessing, model training, and validation throughout the forecasting process. An openly available dataset containing hourly records from multiple European wind farms is used, focusing on a single wind farm subset to evaluate forecasting performance under realistic single-site deployment conditions. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model combined with lag-based and nonlinear feature engineering techniques is implemented to capture operational relationships without relying on complete external meteorological fields. Experimental results show that feedforward architectures can provide competitive forecasting performance under constrained data scenarios. The findings highlight the importance of balancing model complexity, data availability, robust validation, and deployability in real-world wind energy forecasting applications. © 2026

Title: Faulted phase selection using paraconsistent annotated logic
Abstract: Accurate faulted phase selection is an essential function in the protection of long transmission lines. However, conventional schemes based on deterministic thresholds or impedance estimation may fail under remote and high-resistance fault conditions, where fault indicators often provide contradictory information. This paper proposes a robust decision-level framework based on paraconsistent annotated logic for faulted phase selection in long transmission lines. The proposed approach fuses multiple fault indicators, including voltage magnitude variations, phase angle relationships, and symmetrical component ratios, while explicitly handling inconsistent and uncertain evidence. Extensive simulation studies were conducted considering different line lengths. The proposed method correctly identified the faulted phases, demonstrating superior performance compared to a conventional selection scheme for lines longer than 320 km under weak-infeed conditions, as well as in high-resistance fault scenarios. Misoperations of the conventional algorithm occurred in 189 out of 9156 fault cases. A real fault case is also analyzed to illustrate the practical applicability of the proposed algorithm. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zuo X.; Lin L.; Zhan Q.; Ji J.; Wu W.; Li Z.
Title: Strength-plasticity synergic and low-thermal-resistance sapphire/Cu joints via ultrafast laser micro-welding with intermediate Cu2O nanolayer
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-quality interfacial bonding between sapphire and Cu is crucial for effective thermal management in power electronic modules. In this work, ultrafast laser micro-welded sapphire/Cu heterostructures with synergetic strength-plasticity and low thermal resistance have been achieved by introducing an intermediate Cu2O nanolayer. The spatially confined ultrafast laser-ablated plasma is strategically regulated by this nanolayer, which activates the inert sapphire surface and tailors a multi-mechanism interfacial micro-nano architecture. The resulting joint features an interlayer composed of amorphous Al2O3, CuAlO2, and embedded Cu nanocrystals, effectively mitigating residual stress and material incompatibility. Concurrently, Al2O3 nano-anchors extending from the base material provide abundant binding sites, facilitating robust mechanical interlocking between sapphire and Cu. The shear strength of the joint with the Cu2O nanolayer reaches 121.1 ± 3.3 MPa, representing an 11.1% improvement over joints welded without the oxide layer. A remarkable 270.1% increase in shear displacement is also achieved, accompanied by ductile fracture on the Cu side, indicating superior room-temperature plasticity. The welded heterojunction shows robustness against thermal cycling with strength deterioration below 21.6% after 500 cycles from −40 to 120 °C. Additionally, the interface exhibits good resistance to dye penetration and excellent interfacial thermal conductance, with a remarkably low thermal resistance of 1.89 ± 0.24 K mm2 W−1 at room temperature. This work demonstrates the feasibility of integrating metal-oxide heterostructures with superior mechanical and thermal properties via ultrafast laser micro-welding, showing great potential for application in advanced thermal management substrates. © 2026

Title: Lightning impulse discharge characteristics and insulation coordination failure mechanisms of insulator strings and surge arresters on distribution lines under wet pollution conditions
Abstract: Based on-site investigations of 35 kV transmission lines in Kumishi Town, 1080 artificial lightning pollution flashover tests were conducted on commonly used insulator strings and surge arresters. By evaluating the insulation coordination margin and observing the entire arc development process were analyzed in depth through statistical analysis of the flashover probability of the insulation sections. The results show that under low contamination conditions, when the discharge path remains the grading ring air gap, the lightning pollution flashover voltage of the surge arrester remains nearly unchanged but increases approximately linearly with the gap distance. The lightning pollution flashover voltage of the insulation sections of insulator strings and surge arresters decreases following a negative power exponential relationship as the ESDD increases. The arc development velocity of the insulation sections of insulator strings and surge arresters is positively correlated with ESDD. The arc development velocity of the gap section can reach 52.5 mm/μs, while that of the insulation section of surge arresters is only 31.9 mm/μs, representing a decrease of 39.23%, which hinders the fast operation of surge arresters. The flashover probability of the insulation section shows a positive correlation with both gap distance and ESDD, and a negative correlation with lightning amplitude. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Controller hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) testing of a hybrid control architecture for multi-feeder microgrids with heterogeneous generation
Abstract: This paper designs and validates a control architecture for multi-feeder heterogeneous microgrids that supports seamless transitions across various topologically distinct modes. The validation process is carried out in a controller hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) testbed that integrates a real-time high-fidelity emulation of the microgrid power generation assets, the network, and the loads, and commercially available industrial-grade control hardware to implement the suite of controls. As the test system, we adopt the Banshee system, which is a radial three-feeder microgrid comprising heterogeneous resources including two synchronous generators (SGs), a grid following (GFL) inverter and a droop-based grid forming (GFM) inverter. The control architecture is hybrid in the sense that it implements both logic controls and continuous controls. The continuous controls ensure stability is maintained and include tie-line power controls, synchronization controls, secondary frequency control, and secondary voltage control, while the logic controls facilitate topology (mode) changes by opening and closing circuit breakers. Specifically, the logic controls enable: feeder islanding and re-connection, networking of multiple microgrids, and backfeeding power to islanded feeders through other grid-connected feeders for the 38 modes of the Banshee system. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: He H.; Li Y.
Title: Anisotropic orthogonal random feature-based ridge regression for data-scarce short-term load forecasting
Abstract: Accurate day-ahead short-term load forecasting is essential for the operation of microgrids, yet many practical scenarios involve limited historical data, short input sequences, and strict computational constraints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an anisotropic orthogonal random feature-based ridge regression (AORF-RR) framework with a transfer-learning strategy. By embedding group-wise anisotropic scaling into finite-dimensional orthogonal random Fourier features, the proposed anisotropic orthogonal random feature (AORF) mapping preserves the small-sample generalization capability of kernel learning while substantially reducing the computational cost of model training. The resulting primal-space ridge-regression model improves expressiveness for heterogeneous feature groups without introducing scenario-dependent kernel weights or the high computational burden associated with exact kernel learning. The developed transfer-learning scheme further enables effective adaptation from data-rich source domains to data-scarce target domains within a shared AORF feature space. Numerical studies on benchmark datasets show that AORF-RR consistently outperforms representative neural-network-based baselines and achieves competitive or superior accuracy relative to kernel-based baselines, particularly under short-input and data-scarce settings. Paired statistical significance analysis confirms that the observed error reductions are stable across testing tasks. Large-scale forecasting experiments further demonstrate substantially reduced training cost, supporting scalable and cost-effective deployment in modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: An advanced deep learning framework for scalable smart grid intrusion detection
Abstract: The smart grid is a critical component of modern energy distribution system; however, it faces several cybersecurity challenges, including firmware exploitation, data leakage, unauthorized access, and data manipulation. To overcome these challenges, a deep learning-based intrusion detection system (IDS) for the IEEE-39 and 118 bus smart grid framework is proposed in this research. First, communication traffic is collected, interpreted, and processed to obtain meaningful features for intrusion detection. The proposed model combines three novel techniques: transductive few-shot learning enhanced by spectral-spatial embedding for sequential pattern recognition and temporal heterogeneous graph contrastive learning for static relationship learning. Furthermore, a graph convolution network with a self-attention mechanism is optimized by the spotted deer optimization algorithm for efficient learning. This hybrid approach is effective for both temporal and spatial dependencies in network data. The experimental findings represent the suggested IDS detecting the attack with high accuracy of 98.6% and a lower false alarm rate. The proposed methodology is validated via MATLAB simulations on IEEE-39 and 118 bus systems and is superior to existing methods in the smart grid environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Xue X.; Xu L.; Chen X.; Wang Y.; Kong L.; Wu R.; Koo B.W.; Wang Y.; Kim H.S.
Title: DSCR-mediated recrystallization pathway control enabling strength-ductility-conductivity balance in a heterostructured Cu-Sn alloy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Balancing strength, ductility, and electrical conductivity remains challenging in Cu alloys because conventional strengthening approaches often increase electron scattering and compromise ductility. Here, a Cu-0.1Sn alloy was subjected to dynamic offsets and shear force adjustment cryorolling (DSCR) followed by annealing to regulate recrystallization and heterostructure formation. Compared with the symmetrically rolled and annealed sample, the DSCR-annealed (DSCRA) sample exhibits an earlier recrystallization onset and faster apparent recrystallization kinetics. This behavior is reflected in its lower softening temperature (594 versus 610 K) and apparent activation energy for recrystallization (113.1 versus 126.4 kJ/mol). After annealing at 598 K, DSCRA develops a partially recrystallized heterostructure comprising recrystallized soft domains and retained hard lamellar domains, some of which contain locally preserved deformation nanotwins. DSCRA also exhibits weaker rolling-texture inheritance and greater orientation dispersion, consistent with a recrystallization pathway involving competition among multiple orientations. DSCRA achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 401 MPa and a uniform elongation of 11.1% while maintaining an electrical conductivity of 87.6% IACS. The favorable property balance is associated with plastic accommodation by the soft domains and strength retention by the hard lamellar domains. Locally retained deformation nanotwins provide additional strengthening, while interactions between the soft and hard domains promote strain partitioning and hetero-deformation-induced hardening. Recovery and partial recrystallization concurrently help reduce defect-induced electron scattering. These findings indicate that regulating the initial deformation state and subsequent recrystallization pathway offers a route to tailoring the strength-ductility-conductivity balance of dilute Cu-Sn alloys. © 2026

Title: Capillary-suspension-structured cellulose/fish oil oleogel-based bigels: Ratio-driven phase organization and swallowing performance
Abstract: Dysphagia-friendly foods require tunable texture, structural stability, and controlled oral deformation. In this study, cellulose/fish oil oleogels were constructed through capillary suspension structuring, and further combined with fish gelatin hydrogels to produce bigels with adjustable swallowing properties. Oleogel formation was jointly regulated by cellulose and water contents. The oleogel containing 25 wt% cellulose and 5 wt% water formed a stable bridged network with improved oil-holding capacity, reaching 73.32 ± 0.45%, and its structural recovery increased from 11.85% to 66.00% with increasing cellulose content. The oleogel/hydrogel ratio markedly affected bigel phase organization, rheology, texture, stability, and IDDSI performance. Increasing oleogel fraction induced a structure transition from hydrogel-continuous phase structure to semi-bicontinuous transitional structure and finally to an oleogel-rich structure. BG50 exhibited favorable structural and mechanical performance, with compact network, enhanced gel strength, and stable deformation resistance. IDDSI tests showed that bigels containing 10∼50% oleogel corresponded to Level 6, whereas those containing 70∼90% oleogel shifted to Level 5. Additionally, bigels with an oleogel content below 50% exhibited higher centrifugal stability, supporting their potential for processing, storage, and transport. Overall, this study provides new insights and methods for the design of dysphagia-friendly foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Artificial intelligence for stability assessment and early-warning in converter-dominated power systems: A unified review and risk-envelope framework
Abstract: Converter-dominated power systems with high penetration of inverter-based resources exhibit fast, nonlinear, and multi-timescale dynamics that introduce new stability modes and operational risks beyond the scope of traditional assessment techniques. In recent years, artificial intelligence and machine learning methods have been widely applied to small-signal, transient, voltage, and frequency stability prediction using simulation data and wide-area measurements. Although many studies report high predictive accuracy, the literature remains fragmented across stability categories, data regimes, and model classes, and typically emphasizes point prediction rather than uncertainty, regime transitions, and control-oriented early-warning. This review presents a systematic and literature-rich synthesis of AI-driven stability assessment approaches for converter-dominated power systems, covering learning architectures, feature representations, graph-based methods, and real-time monitoring integration. Key gaps are identified in uncertainty-aware prediction, cross-timescale stability coupling, interpretability for control action, and operational risk quantification. To address these limitations, a novel AI-Based Stability Risk Envelope Framework is proposed, linking predictive models with uncertainty bounds, operating-region tracking, and decision-triggered early-warning mechanisms for dynamics-informed grid operation. © 2026 The Author(s)
