Authors: Sagadevan M.; Selvaraj J.
Title: A Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion Hypergraph Framework for Real-Time Power Quality Assessment in Grid-Connected and Islanded Microgrid Clusters
Abstract: The growing importance of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) has dramatically transformed the modern power system, leading to the development of microgrids with dynamic, complex operating conditions. Nevertheless, the intermittent nature of renewable production and presence of nonlinear loads lead to severe Power Quality (PQ) disturbances, including voltage sags, swells, harmonics, and discontinuities. Proper detection, prediction, and interpretation of these disturbances remain a major challenge, especially in real-time grid-connected and islanded microgrid systems. To address these issues, the present research introduces a new Neuro-Symbolic Hypergraph (NSDH) model for real-time PQ evaluation. The proposed model combines hypergraph-based spatial modeling to learn higher-order relationships among sensor nodes, a neuro-symbolic reasoning layer to increase interpretability and adherence to domain-specific rules. Also, the Brownian Black Kite Optimizer (BBKO) is used to optimize parameters and enhance convergence efficiently. Benchmark datasets are used to evaluate the model, such as SEED and IEEE 1159 PQ disturbance datasets. Experimental findings indicate the model proposed in the article has a higher performance of 98.6% accuracy, 97.9% Positive Predictive Value (PPV), 98.1% recall, and 98.0% F1-score than the current Deep Learning (DL) and graph-based frameworks. Moreover, the model has a high level of robustness, scalability, and a low level of computational latency; hence, it is applicable in real-time applications. In general, the suggested NSDH models are able to offer a highly efficient, scalable, and interpretable approach to advanced PQ monitoring of contemporary microgrid systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Maiti S.; Ganguly B.
Title: An adaptive multi synchrosqueezing transform driven deep network for partial discharge defects discrimination
Abstract: Accurate localisation and categorisation of partial discharge (PD) defects are very important to analyse insulation degradation in high-voltage equipment. However, due to the transient discharge characteristic of PD signals, feature representation quality and classification accuracy often degrade. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an advanced time-frequency representation (TFR) in combination with a deep learning (DL) framework for PD defects classification. This article presents an adaptive multi-synchrosqueezing transform (AMSST) driven customized ConvNeXt framework for automatic PD defect discrimination. Proposed AMSST applies Rényi entropy guided iterative TF representation for PD signals. These TFRs are subsequently fed to a customised ConvNeXt architecture, which incorporates adaptive multi-kernel depth-wise convolution for feature extraction and classification. Experimental verification was executed using three independent PD datasets, consisting of 2 laboratory-acquired datasets and an openly available IEEE data port benchmark dataset. A comparative study against conventional TF plots and other conventional classifier models has also been done. This highlights the capability of the proposed framework in improving PD feature extraction and classification performance. Cross-dataset assessment further demonstrated flexibility across independently acquired PD datasets. The results demonstrate that the implementation of adaptive TF enhancement and lightweight multiscale feature learning delivers an effective framework for intelligent PD diagnosis while maintaining moderate computational complexity. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed framework, gaining 100% accuracy during classification on the laboratory-acquired dataset, and portraying strong generalisation capability on the IEEE benchmark dataset. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Pramudi G.; Ismail N.I.
Title: Mechanical Properties of Sandwich Composite with Polyurethane Core Reinforced by Biaxial Geogrid and Carbon-Glass Fiber/Polyester as Skin
Abstract: The development of sandwich panels as structural materials is increasingly driven by the diversification of constituent materials. In this study, carbon-glass/polyester fibers were selected for the outer skins due to their high strength-to-density ratio, while polyurethane foam was used as the core for its lightweight characteristics despite its relatively low mechanical strength. To enhance the core’s performance, two-way geogrid reinforcement was incorporated. The primary objective of this research is to investigate the effect of geogrid reinforcement and the influence of core thickness on the mechanical properties of the resulting sandwich composite, with particular emphasis on identifying the optimal geogrid configuration and core thickness that yield the highest structural performance. The novelty of this research is the addition of a geogrid used as a sandwich composite reinforcement. Variations in the number of geogrid layers and core thickness were examined. The composite sandwich panels undergo flexural and compressive tests. The results indicated that the composite with a core thickness of 50 mm and five layers of geogrid reinforcement exhibited the highest performance, achieving a flexural strength of 47.59 MPa and a shear stress of 1856.68 MPa. In contrast, one layer of geogrid achieved a flexural strength of 45.46 MPa and a shear stress of 1768.60 MPa. Similar results were observed in the composite compression tests, where the composite with five geogrid layers achieved a compressive strength of 0.18 MPa, significantly higher than the 0.12 MPa achieved with a single layer of geogrid. The decreasing distance between geogrid layers increases the core density, thus enhancing resistance to compressive loads. This material can be used as a structural material to withstand vibrations such as earthquakes. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Kobayashi T.; Nakasato R.
Title: Analyticity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations with the zero sound speed in scaling critical spaces
Abstract: We consider the initial-value problem in the d -dimensional Euclidean space Rd ( d ≥ 3) for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations under the zero sound speed case (namely, P′(ρ*)=0, where P=P(ρ) stands for the pressure). The system is well-known as the Diffuse Interface model describing the motion of a vaper-liquid mixture in a compressible viscous fluid. Title: Two-pattern cascading failure modeling with high renewable energy penetration considering the cascading protection characteristics
Abstract: Cascading events such as the Spain “4.28” blackout were mostly triggered by protection misoperation and aggravated by the successive off-grid of renewable energy. The existing CF models still need improvement in depicting the CF dynamics with high renewable energy penetration. This paper proposes a two-pattern CF dynamic modeling method for power systems with high renewable energy penetration. Integrating the influence of random variation in external environmental factors and hidden faults in relay protection, the two-pattern representation models for renewable energy voltage/frequency protection and line overload protection are established. Considering the multi-time sequence response characteristics of cascading protection, a multi-time sequence dynamic model for CF with high renewable energy penetration is established. The risk analysis indices are further designed for CF risk evaluation. The simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus system and IEEE 300-bus power system show that the CFs with high renewable energy penetration exhibit multi-time-scale cascading characteristics. Title: OptiRT-DETR: A lightweight transformer-based framework for real-time insulator defect detection in power transmission systems
Abstract: Insulator defect detection is a critical task in ensuring the safety and stability of power transmission systems. The model integrates a ConvNeXtV2 backbone for efficient feature extraction, an enhanced adaptive sparse Transformer encoder for global context modeling, a multi-scale feature fusion network for robust representation, and a quality-aware dynamic sample assignment loss to improve optimization stability. These components are jointly designed to balance detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Title: Prioritizing resilience criteria and indicators in urban disadvantaged areas using the Best-Worst Method (BWM)
Abstract: Urban disadvantaged areas are highly vulnerable to natural hazards due to physical, social, economic, and institutional deficiencies. These areas-such as historic residential area, decayed residential areas, informal settlements, and social housing-experience distinct challenges that necessitate tailored resilience strategies. Existing resilience literature often adopts a generalized, city-wide perspective, lacking the granularity for effective local-level resource allocation in diverse disadvantaged areas. Physical-environmental aspects (building quality, infrastructure) dominate historical and decayed areas. Institutional dimensions (governance, accountability, policy support) are most influential in social housing resilience. Cross-area comparison reveals shared and context-specific determinants, underscoring the need for integrated, area-sensitive resilience planning. Title: Vulnerable node identification in active distribution networks under multi-scenario quasi-static time-series operation: A CVaR-based conditional-consequence screening framework
Abstract: Expected-loss and composite-score rankings can underrepresent active distribution network (ADN) nodes whose severe consequences concentrate in stressed operating states. CVaR, tail amplification, and resampling-based selection probability distinguish mean-driven from tail-dominated consequence profiles. A current-domain diagnostic using a literature-based 255-A surrogate and ± 20% sensitivity further separates baseline-relative branch-loading stress from absolute current utilization: observed exceedances occur on solved main-grid branches, whereas the terminal GFM-supported-island pattern is associated with departures from branch-specific daily baselines. Title: A parallel ensemble framework with multiscale convolution and validation-optimized weighting for wind power forecasting
Abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting remains difficult because wind-related variables are nonlinear, non-stationary, and strongly multi-scale. To address this problem, this paper proposes a parallel ensemble framework that combines multiscale feature extraction with validation-optimized output fusion. A refined Tetragonula carbonaria optimization algorithm (RTGCOA) is firstly developed for feature selection and parameter optimization. Using a random forest (RF) based importance analysis, four dominant meteorological variables are retained: 30 m, 50 m, 70 m and hub-height wind speed. Secondly, a multiscale feature fusion convolution module (MSFCM) is designed to capture temporal patterns at different resolutions from the historical power series. Then, an improved bidirectional long short-term memory network (IBiLSTM) with coupled input-forget gates, peephole connections, and gated residual links is run in parallel with an enhanced Patch-based time series transformer (EPatchTST) that incorporates adaptive patch division and a hybrid enhanced attention mechanism. Finally, an RTGCOA-based validation-optimized ensemble strategy is introduced to determine the optimal global weights of the two branches, thereby improving overall forecasting robustness. Experiments conducted on real-world wind farm datasets covering different seasonal and perturbation conditions demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms the comparison models in terms of forecasting accuracy and error stability, confirming the effectiveness of the coordinated multiscale representation, heterogeneous parallel prediction, and validation-optimized output fusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A novel edible, all-biomass Pickering emulsion coating based on Lys/Alg composite nanoparticles for curcumin delivery and active fruit preservation
Abstract: The integration of nano-encapsulation with edible coatings holds great potential for active fruit preservation. Title: Electronic and interfacial water regulation in Ti-modulated NiFe oxide for industrial current density bifunctional water splitting
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing efficient and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts is of great importance for large-scale green hydrogen production via anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolysis. Atomic-scale characterizations and spectroscopic analyses reveal that Ti incorporation induces local lattice distortion, regulates the electronic states of Ni/Fe sites, and enriches defect-related oxygen species on the surface. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further demonstrate that Ti promotes a more ordered interfacial water arrangement and a stronger hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transfer as well as OH− adsorption and migration. Authors: Pansari D.; Yadav A.
Title: Deep Bi-LSTM-based intelligent detection of loss-of-excitation faults in STATCOM-integrated power system
Abstract: Loss of excitation (LOE) and partial loss of excitation (PLOE) are critical faults in synchronous generators that can compromise system stability and lead to severe equipment damage if not identified promptly. Conventional impedance-based protection techniques often experience degraded performance under dynamic conditions and in the presence of power electronic compensation. This work proposes a data-driven framework for excitation fault diagnosis using multivariate time series analysis of generator signals. A synchronous generator model integrated with a Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) is used to generate simulation data for six operating conditions, including normal operation, full LOE and partial LOE under both compensated and uncompensated scenarios. A set of electromechanical and electrical variables, including electromagnetic torque (Te), active power (Pe), reactive power (Qe), q-axis voltage (Vq), stator current (Is), rotor speed deviation (Δω), rotor speed (Wm), voltage deviation (Dv), torque-speed interaction (Te*Δω), field voltage (Vf), field current (If) and q-axis current (Iq) is extracted within a fault-centered time window. To enhance fault discriminability, first-order temporal derivatives and RMS-based envelope features are incorporated, resulting in a 26-dimensional feature representation for each sequence. Two sequence learning models are evaluated: a baseline recurrent neural network (RNN) and a deep bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network. The results demonstrate that while the baseline RNN achieved a classification accuracy of 91.0%, the Deep Bi-LSTM significantly improved performance, attaining an accuracy of 99.58%, F1-score of 99.6%, and an MCC of 0.995. These results confirm the effectiveness of deep bidirectional temporal learning for accurate and reliable LOE and PLOE detection. The proposed approach demonstrates strong potential for development of reliable, data-driven protection schemes for synchronous generators in modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Research on multi-objective optimization strategy of three-level dual active bridge converter based on model predictive control
Abstract: To address the problems of hard turn-on of power switches, poor dynamic performance and large backflow power in the three-level dual active bridge (3L-DAB) DC-DC converter, a multi-objective optimization strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed in this paper. Second, the power regions are divided by combining the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) turn-on conditions and the backflow power optimization criteria. The optimal phase-shift angles are solved according to the operating characteristics of different regions, and a comprehensive optimization control strategy that takes into account ZVS turn-on, backflow power suppression and dynamic performance improvement is formulated. Title: Dielectric properties of synthetic ester-based nanofluid under various electrode configuration, cellulose contamination, and circulation velocity

Title: Deterministic branch-and-bound global MPPT using surrogate-derived power bounds for partially shaded PV arrays
Abstract: Partial shading fragments the power–voltage characteristic of series-connected photovoltaic (PV) arrays into multiple local peaks, rendering conventional trackers ineffective and exposing the reliance of metaheuristic global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) methods on random initialization and empirical tuning coefficients. An offline polynomial calibration recovers the remaining parameters from short-circuit current. During discovery, an optimistic branch-and-bound rule maintains an upper power bound for each unconfirmed layer and permanently discards candidates that cannot exceed the incumbent confirmed power, contracting the admissible search space without exhaustive probing. A five-state finite-state machine governs initialization, shading-topology detection, discovery, winner refitting, convergence, and adaptive reinitialization. Experimental validation using a Chroma 62150H solar array simulator and a dSPACE DS1104 platform on five-module benchmark cases and additional eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases demonstrates average tracking efficiencies of 99.94% under partial shading and 99.98% under uniform irradiance, with corresponding average convergence times of 0.25 s and 0.21 s, respectively, for the five-module test set. Title: An ensemble mean Q-networks algorithm with prioritized sampling for automatic generation control of multi-area power systems
Abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy has intensified stochastic disturbances in power grids. This poses significant challenges to Automatic Generation Control (AGC), which is responsible for maintaining frequency stability and scheduled tie-line power exchange in multi-area power systems. Under highly stochastic operating conditions, conventional PID-based controllers have limited adaptability. Existing RL-based AGC strategies may also suffer from high value-estimation variance and overestimation, which can impair learning stability and control performance. The proposed framework introduces two main design enhancements: first, multiple Q-networks are integrated through ensemble learning to reduce estimation variance and alleviate overestimation; second, a network-specific prioritized sampling scheme is designed to weaken the correlation among ensemble members and further improve learning stability and sample efficiency. Title: Fibrillation-induced compositional remodeling of egg white protein: Differential glycerol regulation of cryogel networks and thermomechanical performance

Title: Fabrication of bioactive hydrogels stabilized by gluten amyloid fibrils and ε-polylysine: Effects of fibril morphology and blending ratios

Authors: Pal R.S.; Roy M.
Title: Experimental realization and nonlinear modelling of ferroresonance in a transformer–capacitor circuit
Abstract: Ferroresonance is a nonlinear phenomenon capable of producing sustained overvoltages in power systems due to the interaction between system capacitance and the nonlinear magnetizing characteristics of transformers. This paper presents the development of a controlled laboratory platform for the experimental realization and analysis of ferroresonance in a transformer–capacitor circuit. The required series capacitance was determined using Rudenberg's graphical method, and protective arrangements are incorporated to ensure safe operation during high-voltage conditions. Experimental results confirm the successful initiation of ferroresonance and reveal a distinct jump phenomenon at a particular voltage. Bistable behavior is observed near the transition region, where ferroresonant and non-ferroresonant responses coexist under identical supply conditions. It is further found that the time required to reach steady-state ferroresonance decreases with increasing supply voltage. To support the experimental findings, the transformer's nonlinear magnetization characteristic is derived from open-circuit test data and used to formulate the governing nonlinear differential equations of the system. A numerical simulation predicts the ferroresonance transition at a voltage, in close agreement with the experimental observation. The minor deviation is attributed to practical non-idealities that the model does not fully capture. The strong correlation validates the proposed nonlinear framework and provides deeper insight into ferroresonance dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Machining Behavior of Al-MMC Reinforced with Hybrid Additives: Effects of Cutting Parameters – A Taguchi Approach
Abstract: Aluminum-based composites reinforced with Mg₂Si particles are valued for their engineering properties. This study examines how cutting parameters and Ag, Bi, and Sr additives affect tool wear and surface roughness during both dry and wet turning of Al–Mg₂Si composites. Using a Taguchi design, we varied spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and lubrication to determine their relative impacts on tool wear area and surface roughness. Composites were fabricated through casting and examined using SEM–EDS techniques to assess microstructural characteristics and wear morphology. Feed rate emerged as the most critical factor, while wet machining with a biodegradable fluid markedly improved both tool life and finish. Among the materials tested, the composite containing all three additives delivered the lowest wear and finest surface. Specifically, the 14.47% improvement in dispersion uniformity was observed when all additives were used, while tool wear was reduced by 24.04%, and surface roughness improved by 18.94% under optimized machining conditions (spindle speed of 1000 rpm, feed rate of 0.12 mm/rev, and depth of cut of 1 mm). Regression modeling supported the experimental findings and demonstrated strong predictive accuracy. Confirmation trials under optimized conditions verified these trends. These results highlight the role of additive elements not only in modifying microstructure but also in enhancing machinability. The findings provide clear guidance on selecting additive combinations and machining settings to maximize productivity, extend tool life, and achieve superior surface integrity in Al–Mg₂Si composite turning. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Active-site decoupling and reactor-scale thermal coupling for simultaneous NOx and CO removal over Pd/V–Mo/TiO2
Abstract: Simultaneous NOx and CO removal from oxygen-rich industrial flue gases is constrained by NH3 nonselective oxidation and deactivation under SO2-containing conditions. Here, a hierarchically organized Pd/V–Mo/TiO2 catalyst was developed by introducing trace PdOx species and high-density Brønsted acid onto industrially relevant V2O5/TiO2 catalysts, and the same loading strategy was subsequently transferred to a V-based honeycomb catalyst. The optimized 0.3 Pd/2V9MoTi powder catalyst achieved CO and NO conversions and N2 selectivity above 90% at 240–300 °C. Dynamic atmosphere-switching experiments and apparent reaction-order analysis showed that CO oxidation and NH3-SCR were functionally separated and exhibited limited kinetic cross-interference. XAFS and XPS indicated that highly dispersed oxidized Pd species, predominantly Pd2 +–O, serve as the major active sites for CO oxidation, whereas preserved V5+–O species were associated with low-temperature NH3-SCR. CO/NH3-TPD and in situ DRIFTS further suggested that a Mo-associated Brønsted acidic environment preferentially retained NH3 and restricted its access to Pd2+–O sites, thereby suppressing competitive adsorption and NH3 nonselective oxidation. A reduced-order CFD model incorporating experimentally derived kinetics predicted favorable operating ranges of 6000–9000 h−1 for GHSV and 0.6–0.7 for bed porosity. Under the simulated conditions, 5,000 ppm CO oxidation increased the catalyst-bed temperature by more than 40 K, and enhanced NOx conversion by over 30% at 30,000 h−1 relative to standalone NH3-SCR. After transfer to an extruded honeycomb catalyst, NO and CO conversions remained at approximately 83% and 75% at 40,000 h−1, respectively, during 100 h of operation at 230 °C in the presence of 10 vol% H2O and 100 ppm SO2. These results demonstrate the preliminary engineering feasibility of combining functional active-site separation with reactor-scale thermal coupling for integrated NOx and CO removal. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Defect-rich PtCo multilayer nanobowls for the efficient glycerol electrooxidation and coupled hydrogen evolution

Title: Vision-based monitoring of transmission line icing via generative augmentation and improved RF-DETR
Abstract: Severe transmission line icing threatens power grid safety by causing conductor breakage and tower collapse. We propose an integrated deep learning-based monitoring framework. Concurrently, an improved Roboflow Detection Transformer (RF-DETR) model, integrating Icing Feature Enhanced Attention (IFEA) and a Mixed-scale Feature Pyramid (Mix-FPN), is introduced to accurately detect slender lines and preserve topological continuity. Furthermore, an Inverse Perspective Mapping (IPM) algorithm is applied to correct geometric distortions. Experimental results over five repeated scene-level splits demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently and statistically significantly improves detection, segmentation, and thickness-estimation performance. The improved RF-DETR trained with the final augmentation strategy achieves 69.6 ± 0.8 % mAP50:95 and 85.5 ± 0.6 % Dice, significantly outperforming the RF-DETR baseline. Title: Power quality–driven electromagnetic risk amplification in co-located critical energy infrastructures
Abstract: The increasing integration of power electronic converters, renewable energy interfaces, and nonlinear industrial loads has significantly degraded power quality in modern transmission networks, leading to elevated total harmonic distortion (THD) and reduced power factor (PF). While the impact of these phenomena on energy efficiency is well documented, their influence on electromagnetic interference (EMI) and AC-induced corrosion of co-located buried pipelines remains insufficiently quantified. This study investigates the coupled effects of power quality degradation on electromagnetic induction and corrosion risk in shared transmission line–pipeline corridors. A multi-frequency extension of the classical Carson–Clem formulation is developed to incorporate harmonic-specific current spectra and frequency-dependent mutual impedance. The induced current density at pipeline coating defects is evaluated for THD levels ranging from 0% to 20% and for PF variations between 0.8 and 0.99. To account for electrochemical behavior, a frequency-dependent corrosion efficiency model is integrated, enabling computation of an effective corrosion-driving current density. Results demonstrate that power quality degradation amplifies corrosion risk through two concurrent mechanisms: (i) reduction of THD leading to increased RMS current and enhanced electromagnetic coupling, and (ii) harmonic redistribution of spectral components that modifies corrosion efficiency at the steel–soil interface. Low-order harmonics are found to dominate corrosion risk, and conventional fundamental-frequency assessments may significantly underestimate the spatial extent of corrosion-critical zones under harmonic-rich conditions. The proposed framework establishes a direct link between power quality metrics and infrastructure integrity, providing a quantitative basis for incorporating harmonic considerations into pipeline interference assessment and critical energy infrastructure protection strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Energy trading and demand response strategies for energy flexible manufacturing systems under temporary electricity shortages: A noise-robust multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
Abstract: This paper investigates the energy management of energy flexible manufacturing systems (EFMS) under temporary electricity shortages (TES). TES disrupt the real-time balance of energy supply and demand. Meanwhile, multi-source measurement noise can degrade dynamic state estimation and affect scheduling decisions. To address these challenges, a hybrid approach integrating a generalized loss cubature Kalman filter (GLCKF) and a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is proposed. First, a dynamic pricing model based on the real-time demand-supply ratio, retail price, and feed-in tariff is designed to keep local trading prices within the grid price bounds. Second, GLCKF is used to suppress the effects of non-Gaussian measurement noise and random outliers. The resulting state estimates are used by MADDPG to jointly optimize real-time energy trading and demand response (DR) strategies. The framework is evaluated using a simulated four-EFMS cluster over a one-day scheduling horizon. The case incorporates industrial load profiles, photovoltaic generation, energy storage parameters, and time-of-use electricity prices. Comparative results show a 53.76% reduction in state-estimation root mean square error relative to CKF-MADDPG under the selected mixed-Gaussian noise setting. The results indicate that the framework improves economic performance and supports supply-demand balance in the tested TES scenarios. © 2026

Authors: Raouf I.; Kim H.S.; Wang P.
Title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
Abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. The framework uses a condition-normalized residual adaptation mechanism in the latent space. First, a structured representation is learned from the source robot. The learned representation is then adapted to the target robot using only normal samples. Compactness-based constraints and statistical modeling of normal behavior are used to detect unknown faults as deviations from the normal representation. The framework is evaluated on two industrial robots under variations in load, speed, and motion. Two evaluation strategies are also considered: sequential normal-only adaptation to welding motion and direct open-set detection without further adaptation. The results show consistent fault detection across different robots and operating conditions. A comparative benchmarking analysis further demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its ability to maintain reliable fault detection performance under different loading and motion conditions. This demonstrates the potential of the framework for practical industrial health monitoring. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/

Title: Research on rapid diagnosis of transmission tower abnormal state under subsidence condition based on 3D laser point cloud scanning
Abstract: Traditional methods for inspecting the status of power transmission towers are inefficient and labor-intensive, while existing remote sensing techniques primarily assess overall geometric tilt, lacking the ability to diagnose localized structural anomalies. This paper proposed a rapid diagnosis technique based on 3D laser point cloud scanning and finite element method for abnormal state of transmission tower under ground settlement condition. The stress and displacement distribution of the tower under different foundation settlement conditions have been analyzed. With the first diaphragm plane of the tower as the reference plane, the multi-phase point cloud registration based on Super4PCS and ICP algorithm are proposed. The displacements of key nodes have been extracted to realize the rapid diagnosis of the abnormal state of the transmission tower. Application results show that displacement-to-height ratios of all key nodes exceed 16.69‰, and the tower is in a state of structural anomaly, which is consistent with detailed field investigation and quantitatively validated against independent total station measurements. Authors: Chen Y.; Wu M.; Lu J.; Liu Z.; Yang X.; Peng Y.; Hu L.
Title: Surrogate-Assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning for Bi-Level Multi-Objective Capacity Sizing of Railway Collaborative Power Supply System
Abstract: The Grid-Source-Storage-Vehicle collaborative power supply system (GSSV-CPSS) enables railway power supply to evolve from a grid-only supply to coordinated multi-source supply with flexible regulation, thereby improving renewable energy (RE) utilization and source-load matching under high renewable penetration. However, short-term source-load fluctuations, long-horizon temporal variability, and strong planning-operation coupling make capacity sizing computationally expensive, because candidate schemes must be repeatedly evaluated through fine-resolution, long-horizon chronological dispatch. To address this issue, a planning-operation coordinated capacity sizing framework is developed. The planning-layer targets annual economic performance and RE utilization, and formulates capacity sizing of photovoltaic (PV), energy storage systems (ESS), and power converters as a single-step continuous decision problem. The operation-layer evaluates candidate schemes through year-long chronological rolling-horizon optimization and feeds the annual return back to the planning-layer. Building on this framework, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) is adopted as the policy-optimization backbone to realize unified policy optimization across different objective-weight preferences. Furthermore, a surrogate-assisted (SA) mechanism is introduced, in which a learned reward surrogate predicts the expected return and uncertainty of candidate capacity schemes. The predictive mean and uncertainty are then used for candidate-scheme scoring and screening, so as to reduce unpromising real operation-layer evaluations. The resulting method is termed SA-SAC-Select. Case studies show that the proposed method makes more effective use of costly annual operation-layer evaluations and supports efficient capacity sizing across different objective-weight preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Photovoltaic generation forecasting for newly-built sites based on transfer learning with global adversarial and local contrast learning
Abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) generation forecasting is vital for efficient renewable energy integration and operation. However, the newly-built PV sites are constrained by insufficient training data. First, ST-Net is constructed for both source and target domains to comprehensively model the spatial-temporal characteristics of PV generation. Then, the global adversarial network is designed to learn domain-invariant feature representations through discriminator, and to effectively alleviate the issue of domain shift. Moreover, the local contrast learning is devised to effectively capture local key features by optimizing sample similarity relationships, and compensate for potential local information loss caused by global alignment. Title: Effect of additive diffusion on radial differences in thermal aging characteristics of XLPE in high-voltage AC cables
Abstract: Thermal aging of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) in high-voltage cables threatens its operational reliability, and the increase in insulation thickness leads to radial non-uniform degradation. In this regard, this paper investigates the effect of additive diffusion on radial performance degradation during thermal aging at 135 °C. The results show that both types of cables exhibit obvious radial non-uniform degradation. The outer layer, with a high initial cross-linking density and good insulation performance, is preferentially affected by thermal-oxidative aging, undergoing post-crosslinking followed by thermal scission. The middle and inner layers have slightly lower initial performance than the outer layer, and their degradation phenomenon lags behind that of the outer layer during thermal exposure. The diffusion of antioxidants and DCP, as well as its correlation with XLPE performance degradation, was revealed through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and microstructural characterization. It is found that the migration ability of antioxidant in XLPE is restricted as the cross-linking degree increases, and they tend to combine with oxygen. Antioxidants in the middle layer diffuse outward, compensating for the rapid oxidation effect in the outer layer. The diffusion behavior of DCP is weakly dependent on the cross-linking degree, and it induces post-crosslinking reactions. The non-uniform diffusion of additive molecules leads to a time lag in post-crosslinking and thermal scission reactions among different layers, thereby causing a multi-level effective threshold decrease and nonlinear changes in breakdown strength. The above findings provide a basis for revealing the radial degradation mechanism of XLPE in coaxial-structure cables under thermal-oxidative aging. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Intertwined escort dynamics: A dynamical framework for constrained optimization

Title: Translating alcohol dehydrogenation into H2O2 photosynthesis through proton-coupled electron transfer
Abstract: Photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis coupled with selective alcohol oxidation offers a promising route for solar-driven chemical manufacturing, yet the disconnected transfer of protons and electrons between alcohol dehydrogenation and O2 reduction remains a fundamental bottleneck that limits H2O2 selectivity and redox efficiency. To address this challenge, here we describe a Ce-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET)-bridged photocatalysis strategy by incorporating buried Ce into zinc indium sulfide (ZIS) to form ZIS-Ce, where the local Ce-S coordination environment functions as a cooperative PCET bridge connecting benzyl alcohol dehydrogenation with O2 hydroperoxidation. Rather than accelerating isolated half-reactions, the buried Ce site couples a reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ 4 f electron mediator with a polarized Ce-S proton relay, thereby translating benzyl alcohol dehydrogenation into selective O2 hydroperoxidation through synchronized H+/e- delivery. Title: Optimal scheduling of droop-controlled islanded microgrid with mixed DERs considering voltage/frequency-dependent load models using fuzzy-grey wolf optimization
Abstract: In an islanded microgrid (IMG), dispatchable distributed energy resources (DERs) are typically operated in droop control mode to satisfy real and reactive power demand, which results in permissible deviations in frequency and voltage from their nominal values. The actual power consumption of loads varies with voltage and frequency; however, the voltage- and/or frequency-dependent nature of loads have been neglected in most existing studies. The uncertainties associated with PV and WT generation are modeled using probabilistic techniques, and a novel coordinated BESS charging-discharging strategy is implemented to compensate for PV power fluctuations. The proposed fuzzified grey wolf optimization (Fuzzy-GWO) technique is employed to solve the multi-objective problem, and its performance is benchmarked against Fuzzy-PSO and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) methods. Title: Multi-objective placement of EV charging stations integrating distribution network constraints and traffic demand using hybrid TLBO–PSO
Abstract: The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) has accelerated the need for strategically planned charging infrastructure capable of supporting both transportation demand and distribution network operation. Inappropriate placement of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) may increase network power losses, degrade voltage performance, and influence distribution system reliability. This study presents an integrated multi-objective planning framework for optimal EVCS placement that simultaneously considers electrical network performance, reliability assessment, and transportation demand characteristics. The optimization model incorporates real power loss, voltage deviation index (VDI), system average interruption duration index (SAIDI), system average interruption frequency index (SAIFI), customer average interruption duration index (CAIDI), EV traffic flow, and accessibility within a unified objective formulation. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO), and a hybrid TLBO–PSO optimization strategy are employed to solve the proposed planning problem, while Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Simulated Annealing (SA) are additionally included as conventional benchmark methods. The proposed framework is evaluated on the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution system using MATLAB, with algorithmic performance assessed through 30 independent simulation runs to examine convergence behaviour and solution consistency. The results demonstrate that the integrated planning framework effectively balances electrical and transportation-related objectives while achieving consistent optimization performance. The compared optimization methods produce similar network operating characteristics, while the hybrid TLBO–PSO approach exhibits a low mean power loss and the smallest standard deviation across repeated runs, indicating consistent solution behaviour. Furthermore, the optimized EVCS deployment enhances distribution system reliability while maintaining satisfactory voltage performance under the considered operating conditions. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive decision-support methodology for coordinated EV charging infrastructure planning and offers a flexible foundation for future extensions involving uncertainty modelling, large-scale distribution networks, and advanced transportation network representations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Ultrasonically modified coconut protein hydrogel-sunflower seed oil oleogel bigels: Effects of hydrogel/oleogel ratios on physicochemical properties and freeze-thaw stability
Abstract: Bigels, integrating protein hydrogels and oleogels, have emerged as promising solid fat substitutes due to their tunable texture and nutritional profiles. However, their practical application in frozen foods is critically limited by structural degradation caused by ice crystallization and repeated freeze-thaw cycles. The central scientific question of this study is how the hydrogel-to-oleogel ratio modulates the interpenetrating network architecture and freeze-thaw resilience. To address this, we fabricated bigels using ultrasonically modified coconut protein isolate hydrogel (HG) and beeswax-structured sunflower seed oil oleogel (OG) at varying ratios, and benchmarked their performance against neat HG and neat OG. The optimal formulation H1O3 exhibited a 77.73% increase in hardness compared with either single component, alongside a superior water-holding capacity of 98.13% and enhanced rheological moduli. Crucially, after three freeze-thaw cycles, H1O3 retained approximately 50% of its initial hardness, whereas neat HG and neat OG suffered severe textural collapse. Microstructural (CLSM) and spectroscopic (XRD, FTIR) analyses confirmed that the H1O3 ratio fosters a densely entangled bicontinuous interpenetrating network without new chemical bonds, while differential scanning calorimetry revealed a melting peak at 30.37°C and an onset temperature of 63.72°C. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the synergistic interplay between ultrasonication-induced protein conformational flexibility and oleogel network density, governed by the Hydrogel and Oleogel ratio, dynamically redistributes water and oil phases to buffer freeze-thaw stress. Therefore, this study established a rational ratio-based design strategy for developing plant-based fat substitutes with strong structural integrity that can withstand freezing, which are expected to find applications in frozen desserts, plant-based meat products, and other frozen convenience foods that require stable texture during freeze-thaw cycles. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen S.; Yan X.; Zhang Y.; Yang G.; Liu S.; Fan Y.; Lyu W.; Chen L.
Title: Impulse transient characteristics of a long vertical grounding conductor under various triggered-lightning discharge processes
Abstract: Lightning grounding performance depends strongly on the temporal characteristics of the injected current, yet field evidence comparing different lightning discharge processes remains limited. This study examines the impulse transient behavior of a 24-m-long vertical grounding electrode during artificially triggered lightning, with particular focus on initial continuous current pulses and return strokes. Synchronously measured lightning current and ground potential rise from two triggered-lightning events were analyzed, including five initial continuous current pulses and ten return strokes. Impulse grounding resistance was evaluated from the corresponding peak voltage and current values and compared with the measured power-frequency grounding resistance. Results show that, during the initial continuous current pulses, the mean impulse grounding resistance represented an average reduction of 29.45% from the power-frequency value. In contrast, the return strokes produced an average increase of 26.76% relative to the power-frequency one. Although impulse grounding resistance generally decreased with increasing peak current for both discharge processes, the two groups remained clearly separated. The contrasting behavior is attributed to competition between the inductive response of the long electrode under steep current fronts and the resistance-reducing effect of soil ionization during slower, broader pulses. Findings here demonstrate that transient grounding performance should account for the complete lightning-current waveform. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Development of hydrocolloid-structured choline chloride–lactic acid eutectogels enriched with Terminalia catappa extract through intermolecular hydrogen bonding for active fruit coating and postharvest quality preservation
Abstract: Eutectogels have gained attention as soft structured materials due to their ability to form stable, biocompatible, and viscoelastic networks suitable for edible and active coating systems. In this study, hydrocolloid-based eutectogels were developed using choline chloride–lactic acid (ChCl: LA) as the eutectic solvent system and xanthan gum as the structuring agent at concentrations of 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and 1.25% (w/w). Rheological analysis showed that all eutectogels exhibited non-Newtonian flow behavior with weak gel-like characteristics. Textural evaluation demonstrated desirable gel strength, adhesiveness, springiness, cohesiveness, and resilience. Increasing xanthan gum concentration progressively improved the rheological and textural attributes. Among the formulations, DESG-0.5 was selected as the most suitable coating matrix based on its visual appearance, flow behavior, and texture. To obtain a bioactive coating, Terminalia catappa extract was incorporated into DESG-0.5, forming DESGE. FTIR analysis indicated enhanced functional group expression, confirming extract integration within the eutectogel matrix. DESG-0.5 and DESGE showed transmittance of 63.24–87.30%, absorbance of 0.06–3.67 a.u., effective gas and water vapor barrier properties, and high weight-holding capacity of 98.22–99.03%. Authors: Gu Q.; Li Z.; Fan Y.; Tan Y.; Yan J.; Zhao C.; Liu J.
Title: High internal phase Pickering emulsions stabilized by plant protein and polysaccharide composite particles: Construction, stability, application, and research advance
Abstract: High internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs) stabilized by plant protein-polysaccharide composite particles represent a core innovation direction in the field of plant-based foods. Physicochemical structures of composite particles can be directionally regulated via molecular modification, covalent/non-covalent crosslinking, and physical modification methods including ultrasonication and high-pressure homogenization, thereby compensating the functional defects of single protein or polysaccharide. Formed by a dual-network composed of particulate interfacial film and continuous phase gel, HIPPEs possess prominent storage stability, antioxidant capacity, digestive stability and sustained release capacity of bioactive substances. Benefiting from solid-like rheological properties and high encapsulation loading capacity, HIPPEs can be applied to artificial plant-based fats, delivery carriers for functional factors and 3D-printable edible materials, facilitating the industrialization of healthy plant-based foods. There are still bottlenecks restricting the industrial application of this system at present: inherent off-flavors of raw materials impair product sensory quality, in vitro digestion models fail to reproduce real in vivo digestive behaviors, and large-scale production is limited by process scaling, batch variations of raw materials and high production costs. Subsequent research should be guided by green sustainability. Low-cost raw materials such as grain-oil processing by-products need to be developed, and the technical challenges of deodorization and decolorization should be addressed. Integrating soft matter physics, artificial intelligence and molecular simulation technologies can precisely match raw materials, preparation processes and emulsion performances. Relying on its edible and biodegradable structural merits, HIPPEs can break the limitations of food applications and expand to biomedicine and eco-friendly materials, broadening its industrial application scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Making large time series models work for urban load forecasting: A dual-stream large-lightweight hybrid framework with trend–fluctuation decomposition
Abstract: Accurate short-term urban aggregate load forecasting (SULF) supports power system operation. At 15-minute resolution, urban load combines lower-variation temporal structure with rapid fluctuations associated with weather, calendar effects, and recurring operating schedules. Large time-series models (LTMs) provide reusable long-context representations. However, their rigid architectures make it difficult to model the joint effects of exogenous covariates and load composition heterogeneity in SULF, limiting cross-regional deployment. We propose CRD-DLF, a dual-stream framework that combines an LTM with a lightweight multivariate MLP-Mixer through trend–fluctuation decomposition. The LTM forecasts the lower-variation stream, while the MLP-Mixer models the rapidly varying stream. Within the latter, the Industrial Load Separator (IndSep) extracts a schedule-dependent, covariate-insensitive forecasting component associated with recurring industrial operating patterns in aggregate observations. The remaining fluctuations are modeled using meteorological and calendar covariates. Adaptive fusion combines the branch forecasts, and the Patch Structural Loss encourages structural consistency during training. Tests on the Lishui citywide and county-level datasets show that CRD-DLF improves forecasting accuracy and stability relative to the plain LTM and other state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention networks for multi-regional load forecasting in modern power systems with missing data
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy and multi-regional power system operation creates new challenges for short-term load forecasting (STLF), particularly under missing data, dynamic spatial dependencies, and uncertainty. Existing approaches often separate data imputation from forecasting, rely on static spatial structures, and provide deterministic predictions, limiting their applicability in risk-aware power system operation. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Graph Attention Network (UA-DGAT) for multi-regional load forecasting under incomplete and uncertain data conditions. The proposed framework integrates probabilistic masked self-attention imputation, uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale temporal modeling based on discrete wavelet transform within an end-to-end architecture. Unlike conventional pipelines, UA-DGAT explicitly propagates imputation uncertainty, spatial dependency uncertainty, and predictive uncertainty throughout the forecasting process. Extensive experiments on NYISO and ISO-NE datasets demonstrate that UA-DGAT achieves superior performance in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting metrics, reducing MAE and RMSE while attaining approximately 87% prediction interval coverage. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each component and confirm the significant role of uncertainty-aware conditioning. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains robust forecasting performance under missing data rates up to 50%, with particularly improved resilience under block missing patterns. The results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware modeling of data reconstruction and spatial dependency learning enables more accurate, reliable, and risk-aware load forecasting for modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Stabilization of sesame paste via a capillary bridge-driven oleogel strategy
Abstract: Sesame paste is susceptible to phase separation during storage, which results in the formation of an upper oil layer and a lower solid sediment, which impairs product consistency and consumer acceptability. This study systematically investigated a simple strategy without additional chemical additives that leverages capillary bridge-mediated particle assembly to stabilize sesame paste. By controllably introducing water as the secondary fluid, a three-dimensional particulate network was formed, transforming the paste into a self-supporting oleogel. The stabilization effect was critically dependent on the secondary fluid saturation (S). At S = 35%, the system reached an optimal water-in-oil microstructure (funicular state), exhibiting maximum rheological moduli and texture parameters, and zero oil leakage during 90-day storage. Nevertheless, this enhanced physical stability was accompanied by accelerated oil oxidation at higher water content and a significant deterioration in sensory quality when S exceeds 10%. In contrast, at a lower saturation (S = 4%), the paste retained sensory attributes indistinguishable to the control while substantially enhancing physical stability, presenting a promising balance for practical application. Moreover, at S = 35%, the mechanical strength of the gel network was highly sensitive to environmental conditions: strongly acidic pH (2) reinforced the network, whereas increasing ionic strength weakened it. Collectively, this research established capillary bridges regulation as a scalable, clean-label approach to enhance the physical stability of sesame paste, offering fundamental insights into the structure-performance relationship of oil-continuous systems in food matrices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Cinnamaldehyde-lactic acid deep eutectic solvent modified chitosan composite film and its application in grape preservation
Abstract: To address the issues of non-degradability in traditional petroleum-based packaging materials and the limitations of chitosan (CS) films (e.g., poor mechanical properties, insufficient water resistance, and single functionality), this study incorporated a deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of cinnamaldehyde (CIN) and DL-lactic acid (LA) into the CS matrix to fabricate high-performance composite films. The effect of DES content on the structure and properties of the composite films was investigated. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that a fraction of the aldehyde groups of CIN participated in Schiff base formation with the amino groups of CS. Together with hydrogen-bond reorganization and LA induced protonation of CS amino groups, these interactions contributed to the regulation of the CS network. When the DES content was 60% of the dry weight of CS, the resulting CS(CIN:LA)60 film exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance: its tensile strength (TS) reached as high as 41.57 MPa; the water contact angle (WCA) was approximately 100°, indicating good hydrophobicity; the water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) was reduced to 560.2 g/(m2·24h); meanwhile, it possessed excellent ultraviolet (UV) shielding ability, remarkable anti-fogging performance, and good antibacterial activity. Grape preservation experiments demonstrated that the CS(CIN:LA)60 film could effectively inhibit microbial growth, reduce water loss, and delay fruit softening and the degradation of nutritional components. Compared with commercial polyethylene (PE) cling film, the composite film showed advantages in antibacterial activity, anti-fogging performance, and the maintenance of several grape quality attributes. This study provides a new strategy for the development of green food packaging materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A hybrid GRA-D-PRGO-BP model incorporating dynamic decay strategy to enhance ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting accuracy
Abstract: Photovoltaic power generation is characterized by significant intermittency and stochasticity, making accurate ultra-short-term PV power forecasting essential for ensuring secure and stable grid operation and improving renewable energy accommodation. However, in ultra-short-term forecasting scenarios, existing BP-based forecasting methods still suffer from input redundancy, parameter sensitivity, and insufficient optimization stability. To address these issues, this study proposes a hybrid GRA-D-PRGO-BP model for ultra-short-term PV power forecasting. First, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) is employed to evaluate the relevance of candidate input features with lag information, so as to identify key input variables and reduce feature redundancy. Second, a dynamic plant root growth optimizer (D-PRGO) is proposed. By introducing nonlinear dynamic decay weights into the dual-root growth mechanisms, the proposed algorithm enhances the coordination between global exploration and local exploitation. Finally, D-PRGO is used to optimize the initial weights and biases of the BP neural network, thereby improving forecasting accuracy and stability. Experimental results show that the proposed GRA-D-PRGO-BP model achieves an MAE of 9.9179 ± 0.5092 kW, an RMSE of 23.6070 ± 1.0767 kW, and an R² of 0.8924 ± 0.0099. It outperforms BP-based benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and run-to-run stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Adaptive cyber-resilient frequency regulation in isolated interconnected microgrids under false data injection attacks using empirical distribution-based statistical analysis
Abstract: Frequency regulation of isolated interconnected microgrids (InMGs) relies on continuous exchange of measurement signals among control areas via communication channels, making the system vulnerable to cyberattacks, particularly false data injection (FDI) attacks. This paper proposes a model-free cyber-resilient framework for detecting and mitigating FDI attacks in isolated InMGs. A nonlinear autoregressive with exogenous inputs (NARX) neural network-based estimator is trained exclusively on local measurements to reconstruct the nominal frequency deviation without reliance on an explicit system model. The estimation residual is then analyzed using a non-parametric statistical method based on the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF), from which an online probabilistic score is derived for attack detection and compromised-area localization. Upon detection, an artificial neural network-based adaptive mitigation controller dynamically reconstructs the injected attack signal from the residual and subtracts it from the compromised frequency measurement, thereby mitigating the attack impact without requiring manual retuning under varying attack conditions. The proposed framework is validated on a two-area InMG under constant, incremental, bounded, and unbounded time-varying FDI attack profiles, and its scalability is demonstrated on an eight-area network. Simulation results confirm reliable attack detection and localization across all scenarios, with frequency recovery achieved within approximately 3 s following mitigation activation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The diffusion characteristics and mechanism of O3 caused by corona discharge under the coupling of temperature and humidity conditions
Abstract: High-voltage switchgear is an indispensable core equipment in power distribution networks. Its interior is susceptible to corona discharge, which inevitably leads to substantial energy loss and degradation of equipment insulation performance. In this paper, experimental verification and simulation modeling methods were employed to investigate the generation, diffusion patterns of O3 caused by corona discharge within the high-voltage box under various temperature and humidity conditions, as well as the correlation characteristics between O3 production and the degree of discharge. By establishing an O3 diffusion simulation model, the evolution characteristics of O3 over time and space under the influence of different temperature and humidity were calculated and analyzed, and the influence mechanism of multiple factors on O3 diffusion was revealed. The results show that for the actual process of O3 generation, the concentration of O3 shows a saturation trend in the later stage of discharge. An increase of 20 °C in ambient temperature leads to an approximate 60% rise in O3 content, while a 20% rise in relative humidity results in an around 80% reduction in O3 content. With the increase of applied voltage, the concentration of O3 generated by discharge rises significantly. Under the same temperature and humidity conditions, the O3 concentration at an applied voltage of 15 kV is approximately three times that at 10 kV. During the process of ozone diffusion and decomposition. The concentration of O3 declines significantly as temperature rises and shows a decreasing trend with increasing humidity. The O3 concentration at 40 °C is 50% lower than that at 20 °C, and the concentration at 80%RH is about 20% lower than that at 40%RH. The research can provide theoretical and experimental references for the monitoring of corona discharge O3 and the status assessment of high-voltage switchgear cabinet type box-type equipment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Reduction-induced non-monotonic Cu redispersion on hydroxyapatite creates functionally differentiated interfaces for furfural hydrogenation
Abstract: Constructing non-noble-metal hydrogenation catalysts with high activity, chemoselectivity, and durability under mild conditions is a key challenge in biomass valorization. While strong metal–support interactions on hydroxyapatite (HAP) typically involve noble metals via oxidative pathways, we report a reduction-induced interfacial reconstruction for Cu-HAP. During temperature-programmed reduction, Cu shows non-monotonic evolution: aggregation then redispersion into an anchored state at 600 °C, bypassing sintering. Spectroscopic and DFT reveal that HAP retains long-range order, while the Cu–HAP boundary stabilizes Cu0/Cu+ and HPO42-, enabling cooperative H2 dissociation and carbonyl polarization. The optimized catalyst achieves quantitative furfural conversion with > 99% furfuryl alcohol selectivity (80 °C, 1.5 MPa H2). Kinetic benefits include decreased Ea (88.1→69.3 kJ/mol) and shifted H2 order (1.20→0.25). The catalyst also maintains stable performance over five cycles with negligible leaching. These findings highlight the distinctive role of HAP's Ca–PO4–OH environment in reduction-induced Cu redistribution and interfacial reconstruction, providing new insights into the design of cooperative metal–support interfaces for selective hydrogenation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Uniform CO2-enriched microenvironment enabled by sequentially functionalized hollow double-shell structure for maximal active site utilization in CO2 electroreduction
Abstract: Sequentially functionalized hollow multishell architectures typically boost catalysis via enhanced site exposure and reactant enrichment; however, their potential to modulate intrinsic activity through spatiotemporal ordering remains elusive and underexplored. Here, we demonstrate that the sequentially functionalized double-shell architecture homogenizes mass transport to establish a uniform microenvironment, which synchronizes the electronic structures of active sites for equivalent excitation and maximized collective utilization, thereby enhancing catalytic activity and selectivity. COMSOL simulations reveal that temporal-spatial ordering enhances both the magnitude and spatial uniformity of local CO2 concentration at the active sites. Title: Structural-function relationship of β-cyclodextrin derivatives in regulating encapsulation and humidity-triggered release of essential oils
Abstract: Understanding how cyclodextrin cavity microenvironment and key physicochemical properties of guest molecules govern the encapsulation and release behaviors of essential oils is critical for designing efficient delivery systems, yet the relevant mechanisms remain unclear. In this work, we systematically investigated this structure-function relationship using three β-cyclodextrin variants (native, methyl-β-cyclodextrin and hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin) and four representative essential oil molecules (cinnamaldehyde, carvacrol, eugenol and terpinyl acetate). We find that the relative contributions of guest hydrophobicity and molecular size to encapsulation efficiency are not intrinsic, but are dictated by the substituents on the cyclodextrin rim. Multiscale characterizations including XRD, FTIR and 1H NMR verified stable 1:1 inclusion complexes across all systems. Release kinetics exhibited a pronounced humidity-triggered pattern, governed by a balance between cyclodextrin hydrophilicity and crystallinity that linked water-mediated cavity hydration and diffusional resistance. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that hydrophobic interactions dominate host–guest binding, while substitution enhances cavity flexibility and alters guest embedding depth, thereby modulating the encapsulation and release of essential oils. Authors: Cheng H.; Gao Q.; Xu J.; Wan S.
Title: Optimization of train operation for electrified railway considering source-load matching
Abstract: To address the low local consumption and high operating costs caused by temporal mismatch between traction load and photovoltaic (PV) generation in electrified railways with distributed PV, this paper proposes a train operation optimization method considering source–load matching. The train operation process is simplified into a two-stage model (constant-speed traction and constant braking), and a multi-train power model incorporating regenerative braking energy balance is established based on average inter-station speeds. After analyzing the conflict between regenerative braking and source–load matching, a multi-objective optimization model is formulated with three objectives: source–load matching degree, total operation time, and system economy. Decision variables include departure time offsets, inter-station running time adjustment coefficients, and braking intensity adjustment coefficients. A differentiated braking intensity strategy is introduced to resolve the identified conflict. The NSGA-II algorithm is applied to obtain the Pareto-optimal timetable. Case studies using operational data show that the optimized timetable improves the local PV consumption rate by 20.5% over the baseline, and the variable braking intensity further reduces the traction system operating cost by 4.6% compared with the constant braking intensity under the same optimized timetable. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing PV utilization and the coordinated use of regenerative braking energy. © 2026

Title: An optimized single-machine equivalent model for doubly-fed wind farms based on controller aggregation
Abstract: Due to the influence of the voltage distribution (VD) and power distribution (PD) within the WF, the traditional single-machine equivalent model (SMEM) and feature-based clustering methods may introduce large errors in characterizing the whole WF. In this paper, based on detailed fault-stage division, the causes of control errors in each stage, and the mutual influence between PD and VD, the optimizations and principles for instruction aggregation are presented. An optimized single-machine aggregation model of the WF is developed through mathematical analysis and controllability considerations, and this model features mechanistic interpretability. The structure and parameter-acquisition principles of the single-machine aggregated equivalent model are presented. Based on the structured single wind turbine (WT) model and the aggregated control of the WF equivalent model presented herein, a structured WF equivalent model suitable for different WFs and different internal unit types of WFs is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the constructed model are confirmed across varying wind speeds, voltage dip depths, WFs and short-circuit ratios (SCRs). Title: Voltage stability in a high renewable distribution system via safety-guided deep reinforcement learning and MACPO
Abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources within distribution networks necessitates sophisticated coordinated Volt-VAR Control (VVC). Ablation studies demonstrate that the framework exhibits robustness toward parameter variations and different gradient estimation techniques. Although the offline training phase is computationally demanding, the online execution time is in the sub-millisecond range, thereby facilitating decentralized control applications. Title: Amorphous zirconia supported on nickel foam for efficient catalytic oxidation of ventilation air methane

Abstract: Ventilation air methane (VAM) is the largest source of coal mine methane emissions, and its efficient catalytic oxidation requires low-cost catalysts with high sulfur tolerance. The excellent catalytic performance stems from the unique structural characteristics of a-ZrO2, such as optimal mesoporous structure, high specific surface area, increased surface oxygen vacancies, and high oxygen mobility. Synchrotron-based spectroscopy further reveals strong interfacial electronic interaction between amorphous ZrO2 and NiO, facilitating lattice oxygen activation. DFT calculations further confirm that the disordered amorphous surface of a-ZrO2 provides significantly stronger methane adsorption sites compared to the crystalline phase, effectively polarizing C–H bonds for easier activation. Title: Research on multi-time scale optimal scheduling of virtual power plants based on improved HHO-CVaR

Title: Controllable product selectivity in electrochemical nitrate reduction over CuCo2S4 catalyst
Abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (eNO3RR) offers a promising route for nitrate removal and conversion into value-added nitrogen products such as nitrite, hydroxylamine, ammonia, and dinitrogen. However, controlling product selectivity remains a major challenge, as the reaction pathway is highly sensitive to catalyst surface properties and operating conditions. Here, we address this challenge by demonstrating that selectivity can be systematically tuned through electronic structure of catalyst, applied potential and electrolyte-controlled reaction environments. In particular, the thiospinel CuCo2S4 catalyst exhibits unique active sites that regulate the adsorption and reduction of nitrate-derived intermediates, enabling selective ammonia formation. Comparative studies on respective monometallic sulfides reveal that CuS favors nitrite production, whereas CoS and CuCo2S4 show enhanced ammonia selectivity, highlighting the critical role of catalyst structure in directing reaction pathways. Beyond catalytic structure, applied potential and nitrate concentration further modulate selectivity. On CuS, ammonia selectivity increases from 44% to 88% as the potential shifts from 0.0 to −0.5 V vs. RHE. More importantly, nitrate concentration governs surface intermediate coverage, driving a transition in product distribution from hydroxylamine (47%) at ultra-low concentrations to ammonia (96%) at moderate concentrations (>0.05 M), and to N2 formation (64%) at high concentrations, reflecting a shift between hydrogenation and N–N coupling pathways. Authors: Fang Y.; Gui L.; Li Z.; Chen J.; Huang K.
Title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
Abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Under fixed online time budgets, the MOA framework improves the mean HV by 31.13%–80.04% relative to five comparison methods and achieves the lowest mean inverted generational distance (IGD) on 14 of the 15 instances. Title: Regulating H2O dissociation on Ni-doped Cu nanowires to promote electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia

Title: Noise-resilient meta-learning on the Grassmann manifold for few-shot fault diagnosis of industrial robots
Abstract: Fault diagnosis for industrial robots is critically challenged by the limited labeled data and noise. Conventional meta-learning methods assume Euclidean data structures and lack adaptive mechanisms to cope with noise. Thus, they are highly vulnerable to noisy perturbations, resulting in suboptimal discriminative power and unstable prototype estimation. To address these challenges, we propose a noise-resilient meta-learning (NRML) framework on the Grassmann manifold. Specifically, a noise-aware damped distance (NADD) is developed to provide a robust similarity measure under varying noise levels. NADD employs a task-adaptive damping mechanism that dynamically balances the discriminative sensitivity and noise robustness, and it is formally proven to be a valid distance. Furthermore, an energy-thresholded subspace prototype (ETSP) is designed for adaptive and compact class representation on this manifold under extremely limited and noisy support samples. Comprehensive experiments on a public bearing dataset and a homemade industrial robot dataset demonstrate that NRML consistently outperforms multiple classical and state-of-the-art few-shot diagnosis methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed manifold-based adaptive framework offers a practical and effective solution for robust few-shot fault diagnosis of industrial robots. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Time series power load forecasting based on PCC-MIC hybrid feature selection and differential attention improved PatchTST

Title: Weakly-C1 solutions to the biharmonic problem on multi-patch domains

Abstract: Solving fourth-order problems typically requires C1-smooth splines. While straightforward on cuboidal patches, constructing these spaces on complex multi-patch geometries is challenging, often leading to complex and restrictive implementations, limitations on spline degrees, or reliance on constrained non-conforming approaches. Title: Coordinatively unsaturated Cu/Cu2O enables coupled hydrogen delivery and carbonyl activation for HMF electrohydrogenation
Abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of biomass platform molecule offers a promising route for sustainable chemical synthesis, yet its practical application suffers from suboptimal product productivity and insufficient catalytic efficiency under high substrate concentration conditions. Title: Finite-Element Assessment of Concrete Mine-Shaft Lining: Lamé Validation and Groove Effects
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This paper presents a Lamé-verified finite-element workflow for assessing the stress–strain state and residual load-bearing capacity of concrete linings in vertical mine shafts with local technological grooves. A full three-dimensional 1 m high lining ring with an internal diameter of 6 m was modeled in Abaqus and verified against the analytical Lamé solution for a thick-walled cylinder under external pressure. Four scenarios were analyzed: an elastic intact reference model, an elastic model with an inner technological recess, a zonal concrete damage-plasticity model (CDPM2) without groove, and a zonal CDPM2 model with groove. The groove caused pronounced stress redistribution, including a tensile hoop-stress concentration of approximately 24 MPa on the outer side of the lining opposite the groove and inner-contour ovalization with radial displacement from −9.0 to +7.4 mm.
