Title: Multi-objective optimization and decision-making for renewable energy production and enhancement of wind turbine selection in Morocco
Abstract: Selecting an appropriate wind turbine for a specific location requires the simultaneous evaluation of energy output, cost, and site-specific deployment constraints. This research introduces a comprehensive framework that integrates simulation, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), and hybrid deep learning to enhance the selection of turbines for various sites. One year of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis version 5 (ERA5) reanalysis data and geographical information from satellite and elevation datasets was used to model the energy output of 40 commercial turbines in 15 Moroccan cities. A weighted scoring procedure was developed to evaluate turbines based on their capacity factor, annual energy production (AEP), capital and operating expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), topographical constraints, and proximity to infrastructure. Two hybrid models, convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural network-Transformer (CNN–Transformer), were trained on structured inputs that included meteorological, topography, and spatial data to enhance decision assistance. The CNN–Transformer model outperformed the CNN–LSTM model in predictions and closely aligned with the expert rankings derived from simulations. Constraint-aware filtering and cost-performance trade-offs were employed to enhance the final turbine suggestions. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning for large-scale energy planning at specific locations. This framework supports future upgrades to renewable energy systems, including AI-based digital twins, real-time monitoring, and use across more locations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Spatially separated redox reactions over a floatable Fe–Co MOF/S-doped carbon nitride heterojunction for in situ H2O2 generation and ciprofloxacin oxidation
Abstract: Photocatalytic H2O2 generation coupled with contaminant oxidation offers a promising route for solar-driven water treatment. However, the efficiency is often hindered by charge recombination, competing redox pathways, and poor catalyst recovery. Here, we report a floatable cobalt-doped MIL-101(Fe)-NH2, (MNH(FeCo)) and sulfur-doped porous tubular carbon nitride (PTCN) heterojunction on expanded perlite (EP), MNH(FeCo)/PTCN@EP, enabling spatially separated redox reactions under visible light. Ciprofloxacin-assisted hole consumption further enhanced H2O2 yield. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in-situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveal that Fe-Co sites promote O2 activation and decreases energy barrier for formation of •OOH. The expanded perlite support provides buoyancy and enables facile catalyst recovery with stable long-term performance during repeated cycles. Title: Physics-enhanced dynamic graph network for wind power forecasting with directional delays and aerodynamic interference
Abstract: Multi-turbine wind power forecasting is challenging because of the complex, time-varying aerodynamic interactions among turbines. Existing graph-based methods introduce physical knowledge but treat these interactions as instantaneous, ignoring the finite time required for wind to propagate across a farm. To address this gap, we propose DPGNet, a physics-enhanced dynamic graph network that explicitly models directional propagation delays and wake-induced aerodynamic interactions. At each time step, the optimal inter-turbine delay is identified by maximizing the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC), and a dynamic directed graph is constructed whose edge weights learnably combine spatial distance, MIC-based dependence, and Gaussian-wake aerodynamic coupling; a delay-aware spatio-temporal network then learns turbine dependencies for multi-step forecasting. On real wind farm data over a 1–10 h horizon, DPGNet reduces the average Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by about 9% over the strongest physics-enhanced baseline, and under 30% missing data its MAE increases only from about 243 to 248 kW, confirming its robustness and generalizability. © 2026

Title: In-situ SEM/DIC analysis of crack propagation path selection in TiAl/Ti2AlNb laminated composites: Pre-notch positioning dictates the fracture toughness in three-point bending tests

Abstract: TiAl/Ti2AlNb laminated composites were fabricated by vacuum hot-pack rolling, forming three distinct interfacial regions: brittle regions I (βo + α2 + γ + ω) and II (βo/B2 + α2 + ω), and ductile region III (O). The intrinsic toughening is associated with slip deformation of B2 grains in the Ti2AlNb layer and grain-boundary obstruction to crack propagation, whereas the extrinsic toughening originates from interfacial crack branching in regions I and II, together with crack deflection and blunting in region III. Furthermore, the critical role of the pre-notch position was emphasized. When the notch terminates in the Ti2AlNb layer, interfacial crack branching effectively alleviates stress concentration, increasing KQ to 40.2 MPa m1/2. Conversely, when the notch terminates in the TiAl layer, rapid crack initiation caused by the low damage tolerance of TiAl triggers premature structural instability, reducing KQ to 29.5 MPa m1/2. These findings provide guidance for interfacial design and toughening optimization of TiAl-based laminated composites. © 2026

Title: Distance protection scheme for low frequency transmission system with offshore wind power: problems and solutions
Abstract: Apparent impedances of conventional distance relays cannot reflect the fault distance correctly in low frequency transmission system (LFTS) since the uncertain phase relationship between local and remote currents makes the voltage drop across fault resistance unpredictable. This paper reveals the mechanism by which a widely used phase selectors based on sequence voltage angles mis-operates in LFTS and indicates that negative-sequence current is the sufficient condition to ensure selectors reliable. Then a distance protection is proposed to eliminate the effect of fault resistance. By means of zero-sequence network, distance protection for single-line-to-ground and line-to-line-to-ground faults can be designed as a source-agnostic scheme. As for line-to-line faults, a uniform calculation expression for fault distance is derived to cope with various control operations. A control-based distance protection for a symmetrical fault is proposed to make the angle of local current be consistent with that of remote current. Simulation tests prove the effectiveness and precision of the proposed distance protection. The above solutions are also applicable to systems consisting of 100% converter-based sources. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Non-iterative coordinated robust scheduling method for virtual power plant-distribution network system based on feasible region projection
Abstract: To address the problems of low computational efficiency and high complexity of information exchange in the iterative solution methods for collaborative scheduling between virtual power plants (VPPs) and the distribution network (DN), this study proposes a non-iterative cooperative robust optimal scheduling strategy for VPP and the DN based on equivalent projection feasible region (EPFR). Title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
Abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Xin Y.; Brockmeyer J.; Ding Y.; Zhao M.; Shu G.; Shang Y.; Chen L.; Chen J.; Chen L.
Title: Ligand-based intelligent modification of β-lactoglobulin: multi-target virtual screening, interaction mechanism elucidation, and functional validation
Abstract: Phenolic acids offer a natural strategy for modulating the structural and functional properties of dairy proteins. Bovine β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) is a protein with structural plasticity, multiple ligand-binding cavities for bioactive molecules but is limited by its antigenicity and intrinsic antioxidant activity. Phenolic modification is a targeted means to modulate function of β-LG. Phenolic acids were selected based on docking performance, followed by residue-level prediction using a previously developed deep-learning model, and four target phenolic acids were ultimately identified: punicalagin (PG), 3,4-dicaffeoylquinic acid (DCQ), chicoric acid (CCA), and gallic acid (GA). Hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic associations are the dominant stabilizing forces identified from molecular docking results in binding to phenolic acids to β-LG residues. The model can estimate the interaction probabilities of novel uncharacterized binding sites on β-LG. This research focuses on evaluating how non-covalent β-LG-phenolic acid complexation can improve the protein's structural and functional properties. Multiscale multi-spectroscopic (UV-Vis, fluorescence, FTIR, CD) analysis clarified interactions and conformational changes. UV-Vis and fluorescence characterization confirmed the association of the β-LG-phenolic acid complex via elevated UV absorption peak intensity and obvious fluorescence quenching. FTIR and CD further revealed transformation of protein secondary structure after complexation. The antigenicity inhibition rates of β-LG-PG, β-LG-DCQ, β-LG-CCA, and β-LG-GA were 41.26%, 12.22%, 20.73%, and 42.36%, respectively. The complex's antioxidant potential was also enhanced before and after in vitro digestion. This study provides a strategy for screening phenolic acids and developing β-LG complexes with reduced antigenicity and enhanced antioxidant capacity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Luo G.; Tang Y.; Wang S.; Xu K.; Pu Y.
Title: Transient three-phase short-circuit current calculation based on the dynamic phasor model for grids with high-penetration inverter-based resources
Abstract: Due to the complex topological and control structures of inverter-based resources (IBRs), transient short-circuit current calculation of grids with IBRs currently relies mainly on electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation. However, EMT simulation usually requires detailed modeling and a small simulation step, which limits its application in rapid transient-current feature extraction. In this paper, a transient short-circuit current calculation method for three-phase faults in grids with high penetration of IBRs is proposed based on the dynamic phasor (DP) model. The IBR is represented as a stage-separated nonlinear time-varying current source, in which low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategy, current limitation, voltage outer-loop saturation, PLL dynamics, current-loop dynamic response, and staged LVRT activation are considered. DP models of IBRs and conventional grid components are then established and solved using the weighted trapezoidal method. The proposed method is intended to extract system-level transient current features, including the current envelope, peak value, peak time, and DC component, rather than switching-frequency electromagnetic transients. Validated by numerical examples, the proposed method achieves satisfactory accuracy compared with EMT simulation while significantly reducing the computation time. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu F.; Ren J.; Chen X.-L.; Lei Y.-T.; Cui H.-L.; Yang H.; Wang J.-J.
Title: Modulating excited-state dynamics in RhB@Cd-MOF composites: spectroscopic elucidation of PET-driven quenching and ACQ- suppressed radiative enhancement for differential fluorescence sensing
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Tuning host–guest interactions in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical pathways of encapsulated chromophores. Herein, a dual- emissive composite (RhB@ 1 ) was constructed by encapsulating rhodamine B (RhB) within a Cd-MOF ( 1 ). Under 350 nm excitation, RhB@ 1 exhibits two well-resolved emission bands at 433 nm (MOF host) and 585 nm (RhB guest) via efficient host-to-guest energy transfer, enabling a rare differential fluorescence behavior: a selective “turn-off” response to Fe3+ and a distinctive “turn-on” response to o-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA). Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy reveals that the fluorescence lifetime decreases from 2.22 ns to 1.68 ns upon Fe3+ addition, confirming dynamic quenching through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) pathway, while Stern-Volmer analysis further supports this mechanism. In stark contrast, the turn-on effect for o- NBA is attributed to the suppression of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) via supramolecular rigidification of RhB molecules, which restricts intramolecular rotation and enhances radiative decay. The composite also demonstrates outstanding photostability and recyclability, benefiting from efficient host-to-guest energy transfer. The practicality of the method was verified by visual detection of Fe3+ using test strips, Fe3+ recovery by standard addition in Yanhe River water, and o-NBA recovery by standard addition in tap water. Overall, this work not only provides a dual-responsive sensing platform but also offers direct spectroscopic evidence for how MOF nanoconfinement dictates the excited-state dynamics of guest dyes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhou R.; Cao X.; Shi X.; Li R.
Title: Grounding grid state identification method based on the strong coupling effect of the return line
Abstract: To address weak corrosion and fracture responses in grounding grids under variable soil conditions, this paper proposes a state identification method combining the strong coupling effect of the return line with multidimensional time-frequency feature fusion. The routed return path increases the contribution of defect-sensitive branches to the measured loop impedance, thereby enlarging defect-induced perturbations. Frequency-domain spectra are reconstructed into time-domain responses; the wavelet power ridge peak, effective pulse width, root-mean-square (RMS) bandwidth curve integral, low- and high-frequency power proportions, and differential local wavelet power map morphology are normalized to the complete grounding grid reference. Over 30–1000 Ω·m, the maximum complete grounding grid ridge and RMS ratios (1.0039 and 1.0030) remain below the minimum fracture ratios (1.0099 and 1.0164). The dataset uses midpoint thresholds of 1.0069 and 1.0097: fracture requires both thresholds plus temporal, spectral, or morphological corroboration, whereas conflicting evidence is reported as indeterminate. Corrosion produces smaller coordinated amplitude and spectral changes, minimal pulse-width change, and localized patterns dependent on severity and position. Simulations reveal two-level location sensitivity: outer frame defects generally produce larger deviations than internal branch defects, and electrically path-weighted locations respond more strongly within each topological category. The intact, corroded, and fractured states exhibit distinct resistivity-dependent map evolution: the complete grounding grid develops a distributed high resistivity negative-left/positive-right band; corrosion shows the opposite low resistivity polarity sequence and a localized high resistivity positive-left/negative-right band; fracture shows broader discontinuity-related patterns with a negative-dominated transition. Field tests reproduce the principal simulated fracture trends and support the method's engineering applicability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen Q.; Deng R.; Shu S.; Li J.; Zhou Q.; Li J.; Fan M.
Title: Water-assisted *CO protonation decouples C2+ formation from carbon loss in acidic CO2 electroreduction
Abstract: Electroreduction of CO2 to multicarbon (C2+) products in acidic electrolytes offers a carbon-efficient route for producing value-added fuels and chemicals. However, high C2+ selectivity in acidic media typically relies on concentrated alkali-metal cations, which stabilize *CO and promote C-C coupling but reinduce (bi)carbonate formation and salt precipitation. Reducing cation concentration alleviates (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss, but weakens cation-mediated interfacial regulation, causing adsorbed *CO to favor desorption over C-C coupling toward C2+ products. Here, we develop a water-assisted protonation layer (WAPL) on Cu to decouple C2+ formation from (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss under low-cation acidic conditions. WAPL regulates the Cu-water interface through interfacial charge redistribution induced by electron-accepting interactions, promoting water-assisted *CO protonation and *CO-*CHO coupling. In 0.5 M K+ acidic electrolyte, a total C2+ FE of 63.0% was achieved at 150 mA cm−2, while limiting CO2-to-(bi)carbonate conversion to 2.8%, a 5.5-fold decrease compared with concentrated-K+operation. In situ fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveal that WAPL restructures interfacial water and facilitates *CO protonation to *CHO, enabling asymmetric C-C coupling. This work provides an interfacial proton-transfer strategy for achieving high C2+ selectivity in acidic media while suppressing the (bi)carbonate-derived carbon loss associated with concentrated-cation operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Jiang E.; Cui Z.; Mi Y.; Zhang J.; Li R.; Wang C.
Title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning for load restoration of distribution networks under typhoon disasters
Abstract: Under typhoon disasters, distribution-network faults evolve over time and progressively alter the feasible topology and available supply regions, making load restoration a sequential problem that couples discrete network reconfiguration with continuous resource dispatch. This paper proposes a restoration-specific hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for automated load restoration during fault evolution. A dynamic environment incorporates the time-varying typhoon wind field, line-failure probability, fault latching, and load scaling. The high-level agent uses a deep Q-network (DQN) to select tie-line command templates, while the low-level Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent dispatches distributed generation (DG) and interruptible loads (ILs) within the resulting topology. An AC-power-flow-based safety layer screens bounded continuous actions, applies deterministic backtracking correction when necessary, and invokes a conservative fallback if correction fails; only reverified feasible states are executed. A critical-load-first allocation rule and a marginal-gain high-level reward are further incorporated and separately evaluated by ablation. Tests on the IEEE 33-bus system over 30 Monte Carlo typhoon scenarios show that the proposed method reduces weighted unserved power by 63.43% relative to fixed-topology dispatch. It achieves a 95.54% restoration rate and 98.64% critical-load restoration, close to the MISOCP benchmark (96.08% and 98.91%), while reducing mean online decision time from 0.548 s to 0.019 s. These results demonstrate a favorable restoration-quality-latency tradeoff for rolling load-restoration decisions under evolving typhoon faults. © 2026

Authors: Duan W.; Xie Y.; Ding K.; Tang Q.; Xu S.; Zhang Y.; Qiao X.; Jiang N.; Shan Y.; Ding S.
Title: Starvation trap strategy: An amylase-responsive potato starch-based Pickering emulsion for inhibiting foodborne microorganisms and preserving starchy foods
Abstract: Inspired by microbial carbon-source uptake, we developed polysaccharide-based intelligent responsive cinnamaldehyde (CIN) nanoemulsions (NEs) stabilized by the metal–phenolic network (MPN)-modified potato starch particles (PSEF). This system achieved amylase-responsive CIN release and inhibition of Bacillus cereus in starchy foods, while continuously releasing CIN to control other foodborne microorganisms. The results confirmed that the prepared 5% CIN NEs showed high encapsulation efficiency (98.66%), sustained release, and reliable biosafety (relative hemolysis rate <5%), effectively inhibiting Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Bacillus cereus, Burkholderia gladioli, and Aspergillus niger. Co-incubation with Bacillus cereus further supported the amylase-responsive release behavior of the system. Finally, the 5% CIN NE coating extended the shelf life of fresh-cut kiwifruit, lotus root, and rice noodles by 1.5–2.0-fold, showing better preservation performance than the commercial preservative ε-polylysine hydrochloride (ε-PLH). This safe and intelligent responsive coating may provide a sustainable solution for extending the shelf life of starchy foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A novel fast and secure detection algorithm for loss of excitation (LOE) protection in synchronous generators
Abstract: Loss of excitation (LOE) events have the potential to seriously harm the generator and the power system. The impedance trajectory seen by the generator terminal was mostly used in the first applicable LOE detection systems, which had many disadvantages such as slow performance and mal-operation during SPS. Thus, this work presents a new setting-free LOE detection method that is quick and secure. For this aim, three distinct novel indices are created by applying the derivative of various values, seen from the generator terminal, including: resistance (R), reactance (X), reactive power (Q), and flux (φ). In order to achieve the most suitable index, the operation of them have been evaluated through the simulation of multiple situations, taking into account all of the suggested indices. It is important to note that, MATLAB software has been employed for all the simulations that were conducted. According to the final results, the third suggested index, which is based on applying the derivative of R, Q, and φ, operates the best. When compared to conventional impedance-based and also other methods, the aforementioned index exhibits significantly greater speed and accuracy in detecting LOE and also reliable discrimination of LOE with stable power swing (SPS). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Arós Á.; Fernandes C.
Title: Numerical analysis of elastic elliptic membrane shells in frictional contact with wear
Abstract: We consider a family of linearly elastic and elliptic membrane shells, all sharing the same middle surface, with thickness 2ε, clamped along their entire lateral face, which upon deformation may enter in frictional contact with a moving foundation along its lower face. As a result of friction, material might be removed from the interface, thus causing wear. In this paper, we focus in the numerical analysis of our model and provide a priori error estimates for displacements, stress and wear fields. We have implemented the fully discrete scheme with the FreeFEM++ programming environment, by using an intrinsic (basis free) formulation, reduction of order, penalization and Newton method. We carried on a series of numerical simulations to demonstrate the capabilities of our code, providing experimental evidence of our theoretical results regarding the convergence with respect to the thickness parameter ε and mesh size h . As a practical application, we have also included the results of a simulation of the wear that undergoes the tyre of a vehicle braking on a road. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Influence of structure and non-Newtonian rheology on the lubrication of emulsion gels in soft contacts
Abstract: The microstructural complexity and rheology of emulsion gels significantly influences their lubrication behaviour in soft contact tribology, resulting in experimental observations that are difficult to interpret. To investigate this, model emulsion gels (acidified milk gels) were prepared with systematic variations in protein to fat ratio, total solid content, and fat particle size. The lubrication of these multiphasic gels with semi-solid rheology deviates notably from the typical Stribeck “master curve” by showing the existence of a secondary transition in mixed lubrication (ML) regime. This behaviour generally occurs for shear-thinning lubricants, and we show how this secondary transition in ML relates to the presence of a yield stress, which relates to the strength and integrity of gels’ microstructure and the fat content. This distinct tribological behaviour of emulsion gels diminishes as the system enters the elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) regime due to the enlarged interfacial separation so that the response depends on high-shear viscosity. For systems where there is a significant amount of free fat (i.e. the fat is not strongly associated with the protein network), local phase separation can occur whereby the fat phase dominates tribological response at low entrainment speeds (narrow gaps). By systematically decoupling the effects of composition, rheology, and microstructural integrity within a common emulsion-gel platform, this study establishes a mechanistic framework for interpreting the lubrication behaviour of complex multiphasic food gels. The findings demonstrate how structural evolution during oral processing influences tribological response in complex foods. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Pan A.
Title: Near-optimal loop opening with a rotary power flow controller: Global-optimality conditions, certified domains, and practical-band fragmentation
Abstract: Opening an RPFC-supported loop without a fresh voltage disturbance hinges on how the controller withdraws to zero injection. Field practice uses a two-step rule—suppress the injection magnitude, then reset the residual angle—yet no path-level theory explains when this rule is optimal or how it fails. This paper casts the exit stage as a continuous path problem on the control plane with voltage excursion as cost. An exact identity equates the two-step excess above the endpoint lower bound to the sum of two endpoint-envelope violations; when both vanish, the path is globally optimal. A counterexample rules out any unconditional theorem; implicit-function arguments then yield checkable pointwise and domain certificates. On the IEEE 69-bus feeder, a 625-point operating rectangle is certified with zero excess and a monitored, nonsingular load-flow Jacobian; certification persists out to ± 30% load, carries over to a meshed variant, a non-ideal excitation-branch model, and a 118-bus feeder, and survives 500 paired Monte Carlo draws on two topologies with heterogeneous load and photovoltaic uncertainty. On the reduced plane, 78.1% of feasible points are safely near-optimal at the 0.01 kV threshold, with the worst path-induced gap at 0.0063 kV. Execution stress contracts the practical band from 1.389 to 0.906 kV and fragments it into up to four islands; sensitivity sweeps expose a sharp bias-driven collapse between 0.75∘ and 1.25∘, whereas ± 20% load shifts barely matter. External reactive support of up to 1 Mvar widens the band edges yet heals none of the bypass-limited gaps, confirming where the remediation budget belongs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Golpayegani M.; Damchi Y.
Title: A one-end current-based method for single line to ground fault location in the stitched transmission lines
Abstract: Due to economic constraints and the limited availability of bays in high-voltage substations, some transmission and sub-transmission networks employ stitched lines—a special configuration of double-circuit lines connected to a single bay at both ends. Although these lines offer cost and space advantages, they present significant challenges for fault location because the currents of the two circuits cannot be measured separately. So far, no one-end fault location method has been proposed for fault location in stitched lines. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel impedance-based fault location method that utilizes negative- and zero-sequence networks and relies solely on current measurements from one end of the line to locate single-line-to-ground faults. The method's performance is evaluated for single-line-to-ground faults in different phases, locations, and fault resistances, while considering uncertainties in Thevenin and line impedances, as well as the effects of noise, variations in sampling frequency, fault inception angle, and fault clearing time. Simulation results demonstrate that the method achieves high accuracy, with an average error below 1% in most cases, confirming its effectiveness and reliability for fault location in stitched transmission lines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: De la Varga J.G.; Pineda S.; Stratigakos A.; Morales J.M.
Title: End-to-end pseudo-measurement learning for state estimation under limited observability
Abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is becoming increasingly important with the integration of Distributed Energy Resources and the active operation of distribution networks (DNs), but it remains challenging due to the limited and heterogeneous monitoring infrastructure available in these networks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel DSSE framework that restores observability through data-driven pseudo-measurements generated by a Neural Network (NN), while preserving the exact non-linear AC power flow model within a classical Weighted Least Squares (WLS) estimator. Unlike conventional approaches that generate pseudo-measurements independently of the downstream state estimation, the proposed method explicitly couples both components through an end-to-end learning formulation. Specifically, the WLS estimator is embedded as a layer within the NN architecture, enabling implicit differentiation to propagate the impact of pseudo-measurements on the final estimation error back to the NN parameters. Extensive numerical experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 33-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in state estimation (SE) accuracy under a wide range of loading conditions and measurement configurations. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Impact of gamma irradiation as a non-thermal technology on the structural, digestive, and rheological properties of rice bean (Vigna umbellata) protein isolate and its application in the development of 3D printable food ink
Abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effect of gamma modification on the functional properties of rice bean protein isolate (RBPI) at doses of 3, 5, and 10 kGy. Both native and gamma-irradiated RBPI were characterized through structural, molecular, functional, rheological, and digestive analyses to evaluate the influence of different irradiation doses and identify a suitable dose for 3D food ink formulation. Gamma irradiation induced dose-dependent structural modifications, as evidenced by FTIR and UV–visible spectroscopy, particle size analysis, SDS–PAGE, and SEM, suggesting irradiation-induced structural modifications, alteration in particle organization, and microstructural changes without evidence of extensive protein degradation under the studied conditions. These structural modifications significantly (p < 0.05) improved solubility and water-binding capacity, particularly at moderate irradiation doses (3-5 kGy), whereas the highest in vitro protein digestibility was observed at 10 kGy. Rheological evaluation revealed enhanced shear-thinning behaviour, elastic dominance (G′ > G″), and improved viscoelastic stability in gamma-irradiated RBPI, reflecting stronger protein–protein interaction networks. Based on its favourable functional and rheological characteristics relevant to 3D printing, the modified RBPI was further applied to develop a fruit-based 3D-printable ink formulated with agar and guar gum. The rheological behaviour of native and gamma-irradiated RBPI-based inks was characterized, revealing enhanced shear-thinning, elastic dominance, and viscoelastic stability, which are considered favourable for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Textural analysis further indicated higher mechanical strength, cohesiveness, and structural integrity of the gamma-irradiated RBPI food ink, suggesting its potential as a component of a composite formulation for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Representative self-supporting printed structures were obtained under the selected printing conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Atomic-scale interfacial welding unlocks the electrochemical potential of chemically robust proton-conducting electrolytes
Abstract: Solid-state electrochemical devices face a fundamental trade-off: chemical stability for durable operation often comes with surface inertness that passivates the electrode−electrolyte interface. This challenge is especially acute in proton-conducting ceramics like BaZr0.8Y0.2O3−δ (BZY), where chemical inertness suppresses interfacial kinetics, limiting conductivity to nearly two orders of magnitude below theoretical values. Here, we report an atomic-scale interfacial welding strategy that leverages the superior sintering activity of nanoparticles. Taking CuO as a model system, this welding agent drives bidirectional elemental interdiffusion between inert electrolyte and porous air electrode, transforming initially void-containing and discontinuous junctions into a continuous chemical continuum. Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry and aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy confirm overlapping elemental gradients and intimate interfacial contact across the reconstructed junction. By eliminating interfacial discontinuities, the welded interface achieves a 2.85-fold increase in adhesion strength while establishing more continuous charge/ion-transfer pathways. The resulting BZY cell delivers a 3.94-fold enhancement in peak power density over the pristine counterpart, together with an apparent conductivity of 0.015 S cm−1 at 700 °C. Authors: Hui L.; Runxin G.; Lingyun S.; Xiaomei Z.; Bing S.
Title: Influences of dissolved organic matter and halide ions on the photodegradation of amitriptyline: Kinetics and characterization of transformation products
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Amitriptyline (AMT), a widely used tricyclic antidepressant, is frequently detected in both freshwater and marine environments, where its photochemical fate may differ. In this study, the photodegradation of AMT was investigated in reservoir water and seawater, and dissolved organic matter (DOM) and halide ions were identified as the key factors controlling its photolysis. The photodegradation behavior of AMT was systematically examined in the presence of humic acid (HA) and halide ions. HA promoted AMT photodegradation, and higher HA concentrations led to more pronounced enhancement. In halide-containing systems, both ionic strength and specific halide effects jointly influenced AMT photodegradation. When HA coexisted with halide ions, the excited triplet state of HA (3DOM) and the resulting reactive halogen species (RHS) were identified as the key drivers promoting AMT photodegradation. In freshwater, AMT was photodegraded mainly through ROS-mediated oxidation and hydroxylation, whereas in saline water it reacted with RHS to form a halogenated intermediate that was further oxidized and hydroxylated into low-toxicity final products. Overall, AMT photodegraded faster under saline than under freshwater conditions, and the toxicity of its major transformation products decreased accordingly. These findings improve our understanding of the photochemical fate of AMT in freshwater and saline waters and provide valuable insights for the ecological risk assessment of AMT and structurally analogous pollutants in estuarine and coastal systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Comparative structuring of goat, yak, and camel casein isolates in moldable emulsions via calcium-mediated association, TGase crosslinking, and ultrasound-assisted emulsification
Abstract: Acid-isolated caseins from goat, yak, and camel milk were compared within a common processing framework to evaluate differences in the structuring of moldable oil-in-water emulsions among the three casein sources. Casein preparations were subjected to sequential calcium-mediated association and microbial transglutaminase (TGase) crosslinking, followed by ultrasound-assisted emulsification at an oil-to-aqueous-phase volume ratio of 2:1. Calcium source, Ca2+ concentration, TGase activity, redispersed casein concentration, sonication duration, and ultrasound set power were screened in independent one-factor series. Processing responses were generally nonlinear and differed markedly among the three casein sources. Within the tested formulation space, CaCl2 supplying 5 mmol/L Ca2+, 3% (w/v) redispersed treated casein, and an ultrasound set power of 2.0 kW provided the most consistent overall balance of oil incorporation, macroscopic homogeneity, physical stability, low apparent flowability, and moldability. The selected TGase activities were 4, 8, and 4 U/g casein for goat, yak, and camel caseins, respectively, with corresponding sonication durations of 15, 15, and 10 s. Maximum apparent viscosity did not consistently predict the selected formulation: low-shear viscosity reached approximately 240 Pa s for goat casein and approximately 300 Pa s for camel casein under intermediate treatment conditions, whereas higher treatment levels could markedly increase instability, with TSI values exceeding 20 in the camel system. Confocal microscopy further showed a comparatively fine and densely interspersed goat emulsion, large incompletely dispersed casein-rich aqueous domains in the shape-retaining yak emulsion, and a broader heterogeneous domain-size distribution in the camel emulsion. These findings demonstrate that macroscopic moldability can emerge through different multiscale structural pathways and does not necessarily imply microscopically uniform emulsification or elastic gel formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhong J.; Lu Q.; Zeng Y.; Peng S.; Wu Y.; Yan D.; Feng F.; Huang H.
Title: Quantitative decoding of Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O in nonradical peroxymonosulfate activation over waste PET-derived FeCo-N-C
Abstract: This study quantitatively decodes the individual contributions of Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O in nonradical peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation over a waste PET-derived FeCo dual-site catalyst (FeCo-N-C). The catalyst, featuring atomically dispersed FeN4-CoN3 heteronuclear pairs, was prepared via a facile one-step pyrolysis. It achieved 99.78% tetracycline (TC) removal within 30 min, significantly outperforming its single-metal counterparts. Quantitative ROS analysis revealed that nonradical oxidation dominated the degradation process (96.11%), in which Fe(IV)=O and Co(IV)=O contributed 20.92% and 71.05%, while radicals and singlet oxygen (1O2) accounted for only 3.89% and 4.14%. Quenching, EPR, steady-state concentration measurements, and PMSO probing verified the dominant high-valent metal-oxo (HVMO) pathway. DFT calculations revealed that Fe-Co electronic coupling lowers the O-O bond cleavage barrier, steering PMS toward selective HVMO formation. This work quantitatively deciphers the contributions of individual HVMO species in a Fe-Co dual-site catalyst system and provides new insights into the rational design of selective PMS activation catalysts for environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Degradable PLA/PBAT/ZnO@SiO2 composite film with micro/nanostructures for breathable, antibacterial, and thermally regulated medical protection
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Medical protective films are crucial for public health, yet traditional materials often compromise wearer comfort and pose significant environmental challenges due to their non-degradable nature. Herein, a biodegradable and multifunctional composite film is fabricated via micro-extrusion roll forming, composed of a polylactic acid (PLA)/poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) matrix featuring surface and interface micro/nanostructures. The surface micro/nanostructures and interconnected microporous interface endow the medical protective film with a water vapor transmission rate of 203.47 g m−2 h−1, ensuring excellent breathability and wearing comfort. The synergistic effect of uniformly dispersed ZnO@SiO2 nanoparticles and the surface micro/nanostructures achieves an antibacterial rate of 97.69% and effectively inhibits contaminant adhesion. Furthermore, the micro/nano structures and micropores are engineered to manipulate radiative properties, resulting in a passive cooling effect with a surface temperature approximately 10 °C lower than that of commercial fabrics. Crucially, addressing the critical issue of plastic pollution, the film exhibits excellent biodegradability through enzymatic, composting, and alkaline pathways, offering a sustainable solution that mitigates the secondary environmental pollution caused by conventional medical films. This work provides a feasible strategy for the scalable production of next-generation medical protective materials that seamlessly integrate wearable comfort, high performance, and environmental sustainability. © 2026

Authors: Wen X.; Tang J.; Gao X.
Title: Multiscale adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with cross-variable learning for short-term electricity price forecasting
Abstract: With the transition of electricity markets toward low-carbon and market-oriented structures, the electricity price time series exhibits strong non-stationarity, multi-scale fluctuations, and complex nonlinear dynamics, which pose significant challenges for Electricity Price Forecasting (EPF). However, existing models often fail to completely capture these complex patterns. To address the limitations of current methods, we propose a Multiscale Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with Cross-Variable Learning (MKAN-CL), which is combined with the Adaptive Lemming Algorithm (ALA) for automatic hyperparameter optimization. MKAN-CL integrates spectral decomposition with adaptive modeling to capture complex temporal dynamics in short-term electricity price series. Specifically, the method consists of four key components. First, a multi-lag cross-variable modeling mechanism is designed to capture cross-scale dependencies between electricity prices and exogenous variables. Then, hierarchical spectral decomposition is applied to separate non-stationary sequences into distinct frequency components. Subsequently, Chebyshev-based Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) are employed to perform adaptive nonlinear modeling across frequency bands. Moreover, the Adaptive Lemming Algorithm (ALA) is employed to automatically select key hyperparameters for the proposed model, reducing reliance on manual tuning. Finally, experiments on the Australian and Singapore electricity markets demonstrate the effectiveness of MKAN-CL. On the AEMO dataset, MKAN-CL reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 4.97%, 13.75%, and 12.95%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline, CrossLinear. Overall, MKAN-CL provides an effective solution for short-term electricity price forecasting in complex environments and offers data-driven support for price volatility assessment and operational decision-making in renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cheng X.; Hu T.; Xie Y.; Chen W.; Yuan Y.; Hu H.
Title: Soy protein isolate composite gels fabrication via short-term high-intensity ultrasound
Abstract: Dual-protein systems offer advantages for improving soy protein isolate (SPI) gelation. However, conventional gelation approaches still rely on complex procedures and prolonged heating, resulting in high energy consumption. Herein, short-time high-intensity ultrasound (HIU; 20 kHz, 400 W, 4-6 min) was used to directly fabricate SPI composite gel without additional heating, with ovalbumin (OVA), peanut protein isolate (PPI), and pea protein isolate (PAPI) serving as added proteins. The results indicated that SPI-OVA gel at a mass ratio of 2:4 exhibited the highest gel strength (183.02 g), the strongest viscoelasticity, and the greatest water immobilization (T22 = 54.789 ms), corresponding to a highly compact and dense network. Importantly, intermolecular force analysis revealed that OVA promoted the formation of a highly compact network dominated by hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds. The SPI-PPI composite gel network was mainly maintained by ionic bonds, while the dominant forces in the SPI-PAPI composite gel network shifted from ionic bonds to hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds as PAPI concentration increased. Furthermore, free sulfhydryl and surface hydrophobicity results indicated that HIU thermal effects facilitated protein unfolding and sulfhydryl exposure, while excessive hydrophobic aggregation in SPI-PPI and SPI-PAPI gels partially buried hydrophobic groups and weakened network formation. This study reveals mechanistic insights into HIU-induced fabrication of SPI composite gels and supports the rational design of high-performance dual-protein gel systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang L.; Li Y.; Li Y.; Tan Y.; Gao C.; Huang H.; Zhou X.; Wang J.; Zhang B.
Title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
Abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Bono R.; Saltão V.A.C.; Uglietti R.; Wen F.; Khaleghi Abasabadi R.; Berlier G.; Bordiga S.; Dreizler A.; Votsmeier M.
Title: A unified Cu-solvation and redox model for standard SCR on Cu-CHA: Explaining seagull-shaped light-off and driving-cycle performance
Abstract: NH3-assisted Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) over Cu-Chabazite (CHA) proceeds via redox cycling of NH3-solvated Cu(I)/Cu(II) ions, with the Cu solvation state governing the shift between low- and high-temperature mechanisms. Despite considerable progress, existing dual-cycle models do not fully reconcile NH3 solvation effects, in-situ spectroscopic data, and real-world catalyst behaviour. This work introduces a triple-cycle SCR model featuring three parallel redox cycles involving highly-solvated, partly-solvated, and bare Cu ions, whose relative distribution is determined by an experiment-derived NH3 solvation model. For the calibration of redox kinetics, we then propose a novel method which combines steady-state conversion and Cu oxidation-state quantification during SCR, aligned with industrial practice. The model accurately reproduces the characteristic “seagull” NO conversion profile under various experimental conditions. We report the experimental observation of a similar seagull profile also in the Cu oxidation state during SCR, as confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy. The model correctly reproduces this trend as well, confirming proper repartition between reduction and oxidation paths, as validated with half-cycle transient experiments. Finally, to the best of the author's knowledge, this work presents the first application of a redox-based SCR model to the simulation of driving cycles, marking a significant advance toward chemically-consistent reactor models for real-world after treatment applications. © 2026

Title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
Abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Hierarchical heterostructure-driven high-efficiency co-generation of electricity and ethylene
Abstract: Steam cracking of alkanes such as ethane accounts for over 90% of global ethylene production, but relies on energy-intensive, high-temperature pyrolysis, leading to significant carbon emissions and complex by-products that require costly purification. Enabling the co-generation of ethylene and electrical energy in oxide-ion-conducting solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), we design a highly selective anode for the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (EOD-eth). The anode consists of a hierarchical heterostructure featuring oxygen-vacancy-rich FeCu-FeOx anchored onto a Sr2Fe1.26Cu0.24Mo0.5O6-δ double-perovskite/Ruddlesden-Popper matrix (FeCu-FeOx@SFCu0.24M-DP/RP). The SOFCs demonstrate outstanding performance, maintaining CO2-free operation for over 400 h, while delivering a high-power density of 0.51 W cm−2 with an ethylene selectivity of 81.7% and an ethane conversion rate of 78.4% at 750 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that FeOx acts as both an effective oxygen-ion channel and an oxygen storage reservoir, activating ethane C–H bonds and promoting dehydrogenation, while FeCu enhances both ethylene selectivity and electronic conductivity. Beyond this specific reaction, the FeCu–FeOx–SFCu0.24M-DP/RP architecture embodies the essential attributes universally required of fuel electrode—including multivalent redox adaptability, robust structural resilience, and compatibility with diverse hydrocarbon or syngas fuels—thereby representing a broadly applicable catalytic platform for next-generation fuel-flexible SOFCs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Transformer partial discharge identification via supervised contrastive learning and Multi-scale perceptual networks
Abstract: Accurate partial discharge (PD) identification is essential for the operational integrity of traction transformers in electrified railways, yet intense electromagnetic interference and similar discharge patterns often diminish diagnostic robustness. This study proposes a framework integrating supervised contrastive learning with a Multi-scale Perceptual Network (MSDP-Net) to enhance diagnostic reliability. A dual-view adaptive augmentation strategy, involving Gaussian noise injection and temporal shuffling, is first applied to improve invariant representation learning. The physics-informed MSDP-Net utilizes a morphological branch with dilated convolutions for long-range envelopes and an instantaneous branch with singularity-aware operators for energy mutation detection. Supervised contrastive learning is then employed to optimize the latent feature space, strengthening intra-class compactness. Additionally, a new electromagnetic pulse amplitude sequence dataset is established and publicly released to address the scarcity of PD benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 98.42% identification accuracy across four typical defects, surpassing both general-purpose deep architectures and re-implemented PD-specific strategies. To exclude session-level information leakage, run-wise group-wise and leave-one-run-out cross-validation, in which all pulses of a given experimental run are confined to either the training or the test partition, are additionally conducted and retain 97.29% and 96.88% accuracy respectively. The framework exhibits exceptional robustness in high-noise environments, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art models and offering a more reliable solution for railway power supply monitoring. Finally, a complexity analysis shows that the framework requires only 0.0882 GFLOPs and 0.94 ms per-pulse inference latency, and that the contrastive projection head is discarded at inference and therefore adds no deployment cost. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fang J.; Shang Z.; Yuan X.; Xue A.
Title: An improved isolation forest based on kernel principal component analysis for anomaly detection in helicopter-based power-line inspection data
Abstract: For helicopter inspection data, including flight trajectories, task status, and equipment operating status, conventional anomaly detection methods still suffer from difficulties in separating high-dimensional nonlinear data, insufficient anomaly isolation capability, and low anomaly discrimination. To address these problems, this paper proposes an improved isolation forest anomaly detection method based on kernel principal component analysis (KPCA). The proposed method extracts five categories of features from inspection data, including standard deviation, coefficient of variation, centroid, resilience, and scale features, and constructs a fused feature matrix through sliding windows. KPCA is then used to perform nonlinear reconstruction and dimensionality reduction on the feature matrix to obtain a low-dimensional subspace. In this subspace, the single axis-aligned splitting strategy of the conventional isolation forest is improved into multi-directional splitting along principal-component directions and their combined directions. In addition, the path length is corrected according to the distance between each sample and the normal center. Experimental results based on 7027 real records from a helicopter inspection platform show that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in terms of Precision, Recall, F1-score, FAR, and PR-AUC. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify flight-trajectory deviations, equipment operation anomalies, and task-execution anomalies, providing a feasible data-driven technical approach for improving the intelligence and reliability of power-line inspection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Effect of Aspect Ratio on the Workability of AA6082/Metakaolin/Nano Silicon Nitride Composites: An Experimental Investigation and Predictive Modeling using RSM and ANN
Abstract: Understanding the impact of aspect ratio on the deformation and load-bearing capacity of aluminium matrix composites is crucial in tailoring their forming performance. In this study, aluminium alloy (AA) 6082/Metakaolin (MK)/nano silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) composites containing 7.5 wt.% MK and 1.5 wt.% Si₃N₄ were fabricated using ultrasonic cavitation-assisted stir casting and tested under quasi-static compression with cylindrical specimens of aspect ratios 0.5, 1, and 1.5 in both as-cast and T6 heat-treated conditions. The results showed that lower aspect ratios significantly enhanced workability. The as-cast composite at aspect ratio 0.5 sustained compressive deformation up to a 50% reduction in height without visible cracks, achieving a maximum axial stress of 573.25 MPa. The T6 heat-treated samples exhibited a maximum compressive strength of 543.31 MPa and fractured at lower strain due to embrittlement caused by eutectic Si and Mg₂Si phases. Microstructural analysis indicated pore closure as the governing deformation mechanism in as-cast specimens, while brittle fracture dominated the T6 samples. Instantaneous strain hardening exponent (nᵢ) and strength coefficient (kᵢ) trends confirmed contributions from both matrix and geometric work hardening during deformation. In order to predict the workability parameters for different aspect ratios and loadings, response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural network (ANN) were employed. ANN yielded superior prediction accuracy for the workability parameters compared to RSM. These findings confirm that aspect ratio strongly controls the deformation mechanisms, with shorter cylindrical specimens offering optimum workability for practical forming operations. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Experimental evaluation of ensemble learning models for partial discharges detection in transformer insulation mediums
Abstract: The reliability and stability of power systems largely depend on the integrity of power transformer insulation systems. Early detection of partial discharge (PD) activity plays a crucial role in preventing catastrophic failures, as PDs are localized dielectric breakdowns that indicate insulation degradation and may develop into severe faults if left undetected. Most conventional diagnostic techniques rely on single-sensor measurements, which may not fully capture the characteristics of PD events under varying operating conditions. This paper proposes a multi-signal ensemble learning framework for the accurate detection, identification, and classification of PDs in transformer insulation systems. Current, voltage, and acoustic PD signals were collected, filtered, and analyzed using time-domain feature extraction. The results show that RF achieved the highest classification accuracy of 96.51% using acoustic signals, outperforming GB, which achieved 95.87%. Compared with the best directly comparable previously published acoustic-sensor-based method, which reported an accuracy of 93%, the proposed RF approach achieved an improvement of 3.51 percentage points, equivalent to a relative improvement of 3.77%. Title: Fast and Accurate Time-Domain simulation of Lightning Response in Grounding systems Considering Frequency-Dependent Soil parameters and Ionization
Abstract: It has been demonstrated that most pole-residue sets proposed in the literature to represent the Alipio–Visacro (AV) model—which accounts for the frequency dependence of soil parameters using rational functions—result in high computational cost, making time-domain simulations inefficient for larger or more complex grounding systems. Title: Improving closing stability of high-voltage SF₆ circuit breakers via multi-physics modeling and genetic algorithm
Abstract: For 550 kV and above SF₆ circuit breakers, phase-selective closing requires high repeatability of the mechanical closing process to ensure the accuracy of the target closing phase. Prototype tests on a 550 kV SF₆ circuit breaker show that the simulated and measured motion characteristics agree well, with the maximum time deviation within 2 ms and the relative error below 5%. Title: Multiscale-engineered monolithic single-atom cobalt catalysts with micro-channels for self-driven water purification
Abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer high atom utilization and tunable active sites, making them promising for Fenton-like water purification. The system achieved nearly complete propranolol removal within 10 min, exhibiting a rate constant 14.3-fold higher than that of granular catalysts and exceeding most reported alumina-based monolithic catalysts in both active-site utilization and geometric efficiency. Title: Cross-month reliability-oriented capacity planning and grid integration validation of battery-hydrogen hybrid storage for a PV microgrid
Abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic microgrids face intraday power fluctuations and cross-month source-load mismatch. This paper proposes a cross-month reliability-oriented capacity planning and grid-integration validation method for battery-hydrogen hybrid storage. The planning stage uses the point of common coupling as the exchange boundary with the external distribution network and formulates a two-stage risk-averse mixed-integer linear programming model for 12 monthly representative days, 24 hourly time steps, and seven seasonal risk scenarios. The model considers mutually exclusive operating states, expected and scenario-level energy-not-served constraints, a low-hydrogen security margin, conditional value-at-risk, and a battery-degradation model segmented by depth of discharge. After capacity planning, the fixed capacity is validated through an 8760 h operational simulation and mapped to the IEEE 33-bus system for LinDistFlow post-checking, network-constrained correction, and sensitivity analysis across multiple connection schemes. The selected capacity achieves a probability-weighted expected energy not served of 0.646 MWh/a in the 8760 h validation. Additional robustness checks show that the selected capacity remains within the reliability limit under scenario-weight perturbations and tested cloudy-window stresses. The network correction results further show that energy adequacy at the point of common coupling and feeder-level voltage feasibility are interconnected but distinct assessment layers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Dual-seed induction of cross-linked reinforced corncob enables graphite-like subcrystalline carbon for high-performance sodium storage
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Graphite-like subcrystalline carbon (GLSC) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), featuring nearly parallel carbon sheets with expanded interlayer spacing and few defects, in contrast to the disordered structure of hard carbon. However, converting low-grade biomass like corncob into GLSC is hindered by the structural collapse of the precursor during pyrolysis. Herein, we overcome this limitation by engineering an epoxy resin-reinforced corncob powder composite, where hemicellulose-derived voids are in situ infiltrated and cross-linked by epoxy network during curing. Title: Coordinated current-limiting and transient stability control of grid-forming VSGs under grid-voltage sags
Abstract: When power systems experience large disturbances such as grid-voltage sags, virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) can suffer from power-angle instability and output overcurrent. To address this challenge, this paper analyzes the transient instability mechanism and current-limiting characteristics of VSGs and proposes a transient stability control strategy that coordinates steady-state current regulation and instantaneous-overcurrent suppression. The proposed strategy maintains power-angle stability by improving the active-power loop; reconstructs the reactive-power loop through output-current closed-loop integral control to achieve accurate steady-state fault-current limiting while preserving voltage-source characteristics; and uses adaptive virtual impedance to suppress instantaneous overcurrent at fault inception and clearance. Title: An Experimental Vision-Based Predictive Framework for Lane Detection and Vehicle Localization Under Low Visibility Conditions During Driving
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Reliable lane detection and vehicle localization are essential for advanced driver assistance systems, particularly under low-visibility conditions such as fog, shadows, low illumination, and degraded lane markings. Title: GridSage: A Skill-grounded LLM platform for scenario-oriented reinforcement learning evaluation in distribution networks
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) research in distribution networks continues to face challenges associated with complex scenario construction, high configuration overhead, and limited experimental reproducibility. Although existing RL platforms such as PowerGym and PowerGridworld provide standardized simulation and interaction interfaces, translating research intent into executable scenario configurations still relies heavily on manual effort. To address this issue, this paper proposes GridSage, an integrated platform that combines large language models (LLMs) with physics-aware power system simulation. GridSage adopts a Scenario Skill retrieval and incremental semantic editing framework, enabling users to construct customized scenarios through natural-language instructions. All generated scenarios are further subjected to safety validation to verify their physical validity and operational consistency. The validated scenarios are subsequently deployed into a Gymnasium-compatible RL environment incorporating photovoltaic generation, wind power, energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interaction, supporting the training and evaluation of mainstream RL algorithms. On an independently prepared 600-instruction benchmark, incorporating Scenario Skill retrieval increased semantic success from 36.50% to 80.33%. The layered safety validator achieves a classification accuracy of 89.52% on 210 test cases. In a comparison involving four participants, GridSage reduces the average scenario-configuration time by 43.58%. Cross-LLM experiments further demonstrate that the proposed configuration workflow can operate effectively across different LLM backends. These results show that GridSage provides an effective and auditable approach for translating natural-language research intent into reproducible RL scenarios for active distribution networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Real-time pricing strategy for photovoltaic prosumer communities based on a bi-level optimization in coupled electricity and carbon markets
Abstract: The coordinated operation of electricity and carbon markets is crucial for low-carbon power system transition. This paper proposes a bilevel real-time pricing framework for photovoltaic (PV) prosumer communities in coupled electricity-carbon markets. The upper-level Electricity-Carbon Regulation platform determines internal electricity and carbon prices to minimize its net settlement and residual balancing cost, considering internal settlement with prosumers and external balancing transactions. The lower-level prosumers maximize welfare by optimizing electricity consumption under logarithmic utility, subject to PV generation and carbon-allowance/emission constraints. The bilevel model is transformed into a single-level nonlinear program using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and solved by the augmented Lagrangian method. Numerical results show that the proposed strategy achieves the highest prosumer welfare among all considered pricing schemes, while maintaining a relatively low level of carbon emissions, thereby demonstrating the superior economic–low-carbon performance of coordinated electricity–carbon pricing. Title: Subsynchronous resonance analysis in large wind farms: a probabilistic approach incorporating wake effects and wind uncertainty
Abstract: Subsynchronous resonance (SSR) in large wind farms is strongly influenced by aerodynamic uncertainty and wake-induced flow distortions—two factors that conventional deterministic studies often neglect. This paper introduces a probabilistic SSR assessment framework for a doubly-cage induction generator (DCIG)-based wind farm connected to a series-compensated transmission line. The proposed approach explicitly incorporates wind speed uncertainty modeled via a joint Weibull–von Mises distribution, multiple wake interactions captured through a multi-wake aerodynamic model, a six-mass drivetrain, and equivalent collector cable impedance. The collector cable X/R ratio is identified as a key determinant: a higher ratio reduces effective damping and shifts the critical series compensation threshold lower, amplifying both instability probability and severity. Moreover, the proposed probabilistic method substantially outperforms deterministic approaches, closely matching actual-value post-analysis with markedly lower error. A fuzzy C-means clustering-based approach reduces computational burden by over 85% compared with full Monte Carlo simulation while preserving accuracy, making large-scale or real-time probabilistic SSR assessment practical for wind farm planning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Computationally efficient oscillation stability analysis of large-scale renewable power systems via partitioning
Abstract: With the increasing penetration of large-scale renewable generation, inverter-induced oscillations pose significant threats to the secure operation of modern power systems, creating an urgent need for efficient oscillation stability analysis. However, conventional analysis methods become computationally expensive for large-scale systems due to the large number of connected devices and the complex network topology, which together result in high-order system models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a partition-based oscillation stability analysis method. A fast partitioning algorithm is developed to decompose the original system into smaller subsystems, thereby reducing computational complexity. A dynamic equivalent method is further introduced to represent the external areas of each subsystem. The consistency between the oscillation modes of the partitioned subsystems and those of the whole system can be maintained. Case studies on practical systems verify that the proposed method achieves agreement with whole-system analysis results while significantly improving computational efficiency, demonstrating its feasibility for extremely large-scale power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Core-shell supported NiCo bimetallic catalysts with alloying synergy for oleic acid hydrogenation to bio‑jet fuel
Abstract: Reducing carbon emissions from the aviation sector represented a pressing environmental challenge, and the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to produce high‑value bio-jet fuel offered one of the most promising and economically viable pathways. Herein, we reported a novel bimetallic alloy catalyst with a tunable Ni/Co ratio, specifically designed for the selective hydrogenation of oleic acid to bio-jet fuel. This system delivered 100% conversion of oleic acid and a higher bio-jet fuel yield of 57.2%, while maintaining high iso-alkanes selectivity, which demonstrated superior performance compared to previously reported dazzling heterogeneous catalysts. The introduction of Co promoted the formation of a NiCo alloy phase and facilitated electron transfer from Co to Ni species. The resulting electronic and geometric synergies collectively enhance the dissociation and activation of H2, as well as the hydrogenation activity of substrates. Moreover, the Ni/Co ratio directly modulated the catalyst acidity, and the optimized acid properties played a critical role in the subsequent cracking and isomerization of deoxygenated intermediates. Title: A multi-branch arc fault detection method based on time-frequency feature fusion and random forest
Abstract: With the rising global demand for electrical energy, ensuring power system operational reliability has become critically important. In this background, electrical fire prevention, particularly arc fault detection, has gained significant attention. However, in complex multi-branch load networks, coupling interference between different branches results in unacceptably high false alarm rates in conventional detection methods. To address this problem, this study proposes an arc fault detection method based on multi-branch time-frequency feature fusion and random forest (RF). First, a multi-branch arc simulation experimental platform is designed to acquire original current waveform datasets. Time-frequency features are subsequently extracted and fused of all branches. An RF-based detection framework is then developed to identify the fused feature. On this base, evaluation of different feature fusion strategies is conducted to determine the optimal strategy. Finally, experiments validate that the proposed detection framework achieves a 99.89% detection accuracy and a 0.0106‰ false alarm rate. When deployed on embedded systems, the framework achieves a response latency within 20 ms while maintaining 100% fault detection accuracy within 80 ms, confirming its hardware implementation feasibility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Optimizing Cooling Mode Switchovers in Green Data Centers via a SC Metric and TRNSYS-PSO Simulation
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Driven by the demand for green and efficient data center cooling, this study develops a rack-level rear-door heat pipe (RDHP) cooling system and proposes a comprehensive metric SC by integrating Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), and scoring components from the Chinese green data center standard GB/T 44989-2024. Optimizing the switchover between free, hybrid, and mechanical cooling modes is critical for improving the energy efficiency and reducing the carbon footprint of data centers. A delimiting temperature (T_delimit) of 17°C was established to optimally balance enhanced free cooling utilization with operational safety, ensuring server inlet temperatures remained within the limits. The switchover temperatures were optimized for four climatically diverse Chinese cities using TRNSYS simulations coupled with the GenOpt tool and a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. Results show that SC-oriented optimization effectively prolongs free cooling duration, reduces PUE, WUE, and CUE simultaneously, and outperforms empirical temperature settings. Also, the SC metric presents higher sensitivity than single indicators, while its optimization remains stable under varying grid carbon emission factors. This work provides a valuable methodology and a practical tool for advancing the green and low-carbon transformation of data centers, offering significant implications for policy-making and sustainable infrastructure planning. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Numerical Estimation of the Effective Mechanical Properties (EMP) of Steel AISI 4340 Fiber-Reinforced Concrete
Abstract: This study aims to estimate the effective mechanical properties (EMP) of a composite material consisting of two phases: a concrete matrix and randomly distributed cylindrical fiber reinforcements. To determine the composite's effective mechanical properties, several key parameters are considered, including the fiber volume fraction, fiber geometry (expressed as the length-to-diameter ratio), and the void volume fraction. The voids are modeled as spherical inclusions, randomly dispersed within the matrix phase only, with strict non-intersection constraints, ensuring they do not overlap or touch the fibers. This configuration reflects realistic entrapped air porosity while preserving the integrity of the fiber-matrix interface. The effective elastic properties are estimated using a numerical homogenization procedure based on the finite element method (FEM) and the representative volume element (RVE) concept. Periodic boundary conditions (PBC) are applied to ensure representativeness, and a progressive mesh refinement strategy is employed, with a finer mesh around the inclusions, to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. The 3D fiber distributions are generated using a custom Python 3.9 script that enforces non-overlapping conditions between fibers, thereby preventing interpenetration during RVE construction. © 2026 Semnan University Faculty of Mechanical Engineering.
