Title: Advanced AI and deep learning enabled techniques for anomaly detection in EV charging behavior using real-time household smart meter data
Abstract: Electric Vehicles (EV) are critical for monitoring and maintaining the health, performance, and safety of electric vehicle batteries. However, these systems often face challenges due to unexpected faults, irregular battery behaviour, and noisy sensor data, which lead to inaccurate monitoring or potential system failures. In this manuscript, Advanced AI and Deep Learning Enabled Techniques for Anomaly Detection in EV Charging Behavior Using Real-Time Household Smart Meter Data (AD-DBMS-EV-SIGNN) is proposed. Initially, real-time electricity consumption data collected from smart meters installed in 900 households is utilized to detect anomalies in EV charging behavior by capturing grid-level voltage, current, and power fluctuation patterns, reflecting the impact of EV charging load on the home grid. Under Robust Consensus Tobit Kalman Filtering (RCTKF), then the input data is pre-processing for cleaning, normalization and denoising. The pre-processed data is given to the Spike Induced Graph Neural Network (SIGNN) to accurately detect anomalies in EV Charging Behavior. Generally speaking, SIGNN does not include any adaptation of optimization techniques for identifying the best parameters to guarantee precise anomaly detection in EV systems. Therefore, SIGNN is optimized under the House Swallow Optimizer (HSO) to accurately identify anomalies in EV Charging Behavior. The performance of the proposed AD-DBMS-EV-SIGNN method is 99.43% for accuracy, 98.14% for precision, and 98.37% for recall when compared to other existing methods. © 2026

Title: Mung bean protein fibrils reinforce whey protein gels at neutral pH: Effects of fibril maturity, concentration, and microstructure
Abstract: The effect of mung bean protein fibrils (MF) as active nanoscale scaffolds on the heat-induced gelation of whey protein isolate (WPI) at pH 7 was studied. The microstructural features, intermolecular interactions, and rheological properties of WPI-MF composite hydrogels formulated with MF induced from different heating times (4 h, 8 h, and 12 h) and MF concentrations (0.1 wt%, 0.3 wt%, and 0.5 wt%) were investigated compared to pure WPI gels (Control). The CLSM images of gelled samples were analysed by a novel ResNet-34 transfer learning framework coupled with principal component analysis (PCA) to obtain the microstructural differences, indicating that 0.3 wt% MF was a critical concentration for structural reinforcement. The WPI-MF composite gels demonstrated significant rheological reinforcement, leading to an exceptional growth in the storage modulus (G′). This might be because MF efficiently recruited WPI molecules, resulting in the non-network protein fraction dramatical decrease of more than 30%. Furthermore, the solvent-extraction results suggest that hydrophobic associations made the largest operational contribution to maintaining the WPI–MF gel network. Title: Towards global location of inter-turn short-circuit faults in transformer homogeneous windings via double-end excitation and admittance response subtraction
Abstract: The frequency response analysis (FRA) is considered the common method for diagnosing transformer winding deformations, including short circuit (SC) faults. However, for a transformer with a homogeneous winding, it exhibits symmetry and uniform characteristics; each equivalent electrical circuit unit of the winding is almost identical. Consequently, SC faults in symmetrical positions cannot be located by traditional FRA. Besides, the health history FRA curve, namely the fingerprint, is overly dependent on the traditional FRA method. In this article, an improved transformer inter-turn short circuit fault method, namely, combination method of the double-end excitation and admittance response subtraction, is proposed. It breaks the symmetry of the transformer and makes “global” location within the entire winding, from top to bottom, possible. Firstly, the principle of the introduced method is presented. Criteria for establishing the external circuit and sensitivity analysis is studied. The method is then verified on three different transformers, including simulations and experimental tests. Finally, machine learning is used for localization analysis. The results show that the proposed method has “global” diagnosis ability for SC faults and does not rely on complex neural networks, which can achieve satisfactory performance. © 2026

Title: Impact of surface protrusions on negative corona discharge onset voltage for high–voltage stranded conductors
Abstract: The onset voltage of negative corona discharge on high-voltage conductors is strongly influenced by surface irregularities and electric field non-uniformity. Previous studies have investigated corona inception on stranded conductors and the effect of conducting protrusions on electric field enhancement; however, their combined influence has not been adequately addressed. In this paper, a three-dimensional numerical model is developed to investigate the onset of negative corona on a stranded conductor with a conducting protrusion in the presence of a grounded plane. The electric field distribution is computed using an extended charge simulation technique, in which the stranded conductor is represented by helical line charges, while the protrusion is modeled using ring and point charges. Image charges are implemented to simulate the grounded plane. To ensure high computational accuracy, the boundary conditions were evaluated, demonstrating that for all investigated protrusion geometries, the maximum percentage potential error remained below 1.06 %. The proposed algorithm is tested against previous experimental work, and excellent agreement is reached. The results show that a conducting protrusion dramatically increases the local electric field compared to a stranded conductor without protrusions, which in turn decreases the corona onset voltage. The proposed method is implemented to study the effect of different dimensions of protrusions on the surface electric field and the corona onset voltage, aiding the performance analysis of irregular practical stranded conductors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Stepwise identification method for SVG fault ride-through control parameters in multiple solution spaces
Abstract: Accurately obtaining the controller parameters of the Static Var Generator (SVG) is crucial for modeling new energy stations and analyzing grid-connected characteristics. However, due to the lack of observation characteristics and the coupling between the control loop parameters, all the parameters that are identified together in the entire solution space easily cause large errors. Given this, a stepwise identification method for SVG fault ride-through control parameters in multiple solution spaces is proposed. First, the maximum information coefficient is used to analyze the correlation between the control parameters and observations. The control parameters are divided into multiple solution spaces for decoupling, and the stepwise identification order is determined according to the difference in parameter sensitivity in each solution space. Second, in multiple solution spaces, the observed features are used to train the XGBoost algorithm to optimize the initial values of the control parameters. The IHHO algorithm is employed for the precise identification of the SVG fault ride-through control parameters. Finally, through hardware-in-the-loop testing, the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed method were verified under various operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Study on the physicochemical properties and biocompatibility of proanthocyanidin cross-linked collagen hydrogels mediated by laccase
Abstract: The discarding and low-value utilisation of by-products from silver carp processing caused serious environmental pollution and waste of resources. The study employed silver carp skin as the primary raw material in the fabrication of collagen hydrogels, focusing on the impact of laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking on the physicochemical properties and biocompatibility of collagen hydrogels. This investigation is undertaken with a view to promoting the high-value utilisation of silver carp by-products. The results indicated that laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking significantly improved the mechanical properties and thermal stability of collagen hydrogels. The maximum cross-linking degree of the laccase-mediated proanthocyanidin cross-linking (PL) group reached 81.26% nearly double that of the proanthocyanidin cross-linking (PA) group, while the maximum hardness was 6.02 N. It was evident that both the heat deflection temperature and the thermal degradation temperature had increased. Furthermore, the study findings demonstrated that proanthocyanidins primarily form hydrogen bonds through their phenolic hydroxyl groups with the carbonyl groups on proline residues in collagen. In contrast, the laccase-mediated cross-linking mechanism of proanthocyanidins involves a Michael addition reaction between the quinone groups and the amino groups in the collagen hydrogel, thereby achieving covalent cross-linking. The biocompatibility assays using NIH3T3 cells revealed that cross-linked hydrogel extracts were highly biocompatible and upgraded the expression of wound healing-related factors in fibroblasts. This study provided novel insights into the application of silver carp skin collagen in bio-based materials, thereby expanding avenues for the comprehensive utilisation of silver carp by-products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Self-sacrificial in-situ carboxylation for dynamic donor-acceptor optimization in metal-free photothermal catalytic H2O2 synthesis
Abstract: The static donor-acceptor (D-A) architectures of conventional organic photocatalysts are poorly adapted to the dynamically evolving redox environment of photoelectrochemical interfaces, leading to exciton trapping and progressive catalytic site deactivation. While pre-synthetic functionalization can tune frontier orbital levels, it produces fixed configurations that cannot adapt to operational degradation or fluctuating interfacial potentials during catalysis. Here we report a self-sacrificial dynamic optimization strategy, in which hydroxymethyl groups undergo photothermal oxidative dehydrogenation to form electron-withdrawing carboxyl functionalities in-situ, enabling operando reconfiguration of D-A push-pull structures for enhanced catalytic function. This in-situ carboxylation scavenges photogenerated holes, suppresses early-stage recombination, and promotes exciton dissociation by withdrawing electron density from acceptor units. Critically, it optimizes the catalytic carbon active sites, lowering the O2 activation barrier from 0.80 to 0.29 eV. As a result, the charge-separated state lifetime increases from 454 to 988 ps, and the reconstructed catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 3216 μmol g⁻1 h⁻1, a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 4.03% (optimized high-loading condition), and catalytic stability exceeding 50 h with negligible activity loss. Title: Evaluation of voltage sag tolerance capability for sensitive equipment based on hybrid density method
Abstract: Evaluating the voltage-sag ride-through capability of sensitive equipment is important for voltage-sag mitigation. Second, failure probabilities of the random variables are evaluated by combining the total probability integral and the Gauss–Hermite method. Finally, based on the IEEE 30-bus system, the failure probability of sensitive equipment is evaluated. Title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
Abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: HPC-accelerated parallel algorithms for large-scale power system contingency analysis
Abstract: The extension of static security assessment from N-1 to N-2 contingency analysis poses significant computational challenges because of the combinatorial growth in outage scenarios and the repeated execution of AC load-flow solutions. This paper proposes a high-performance computing (HPC) framework for efficient N-1 and N-2 contingency ranking using the fast decoupled load flow (FDLF) method on heterogeneous CPU-GPU platforms. Contingency severity is evaluated using a composite performance index based on line overloads and bus voltage deviations. The framework incorporates MPI-based CPU parallelization, CUDA-based GPU acceleration, and hybrid CPU-GPU execution, with cuBLAS-assisted LU factorization to accelerate the dominant FDLF linear solves. The proposed framework is validated on the IEEE 118-bus, Indian Northern Regional Power Grid (246-bus), and Polish 2383-bus systems under extensive N-1 and N-2 contingency sets. The MPI implementation achieves speedups of up to 19 × over the sequential implementation, while the hybrid implementation provides superior performance for GPU-enabled systems with limited CPU resources. Title: Spray-assisted evaporative crystallization of conformal drug-encapsulated MOF coatings on macroporous substrates for infected wound healing

Abstract: Constructing metal-organic framework (MOF) coatings on macroporous substrates is important for translating MOF functions into practical biomedical materials, but nonuniform crystal growth and pore narrowing remain common challenges. Herein, we developed a sequential spray-assisted evaporative crystallization strategy to prepare MOF coatings on selected macroporous substrates. ZIF-8 and CuBDC were grown on filter paper, nonwoven fabric, and chitosan quaternary ammonium salt/polyvinyl alcohol (HP) aerogel, and the HP-based aerogels retained highly accessible scaffold macroporosity under the selected conditions. ZIF-8/HP was further used as a drug-loading platform for in situ curcumin (CUR) incorporation, yielding CUR-ZIF-8/HP with a CUR loading content of (4.3 ± 0.2)wt.% and an encapsulation efficiency of (68.5 ± 2.1)%. Title: A haptic feedback architecture for bionic teleoperation blade cleaning tasks
Abstract: Hazardous environment operations cannot eliminate the need for human intervention. Teleoperated robots can prevent operators from being exposed to danger. Title: Impact of nanoemulsion-Filled algal hydrogels structure on the in vitro digestibility and β-carotene bioaccessibility
Abstract: Bioactive compounds encapsulated in nanoemulsions (NEs) can gain additional protection when the NEs are incorporated into hydrogels and forming NE-filled hydrogel. Title: Deep learning architectures for fault analysis in power system protection: A reproducible evaluation on public waveform data
Abstract: The increasing operational variability of power systems motivates data-driven methods for fault analysis in protection applications. This paper presents a systematic evaluation of deep learning models for fault detection, classification, line identification, and localization. Models are trained on EMT-simulated voltage and current waveforms from the public PROTECT-90 dataset, a 90 kV double-line benchmark. Recurrent, convolutional, hybrid, and transformer-based architectures are compared under shared data splits, temporal decision horizons, and leakage-aware validation protocols to assess predictive performance, inference latency, and model complexity. Detection, classification, and line identification reach near-saturated performance once short post-fault transients are available, whereas localization depends strongly on temporal context and improves with longer observation windows. Additional sensitivity analyses contextualize localization under reduced relay observability, test-time communication perturbations, and impedance-based reference methods. Across tasks, compact recurrent and hybrid architectures nearly match the predictive performance of larger architectures while maintaining shorter inference times, indicating diminishing returns from increased capacity under centralized EMT-based measurements. Title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
Abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhao H.; Cui S.
Title: A study on the site selection of pumped storage power plants based on GIS and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Models: A case study of China
Abstract: Pumped storage power plants (PSPPs) are essential for enhancing power system flexibility and supporting renewable energy integration. However, PSPP site selection involves complex spatial constraints and multi-dimensional trade-offs among technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. This study proposes a two-stage GIS–MCDM framework for PSPP site selection. First, GIS-based spatial screening with veto criteria is applied to identify feasible candidate sites. Subsequently, an integrated AHP–entropy weighting approach and TOPSIS method are employed for comprehensive evaluation, with VIKOR, TODIM, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation used to verify robustness. A case study in Guangxi, China identifies the optimal site among seven alternatives, and the results demonstrate the stability of the proposed framework under different weighting scenarios. Furthermore, theoretical energy storage assessment and comparison with an approved PSPP project provide additional evidence for the engineering feasibility of the selected site. The proposed approach offers an effective decision-support tool for PSPP planning and clean energy development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Development of a new recombineering system for Edwardsiella species
Abstract: Edwardsiella species are important aquaculture pathogens that also cause opportunistic infections in humans, necessitating efficient genome editing tools to study their pathogenesis and develop control strategies. In this study, we identified and characterized six endogenous recombinases pairs from Edwardsiella and its phages. Among these, the BAS_MS17 system exhibited the highest recombination efficiency in E. piscicida EIB202Δp. Extending homology arms from 150 bp to 200 bp improved editing efficiency by 2-fold, while the addition of Redg or Plug further enhanced recombination by 3-fold and 2.5-fold, respectively, without compromising accuracy (100%). More importantly, when applied to E. piscicida sdu12S, Redg or Plug improved the editing efficiency by 8-fold and 7-fold, respectively. Deletion of the phage-derived single-strand binding protein (SSB) reduced efficiency to 25% of the BAS_MS17 level, whereas expression of the endogenous RecA-family SSB (rSSB) increased recombinant yield by 5-fold, highlighting functional conservation. Furthermore, SSB proteins from heterologous hosts failed to enhance recombination efficiency. Using the optimized system, we successfully knocked out ten distinct genes, including virulence-associated loci, with editing accuracy exceeding 85%. Phenotypic analysis revealed that luxR , but not the other tested genes, contributes to biofilm formation. Virulence evaluation results showed that aroA , fur , and hfq are critical virulence-associated factors. Collectively, this streamlined recombineering system provides a simple, rapid, and efficient genetic tool for Edwardsiella , supporting mechanistic studies of virulence and the development of live attenuated vaccine candidates. Title: Electronegativity-guided construction of bimetallic centers on black phosphorus for CO2-to-C2 electroreduction: A DFT study
Abstract: Dual-atom catalysts (DACs) hold great promise for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) owing to their synergistic effects and full atom utilization efficiency. However, a general strategy for precise structural control remains lacking, which limits the activation of key intermediates and the selectivity toward C2 products. Herein, we propose an electronegativity-difference strategy to construct black phosphorus (BP)-supported heteronuclear DACs. Co and Pd, with electronegativity lower and higher than P, respectively, form a stable Co-Pd@BP structure. Electronic structure calculations reveal that the electronegativity difference between the bimetallic sites and BP induces directional charge redistribution and creates efficient electron transfer pathways. Such characteristics promote electron injection into adsorbed CO2, activate the inert CO2 molecules, and lower the formation energy of the key *COOH intermediate. Gibbs free energy calculations confirm that Co-Pd synergism optimizes the *CO-*CHO coupling step both thermodynamically and kinetically, overcoming the limited C2 production capability. The acetaldehyde evolution pathway exhibits the lowest energy of 0.36 eV. Moreover, this electronegativity modulation strategy is extendable to Ru-Co and Rh-Co heteronuclear systems with comparable CO2RR activity, showing preliminary extendability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Credible flexibility envelope learning for renewable curtailment reduction in export-constrained power systems
Abstract: Renewable-rich areas often experience curtailment because local demand and export capacity cannot absorb short-duration surpluses. Flexible loads and storage can help, but nameplate capability does not necessarily represent reliable market capacity when availability, internal state, rebound, telemetry quality, and baseline error vary between events. This paper develops a credible flexibility envelope by eroding a multi-period physical feasible set with a calibrated trajectory-error set. A class-conditioned recurrent state captures recent operation, a hierarchical Bayesian decoder updates uncertain physical parameters, and weighted block-conformal calibration adjusts residual margins under temporal dependence and drift. Offers, cleared capacity, dispatch instructions, and verified delivery are modeled separately, and the resulting envelopes are embedded in a loss-aware, multi-corridor network clearing model with voltage, thermal, feeder, settlement, and credit constraints. A controlled three-year synthetic benchmark uses a modified IEEE RTS-24 system, three radial feeder equivalents, seven resource classes, 20 random seeds, and 540 stress-test combinations. At a 95% coverage target, the proposed method achieves 95.0% empirical coverage, reduces non-delivery from 10.1% to 4.6%, increases curtailment reduction from 22.6% to 40.0%, and raises mean net surplus from 62.7 × 103 to 193.0 × 103 USD. Ablation and stress tests further examine drift, forecast error, telemetry loss, baseline bias, correlation, network changes, and extreme renewable conditions. The results are specific to the modified RTS-24 benchmark and motivate further evaluation on other networks and measured data. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Li M.; Yi D.; Wu T.; Li C.; Hu B.; Shao C.
Title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

Authors: Saha K.; Kumar N.
Title: Physics-inspired Bayesian estimation of multilayer soil resistivity incorporating thermo-hydro-groundwater effects for grounding design
Abstract: Soil resistivity estimation plays a critical role in the development of grounding systems, affecting the earth potential rise (EPR) and touch and step voltages. Traditional multilayer inversion techniques estimate soil properties based on the fit of observed apparent resistivity curves, assuming soil resistivity parameters to be static and dependent only on depth. Nevertheless, in reality, soil resistivity is characterized by high levels of temporal variability influenced by changes in temperature, moisture content, precipitation, and groundwater. These dynamic factors are seldom considered in the inversion process. This paper presents a Bayesian multilayer inversion and uncertainty-quantification framework integrated with a physics-inspired phenomenological environmental model. The environmental model uses simplified and bounded correction functions motivated by established temperature, moisture, rainfall, and groundwater effects rather than directly solving the coupled governing equations of heat transfer, unsaturated flow, and groundwater movement. A fast Sum-of-Exponentials (SoE) forward model is used to achieve computationally efficient responses in multilayer soils. The inverse problem is solved using bounded stochastic optimization with a regularized log-domain misfit, followed by Bayesian uncertainty quantification using Metropolis-Hastings sampling. A penalty-based model-complexity criterion is applied to avoid unnecessary layers. The proposed approach provides physically plausible seasonal soil-resistivity scenario estimates together with Bayesian parameter and predictive uncertainty measures conditional on the adopted phenomenological model structure, thereby supporting conservative grounding-system design assessment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Sulfone-bridged connectivity modulation induces favorable spatial configuration and electronic structure in polymer photocatalysts for enhanced overall H2O2 production
Abstract: Insufficient charge separation efficiency and sluggish two-electron water oxidation kinetics are the primary limitations for photocatalytic H2O2 production over polymer photocatalysts. Herein, we proposed an innovative connectivity engineering approach for functional groups to tackle these drawbacks. Specially, we developed two polymer photocatalysts with distinct sulfone group connectivity configurations, namely sulfone-bridged Tp-DASO-B and sulfone-fused Tp-DPSO-F. In situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that the sulfone-bridged configuration in Tp-DASO-B introduced a non-coplanar twist and modulated the electron delocalization. This structural feature enhanced exciton dissociation and increased the spatial distance between holes and electrons, thereby promoting charge separation and transfer. Meanwhile, the strong electron-withdrawing effect of the sulfone group in Tp-DASO-B activated the water oxidation sites on adjacent benzene rings, enhancing the adsorption and activation of water molecules and significantly promoting two-electron water oxidation. Title: Preference-guided graph reinforcement learning for multi-objective quality-aware hybrid flow shop scheduling with multilevel assembly
Abstract: Product quality is crucial to the competitiveness of manufacturing enterprises. However, existing quality-aware scheduling studies mainly approximate product quality evolution using indirect factors such as processing time, making it difficult to characterize the integrated effects of equipment health conditions and operation precedence relationships on product quality. To address this issue, a quality-aware hybrid flow shop scheduling problem with multilevel assembly (QHFSP-MA) is formulated by incorporating multilevel assembly processes and processing-assembly quality propagation mechanisms of complex precision products. Due to the large solution space and multi-objective characteristics of QHFSP-MA, existing multi-objective reinforcement learning methods still struggle to obtain high-quality Pareto fronts. Therefore, a preference-guided graph reinforcement learning framework (PGRL) is proposed. A heterogeneous graph is first constructed to represent the processing-assembly system. Then, a preference-guided meta-relation heterogeneous graph neural network is developed to dynamically adjust the importance of different meta-relations according to objective preferences, enabling generalized policy learning under diverse preferences. Furthermore, an adaptive preference weight mechanism (APWM) is designed to reduce the mismatch between uniform preference sampling and irregular Pareto front distributions, thereby improving Pareto front approximation. Experimental results demonstrate that PGRL outperforms dispatching rules, metaheuristic algorithms, and two advanced multi-objective deep reinforcement learning methods in terms of optimization performance, generalization, and computational efficiency. An automotive engine manufacturing case further validates its practical effectiveness, reducing makespan, quality loss cost, and maintenance cost by 27.3%, 25.7%, and 8.8%, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Improved response of grid forming doubly fed induction generator under grid disturbances
Abstract: The response of grid-forming (GFM) doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is influenced by its power synchronization control loop (PSCL) as it establishes frequency and synchronizes the DFIG in network. A large deviation in the phase and frequency of GFM DFIG during fault may cause it to become unstable. Additionally, the response of the DC-link following a disturbance may cause the DFIG to be unstable. Addressing these challenges, an analogy is established between DC-link dynamics and swing equation through detailed modeling of DC-link, which incorporates dynamics of PSCL. This model is subsequently utilized to design proposed synchronizing and damping control. In proposed synchronizing control, a power-based synchronizing multiplier term is integrated into PSCL to minimize frequency and phase deviations of DFIG's terminal voltage, resulting in a stable response of DFIG. In the proposed damping control strategy, the current compensation term is integrated into the active current loop of the GSC. This integration minimizes variations in the DC-link voltage, resulting in a stable response of DFIG. Along with proposed control, the active and reactive currents of DFIG are controlled to meet the reactive current criterion as per the grid code. Title: Line outage impact factor (LOIF): A new sensitivity factor for enhanced transmission observability
Abstract: Undetected transmission line outages degrade operator situational awareness and can increase the risk of incorrect control actions and escalating system stress. To improve transmission observability for outage detection under limited monitoring, this paper introduces the Line Outage Impact Factor (LOIF), a new sensitivity indicator that quantifies the relative change in power flow experienced by an observed line following an outage elsewhere. Unlike the conventional Line Outage Distribution Factor (LODF), which normalizes by the pre-outage flow on the disconnected line, LOIF normalizes by the pre-outage flow on the observed line, offering a better indicator for the sensitivity of the observed line to another line's outage and, thus, facilitating the selection of monitored lines that enhance system observability. Building on LOIF, we propose two observed transmission line (OTL) selection strategies to maximize outage coverage with a small number of monitoring locations. With OTLs selected in the IEEE 30-bus, 118-bus, and the Wisconsin 1664-bus systems, we performed outage detection using different machine learning classifiers. Results show that, for the same number of OTLs, LOIF-based selections generally achieve higher F1-scores than LODF-based selections, with the most consistent gains observed in the large 1664-bus system, demonstrating LOIF's potential for scalable transmission monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Synthesis of highly active R‑ZIF-67 from spent lithium‑ion batteries for peroxymonosulfate activation: Distinct roles of Ni and Li impurities
Abstract: The distinct roles of framework-doped Ni and free Li+ in R‑ZIF‑67 catalysts derived from spent LiCoO2 were investigated for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation toward metronidazole (MNZ) degradation. Title: A non-standard protection scheme for coordinated and stable SDGs operation
Abstract: The integration of distributed generation, especially synchronous distributed generators, into power distribution networks has introduced new protection and stability challenges. One critical issue is that the coordination of protection devices could be disrupted because of the fault current provided by distributed generations. Another problem is the transient instability of synchronous distributed generators due to their low inertia during fault events. This paper presents a novel protection strategy that simultaneously addresses both problems. A customized non-standard time-current-voltage characteristic is proposed for overcurrent relays where the adaptive coordination is obtained. It also improves stability while satisfying both Coordination Time Interval and Critical Clearing Time constraints. This approach includes an offline phase involving power flow, fault, and protection coordination studies. If transient stability constraints are violated, an online adaptive phase is activated by using local voltage measurements at the synchronous distributed generator buses. The proposed method is implemented and validated on the IEEE 33-bus distribution system by using ETAP software. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the method to maintain coordination time intervals and ensuring synchronous distributed generators stability, even under severe fault conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cao Z.; Fu Z.; Li K.; Zhou X.; Rao H.
Title: Sample-preserving evaluation and frozen rank consensus for UAV transmission-line anomaly detection under detector uncertainty
Abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) power-line inspection aims to identify defective assets using models trained only on normal data. In detector-derived region-of-interest (ROI) pipelines, however, upstream localization errors can silently remove difficult samples, alter crop geometry, and make retained-subset metrics overstate full-population performance. This study presents FRC-KARP (Frozen Rank Consensus with Keep-All Region Priors), a reliability-oriented evaluation and consensus framework rather than a new anomaly-feature extractor. FRC-KARP combines three elements: a strict sample-preserving full-population protocol, frozen percentile-rank consensus over raw-image and region-prior score streams using fixed equal weights, and a separate detector-conditioned reliability audit for retained-subset bias, aggregation-rule sensitivity, and crop completeness. The audit reads frozen scores and ROI metadata after score export; it neither feeds back to nor changes the final FRC-KARP score. No fitted fusion weights, anomalous training samples, or test-label-tuned stream selections are used. On the primary InsPLAD object-centric glass-insulator/missingcap task, FRC-KARP achieves AUROC 0.8870, AP 0.4893, and Max F1 0.6058 over all 671 test images. On two additional InsPLAD asset tasks, it gives the highest AUROC among the three reported outputs and raises the three-task macro AUROC to 0.8519. Under controlled image shifts and 10–30% proposal dropout, performance degrades measurably, but FRC-KARP loses less AUROC than the Padded-ROI stream. The evidence supports sample-preserving reliability analysis within InsPLAD; external-domain and genuine full-frame UAV generalization remain unverified. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Maximizing photovoltaic efficiency using dual core boost converter and artificial intelligence-based MPPT

Title: Research on the fuzzy adaptive VSG-MPC coordinated control strategy considering regenerative braking
Abstract: In urban rail transit AC/DC microgrids, the injection of regenerative braking energy from trains and power absorption by traction loads can cause severe fluctuations in DC-bus power. First, grid-forming VSG control is employed as the fundamental control scheme for the converter. The angular frequency deviation and its rate of change are used as inputs to a fuzzy controller, which regulates the virtual inertia and damping online. This improves the dynamic frequency support capability of the VSG under power disturbances.Second, an MPC prediction model is constructed based on the DC-bus energy state, and the equivalent VSG power-response time constant is updated online according to the adaptive inertia and damping coefficients to match the current VSG dynamics. Receding-horizon optimization of the active-power reference then stabilizes the DC-bus voltage and smooths bidirectional power regulation. MATLAB/Simulink simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses DC-bus voltage fluctuations and frequency deviations under inverter feedback, rectification-based energy absorption, and mode-transition conditions, while improving the dynamic active-power response of the VSG. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Karadeniz A.
Title: Data-Driven harmonic forecasting in wave energy conversion systems using machine and deep learning
Abstract: This study proposes a data-driven harmonic forecasting framework for a power take-off (PTO) and permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wave energy conversion system (WECS). A detailed Simulink model represents the end-to-end wave-to-electrical chain, including PTO conversion, generator-side power conversion, grid interfacing, and harmonic monitoring at the 575 V bus. The dataset is constructed from real NOAA/NDBC station 46042 metocean records spanning 2020–2023. After quality filtering (203,380 raw observations reduced to 38,744 valid records) and Simulink-based simulation with transient removal, the final learning-ready dataset contains 8,751 synchronized wave–electrical snapshots. Wave, wind, and electrical state variables are used as multivariate predictors, and voltage total harmonic distortion (THDV) at the 575 V bus is forecast one step ahead. The benchmark includes Random Forest and XGBoost as machine-learning baselines, together with LSTM, GRU, and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) as sequence-based deep-learning models. Performance is evaluated using RMSE, MAE, normalized RMSE (nRMSE), and R2, with additional trajectory and residual analyses. Over the available Q4 2023 evaluation window ending on 2023-11-25, GRU achieves the best performance, with nRMSE = 11.99% and R2 = 0.611. LSTM follows closely, GRU slightly outperforms the naive persistence baseline, and both recurrent models outperform the tree-based baselines and TCN. The framework supports proactive harmonic supervision for offshore and subsea-connected WECS architectures. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Faulty feeder selection for high impedance faults in resonant grounding systems via physics-guided neural networks with physical posterior verification

Title: Solving multi-objective optimal power flow with renewable energy sources using an improved non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm
Abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) into power systems poses challenges to multi-objective optimal power flow (MOOPF) problems, including uncertainties and complex constraints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an improved NSGA-II algorithm based on an adaptive geometric crowding distance (AGCD) strategy, referred to as AGCD-NSGA-II. The proposed algorithm inherits the nondominated sorting and genetic evolutionary mechanisms of NSGA-II and introduces an adaptive geometric crowding distance strategy, which dynamically captures the distribution characteristics of nondominated solutions in the objective space and incorporates a nearest-neighbor density evaluation mechanism to achieve an effective balance between convergence performance and solution diversity. To address the uncertainties of wind speed and photovoltaic (PV) generation, Weibull and lognormal probability distributions are employed to model the uncertainties of wind power and PV outputs, respectively. First, the proposed algorithm is compared with several multi-objective optimization algorithms on the Viennet (VNT) benchmark functions using the inverted generational distance (IGD) and hypervolume (HV) metrics. The experimental results demonstrate that AGCD-NSGA-II exhibits competitive performance in terms of convergence and solution distribution. Subsequently, eight case studies are conducted on the modified IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 57-bus systems considering renewable energy integration. The objectives include generation cost, pollutant emissions, active power loss, and voltage deviation. In addition, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test is performed to further verify the statistical significance of the performance differences among the algorithms. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve MOOPF problems considering renewable energy uncertainties and exhibits excellent optimization performance and robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Generalized error bounds in the recovery of solitary wave profiles

Title: Wind power prediction based on a deeply coupled IT2FNN-attentional GRU network
Abstract: The prediction of wind power output is crucial for the safe and stable operation of power grids with a high proportion of renewable energy. We establish a deeply coupled architecture of interval type-2 fuzzy neural networks and gated recurrent units, which combines uncertainty quantification capabilities with time-series feature extraction abilities. The proposed Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Neural Network-Attentional Gated Recurrent Unit (IT2FNN-AGRU) network effectively addresses the high volatility and complex uncertainties of wind power output. To evaluate its practical performance, the proposed model was empirically validated using operational data collected from two wind farms located in Turkey (3.6 MW) and France (1.85 MW). Authors: Hu X.; Mu L.
Title: A robust lowest-order method for the Brinkman equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The Brinkman equation couples the Stokes and Darcy equations by varying viscosity and permeability parameters to accommodate broad applications. Developing a numerical solver that remains robust and efficient across all parameter regimes presents significant research challenges. In this paper, we propose a uniform and pressure-robust finite element method of the lowest order to solve the Brinkman equation. In our discretization, the velocity variable is approximated by a linear Lagrange polynomial enriched by the lowest order Raviart-Thomas element, while the pressure variable is approximated by piecewise constant functions. We provide a rigorous theoretical analysis and numerical validation to demonstrate the method's uniform convergence. Furthermore, to address the high computational costs associated with large-scale practical problems, we design an effective preconditioner that ensures high efficiency and scalability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Twin-boundary-rich PtPd metallene suppresses CO poisoning for efficient methanol electrooxidation
Abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are regarded as a highly promising clean-energy technology. Herein, an ultrathin two-dimensional twin-boundary-rich PtPd metallene (TB-PtPdene) is successfully synthesized using a salt-templating method. Mechanistic studies reveal suppressed accumulation of poisoning CO intermediates and altered behavior of oxygenated intermediates on TB-PtPdene. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that the twin-boundary-rich PtPd structure modulates the adsorption energetics of MOR intermediates and reduces the uphill free-energy change of the *CHO-to-*HCOO step. When TB-PtPdene is implemented in DMFCs, the assembled device achieves a peak power density of 14.2 mW cm−2, significantly exceeding that of Pt black-based devices. Title: Identification and characterization of biofilm-degrading aptamers against Escherichia coli by Inhibition-SELEX and analysis of their target proteins and interactions

Title: A gated risk assessment and alarm-screening framework for wildfire monitoring in transmission-line corridors
Abstract: Wildfires near transmission-line corridors threaten secure power-system operation, while early flames and thin smoke are small, low-contrast, and readily confused with haze, steam, reflection, lighting artifacts, and other corridor interference. Title: Promoting effects of Cr2O3 Lewis acid on the multi-component metal glass for seawater electrolysis

Title: A Low Voltage Ride-Through control strategy for cascaded H-bridge photovoltaic grid-connected inverters considering asymmetric current injection under phase-to-phase short-circuit fault conditions

Based on this analysis, a typical phase-to-phase short-circuit fault is selected to evaluate several control strategies for suppressing real power reversal. By integrating different control methods, the proposed approach effectively narrows the range of real power reversal during asymmetric faults. Title: A Node voltage violation risk based adaptive partitioning and distributed voltage control method of ADN
Abstract: High penetration of distributed photovoltaics (PV) aggravates voltage violations in active distribution networks (ADNs). This paper proposes a risk-adaptive partitioning and distributed voltage control method. A risk-adaptive partitioning index is defined for network clustering incorporating a comprehensive performance index combining the regional voltage regulation capability for both overvoltage and undervoltage cases and an improved modularity index. A risk-adaptive double-layer distributed voltage control method with a risk-adaptive penalty mechanism is developed. The risk-adaptive penalty mechanism is introduced into the upper-layer objective function by updating the penalty coefficients of on-load tap changer (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CBs) operations. In the upper layer, the OLTC and CBs are coordinated on an hourly timescale to suppress the voltage violations and minimize active power losses while reducing the mechanical equipment actions. In the lower layer, the controller provides fast intra-partition voltage support and reduces power losses with a control period of 15 min. Authors: Deng C.; Zhou Y.; Cai X.; Wang Y.; Li P.; Qi J.; Yang Y.; Zhu Z.; Li J.
Title: Hierarchically confined electrode enabling surface-enhanced atomic hydrogen concentration for advanced electrocatalytic hydrodehalogenation
Abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodehalogenation (ECH) is a promising strategy for detoxifying chlorinated organic pollutants; however, its efficiency is often limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in low electron utilization efficiency. Because both ECH and HER share atomic hydrogen (H*) as a common intermediate, regulating the fate of H* is critical for improving reaction selectivity and energy efficiency. Here, we propose a hierarchically confined electrode design by embedding a core–shell confined architecture into a sandwich-type electrocatalytic membrane. The core-shell structure acts as a local reservoir to enhance the surface concentration of H* in the cavity, while the hierarchically confined graphene oxide (GO) layers is engineered to improve mass transport. By prolonging the residence time of H* and suppressing its recombination into molecular hydrogen, the confined membrane preferentially promotes H*-mediated hydrodehalogenation. Using 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (2,4,6-TCP) as a model pollutant, the freestanding electrocatalytic electrode achieved 91.5% degradation within 120 min. Scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) and COMSOL verified the H* confinement capability within the core–shell structure, while electrochemical characterizations and scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) revealed effective suppression of HER and regulation of current density distribution by GO layers. This study elucidates how hierarchically confined, diffusion-limited electrocatalytic electrode govern the fate of H* and provides a structure-based strategy for enhancing electron utilization efficiency and energy efficiency in ECH. Title: Comparative Investigation of Epoxy-terminated and Carboxyl-terminated Butadiene Nitrile Rubber for Toughened Epoxy Resins
Abstract: The research presents how Carboxyl Terminated Butadiene Nitrile (CTBN) and Epoxy Terminated Butadiene Nitrile (ETBN) types of Reactive Liquid Rubber (RLR) influence epoxy resins through rheological, thermal, and mechanical property assessments. The thermal stability of the ETBN and CTBN systems was analyzed by using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) to determine decomposition temperatures and stability measurements. A complete set of mechanical tests measured tensile strength, flexural strength, and impact strength. Toughness improvements reached their peak with 2.5 wt.% ETBN addition resulting in a 42.2% increase in ultimate tensile strength, a 103.8% increase in tensile modulus, a 26.9% improvement in toughness, and a 67.65% increase in impact strength while maintaining all other properties. Also, 5 wt.% CTBN incorporation into the epoxy polymer leads to 30% increment in ultimate tensile strength, 49.5% increase in ultimate flexural strength, 68% increase in tensile modulus, and 300% increase in impact strength. So, both CTBN and ETBN are said to be effective tougheners that can be used to enhance the toughness of the overall matrix system while balancing other mechanical properties. The investigation highlights how the termination chemistry affects phase separation and interfacial adhesion, ultimately leading to improved performance for its applications in automotive and aerospace industries. Title: A dispatch strategy for islanded multi-energy microgrid incorporating gravity-based energy storage based on an IGWO algorithm
Abstract: Addressing the challenges of abundant yet highly fluctuating wind and solar resources in mountainous regions, high costs of power and heat supply, and difficulties in matching supply and demand alongside carbon emission issues within the coordinated dispatch of “electricity-gas-heat-carbon” multi-energy systems, this paper proposes a dispatch scheme for mountainous islanded multi‑energy microgrid incorporating gravity storage, based on an improved grey wolf optimization algorithm. First, integrating mountainous terrain characteristics with the “electricity-gas-heat-carbon” coordination framework, the scheme leverages the topographical adaptability of gravity storage and the resource recycling advantages of carbon-closed-loop technology to overcome traditional system limitations. Second, considering the fluctuation characteristics of wind and solar predicted output and time-series differences in multi-energy loads under a typical daily deterministic scenario, and carbon emission constraints, an optimization dispatch model is established with the objective of minimizing overall system costs, clarifying the coordinated operation mechanism for multiple devices. Finally, an improved Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm—combining Latin Hypercube Sampling for initialization with particle swarm optimization for local search—solves the model. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach can enhance renewable energy integration rates, reduce system carbon emissions and operational costs. Further comparative simulations under summer and winter typical-day conditions verify the good robustness and engineering applicability of the proposed dispatch strategy under distinct mountain climatic conditions, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for low-carbon, stable, and economical operation of multi-energy systems in mountainous regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimental Study of Woven Glass, Bamboo, and Jute Fibre Reinforced in Epoxy Composites

Title: Photoswitchable pollutant adsorption regulates spin electron transport channels to reversibly switch radical and nonradical peroxymonosulfate oxidation pathways
Abstract: Heterogeneous photo-Fenton-like systems for oxidative degradation of organic pollutants represent a promising sustainable technology for wastewater remediation. However, precisely regulating oxidation pathways to tolerate complex water matrices while maintaining high-efficiency treatment performance remains a critical challenge. Herein, a confined heterojunction was developed to achieve light-responsive switching between radical and electron transfer pathway (ETP)-dominated nonradical PMS activation through reversible control of pollutant adsorption and desorption. Integrated experimental investigations and in situ characterizations revealed that spatial confinement promoted pollutant enrichment and interfacial electron transfer, facilitating the formation of ETP-dominated oxidation under dark conditions. Upon visible-light irradiation, photoinduced electronic redistribution weakened pollutant–catalyst interactions and triggered pollutant desorption, thereby disrupting the ETP route and promoting PMS activation through photoinduced metal redox cycling toward O2•―-mediated radical oxidation. The resulting system exhibited robust degradation performance and operational stability, maintaining over 90% pollutant removal after 900 min of continuous-flow treatment in practical water matrices. This study provides a photo-responsive strategy for dynamically regulating PMS oxidation pathways and reveals the critical role of interfacial adsorption and electron-transfer regulation in selective nonradical oxidation. © 2026

Title: Variable reactive power compensators versus fixed and switchable capacitor banks in providing ancillary services considering voltage fluctuations
Abstract: Voltage fluctuations across distribution network buses can significantly influence both load consumption patterns and the reactive power output of compensation devices. To address these effects, strategic placement of reactive power support equipment is essential. While prior research has extensively examined the positioning of capacitors for loss minimization and voltage enhancement, limited attention has been given to the economic implications of deploying variable reactive power compensators—such as thyristor-switched capacitors (TSCs) or static VAR and static synchronous compensators (SVCs and STATCOMs)—for ancillary service provision under dynamic voltage conditions. Moreover, representative analytical approaches may rely on nonlinear optimization techniques or simplified linear models, creating a tradeoff between model fidelity and computational effort when the sensitivity of reactive power output to voltage variations. Nonlinear approaches can be computationally intensive and difficult to implement. In this paper, a computationally efficient mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) framework is proposed to incorporate voltage fluctuations into the economic evaluation of fixed and switchable capacitors, and variable reactive power devices. The model is solved using commercial linear solvers and enables effective planning of reactive power resources while maintaining computational tractability. Case studies on standard 33- and 69-bus distribution systems declare that the proposed approach improves technical and economic indicators in the investigated cases. In the 33-bus system, variable reactive power compensators reduced total annual cost by 76.3% compared with fixed capacitors while improving the minimum voltage from 0.93 to 0.981 pu and generating annual ancillary service revenues of up to 13,578$. In the 69-bus system, variable reactive sources achieved up to 13.2% greater cost savings and 11.7% higher loss reduction than fixed capacitors. The results further show that voltage-dependent load modeling significantly affects the optimal allocation and sizing of reactive compensation devices, with constant-impedance loading conditions generally yielding the lowest losses and best voltage profiles. Furthermore, the proposed framework obtained high-quality solutions within only a few seconds, demonstrating its computational efficiency. These findings demonstrate, for the investigated systems, the potential technical and economic benefits of integrating voltage-dependent load and reactive power behavior, flexible reactive power resources, and ancillary-service revenues into distribution system planning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Real-time environmental understanding through active classification using tactile sensing in robotic disassembly
Abstract: This paper proposes a generalized active classification framework designed to classify the environment of a robot through controlled tactile interaction, with direct application to robotic disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE). In this domain, purely vision-based systems frequently fail due to occlusions, dust, and reflective surfaces, making haptic identification an operational necessity. By formulating environment identification as an active sensing problem, we utilize the entropy of learned interaction models and a receding-horizon optimization to select control inputs that maximize information gain from force–torque feedback. Our approach transitions from a passive classifier to an active framework that dynamically probes the environment to resolve belief uncertainty across six distinct tactile classes, demonstrated through the high-precision detection and unfastening of screws using an industrial 6-DOF robotic arm. Experimental results on a consumer microwave demonstrate that the active framework achieves a 51% reduction in detection latency for screws compared to passive baselines and consistently outperforms expert-designed heuristics. Furthermore, the system exhibits robust zero-shot generalization to novel industrial objects, indicating that learned tactile signatures are invariant to the global object context. These results provide a scalable foundation for autonomous disassembly in high-variance environments like electronic waste recycling, while offering a broader methodology for any robotic classification task where control can be leveraged to accelerate information gain. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Dynamic modeling, grid synchronization, and power quality analysis of a geothermal ORC power plant using a coupled thermodynamic–Simulink framework
Abstract: This study presents a site-specific coupled thermodynamic–electrical simulation framework for evaluating the grid-integration performance of the Afyon Geothermal Power Plant, a low-temperature geothermal Organic Rankine Cycle facility. The proposed approach combines EES-based thermodynamic property calculations with a dynamic MATLAB/Simulink electrical model, enabling simultaneous assessment of ORC performance, grid synchronization, transient voltage–frequency response, and power-quality behavior. The grid interface is represented by a synchronous generator, transformer, transmission line, RLC load, circuit breaker, measurement blocks, and a Phase-Locked Loop based synchronization unit. The model was parameterized using published operating data from the Afyon plant, including a geothermal fluid temperature of 110 °C, a mass flow rate of 150 kg/s, R134a as the working fluid, and a reported plant capacity of approximately 3 MW. Simulation results show that the system achieves stable synchronization within approximately 0.5 s after breaker closure, with the frequency converging to the nominal 50 Hz value and the voltage/current responses reaching steady-state without sustained oscillations. FFT-based harmonic analysis was performed for both grid-connected and standalone operating conditions. The calculated THD values were 0.49% for grid-connected current, 0.02% for grid-connected voltage, 0.01% for standalone current, and 0.02% for standalone voltage, remaining well below the IEEE 519-based 5% reference limit. The validation and sensitivity results indicate that the net-equivalent power output approaches the reported 3 MW plant capacity, while geothermal temperature and brine-flow variations mainly affect the ORC power output without destabilizing PLL-based synchronization. A simplified techno-economic assessment further shows a unit electricity cost of approximately 0.0233 $/kWh and a simple payback period of about 3.2 years under base Afyon operating conditions. The developed framework provides a reproducible benchmark model for assessing thermodynamic performance, grid compatibility, and power quality in low-temperature geothermal ORC power plants. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Adaptive physics-constrained ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on deep spatio-temporal fusion of multimodal data
Abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation, ultra-short-term power forecasting is crucial for grid dispatch and renewable energy integration. However, the high uncertainty of cloud motion makes conventional data-driven methods with single-source inputs and limited spatio-temporal modeling inadequate for minute-level prediction. This paper proposes a multimodal fusion model with adaptive physical constraints for ultra-short-term PV power forecasting. The model employs a Vision Transformer (ViT) to extract spatial features from ground-based all-sky images, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies in historical power, and the Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT) optical flow algorithm to compute optical flow between two adjacent cloud frames for extracting motion features; a cross-attention module achieves deep fusion of the three modalities. Based on the optical flow field, divergence, acceleration, and boundary constraints are embedded into the loss function, and their weights are adaptively adjusted according to cloud physical indicators, dynamically balancing numerical accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments on a public dataset show that, compared with the best dual-modality model, the proposed method reduces MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 56.8%, 63.4%, and 30.4%, respectively; relative to models without physical constraints, the reductions are 47.9%, 54.9%, and 22.1%. Title: Current amplitude and phase-based adaptive differential protection for distribution networks with unmeasured T-taps
Abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources via T-taps introduces strong source-load fluctuations that often cause maloperations in conventional two-terminal current differential protection. Title: Research on Bi-level cooperative optimization algorithm of wind turbine layout and cable topology in floating offshore wind farm
Abstract: A bi-level cooperative optimization strategy is proposed in order to optimize the location layout of floating offshore wind turbines(FOWT) and the topology of cable path, while considering the system's power generation efficiency and investment costs in this paper. Results show that the optimal number of wind turbines is 150, which achieves the best economic performance. Title: When static Volt–VAr control helps and when it does not: Operational and planning lessons from a weak radial distribution feeder
Abstract: Long radial distribution feeders are increasingly exposed to sustained undervoltage as electrification-driven load growth outpaces reinforcement. This paper evaluates the operational and planning value of feeder-specific static Volt–VAr settings under data conditions commonly available to distribution system operators: sparse voltage measurements, hourly feeder-level inputs, and offline parameter updates. The study applies the slope-selection procedure developed in [1] to a predefined BESS Volt–VAr curve and evaluates the resulting setting through quasi-static time-series power flow for a real 22 kV radial feeder in Northern Norway. During the constructed 168 h high-load/no-generation stress period, the model-based, condition-matched comparison produced 153 h within the adopted target band with the full feeder-specific setting, compared with 8 h under the IEEE 1547-type setting and 1 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. An independent 2025 operating period was used for quantitative comparison with field measurements. The model reproduced the average voltage and voltage-band occupancy, while the disagreement in hourly variation limits its use to comparative screening rather than point-by-point prediction. The transferred feeder-specific setting produced 0 h outside the target band, compared with 16 h under the IEEE-type curve and 55 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. Higher-resolution measurements from the BESS and hydropower plant were used separately to examine interaction between the two local controllers. Under the 59% industrial-growth stress scenario, 4 MVAr was the smallest tested reactive-power rating that kept all 168 hourly voltages at or above the lower limit of the adopted target band after feeder-specific slope selection. Title: An embedded fault detection method for wind farm collector lines using adaptive statistical thresholding
Abstract: In recent years, energy transition has boosted the expansion of new electrical generation sources, most of which are inverter-based, significantly altering the behavior of voltage and current signals. Title: PC-TD3-based multi-objective adaptive dispatch method for microgrids guided by a meta-policy
Abstract: To address the dynamic multi-objective trade-off between economic performance and system safety in microgrid operation, this study proposes a meta-policy-guided PC-TD3-based adaptive multi-objective scheduling method for microgrids. The method uses a high-level meta-policy network to generate scheduling preferences online, while a lower-level preference-conditioned TD3 policy is trained over the full preference space so that a single model can approximate continuous economy-safety trade-offs. A two-layer safety projection mechanism is further introduced to embed local battery constraints and global voltage constraints into action execution. Long-horizon simulations based on real-world data show that PC-TD3 achieves the lowest average daily operating cost among the compared methods, at 111,405 CNY, and the lowest average number of voltage violations, at 22.1 counts/day. Across 100 test days, the cumulative economic benefit of PC-TD3 relative to the average baseline reaches approximately 0.56 million CNY. Title: The π-orbital axis vector-gated peroxymonosulfate activation: Switching from O-O bond cleavage to nonradical pathway
Abstract: Although peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation is commonly divided into radical and nonradical routes, controllably switching between these pathways by catalyst design remains challenging. Here, we show that surface curvature, quantified by π-orbital axis vector (POAV) analysis, can regulate PMS activation in a Co-cluster/Mn-N₄ porous carbon catalyst. With polystyrene spheres as sacrificial templates, Co clusters and Mn-N₄ single-atom sites are anchored on a curved N-doped carbon framework. POAV analysis shows that increasing curvature enhances local carbon pyramidalization and π-σ rehybridization, which in turn modulates the local ligand field and d-orbital splitting of the metal sites during the PMS adsorption and activation. This geometry-driven electronic regulation changes the role of the two metal centers: planar carbon favors PMS adsorption and O-O bond cleavage at Co-clusters, leading to radical generation, whereas curved carbon shifts PMS activation to Mn-N₄ sites as PMS*, and promotes nonradical electron transfer. Beyond pathway control, the 3D curved porous framework also improves solar absorption and heat confinement, enabling photo-accelerated oxidation and interfacial evaporation. Authors: Xu P.; Li Z.; Lei L.; He C.; Guan W.; He S.
Title: Dynamic performance enhancement of a three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC using adaptive disturbance compensation
Abstract: Offshore wind energy is emerging as a critical renewable energy source. For the three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC considered in this study, load variations, input-voltage fluctuations, and modeling uncertainties may degrade output-voltage regulation performance. To improve the transient response and disturbance-rejection capability of the converter, a backstepping dynamic surface control strategy assisted by a Zernike neural-network-based adaptive compensator is proposed. First, a state-space model of the three-phase interleaved parallel MMC boost converter is established. Then, the Zernike neural network is employed to adaptively approximate the unknown load-dependent term in the output-voltage dynamics and generate an online compensation signal. with a compact basis-function structure compared with the conventional RBF neural network used for comparison. Meanwhile, DSC is incorporated into the backstepping framework to avoid the derivative explosion problem and reduce implementation complexity. Lyapunov analysis proves that all closed-loop signals are bounded and the tracking error is semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. The inherent low-ripple and self-balancing characteristics of the topology are validated before the dynamic control performance is investigated. The proposed method achieves smaller overshoot and requires less execution time than the RBF-NN-assisted ABDSC under the adopted implementation settings. Therefore, the proposed strategy provides a preliminary methodological reference for improving the dynamic performance of MMC-based converters, with potential relevance to future offshore wind power HVDC applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: FCGNet: A fractional- condition-aware gated network for wind power forecasting
Abstract: Wind power forecasting is challenging due to the pronounced nonstationarity, multi-scale coupling, and abrupt fluctuations of wind power time series under complex meteorological conditions. Existing forecasting methods either lack explicit modeling of temporal structures or have limited ability to adaptively integrate heterogeneous dynamic features. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Fractional-Condition-Aware Gated Network (FCGNet) for wind power forecasting. The framework consists of three stages: adaptive input reconstruction, heterogeneous temporal modeling, and collaborative feature fusion. First, an Adaptive Feature Gating module is employed to enhance multivariate input representations through global importance recalibration and local perturbation correction. Then, a Fractional-Order BiGRU branch is introduced to model long-range dependencies via power-law memory accumulation, while a condition-aware PatchTST branch captures operating-condition-dependent multi-scale patterns through physically guided scale weighting. Finally, a cross-branch attention fusion module is designed to achieve dynamic interaction and adaptive integration of the two heterogeneous representations. For a 12 h-ahead forecasting task, Experimental results on two real-world wind power datasets show that FCGNet achieves superior forecasting performance compared with representative baseline models and exhibits strong robustness across different data distributions and wind conditions. The proposed method provides an effective and interpretable solution for high-precision wind power forecasting in renewable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Saha K.; Kumar N.
Title: Mixed-Discrete optimization of spacer configuration for Short-Circuit force reduction in EHV bundled conductors
Abstract: Short-circuit events in extra-high-voltage (EHV) air-insulated substations produce strong electrodynamic forces on flexible bundled conductors, resulting in high tensile stress, pinch interaction between sub-conductors, conductor swing, and possible reduction in phase-to-phase clearance. In such cases, the system's reaction depends on spacer span, spacer mass, and bundle spacing, determining the system's equivalent mass and dynamic behavior. In this study, the governing force is defined as the maximum value among the tensile, drop, and pinch forces, which must be minimized while satisfying mechanical and clearance constraints. Given the discrete nature of design variables, this is a nonlinear and mixed-discrete optimization problem. The resulting problem is formulated as a nonlinear, constrained, mixed-discrete optimization problem in which spacer span, spacer mass, and bundle spacing are optimized simultaneously. A hybrid CSS-EM solver is adopted as the computational optimizer for the proposed mixed-discrete formulation. The main novelty of the work lies in the spacer-configuration optimization formulation rather than in the development of a new metaheuristic algorithm. A practical 220 kV case study shows the existence of a complex and nonlinear design space with transition zones where the governing force mechanism changes. Existing standards such as IEC 60865 and IEEE Std. 605 provide procedures for short-circuit-force calculation; however, they do not explicitly consider spacer-configuration optimization. The proposed methodology addresses this design gap. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Korejo S.N.; Wang S.
Title: A hierarchical hybrid control framework for networked microgrids: Integrating primary droop, distributed consensus, and economic dispatch
Abstract: The integration of multiple interconnected microgrids presents significant challenges in maintaining stability, ensuring power quality, and optimizing economic operation. This paper presents a comprehensive hierarchical hybrid control framework that coordinates primary, secondary, and tertiary control layers to address these challenges systematically. The proposed architecture employs decentralized droop control for immediate power sharing, distributed consensus algorithms for voltage and frequency restoration, and economic dispatch optimization for cost-effective operation. This study developed a complete mathematical formulation and implemented a detailed simulation environment in Python to validate the framework's performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains frequency within ±0.5 Hz of nominal values during steady-state operation and within ±0.5 Hz during islanding transitions, achieves proportional power sharing with less than 5% deviation from ideal ratios, and reduces operational costs by 23.7% compared to conventional decentralized control strategies. The framework's scalability is verified through small-signal stability analysis, showing all non-zero eigenvalues with negative real parts and a minimum damping ratio of 0.12 across various network configurations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
