Title: K+-driven interfacial water reconstruction via charge-enriched heterointerfaces for accelerated alkaline hydrogen evolution
Abstract: The sluggish water dissociation kinetics in alkaline media remains a major bottleneck for efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Beyond intrinsic active sites, the interfacial microenvironment, particularly local charge distribution and water structure, plays a decisive role in governing reaction pathways. Herein, we report a two-dimensional Cu-modified RuOx catalyst containing carbonaceous components (denoted as Cu-RuOx/C), featuring crystalline-amorphous heterointerfaces that create charge-enriched interfacial regions for regulating the interfacial water network. Cu incorporation generates a charge-enriched surface that promotes the accumulation of K+ near the catalyst interface, thereby reconstructing the interfacial hydrogen-bond network. This regulation shortens the K+-surface distance and weakens hydrogen-bond connectivity within interfacial water, leading to a decreased fraction of tetracoordinate hydrogen-bonded water and an increased proportion of free water. Such an optimized interfacial water structure ensures sufficient proton supply during the HER process. As a result, Cu-RuOx/C delivers an ultralow overpotential of 13 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and sustains 800 h of operation at 1000 mA cm−2 in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer. This work demonstrates highly dispersed Cu modulation as an effective strategy for engineering catalytic microenvironments to enhance alkaline HER. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Learning fuzzy normal-operation regimes for interpretable power system anomaly detection
Abstract: This paper presents an interpretable one-class anomaly detection framework for power systems based on adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS). The proposed method is trained exclusively on benign operational data and learns a compact set of fuzzy regimes describing normal cyber-physical behavior. The learned regimes are used to define rule-local invariant bounds and regularized Gaussian compatibility models. A fuzzy rule-weighted Mahalanobis score then measures the compatibility of each new observation with the activated benign regimes. Unlike supervised detectors, the proposed method requires no fault or attack samples during training and evaluates anomalous observations through deviations from learned normal operation. The framework is evaluated on the Mississippi State University and Oak Ridge National Laboratory Power System Attack Dataset, which contains benign operation, natural faults, and cyberattacks. The proposed detector achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.9773, a PR-AUC of 0.9998, precision of 0.9994, recall of 0.9265, specificity of 0.9138, and an F1-score of 0.9616. In addition to anomaly detection, the framework provides rule and feature-level explanations by identifying the activated fuzzy regime, the measurements contributing most strongly to the anomaly score, and any violated invariant conditions. Title: Segmented variable impedance controller with trajectory adaptive adjustment for robotic polishing tasks
Abstract: In robot contact force control, adaptive variable impedance control reduces force tracking error compared to constant impedance control, but there is a collision between the end effector and the environment, resulting in overshoot of the contact force. To reduce contact-force overshoot and further improve force-tracking accuracy, an adaptive reference trajectory-based adaptive variable impedance control (ART-AVIC) method is proposed. The controller’s reference trajectory is adjusted in real time based on the magnitude of the force error. Meanwhile, the damping parameters are updated in a segmented manner according to the contact force error in contact stage. This approach effectively reduces the system’s steady-state error and significantly reduces overshoot and settling time during robotic polishing. In the simulations that account for environmental changes, desired force variations, and practical factors, the ART-AVIC method exhibits better overall performance. In curved surface polishing experiments, compared with other control methods, ART-AVIC reduces the contact-force overshoot by 13.61%-54.93% and the steady-state contact-force RMSE by 11.11%-61.90%. In addition, polishing experiments on blade and cage have demonstrated the potential of the ART-AVIC method for industrial applications. Simulations and experiments validate that the ART-AVIC method performs better and is suitable for robotic polishing tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Thermal Behaviour and Coupling Effects in Laminated Composite Beam Structures Using Refined Shear Deformation Theory
Abstract: This study investigates the thermoelastic behaviour of laminated composite beams with symmetric (0/90/0) and asymmetric (0/90) layer-ups subjected to sinusoidally distributed thermal line loads. A quasi-3D shear deformation theory incorporating parabolic and trigonometric through-thickness functions based on Reddy’s refined model forms the core analytical framework. The governing equations are derived from the principle of virtual work and solved in closed form via a Navier-type series. The classical beam theory and first-order shear deformation theory are employed solely for comparative analysis. The thermal line load model, representing realistic non-uniform heating scenarios, enables assessments of coupling effects due to laminate asymmetry. Results reveal that asymmetric configurations exhibit significant thermal coupling leading to higher displacements and stress concentrations, while symmetric laminated beams offer improved thermal stability. Title: A single-ended fault location method based on active boundary control for multi-terminal flexible DC grids
Abstract: In modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based multi-terminal flexible DC (MTDC) grids, fault current limiting suppresses post-fault electrical transients and weakens available fault characteristics, thereby reducing the sensitivity and reliability of conventional fault location methods. To address this issue, this paper proposes a single-ended fault location method based on active control and boundary self-validation. First, a coordinated MMC control framework integrating fault current limiting and characteristic-frequency signal injection is developed to construct controllable electrical features after fault occurrence. Then, an active boundary control strategy is proposed at the converter where fault model selection is required. By coordinating with a local directional criterion, different terminal responses are constructed for different fault regions, enabling invalid location results caused by incorrect fault model selection to be rejected. On this basis, frequency-domain fault location models are established for both pole-to-ground (PTG) and pole-to-pole (PTP) faults, with detailed discussion on parameter selection. The fault distance and transition resistance are identified through multi-frequency residual minimization, after which the relative residual variation is used to validate the location result and determine the final fault distance. Simulation results on a three terminal flexible DC system demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately locate PTG and PTP faults on different line sections under various fault distances and transition resistances, with fault location errors below 1%. The proposed method enables single-ended fault location without inter-station communication and can potentially serve as a backup protection function, thereby facilitating faster post-fault restoration in MTDC grids. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Parameter determination method for model of ZnO varistors based on dynamic V-I characteristics
Abstract: This study investigates the dynamic volt-ampere characteristics and residual voltage responses of ZnO varistor of five different sizes under various impulse waveforms, including 8/20 μs lightning current, 30/80 μs operating wave, 1/5 μs steep wave, and 2 ms square wave impulses. To address this, the circuit structure and nonlinear resistance parameters in the IEEE model were revised based on experimental dynamic volt-ampere data. Title: Reconstruction-driven bifunctional electrocatalysis over CeO2@Ni3S2 heterostructures: Boosting biomass and OH– adsorption for efficient HMFOR
Abstract: Anodic value-added chemical production paired with cathodic H2 evolution is highly practically valuable. Title: Steering CO2 electroreduction selectivity: Pulse-induced switching between C2H4 and CH4 over Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6 pre-catalyst
Abstract: Manipulating competitive reaction pathways to obtain target hydrocarbons from electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) holds promise yet is still challenging. While pulsed electrolysis has been widely employed to tune CO2RR selectivity on Cu catalysts, the role of the pre‑catalyst structure in pulsed CO2RR has remained largely unexplored. Herein, we achieve switchable CO2 electroreduction between C2H4 and CH4 by coupling a customized pulsed potential protocol with a rose‑like Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6 pre‑catalyst. Its distinctive layered structure enables a rapid reconstruction within the first pulse cycle, generating a defect‑rich, derived Cu active phase that is highly responsive to pulsed potential tuning. Pulse parameter screening reveals that the anodic potential is the primary factor governing the selectivity switch for Cu4(NO3)2(OH)6-derived Cu. The two optimized pulsed protocols, differing primarily in the anodic potential, establish two distinct near‑surface oxidation states on the derived Cu: a Cu0/Cu+‑enriched region that favors C–C coupling to C2H4, and a Cu+/Cu2+‑enriched region that promotes *CO hydrogenation to CH4. This strategy thus delivers a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 52.5% for C2H4 and 43.05% for CH4. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations further elucidate that the near-surface oxidation state determines *CO coverage and the subsequent reaction pathway branching. Title: Spatiotemporal distribution and statistical characteristics of lightning activity before and after the construction of 345 m UHV large-span transmission towers based on LLS Data
Abstract: Ultra-high-voltage (UHV) large-span transmission towers are characterized by large structural height, long span length, and complex overhead ground-wire systems. Their construction may affect the local distribution of lightning flash locations and the statistical characteristics of lightning current parameters. In this study, two UHV large-span towers, N6750 and N6751, in the Chizhou–Tongling section were selected as the case study. Based on Lightning Location System (LLS) data from 2004 to 2025, a statistical framework including spatial filtering, kernel density estimation, trend testing, and distribution difference testing was established. The lightning stroke distribution, lightning frequency, current amplitude, and polarity before and after tower construction were compared. The results show that lightning flash density was redistributed after tower construction, with a decrease in the middle region of the crossing span and an increase near the two tower bodies. This suggests that the ultra-tall towers and their overhead ground-wire system may have modified the local lightning attachment pattern. The LLS-estimated current distribution also shifted toward higher amplitudes: the mean current amplitude of negative cloud-to-ground flashes increased from 20.4 kA to 38.0 kA, and the proportion of high-current events increased. In addition, more positive lightning records were observed after tower construction. These findings provide observational support for lightning performance assessment, grounding-system thermal stability evaluation, and differentiated operation and maintenance of UHV large-span transmission lines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Grid-connected solar photovoltaic-supported dynamic voltage restoration for enhanced voltage stability and power quality
Abstract: Grid-connected PV systems are important in modern power systems as they enhance voltage stability, improve power quality (PQ), and support renewable energy integration under varying solar generation conditions. However, optimizing voltage restorers remains challenging due to reactive power compensation requirements, system stability issues during PV variations, and diverse grid conditions and load profiles. To overcome this problem, this work proposes a grid-connected solar photovoltaic fed quasi-impedance source driven dynamic voltage restorer employing optimized switching strategy for enhanced voltage gain and power quality. The proposed technique is the joint execution of both House Swallow Optimizer (HSO) and Skeleton guided convolutional neural network (SGCNN) and is commonly referred as HSO- SGCNN method. The main objective of the proposed technique is to reduce the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and enhance power output quality. The proposed HSO is utilized to optimize THD performance and SGCNN is used for maximizing the power of PV. The proposed technique is simulated in MATLAB and its performance is compared with various existing techniques includes Multi-Objective Bees Algorithm (MOBA), Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA). The proposed control and HSO-SGCNN achieve the better performance, with voltage gain exceeding MOBA 16, GA 12, and BOA 9 at modulation index 0.5, reaching over 15 at M = 1, voltage stress reducing to 1.1 pu, and THD minimized to 4 % compared to 8–10 %, ensuring maximum stability analysed to other existing techniques. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Elucidating the contributions of alginate and fucoidan to algal cell wall structure and rheology using bacterial cellulose gels
Abstract: Bacterial cellulose gels (BC) containing alginate or fucoidan were developed to investigate cellulose-algal polysaccharide interactions and, their impact on gel structure, mechanics, rheology and processing stability. Title: Adaptive trajectory unified framework for stressed AC optimal power flow
Abstract: Stressed AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) often exposes a difficult start bottleneck in which, from poor starts, the algorithm must reduce large power balance residuals and active operating limit violations before cost optimization becomes meaningful. This paper proposes the Adaptive Trajectory Unified Framework (ATJU), a residual shaped trajectory homotopy for stressed ACOPF. Title: Experimental Investigation and RSM-Based Optimization of Phenolic/PTFE/SiC Composites
Abstract: Resole phenolic resin, valued for its excellent heat resistance, strong adhesion, and chemical stability, has long been utilized in aerospace, automotive, and protective material applications. However, its relatively low toughness and brittleness limit broader use. In this study, the thermal and mechanical characteristics of phenolic composites were improved by incorporating Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) powder, Silicon carbide (SiC) particles, carbon, and high-silica fibers. A D-optimal response surface methodology (RSM) design was employed to evaluate the effects of fiber type, curing temperature, and particle loading. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed that the addition of reinforcing particles altered fracture morphology by promoting crack deflection and improving resin–fiber interaction. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) results confirmed a 7% increase in glass transition temperature (Tg) with 10% particle loading, indicating enhanced thermal stability. Mechanical testing demonstrated that the addition of 10 wt% reinforcing particles enhanced both tensile and flexural properties, regardless of the fiber type; however, the fiber type itself had a significant influence on performance. Carbon fiber composites achieved the highest tensile strength (264.8 MPa), which was 13% above hybrid laminates (235.2 MPa) and 185% above high-silica composites (93.0 MPa). Conversely, hybrid laminates exhibited the best flexural strength (219.9 MPa), exceeding carbon by 72% and high-silica by 150%. Quantitative ANOVA validation confirmed the reliability of the developed models for both tensile and flexural strength. Title: A study on the mechanism of arc fault branch localization based on load response characteristics
Abstract: Accurate localization of arc fault is a prerequisite for effective mitigation of electrical fire hazards; however, the underlying physical mechanisms that affect precise localization remain unclear. This paper systematically investigates the influence of load type, power level, and arc fault incandescence intensity on the intrinsic electrical and physical processes, by integrating experimental data with a mathematical model of arc fault current. First, empirical measurements are used to identify both commonalities and differences in arc fault responses across various load types. Subsequently, a coupling model—termed the dispersion relation—is established between load current loss ratio and arc fault characteristics based on the mathematical representation of fault current signals. This model systematically characterizes the interrelationship between arc fault features and load properties under varying degrees of incandescence, thereby revealing the fundamental mechanism of arc fault branch localization. Furthermore, it elucidates the root causes of response ambiguity under interference from homogeneous loads and proposes a technical pathway for resolution. The findings of this study provide theoretical foundations and directional guidance for developing future branch localization models for arc faults based on load response characteristics. © 2026

Title: Tandem catalysis of Al-rich Cu/FAU-EMT intergrowth zeolites for boosting the selective catalytic reduction of NOx with ammonia
Abstract: Different topological ratios of Al-rich FAU-EMT intergrowth zeolites were synthesized via one-pot hydrothermal method with double templates. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Cs-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) coupled with an annular dark field (ADF) images jointly confirmed the presence of twinned FAU-EMT interfaces. 29Si magic angle spinning (MAS) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) revealed the FAU-EMT zeolites have excellent skeleton crystallinity, along with more pronounced SBET compared to sole-phase zeolites. In particular, the Cu/FAU-EMT-50% showed the surprising low-temperature activity, achieving nearly complete NO conversion across wide-temperature window (150–550 °C). Series of copper species characterization demonstrated the highly active [Cu(OH)]+ ions are primarily active sites over Cu/FAU-EMT, and no significant distribution of less active copper species has been detected. In addition, the [Cu(OH)]+ ions on FAU-EMT interface have an appropriate d-band center, which are conducive to both ammonia adsorption and intermediate species activation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that the EMT phase is more conducive to the adsorption of sufficient NH3, which then carries the reactive [Cu(OH)(NH3)3]+ species to migrate locally to the FAU phase, where SCR reactions are favored, thereby achieving synergistic effects at twinned FAU-EMT interfaces. Title: Critical review on hybrid models for state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries in wide temperatures
Abstract: This paper systematically reviews state of charge (SOC) estimation methods for lithium-ion batteries, with a focus on wide-temperature-range and low-temperature applications. Authors: Xiang R.; Lin X.; Ma X.; Wang J.
Title: Numerical investigations of electromagnetic time reversal for locating partial discharge in power transformers using a stable discontinuous Galerkin time-domain method
Abstract: The localization of partial discharge (PD) inducing ultra-high frequency (UHF) electromagnetic radiation is crucial for the safety of power transformers. Compared with conventional localization techniques based on the time difference of arrival (TDOA) of UHF signals, the emerging electromagnetic time reversal (EMTR) methods are less sensitive to noise and more accurate under the complex geometry of transformers, hence are promising alternatives. However, the postprocessing of UHF signals in TDOA-based methods is straightforward, yet in EMTR framework, the counterpart is transient electromagnetic analysis with heavy computational overheads. In this paper, a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) solver with novel time integration schemes is proposed to overcome the efficiency bottleneck. The essence is that the lossy terms in governing equations are discretized via implicit Crank–Nicolson (CN) method, while the remaining terms are integrated by explicit Runge–Kutta (RK) methods, so that the impact of the conductive media in transformers on the time-step size vanishes without spoiling the favorable explicit nature of the classic DGTD method. The performance of the EMTR method using the proposed CN–RK-DGTD solver is demonstrated in the PD localization in a three-phase transformer, and the influences of the position and number of UHF sensors, PD locations, noise, etc., are further investigated numerically. Subsequently, the feasibility of the proposed EMTR-based method for locating PD in an actual complex transformer is verified experimentally. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A regional partition-aided multi-task prediction framework for substation flooding and secondary disasters based on improved Transformer
Abstract: Frequent extreme rainstorms have seriously threatened the safe operation of substations, causing enormous economic losses. Accurate prediction of substation flood depth and the resulting equipment damage and outage risks is crucial for enhancing disaster resilience. Traditional models face great challenges due to strong spatial correlations among substations, multi-scale temporal dependencies, heterogeneous data types, and data imbalance. To address these limitations, the proposed substation multiple flooding risks Transformer (SMFR-Former) adopts an integrated design that simultaneously couples regional spatial partitioning, dynamic-static heterogeneous representation, and train loss-balancing mechanism within a unified architecture for the joint prediction of the three risks.A regional partitioning strategy is introduced to characterize latent spatial correlations among substations, while adaptive temporal encoding strengthens the extraction of complex temporal dependencies. To achieve effective heterogeneous data fusion, distinct encoders are designed for different data modalities, and adaptive weighting is employed to dynamically optimize feature integration. Furthermore, a dynamic train loss-balancing mechanism is developed to alleviate inter-task optimization conflicts during multi-task learning. The experimental results show that each strategy is effective and compatible with each other. SMFR-Former outperforms Transformer model, reducing the RMSE of flood depth and equipment damage degree prediction by 30.00% and 26.94%, respectively, while improving the F1 score of outage probability prediction by 18.31%. Furthermore,cross-regional validation results demonstrate that the proposed SMFR-Former maintains strong generalization capability under different spatial distributions and regional characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Single-ended fault location method for multi-terminal overhead-cable hybrid transmission line using alternating search algorithm
Abstract: With rapid urbanization and power grid expansion, multi-terminal overhead-cable hybrid transmission lines have been increasingly utilized. However, the significant differences between overhead lines and cables, combined with the complexity of multi-terminal structures, lead to complicated refraction and reflection of travelling waves (TWs). Therefore, conventional single-ended TW-based fault location methods, which rely on accurate identification of reflected waves and a high sampling frequency in the MHz range, are not suitable. To address this issue, the paper proposes an enhanced TW-based fault location method based on waveform similarity. First, this method incorporates a frequency-dependent multi-terminal hybrid transmission line analytical model to reproduce fault transient voltage waveforms. On this basis, dynamic time warping and normalized mean square error collaborative similarity metrics are established to evaluate calculated and actual fault transient waveform characteristics, and the sensitivity analysis of the similarity metrics shows that there is a coupling relationship among the fault variables. Then, a variable-step, dual-metric alternating search algorithm is proposed to accurately identify fault variables (e.g., fault inception angle, fault resistance, and fault distance). Title: Temperature gradient-dependent space charge accumulation and electric field distribution in bi-layer cable-accessory insulation
Abstract: Space charge preferentially accumulates at bi-layer insulation interface in high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) cable accessories, rendering this region particularly susceptible to insulation degradation. During cable operation, the bi-layer cable-accessory insulation is inevitably subjected to a temperature gradient (TG) superimposed on DC voltage, yet how TG affects space charge dynamics in the cable-accessory insulation remains insufficiently elucidated. Space charge distributions in cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE)/silicone rubber (SR) bi-layer dielectrics subjected to TG are characterized via the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) technique. An expanded charge transport model incorporating surface states, impurity ions, and field- and temperature-dependent conductivity is proposed to simulate the charge behavior in the bi-layer dielectrics under TG. The simulations reproduce the principal characteristics of the measured distributions and their variation trends with increasing TG. The results demonstrate that homocharge emerges and progressively intensifies in the vicinity of the high-temperature anode, while heterocharge in the vicinity of the low-temperature cathode continuously accumulates as TG is elevated. The XLPE/SR interface charge density initially increases and subsequently decreases as TG increases. The maximum electric field invariably resides within the high-temperature XLPE adjacent to the XLPE/SR interface. The field distortion is further intensified as TG rises, with the maximum field strength increasing by 20.2% and 28.6% at TG of 15 °C and 35 °C, respectively, and the position of the maximum field strength shifting progressively towards the XLPE/SR interface. These findings provide practical guidance for space charge regulation and insulation design optimization of HVDC cable accessories. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Diffusion characteristics of SF6 decomposition products in typical structural units of 500 kV GIL equipment
Abstract: Partial discharge (PD) induced by insulation defects in gas-insulated transmission lines (GILs) during operation can lead to SF6 decomposition and generate a series of characteristic gases, whose diffusion behavior directly affects the effectiveness of equipment fault detection and early warning. This paper investigates the diffusion characteristics of H2S, SO2, and CF4 in linear GILs under continuous and transient fault conditions. The results indicate that H2S diffuses the fastest and provides the most sensitive warning response. Under continuous fault conditions, the diffusion effect is mainly manifested as an increased warning delay, whereas under transient fault conditions, it is mainly reflected in enhanced concentration attenuation. Compared with the point at x = 1 m, the maximum SO2 concentration at x = 49 m decreases by approximately 99.4%. The initial inlet concentration not only affects the fault warning delay but also determines the spatial range over which an alarm can be triggered. Larger equipment configurations increase the risk that characteristic gases may fail to trigger alarms effectively in the later stage of a fault. In practical detection, concentration thresholds should be dynamically optimized according to equipment dimensions. Gases with larger diffusion coefficients and higher concentrations, such as SO2, should be utilized as early warning gases, while incorporating other characteristic fault gases to improve fault discrimination accuracy. The results provide a theoretical reference for optimizing characteristic gas detection and fault early-warning strategies in GILs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Real-time adaptive DC bus voltage control using Jellyfish search algorithm for SAPFs under dynamic operating conditions
Abstract: Electrical networks are often subjected to various operational disturbances, among which load variation plays a major role in increasing harmonic distortion and current waveform deformation. Conventional power quality improvement techniques generally depend on simplified mathematical models and fixed parameters, which makes them less effective when the system operates under dynamic conditions. The proposed control strategy was implemented and experimentally tested against several conventional methods under both steady and dynamic operation conditions using a dedicated test bench. The experimental results demonstrated a noticeable improvement in harmonics mitigation. The proposed control achieved a Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of 2.7 % in steady state. Even applying high load variation, the THD keeps low values with acceptable transients whereas the traditional methods lead to poor power quality. Such experimental evidence demonstrates the capability of the JSA-based approach to adaptively regulate the Vdc* in real time while ensuring that the SAPF performance remains within the harmonic distortion limits defined by IEEE Standard 519–2022. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Open-circuit fault diagnosis method for grid-connected inverters based on endogenous disturbance
Abstract: To address the issues of indistinct residual signal features and detection speeds that are susceptible to load fluctuations in the open-circuit fault diagnosis of grid-connected inverter power switches, this paper proposes an open-circuit fault diagnosis method based on endogenous disturbance observation. First, an improved observer is constructed by introducing the Super-Twisting Algorithm (STA) combined with a hyperbolic tangent function. Through the design of a smooth control law, traditional sliding mode chattering is eliminated, and state tracking accuracy is enhanced. Second, an endogenous disturbance feature extraction method centered on endogenous control gains is proposed. By capturing the compensation amount generated within the observer to bridge the "energy gap" caused by the fault, the fault features are sensitively reinforced. This effectively resolves the problem of indistinct mutations in traditional current residuals. Finally, by utilizing the spatial distribution characteristics of fault vectors in the complex plane, a highly robust fault localization criterion is established using vector dot product operations and adaptive threshold logic. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses interference caused by grid power fluctuations. It achieves accurate identification of switch open-circuit faults under various operating conditions, offering the advantages of rapid diagnosis speed, low computational overhead, and no requirement for additional sensors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Complete selectivity switching between CO and CH4 for CO2 photoreduction on Pd-SrTiO3 nanocrystals
Abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) photoreduction to methane (CH4) encounters low selectivity. Herein, we designed Pd nanoparticle-loaded semiconductor oxides nanocrystals, in which Pd not only facilitates water dissociation to generate protons, but also enables the construction of interfacial dual sites for bridge-mode adsorption of reaction intermediates. Hence, the Pd-SrTiO3 nanocrystals achieved nearly 100% selectivity toward CH4, whereas the SrTiO3 nanocrystals only produced CO. Title: Phase-engineered manganese dioxide for decoupling oxygen reduction and ammonia poisoning in direct ammonia fuel cells
Abstract: The inevitable crossover of ammonia from the anode to the cathode in direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs) severely poisons conventional platinum cathodes, fundamentally necessitating the development of resilient alternatives. Title: Steric hindrance engineered through-space conjugation for the emission wavelength control of organic room-temperature phosphorescence

Abstract: Owing to the structural diversity and excellent biocompatibility, single component organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have intrigued considerable interest in the past two decades. As the steric hindrance increased, the rotation of the two benzene rings was restricted, thereby rigidifying the molecular skeletons and effectively promoting TSC. Title: Enhancing the foaming properties of spirulina biomass via microfluidization and enzymatic polysaccharide hydrolysis for egg white substitution in cakes
Abstract: This study utilized high-pressure microfluidization (HPM) coupled with enzymatic polysaccharide hydrolysis to enhance the foaming properties of spirulina biomass for partial egg white replacement in cakes. HPM disrupted cell walls, releasing intracellular proteins that promote the formation of fine, uniform bubbles. Compared with untreated spirulina, HPM treatment reduced surface tension and contact angle by 6.46% and 13.86%, respectively, and increased foaming capacity by 42.86%. Proteins were identified as the key foaming-active substances in the HPM-treated spirulina supernatant, and low polysaccharide concentrations (≤30%) facilitated foam stability. However, the polysaccharide components in HPM-treated spirulina suppressed foaming through a viscosity-enhancing effect, limiting the egg white substitution ratio to ≤25%. Pectinase (PE) treatment reduced the viscosity from 10.20 to 3.65 mPa s and increased the substitution ratio to 50%. Compared with HPM alone, the HPM-PE treatment further enhanced foaming capacity by 41.24%, decreased batter specific gravity by 26.15%, and improved cake specific volume by 24.71%. The spirulina-substituted cake possessed superior nutritional value and a distinctive aroma contributed to 11 key volatiles, including (E)-β-ionone, nonanal, (E, E)-2,4-nonadienal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 2-pentylfuran. These results suggest that HPM-PE treatment markedly enhances the egg-white replacement capacity of spirulina biomass-derived fraction, providing a scientific basis for sustainable plant-based food development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Structural and causal knowledge-guided defect detection for transmission-line suspension clamps and anti-vibration dampers
Abstract: To address small inter-class differences, large intra-class variations, and co-occurring defects in UAV inspection images of transmission-line suspension clamps and anti-vibration dampers, this paper proposes a defect detection framework guided by structural and causal knowledge. The framework features three core components. First, a Structural Knowledge Module (SKM) combines deformable convolution and symmetry-aware feature modeling to enhance structure-sensitive feature representation of geometric variations and structural anomalies. Second, a Causal Knowledge Loss (CKL) incorporates a causal matrix constructed from fitting-instance-level defect co-occurrence statistics into the classification loss. Third, an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism performs channel-wise feature recalibration to emphasize defect-related features and suppress background interference. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves the highest detection accuracy among the compared detectors, with an mAP50 of 81.7%, representing a 6.0-percentage-point improvement over the YOLOv11 baseline. The model contains 10.8M parameters, has a computational complexity of 37.2 GFLOPs, and achieves an inference speed of 73.1 FPS. These results indicate that the proposed framework achieves a favorable balance between detection accuracy and inference efficiency for suspension-clamp and anti-vibration-damper defect detection. © 2026

Title: Enhancing robotic interoperability: An approach for ROS 2-driven system integration
Abstract: Reconfigurable manufacturing requires robotic workcells that can adapt to changing products, processes, and equipment without extensive redesign or manual reprogramming. Product, process, and equipment information is formalised through UML domain models and serialised in AutomationML(AML), enabling automated correspondence between assembly requirements, available skills, and executable recipes. The framework integrates automated programme generation, reinforcement learning based recipe optimisation, and a modular CAD informed six degree of freedom perception layer to support both technical and semantic interoperability across simulated and physical workcells. The approach is evaluated through Cube Kitting and Cylinder Stacking use cases implemented on distinct robotic platforms, including ABB and Universal Robots systems. Experimental results show high reliability, with environment launch performance reaching up to 99.93%, standard skill sequences achieving 100% execution success, and full use case trials exceeding 97% success in simulation and reaching 100% on physical hardware. Title: Enhancement of chitosan coating properties by carrier-free self-assembled coptisine-cinnamic acid nanoparticles and their application in cherry tomato preservation
Abstract: Chitosan is an important hydrocolloid for edible films; however, its strong water affinity, swelling tendency, and limited moisture-barrier capacity restrict its application in high-humidity food storage. In this study, we synthesized carrier-free coptisine–cinnamic acid nanoassemblies (COP–CA NPs) and incorporated them as active nanofillers into chitosan coatings. The optimized nanoparticles had an average particle size of 55.09 nm, a PDI of 0.205, and a relatively narrow particle size distribution, while retaining good in vitro free radical scavenging and antibacterial activities. Strong antibacterial functionality was also maintained after incorporation into the CS matrix. The incorporation of COP–CA NPs reduced the water wettability, water solubility, and swelling degree of the chitosan film, while simultaneously enhancing its moisture barrier properties and mechanical strength. The water vapor permeability of the 0.20% composite coating film (0.20% CS@NPs) decreased by 56.1%, while its tensile strength increased by 53.5%, without markedly affecting elongation at break. Physical characterization and multiscale simulations indicate that COP–CA NPs form multisite interfacial associations with chitosan through hydrogen bonding, local electrostatic interactions, aromatic contact, and van der Waals forces, thereby limiting water absorption, swelling, and water migration within the film. After 14 days of storage, the 0.20% CS@NPs coating reduced the weight loss of cherry tomatoes from 14.75% to 6.89%, and better maintained fruit firmness and total soluble solids. The COP–CA carrier-free nanoassemblies can effectively enhance the water resistance, moisture barrier properties, and fruit preservation capacity of the chitosan coating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Akdağ O.
Title: A two-layer degradation-aware energy management framework for renewable power grids with battery and hydrogen storage
Abstract: High renewable energy penetration supports sustainable power generation; however, intermittency, component aging, and long-term performance uncertainty may pose operational challenges for power systems. This study proposes a degradation-aware, two-layer framework that jointly evaluates short-term system operation and long-term component performance. In the first layer, the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm (TSA) determines system capacities and energy-sharing parameters for a 24-h period. An objective function includes operating costs, emissions costs, BESS costs, hydrogen system costs, demand response, and renewable energy curtailment. In the second layer, the optimized system and energy management strategy (EMS) parameters are transferred without re-optimization to a 365-day simulation under variable renewable generation and load. BESS energy/SOH, hydrogen inventory, PEM electrolyzer degradation, and PEM fuel-cell efficiency are updated continuously. The novelty lies in directly testing the long-term operational robustness of short-term optimized system and EMS decisions within a continuous annual power-balance model. Selected load and conventional generation data from the IEEE 24-bus RTS are used as reference inputs. At the same time, the RES capacities, BESS configuration, DRP parameters, and P2H–H₂ storage–PEMFC system are defined and adapted specifically for the present study. The results show that the BESS state of health decreases from approximately 1.00 to 0.9785 (yearly), while the average PEM electrolyzer effective conversion coefficient decreases from approximately 0.649 to 0.62. The integrated BESS and hydrogen storage structure also supports renewable power balancing under variable operating conditions. Thus, the proposed framework shows the long-term technical effects of short-term energy-management decisions in renewable power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A data-driven framework based on signal processing and transformer model for fault detection, classification, and localization in microgrids
Abstract: This paper proposes an integrated machine learning framework for fault detection, classification, and localization in microgrids, utilizing a hybrid Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Transformer architecture. To eliminate the need for complex voltage sensing equipment (i.e., potential transformers), the framework relies on current measurements, thereby reducing both data acquisition costs and computational complexity during training. In the proposed scheme, transient features are extracted from current signals via VMD and fed into a Transformer model to identify patterns associated with various states. The framework is evaluated under diverse operating conditions, including different fault types, load variations, changes in the generation level of distributed sources, and noisy environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a fault localization accuracy of 99.57% and a detection and classification accuracy of 99.13%, maintaining a high accuracy of 98.08% even under a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 10 dB. Furthermore, the model issues tripping commands in <25 ms (under 1.5 cycles), outperforming conventional models that require >30–35 ms. These findings confirm the framework's reliability, speed, and robustness for microgrid protection and monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: MOF-derived Ni-Co bimetallic catalyst enabling photothermal dry reforming of methane at the thermodynamic limit
Abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) is an attractive route for CO2 utilization and high-value energy conversion, yet conventional thermal catalysis suffers from high energy consumption and serious catalyst deactivation. To address these challenges, efficient photothermal catalysts were rationally designed through metal-organic framework (MOF) derivation to promote low-carbon DRM and enhance catalytic performance. A series of MOF-derived Ni-based catalysts were synthesized by post-synthesis modification combined with atmosphere-mediated treatment. The optimal NiCo-CeO2-M exhibited full UV-Vis-NIR spectral response and delivered enhanced photothermal synergistic DRM performance. Under the operating conditions of 600 ℃, 72 L·gcat−1·h−1 and 2.55 W·cm−2, it achieved a good balance between reactant conversion and syngas production rate, maintaining 100 h of stable operation without deactivation at the thermodynamic limit level. Characterizations revealed a hierarchical pore structure favorable to mass transfer and light harvesting, while high metal dispersion and abundant interfacial sites facilitated reactant activation and migration. Co doping narrowed the bandgap and constructed Co3O4/CeO2 heterojunction, improving light absorption and carrier separation efficiency. Theoretical calculations and electromagnetic simulations further clarified the synergistic mechanism originating from the precise regulation of the Ni-Co bimetallic system and interfacial structure, which optimized charge transfer, lowered activation barriers and strengthened localized electric fields. In this photothermal system, the synergistic interaction between light-assisted electronic effects, surface-defect-associated CO2 activation, and thermal driving forces contributes to enhanced DRM performance and stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Coordination and K-induced electronic effects promote efficient COS hydrolysis over K-Nd/Al2O3 catalysts
Abstract: The development of efficient alumina-based catalysts for carbonyl sulfide (COS) hydrolysis remains a significant challenge, as their application in real blast furnace gas is largely hindered by insufficient activity and poor long-term durability. Here, K-Nd/Al2O3 maintains nearly complete COS conversion for 20 h at 120 °C and achieves a cumulative COS conversion capacity of 1.46 g/g under a simplified H2S/O2-containing atmosphere. Comprehensive characterization reveals that K-Nd co-modulation tailors acid-base site distribution, preserving active sites. Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and XAFS analyses confirm that Nd is predominantly atomically dispersed, existing as isolated, low-coordinated Nd-Ox single-sites. During reaction, the Nd-O coordination number increases from 4.2 to 8.0 without aggregation, demonstrating reaction-induced reconstruction of the first coordination shell. Surface characterization, in-situ DRIFTS, and DFT calculations further show that K enhances surface electron density and fine-tunes Nd Lewis acidity, promoting H2O dissociation and nucleophilic *OH attack on COS, stabilizing *HOCOS and *HSCOO intermediates while facilitating H2S desorption. Title: Mitigation of wind-induced deflection of oversized composite-insulator sheds using a −1° lower-surface inclination and disk-type rib structures
Abstract: Silicone rubber composite insulators with oversized sheds can effectively reduce the risk of external insulation flashover caused by bird-dropping bridging. However, the wind-induced deflection of oversized sheds under strong-wind conditions and the effects of their lower-surface geometry on the deflection response have not been sufficiently investigated. In this study, a typical silicone rubber composite insulator with an oversized shed was investigated. The deflection characteristics of the oversized shed at an airflow velocity of 30 m/s were experimentally determined using an open-circuit wind tunnel. A fluid–structure interaction model benchmarked against the wind tunnel measurement was subsequently established to systematically investigate the effects of airflow velocity, lower-surface inclination, and disk-type rib-reinforced structures on shed deflection, surface pressure, and shed-root stress. The results show that changing the lower-surface inclination from 6° to −1° reduces the maximum deflection from 71.3 mm to 1.7 mm, corresponding to a reduction of 97.6%. At the original inclination of 6°, the addition of straight-rib and curved-rib disk-type structures reduces the maximum deflection to 45.0% and 35.9% of that of the original structure, respectively. In addition, a low-cost deflection measurement method based on suspended mass loading is proposed for the preliminary comparison of different anti-deflection structures when wind tunnel facilities are unavailable. The findings provide a reference for the anti-deflection design and field retrofitting of oversized-shed composite insulators in strong-wind regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fully distributed security control for wind farms subject to hybrid cyberattacks
Abstract: Modern wind farms (WFs) increasingly integrate information technologies with wind power generation, which introduces new cyber-physical vulnerabilities. As the penetration of wind power in power systems continues to increase, secure communication and stable operation of WFs become increasingly important. However, coordinated control of WFs under hybrid false data injection (FDI) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks remains insufficiently addressed. To fill this gap, this paper develops a fully distributed security control strategy for cyber-physical WFs under hybrid cyberattacks. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) wind turbine (WT) model is integrated with a WF communication network model to characterize the effects of FDI and DoS attacks on active power tracking and fair load sharing. A distributed security control strategy based on an auxiliary layer is then designed to track grid-side active power demand while preserving fair load sharing. Lyapunov stability analysis establishes closed-loop convergence under nominal and admissible DoS conditions and characterizes the recovery error under FDI attacks, thereby clarifying how control gains and network structure affect resilience. Case studies on a grid-connected WF demonstrate that the proposed strategy maintains active power tracking and fair load sharing under FDI, DoS, and hybrid attack scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Molecular characterization and nonlinear rheology of native and carboxymethylated carrageenans
Abstract: Carrageenans are important marine polysaccharides extracted from red algae and are widely used for their ability to form ion-induced hydrogels. In food and pharmaceutical applications, these hydrogels are often subjected to large-amplitude, rapid shear deformations, making the study of their nonlinear rheological responses highly relevant. Herein, carboxymethyl derivatives with varying degrees of substitution (DS) were prepared from κ-, ι-, and λ-carrageenans. Structural characterization using FT-IR, NMR, elemental analysis, and gel permeation chromatography confirmed successful carboxymethylation, accompanied by partial desulfation and changes in molecular weight. Steady and dynamic shear tests revealed shear-thinning behavior in the solutions; carboxymethylation converted the original gel-like response to a more liquid-like viscoelasticity by altering chain conformation and electrostatic interactions. Large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS), combined with Fourier-transform and Chebyshev analyses, showed that κ-carrageenan gels exhibit weak strain overshoot and a narrow linear viscoelastic region, whereas ι-carrageenan and most carboxymethylated derivatives display strong strain overshoot and a broader linear region. Notably, increasing DS progressively enhances resistance to nonlinear deformation. These findings elucidate transient network dynamics and establish a structure–rheology relationship for carboxymethylated carrageenans, guiding the design of soft, tough hydrogels for food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Remaining electrical life prediction of AC contactors based on PA-OT-PSM stage transfer
Abstract: To address the complex degradation process of AC contactors, large cross-device lifetime data discrepancies, and limited generalization of traditional data-driven prediction models, this paper proposes a remaining electrical life prediction method based on physics-guided stage manifold-constrained transfer learning, namely Prototype Alignment–Optimal Transport–Physics-guided Stage Manifold (PA-OT-PSM). First, feature parameters are extracted from full-life tests, and degradation feature sequences are constructed using Euclidean distance. A change-point detection algorithm is then used to divide the degradation process into multiple stages. Based on this, a stage prototype alignment mechanism is introduced to align feature centers of corresponding degradation stages in the source and target domains, preserving stage structural consistency. Furthermore, an optimal transport mechanism is embedded within each stage to achieve sample-level relational transfer, while source-domain lifetime labels are used to generate soft supervision for target-domain samples. To ensure physical consistency, degradation monotonicity and remaining-life monotonicity constraints are incorporated into model training. In addition, a few labeled target-domain samples are used for lightweight fine-tuning of the prediction layer and key alignment parameters, enabling target-domain distribution calibration and lifetime mapping correction. Finally, the model is optimized through a joint loss function to obtain target-domain remaining useful life predictions. Experimental results show that, after few-shot target-domain fine-tuning, the proposed method achieves high prediction accuracy and strong cross-device generalization in both same-type and cross-type transfer scenarios, providing a useful reference for condition assessment and predictive maintenance of electrical equipment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Distributed adaptive event-triggered secondary control for electricity-hydrogen coupled microgrid
Abstract: The integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources and electricity-hydrogen coupling units significantly increases the dynamic complexity of islanded microgrids. Traditional centralized secondary control suffers from issues such as single-point failures and heavy communication burdens, while existing distributed cooperative control strategies commonly rely on continuous communication, leading to inefficient resource utilization. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a distributed cooperative secondary control method for electricity-hydrogen microgrids based on an adaptive event-triggered mechanism. First, a nonlinear large-signal model is established for each inverter-based distributed generator and its coupled electricity–hydrogen interface. Then, input–output feedback linearization is applied to the fast electrical subsystem of each DG, while the hydrogen-side dynamics are retained as bounded slow-varying perturbations. Subsequently, an adaptive event-triggering scheme is introduced for each unit, in which the triggering threshold is dynamically adjusted according to the system state. Communication with neighboring units and control updates occur only when local state variations exceed the triggering condition. The asymptotic stability of the overall system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov theory, and Zeno behavior is excluded. Simulation studies conducted on a four-node islanded microgrid with electricity-hydrogen coupling units demonstrate that the proposed method achieves dynamic and steady-state performance comparable to periodic sampling control, while reducing communication events by >88.1%, thereby significantly alleviating communication and computational burdens. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Electromagnetic and temperature field analysis of a 20 MW-class wind turbine generator with slot-opening internal evaporative cooling
Abstract: To address the stator-winding heat-dissipation bottleneck in high-power offshore wind turbine generators, this study proposes a slot-opening internal evaporative cooling scheme for a 19 MW permanent-magnet synchronous generator. A hollow 316 stainless-steel heat-conducting tube is embedded near each stator slot opening, enabling near-source heat removal through the phase-change latent heat of a low-boiling insulating working fluid. Electromagnetic analysis shows that the 240 tubes introduce only 6.2 kW of additional eddy-current loss, while the air-gap flux-density waveform and harmonic spectrum remain essentially unchanged. A quarter-unit multi-parallel-branch evaporative cooling test platform was then constructed with 1:1 fidelity in single-tube geometry and thermal boundary conditions, reproducing the heat-input and flow-distribution characteristics of the prototype. Experiments over heat loads of 500–700 W confirmed stable heat-transport capability, and an equivalent evaporative heat-transfer coefficient of approximately 4901 W/(m²·K) was derived at the 600 W design condition. Title: Fault detection methods for medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems under active current limiting control at MMC converter stations
Abstract: In medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems, conventional protection of Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) typically relies on MMC blocking, which may result in converter station shutdown. This strategy enables DC-side faults to be detected before the MMC converter station is blocked or shut down, thereby providing sufficient transient time for subsequent fault detection and selective isolation. However, the suppression of fault currents via active current-limiting control may reduce the accuracy of conventional. protection methods in fault detection. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Logistic-Gauss Circle- Feature Mode Decomposition(LGC-FMD)-based fault detection method for medium-voltage flexible DC power supply systems that incorporates converter-station current-limiting control. By combining this method with a Joint Judgment Criteria of IMF based on Approximate Entropy(AE) and the Maximal Information Coefficient(MIC), Despite the fault current suppression provided by active current-limiting control at the converter station, faults can still be accurately detected. Title: SISO equivalent impedance modeling with mirror frequency effect and mitigation of sub-synchronous resonance for single-phase grid-forming converters
Abstract: Grid-forming converters have gradually become critical equipment for supporting modern power systems. With the rapid development of distributed generation, single-phase grid-forming converters (SGFMCs) have attracted extensive attention. However, SGFMCs face the challenge of impedance modeling, which affects the stability analysis and controller design. This paper investigates the impedance modeling, interaction mechanisms, and sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) mitigation methods. Regarding the impedance modeling, SGFMCs have more complex internal relationships than three-phase grid-forming converters owning to their orthogonal signal generation unit. Existing impedance models for double-power loops SGFMCs rarely account for the mirror frequency effect (MFE), resulting in inaccurate impedance characterization. To fill this research gap, this paper adopts the harmonic linearization method to derive two single-input single-output impedance models that fully capture the MFE for two typical SGFMCs. Furthermore, the interaction mechanism between SGFMCs and grid is explicitly elucidated. Analytical results demonstrate that both SGFMCs are susceptible to SSR under strong grid conditions. To improve the system stability, an impedance shaping method is proposed to mitigate SSR for SGFMCs under strong grid conditions. Finally, experimental results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fang Y.; Zhao Z.
Title: Gelatin-based hydrogels modified by transglutaminase and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates: Experimental characterization
Abstract: Conventional cold-set gelatin hydrogels have limited mechanical strength and thermal stability. This study examined gelatin (GEL)-based formulations modified with transglutaminase (TGase) and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates (AHOA). Short-time characterization of acid-heated ovalbumin showed spectroscopic changes consistent with amyloid-like aggregation and an increased elastic response. AHOA prepared by an 8-h acidic heat treatment was incorporated into gelatin formulations. At a common TGase reaction time of 6 h, the GEL:AHOA volume ratio of 6:4 gave the highest hardness and springiness among the tested formulations. Because changing this ratio also changes protein concentrations, the maximum describes a formulation-dependent response. TGase-treated gelatin hydrogels exhibited higher moduli and altered hydration behavior than the untreated control. In the extended in vitro digestion test, treated groups showed lower early but higher final cumulative betacyanin release, and a higher fraction of endpoint-recovered betacyanin in the liquid phase. The storage tests showed higher betacyanin retention at 8 days and lower loss at 28 days for the TGase-treated groups than for GH in the respective series. These results distinguish the mechanical response to AHOA incorporation from the hydration and pigment-release properties measured for gelatin hydrogels with and without TGase. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Comparative study of curcumin- and limonene oil-encapsulated Pickering emulsions stabilized by pH-Responsive chitosan nanoparticles: Structural, rheological, and controlled release properties
Abstract: Curcumin and limonene oil, bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential, are vital for human health but face limitations due to poor solubility, stability, and bioavailability. Chitosan (CS), a pH-responsive natural polysaccharide, serves as an effective stabilizer in Pickering emulsions (PEs), thereby enhancing their delivery. This study focuses on preparing stable CS nanoparticles (CSNPs) via a pH-responsive self-assembly method for encapsulating bioactive compounds. Optimal stability of CSNPs was observed at pH 6, as indicated by a higher contact angle reflecting enhanced hydrophobicity. At pH 6.5, the contact angle decreased due to the formation of large, unstable aggregates that settled out, resulting in a reduced hydrophobicity of CS. Curcumin-loaded PEs prepared at pH 6 exhibited uniform droplet size and distribution, which can be attributed to the strong hydrophobic interactions of the CSNPs. Below pH 6, the CSNPs became hydrophilic, resulting in the phase separation of the PEs. Increasing the concentration of CSNPs and oil content promoted the formation of interconnected networks, resulting in elastic gels that are stable at 35°C. At elevated temperatures (70°C), the enhanced kinetic energy of CSNPs induced a gel-to-semi-gel transition, while elevated ionic strength further liquefied PEs. Limonene oil-encapsulated PEs were stable at pH 5.5 and 6.0, differing from curcumin systems due to limonene's lower viscosity and the pH-sensitive behavior of CSNPs. This study demonstrates that slight pH variations in CSNPs have a significant impact on bioactive encapsulation and stability. Curcumin- and limonene-loaded PEs achieve high efficiency, capacity, and controlled release, providing a versatile method to improve bioactive delivery in food and pharmaceutical systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Han X.; Wu L.; Wang L.; Zheng L.
Title: Bioactive nanocomposite-reinforced biopolymer films for multifunctional food packaging
Abstract: Developing sustainable food packaging materials with mechanical strength, antibacterial activity, and biodegradability remains challenging. In this study, a multifunctional konjac glucomannan (KGM)/quaternized nanocellulose (QNC)-zinc oxide (ZnO) composite film was fabricated through a triple interfacial synergistic reinforcement strategy using KGM, QNC, and ZnO nanoparticles. The incorporation of QNC and ZnO enhanced film performance via strong interfacial interactions. The optimized film exhibited a tensile strength of 139.6 MPa and elongation at break of 21.7%. Moisture resistance improved, with a water vapor transmission rate of 78.2 g m−2·day−1 and a water contact angle of 88.6°. The composite exhibited strong antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus with antibacterial rates of 99.75% and 99.99%. The composite also showed good biodegradability and excellent cytocompatibility. Grape preservation tests indicated a weight loss of only 15.49% after 18 days. This study provides a green and feasible strategy for constructing biodegradable multifunctional packaging films with enhanced mechanical properties, antibacterial activity, and preservation functionality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: 2D Bond-Based Peridynamic Simulation of Phase Transformation in 3Y-TZP Dental Ceramics Using ABAQUS
Abstract: In this research, the fracture behavior of 3 mol% yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia polycrystals (3Y-TZP) dental ceramics is investigated. The focus is on the tetragonal (t) to monoclinic (m) phase transformation using ABAQUS and bond-based peridynamics. We conducted two-dimensional simulations of a single grain undergoing uniform dilational expansion within a homogeneous m-phase environment. The effects of transformation time, biaxial stress, and strains on fracture were analyzed. It was found that increasing stress in the surrounding t-phase elevated the elastic strain energy associated with the transformation. By varying stress from-1.1 GPa to 400 MPa, elastic strain energy started to decrease from 3.41, 3.32, 3.11, and 2.85 pJ at fracture strain values of S0= 0.00711, 0.00553, 0.00395, and 0.00237, respectively. These correspond to reductions of 83%, 87%, 90%, and 96%. In addition, damage fractions increased from 0.001, 0.002, 0.003, and 0.004 to 0.005, 0.011, 0.022, and 0.058, respectively. This demonstrates the significant impact of applied stress on the fracture mechanics of 3Y-TZP. Moreover, increasing the elemental parameter S0 from 0.00237 to 0.00711 in the simulations corresponds to a considerable decrease in defect density, resulting in a substantial increase in the total energy required for material division from 0.25 to 2.2 J/m2. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
Abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang N.; Gao L.; Wu X.; Zhang F.; Ren X.; Qin L.
Title: A hybrid framework for short-term load forecasting via frequency-domain decoupling and spatio-temporal graph fusion
Abstract: Load forecasting, as a crucial component of the electricity market, plays a significant role in ensuring the secure operation and rational planning of the power grid. However, accurate short-term load forecasting (STLF) remains challenging due to strong non-stationarity caused by complex meteorological conditions and abrupt load fluctuations. To mitigate these prediction errors and enhance load feature extraction, this paper proposes a hybrid forecasting framework combining frequency-domain decoupling with a spatio-temporal graph neural network. Specifically, a secondary decomposition strategy based on secondary variational mode decomposition (SVMD) and wavelet packet threshold denoising (WPTD) is employed to refine multi-scale modal representations by attenuating weak noise-like wavelet-packet coefficients while retaining meaningful high-frequency load variations. An Energy-Driven Reconstruction (EDR) mechanism is then introduced to reorganize the decomposed modes into dominant low-frequency and high-frequency fluctuation components according to their energy distribution. Subsequently, a heterogeneous dual-branch architecture is deployed: the low-frequency branch employs a multi-basis trend modeling module to track long-term patterns, while a wide-receptive-field temporal convolutional network (TCN) captures transient high-frequency fluctuations. Furthermore, a Weather-GAT module is integrated to aggregate multi-site meteorological features. Employing real-world load data from the Panama National Grid, the proposed framework achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.6837% in 24-hour-ahead forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that the model exhibits strong robustness across regular workdays, holidays, and meteorological disturbance scenarios. © 2026

Title: Fermentation-driven remodeling of whey macromolecules: Mechanisms, functional outcomes, and industrial implications
Abstract: Whey, a protein- and carbohydrate-rich dairy byproduct, presents significant valorization potential yet remains largely underutilized due to the high cost and energy intensity of conventional fractionation technologies. Fermentation offers a biologically driven, scalable alternative that fundamentally remodels whey macromolecules through microbially mediated enzymatic and metabolic cascades. This review critically examines fermentation-induced structural, conformational, and interactional modifications of whey proteins, glycoproteins, and associated carbohydrate fractions. We delineate how strain-specific proteolytic systems, pH-dependent conformational unfolding, and non-proteolytic transformations (e.g., glycation, phenolic–protein complexation, and microbial transglycosylation) govern macromolecular hydration, interfacial behavior, and network assembly. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic evidence demonstrates that optimal bioactivity and matrix stability emerge at a substrate-dependent degree of hydrolysis: 8–12% for sweet whey (native protein conformation), 6–10% for acid whey (partially denatured proteins), and 10–15% for pre-heat-treated whey (exposed hydrophobic domains). Beyond these thresholds, excessive cleavage compromises functional epitopes, triggers bitterness via hydrophobic 3–8 residue peptides, or exposes neo-allergens. By establishing a structure–function framework for fermentation-mediated whey remodeling, this work positions microbial bioprocessing as a precision tool for engineering next-generation hydrocolloid-functionalized dairy matrices, aligning with circular bioeconomy and sustainable food system objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li J.; Li Y.; Hu X.; Wang S.; Chen W.; Lan S.
Title: Wind–photovoltaic joint power modeling based on a two-stage optimal selection of marginal distributions and dependence structure
Abstract: To address uncertainty challenges caused by high renewable energy penetration, generating joint distribution scenarios that accurately reflect the dependence structure of wind–PV joint output is essential for planning and operating modern power systems with high renewable penetration. Traditional methods often rely on fixed distributional assumptions, limiting their adaptability to different data characteristics. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a wind–PV joint output scenario generation method based on an integrated two-stage adaptive marginal distribution and dependence structure selection and validation framework. First, root mean square error, Kullback–Leibler divergence, Jensen–Shannon divergence, and Wasserstein distance are used as evaluation criteria to adaptively select marginal distributions with the best goodness of fit to historical wind and photovoltaic power output data. Second, log-likelihood, Akaike information criterion, and Bayesian information criterion are used as evaluation criteria to select the Copula function that best captures the dependence structure and tail dependence of historical wind–PV joint output. Finally, we develop a scenario quality evaluation framework including Kendall's tau coefficient, Spearman's rho coefficient, tail dependence coefficients, and energy distance. Time-block cross-validation and mean-rank-based comprehensive ranking are introduced to verify the effectiveness and stability of the two-stage selection and validation results. A case study using measured wind and photovoltaic power output data from Henan Province shows that the selected combination outperforms other candidates in accurately reproducing dependence and tail joint-output characteristics. The generated scenarios reproduce the 24-h hourly mean output profiles and cover seasonal fluctuation scenarios and high- and low-output wind–PV scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A novel approach to optimal PMU placement for state estimation in electric power systems
Abstract: This paper proposes a new method for the optimal placement of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in power systems. The proposed method minimizes the number of PMUs to be embedded in the network by leveraging virtual current injection measurements at zero-injection buses. This approach guarantees full system observability under normal and N-1 operating states without requiring conventional post-placement observability propagation rules. Unlike other approaches, the proposed optimization model uses equality constraints to account for the virtual measurements, thereby avoiding the need to change the network topology or use merging techniques to eliminate nodes with virtual measurements during the PMU placement process. The proposal's effectiveness is demonstrated on several benchmark IEEE power systems and the Polish 2383-bus large-scale system, considering base topology cases and N-1 contingency scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Study of optimum photovoltaic energy ingress in conventional grid system without compromising stability margins
Abstract: Due to growing energy demand, rising greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and a rising global average temperature, replacing fossil fuels with sustainable renewable energy sources is the ultimate global target. However, variable renewable energy sources have repercussions for existing grid systems due to their inherent volatility and uncertainty. Such drastic variations can lead to transient stability issues and need to be considered when planning high ingress of renewable energy sources in a conventional grid system. This paper provides an optimization model based on the genetic algorithm technique to allow maximum possible photovoltaic (PV) energy ingress in the system, keeping system parameters within stipulated stability limits. Certain design variables have also been defined and constrained to achieve the optimization objective. The resulting design variables from the optimization model are then plugged into the IEEE 30-bus test system for simulation of transient stability. The system shows complete recovery from the applied transient disturbance from sudden generation and load drop events. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
Abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Step-level screening-driven reasoning enhancement for large language models in prefabricated substation fault diagnosis
Abstract: Prefabricated substations are core components of novel power systems, yet inter-compartment coupling triggers cascading faults, while high-dimensional asynchronous multi-source monitoring data severely reduces manual fault diagnosis efficiency. Vanilla large language models (LLMs) produce opaque single-path inference lacking traceability. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves reasoning transparency but suffers from single-trajectory bias. Self-Consistency (SC) adopts multi-trajectory voting, yet it fails on open-ended fault diagnosis when outputs differ drastically in semantics and format. This study proposes a Step-level Screening-driven Reasoning Enhancement Method (SS-REM) to select optimal reasoning trajectories for substation fault diagnosis. SS-REM generates diverse reasoning paths via temperature sampling, decomposes them into atomic steps, and integrates TF-IDF semantic consistency scoring and length regularization for fine-grained step-level screening. We construct PMEESET—the first multi-compartment prefabricated equipment fault dataset—and propose a three-dimensional DDM quantitative evaluation principle tailored to power engineering. Experiments on PMEESET show SS-REM lifts average reasoning scores by 35.9% and 27.9% compared with vanilla LLMs and CoT, respectively. As a lightweight inference-stage post-processing module without model fine-tuning, SS-REM delivers remarkable improvements in diagnostic reliability and logical traceability, supporting edge intelligent maintenance of prefabricated substations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
