Authors: Guo Y.; Su N.; Wu G.; Mei Z.; Zeng J.; Cao Y.; Zhang C.; Zhang X.
Title: Neutral current redistribution and differentiated dc bias protection of multiple main transformers in one substation via a refined metro–grid coupling model
Abstract: Significant differences in neutral currents exist among different grounded main transformers within the same substation. Simplifying the substation as a single conductor fails to resolve the internal distribution of metro-induced stray current, thereby masking potential DC bias risks. To prevent such failures, a refined metro–power system coupling model that considers multiple main transformers is established using actual parameters of the metro system, power grid, and local soil. The model accurately calculates neutral current of different interconnected transformers, enabling early identification of uneven current distribution that may lead to DC bias. Results show that the maximum ratio of absolute neutral currents among transformers reaches 2.76, while the minimum mean absolute current error against field measurements is 3.74%. A reduced-scale physical analogue provides supplementary validation of the model's ability to reproduce current redistribution among multiple transformer grounding branches. Based on this model, the influence of various metro operating conditions on stray current is analyzed to identify failure-prone scenarios. A neutral-point resistance model, combined with global optimization algorithms with verified stability, designs three-level differentiated protection schemes. The resulting schemes keep all transformer neutral currents within specified limits under the actual topology—unlike traditional-model-based schemes—thereby preventing DC bias-induced failures in multiple main transformers within the same substation. © 2026

Title: Unlocking cooperative geometries in inverse spinel CuCo2O4 for superior catalytic oxidation of chlorinated VOCs
Abstract: The low-temperature catalytic oxidation of chlorinated volatile organic compounds (CVOCs) is challenged by chlorine poisoning and toxic byproducts, while the correlation between tetrahedral(Td)/octahedral(Oh) cation geometric configurations and dechlorination pathways remains unclear. Herein, a series of cation-regulated spinel catalysts were constructed to unlock cooperative geometric sites for dichloromethane (DCM) oxidation. Structural characterizations verified that Cu2 + preferentially occupies Oh sites, inducing an inverse spinel (CoTd3+[CuOh2+CoOh3+]O4) that triggers Jahn–Teller lattice distortion, enhances oxygen vacancy and optimizes Co electronic structure. Consequently, CuCo2O4 achieves 91% DCM conversion and 94.1% CO2 selectivity at 200 °C, with excellent stability and negligible polychlorinated byproducts. Title: Molecular structure governs intermolecular interactions and rheological properties of three seed mucilage polysaccharides
Abstract: Seed mucilage polysaccharides are promising plant-derived hydrocolloids. This study selected three seed mucilage polysaccharides: chia seed gum (CSG), Artemisia sphaerocephala Krasch polysaccharide (ASKP) and Plantago ovata seed mucilage (POSM), and elucidated the relationships between structure, intermolecular interaction and rheological relationship through structural characterization, chain conformational analysis and steady shear/oscillatory rheological measurements. Although all three samples consisted of two molecular fractions, they exhibited significant differences in molecular weight, degree of branching and uronic acid content. POSM has the highest molecular weight, exhibited the highest viscosity and the strongest intermolecular association, which was related to its highly branched structure promoting intermolecular hydrogen bonding. CSG had a lower molecular weight but a high terminal uronic acid content, causing its rheological behavior to be strongly influenced by electrostatic repulsion. ASKP exhibited weaker network formation, linked to weaker intermolecular interactions resulting from differences in its composition. These results indicate that molecular weight, branching structure, uronic acid content and intermolecular interactions collectively govern the rheological behavior of seed mucilage polysaccharides. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A voltage imbalance prediction technology for wind turbine generator sets with DFIG
Abstract: Grid voltage imbalance degrades wind turbine performance and injects distorted currents, significantly reducing power quality and conversion efficiency. This paper first analyzes the underlying causes of voltage imbalance in Doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG). Subsequently, the three-phase unbalance calculation for wind turbine voltage data is implemented to establish a standardized dataset for imbalance analysis. This paper proposes a forecasting model based on the gated recurrent unit–multi-head attention (GRU-MHA) architecture. By combining recurrent temporal modeling with attention-based feature enhancement, the proposed model predicts the positive voltage unbalance rate (PVUR) using historical voltage data and external meteorological data. By learning the variation trend and local fluctuation characteristics of PVUR, the model can provide data support for voltage-unbalance risk early warning in wind farms. Meanwhile, Optuna is employed for an automatic optimizer and hyperparameter tuning, enabling the training process to better adapt to complex temporal dynamics and thereby improving forecasting accuracy and robustness under different operating conditions. Real measured data from two wind farms, four WT units, and three representative months are used to construct 12 datasets. Comparative and ablation results show that GRU-MHA-O achieves superior overall PVUR forecasting accuracy and stability while maintaining acceptable computational efficiency, supporting its application in short-term monitoring and early warning. © 2026

Title: Kinetics of starch digestion in Australian pigeonpea [Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp.] genotypes and consequences for nutrient asynchrony
Abstract: In view of pigeonpea global food importance, the in-vitro starch digestibility of Australian genotypes ICPLs 14425, 86022, 88039, 90048, 91039, and 98011 was investigated, objectively revealing monophasic and biphasic digestograms. The digestograms were adequately modelled (r2 > 0.89, p < 0.001) by the 1- and 2-term exponential and non-exponential plus the recommended sequential modified first-order kinetic model. Genotypes ICPLs 86022, 88039, and 91039 were monophasic with digestion rates (KST x 10−3 min−1) 6.9-11.3. The biphasic genotypes ICPLs 14425, 90048, and 98011 exhibited a rapid-slow digestion phenomenon with KST 13.8–30.8 for the rapid first phase and 0.5–5.2 for the slow second phase. The maximum digestible starch (D∞, g/100g dry starch) ranged from 8.4 to 100.0, indicating remarkable genotypic differences (heterogeneous amylolysis), also revealed in the very rapidly (2.7–4.2), rapidly (3.9-9.8), and slowly (2.0–4.9) digestible and resistant (85.4–92.7) starches. Moreover, the genotypes significantly (p ≤ 0.05) differed in their low glycaemic indices (eGIAVG, 22.1–38.9%) and loads (eGL, 6.7–11.8%) relative to white wheat bread. The relative release (nutrient asynchrony) of amino acids and glucose during digestion was examined by comparing the starch hydrolysis index (HISTARCH) and eGIAVG (current study) with their protein parameters (HIPROTEIN, in-vitro protein digestibility [IVPDAVG], Malau & Sopade [2026]. Food Science and Processing 2 {2}: 8). The nutrients could be comparably released in ICPL 90048, but amino acids could be released slower in ICPL 14425 and faster in ICPLs 86022, 88039, 91039, and 98011. Title: A Dual-capacitor converter-type hybrid DC circuit breaker with adaptive reclosing capability
Abstract: DC circuit breakers are critical equipment for fault clearance in DC power systems. Existing circuit breakers suffer from high costs, limited current-limiting capabilities, and insufficient reliability. This paper proposes a dual-capacitor converter-based hybrid DC circuit breaker topology with adaptive reclosing capability. This topology incorporates current-limiting branches to suppress the rise of fault currents. Its adaptive reclosing capability enhances circuit breaker reliability, preventing erroneous reclosing. The proposed topology primarily employs thyristors, diodes, and conventional mechanical switches for transitions during fault clearance at various stages, eliminating the need for separate capacitor charging equipment or fully controllable devices, thus offering significant economic benefits. A single-terminal equivalent DC system and a four-terminal flexible DC transmission system model are established based on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation software. Simulations are carried out in both the single-terminal equivalent DC system and the four-terminal flexible DC transmission system. The results demonstrate that the proposed circuit breaker exhibits certain advantages in terms of reliability and economy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Deep reinforcement learning-based model-free voltage regulation in an active distribution network using demand-side flexibility aggregation
Abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources is challenging the operational stability of low-voltage distribution networks, leading to frequent voltage fluctuations that conventional devices, such as on-load tap changers (OLTCs) and capacitor banks, struggle to manage under dynamic and varied operating conditions. Voltage regulation in active distribution networks typically relies on accurate network models for optimization or on reactive-power support from inverter-based resources, which can be difficult to deploy in community-scale settings with limited observability. This paper presents a real-time, model-free voltage regulation framework that uses only residential active-power demand-side flexibility and a single-point voltage measurement at the point of common coupling, without requiring the network topology, line parameters, or reactive-power actuation for online execution. The proposed adaptive droop learning framework follows a centralized-training distributed-execution architecture: a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) coordinator maps PCC voltage deviations to aggregate flexibility requests and learns to dynamically allocate them across load buses by learning implicit voltage–power sensitivity structure from data without explicit sensitivity calculations. Distributed SAC bus-agents disaggregate allocated requests into appliance-level setpoints using XGBoost-based flexibility bounds and a quadratic-programming feasibility layer to enforce device constraints and satisfy dynamic grid response requirements. Experimental validation on an RTDS with an IEEE 13-bus radial distribution system demonstrates 88.5% voltage compliance within a ± 10 V band, a 73% reduction in OLTC operations, and 96.9% flexibility-tracking accuracy, outperforming TD3, DDPG, and PPO baselines. Authors: Yu J.; Xu B.; Zhao J.; Ruan J.
Title: Multi-stage siting and sizing of PV stations under long-term carbon price: a branch-and-bound embedded progressive hedging approach
Abstract: Reasonable programming of photovoltaic (PV) site selection and sizing is essential for boosting renewable energy penetration and power system carbon emission reduction, thereby mitigating future electricity procurement cost risks under dynamic carbon pricing. However, the problem of optimal PV siting and sizing with integer decision variables is complicated by the long-term uncertainty of carbon prices. To address the above issue, this paper proposes a PV site selection and capacity determination mixed integer multi-stage stochastic programming model considering the long-term uncertainty of carbon prices, and designs a collaborative solution framework of the Progressive Hedging (PH) algorithm and Branch-and-Bound (BB) to optimize the low-carbon and economic performance of the system. Firstly, a multi-stage stochastic programming model for PV siting and sizing is constructed, employing scenario trees based on an enhanced binomial tree model to depict the stochastic evolution of carbon prices over the long term. Secondly, the PH algorithm solves the subproblems for individual scenarios and refines the solutions through interaction to meet the nonanticipativity constraints in carbon prices. Finally, the PH algorithm is embedded within the BB framework to optimize the integer decisions related to PV siting locations. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in identifying adaptive PV deployment strategies under long-term carbon price uncertainty. A 10% decrease or increase in carbon prices changes the expected final-stage PV capacity by approximately -11.2% and +10.7%. These results highlight the capability of the framework to capture the impacts of carbon price uncertainty on PV investment decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A Parameter-Efficient Entropy-Guided feature suppression framework for accurate insulator fault detection in edge-Compatible drone inspection
Abstract: This paper presents a lightweight and computationally efficient deep learning system for real-time detection of insulator defects. It was made to work on edge platforms that don't have a lot of resources. Starting with a basic You Only Look Once 11 Nano (YOLOv11n) detector, the proposed method uses a Transfer Learning architectural optimisation strategy that combines depth-width scaling, entropy-guided feature suppression, and lightweight convolutional blocks to make a hybrid architecture called Entropy-guided Lightweight Transfer-learning Architecture (ELTA)-YOLOv11. The model keeps good detection accuracy through this hybridisation, and it also reduces the number of parameters by a significant and clear 40.70%, from 2.56M to 1.53M. Even though architectural compression lowers accuracy at first, adding our proposed technique makes it possible to recover performance very well. This results in a final mAP@0.5 of 96.4%. Through extensive inference benchmarking, it has been shown that the model is suitable for edge deployment. The proposed model was deployed in real-time on a Raspberry Pi 5, with an inference time of about 54.48 ms. The inference latency is much lower on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with TensorRT optimisation, at about 48 ms. The suggested framework's efficiency is also shown by the lower computational complexity ( ∼ 5.6 Giga Floating-Point Operations Per Second (GFLOPs)). The results show that ELTA-YOLOv11 strikes a good balance between deployability, accuracy, and efficiency. This makes it a good choice for real-world edge-based power infrastructure inspection systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Coupling Ti-assisted secondary-hydroxyl activation with H-regulated radical overoxidation control on WO3 photoanodes for highly selective glycerol to dihydroxyacetone conversion
Abstract: Selective photoelectrochemical oxidation of glycerol to dihydroxyacetone (DHA) offers a compelling strategy for integrating solar energy conversion with biomass valorization. However, efficient DHA accumulation remains challenging because two key issues are often underemphasized: the atomic level control of glycerol adsorption geometry for secondary-hydroxyl oxidation, and the suppression of radical mediated overoxidation of the formed DHA. Herein, we report a H, Ti-dual-modified WO3 photoanode (H,Ti)/WO3 that enables highly selective glycerol oxidation to DHA via cooperative interfacial pathway regulation. The (H,Ti)/WO3 photoanode achieves a DHA selectivity of 71.9%—a sharp rise from 35.7% for WO3, and a DHA production rate of 264.5 mmol m−2 h−1, roughly 5 times that of the unmodified counterpart. Mechanistically, highly dispersed Ti sites enhance adsorption of the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol, directing the pathway toward DHA via two‑electron transfer. H‑insertion, in contrast, shifting hydroxyl chemistry away from free •OH mediated deep oxidation toward more surface-bound hydroxyl species and thereby suppressing DHA overoxidation. With this dual-pronged strategy, our work provides new insights into the selective formation and stable accumulation of DHA in biomass photoelectrochemical systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimental Evaluation of Low-Velocity Impact Performance of Glass–Basalt Hybrid Composites: Influence of Fiber Weight Fraction and Impact Energy Levels
Abstract: The growing demand for lightweight structural materials with high impact resistance and energy absorption has driven research into hybrid composites. This study aims to develop a hybrid composite by combining natural basalt fiber with synthetic glass fiber and evaluating the effect of basalt fiber weight fraction on low-velocity impact performance. Composite laminates were fabricated using the hand lay-up technique with epoxy as the thermosetting matrix and reinforced with glass and basalt fibers at varying basalt contents: 0%, 18%, 36%, 52%, 72%, and 100%. Low-velocity impact tests were carried out as per the ASTM D7136 guidelines at three distinct energy levels: 20 J, 40 J, and 80 J. Internal damage was assessed using visual inspection and C-scan imaging, while ANOVA was used to statistically analyze the influence of fiber weight fraction on impact force, energy absorption, and damage area. Pure basalt laminates demonstrated high stiffness but brittle failure, while pure glass laminates absorbed more energy due to their higher ductility. The results revealed that among the hybrid laminates, the laminate with 52% basalt fiber demonstrated the most balanced combination of stiffness, energy absorption, and damage area, exhibiting strong hybrid synergy across all energy levels. Title: Optimal pricing and charging design of the EVCS-EVs network based on a Stackelberg mean field game approach
Abstract: With the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and charging networks, the design of dynamic pricing (DP) and dynamic charging (DC) strategies has become critical for maintaining grid stability and improving economic efficiency. However, traditional DP methods often fail to capture strategic interactions between electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) and large-scale EVs. This paper proposes a Stackelberg mean field game (SMFG) framework for the joint optimization of EVCS's DP and EVs’ DC. The framework models the EVCS as the leader, optimizing DP via Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP), while EVs act as followers whose DC is described by an N-player differential game (DG) and approximated by a MFG. The mean field equilibrium is obtained by solving the coupled Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman and Fokker–Planck–Kolmogorov equations. A hierarchical DP–DC algorithm is developed and proven to converge to a SMF εN-Nash equilibrium (NE). Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves efficient and scalable coordination between DP and DC decisions, while improving computational efficiency and maintaining stable system performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Complex-impedance features for transformer winding-fault diagnosis: Finite-element classification with laboratory frequency-response corroboration
Abstract: Automated interpretation of transformer frequency-response analysis (FRA) often retains impedance magnitude but discards signed real and imaginary components. This study evaluates complex (R, X) features for five-class winding-fault classification and fault-specific severity estimation. A finite-element model supplies network parameters for 210 labelled cases, and a state-space solution supplies the complex frequency response. Evaluation uses repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (20 repeats) with one common healthy reference and fold-local preprocessing. Relative to magnitude-only features, complex frequency-domain features increase LightGBM accuracy from 93.57 % to 94.95 % (+1.38 percentage points, paired p=0.0012). A stacked ensemble reaches 95.45 % accuracy and 94.87 % macro-F1, compared with 95.93 % and 95.52 % for XGBoost; the difference is unresolved (p=0.169), so no superiority is claimed. Laboratory impedance sweeps from one disc-winding specimen corroborate the directions of inductance and anti-resonance changes for controlled axial, disc-space, radial and short-circuit interventions. They also reveal a low-frequency resistance-resolution floor and the absence of decay structure in the inverse-transformed response. A public converter-transformer magnitude–phase record additionally confirms that signed R and X inputs can be reconstructed from an in-service measurement. Because the measured set contains only one healthy sweep and ten retained deformations, it tests physical premises but does not externally validate the classifier. Title: Nonlinear mechanical characteristics of high-voltage circuit breaker based on rigid-body dynamic model with clearance joint
Abstract: The manufacturing and assembly technology of the operating mechanism of the high-voltage circuit breaker leads to clearance joints between components, which significantly affect the mechanical characteristics of the operating mechanism. Based on Lagrangian theory, the mathematical rigid-body dynamic model of the operating mechanism is constructed by integrating the optimized Lankarani-Nikravesh normal contact force model and the optimized tangential friction force model. Essential nonlinear factors, such as cam-roller contact, spring force, buffer force, and mass parameter of components, are considered. The established model possesses the advantages of modularity and parameterization. The nonlinear dynamic behaviors of the operating mechanism are examined under diverse conditions, including the position, size, friction coefficient, and quantity of the clearance joints. The clearance joint results in an increase in instantaneous impact and fluctuations of acceleration. The clearance position with the most pronounced effect causes the peak acceleration to exceed twice that under the ideal operating condition. The simulation results offer essential data foundation for the structural optimization and durability analysis of the operating mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: State-enhanced surrogate environment and multi-time-scale deep reinforcement learning for robotic grinding optimisation
Abstract: Robotic grinding parameter optimisation requires reliable evaluation of how candidate parameter actions affect grinding performance. Title: Asymmetric built-in electric fields in a MoS2/TiO2/CuS S-scheme heterojunction enhance photocatalytic tigecycline degradation and solar-driven interfacial evaporation
Abstract: A ternary MoS2/TiO2/CuS S-scheme heterojunction with asymmetric built-in electric fields was constructed for photocatalytic tigecycline (TGC) degradation and solar-driven interfacial evaporation. Combined UPS-derived band alignment, dark-state XPS, in situ XPS, and DFT analyses revealed opposite interfacial charge-redistribution trends before and under illumination, confirming the S-scheme charge-transfer pathway and supporting the formation of asymmetric built-in electric fields. MTC achieved 96.38% TGC removal within 80 min, with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.0358 min⁻¹ . Scavenging and EPR experiments identified h+ and 1O2 as the main reactive species. LC-MS and ECOSAR analyses were used to explore possible TGC transformation pathways and toxicity trends. After immobilization on melamine foam, MTC-MF maintained approximately 90% TGC removal during 10 h of illuminated single-pass operation and achieved evaporation rates of 1.80 kg·m−2·h−1 in water and 1.72 kg·m−2·h−1 in a 1 mg·L−1 TGC solution. During simultaneous photocatalytic treatment and interfacial evaporation, the TGC removal efficiencies in the solution and condensate reached approximately 85% and 90%, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of MTC-MF for integrated photocatalytic treatment and solar-driven interfacial evaporation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li Z.; Mond M.A.; Wei Z.; Zhang X.-P.

Title: A novel start-up control method for a bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system considering the DC current limiting capability of LCC
Abstract: A bipolar hybrid cascaded multi-terminal high-voltage direct current (MTDC) system is being implemented in the Baihetan–Jiangsu HVDC project in China, where line-commutated converters (LCCs) and modular multilevel converters (MMCs) are integrated in a hybrid DC transmission structure. The uncontrolled charging of MMC submodules can generate large inrush currents, DC voltage fluctuations, and stress on the converter devices for such a hybrid MTDC system during its start-up. To solve these problems, a novel fast and smooth start-up control method of the bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system is proposed which makes full use of the DC current limiting capability of LCCs. The proposed method removes the traditional charging stage which is uncontrollable, and directly charges the MMC submodules under a controlled charging process. 1) A current limiting control strategy is designed for the LCC to limit the charging current of the DC side current to a safe range. 2) MMC submodule charging control strategy is proposed to maintain DC voltage stability and minimize inrush current during the controlled charging process. 3) The smooth transition strategy from start-up control strategy to normal operating control strategy is used to avoid the sudden change of DC voltage, DC current and converter power during the start-up process. The proposed start-up control method has been verified to be able to suppress the inrush current of the charging system, stabilize the DC voltage, and realize fast start-up and smooth start-up of the bipolar hybrid cascaded MTDC system through PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fei W.; Moses P.
Title: Integrating distance relay blinding constraints into security-constrained economic dispatch via protection shift factors
Abstract: The rapid integration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) is introducing new couplings between market-based dispatch and distance-relay security. In meshed transmission networks, economy-driven dispatch of low-cost IBRs can increase reverse fault-current infeeds and erode Zone 1 security margins. This paper proposes a new preventive dispatch framework that integrates specific distance-relay blinding margins into linear Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) constraints through a developed Protection Shift Factor (PSF). The proposed method separates a post-fault network-side transfer factor from an IBR-level fault-current sensitivity using a source-resolved current tracing methodology. This separation reveals whether higher IBR dispatch increases the relay-relevant fault current. Results from Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) simulations of the IEEE 14-bus network using a generic Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC)-type IBR control policy show the IBR's fault-current contribution decreases as its pre-fault power dispatch increases. Conversely, under a retained-active-current policy, the IBR's fault-current contribution increases with higher pre-fault dispatch, thereby establishing an operationally meaningful protection constraint for SCED. The study also demonstrates realistic distance-relay underreach scenarios considering a nearby dispatch-boundary case used for SCED. In the SCED example, conventional dispatch exceeds the EMT-identified projected-current limit, while the protection-constrained dispatch curtails the network-sensitive low-cost IBR and produces a protection-induced nodal-price deduction. Furthermore, the scalability of the framework is validated on the WECC 240-bus system, demonstrating that the linear surrogate maintains exceptional accuracy across bulk grids and successfully arbitrates numerous interacting distance-relay constraints. The developed framework provides a practical route for carrying EMT-identified relay-security margins into linear market clearing and helps mitigate pricing protection-security congestion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
Abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhang S.; Bai Y.; Li C.; Wang J.
Title: Demand-side regulation potential enabled by user-point voltage control
Abstract: Demand-Side Response (DSR) could play a significant role in balancing power supply and demand. This paper exploits the correlation between load voltage and power consumption, whereby load power can be regulated by adjusting supply voltages. A User-Point Voltage Control (UPVC) DSR mechanism is proposed. Compared with the existing approaches, UPVC enables a more flexible way for load regulation as it regulates the voltage supplied to each load, and is able to facilitate full utilisation of load regulation potential and enhanced implementation flexibility. The paper presents a quantitative analysis of the load regulation capacity enabled by UPVC to understand its DSR potential and benefits. The analysis applies initially to a generic Great Britain (GB) medium voltage/low voltage distribution network, with reference to high resolution daily load profiles, and is then extended to urban areas across GB and the entire United States (U.S.). The results are very encouraging as up to 2.4 GW in GB and 30.5 GW in U.S. load power regulation could be achieved for DSR, which indicates that the proposed scheme could serve as a new source of load flexibility in both countries. An economic feasibility analysis further confirms that large-scale deployment of UPVC is economically attractive. © 2026

Title: Investigation of the Mechanical and Tribological Behaviour of Al Alloy and Al/ZrO2Ex-Situ Nano Composites
Abstract: The present study investigates the mechanical and tribological behaviour of Al alloys and Al/ZrO2 ex-situ composites, focusing on their microstructural evolution and property enhancement. Al/ZrO2 composites were synthesised using stir casting, incorporating 1, 3, and 5 wt.% ZrO2 particles. Alloys and composites were characterizedusing X-ray diffraction (XRD), optical microscope (OM), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)to analyse phase formation, particle distribution. Microstructural analysis revealed homogeneous dispersion of ZrO2 particles, promoting load transfer and matrix strengthening. Mechanical properties were analysed using Vickers microhardness and uniaxial tensile tests, demonstrating substantial increases in hardness and tensile strength with increasing ZrO2 content due to grain refinement, dislocation strengthening, and Orowan strengthening mechanisms. Tribological performance was evaluated using a pin-on-disc apparatus under varying loads (10N-30N) and sliding speeds (1 m/sec-3 m/sec). The Al/ZrO2 composites exhibited a significant reduction in the wear (up to 50%) compared to the unreinforced alloy, attributed to the load-bearing capacity of ZrO2 particles and the formation of a protective tribolayer. Surface morphology of the worn samples, analysed using SEM, indicated a transition from abrasive to mild adhesive wear with the addition of ZrO2. Further topographical parameters were studied using atomic force microscopy (AFM), which suggests a decrease in surface roughness from 0.87 µm to 0.70 µm at3wt. % of ZrO2 compared to the base alloy. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Xi S.; Du J.; Li Z.; Li M.; Liu S.; Yuan S.
Title: Structured-DGA transformer for power transformer fault diagnosis under missing-gas setting
Abstract: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is widely used for power transformer fault diagnosis, yet practical DGA records can be incomplete and fault types are long-tailed. To address these issues, we propose a Structured-DGA Transformer (SDGA-Transformer) for fault diagnosis under complete-gas and missing-gas settings. The proposed method represents each DGA record as a structural ratio matrix that encodes pairwise ratios among the five gases, and places concentration-level information on the diagonal. To support missing-gas diagnosis, SDGA-Transformer introduces a missing-indicator matrix and adopts masked self-attention so that the prediction relies only on observed gas-related entries. To mitigate long-tailed data, we adopt inverse-frequency sampling during training. Moreover, we incorporate IEC 60599, Rogers ratios, and the Duval triangle as a rule-guided teacher prior, and use a reliability-aware gating mechanism to activate rule guidance only when it is applicable and consistent. The revised evaluation uses repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing, training-time Missing-{0, 1, 2} augmentation, and identical missing masks for all learning-based baselines. Under this protocol, complete-gas accuracy and macro-F1 are 86.66 ± 5.06% and 85.83 ± 5.67%, respectively. The corresponding values are 79.58 ± 3.93% and 78.80 ± 4.09% under Missing-1, and 67.91 ± 3.33% and 67.02 ± 3.33% under Missing-2. Finally, decision matrices of SDGA-Transformer aligned with the structural ratio matrix provide decision-faithful explanations and fault-type gas-importance for diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enhanced power quality using wind energy based DSTATCOM with decoupled neural network control
Abstract: Modern energy infrastructure is swiftly progressing with increased integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), deregulation of power sector, growing energy demands and advancements in technology. However, these developments present significant obstacles in sustaining Power Quality (PQ) in energy system. Therefore, an innovative PQ enhancement approach, using Wind Energy-based Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) with a Novel Decoupled Neural Network (DNN) based control strategy, is introduced in this work. The proposed system integrates DSTATCOM powered by wind energy to compensate PQ issues. A key feature of the control strategy is the implementation of Decoupled Neural Network (DNN), which includes reactive power compensation and harmonic mitigation sub-networks. The system also features a DC-link voltage control mechanism employing Class Topper Optimized (CTO)-PI controller, which optimizes the DSTATCOM operation by maintaining a stable DC-link voltage. The system is evaluated using MATLAB/Simulink, which demonstrate its ability to curtail PQ disturbances. Additionally, the practical applicability of the proposed DSTATCOM with DNN control, is validated through the development and testing of a laboratory prototype. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhu Y.; Wang Y.; Chen Y.; Zhang L.; Zou L.; Chen X.; Liu W.
Title: Electro-assembly of soy protein and konjac glucomannan into biomimetic scaffolds for cultured meat: Structural and biological performance
Abstract: Anisotropic porous scaffolds for cultured meat were fabricated by freeze-dried soy protein isolate (SPI) and konjac glucomannan (KGM) hybrid hydrogels aligned under a low-voltage electric field. The scaffolds exhibited well-defined oriented pore structures with porosity exceeding 80%, where freezing temperature governed pore architecture: scaffolds prepared at −20 °C produced pores of 50–200 μm, while −80 °C generated finer pores (0–100 μm). SEM analysis revealed an ordered lamellar structure, and mechanical testing further demonstrated higher transverse strength than longitudinal strength. Optimal KGM content (1.0–1.5 wt%) enhanced stiffness (up to 160 kPa), whereas excessive KGM (2.0–2.5 wt%) reduced mechanical strength to 40-80 kPa. The scaffolds displayed excellent water absorption (800%–1147%) and maintained structural integrity after swelling (KGM concentrations: 1.0–2.5 wt%). C2C12 myoblasts showed high seeding efficiency (up to 90%) with enhanced robust adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation. Scaffolds prepared at −20 °C, with pore sizes of 50–200 μm, provided a more favorable microenvironment for cell growth, whereas the overly dense structure formed at −80 °C likely limited cell proliferation and nutrient diffusion. Notably, constructs fabricated at −80 °C with 1.5 wt% KGM achieved excellent mechanical properties (∼56 kPa). This study established an in-house, laboratory-scale, low-voltage direct-current electric-field system and provides a potential sustainable strategy for designing anisotropic scaffolds for cultured meat and highlights the potential of hydrogels in next-generation food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Artificial-intelligence-driven wide-area fault location for transmission systems: A traveling wave-based approach
Abstract: Accurate and timely fault location (FL) is essential for improving grid resilience, minimizing service interruptions, and accelerating system recovery in power transmission networks. Among the various approaches, traveling wave (TW)-based methods-particularly wide-area TW-based techniques-offer high speed and accuracy, making them attractive for modern grids. However, existing TW-based methods often rely on ideal assumptions such as uniform propagation velocities, perfect sensor coverage, and noise-free measurements. These limitations hinder their performance in realistic settings, where line parameters vary, sensors may fail, and data may be incomplete or distorted. This paper presents a novel approach that leverages TW arrival times and a multi-task artificial neural network (ANN) architecture to jointly identify the faulty line and the FL. By formulating sensor placement as an optimization problem and solving it via Integer Linear Programming (ILP), the method significantly reduces hardware requirements while preserving high accuracy. Extensive simulations on a modified IEEE 39-bus system—featuring realistic grid conditions including underground cables, overhead lines, hybrid lines, and substation impedance—show that, for the final enhanced configuration, the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy of 99.62% and a mean absolute fault-location error (MAE) of 166.16 m. © 2026

Title: Online state estimation based on forecasting-correction-refinement framework for active distribution systems
Abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and new types of loads introduces rapid power fluctuations and uncertainties into active distribution systems (ADSs), posing challenges to online distribution system state estimation (DSSE) under sudden power changes. This paper develops a functionally decoupled forecasting-correction-refinement framework for online forecasting-aided DSSE. First, recursive least squares (RLS) generates one-step-ahead forecasts of the system states. The resulting forecasts are then rapidly corrected by a covariance-informed linear least-squares estimation (LLSE) stage using fixed and continuously available micro-phasor measurement unit (μPMU) voltage measurements. Subsequently, weighted least squares (WLS) uses the corrected forecasts as prior information and incorporates the remaining heterogeneous measurements to obtain the final current-slot estimates. To maintain stable recursive updating, the LLSE-corrected forecasts, rather than the final WLS estimates, are fed back to update the RLS model. Case studies on modified IEEE 34-bus and IEEE 123-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves state-estimation accuracy over the benchmark methods. It effectively suppresses large forecasting deviations while maintaining stable recursive operation, and exhibits satisfactory scalability and computational efficiency for online applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
Abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. More broadly, physically modified cereal ingredients can be designed as functional phase-state regulators in frozen staple foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A pre-deployment framework for simulation-driven optimization of robotized manufacturing tasks
Abstract: The pre-deployment configuration of robotic workcells encompasses layout design, task allocation, motion planning, and safety assessment. Despite their strong interdependence, these aspects are still largely addressed through expert knowledge and empirical rules, often in a sequential manner and without a formal optimization framework. This paper proposes a simulation-driven optimization framework that jointly optimizes these interdependent domains during the early design stages. To ensure general applicability, we formulate the overall problem as a hierarchy of nested optimization layers, each dedicated to a specific domain of the robotic task, while accounting for the coupling between them. The overall problem is treated as a black-box iterative optimization, where the unknown underlying function is replaced by a high-fidelity digital model, allowing to evaluate system performance through simulation rather than analytical cost functions. By decoupling domain-specific decisions while preserving their inter-dependencies, the proposed approach can be flexibly applied to heterogeneous scenarios, ranging from fully autonomous robotic operations to human–robot collaborative assemblies within the same manufacturing cell. The framework is evaluated on representative robotic tasks, including both collaborative and human-free scenarios, and its performance is compared against experience-based design solutions. The results show that the proposed method consistently attains better performances than the benchmark strategies enforced as a baseline, demonstrating its effectiveness as a systematic alternative to traditional heuristic-driven design practices. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: TriPort X-gain boost converter integrated with PV and battery sources using optimized PI controller for improved energy management
Abstract: High-efficiency, multi-source DC converters that integrate Renewable Energy Systems (RES) with dynamic load flexibility are in high demand. This work proposes a novel TriPort X-Gain Boost Converter (TXGBC) for efficient energy integration of Photovoltaic (PV) and battery sources that feed a common Direct Current (DC)-load. The proposed converter offers higher voltage conversion ratio, less current ripple and better dynamic stability. By simultaneously utilizing boost, switched-capacitor and reboost actions across the ports, the X-Gain arrangement improves the power transmission capacity and permits wide voltage adaptability under changing irradiance and state-of-charge conditions. To achieve precise regulation and low output voltage overshoot, an Animated Oat Optimization (AOO) based PI controller is introduced. In contrast to classical and swarm-based approaches, the proposed OAT algorithm ensures quick convergence and reliable global optimization of PI gains by dynamically stimulating the search trajectory in multidimensional parameter space. Through error minimization and load-demand prediction, the control technique adaptively balances the PV and battery power flow, ensuring stable operation during sudden transients. The proposed system is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink, simulation results demonstrate that TXGBC performs better than conventional converters due to its substantial static voltage gain, low ripple content, and high efficiency of 97.24%. The proposed controller exhibits a settling time of 0.08 s and overshoot of 0.06%. Additionally, a hardware prototype is developed, and the experimental results are validated with comparison analysis, demonstrating the converter's higher performance and practical viability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Multimodal Fusion of Wavelet-Decomposed MRI and PET for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is crucial for timely clinical intervention and treatment planning. Recent advances in deep learning have facilitated the automatic extraction of informative biomarkers from neuroimaging data. In this study, we proposed a multimodal framework that integrates structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional positron emission tomography (PET) using three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) with wavelet-domain feature extraction (CO.2). First, MRI and PET volumes are decomposed into multiple sub-bands via discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to capture complementary frequency-domain patterns. Next, a custom 3D-CNN extracts multi-scale hierarchical features from each modality (CO.3,4). The resulting modality-specific embeddings are fused at the decision level through a stacked one-dimensional CNN (1D-CNN) ensemble to classify subjects into AD, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal control (NC) groups. Experiments on the ADNI dataset show strong performance across three binary tasks, achieving 97.9% (AD vs. NC), 97.5% (MCI vs. NC), and 99.6% (AD vs. MCI, AUC ≈ 0.997). These results demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-enhanced stacked multimodal model provides a robust and generalizable tool for early-stage AD detection, particularly in distinguishing subtle transitions between MCI and AD (CO.2). ©2027 The author(s). Title: Programming-Based Computational Modelling for Freight Distribution Using Clarke-Wright Savings Method for Route Optimization: A Case Study in Surabaya, Indonesia
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Urban freight pickup in dense metropolitan areas is constrained by short service windows, congestion, and limited vehicle capacity. This study evaluates a practical hybrid heuristic—Clarke-Wright Savings for clustering and Nearest Neighbor for sequencing—for evening pickup operations at a major Indonesian postal logistics hub in Surabaya. Using 46 pickup locations, the MATLAB implementation assesses service coverage, route-time feasibility, fleet requirement, distance efficiency, and capacity utilization under a 500-unit vehicle capacity and a 150-minute maximum route duration. The optimized plan serves all 46 pickup locations with five vehicles, compared with 22 locations served by seven vehicles in the existing operation, and reduces distance per served point from 14.57 to 4.08 km/point while keeping the longest route at 144 minutes. The case also reveals a transferable operational pattern: early routes tend to be filled efficiently in demand-concentrated areas, whereas residual spatially dispersed demand tends to create lower-utilization tail routes. A fixed-seed Genetic Algorithm benchmark further reduced total distance to 152.79 km under the same constraints, but required a longer average runtime of 60.52 seconds compared with 1.13 seconds for the proposed MATLAB-based heuristic. These findings show that transparent classical heuristics can still deliver implementable gains in urban pickup logistics when capacity and time feasibility are evaluated jointly. ©2027 The author(s). Title: Simultaneous fault classification and location estimation in transmission lines using wavelet-based features and a MTL-LSTM network
Abstract: Accurate fault classification and location in transmission lines are essential for improving the reliability and protection performance of modern power systems. Conventional fault location techniques based on impedance or traveling waves often suffer from reduced accuracy under varying operating conditions and fault scenarios. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid intelligent framework based on a Multitask Learning Long Short-Term Memory (MTL-LSTM) neural network for simultaneous fault classification and fault location estimation in transmission lines. First, power system is modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate a comprehensive dataset of fault conditions. Different types of faults conditions including single-line-to-ground (SLG), line-to-line (LL), double-line-to-ground (LLG), three-phase (LLL), and three-phase-to-ground (LLLG) faults with different fault impedances are simulated at multiple locations along the transmission lines. Three-phase voltage and current signals are recorded and processed in MATLAB. To capture transient characteristics of fault signals, the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is applied to extract informative features from voltage and current waveforms. These features are then used as inputs to a MTL-LSTM network designed to perform both fault type classification and fault location estimation simultaneously. In addition to wavelet-based transient features, physics-based indicators derived from conventional fault analysis are incorporated as auxiliary inputs, enabling the network to learn nonlinear relationships between multiple fault-related features and the actual fault characteristics. The proposed method achieves about 89% fault classification accuracy while maintaining the fault location error below 1% of the transmission line length. Furthermore, comprehensive performance evaluations, including robustness analysis under noisy conditions, sensitivity analysis under high-resistance faults, and potential generalization to diverse power system configurations, demonstrate the method's effectiveness and reliability for real-world intelligent transmission line protection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
Abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Comparative Investigation of Deflection in a Bi-directional Curved Functionally Graded Porous Beam Using Unified Shear Deformation Theory
Abstract: The present study investigates the bending characteristics of a two-dimensional functionally graded curved porous beam using unified shear deformation theory (USDT), incorporating shear functions and a modified power law. This approach integrates potential energy, the neutral surface concept, and equilibrium equations to enhance accuracy. Various boundary conditions, such as simply supported (SS), clamped-supported (CS), clamped-clamped (CC), and clamped-free (CF), are employed in the analysis. A metal-ceramic functionally graded beam with both even and uneven porosity is modelled. The symmetrical material gradation ensures that the physical neutral surface aligns with the geometrical neutral surface, which is considered in the formulation. A displacement-based formulation and energy principles are adopted, providing a more comprehensive and precise analysis of the beams. This method accounts for higher-order shear deformation effects, eliminates the need for shear correction factors, and effectively manages the continuous variation of material properties in FGMs. Consequently, it leads to improved predictions of structural behavior, making USDT particularly valuable for advanced material applications. The Hamilton method is employed to derive equilibrium equations for the beams, which are subsequently solved using the Kuhn-Tucker conditions. © 2025 The Author(s).

Authors: Zhang T.; Liu J.; Duan Y.; Yang T.; Jiang H.
Title: Gallic acid modulates the balance among network structure, water stability, and antioxidant function in corn peptide-konjac glucomannan gels
Abstract: Plant-based gels increasingly need to reconcile mechanical integrity, water stability and bioactivity, yet most designs still rely on intact proteins whose folded or aggregated structures limit molecular accessibility. Corn peptide (CP) offers a distinct but underused route: a short-chain, mobile and chemically exposed plant-peptide fraction with intrinsic antioxidant potential, but limited ability to form self-supporting networks. This study treated CP as an interaction-active, network-modulating component within a konjac glucomannan (KGM) scaffold and examined how gallic acid (GA) concentration translated peptide-associated reactivity into macroscopic gel performance. GA regulated the CP-KGM matrix in a concentration-dependent manner. At 0.3% GA, the gel combined low syneresis and freeze-thaw water loss, shorter water-relaxation times, high cohesiveness, rapid stress relaxation, and greater microstructural continuity. Higher GA levels further enhanced ABTS and T-AOC responses but were associated with larger operational hydrophobic-association indices and reduced network uniformity. Operational extraction indices and FTIR changes were consistent with concentration-dependent reorganization of non-covalent association. In simplified docking models, the two representative CP fragments yielded scores of −4.3 and −3.7 kcal/mol, whereas the KGM oligomer yielded −2.9 kcal/mol under the respective docking setups. This descriptive pattern suggests a possible peptide-biased interaction tendency. Accordingly, peptide-biased association is proposed as a working model for interpreting how GA may couple peptide-rich domains with the KGM-rich environment. These findings identify CP as a reactive plant-peptide component and establish a property-dependent formulation map: 0.3% GA favors an integrated combination of water stability, cohesion, stress dissipation, and microstructural continuity, whereas higher GA levels favor in vitro antioxidant output. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A fast adaptive finite element method for nonlocal diffusion problems on octree-based adaptive Cartesian multilevel mesh formulation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We propose a novel adaptive finite element method (AFEM) algorithm for nonlocal problems discretized on an n-dimensional Cartesian mesh. Based on the octree data structure, an efficient mesh algorithm on the Cartesian mesh is implemented, improving search efficiency for elements in the nonlocal neighborhood. We prove that when the nonlocal kernel function is radially symmetric, the number of distinct entries in the stiffness matrix on the Cartesian mesh depends only on the mesh depth. Based on this property, a fast assembly algorithm is designed to reduce the computational cost of solving nonlocal problems with AFEM. Numerical experiments successfully implement adaptive solutions for 2D and 3D nonlocal problems, verifying the effectiveness of the new AFEM algorithm. © 2026

Title: Enhancing DER hosting capacity of unbalanced low-voltage distribution networks with network exchangers: An Australian case study
Abstract: The rapid growth and subsequent utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly in low-voltage networks, is pushing distribution networks to the brink of their hosting capacity. Distribution network operators, especially in DER-rich countries such as Australia, are exploring novel technologies and effective strategies to enhance DER integration while maintaining network integrity, as an alternative to costly network upgrades. One such technology developed and introduced is the network exchanger (NEx), which aims to enhance hosting capacity by regulating voltage, mitigating current imbalance, and power factor correction at the distribution transformer. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of NEx, compared with on-load tap changers and distribution static synchronous compensators, through an extensive simulation study that models projected growth in photovoltaic and electric vehicle penetration as per the Integrated System Plan released by the Australian Energy Market Operator, using a large-scale, real-world distribution network comprising over 8000 buses, and located in Queensland, Australia. Simulation results indicate breaches in network integrity under business-as-usual conditions in both step-change and progressive-change scenarios. The performance of each technology is benchmarked across six low-voltage networks that exhibit higher levels of network violations and photovoltaic curtailment, with NEx resolving all voltage breaches and reducing transformer loading and photovoltaic curtailment by noticeable amounts, which can aid in delaying costly network augmentation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposites with direct catalyst-support junctions for low-iridium proton exchange membrane water electrolysis
Abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is considered a promising technology for sustainable green hydrogen production, but it is still limited by the sluggish acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), which requires scarce Ir-based catalysts. Herein, Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposites were designed to reduce Ir loading in PEMWE anodes. By controlling the Ir/W ratio, the density of direct Ir/IrOx-WO3 junctions was systematically tuned. Ir/IrOx-WO3 nanocomposite with an Ir content of 30 wt% (IW-30) exhibited the highest acidic OER activity, achieving an overpotential of 278.3 mV at 10 mA cm-² and a mass activity of 457 A gIr-¹ (1.55 V vs. RHE). Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy revealed that residual metallic Ir in IW-30 was oxidized more rapidly during acidic OER than in IW-55, indicating that direct Ir/IrOx-WO3 junctions facilitate the formation of catalytically active oxidized Ir species. In PEMWE tests, IW-30 delivered 3 A cm-² at 1.9 V and maintained stable operation for 450 h at 2 A cm-² with an ultralow Ir loading of 0.25 mgIr cm-². These findings reveal that direct Ir/IrOx-WO₃ junctions accelerate Ir oxidation under OER conditions, providing a viable strategy for developing low-Ir and durable PEMWE anode catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Incremental resistance MPPT algorithm with proportional integral compensator for extended DC-DC buck-boost converter in PV systems
Abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power output is significantly influenced by environmental and climatic variables, such as the sun's irradiance, air humidity, and ambient temperature. In addition, most PV power sources have relatively small output voltages not suited for direct utilization by common loads. Additionally, PV power output depends also on the PV operating voltage and current. In this sense, a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is required to achieve maximum power output and improved efficiency in PV systems. Due to shadowing or fast irradiance changes, MPPT algorithms must operate at high speed and accuracy. Thus, this paper proposes a MPPT control strategy based on incremental resistance (INR) combined with a proportional-integral (PI) compensator (INR-PI). This approach modifies the seldom used INR MPPT algorithm to set the current and combines it with a proportional-integral compensator to regulate the I-V operating point of the PV panel. This reformulates the INR principle as a PV panel voltage regulation problem ensuring closed-loop stability and disturbance rejection. The theoretical analysis considers the dynamics of the input current in a quadratic Buck-Boost converter with an extended duty-cycle range in the Buck voltage region, connected to a DC microgrid. The proposed MPPT technique is designed to ensure fast and efficient operation of PV systems under rapidly changing environmental conditions. To validate this control system, initial simulations were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, followed by experimental testing with a laboratory prototype setup. Both numerical and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the feedback-based incremental resistance algorithm in tracking the maximum power point (MPP) of PV systems when irradiance fluctuates quickly. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Hydroxyl reinforcement effect on the heterointerfaced Rh/CoP remarkably accelerates hydrogen evolution reaction in alkaline media
Abstract: The heterointerfaced Rh-CoP/C was designed and evaluated as a robust electrocatalyst towards the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), offering an immense playground for an anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). Notably, Rh-CoP/C spontaneously converses to OH-Rh-CoP/C during alkaline HER via hydroxyl (OH) adsorption and its OH reinforcement effect on the alkaline HER performance was deeply explored by density functional theory (DFT) calculations coupled with experimental measurements. The results demonstrate that OH adsorption at the heterointerface not only promotes water dissociation but also creates a pathway for efficient hydrogen spillover to boost hydrogen (H2) release, thereby obviously enhancing alkaline HER. Moreover, OH adsorption stabilizes the heterointerface by suppressing P atom migration, ensuring long-term structural integrity. In addition, the optimized heterointerfaced OH-Rh/CoP catalyst exhibits excellent alkaline HER activity, achieving an ultralow overpotential of 10 and 186 mV at 20 and 500 mA cm−2, respectively, even surpassing commercial 20 wt% JM-Pt/C catalyst and most of previously reported noble metal-based catalysts. When deployed in an anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE), it requires a low cell voltage of 1.731 V to reach 1 A cm−2, along with outstanding operational stability over 2100 h with a minimal degradation rate of 61 µV h−1. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Area-based SEL–Π control for voltage safety under disturbances and topology changes
Abstract: Maintaining voltage safety in DER-rich distribution feeders is essential for reliable operation, equipment protection, and renewable-energy integration. This paper proposes an online robust voltage-control framework that separates sensitivity/uncertainty adaptation from real-time constraint enforcement. The main novelty is an area-based SEL–Π realization, where Structured Error Learning (SEL) updates within-area voltage–reactive sensitivity blocks and disturbance bounds from closed-loop measurements, while projected control (Π) solves local robust quadratic programs (QPs) with tightened voltage limits, inverter constraints, and slack-assisted feasibility. Centralized operation is recovered as the special case K=1. On the Southern California Edison 56-bus feeder over a 24 h real-data-driven stress study with 14 controlled buses, decentralized SEL–Π eliminates severe open-loop violations, maintains the prescribed voltage band in the tested topology-change case, and achieves centralized-reference-level voltage safety. Additional diagnostics show substantial cross-area coupling and 96.7–98.8% realized residual-envelope coverage, with QP slack numerically zero at a 10−4 tolerance. Compared with tuned local PI feedback, SEL–Π achieves voltage safety with substantially lower actuation, while Π-QP computation remains well below the 6-s control interval and SEL is executed only intermittently. © 2026

Title: Operation-oriented dependency-aware joint probabilistic forecasting of load and renewable generation for microgrid dispatch
Abstract: This paper presents a forecasting–scenario–dispatch framework for day-ahead microgrid operation. Its forecasting component, termed the Dependency-Aware Fusion Quantile Network (DAFQ-Net), jointly trains three marginal quantile forecasts for electricity load, wind power, and photovoltaic (PV) generation. The main architectural design is an adaptive gate that balances shared historical context and cross-task attended future context for each target. The network uses learned associations to control information exchange, but it does not directly estimate the full joint probability distribution. A Gaussian copula subsequently combines the marginal quantiles and reconstructs cross-variable and 24-hour temporal dependence from training-period forecast errors. The resulting scenarios are evaluated in a proof-of-concept stochastic dispatch model. Tests on two hourly microgrid datasets show improved marginal scores and, for the complete DAFQ-Net–copula pipeline, improved scenario and dispatch metrics against the implemented baselines. The results are case-study evidence under the stated data, copula, and dispatch assumptions, rather than evidence of a general joint-density model or universal operating-cost reduction. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Analysis of the electro-thermal characteristics of MOA with average power equivalent method by incorporating stray capacitance
Abstract: The voltage distribution across the varistor blocks of metal oxide arrester (MOA) becomes non-uniform due to stray capacitance which imposes greater electrical stress on varistor block located near the high-voltage electrode. Consequently, the upper varistor blocks undergoes greater thermal stress during operation, resulting in accelerated aging. An enhanced wide-range MOA model incorporating stray capacitance is proposed in this paper to accurately characterize the electrical behavior of the arrester. By integrating the circuit model with the electro-thermal model through the average power equivalent method (APEM), APEM effectively solves the challenge of computational resources due to time-varying excitations. Experiment is conducted to validate the accuracy of APEM and both models. This paper systematically examines the effects of stray capacitance and harmonics on the electro-thermal behavior of MOA. It is found that stray capacitance causes higher voltage on the top varistor block while also causing an overall increase in temperature and thermal non-uniformity. These effects are further significantly amplified in the presence of odd-order harmonics. The conclusions provide a theoretic reference for optimizing the durability and heat dissipation performance of MOA. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fast frequency parameter adaptive optimization strategy for TD3 wind turbines guided by frequency response mechanism
Abstract: With growing wind penetration, reduced inertia raises frequency instability risks. To fully exploit wind frequency regulation capability, this paper proposes a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)-based adaptive optimization strategy for wind turbine (WTG) fast frequency parameters guided by frequency response mechanisms. First, a time-domain analytical model of WTG frequency response with deadband is established, revealing coupled effects of deadband threshold, regulation coefficient, and wind penetration on system frequency dynamics. On this basis, a deep reinforcement learning framework is developed: the frequency response model is embedded into a three-stage mechanism-guided reward function, where physical safety boundaries constrain the minimum regulation coefficient in the linear penalty region, and unsafe actions are penalized quadratically proportional to deviation. Meanwhile, dual experience replay buffers with linearly decaying sampling are constructed, enabling smooth transition from a safe baseline to autonomous exploration via knowledge pre-filling. Finally, simulations under varying wind speeds, multiple disturbances, and complex conditions are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink. Title: Joint clearing strategy for power-carbon-frequency regulation markets considering dynamic carbon pricing and green certificate mechanisms
Abstract: To promote multi-market integration and drive the low-carbon transformation of the energy system, this paper focuses on the coordinated operation of the electricity-carbon-ancillary service market. It introduces a dynamic carbon pricing mechanism to reflect real-time carbon cost signals and incorporates a green certificate trading mechanism to incentivize clean energy consumption. A bi-level joint market clearing model considering the dynamic carbon pricing mechanism and the green certificate mechanism is established. The upper-level model aims to maximize energy system profits, obtaining optimal bidding strategies by incorporating declared capacity and price constraints. The lower-level model seeks to minimize system operating costs, determining the optimal clearing prices and winning quantities for each market based on constraints such as power balance, carbon balance, frequency regulation balance, and market clearing rules. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint clearing mechanism effectively increases clean energy consumption by 73.90%, reduces carbon emissions by 26.88%, and enhances total profits by 10.22%. Additionally, it guides flexible resources to participate in frequency regulation ancillary services through electricity-carbon price signals, promoting the synergistic achievement of economic and environmental objectives. Title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
Abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Based on Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) for uncertainty quantification, a three-layer robust optimization model is formulated to maximize the uncertainty radius under a predefined power loss target. By incorporating the worst condition defined as minimized power generation coupled with maximized load, the original three-layer model is converted into a two-layer model for efficient solution. Furthermore, the Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm (RVEA) is employed to solve the model, obtaining a Pareto solution set that reflects the trade‑off between robustness and economy. Simulations based on the IEEE 33‑bus system demonstrate that ESS forms differentiated charging and discharging strategies for different operating scenarios, and the system exhibits higher sensitivity to wind power fluctuations. Title: Nonlinear Behavior of Honeycomb Structure Under Large Deformations Using Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation and Periodic Homogenization
Abstract: This study determines the elastic constants and evaluates the in-plane mechanical behavior of hexagonal and re-entrant (auxetic) honeycomb structures under large deformations by utilizing the Absolute Nodal Coordinate Formulation (ANCF) for modeling elastic forces and applying periodic boundary conditions (PBCs) to precisely control deformations at the boundaries. A representative volume element (RVE) was selected, and static equations were derived by modeling cell walls as beam elements using the ANCF based on the finite element method (FEM) and the periodic boundary conditions were subsequently implemented. After solving the static equations, analytical validation was performed for small deformations. The results demonstrate that honeycomb structures exhibit nonlinear behavior under large deformations, which is crucial to determine for dynamic applications. Authors: Yin Q.; Peng S.; Li Y.
Title: Phosphomolybdate-guided synthesis of large-interlayer-spacing phosphate-modified NiOOH array for ampere-level oxygen evolution reaction
Abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is a promising route for green hydrogen production, but the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) limits the overall efficiency. Layered NiOOH is a cost-effective OER electrocatalyst, yet its activity and stability—especially at high current densities—remain insufficient. Herein,we propose a novel design strategy that combines phosphate ion (Pi) modification with interlayer spacing enlargement in NiOOH. A large phosphomolybdate (PM) anion serves as an situ self-removable pillaring agents during the reconstruction of nickel molybdate into a Pi-intercalated Ni(OH)2 precatalyst (Ni(OH)2-PM-Pi), which is then electrochemically activated to form NiOOH-PM-Pi. This material features enhanced Ni4+ content, abundant oxygen vacancies (V..o), and expanded interlayer spacing. The elevated Ni4+ and V..o cooperatively accelerate OER via the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), while the expanded interlayer spacing enhances mass transport within the NiOOH interlayers, greatly suppressing interlayer localized acidification and increasing interlayer utilization, thereby improving the catalyst's stability and activity. Consequently, the resulting catalyst exhibits an iR-corrected overpotential of only 324 mV at 1000 mA cm−2 and maintains excellent stable operation for 500 h at ~1000 mA cm−2 in Pi-containing KOH electrolyte, outperforming most reported Ni-based OER electrocatalysts. This work offers a design approach to achieve both high activity and high stability in OER catalysts under ampere-level current densities. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Edge-weight coupled Gaussian masking for resilient operation optimization of multi-energy virtual power plants under eavesdropping-injection attacks
Abstract: Multi-energy virtual power plants (VPPs) coordinate distributed electricity and heat resources through communication links that may expose incremental-cost data and permit false-data injection. This paper develops an edge-weight coupled Gaussian masking (EW-CGM) method for resilient VPP operation under eavesdropping-injection attacks. The operation layer embeds electrical and thermal loss sensitivities in the incremental-cost conditions. An attacker model uses intercepted historical data to estimate private cost coefficients and construct ramp-type false commands. EW-CGM applies antisymmetric, time-decaying Gaussian masks to individual links, preserving global aggregation while increasing parameter-estimation uncertainty. Residual detection and predicted-state recovery address the resulting deviations. The analysis and case studies evaluate parameter inference, convergence, detection, recovery, and sensitivity to load volatility and repeated sub-threshold attacks, while retaining the loss-aware operating reference under the nominal tested attack, outage, and recovery conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
