Title: From centralized monitoring to cooperative aerial intelligence: A MARL–FANET approach for smart microgrid monitoring and defect analysis
Abstract: A key requirement of smart microgrids is the need for rapid and reliable monitoring that adapts to changing circumstances to ensure system stability, security, and efficiency. Traditional monitoring techniques using fixed sensor networks and centralized supervision methods can face issues such as low spatiotemporal density, slow response times to faults, and susceptibility to single point failures. To overcome these drawbacks, a UAV-based cooperative monitoring technique for inspection and defect detection of smart microgrids is presented in this paper. These UAVs act like a Flying Ad Hoc Network (FANET), which helps share local observations with each other. A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm, which includes centralised training with decentralised execution, is used for cooperative monitoring. Defect detection is achieved by using a multimodal input of various modalities for each individual UAV. The proposed framework is evaluated in a simulation environment involving representative smart microgrid assets, including transmission lines, photovoltaic panels, and transformers. Experimental results demonstrate an average fault detection accuracy of 95.3%, an average detection latency of 7.9 s, and an average UAV energy consumption of 14.2 Wh while maintaining 91.4% coverage efficiency. In addition, the FANET communication network achieves a packet delivery ratio of 97.6% with an average communication latency of 112 ms. To ensure fair performance evaluation, the proposed MARL–FANET framework is compared against multiple baseline approaches, including fixed sensor-based monitoring systems, centralized UAV coordination, and non-cooperative UAV deployment strategies. This comparative evaluation provides a consistent benchmark for assessing improvements in detection accuracy, latency reduction, and energy efficiency achieved through cooperative multi-agent learning and decentralized execution. The results indicate that cooperative UAV-based monitoring can significantly enhance microgrid situational awareness, distributed fault response capability, and operational resilience. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Segura-Duque V.; Griffin L.
Title: Hand clearances in ergonomic design: A scoping review of types, methods, and measurements
Abstract: Hand clearances, the space available for hand access and operation, are essential for manual workspace design. However, clearance types lack systematic characterization, unified methods, and standardized criteria for defining adequate space during manual tasks. This scoping review analyzed 26 records published between 1960 and 2026. Ninety-four unique clearances were identified and organized into four categories: Openings, Operational Clearances, Object-Specific Clearances, and PPE Allowances. Four methodological approaches and eight methodological gaps were identified, including reliance on static measurements, inadequate treatment of PPE, small or outdated samples, and limited reporting standards. Widely cited clearance values originate from small, demographically narrow 1960s studies and have propagated with limited re-validation. The review introduces the functional clearance margin as a conceptual proposition describing the additional space beyond hand dimensions required for functional operation rather than fit alone. These findings provide a foundation for developing more representative, dynamic, and standardized approaches to hand clearance design. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A fault-responsive control strategy for improving superimposed distance protection in mixed GFES–IIDG grids
Abstract: In high-penetration inverter-based resources (IBR) system, the widespread deployment of grid-forming energy storage (GFES) and inverter-interfaced distributed generation (IIDG) introduces complex and time-varying behaviors in power frequency fault component (PFFC) networks. These behaviors, shaped by diverse low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategies, lead to significant uncertainty in the IBR PFFC impedance, undermining the performance of power frequency superimposed distance protection (PFSDP). This paper first constructs fault sequence component equivalent networks under representative GFES and IIDG control strategies. Impedance-plane analysis is used to characterize the transient evolution of characteristic impedance and identify key contributors to PFSDP performance degradation. To address these challenges, a fault-responsive sequence voltage control (FRSVC) strategy is proposed. This control scheme bypasses the outer-loop controls post-fault and output actively shaped sequence current components to emulate synchronous generator impedance behavior. The proposed strategy stabilizes the PFFC impedance, enables PFSDP to maintain correct operation under mixed-source conditions. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving protection sensitivity in systems with both GFES and IIDG. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Modeling the propagation of risk in large-scale power outages: Integrating ETA, directed-weighted CN, and risk chain mining
Abstract: To understand the systemic propagation and interdependencies of various risk factors in large-scale power outages, a novel risk evolution framework is proposed, incorporating Event Tree Analysis (ETA), directed-weighted Complex Network (CN), and risk chain mining. A network comprising 37 nodes and 130 edges is constructed using data from 29 large-scale power outages spanning from 1965 to 2025. Topological analysis identifies critical propagation nodes, including power plant failures and grid instability. Robustness tests reveal the network's resilience to random disruptions but also expose its vulnerability to targeted attacks. Furthermore, high-risk causal chains are directly extracted and classified from the network, and path mining further uncovers 24 high-risk six-node chains, which are categorized into four distinct propagation patterns. This integrated framework offers a data-driven methodology for characterizing large-scale power outage risks, yielding structurally suggestive priorities to inform prevention and mitigation strategies for power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yu D.; Xing Z.; Tan H.; Chen H.; Wang T.; Zhang H.; Wang L.
Title: Effect of atmospheric cold plasma treatment on the structural characteristics and gel properties of hemp protein isolate
Abstract: Hemp protein isolate (HPI) is a promising plant protein source owing to its balanced amino acid composition and low allergenicity; however, its propensity for aggregation severely limits its functional and gel properties. This study investigated the effects of atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment on the structural characteristics and heat-induced gel behaviour of HPI. ACP treatment induced structural modifications in HPI, resulting in increased carbonyl content, enhanced exposure of sulfhydryl and hydrophobic groups, reduced particle size, and improved solubility, which increased from 19.6% to 40.9%. Under optimal conditions (350 W, 5 min), ACP treatment promoted protein unfolding, which increased the accessibility of sulfhydryl groups and hydrophobic regions involved in subsequent intermolecular interactions during gel formation. Consequently, ACP-treated HPI exhibited improved gel hardness, viscoelasticity, and water holding capacity (WHC), with the maximum WHC reaching 78.11% at a protein concentration of 12%. Microstructural observations and low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) revealed that these structural modifications facilitated the formation of a more continuous and compact gel matrix with restricted water mobility. Overall, moderate ACP treatment effectively improved the structural and gel properties of HPI and enhanced the stability of the heat induced gel system. These findings provided a basis for improving HPI gel properties and expanding its application in food products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Cui Z.; Dong Y.
Title: Two-level stochastic programming for optimal operation of wind-thermal-hydropower systems in day-ahead and balancing markets
Abstract: Renewable-rich power systems require flexible scheduling strategies that can coordinate energy, reserve, and storage operation under uncertainty. This study develops a two-level stochastic scheduling framework for a wind–thermal–hydropower–pumped-storage system operating in day-ahead and balancing markets. The framework links day-ahead commitments with scenario-dependent balancing actions to manage uncertainty in wind power, load demand, and hydrological inflow. An initial set of 100 uncertainty scenarios is generated and reduced to 10 representative scenarios, achieving a 90% reduction in scenario count while preserving the system's main stochastic characteristics. The model is validated on a modified IEEE 14-bus system integrating 145 MW of wind generation, 150 MW of thermal generation, a 30 MW hydropower unit, and a 30 MW pumped-storage unit. The optimized daily operating cost is $22,104.52, demonstrating that coordinated hydropower and pumped-storage operation can support renewable integration while maintaining system reliability. Comparative optimization results show that Harris Hawks Optimization achieves a lower best objective value than Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Grey Wolf Optimizer, with improvements of 1.39%, 2.58%, and 1.14%, respectively. Sensitivity analyses further show that reducing thermal ramping capability increases the operating cost to $23,542.49; increasing minimum up- and down-time limits raises it to $23,724.91; and reducing transmission capacity raises it to $24,263.91. These results confirm that hydro-storage flexibility, transmission availability, and thermal-unit responsiveness are key factors in reducing balancing pressure and improving the economic performance of renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026

Title: Coordinating the multi-sites synergistic adsorptions by heterogenizing Ru nanoclusters onto NiCoP nanoarrays for concurrent highly-selective biomass upgrading and efficient hydrogen evolution at large current densities
Abstract: Electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) offers an attractive route for the concurrent production of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and hydrogen, yet insufficient coordination among multiple adsorption sites limits its high selectivity at large current densities. Herein, Ru nanoclusters are heterogenized onto NiCoP nanoarrays to construct Ru–P–(Ni/Co) heterointerfaces, which coordinate the multi-site synergistic adsorption for highly selective HMFOR coupled with efficient HER. Operando and theoretical studies reveal that differentiated adsorption synchronizes HMF activation and hydroxyl supply, thereby lowering key oxidation barriers and promoting FDCA formation. Meanwhile, the Ru–P–(Ni/Co) interfacial ensembles also facilitate H2O activation and H* conversion for alkaline HER. Benefiting from this mechanism, the catalyst exhibits 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.6 V, achieving 93.1% selectivity and 99.4% Faradaic efficiency of FDCA, with excellent stability for HMFOR. It also exhibits outstanding HER activity, delivering 1265 mA cm−2 at −0.7 V and sustained durability for over 100 h. Eventually, the bifunctional catalyst enables simultaneous FDCA and H2 generation at 138 mA cm−2 at 2.0 V in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work provides a mechanistic framework for site-specific co-adsorption and cross-interfacial reactant coupling, offering a promising strategy for highly selective biomass upgrading and efficient hydrogen evolution at large current densities. © 2026

Title: Automated Indentation Geometry Detection for Hardness Measurement: A Vision-Based Nondestructive Evaluation Approach
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. This study introduces an automated framework for indentation geometry detection and measurement using two complementary strategies: a classical image processing pipeline based on OpenCV and a YOLOv10n deep learning model. To replicate realistic industrial conditions, St37 steel blocks with unpolished, roughly machined surfaces and random markings were tested under Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell A hardness standards. A batch of microscope images was gathered, manually annotated, and subsequently expanded via data augmentation to obtain a diverse and reliable labeled image set. The classical pipeline employed brightness enhancement, thresholding, morphological filtering, and contour-based geometry extraction, while YOLOv10n was trained on the augmented dataset and refined using geometry-based post-processing. The YOLOv10n model achieved a mean average precision (detection accuracy) of 94% and reduced mean absolute error by 42–51% compared with classical image processing (p < 0.05). Furthermore, it maintained 96–97% accuracy under brightness variation, rotation, and mirroring, whereas the classical approach deteriorated to 79–84%. YOLOv10n provides a robust, precise, and scalable solution for automated hardness testing, supporting the advancement of automation in industrial quality control. ©2027 The author(s). Title: s-orbital modulated d-band center of Cu1−δ active site via interfacial electron spillover effect for nitrate reduction to ammonia

Title: Influence of natural ester insulating oil on water molecules migration and aggregation behavior in oil-paper insulation systems
Abstract: The hydrophilicity of natural ester insulating oil can maintain the moisture content in transformer insulating pressboard at a relatively low level. To reveal the regulatory mechanism of natural ester insulating oil on the diffusion and aggregation behavior of water molecules. This article conducted Frequency Domain Spectroscopy (FDS) tests on mineral oil and natural ester oil-paper insulation systems with varying moisture content levels. Molecular dynamics simulations were employed to analyze the diffusion behavior of water molecules in both composite systems, while quantum chemical methods were used to calculate and analyze the electrostatic potential interactions between the two types of insulating oils and water dimers. The experimental and simulation results corroborate each other, collectively revealing that the electrostatic attraction interactions, primarily driven by hydrogen bonds, between natural ester insulating oil and water molecules are stronger than the forces required for water molecules to detach from cellulose paper. Title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
Abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Effect of low - methoxy pectin, heat treatment and pH on interfacial properties of purified cricket protein
Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of cricket protein isolate at A/W and O/W interfaces on their interfacial rheology. Dilatational and shear rheological analyses were performed to elucidate the emulsifying and foaming properties, as well as the short- and long-term stability, of cricket protein-stabilized emulsions and foams. Additionally, the adsorption kinetics of the proteins at the interfaces were assessed. The results showed a decrease in interfacial tension at both interfaces, with values at saturation (10% w/w protein isolate) of 35 ± 2 mN/m at the A/W interface and 22 ± 2 mN/m at the O/W interface, similar to those of several vegetable proteins. The dilatational results showed that the films exhibited viscoelastic behavior at both interfaces, with the oil interface appearing more structured. Authors: Lin J.; Hu Y.; Wang Y.; Cheng T.; Liu X.
Title: Research on the superhydrophobic surface of silicone rubber induced by femtosecond laser
Abstract: Superhydrophobic surfaces have become an important research area for enhancing material surface performance due to their excellent water-repellency and self-cleaning properties. In this work, we propose a method to fabricate superhydrophobic silicone rubber surfaces by femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano hierarchical structures. The effects of laser fluence, scanning speed and filling spacing on the surface morphology and wetting performance were systematically studied. Through single-factor experiments, a superhydrophobic surface with a contact angle of 157.7° and a rolling angle of 4.6° was prepared under the conditions of a fluence of 26 J·cm−2, a scanning speed of 50 mm·s−1, and a filling spacing of 15 μm. Scanning electron microscopy analysis indicated that the superhydrophobicity originated from the micro-nano hierarchical structures induced by the laser, which effectively promoted the droplets to maintain the Cassie-Baxter wetting state. Energy spectrum analysis further revealed that the main elemental compositions remained largely unchanged after laser treatment, while XPS analysis indicated the cleavage of C–Si bonds and the formation of non‑polar C–C(H) bonds, which are beneficial for surface hydrophobicity. Combined with the changes in the microscopic morphology, it indicates that the improvement in surface wettability is mainly attributed to the change in morphology. In addition, droplet impact tests showed that the superhydrophobic surface induced by laser could make the droplets rebound rapidly and completely detach, with a contact time of only about 13 ms. © 2026

Authors: Sheoran U.; Rizwan M.; Nangia U.
Title: Contrastive self-supervised temporal transformers with physics-guided regularisation for low-label photovoltaic array fault diagnosis
Abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) arrays under variable irradiance and temperature are susceptible to incipient line-to-line faults (LLF), open-circuit faults (OCF), partial shading faults (PSF), and high-impedance LLF (HILL), whose fault currents fall below the protection threshold at the maximum power point, where the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller masks the fault signature. Data-driven diagnosis achieves high accuracy but typically requires large labeled fault datasets that are difficult to obtain in operational plants. This paper proposes a three-stage self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for PV array fault diagnosis operating exclusively on sequential voltage, current, and power measurements. A temporal encoder (1-D convolutional neural network front end + four-layer Transformer) is pretrained on unlabeled monitoring sequences via NT-Xent contrastive learning with PV-safe augmentations, then fine-tuned with limited labels using a physics-guided regularizer that penalizes violations of the P=VI relation in the embedding space. An evidential Dirichlet-output uncertainty head enables calibrated selective decision-making, achieving an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.0214 and out-of-distribution flagging rates of 41–87% under unseen operating conditions. On a simulated 10 × 3 grid-connected PV array, the framework attains 98.26 ± 0.20% overall accuracy with only 50 labeled samples per class, outperforming the semisupervised ladder network by 1.38 percentage points (pp) and SSL time-series baselines (TS-TCC, TFPred) by 1.90–2.52 pp. Validation on the real experimental GPVS-Faults dataset yields 98.14 ± 0.18% accuracy (AUROC 0.996, ECE 0.012), a sim-to-real gap of only 0.12 pp, and a macro-F1 of 0.961 under realistic class imbalance. The physics loss improves accuracy by +1.65 pp at 10 dB SNR, confirmed significant by McNemar's test (p < .01). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li P.; Jing C.; Liang C.; Shen Y.; Jia Q.
Title: Voltage sag support strategy based on cooperative optimization control of photovoltaic inverter currents
Abstract: Conventional local Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) strategies for photovoltaic (PV) inverters in high-penetration distribution networks lack global coordination and struggle to balance optimal voltage support with real-time responsiveness. To address this, a voltage sag support strategy based on cooperative PV inverter current control is proposed. First, a multi-inverter cooperative voltage-sag support model is established using the nodal impedance matrix and the superposition theorem, quantifying the cross-node voltage-support potential enabled by mutual impedance coupling. Second, targeted global optimization models are developed for symmetrical and asymmetrical faults, aiming to maximize positive-sequence voltage recovery and coordinate positive- and negative-sequence suppression, respectively, to achieve system-level optimal voltage support. Finally, to overcome the computational latency of online optimization, a Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based quasi-static control strategy is proposed. By learning the mapping between grid states and optimal current setpoints offline, this strategy ensures real-time cooperative voltage-sag support while retaining near-optimal performance. Simulations on a 6-node feeder and the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that the proposed strategy increases the minimum residual voltage by up to 10.84% under symmetrical faults, while the quasi-static strategy compresses control delays from 106.34 ms to 4.85 ms, providing an effective, hardware-free solution for voltage sag support. © 2026

Authors: Asghari-Gharakheili M.; Taheri-Otaghsara S.S.
Title: Simulation-based multi-objective optimization of reliability-centered maintenance in power distribution networks considering mode-dependent failure behavior
Abstract: An efficient power distribution system must provide reliable power delivery and maintain voltage levels with minimal fluctuations. To achieve these objectives, regulatory organizations implement preventive maintenance programs to enhance system reliability and extend equipment lifespan. The reliability of a distribution system is one of the key indicators used to evaluate the service quality of electric distribution utilities. Considering the critical importance of reducing operational and capital expenditures, optimizing preventive maintenance programs is essential for minimizing costs while improving reliability. This study proposes a multi-objective model for optimizing the reliability of electrical power distribution systems. The primary objective is to minimize system maintenance costs while simultaneously maximizing the overall system reliability index. The NSGA-II algorithm is employed to solve the multi-objective optimization model, and the resulting Pareto front is presented. A key innovation of this study is the explicit modeling of mode-dependent failure behavior, where each maintenance action selectively restores only the targeted failure modes to their as-new condition. This approach allows for a more realistic representation of component degradation, improves the fidelity of reliability estimation, and enables more precise and cost-effective maintenance scheduling compared with traditional aggregated failure-rate models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Role of a Pd cocatalyst on cuprite dendrites in selective electrochemical nitrate reduction to dinitrogen in a flow-through reactor
Abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for removing nitrate from wastewater while controlling the distribution of nitrogen-containing products. Here, Pd-decorated cuprite dendrites were prepared by sequential electrodeposition and thermal annealing to promote selective nitrate conversion to N2. The dendritic Cu2O framework provided a high-surface-area support for Pd dispersion and abundant Pd-Cu interfacial sites. Among the compositions evaluated, Pd25Cu75 exhibited the best performance, achieving 96% N2 selectivity, 93% Faradaic efficiency, and 94% nitrate removal at −1.0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) from an initial nitrate concentration of 100 mg-N L−1. Density functional theory calculations indicated that Pd substitution rendered the NO2-to-NO step less endergonic and stabilized adsorbed NOx intermediates through Pd-N interactions. A steady-state kinetic model further showed that Pd loading governs the competition between N-N coupling and sequential hydrogenation by regulating the conversion of surface intermediates. The Pd25Cu75 cathode also sustained nitrate removal from industrial wastewater in a flow-through electrolyzer while maintaining low metal leaching and stable N2 selectivity. These findings clarify the composition-dependent role of Pd in Cu2O-based NO3RR catalysts and demonstrate a practical electrode architecture for nitrate remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: System-level frequency stability enhancement in solar PV-dominated low-inertia power systems using robust nonlinear control
Abstract: The rapid integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) is changing the dynamic behaviour of modern power systems. As synchronous generators are replaced by photovoltaic (PV) inverters, system inertia decreases and frequency stability becomes more difficult to maintain. This paper compares proportional-integral (PI) control and sliding mode control (SMC) for PV inverter regulation in an IEEE 9-bus test system. Synchronous generators are progressively replaced by PV inverters to represent low and high IBR penetration levels. In both cases, active power sharing is provided through frequency-based droop control. Four MATLAB/Simulink scenarios are studied under 10% and 15% load disturbances. The results show that PI control provides smoother and better-damped responses under low IBR penetration. However, its performance deteriorates when penetration level and disturbance magnitude increase. In contrast, SMC improves the frequency nadir and shortens the recovery time under high-penetration and large-disturbance conditions. These findings show that PI and SMC have complementary operating characteristics. PI is more suitable for moderate operating conditions, while SMC provides stronger robustness in low-inertia scenarios. The results provide practical guidance for controller selection in renewable-dominated power systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Hybrid Deep Learning Finite Difference Time Domain Modeling via Surface Equivalence Theorem for Accelerating Electromagnetic Simulations
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This work presents a hybrid, deep learning-assisted electromagnetic (EM) solver that accelerates time-domain simulations by integrating neural modeling with the Surface Equivalence Theorem (SET). A deep neural network (DNN), composed of long short-term memory (LSTM) and fully connected layers, is trained to reproduce the scattering behavior of a predefined object enclosed by Huygens' surfaces. Once trained, the DNN is embedded into a Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) solver to replace the corresponding subregion, generating equivalent surface fields in real time while preserving multiple-scattering interactions with the surrounding environment. This hybrid approach substantially reduces the computational cost of repeated forward simulations typically required in optimization-driven analyses, such as inverse design, microwave imaging, and parameter estimation. The proposed network, trained using data generated at a central frequency of 9 GHz, accurately predicts broadband EM responses across the 8-12 GHz range. The training procedure and hyperparameter optimization of the network are presented, and various numerical examples are provided. Numerical experiments demonstrate an acceleration of up to 86.7 compared to conventional FDTD and 85.5 relative to the Huygens Sub-Gridding (HSG) technique, with negligible loss in accuracy. The method provides a physics-consistent framework for fast, reusable forward solvers and offers a promising path toward efficient large-scale EM modeling. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Yang X.; Cui D.; Liu Y.; Xiang Y.; Li F.; Zhu G.
Title: Constructing Lewis acid-base pairs on S-scheme Al-BiOBr/Bi2O3 heterojunctions for highly efficient photocatalytic nitrogen fixation
Abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation has long been constrained by the intrinsic inertness of the N=N bond and the severe recombination of photoexcited electron-hole pairs. Here, we construct an aluminum-doped BiOBr/Bi2O3 S-scheme heterojunction in which Al3 + selectively replaces Bi3+ sites in the BiOBr lattice, while the Bi2O3 phase retains its inherent crystal structure almost entirely. This asymmetric doping configuration strengthens the internal electric field across the S-scheme interface. The strong polarizing ability of Al3+ activates nearby lattice oxygen atoms into Lewis base sites and induces the formation of additional oxygen vacancies (Ov), while simultaneously extracting electron density from adjacent Bi centers via Al-O-Bi bridge bonds, thereby enhancing the Lewis acidity of Bi. The resulting Al/Bi-O Lewis acid-base pair activates N2 through a synergistic push-pull mechanism, in conjunction with the charge modulation induced by the oxygen vacancies. In pure water and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, the optimally designed photocatalyst achieves an NH3 production rate as high as 801.3 μmol g−1 h−1 under simulated sunlight, surpassing transition-metal-doped analogues. This work establishes a lattice-confined Lewis acid-base pair paradigm, opening a new avenue for designing high-efficiency nitrogen-fixing photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu Z.; Zhang D.; Shen X.; Zheng A.; Meng X.; Shi X.
Title: Online transient stability assessment for AC/DC power systems based on clustering BCU and hybrid neural networks
Abstract: The widespread integration of power electronic devices including renewable energy sources and Line Commutated converter (LCC)-based High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) poses significant challenges to the transient stability of AC/DC power grids. To realize the accurate and fast online transient stability assessment of AC/DC power systems, this paper firstly constructs terminal potential energy expressions through the integration of active power with respect to voltage phase angle and reactive power with respect to voltage magnitude. Subsequently, this paper proposes an online transient stability assessment method based on clustering Boundary of stability based Controlling Unstable-equilibrium-point (BCU) and hybrid neural networks to address the computational inefficiency issue of pure mechanism analytical approaches in critical energy determination. The clustering BCU method significantly reduces computational complexity when generating offline critical energy datasets by eliminating redundant calculations for different fault scenarios within the same coherent fault cluster. Besides, the convolutional neural networks-gate recurrent unit (CNN-GRU) based hybrid neural network is presented for real-time online transient stability assessment, which can quickly and accurately require the critical energy during system faults and compare it with the transient energy at fault clearing time to determine system stability. Compared with the multiple parallel CNN-GRU model, the proposed approach further provides physically interpretable indicators, including critical energy, critical clearing time, and stability margin, enabling more reliable evaluation of system stability boundaries. Finally, simulation results under different renewable penetration levels, transmission conditions, and fault scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high assessment accuracy, strong robustness, and improved computational efficiency for online transient stability assessment of renewable-integrated AC/DC hybrid power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A study on hotspot temperature prediction in dry-type transformers based on multiphysics and field synergy analysis
Abstract: Transformers are the primary energy-consuming devices in substations. Accurate loss calculation and hotspot temperature prediction are vital for grid stability. This study focuses on a 5250 kVA dual-winding dry-type transformer. We established a magnetic-thermal-fluid multi-physics coupling model. This model considers non-uniform current density in low-voltage windings caused by magnetic leakage. Through field synergy analysis, we explained the relationship between fluid vortices and local hotspots. Furthermore, we proposed a prediction model using the Grey Wolf Optimizer and Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (GWO-KELM). This model uses load rate, ambient temperature, and fan position as inputs. A digital-twin-oriented prototype platform was also developed to support online monitoring. Temperature rise tests show that the simulation error is within 4%. Compared with the backpropagation neural network (BP) and the standard KELM model, the proposed GWO-KELM model tracks hot-spot temperature variations more accurately and achieves lower prediction errors. This research provides a reliable basis for the status monitoring and predictive maintenance of dry-type transformers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Economic optimization dispatch of microgrids based on finite-time dynamic event-triggered algorithms
Abstract: To alleviate the excessive communication burden in economic dispatch (ED) of microgrids and the lack of convergence rate guarantees in existing event-triggered control (ETC), a finite-time dynamic event-triggered algorithm is proposed. This algorithm is constructed by integrating dynamic event-triggered control (DETC) with a finite-time consensus algorithm. A triggering condition embedding internal dynamic variables is established, and information exchange among distributed units is executed exclusively when the event-triggered conditions are satisfied. This approach achieves power balance between supply and demand in microgrids at the lowest cost and reduces communication overhead, while ensuring system stability. The stability of the algorithm is verified via the Lyapunov stability theorem, and thus, the avoidance of Zeno behavior is guaranteed. Title: A domain-informed forecasting framework for short-horizon carbon emissions prediction in power plants under reduced-history conditions
Abstract: Accurate short-horizon forecasting of CO₂ emissions from thermal power plants is increasingly important for unit-level operational forecasting and emission-aware operation support. In practice, emission forecasting is hindered by limited plant-specific data, operating regime shifts, and the limited interpretability of purely data-driven models. This study proposes a domain-informed predictive framework that uses thermodynamic analysis to construct physically meaningful exogenous variables for a pre-trained time-series forecasting model in combined gas-vapor cycle (CGVC) power plants. By incorporating physically meaningful variables, the framework improves feature relevance and supports stable short-horizon forecasting within the evaluated reduced-history operating conditions. The approach is evaluated on real plant operational data under data-rich, reduced-history, and short-horizon settings. The corresponding observed MAE ranges for TimeGPT and TimeGPT-EF are 2.565–2.584, 2.784–2.792, and 2.115–2.283 t/h, respectively. Lightweight plant-specific fine-tuning further supports rapid adaptation using limited same-day operating data. SHAP-based analysis identifies turbine exhaust duct pressure, steam flow, and temperature-related variables as major contributors to the model predictions. Rolling-origin evaluation provides preliminary within-unit evidence of short-horizon predictive stability, while split-conformal calibration improves the empirical coverage of the original under-calibrated prediction intervals on the May 24 test set. This study provides a practical and interpretable framework for short-horizon carbon emission forecasting in power plants, with potential applicability to emission monitoring after further validation across broader operating conditions. © 2026

Title: A coordinated reclosing strategy for active distribution networks based on fault type discrimination and sectionalized coordination
Abstract: A coordinated reclosing strategy based on fault type discrimination and sectionalized coordination is proposed for active distribution networks with high inverter-based resource penetration, tackling the issues of sustained inverter feeding during faults, complex reverse power flow paths, and complicated coordination among multiple circuit breakers. By analyzing the influence mechanism of time-varying arc resistance during the processes of arc burning, current zero-crossing, extinction, and reignition on Fourier-based impedance calculation, a criterion based on the fluctuation area of mean-removed equivalent reactance is established to achieve rapid discrimination between transient and permanent faults. A sectionalized reclosing strategy is developed among the main circuit breaker, the inverter-side disconnecting breaker, and the downstream sectionalizing breaker, by integrating the faulted section identification, power direction, and breaker functional configurations. The corresponding operation sequences including tripping, blocking, dead-line reclosing, and synchro-check reclosing are specified for various fault sections. For transient faults, the proposed strategy enables sequential reclosing between the inverter-side breaker and the main breaker, restoring supply to healthy sections. For permanent faults, it inhibits the reclosing of the responsible breaker and prevents re-energization of the permanent fault. Dynamic physical testing and PSCAD/EMTDC simulations demonstrate that the proposed fault type discrimination method effectively discriminates between transient and permanent faults, and that the sectionalized reclosing coordination strategy achieves selective fault isolation and orderly service restoration for upstream, midstream, and downstream fault sections, enhancing the security and reliability of the reclosing process in inverter-rich distribution networks. © 2026

Title: Boron doping manipulated local coordination environment of atomically dispersed nickel sites for efficient CO2 electroreduction and Zn-CO2 batteries
Abstract: Atomically dispersed transition metal-nitrogen-carbon catalysts are emerged as promising electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Title: Transient stability enhancement for grid-forming DFIGs under symmetrical grid faults: Seamless mode-switching control based on active-flux decoupling
Abstract: Grid-forming doubly fed induction generators (GFM-DFIGs) are key enablers for voltage and frequency support in high-renewable-penetration power systems. This paper reveals that coupling between the natural and forced components of the stator flux is the root cause of these problems. To address them, seamless mode-switching control based on active-flux decoupling is proposed. Theoretical analysis using the equal-area criterion yielded the critical clearing time (CCT). Verification on a low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) platform under deep symmetrical faults revealed that under an 80% voltage sag, the proposed method accelerated flux attenuation by 73.7% and reduced the peak rotor current by 52.3% compared with conventional VSG-based GFM-DFIGs. Under a 50% sag, the CCT was extended by 68.8%, and no switching oscillations occurred. The experimental results confirmed the effectiveness of the method. Title: Day-ahead energy and ancillary services joint decision of hybrid energy storage with aging-aware frequency response simulation
Abstract: The hybrid energy storage system (HESS), which integrates a battery and a supercapacitor, offers high flexibility and efficiency for peak shaving, frequency regulation (FR), and inertia support. Title: Kinetic matching of desorption and oxidation through functional decoupling in tandem catalysis
Abstract: The simultaneous removal of multicomponent aromatic volatile organic compounds (VOCs), such as benzene and toluene mixtures widely encountered in industrial exhaust streams, is severely hindered by competitive adsorption, intermediate accumulation, and the kinetic mismatch between desorption and catalytic oxidation. Authors: Ma J.; Shui S.; Hou M.; Zhang S.; Zhang J.; Wang X.
Title: Rainfall flashover characteristics of high-speed train roof insulators in a static environment
Abstract: Roof insulators are critical components of high-speed railway traction power supply systems. When trains are stationary at stations under heavy rainfall, rainwater tends to accumulate on the shed surfaces and form water films and inter-shed rain columns, thereby reducing creepage-distance utilization and increasing the risk of flashover. To investigate the rain-flashover characteristics of roof insulators under such conditions, three post insulators with different shed configurations were subjected to artificial-rain flashover tests. The effects of rainfall intensity and rainwater conductivity on flashover voltage were investigated, and finite-element simulations were performed to evaluate the influence of rain-column evolution on the local electric-field distribution. The results show that the flashover voltages of all three insulators decrease with increasing rainfall intensity and rainwater conductivity, following negative pow-er-law relationships. The relative rain-column elongation ratios are 0.39, 0.48, and 0.66, with corresponding bridging proportions of 5.5%, 11.0%, and 12.5%, respectively. As the droplet length increases from 10 mm to 30 mm and subsequently develops into a bridging state, the local peak electric-field strength increases from 6.77 kV/mm to 17.10 and 61.14 kV/mm, respectively. Rain-column elongation shortens the residual air gap and intensifies the electric field at the rain-column tip, thereby increasing the likelihood of local discharge. Based on leakage-current characteristics, flashover-arc behavior, and electric-field simulations, a physical discharge mechanism for roof insulators under static heavy-rain conditions is proposed. Title: Charge-carrier-mediated photothermal synergy in Pt/TiO2-{001} catalysts for low-temperature soot oxidation

Authors: Astan S.; Hajizadeh A.
Title: Latency-robust corridor supervisory control for hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable power systems under communication-constrained low-inertia operation
Abstract: Hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable transmission corridors introduce new supervisory coordination challenges due to reduced inertia, heterogeneous asset dynamics, and non-negligible bounded communication delay. Conventional coordination approaches typically assume ideal communication or treat latency as a secondary implementation issue, limiting robustness under wide-area supervisory operation. This paper proposes Latency-Robust Corridor Supervisory Control (LR-CSC), a reproducible engineering framework for delay-robust supervisory coordination under bounded communication delay. The methodology integrates a compact corridor-level state-space representation, a delay-embedded min–max supervisory formulation, and a digital-twin-based feasibility screening engine. Rather than relying on continuous online optimisation or centralised control authority, LR-CSC evaluates candidate supervisory actions over an admissible state envelope and enforces constraint satisfaction for all delays within a specified design bound. Validation is conducted using a fully specified synthetic nuclear–HVDC–renewable corridor benchmark under disturbance variation, stochastic bounded communication delay, and inertia degradation. Results demonstrate three principal outcomes. First, embedding bounded communication delay directly within supervisory feasibility expands the stable inertia–delay operating region relative to delay-blind coordination strategies. Second, delay-embedded feasibility screening suppresses oscillatory interaction between fast converter dynamics and slower synchronous response, yielding improved frequency nadir, reduced peak RoCoF, and faster settling behaviour. Third, robustness improvements persist across Monte-Carlo disturbance and communication uncertainty scenarios, indicating that performance gains arise from structural delay-embedded supervisory coordination rather than scenario-specific tuning. The proposed framework is intentionally positioned as a supervisory feasibility layer for low-inertia corridor coordination and provides a transparent balance between bounded computation, reproducibility, and practical implementability under communication-constrained operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Cross-graph learning based mating interface identification for CAD-assisted assembly design
Abstract: During CAD model exchange and reuse, explicit assembly metadata may be incomplete even when the geometries of candidate parts remain available. Title: Ferroresonance overvoltage identification in distribution networks based on Markov transition field and GNN–Dual-ViT: A Markov–graph co-design framework
Abstract: Ferroresonance is a typical abnormal operating condition in distribution networks. The wide spectrum and strong nonlinearity of ferroresonance signals render conventional time–frequency methods inadequate. This paper proposes a Markov–graph co-design framework that tightly couples a theoretically grounded encoding stage with a structure-aware classifier. First, the first-order Markov approximation for quantised ferroresonance sequences is assessed using conditional mutual information and a conditional-independence test, with partial autocorrelation and Ljung–Box residual diagnostics used as supporting evidence. The combined results provide an empirical basis for Markov Transition Field (MTF) encoding without imposing an ordinal interpretation on the categorical states. Second, MTF converts one-dimensional voltage signals into weighted directed graphs whose edge weights encode state-transition probabilities. Third, a GNN–Dual-ViT architecture with progressive multimodal fusion exploits the resulting graph topology. The framework is evaluated against seven representative baselines reimplemented on a common ATP–EMTP dataset under identical protocols with multiple random seeds, and is further stress-tested under low SNR and load fluctuation. A cross-voltage study distinguishes same-mechanism transfer to a 35 kV PT system from adaptation to a physically different 110 kV CCVT regime. The results indicate that transfer is feasible with lightweight domain adaptation and limited labelled target data, while regime-specific calibration remains necessary for deployment. A branchwise qualitative analysis, a failure-case taxonomy, and a maximum-mean-discrepancy audit of the sim-to-field domain gap characterise both the mechanism and the boundary of applicability of the proposed framework. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Two-stage data-driven distributionally robust optimization for capacity configuration of pumped-storage used to retrofit cascade hydropower stations
Abstract: The increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic power poses significant challenges to power system operation due to their inherent uncertainty and variability. Retrofitting cascade hydropower stations with pumped-storage units offers an effective way to enhance system flexibility; however, the optimal sizing of pumped-storage units under renewable energy uncertainty remains insufficiently explored. This paper proposes a two-stage data-driven distributionally robust optimization framework for the capacity configuration of pumped-storage units in a hybrid wind-photovoltaic-hydro-thermal system. The proposed framework jointly optimizes capacity investment and operational decisions while characterizing renewable energy uncertainty through a data-driven ambiguity set constructed from historical data. Case studies show that the proposed approach significantly improves both economic performance and operational flexibility. Compared with the benchmark case, the total system cost is reduced by 41.12%. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and robust planning tool for flexible resource deployment in power systems with high renewable energy penetration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu Y.; An H.; Guo Y.; Ma J.
Title: Convolutional tensor completion-based DSSE under high DER penetration and abnormal measurements
Abstract: Unlike transmission systems with sufficient observability and complete network information, distribution networks face persistent challenges such as noisy measurements, limited observability, and incomplete or uncertain topology. Traditional distribution system state estimation (DSSE) methods rely heavily on explicit network models (that is, feeder connectivity and line parameters), whereas existing canonical polyadic (CP)-based tensor completion approaches are limited by purely multilinear representations under distributed energy resource (DER)-related operating variability and measurement anomalies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes ConvCP, a self-supervised tensor completion framework for DSSE in which convolutional learning is embedded within the CP decomposition structure and operates without explicit network models. The method captures nonlinear dependencies through refined factor matrices and improves DSSE accuracy and robustness under diverse missing data scenarios, high levels of DER penetration, abnormal measurements, and suboptimal choices of tensor rank. Furthermore, given the high cost and limited deployment of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in distribution networks, the proposed approach is evaluated under limited-observability conditions with sparse voltage phasor measurements and less stringent phase-angle accuracy requirements than PMU-class measurements. Extensive studies are conducted on an IEEE 123-bus system and a realistic low-voltage distribution network to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Cai L.; Chen G.; Chen M.; Li T.; Tao H.; Gu S.
Title: Influence and modeling of transmission line construction on ground flash density
Abstract: Previous studies of lightning attraction have mainly focused on isolated tall structures, which can be approximated as point-like objects. Ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission lines form continuous elevated corridors, for which conventional point-source models are inadequate. Using 14 years of Lightning Location System (LLS) observations, this study examines changes in local lightning activity associated with the ±800 kV BJ UHV direct-current transmission line. A grid-based normalization method and a line-source lightning-attraction model were developed to compare lightning parameters before and after commissioning.Within 3 km of the line, cloud-to-ground (CG) flash density increased by 6.5%, with the increase decaying nonlinearly with horizontal distance. Return-stroke multiplicity and mean peak current increased by 6.8% and 7.3%, respectively, while the proportion of return strokes exceeding 40 kA increased by 11%. These current-related changes also weakened with distance from the line.Three spatial patterns of CG flash-density change were identified: rise–slow decay, rise–rapid decay, and rise–polarity reversal. Their differences were associated with aerosol concentration, topographic position index, large-scale terrain, and LLS location uncertainty. By extending lightning-attraction analysis from isolated point structures to a linear UHV corridor, this study introduces a line-source lightning-attraction model for transmission lines and links distinct lightning-density responses to environmental and observational factors. The results provide a basis for spatially differentiated lightning-protection design for UHV transmission systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Price-based centralized coordination of grid-edge resources for residential community energy flexibility assessment
Abstract: The growing use of distributed energy resources and flexible loads has transformed residential communities into active participants in distribution system operations. This shift creates opportunities for demand-side flexibility while introducing new operational challenges. This paper presents a price-based, centralized coordination framework to quantify and schedule community energy flexibility from grid-edge resources, including HVAC systems, electric vehicles (EVs), photovoltaic (PV) systems, and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). The framework incorporates customer comfort constraints, fairness considerations for shared EV charging, distribution network operating limits, and battery degradation costs to achieve economically efficient and technically feasible operation under time-of-use and dynamic electricity pricing. The framework is validated on a modified IEEE 123-bus distribution system using retail electricity prices from the Salt River Project (SRP) and Commonwealth Edison (ComEd). Sensitivity analyses assess the impact of battery degradation costs and operational uncertainties, including variations in PV generation and initial EV state-of-charge. A scalability analysis further examines computational performance as the number of participating households increases. Results show that coordinated PV and BESS operation improves flexibility by enabling the temporal shifting of renewable generation. However, fairness constraints and EV charging penalties can reduce available flexibility, while higher battery degradation costs discourage frequent battery cycling and reduce flexibility value. Overall, coordinated scheduling reduces community operating costs and maintains distribution system operating limits when network constraints are considered. These findings underscore the importance of coordinated grid-edge resource management and appropriate pricing strategies for secure and cost-effective residential energy flexibility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Hierarchically porous silicon oxide ceramic coatings for synergistic thermal insulation and radiative heat dissipation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Efficient thermal management under extreme heat flux remains a challenge in aerospace, electronics, and energy systems, requiring materials that maximize radiative heat dissipation while minimizing thermal conduction. Here, inspired by the hierarchical hair structure of camels, we develop a 575 μm-thick amorphous porous SiO2-based coating on the aluminum alloy substrate via an ultrafast (180 s) plasma-assisted oxidation strategy to achieve radiative heat dissipation and thermal insulation. The coating exhibits a high broadband infrared emissivity of 0.95 and an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.23 W m−1 K−1. The exceptional combination of radiative heat dissipation, thermal insulation, and superior ablation resistance arises from the hierarchical and multiscale design. At the macroscale, a roughened SiO2 outer layer with elevated specific surface area enhances infrared radiation. At the microscale, the porous amorphous SiO2 network effectively suppresses thermal conduction, while Si-O vibrational modes enhance radiation. Meanwhile, the Al2O3/mullite inner layer ensures thermal expansion compatibility and mechanical integrity. Under a 1373 K propane flame, the coating limits the backside temperature to 706 K after 60 s, demonstrating outstanding thermal insulation performance. Furthermore, it maintains structural integrity after 9000 W/cm2 laser irradiation for 60 s, exhibiting robust resistance to extreme thermal and laser environments. This work provides a strategy for synergistic improvement of radiative and conductive thermal management in extreme environments, which can be applied in fields such as aerospace, space exploration, electronics, and sensing. © 2026

Title: Effects of calcium hydroxide on the physicochemical and digestive properties of Tartary buckwheat starch: the role of calcium ions and hydroxide ions
Abstract: This study investigated the effects of Ca(OH)2, CaCl2, NaOH, and NaOH + CaCl2 at different addition levels (0%-1.0%) on the structure, physicochemical properties, and in vitro digestibility of Tartary buckwheat starch (TBS) to elucidate the mechanism by which Ca(OH)2 modifies TBS properties. Bound calcium content was higher in the Ca(OH)2 and NaOH + CaCl2 groups than in the CaCl2 group, suggesting that OH− may promote the association between Ca2+ and TBS. The solubility and swelling power of Ca(OH)2 group moderately increased. Rheological results and SEM images revealed that Ca(OH)2 induced TBS to form a gel network with higher elasticity, as well as more uniform and compact microstructures. An appropriate concentration of Ca(OH)2 decreased the relative crystallinity (0.2%-0.6%) and degree of order (0.2%-0.8%), reduced gelatinization enthalpy, increased gelatinization temperatures (To, Tp, Tc) and double helix content, delaying in vitro digestion of TBS. The differences in properties and structures among the four treatment groups suggest that the modification of TBS by Ca(OH)2 may be attributed to the combined action of Ca2+ and OH−. These findings provide insights into the distinct contributions of Ca2+ and OH− in modifying properties and structure of TBS. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhu M.; Zheng H.
Title: Effect of κ-carrageenan and chitosan modification on curcumin-perilla seed oil composite liposomes
Abstract: To address the issues of poor stability and low bioavailability of curcumin and perilla seed oil, this study employed the ethanol injection method to prepare composite liposomes. These liposomes were sequentially modified with a single layer of chitosan (0.2%) and a double layer of κ-carrageenan (0.04%). The physicochemical properties, membrane characteristics, environmental tolerance, and in vitro digestibility of the liposomes before and after modification were systematically evaluated. The results showed that after double-layer modification, the liposomes achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 95.27%, with a particle size of 318.5 nm and a zeta potential of +36.92 mV, exhibiting a distinct core-shell structure. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed that the polysaccharides interacted with the liposomes via electrostatic forces and hydrogen bonding without disrupting the ordered arrangement of the phospholipid bilayer. The double-layer modification significantly increased the phase transition temperature (75.18 °C) and colloidal stability of the liposomes. In vitro digestion experiments showed that, at the end of intestinal digestion, the cumulative release rate of curcumin from the double-layer-modified liposomes was 59.84%, and the release of free fatty acids was 44.58%; both values were significantly lower than those of the unmodified liposomes, demonstrating excellent sustained-release performance. In this study, using curcumin-perilla seed oil composite liposomes as a model system, the feasibility of the κ-carrageenan-chitosan double-layer modification strategy in enhancing liposome stability and controlled-release performance was validated, providing new insights into the co-delivery of hydrophobic bioactive compounds and functional oils. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Harnessing synthetic microbial communities for desert vegetation restoration
Abstract: The core bottleneck for desert vegetation restoration is extreme water stress during early seedling establishment, with hydraulic failure as the primary lethal mechanism. Traditional engineering measures (e.g., irrigation) and single-strain inoculation cannot adequately address these challenges due to high cost, weak sustainability, or limited functionality. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) offer a new approach to synergistically regulate plant water use and soil microenvironment by integrating functionally complementary taxa. This review discusses the soil water characteristics of deserts and the bottlenecks in seedling water use, indigenous microbial resources and their adaptive mechanisms, principles and design strategies for constructing SynComs, as well as the mechanisms by which SynComs improve seedling water use efficiency and survival. We also analyze key challenges and future research directions. Although SynComs have been extensively studied for enhancing plant stress resistance, their application in desert vegetation restoration is still in its infancy. Future research needs to clarify how to design SynComs to ensure their ecological compatibility, persistence, and functionality in the highly variable and extreme environments of desertified landscapes. This review provides a theoretical basis for advancing SynComs application in arid land ecological restoration. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Kumar P.; Singh Y.
Title: Optimization-based dynamic voltage support strategy for inverter-based resources in weak grid conditions: Design, analysis and validation
Abstract: The growing penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) in modern power systems demands effective dynamic voltage support (DVS) strategies, especially during low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) events. This paper proposes an optimization-based DVS method that coordinates active and reactive power while ensuring synchronization stability and robustness against grid impedance uncertainty. The voltage support problem is formulated as a constrained optimization considering current limits and dc-side power availability. An analytical, real-time solution is derived through Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions applied to the nonconvex voltage maximization problem, yielding closed-form expressions for optimal active and reactive current references across three distinct operating regions determined by active constraint combinations. Simulation results under various balanced and unbalanced fault conditions show up to 95% improvement in voltage recovery and enhanced power delivery compared to droop, PI, MPC, and RL-based methods. The inverter dynamic model incorporates dual-sequence current control in the synchronous dq-reference frame with explicit dc-link voltage regulation, enabling coordinated LVRT response under both symmetrical and asymmetrical grid faults. The proposed strategy achieves near-optimal voltage support with low computational cost, making it suitable for real-time deployment in weak and renewable-rich grids. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Constructing In–O bond charge transfer channels in defective In2S3 via CQDs derived from waste biomass for enhanced photocatalytic antibiotic removal
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Rational design of interfacial chemical bonds is crucial for reducing charge transfer barriers in heterojunction photocatalytic materials, yet this remains a challenge. Experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the formation of In–O bonds between oxygen atoms on the CQD surface and coordinatively unsaturated indium sites in In2S3, which provide fast channels for interfacial electron transfer. In addition, an ohmic contact is formed between CQDs and In2S3, and the resulting internal electric field drives the transfer of photogenerated electrons toward CQDs. As a result, the optimized catalyst exhibits a prolonged carrier lifetime of 1627.0 ps, as revealed by femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) spectroscopy, thereby promoting the efficient generation of superoxide radicals and holes. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a tetracycline (TC) removal efficiency of 81.5% within 60 min, with a kinetic rate constant of 0.107 L mg−1 min−1, outperforming defective In2S3 by a factor of 2.1. Title: Electronegativity drives charge polarization in indium single-atom catalysts for low-overpotential CO2 electroreduction

Title: Multi-type transient voltage instability identification for power systems with high renewable energy penetration
Abstract: High renewable energy penetration leads to diversified transient voltage instability patterns and the need for rapid assessment from short post-fault measurement windows. To tackle these critical challenges, this paper presents a transient voltage stability identification method that integrates Koopman operator theory with multidimensional trajectory feature fusion. First, a novel transient voltage stability index is developed, which comprehensively incorporates the voltage sag area and oscillation intensity during the recovery phase to accurately characterize complex instability behaviors. Specifically, the model lifts the nonlinear dynamics of power systems into a high-dimensional linear space, thereby enabling precise extrapolation of transient voltage trajectories. Finally, simulation tests are carried out on the China Electric Power Research Institute (CEPRI) standard test system to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Title: Discrete energy consistency for dynamic finite-strain frictional contact models with inelastic transformation

Title: Curvature-induced electronic asymmetry in hollow nanoreactors dictates pathway-selective radical chemistry for rapid water decontamination

Title: Non-covalent interactions between pectin and volatiles modulate flavor formation in goji berry (Lycium barbarum L.) during pulsed vacuum drying

Title: High-thermal-conductivity GFRP for dry-type air-core reactors: thermal-electrical performance and trade-off analysis
Abstract: Dry-type air-core reactors suffer from localized overheating due to the limited thermal conductivity of conventional glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) insulation. Enhancing the thermal conductivity of GFRP provides a potential approach for improving reactor heat dissipation; however, excessive incorporation of thermally conductive fillers may compromise electrical insulation reliability. This study establishes an integrated material-to-equipment evaluation framework to investigate the thermal-electrical trade-off of high-thermal-conductivity GFRP (HTC-GFRP) for dry-type air-core reactors. HTC-GFRP samples with different alumina contents were prepared, and their thermal conductivity, dielectric properties, AC flashover voltage, and breakdown strength were experimentally characterized. The results demonstrate that increasing alumina loading effectively enhances thermal conductivity by promoting the formation of thermally conductive pathways, whereas excessive filler incorporation leads to deterioration of insulation performance. Considering both thermal enhancement and electrical insulation reliability, a favorable thermal conductivity range of approximately 0.75–0.95 W/(m·K) was identified. Furthermore, multiphysics simulations of a 10 kV dry-type air-core reactor reveal that increasing the GFRP thermal conductivity from 0.35 to 1.3 W/(m·K) reduces the maximum operating temperature by approximately 3 °C. These results demonstrate the thermal-electrical trade-off of HTC-GFRP and provide quantitative guidance for balancing heat dissipation capability and insulation reliability in dry-type air-core reactors. © 2026

Authors: Zhang J.
Title: Horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion for renewable power forecasting: empirical evidence of a consistent horizon–representation relationship across wind and solar systems
Abstract: Accurate renewable power forecasting requires extracting information from both temporal dynamics and frequency-domain fluctuations, yet the optimal balance between these representations across forecasting horizons remains unclear. This study proposes a Horizon-Adaptive Time–Frequency Fusion (HATF) framework that learns horizon-dependent weighting between temporal and spectral features through a lightweight fusion module. Experiments on seven years of operational wind farm SCADA data demonstrate that HATF consistently outperforms recurrent, convolutional, and Transformer-based baselines across forecasting horizons from 15 min to 4 h. Cross-dataset validation on an independent wind turbine dataset and a solar photovoltaic dataset further confirms the robustness of the approach; for the solar dataset, the auxiliary input channels of the model carry irradiance and ambient temperature rather than wind speed and wind direction, preserving the three-channel architecture across energy sources. Ablation studies show that adaptive fusion is essential for effectively integrating time-domain and frequency-domain information. A key finding is that the learned fusion coefficient exhibits a highly consistent approximately linear relationship with forecasting horizon across all datasets (R²>0.98). Autocorrelation analysis indicates that this behavior is linked to the substantially different persistence timescales of low-frequency and high-frequency signal components, causing the model to gradually shift from frequency-dominant representations at short horizons to time-dominant representations at longer horizons. In addition, a Gaussian prediction head provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates with near-nominal 95% prediction interval coverage. The results suggest that horizon-adaptive time–frequency fusion offers both an effective forecasting framework and an interpretable perspective on how predictive information evolves across temporal scales in renewable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu H.; Dai P.; Zhao Y.; Tang X.; Liu C.
Title: System frequency response modeling and frequency control parameters tuning for hybrid wind generation integrating GFL and GFM doubly-fed wind turbines
Abstract: Transforming existing grid-following (GFL) doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) wind farms into grid-forming (GFM) DFIG ones is essential for enhancing system frequency support. Studying frequency response and parameters tuning in hybrid wind farms with both unit types establishes a foundation for frequency control. Frequency response modeling for GFL units is well established, small-signal models of GFM DFIG units fail to capture frequency-active power dynamics due to multi-variable coupling, hindering unified hybrid wind farm modeling. Furthermore, frequency control parameters tuning relies on inefficient trial-and-error methods. These defects limit the application of hybrid wind farms. This paper proposes a comprehensive frequency response model for hybrid wind farms and an efficient parameter tuning method. By analyzing the frequency support process in GFM DFIG turbines, a frequency-active power response model is derived. Considering system inertia sources, wind farm outputs are transformed and aggregated to build a system frequency response model that includes hybrid DFIG wind farms. A multi-objective function based on this model integrates the maximum frequency variation rate, deviation, and steady-state deviation. The improved genetic particle swarm optimization (GPSO) algorithm is applied for parameters tuning under generator output and stability constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model accurately captures frequency and turbine output dynamics, and the tuning method improves system frequency response and stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu L.; Cheng J.; Xu X.; Ren Y.; Zhang C.; Yang W.; Zhou G.; Xu T.; Liu C.; Zheng L.
Title: Phenolic acid-grafted high-amylose maize starch as a multifunctional emulsifier in agarose-based emulsion gels for thymol loading and release: Application in active coatings for strawberry preservation
Abstract: Three benzoic-type phenolic acids with progressively increasing hydroxyl substitution (p-hydroxybenzoic acid, 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid, and gallic acid) were covalently grafted onto native high-amylose maize starch (Na-HAMS) via EDC·HCl/DMAP-mediated esterification, yielding Ph-HAMS, Da-HAMS, and Ga-HAMS at a grafting ratio of approximately 12%. Successful esterification at the C-6 primary hydroxyl groups was confirmed by FTIR, UV-Vis, XPS, and NMR analyses. Phenolic acid grafting significantly enhanced surface hydrophobicity and conferred marked antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, both following a consistent structure-dependent ranking of Ga-HAMS > Da-HAMS > Ph-HAMS, reflecting differences in phenolic hydroxyl number and ortho-cooperative configuration. Thymol-loaded emulsion gels were subsequently constructed using each modified starch as an emulsifier combined with an agarose network. Compared with Na-HAMS, modified starch-based emulsion gels exhibited substantially improved emulsifying activity, reduced droplet size, and enhanced thymol loading efficiency (∼30% to 92%), along with superior physical stability. Rheological analysis confirmed elasticity-dominated viscoelastic behavior (G′ > G″) stable across 20-90 °C, while LF-NMR and MRI revealed more homogeneous internal water distribution within the modified gel matrices. Based on a comprehensive performance evaluation, Ga-HAMS emulsion gel was applied as an active coating for strawberry preservation at 25 °C. Compared with control and Na-HAMS groups, Ga-HAMS coating effectively suppressed microbial growth, reduced decay and weight loss, and better maintained firmness, color, and soluble solids. LF-NMR and MRI further confirmed the preservation of cellular water compartmentalization. This work systematically elucidates the structure-activity relationships of benzoic-type phenolic acid-grafted HAMS and provides a theoretical basis for polysaccharide-based active emulsion gels in postharvest fruit preservation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhao Z.; Xia Z.; Pan Y.; Wang J.; Fu L.; Li H.
Title: Dual-branch network for threat analysis of external-force hazards on power transmission lines
Abstract: External-force hazards have become a major cause of faults in overhead transmission lines. Existing studies focus on hazard detection, but do not localize the transmission-line safety region or analyze whether a detected target is threatening the line. To address this issue, we propose a dual-branch network that integrates hazard detection, transmission-line segmentation, and pixel-level spatial discrimination for line-aware threat analysis. In the detection branch, a multiscale multihead convolutional gated attention mechanism and a multiscale adaptive spatial attention gate are introduced to enhance multiscale hazard perception, and suppress corridor background interference while maintaining a lightweight design. In the segmentation branch, context anchor attention is embedded into TransUNet to improve the extraction of elongated transmission-line structures and generate reliable line masks. The pixel-level positioning and discrimination module fuses the outputs of the two branches and performs line-aware threat screening. Experimental results show that the detection model improves mAP50 by 5.5 percentage points over the baseline model, while the segmentation branch improves IoU by 1.16 percentage points over the baseline TransUNet. More importantly, after pixel-level screening, only 2.08% of the images require further manual verification, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving warning precision in practical transmission-line inspection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Activating slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 on CeO2 with concentrated sunlight to enable ethylene and propylene synthesis
Abstract: Harnessing solar light to convert CO2 and H2O into multi-carbon (C2+) fuels constitutes a critical strategy toward achieving carbon neutrality. This necessitates the development of photocatalytic systems and catalysts capable of breaking the linear activity-selectivity trade-off, which ultimately rests on a fundamental understanding of the key factors controlling C1–Cn (n ≥ 2) coupling selectivity. Herein, with CeO2 and Pr6O11 selected as model catalysts, we clarify that the decisive factor governing C2+ production is interfacial CO2 adsorption strength/coverage, rather than interfacial photogenerated charge carrier density or H2O dissociation/adsorption. Therefore, a solar‑concentrating photocatalytic system was designed to activate slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 with high local coverage, ultimately achieving substantial generation of C2+ products by a *CO–free formaldehyde self–condensation pathway, whereas almost no multi‑carbon products were observed under conventional photocatalytic reaction systems. Intriguingly, within this system, CeO2, despite its inferior photoelectric response and H2O activation capability compared to Pr6O11 and the Pr6O11/CeO2 composite, delivered the highest C2+ yield and molar selectivity. Over 56 h, it produced 109.69 μmol of C2H4 (19.79%) and 31.0 μmol of C3H6 (5.59%). These findings establish that, in concentrated solar light catalytic systems, the formation of C1–Cn bonds is closely related to interfacial CO2 adsorption behavior, and that slightly stronger CO2 adsorption strength is clearly beneficial for the generation of C2+ products. This insight advocates a new design paradigm under concentrated solar catalytic systems, focused on modulating CO2 adsorption strength/coverage rather than that of the *CO intermediate, moving beyond the traditional practice of avoiding either strong or weak binding. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
