Authors: Wang Z.; Zong W.; Qiu B.
Title: Cu/Ni co-doping enhances solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion in M. barkeri-g-C3N4 biohybrids
Abstract: The solar-driven conversion of CO2 into CH4 offers an effective route for carbon utilization and production of value-added fuels. Here, a semiconductor-microbe biohybrid was reported for efficient light-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion. CuNi co-doped graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) was used as semiconductor to construct biohybrids with Methanosarcina barkeri (M. barkeri). The CuNi-g-C3N4 self-assembles with M. barkeri via electrostatic interactions, which enhances visible-light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial electron transfer. This biohybrid achieves a CH4 yield of 957.05 μmol·gcat−1 with nearly 100% CH4 selectivity, a 6.54-fold increase compared to the pristine g-C3N4 counterpart. Density functional theory calculations reveal that CuNi co-doping modulates the electronic structure of g-C3N4 and optimize CO2 activation and reaction selectivity. Transcriptomic analysis confirmed upregulation of methanogenesis genes and electron/proton transfer pathways. This work demonstrates a robust and sustainable approach for solar-driven CO2 utilization, highlighting the critical role of Cu/Ni co-doping in promoting electron utilization in the semiconductor-microbe biohybrid. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Proton-assisted topotactic transformation tailored tunnel-structured (Na, K)-OMS-2 oxides: Synergistic Mn4+ and oxygen vacancies for efficient soot combustion
Abstract: The overcoming of performance bottlenecks in manganese oxide octahedral molecular sieve (OMS-2) remains a critical challenge for catalytic oxidation reactions. Herein, we report the rational fabrication of 2 × 2 tunnel-structured (Na, K)-OMS-2 via a proton-assisted topotactic transformation strategy, enabling the controllable incorporation of multiple cations within the tunnel framework. Catalytic performance evaluations show that (Na, K0.1)-OMS-2 achieves a significant breakthrough in the long-standing performance limitations of OMS-2 materials, exhibiting a remarkably low ignition temperature of soot particles of 267 ℃, with an apparent activation energy of 61.7 kJ/mol. Systematic characterizations reveal that the introduction of K+ into Na-OMS-2 induces synergistic regulation arising from the distinct characteristics of Na+ and K+, thereby significantly increasing the surface concentrations of Mn4+ species and oxygen vacancies while enhancing lattice-oxygen reactivity. These structural and compositional features enrich the catalyst surface with abundant nitrogen oxide and gaseous oxygen anchoring sites, thereby enabling the construction of a dual-functional surface that achieves efficient activation of NO and O2 molecules. Moreover, the catalyst maintains high catalytic stability along with prominent water and sulfur resistance, highlighting its great potential for practical applications in soot elimination. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Thermomechanical and functional performance of fully bio-based formulations from lentil flour and aquafaba
Abstract: Developing sustainable bioplastics from whole pulse flours presents a complex macromolecular challenge due to the interpenetrating networks of starch and proteins, which differ significantly from isolated protein matrices. This study investigates whole lentil flour and its spray-dried cooking water (aquafaba) as renewable feedstocks, for injection-moulded bioplastics, addressing the valorisation of food industry by-products. Thus, prexisting structural alterations in aquafaba (induced by its hydrothermal extraction) could synergistically modulate starch gelatinization and protein cross-linking during subsequent thermomechanical processing. Formulations with varying lentil flour:glycerol ratios (85:15 to 70:30) and aquafaba replacements (0–20 g/100g, at constant 20% glycerol) were processed via thermomechanical mixing and injection moulding. DSC confirmed thermal stability above 150°C, guiding moulding at 120°C. Specific mechanical energy (SME) significantly decreased with both higher glycerol and aquafaba addition, as aquafaba acted as an internal lubricant that improved processability without sacrificing mechanical performance. While water uptake increased with lentil flour, 20% aquafaba replacement yielded water uptake comparable to the 85:15 formulation while providing substantially higher strain at break (from 2.1 to 3.7%). DMA showed that aquafaba reduced the elastic modulus (from 184.9 to 96.5 Pa) and increased frequency dependence (n′ from 0.11 to 0.165), consistent with a plasticizing effect. FTIR revealed a decreased amide I/amide II ratio, indicating greater protein denaturation, and an increased 1025/990 cm−1 ratio, reflecting reduced carbohydrate crystallinity due to the interactions between native flour starch and aquafaba co-solutes. These findings provide a novel pathway for utilizing whole pulse flours and industrial by-products to manufacture stable, high-performance biodegradable thermoplastics for active food packaging. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Novel QUASC–CI converter with HEO-PI controller for hybrid renewable microgrid application
Abstract: The changeover towards resilient and sustainable energy infrastructures has emphasized the integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) into the hybrid microgrids. Still, the non-linear and intermittent behavior of RESs poses issues, in maintaining a stabilized DC bus voltage and grid support. In this research, a hybrid microgrid system is proposed with a novel Quadratic Ultra-Gain Switched-Capacitor Coupled Inductor (QUASC-CI) and an optimized controller to address the instabilities. The Photovoltaic (PV) system is incorporated with a QUASC-CI converter, offering extended gain in voltage at reduced duty ratios, with minimized stress and losses. On the other hand, for regulation of converter, Hare Escape Optimized Proportional Integral (HEO-PI) controller is introduced. The microgrid system, also incorporates Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG), battery and grid interface, guaranteeing that the developed hybrid system effectively manages fluctuating renewable generation, delivering smoother power to load and supporting grid compliance. MATLAB studies prove that the QUASC-CI converter in combination with HEO-PI controller offers superior converter efficiency of 96.49%, improved voltage gain, faster response of 0.15 s and reduced harmonic distortion, while confirming continuous grid integration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Risk assessment of voltage violations during unintentional islanding events
Abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed generators (DGs) has led to the proposal of fault ride-through (RT) requirements. These requirements enhance the reliability of the electrical system; however, reduce the sensitivity of anti-islanding protections, potentially exposing sensitive equipment to severe overvoltages before DG disconnection when an unintentional islanding occurs. To assess the extent of these events, also reported as load rejection overvoltage, this paper introduces the Voltage Violation Region (VVR) concept, i.e., an area in the ΔP × ΔQ plane given by the operating points in which anti-islanding protections fail to rapidly disconnect DGs before violating sensitive load tolerance limits. Based on dynamic simulations and the VVR, a risk assessment method is proposed to quantify the probability of post-islanding voltages violating the tolerance limit of voltage-sensitive loads. Our analysis of practical passive and active islanding detection methods (IDMs) reveals that RT requirements may significantly delay the activation of anti-islanding protections, resulting in high risks of voltage violations, depending on the tolerance curve and power imbalance measurements. When active IDMs are enabled, these violations may occur even in scenarios with deficit of active power imbalance within the islanded grid. The results support distribution engineers in identifying high-risk feeders, requesting end-users to apply additional protection for sensitive loads, or re-setting the DG's anti-islanding protections. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Testing of Multi-Section Deep Well Sampler and Fluid Sampling from Borehole 5G at Vostok Station, Antarctica
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Testing of the Multi-section Deep Well Sampler (MDWS) was conducted during the 70th Russian Antarctic Expedition at Vostok Station in 2024/25. The MDWS is a non-circulating piston sampler designed to collect borehole fluid samples from multiple depths in a single round trip. Surface tests verified the operational integrity of the electromechanical system and identified optimal performance parameters. The MDWS was then tested in Borehole 5G-5 at depths from 1,250 m to 3,597.4 m across six round trips, collecting 18 samples under extreme conditions (temperatures down to −60°C and pressures up to 350 atm). The device successfully passed all tests, proving its efficiency for Arctic and Antarctic applications and confirming its manufacturability at the Empress Catherine II Saint Petersburg Mining University, Russian Federation. ©2027 The author(s). Title: Valorization of camel milk whey into a synbiotic fermented sports beverage enriched with Guddaim fruit extract (Grewia tenax) and coconut milk: Phenolic profile, antioxidant activity, microbiological viability, and storage stability
Abstract: This study investigates the structural, rheological, and functional properties of a synbiotic fermented beverage formulated from camel milk whey and coconut milk, enriched with Guddaim (Grewia tenax) polysaccharides. Camel whey serves as a protein-rich hydrocolloid matrix, while Guddaim polysaccharides and phenolic compounds interact with dairy proteins, modifying the beverage microstructure and viscosity. Probiotic viability remained above 106 CFU/mL during 30 days of refrigerated storage. These findings demonstrate that interactions between camel whey proteins and plant polysaccharides can effectively modulate structure–function relationships in fermented beverages, providing a strategy for valorization of camel whey and development of functional hydrocolloid-rich products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Functional protein extracts and colouring co-products from Chlorella fusca: Towards integrated microalgal bioprocessing
Abstract: The rising demand for sustainable, high-quality protein sources has sparked interest in microalgae as an alternative to conventional proteins. This study aimed to identify the most suitable Chlorella strain for protein extraction and utilisation and to optimise the cell disruption and extraction conditions to maximise protein recovery and functionality. Among the five strains evaluated, Chlorella fusca exhibited the highest growth rate (0.16 d−1) and biomass productivity (83.55 mg⸱L−1⸱d−1) and was therefore selected for further experiments. The optimisation of cell wall disruption revealed the highest efficiency at 100 g⸱L−1, although 10 g⸱L−1 was adopted for practicality. Protein extraction was optimised at pH 11.90 for solubilisation and pH 3.40 for precipitation, yielding a protein content of 44.63 g⸱100 g−1 of biomass. The extracted proteins exhibited good emulsifying (up to 66.1 ± 0.2% at pH 10) and foaming capacities (78.6 ± 0.1% at pH 2), as well as relevant water- and oil-holding capacities (2.5 ± 0.2 and 3.3 ± 0.3 g⸱g−1, respectively). Gel formation occurred only at 20% protein concentration under alkaline pH. The amino acid profile revealed that essential amino acids represented 45.7% of the total amino acids, comparable to those reported for common food protein-rich extracts. Furthermore, the protein extraction leftovers demonstrated strong colouring potential in food matrices, particularly for green tonalities in fondant and pasta products. Overall, these findings highlight C. fusca as a promising, sustainable microalgal source of functional proteins and natural pigments for food and nutraceutical applications. Moreover, the valorisation of extraction residues as natural colourants reinforces the circular and zero-waste potential of microalgal biorefineries. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: SPMask: Sparse convolution-based 3D instance segmentation network for key targets in overhead transmission line scenes
Abstract: Accurately identifying key targets such as transmission lines (TLs) and Towers in overhead transmission line scenes from point cloud data is a critical task in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based power inspection. However, existing methods perform poorly at identifying TLs and Towers from large-scale power inspection scenes. This paper introduces SPMask, a Sparse Convolution-based 3D Instance Segmentation Network designed to identify individual TLs and Towers. Firstly, the Sparse Convolution Feature Chain Extraction Module (SPC) is designed to enhance the ability of the network to extract features from power inspection scenes. Then the Instance Mask Direct Generation Module (Qmask module) is designed to achieve point-level instance prediction, endowing the network with strong robustness. Finally, we validate SPMask using the Power Inspection Dataset (PID) collected via small UAV-mounted LiDAR and the large-scale outdoor public dataset STPLS3D. The results demonstrate that compared to several existing methods, SPMask performs the best on the PID, with an AP of 93.6% for Towers and an AP of 98.3% for TLs. Additionally, SPMask sets a new state-of-the-art on the STPLS3D validation set, with gains of +2.6 AP, +2.9 AP50, and +3.0 AP25. Title: Ultrafast synthesis of two-dimensional rare-earth oxychlorides enables dual-site synergy for efficient nitrate to ammonia electrosynthesis
Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) rare-earth oxychlorides (REOCls), with their unique structural and electronic properties, offer exciting opportunities for applications in catalysis. However, conventional synthesis routes for REOCls generally involve prolonged (≥1 h) and energy-intensive high-temperature pyrolysis, which often lead to surface coking and formation of large particle sizes. In this work, we develop a Joule heating (JH) technique for ultrafast synthesis of 2D REOCls (RE=La, Tb, Nd, and Sm) within an exceptionally short time of only 15 s. As a representative, the as-prepared 2D LaOCl exhibits outstanding electrocatalytic performance toward nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR), achieving an NH3 yield of up to 426 μmol·h−1 cm−2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.88% at a low potential of −1.2 V vs. RHE. Furthermore, in situ Raman spectroscopy, operando attenuated total reflection Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively unveil that 2D LaOCl nanosheets not only enhance the affinity of rare-earth sites for NOx- species but also regulate hydrogen adsorption on chlorine sites, thereby accelerating the hydrogenation steps and sustaining a steady *H generation-consumption cycle. This work demonstrates a highly efficient strategy for the ultrafast synthesis of 2D REOCl materials and highlights their promising potential in catalytic applications and beyond. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Risk governed early warning prognostics for high-voltage substations: calibration and alarm burden aware validation on field telemetry (Badra Oil Field)
Abstract: High-voltage substations in oil-and-gas facilities experience high-impact degradation processes whose weak supervisory signatures can evade conventional threshold alarms while amplifying operator workload. Although physical failure events are rare, the supervised target in this study is an actionable horizon-based degradation label rather than an instantaneous rare-failure indicator. This paper presents a decision-grade, horizon-aware prognostics framework for the Badra Oil Field 120 MW GTPP network using 1-min SCADA/IED telemetry. A leakage-safe protocol applies causal windowing (W=48min), horizon labeling (H=24min), and boundary decontamination via a purge gap G≥W+H=72min, followed by probabilistic calibration and governed alarming (τ*=0.05, cooldown=6h). Models spanning RF/GB/SVM/DNN/LSTM and a stacked ensemble are assessed jointly in discrimination, calibration (ECE/Brier), and alarm-burden sustainability (false alarms/day, event recall, and lead-time). The resulting risk trajectories support auditable escalation under drift and operational label imbalance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li X.; Wu J.; Zhang W.; Wang H.; Chen Y.; Zhang H.; Chen Y.
Title: Influence mechanism of electro-thermal coupling effect on inter-turn insulation damage of high-frequency transformer
Abstract: Existing studies have demonstrated that high-frequency discharge, thermal effect, and charge transport mechanism are the primary causes of high-frequency insulation failure, yet it remains unclear which mechanism plays the dominant role. Therefore, this paper establishes an experimental and simulation platform for partial discharge (PD) in inter-turn insulation under high-frequency (HF) square-wave voltage to investigate the damage mechanism of inter-turn insulation induced by high-frequency electro-thermal coupling. Experimental results show that a transition region exists around 10 kHz. Below 10 kHz, the PD amplitude changes significantly while the temperature rise is relatively gentle, and the failure of HF transformer inter-turn insulation is mainly attributed to the coupling effect of HF PD and thermal effects. Above 10 kHz, the PD amplitude exhibits negligible variation whereas the temperature rises sharply. Notably, the inter-turn insulation breaks down rapidly with an extremely short time to breakdown at 30 kHz, indicating that high-frequency thermal effect becomes the dominant factor. The electric field acts in synergy with the thermal effect to accelerate the degradation of Nomex paper, thereby further promoting the thermal degradation and premature breakdown of the insulation. The findings of this study provide a solid theoretical basis for the life assessment and multi-physics modeling of HF transformer inter-turn insulation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: An incipient fault diagnosis method for substation equipment based on multidimensional temperature gradient features
Abstract: Infrared thermography is widely used for fault diagnosis of substation equipment. However, existing temperature-based methods mainly rely on absolute temperature information and are highly sensitive to environmental disturbances, such as ambient heat sources and wind speed, which limits the reliable identification of incipient faults. To address this issue, this paper proposes an incipient fault diagnosis method for substation equipment based on multidimensional temperature gradient features. The key innovation is to shift the diagnostic basis from absolute temperature analysis to multidimensional thermal variation analysis by introducing temperature gradient as a more robust indicator of local thermal state changes. First, the physical significance of temperature gradient for condition characterization under environmental interference is analysed based on Fourier's law. Second, a YOLOX based detection method is developed to automatically localize substation equipment from infrared images and extract the corresponding diagnostic regions. Third, a multidimensional diagnosis strategy is established by jointly using the hotspot temperature gradient M∇T and the relative temperature gradient difference R∇T, enabling incipient faults to be characterized from both local thermal intensity and spatial thermal variation. By integrating automatic equipment detection with multidimensional temperature gradient analysis, an automatic diagnosis framework for incipient faults is established. Experimental results show that the proposed detection method attains a mean average precision of 97.76%. The diagnosis thresholds derived for incipient faults are 0.88 °C/m for M∇T and 33.00% for R∇T. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Ghost-ResDSCNet:lightweight residual depthwise separable convolution with spatial pyramid pooling for power quality disturbance classification
Abstract: The increasing complexity of power quality disturbances (PQDs) calls for lightweight yet accurate classification methods suitable for edge deployment. This paper proposes Ghost-ResDSCNet, a multi-scale deep network that first converts voltage signals into time–frequency spectrograms via short-time Fourier transform. A residual depthwise separable convolution backbone performs efficient feature extraction, Ghost modules reduce computational cost by cheap feature generation, and a spatial pyramid pooling module captures multi-scale contextual information. On a 21-class synthetic PQD dataset, Ghost-ResDSCNet achieves an average accuracy of 99.34% on clean signals, along with 99.26%, 99.11%, and 95.80% under 40 dB, 30 dB, and 20 dB SNR respectively, with only 0.12M parameters, outperforming MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet. On a real-world five-class dataset, it attains 100.00% accuracy on clean and 40dB signals, and 99.96% and 94.02% under 30dB and 20dB SNR. Grad-CAM++ visualization confirms that the model focuses on physically interpretable time–frequency regions. The results demonstrate an effective trade-off among accuracy, robustness, and efficiency for real-time PQD monitoring in edge computing. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cherif R.; Lawton P.
Title: Spatial analysis of the 15-minute city concept in three historically distinct urban areas across metropolitan greater Cairo
Abstract: This paper explores how the 15-min city concept plays out in Greater Cairo by examining three neighbourhoods: Agouza, Madinaty, and Badya. To do so, it draws on a systematic approach that includes selecting case studies, identifying key service categories, extracting POI and street-network data, mapping service areas in ArcGIS, and presenting the results through service area analysis and thematic mapping. To complement this, accessibility was assessed through four measures: cumulative opportunities, land-use entropy, functional redundancy, and space syntax (integration) metrics. The findings show that access in Cairo depends not just on distance but also on the diversity of available services, the degree of proximity between services, and the way streets connect different areas. Cycling makes a clear difference in widening reach and reducing accessibility inequalities and fragmentation. The findings suggest that, in addition to clinics and schools, social anchors such as souqs, ahwa, and cultural places emerge as vital parts of daily urban life. The paper argues that in Cairo, the 15-min city concept, whether built from scratch or adapted to existing urban fabrics, should not be treated as a universal recipe but as a flexible framework. The concept is part of a longer lineage of planning ideals, adopted in the planning of several areas of Cairo, from the Garden City movement to New Urbanism. It should build on the city’s own urban vocabularies, shaped through layered urban planning and lived experiences, which continue to define how urban spaces and services are used and valued within the 15-min radius or beyond. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Facet-dependent cobalt leaching governs structural reconstruction of spinel cobalt oxides in polysulfide electrocatalysis
Abstract: Electrocatalysts are pivotal in surmounting the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of sulfur redox reaction (SRR) in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries. However, improving the electrocatalytic efficiency remains a formidable challenge due to the insufficient understanding of surface dynamics of electrocatalysts, necessitating atomic-scale insights into the structural evolution under working condition. By deciphering the critical interfacial structures and dynamics of Co3O4 across distinct facets, this work demonstrates that the facet-dependent electrocatalytic efficacy of Co3O4 is intrinsically governed by site-specific Co leaching and the consequently reconstructed oxysulfide shell during SRR. Combined with spatiotemporal in-situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we reveal that the leached Co ions primarily originate from tetrahedral (Td) sites characterized by weaker Co–O covalency, whereas the octahedral (Oh) sites exhibit remarkable stability owing to the robust Co–O bonding strength. Accordingly, the Co3+Oh-terminated (100) facet undergoes a surface-exclusive reconstruction upon cycling, yielding superior electrocatalytic performance and practical potential for Li–S batteries. Conversely, the Co2+Td-terminated (111) facet suffers from rapid deactivation triggered by the excessive bulk-participating reconstruction, accompanied with decayed electrochemical performances. These findings underscore the decisive role of surface configuration in regulating the electrocatalyst reconstruction and associated activity, providing a rational design paradigm for durable Li–S electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Evaluating the effect of physical work in the heat on cognitive performance of construction workers
Abstract: The risk of excessive heat exposure is especially high among outdoor construction workers and can have detrimental effects on their cognitive performance, including impaired attention and reduced memory. Reduced attention might lead to impaired judgement and increased risk of accidents, while reduced memory can diminish workers’ capacity to remember crucial safety procedures, carry out complex tasks correctly, and make wise decisions on the construction site. In this study, the cognitive performance of 20 participants performing manual laboratory-simulated construction work was investigated in a hot environment (36°C, 60% relative humidity) compared to a temperate environment (20°C, 60%). The study also evaluated the effect of physical work in hot and temperate conditions on the mental and physical demands of the performed tasks, as well as the thermal perceptions of participants. There were no significant differences in attention (Go/No-Go test) and memory (simple 2-back test) between hot and temperate conditions. Performance on the more complex memory task (3-back test) was impaired in the hot condition compared with the temperate condition (P < 0.05). Results of the present study revealed that construction workplaces can consider additional safety measures for construction workers performing complex cognitive tasks demanding working memory in hot conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
Abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wu M.; Liu P.; Bao L.; Wang L.
Title: A TeLU-enhanced deep learning approach for state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
Abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of electric vehicles (EVs). However, existing methods often face challenges in real-world applications, particularly in accurate capacity calibration, robust feature extraction, and effective modeling of complex degradation patterns. To address these issues, this study proposes a comprehensive SOH estimation framework based on real-world operational data collected from EVs across diverse geographical regions. First, reliable SOH pseudo-labels are generated by coupling the reverse ampere-hour counting technique with the forgetting factor recursive least squares (FFRLS) algorithm to mitigate the interference of real-world data fluctuations. Second, both time-domain and time-frequency domain features are extracted, with the latter derived through the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to fully leverage complementary degradation information. The core innovation of this paper lies in the comprehensive framework integration of dual-domain feature engineering and deep network design. Within this framework, the pioneering application of the Tangent Exponential Linear Unit (TeLU) activation function serves as a critical enabling component, which significantly improves the nonlinear representation capability and effectively resolves the gradient oscillation problems of conventional activations. Furthermore, a deterministic perturbation-based analysis method is introduced to quantitatively evaluate feature importance, thereby improving model interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively handles real-world data challenges, achieving a MAE below 1.43% and a RMSE under 1.80%, demonstrating superior accuracy and stability compared to the implemented baseline models in strict cross-vehicle generalization tests. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Biomimetic interface-regulated composite coatings on flexible fabrics for microwave absorption, flame retardancy, and ultraviolet shielding

Abstract: Multifunctional coatings combining electromagnetic protection, fire safety, and environmental durability are attractive for flexible protective textiles. Here, an interface-regulated coating was fabricated by embedding Fe3O4@TiO2@polyaniline (FTP) core-shell fillers in an ivy-inspired poly(vinyl phosphonic acid-co-hydroxyethyl acrylate-co-styrene) (PVHS) matrix and depositing it on polyester fabric. The Fe3O4 core provides magnetic loss, the TiO2 interlayer promotes interfacial polarization and ultraviolet attenuation, and the polyaniline shell contributes dielectric loss and conductive pathways. Meanwhile, phosphonic acid groups in PVHS act as proton donors to regulate polyaniline doping, thereby strengthening polarization loss and improving impedance matching at low filler loading. The optimized FTP@PVHS-4 achieved a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −37.25 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.27 GHz, while the coated fabric retained strong absorption with −32.74 dB and 6.73 GHz, respectively. In addition, the fabric exhibited excellent ultraviolet shielding, with a protection factor of 1993.21 and average ultraviolet‑A transmittance of 0.05%, while maintaining coating integrity and textile flexibility. This study demonstrates that interfacial electronic regulation and biomimetic polymer design provide an effective strategy for lightweight, durable, and multifunctional electromagnetic protective fabrics. © 2026

Title: Adaptive ADMM-based optimal power flow for distribution systems via dynamic penalty strategy
Abstract: To mitigate voltage fluctuations caused by intermittent distributed generation (DG), this paper proposes a reactive power optimization strategy based on an Improved Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (I-ADMM). The model coordinates switchable capacitor banks (SCBs), on-load tap changers (OLTCs), and the reactive power capabilities of DGs to balance voltage quality and active power losses. Simulation results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed I-ADMM reduces total voltage deviation by 18.71% and 25.94%, and decreases branch losses by 9.51% and 10.67% compared with T-ADMM and C-OPF, respectively. In addition, a multi-period validation under time-varying DG and load conditions shows that the proposed method maintains effective performance across representative operating periods while preserving voltage security. Additional validation on a modified IEEE 69-bus system further confirms the scalability of the proposed method. These results demonstrate improved computational efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive penalty strategy for distributed OPF under representative time-varying operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yang Q.; Cheng L.; Dai J.; Sun T.
Title: Vulnerability-aware reinforcement learning scheduling of AI data centers under typhoon-induced thermal coupling
Abstract: The rapid growth of AI data-center loads, amplified by typhoon-induced thermal coupling between workloads and cooling systems, poses new challenges to transmission grid vulnerability assessment and scheduling. This paper develops a vulnerability-aware reinforcement-learning (RL) scheduling framework that integrates a measured-data-driven AI load model, a typhoon-day temperature–PUE–cooling model, a seven-indicator vulnerability assessment covering physical, structural, and AI-specific dimensions, and RL scheduling via PPO, SAC, and TD3 with a PTDF-based top-K branch-selection mechanism that confines control to AI-responsive branches. Validation on the IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus systems shows that all three RL algorithms achieve statistically significant VDC reductions of 6.9–9.3% (p < .001), with PPO outperforming an LP comparator by 3.4–8.4% on the 118- and 1354-bus systems. The reduction magnitude correlates with the vulnerability-gradient signal—the product of mean PTDF sensitivity and baseline vulnerability—rather than with system size per se: on the PEGASE 1354-bus system, where the AI load represents only 0.016% of total system demand and the transmission network is highly robust, no scheduling strategy produces a meaningful VDC response, confirming a physical optimization ceiling governed by AI load penetration rather than network size. Under extreme stress at 3.0 × AI load, TD3 reduces EENS by 44%, confirming VDC as a proactive leading indicator of curtailment risk. An ablation study identifies topological sensitivity as the most influential indicator. The proposed framework provides grid operators with ex-ante guidance on when vulnerability-aware scheduling becomes effective, based on the relationship between AI load penetration, vulnerability gradients, and system controllability. © 2026

Title: Weather-guided decomposition and hard-routing expert modeling for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting
Abstract: Solar energy has become a pivotal renewable resource in modern power systems; however, the stochastic and weather-dependent variability of photovoltaic (PV) generation continues to challenge accurate power forecasting and grid operation. This study proposes a weather-adaptive forecasting framework that integrates meteorological classification, signal decomposition, and hybrid deep learning for short-term PV power prediction. Specifically, a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) partitions historical samples into homogeneous weather subsets, after which Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) is applied to each subset to extract intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). A weather-guided hard-routing expert framework is then employed. Three long short-term memory network-Transformer(LSTM–Transformer) experts with identical architectures but independent parameters are trained separately using the sunny, cloudy, and rainy subsets. For each forecasting day, a rule-based weather router activates the expert associated with the dominant weather category. The activated expert jointly models meteorological variables and IMF components to represent weather-induced temporal variations and cross-time dependencies. Experimental results on a two-year PV dataset demonstrate that, compared with the baseline models, the proposed method reduces the average mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) by 33.7% and 30.2%, respectively, while achieving an average coefficient of determination (R²) of 98.69%.These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in the evaluated PV power forecasting task. © 2026

Title: Cross-attention augmented U-Net for surrogate prediction of inter-electrode magnetic field distribution in vacuum circuit breaker
Abstract: To address the high computational cost of magnetic field simulation in vacuum circuit breakers, a cross-attention augmented U-Net (UCA-Net) for fast and accurate prediction of inter-electrode magnetic field distributions is proposed in this paper. First, a dataset for a representative 27.5 kV class vacuum interrupter is generated using finite element method, including structural geometric parameters, spatial coordinates, and the corresponding magnetic field distributions in the target region. Then, these two types of features are encoded separately and fused through a cross-attention mechanism, enabling effective interaction between structural information and field-domain coordinates. And the fused features are subsequently fed into an improved U-Net backbone to predict the magnetic field distribution in the inter-electrode region. In addition, the key training settings, including batch size, loss function and optimizer, are investigated to determine the model configuration. Comparative results show that the proposed UCA-Net outperforms the conventional U-Net in prediction accuracy, while reducing the computation time for a single case from 165.0 s with finite element simulation to 86.0 ms, corresponding to acceleration of approximately 1900 times. Moreover, the maximum prediction error is maintained within 10.0 mT, and the average relative error in the inter-electrode region is below 3.0%. The proposed method provides an efficient data-driven tool for the rapid design and performance evaluation of the investigated 27.5 kV level vacuum circuit breaker. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Sridhar N.; Kumar K.S.
Title: Dynamic performance improvement in photovoltaic systems for hybrid renewable energy systems using enhanced optimized RNN approach
Abstract: Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems (HRES), which combine Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) for grid-connected power networks, present a viable solution to the growing need for clean and dependable energy. System efficiency and dependability are constrained by issues including variable solar irradiation, conversion losses, and intricate control dynamics. Therefore, High-Resolution Pulse Width Modulation (HRPWM) Resonant DC-DC converter with Improved Reptile Optimization Algorithm (Improved ROA)-Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique is presented in this paper. By reducing component stress and preserving a common ground interface, a new HRPWM Resonant DC-DC converter is deployed to maximize voltage gain and efficiency.Moreover, to control battery storage and maintain energy balance under changing generation and load situations, a bidirectional isolated converter is used. On the inverter side, a Decoupled Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) controller is used to achieve grid synchronisation and stable active/reactive power management. With an enhanced tracking efficiency 99.63%, less steady-state oscillation and increased converter efficiency97.56%, the proposed integrated design is ideal for distributed renewable energy and contemporary grid applications, which is proven by MATLAB/Simulink and experimental outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Multispectral correlation of infrared, ultraviolet, and leakage current attributes in a 500 kV substation under coastal environmental stress
Abstract: This study investigates the relationship between infrared (IR), ultraviolet (UV), leakage current, and meteorological parameters for assessing saline contamination in high-voltage insulation systems operating in a coastal environment. A multispectral monitoring methodology was applied to seven 500 kV disconnect switches installed at a coastal substation located approximately 1.5 km from the sea. Infrared thermal attributes, ultraviolet partial discharge indicators, RMS leakage current measurements, and a precipitation-based drought index (derived from rainfall data) were collected and analyzed over several months under real operating conditions. Thermal monitoring was performed using region-based maximum threshold temperature variation (ΔTthreshold), while ultraviolet analysis employed maximum persistence (Pma´x) and corona discharge area (aF) as condition indicators. The monitored parameters exhibited similar temporal behavior, with reductions following significant rainfall events and progressive increases during extended dry periods, indicating the cumulative influence of saline contamination. Correlation analyses indicated strong and statistically significant associations between the monitored attributes and the number of days elapsed since precipitation events ≥ 5 mm. Pearson correlation coefficients ranged from 0.890 to 0.970, while Spearman coefficients reached 0.976 (p ≤ 0.01). Strong associations were also observed among thermal, ultraviolet, and leakage current indicators, suggesting consistency within the proposed multispectral framework. The results suggest that the integrated analysis of IR, UV, leakage current, and precipitation history may provide useful condition indicators for tracking contamination severity and supporting condition-based maintenance of high-voltage assets operating in coastal environments. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Ultrasound pretreatment of Acacia seyal gum arabic before spray drying: effects on interfacial behavior and avocado oil emulsion stability
Abstract: High-intensity ultrasound can modify hydrocolloid functionality, but the processing conditions that improve gum arabic performance without impairing stabilization remain uncertain. This study evaluated a structured screening matrix in which gum arabic dispersions at 20–30% (w/w) were treated at nominal powers of 255–765 W for 0–15 min, spray dried, reconstituted to 20% solids, and used to stabilize avocado oil-in-water emulsions. Intrinsic viscosity, Cross-model rheology, time-resolved interfacial tension, gum-dispersion zeta potential, droplet-size evolution, and Turbiscan stability were evaluated. The intrinsic-viscosity-derived apparent hydrodynamic-size estimate decreased from 0.760 MDa in untreated gum to 0.663 MDa after 10 min, with little further average change after 15 min. Across the tested branches, 10 min gave the most favorable average interfacial and physical-stability response: mean interfacial tension at 1800 s decreased from 15.04 to 11.25 mN/m, the pre-drying gum-dispersion zeta potential shifted from −23.69 to −29.32 mV, and mean day-21 Turbiscan Stability Index decreased from 2.834 to 1.987. A branch-adjusted repeated-measures analysis supported an exploratory association between interfacial-tension reduction and increased zeta-potential magnitude (coefficient 0.938; 9 degrees of freedom; probability below 0.001). The endpoint-specific rankings were not identical: E−10 had the lowest day-21 Turbiscan Stability Index, whereas C-15 had the smallest final droplets. Thus, 10 min is interpreted as an operationally favorable average duration within the tested concentration–nominal-power matrix, not as a universal optimum or direct evidence of a molecular mechanism. The observed differences reflect the complete processing history, including ultrasound pretreatment, heating, spray drying, and reconstitution. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang D.; Wang H.; Yang J.; Zu G.; Yin X.; Ren X.; Wang X.
Title: Suppression strategy of neutral-point potential fluctuation in VIENNA rectifier based on zero-sequence voltage component injection
Abstract: The neutral-point potential fluctuation in the VIENNA rectifier is one of the key factors affecting the charging performance of DC charging systems. To address this issue, the charging and discharging behavior of the DC-link capacitors under different switching states is analyzed, revealing that the neutral-point potential fluctuation mainly consists of an AC fluctuation component and a DC offset component. A time-domain expression for the neutral-point potential fluctuation is derived, showing that its amplitude is proportional to the modulation index and the input current amplitude, and inversely proportional to the grid frequency and the DC-link capacitance. Based on this analysis, a zero-sequence voltage component injection strategy based on neutral-point charge balance is proposed. The strategy regulates the switching-period-averaged neutral-point current, divides the modulation cycle into different intervals according to the polarities of the three-phase input currents, and analytically determines the AC-compensation zero-sequence voltage in each interval. A DC-offset correction component is then superimposed to simultaneously suppress the low-frequency AC fluctuation and DC offset of the neutral-point potential. To verify the proposed strategy, a three-phase VIENNA rectifier experimental platform is built. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage ripple of each DC-link capacitor from ±2.5% to ±1.0%, thereby confirming its effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li M.; Xia Z.; Deng Y.; Li P.; Zhang N.; Ma D.; Wu X.
Title: Turning coal into gold: Earth-abundant calcined coal as a facile photocatalyst for efficient photopolymerization
Abstract: The exploitation of earth-abundant and inexpensive carbonaceous materials as high-performance photocatalysts for controlled radical polymerization remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a serendipitous yet transformative discovery that naturally abundant coal, after a simple calcination treatment in air, can serve as an efficient heterogeneous photocatalyst for PET-RAFT polymerization. Through systematic optimization of the calcination temperature, the catalyst designated as NCC250–2, exhibits an optimal balance of surface functional groups, photogenerated charge-carrier transport kinetics, and lifetime, as well as favorable oxygen adsorption and depletion capacity. This delicate equilibrium endows NCC250–2 with exceptional photocatalytic activity, enabling well-controlled PET-RAFT polymerizations with narrow molecular weight distributions and high chain-end fidelity under visible-NIR light irradiation. Remarkably, compared with previously reported photocatalysts in this field, NCC250–2 not only offers compelling advantages of ready availability, straightforward preparation, and ultralow cost, but also demonstrates superior or comparable catalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of utilizing raw coal in PET-RAFT polymerization, turning this low-grade fossil fuel into a functional catalytic material a true “stone-into-gold” transformation. This work not only expands the palette of photocatalysts for precision polymerization but also opens a new avenue for valorizing abundant natural resources into high value materials for sustainable polymer chemistry. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: From catalyst functional zoning to air oxidation–nitrogen oxide reduction cascade: An effective pathway for ammonia synthesis from air
Abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia, centered on nitrate reduction, faces challenges including insufficient catalyst activity and stability, along with difficulties in integrated application. Using Salen (N-N′-bis (salicylidene)-1,3-propanediamine) as ligand, this work uniformly introduces multi-dimensional iron species onto carbon fibers surface (named FeSCN/CF) via complexation confinement and hard template confinement. FeSCN/CF efficiently promotes nearly 100% electroreduction of nitrate-to-ammonia under various complex conditions, and the Zn-nitrate battery constructed with FeSCN/CF as the core enables self-driven ammonia synthesis alongside stable energy supply. Driven by intermittent electrical energy, a low-temperature plasma air oxidation process cascaded with an electrocatalytic unit enables direct air-to-ammonia conversion, successfully demonstrated in a distributed agricultural ammonia fertilizer supply scenario. Experimental and theoretical calculations confirm that multiscale/multitype sites synergistically promote highly selective electroreduction of nitrogen oxides to ammonia, while a self-driven plasma-air-oxidation cascade electroreduction system powered by green electricity effectively addresses nitrogen source shortages and adapts to distributed ammonia synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Ouyang J.; Xiao T.; Wang Y.
Title: Inherent physical feature extraction and fault cause identification for HVDC transmission systems
Abstract: The accurate identification of line fault causes of LCC-HVDC directly determines the formulation of differentiated operation and maintenance decisions and the reduction of system outage time. However, DC line fault transients are not only driven by physical mechanisms such as lightning strikes and wildfires, but also deeply coupled with the nonlinear reshaping effect of converter station control on transient electrical quantities, which causes DC line faults to be difficult to accurately identify using traditional data-driven models. Therefore, by establishing an analytical model considering the closed-loop control response of the converter station, an analytical extraction method for the fault inherent components of DC electrical quantities is proposed, and the true restoration from controlled waveforms to physical essential characteristics is realized; subsequently, starting from the physical evolution mechanism, the essential differences of lightning strikes, wildfires, wind deviations, and foreign object bridging in electromagnetic characteristics are analyzed; furthermore, a fault cause identification model integrating the multi-branch residual network (MResNet) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) is constructed to extract the local spatial distortion and global temporal evolution features of fault inherent components from multiple dimensions. Based on control response decoupling and inherent physical feature extraction, an identification method for LCC-HVDC fault causes is proposed. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves effective identification of recorded waveform samples, providing theoretical foundations and engineering references for targeted maintenance and rapid recovery of DC lines under controlled environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enhancement of power system steady-state stability through allocation of quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization algorithm-based multiple D-STATCOM Units
Abstract: Modern distribution networks suffer from power losses and voltage instability under various loading conditions. Mitigating these operational issues requires optimal allocation of custom power devices, such as Distribution Static Compensators (D-STATCOMs). To address this challenge, this study develops a quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization (QGWO) algorithm for allocating D-STATCOMs to ensure steady-state stability, improve bus voltage profiles, and reduce power losses. Distinct from existing variants, QGWO models search agents as probabilistic quantum state vectors, utilizing a fitness-driven amplitude scaling and dynamic phase angle adaptation. Using the backward-forward sweep (BFS) load-flow method, the performance is evaluated across base-load, load-increment, and single-phase fault scenarios on practical 44- and IEEE 69-bus test systems. The voltage stability margin (VSM) is utilized to determine maximum loading factors. For the 44-bus system, buses 22, 29, and 41 with capacities of 637.69 kVAR, 503.75 kVAR, and 351.01 kVAR are found as the optimal locations and sizes. With these units, power losses are reduced by 50.894% under the base-load scenario. For the IEEE 69-bus system, buses 11, 17 and 61 with capacities of 358.69kVAR, 254.02kVAR and 1206.75kVAR reduce power losses by 42.76% under the base-load scenario. Using VSM, the maximum loading factor is found as 1.53 and 2.65 for 44- and 69-bus systems. Statistically, the proposed QGWO achieves the lowest mean power loss, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests confirming its advantage over PSO, APSO, GWO, and CGWO. Weight sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the optimal solution remains invariant to changes in objective-function weights. Economically, cost-benefit sensitivity analyses confirm the financial viability of the project. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li W.; Qian C.; Luo W.; Zhu Y.; Jiang C.; Wang L.; Hu J.
Title: Robotic learning from demonstration enabled by improved gaussian mixture model and gaussian mixture regression
Abstract: Robotic learning from demonstration (LfD) can significantly minimize robotic programming difficulties due to its intuitiveness and efficiency. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)/Gaussian mixture regression (GMR) is an effective method to implement LfD. However, there are limitations in GMM/GMR, such as the requirement of creating multiple demonstrations, sensitivity to demonstration defects, and underfitting/overfitting generalization in industrial tasks. To tackle the issues, in this study, an improved GMM/GMR approach with three improvements is proposed. Firstly, a Gaussian noise scattering strategy is designed to minimize the required number of multiple demonstrations and eliminate unsmooth turning areas/jitters defects in the demonstration. Secondly, based on a new evaluation criterion of incorporating the Gaussian cluster number, Bayesian information criterion, and dynamic time warping, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced to achieve an optimal balance between feature preservation and smoothness for a regression solution, thereby effectively mitigating the overfitting/underfitting issues. Thirdly, the B-spline curve-based reconstruction of the regression solution is devised to enhance the adaptability of GMM/GMR to the changes in target positions. Experiments on retired product recycling are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the approach presented in this study, providing a reliable solution to facilitate LfD in industrial environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Han Y.; Zheng J.; Liang X.; Hu K.; Xia M.; Sun Z.
Title: Multi-energy load forecasting based on dynamic relationship awareness and spatio-temporal graph neural networks
Abstract: Accurate integrated energy load forecasting plays a critical role for the efficient power consumption and market transaction execution for nowadays power systems; Yet the field suffers from 2 critical drawbacks, (1) non-sufficient consideration of complex spatio-temporal dynamic correlation between load and meteorological information; (2) non-consideration of anomalies itself of the given data. In order to tackle the above shortcomings, in this paper we put forward a dynamic relation perception based load forecasting model with spatio-temporal graph neural networks, where the developed dynamical low-rank multi-head attention mechanism for complex load dynamics can specifically focus on the most vital information for different time-step nodes and spatial nodes accordingly, leading the model to a strong prediction performance. Moreover, to enhance robustness and stability, this work proposes a learnable anomaly feature process module which can detect anomalous data and use learnable weights for processing it, as a result, it can effectively reduce information loss. The comprehensive experiments of the DLR-DHC model on the Arizona State University Tempe Campus Integrated Energy System data shows that prediction accuracy of the proposed model surpasses most existing models across most metrics and prediction time frames. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Grid-strength mirroring-driven seamless adaptive evolution control for PMSG wind turbines in ultra-weak grids: achieving phase-impedance-energy synergy
Abstract: To address the transient impact issues caused by the lack of synchronous torque in direct-drive wind turbines under ultra-weak grids and the switching between grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) control modes, an adaptive evolutionary control strategy based on real-time mirroring-driven grid strength is proposed. First, a frequency-adaptive improved recursive discrete Fourier transform (IRDFT) and a recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm are introduced to achieve millisecond-level simultaneous identification of grid impedance and inertia characteristics, thereby constructing a two-dimensional digital mirror of the grid in time and space. Second, an evaluation model of grid state of health (SOH) is established based on this mirror, generating a continuously differentiable nonlinear evolution factor to guide the grid connection characteristics from conventional passive phase-locked synchronization to flexible voltage-source synchronous evolution with active support capability. Meanwhile, the virtual reactance is dynamically reshaped using weighting factors to expand the system stability boundary, and combined with the feedforward compensation mechanism on the DC side to achieve adaptive allocation of reserve capacity, effectively balancing the power support strength under ultra-weak grids and the economic efficiency of power generation under strong-grid conditions. Simulation results show that under the extreme condition of a short-circuit ratio of 1.1, this strategy reduces the transient current impact during mode switching by 42.5%; compared with conventional grid-connection control, the 10-year net profit increases by 96.5%, achieving Pareto optimality in terms of safety and economy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Mitigation of dynamic coupling and sub-synchronous oscillations in AC–DC coupled multi-terminal MMC–HVDC networks
Abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic coupling mechanisms and sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) phenomena in multi-terminal modular multilevel converter–based high-voltage direct current (MMC–HVDC) networks and proposes an effective mitigation strategy. A detailed small-signal model is developed to capture internal MMC dynamics, converter control interactions, and the dynamic coupling between offshore and onshore converters through the common DC link. Eigenvalue- and impedance-based analyses reveal that arm capacitor voltages, zero-sequence component of the circulating current, and DC-voltage controller collectively shape the oscillatory behavior and inter-converter coupling within the 0–50 Hz range. Mode sensitivity analysis further demonstrates that droop gain, DC-voltage PI parameters, and damping coefficients significantly affect modal damping. To mitigate coupling-induced instabilities, a modified circulating current controller is introduced to regulate the zero-sequence current component and suppress its participation in SSO modes. Frequency- and time-domain simulations confirm that the proposed controller effectively mitigates oscillations at SSO range, and 150 Hz, limits disturbance propagation through the DC link, and improves both transient and steady-state damping. The frequency-domain responses analysis establishes a comprehensive framework for understanding and mitigating dynamic coupling in MMC–HVDC networks, supporting the stable integration of large-scale offshore renewable energy systems. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Rational N,O co-coordination of Fe-N2O2 single atoms modulates the electronic structure to facilitate 1O2 generation
Abstract: Selective generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) remains a major challenge in single-atom-catalyst-based advanced oxidation systems, especially in complex water matrices. Herein, a Schiff-base ligand was used to regulate the local N,O coordination environment of Fe sites, yielding an N,O-coordinated carbon-supported Fe single-atom catalyst denoted as Fe-N2O2 based on the proposed idealized coordination model. Compared with Fe-N4, Fe-N2O2 exhibited a higher Fe oxidation state, improved electrical conductivity, and enhanced phenol (PN) adsorption (22.3% vs 5.62%). The Fe-N2O2/PMS system also showed enhanced involvement of 1O2 during PMS activation. As a result, PN, a representative electron-rich phenolic pollutant, was completely removed within 5 min. The apparent rate constant reached 2.51 min−1, and total organic carbon removal reached 73.1% within 30 min. Theoretical calculations revealed that N,O co-coordination reduced Fe charge density and lowered the Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) of O* formation, facilitating PMS activation and 1O2 generation. The favorable cycling stability and continuous-flow performance (>94.9% PN removal within 36 h) highlight the practical potential of the Fe-N2O2/PAN membrane. This work demonstrates that Schiff-base-defined N,O coordination is a viable strategy for regulating ROS evolution in PMS-based catalytic oxidation systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Using selected flexibility resources in the power system to eliminate overloads on high-voltage lines
Abstract: With the growing share of distributed energy sources and energy storage, the problem of high-voltage line overloads is becoming one of the key challenges of modern power systems. This paper proposes a method to eliminate transmission line overloads by coordinating power changes among selected generation units, loads, and energy storage units, with network reconfiguration as needed. A key element of the proposed approach is identifying the controllable elements most strongly associated with overload patterns in post-contingency scenarios. These elements were identified using statistical correlation coefficients describing the relationship between line loading levels and the power generated, consumed, or stored at individual buses. Correlation analysis was used to determine a subset of candidate elements most relevant to the observed overload patterns, thereby reducing the dimension of the control problem. Title: Severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS frequency regulation and SoC management
Abstract: This paper proposes a severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS-based primary frequency regulation (PFR) and state-of-charge (SoC) management. Conventional adaptive droop controllers commonly use decoupled gain structures, fixed nonlinear curves, or multi-parameter logistic functions, which complicate tuning and may increase unnecessary battery cycling. The proposed controller introduces a unified Δf–SoC map in which a single concavity parameter β shapes the frequency-severity response. A multiplicative SoC weighting function enforces dynamic participation limits, while a hybrid β-adaptation mechanism distinguishes sustained volatility from high-RoCoF events. A frequency-gated restoration loop is added to recover SoC without interfering with critical frequency support. The controller is evaluated through SFR-model simulations and IEEE 9-bus multi-machine studies, supported by sensitivity analysis, stability verification, and battery degradation assessment. Results show that the proposed method provides a balanced trade-off between frequency regulation and battery utilization. In the continuous stochastic case, it reduces BESS energy throughput and total degradation damage compared with the benchmark controllers. Title: Rethinking transmission line health indices under rising lightning activity
Abstract: Health and condition indices (HI and CI), based primarily on physical inspections, are fundamental in asset management but show severe limitations in regions with high lightning activity. Results demonstrate that KPI deviations align with pronounced interannual increases in lightning activity strongly correlated with the positive phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), confirming the breakdown of climate stationarity and the emergence of localized exposure hot spots. Title: Local ultraconvergence of post-processed finite volume element solutions over quadrilateral meshes for elliptic problems

Abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, the local ultraconvergence properties of post-processed high-order finite volume element methods (FVEM) for second-order elliptic problems with constant coefficients. We rigorously prove that the post-processed solution and gradient attain 2kth order convergence, up to a logarithmic factor, at interior nodes. Title: Transient phase-based faulty feeder identification for high-impedance faults via autocorrelation entropy difference
Abstract: In resonant grounding distribution systems (RGDSs), high-impedance faults (HIFs) generate severely attenuated currents and complex arcing behaviors, making faulty feeder identification particularly challenging. Existing magnitude-based methods suffer from significant performance degradation, while conventional phase-extraction techniques are vulnerable to noise and intermittent arcing. First, based on equivalent models for both fixed-resistance and arcing HIFs, the initial phase disparity of zero-sequence transient currents inherently persists, remaining structurally decoupled from the extreme attenuation caused by HIFs. To circumvent the unreliability of direct phase estimation under low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), the ACED index is formulated to characterize the structural correlation discrepancies of transient signals, achieving robust feature extraction without relying on explicit phase calculation. Simulation and field-test results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains satisfactory performance under extreme fault resistances, nonlinear arcing, and diverse operating conditions. Title: Regulating nitrogen distribution in covalent organic frameworks for dual-pathway photocatalytic H2O2 production
Abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts for H2O2 production, yet the charge separation and transport remain a major bottleneck restricting their photocatalytic efficiency. Title: Biomass-derived amorphous carbon-modified NiFe-LDH for efficient urea electrooxidation: Electron-deficient Ni3+ sites induced by interfacial electron transfer
Abstract: Replacing the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers a promising route for energy-efficient hydrogen production and the electrochemical treatment of urea-containing wastewater. However, the practical application of UOR is still hindered by insufficient anode durability and sluggish UOR kinetics. Herein, biomass chitosan was employed as the carbon precursor to fabricate amorphous carbon-modified coral-like NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH), which was in-situ anchored on nickel foam via a facile one-step hydrothermal strategy. This pre-stabilized Ni3+ facilitated the in-situ generation of active γ-NiOOH at low potential, while γ-NiOOH served as the catalytic phase to drive the UOR; the complementary synergy between the two significantly enhanced the overall catalytic performance. This study affords a versatile interfacial modulation protocol for designing high-performance crystalline/amorphous hybrid electrocatalysts, which may offer a promising route for sustainable energy conversion and the electrochemical treatment of urea-containing wastewater. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Image-based fault diagnosis for reliable operation of photovoltaic generation plants using a modified ConvNeXt model
Abstract: Image-based fault classification is a bottleneck for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants, where unflagged soiling, snow burial, electrical damage and physical defects translate directly into lost generation. Existing deep-learning approaches either rely on very large backbones whose training cost is incompatible with frequent site-specific retraining and whose inference precludes on-board deployment, or on lightweight networks that are fast but unreliable on the small, imbalanced field datasets typical of real plants. This work proposes a Modified ConvNeXt-Tiny that augments an ImageNet-pretrained trunk with multi-scale Convolutional Block Attention Module taps at stages 2–4 of the feature pyramid, a Global Response Normalization block before the deepest attention stage, and a parallel five-convolution texture branch that processes a Jet-recolored rendering of the input image, specialized to fine-grained surface textures. The four descriptors are fused and classified by a three-layer multilayer-perceptron head, giving a 30.6-million-parameter model. Under 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the public Faulty Solar Panel dataset (885 images, six classes), benchmarked against seventeen deep-learning baselines under a common training protocol, the proposed model attains 91.30 ± 0.86 % accuracy and 91.62 ± 1.48 % macro-F1, matching the ConvNeXt-Large baseline within 0.13 percentage points while using 6.4 × fewer parameters, training about 19 × faster per fold, and showing the lowest fold-to-fold variance in the leaderboard. A coupled Grad-CAM analysis confirms that attention concentrates on the actual fault region in every class, supporting a human-in-the-loop O&M workflow that improves the availability of renewable generation assets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Finite Element Analysis and Optimization of the Composite Plate Subjected to Close-Range Explosion
Abstract: Composite materials, particularly glass and carbon fibre composites, are widely used in aerospace, automotive, and defence applications because of their excellent strength-to-weight ratio and superior mechanical performance. Title: Rare earth-dependent modulation of Cu for C2+ selective CO2 reduction: Correlation with the Cu d-band centre
Abstract: Rare earth (RE)-modified Cu-based catalysts have shown enhanced C2+ selectivity in CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), but the role of different RE elements in regulating the electronic structure and catalytic behaviour of Cu remains insufficiently understood. Title: Fast extremum values calculation of electro‑thermal fields for ±800 kV valve‑side resin-impregnated paper bushing under multiple factors
Abstract: Valve-side resin-impregnated paper (RIP) bushings are key insulation components of HVDC converter transformers. Combined AC–DC voltage, high current, and varying thermal boundaries produce non-uniform electro-thermal fields, potentially causing local overheating and electric-field concentration. A three-dimensional electro-thermal finite-element model was developed for a full-scale ±800 kV valve-side RIP bushing and its temperature-field calculation was validated through temperature-rise tests, yielding an MAE of 2.301 °C and an RMSE of 2.467 °C. Single- and multi-factor effects of load rate, ambient air temperature, and transformer oil temperature were investigated. The factors create different temperature and conductivity gradients, producing non-equivalent electric-field responses and non-monotonic variations with thermal boundaries. Temperature-dependent field distortion is dominated by DC redistribution, and electric-field concentration does not necessarily coincide with the thermal hot spot. For 25 independent numerical test conditions, its MAE/RMSE values were 1.437/1.743 °C for hot-spot temperature and 0.060/0.076 kV/mm for electric-field extremum. Compared with conventional Kriging, BP, and LSTM, the proposed model achieved the lowest five-fold validation and independent-test RMSE values for electric-field-extremum calculation while retaining an explicit mathematical form. Title: Fault recovery strategy for active distribution networks with high penetration of DGs considering island merging and sequential repair
Abstract: The integration of high-proportioned DGs into distributed networks has had a profound impact on improving energy utilization efficiency, promoting the utilization of renewable energy, and offering the potential to enhance power grid resilience. To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel fault recovery strategy that simultaneously integrates island merging and sequential repair. First, a new island merging model is developed based on a virtual power flow formulation inspired by single-commodity flow theory, thus enabling coordinated optimization of power sharing and topology reconfiguration. Second, by introducing a set of linkage constraints between sequential repair and island power supply capability into the model obtained above, a co-optimization mechanism that integrates fault repair with dynamic island merging is established. After that, a unified fault recovery model is presented by using the mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model. Validations on the modified IEEE 33-node system demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy. Compared to mainstream benchmark methods, the proposed strategy reduces the total recovery cost by 34.9% to 51.1%, and guarantees a 100% load recovery rate within four repair periods. Title: Rapid identification of Sub-/Super-Synchronous oscillations by interpolated Zero-padding DFT
Abstract: Sub-/super-synchronous oscillations pose significant threats to the safety and stability of the smart grid. Title: Congestion management in electric distribution systems through flexibility services: a bibliometric and analytical review
Abstract: Electricity systems are rapidly evolving toward decentralized architectures with high shares of variable renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources (DERs), increasing congestion in medium- and low-voltage networks. Across jurisdictions, explicit remuneration, interoperable data, and coordinated governance recur, but uneven implementation precludes causal comparisons or effectiveness rankings. Abstract: This article investigates the application and analysis of two substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms namely Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (DNWR) and Neumann-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (NNWR) for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) with time delay. These equations are relevant in numerous physical and engineering contexts, such as wave propagation, biological processes, and control systems, where the system's dynamics are influenced by past states. The study emphasizes the stability, convergence, and computational efficiency of these non-overlapping domain decomposition methods when applied to such problems. Specifically, the DNWR and NNWR algorithms are analyzed using both Fourier and Laplace transforms in asymmetric domain decomposition to assess their capability to manage delayed terms in hyperbolic systems. Using Fourier analysis, we establish linear convergence estimate for the numerical errors. Laplace transform analysis enables a more in-depth study for characterizing finite-step convergence. Additionally, we derive the optimal parameters required to achieve finite step convergence in presence of heterogeneous spatial domain. Theoretical findings are complemented by numerical experiments, showcasing the methods’ effectiveness in maintaining accuracy while reducing computational complexity. Additionally, the study explores potential extensions to more complex problems and diverse applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Autocorrelation-based protection for active distribution networks using current direction and magnitude change detection
Abstract: This paper presents a current-based protection method applicable to various operating conditions of distribution networks, including radial and meshed topologies, as well as scenarios with penetration of distributed generation. The proposed approach is based on two key criteria: changes in current direction and current magnitude. These criteria are extracted solely from instantaneous current measurements by calculating the autocorrelation between each current cycle and its preceding cycle using a sliding window. In lines where bidirectional current flow is possible, a change in current direction at one end of the line serves as a criterion for faulted area identification. Conversely, in line with unidirectional current flow, changes in the average absolute value of the current magnitude act as an effective criterion for identifying the faulted area. The method was validated through two case studies: a simple ring network and a complex radial-meshed distribution network representing a portion of Sirjan city's distribution system in Iran. Simulations were performed in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The results confirm the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method across different operating scenarios. The method successfully identifies the faulted area with high precision, requiring at most one‑quarter cycle of newly acquired current data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lizhen W.; Huan D.; Xiping M.
Title: Cross-domain attack detection in integrated energy systems based on knowledge-data dual-view collaboration
Abstract: To address the challenges of scarce cross‑domain attack samples and strong cooperative stealthiness in Integrated Energy Systems (IES), this paper proposes a detection method based on knowledge–data dual‑view collaboration. First, considering the gas–thermal inertia of IES, a knowledge graph (KG) encoding the spatio‑temporal logic and constraints of Denial‑of‑Service (DoS), False Data Injection (FDI), and Replay attacks is constructed to form the knowledge view. Second, the knowledge view embeds physical constraints via the RotatE embedding model, while the data view employs a Spatio‑Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST‑GAT) to extract dynamic measurement features, thereby establishing a dual‑view collaborative detection framework. Finally, bilinear pooling is applied to fuse heterogeneous features, and anomaly discrimination is performed based on the consistency between domain-knowledge constraints and measurement features. Simulation tests on an IEEE 30‑bus electricity–heat–gas coupled system show that the proposed method attains an F1 score of 0.939 at a 5% attack rate, outperforming the Long Short‑Term Memory Autoencoder (LSTM‑AE), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), RotatE, and ST‑GAT baselines, with markedly reduced false‑positive and false‑negative rates. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
