Title: Experimental harmonic characterization of grid–connected PV inverters using FFT, time–frequency analysis, and VMD–HHT
Abstract: This paper presents an experimental framework for the characterization of harmonic distortion and transient phenomena in grid–connected photovoltaic (PV) inverters operating under non–stationary conditions. In PV–based smart grids, harmonic behavior is influenced by solar irradiance variability, inverter control dynamics, and inverter–grid interactions, which challenge classical stationarity assumptions. Although classical and advanced signal–processing techniques are widely used, their independent application often provides limited insight into time–varying inverter–associated disturbances. To address this limitation, a hybrid and sequential signal–processing framework is proposed, integrating frequency–domain analysis, time–frequency representations, and adaptive signal decomposition to identify stationary, non–stationary, and transient harmonic components. The methodology is experimentally validated using real measurements from a grid–connected PV inverter operating under variable irradiance and dynamic load conditions. The campaign–level average current THD increased from approximately 1.5% under baseline conditions to approximately 7.8% during PV–inverter operation, with peak values exceeding 8%. Dominant low–order harmonics and short–duration current distortions were also observed. The novelty of the proposed framework lies in the hierarchical assignment of complementary diagnostic roles to each method and in the quantitative evaluation of the VMD–HHT stage using experimental measurements. The framework provides a practical methodology for advanced power quality assessment and monitoring in inverter–dominated distribution networks. © 2026

Title: Inside the cooling die: prediction of the flow profile of a high-moisture soy protein melt during extrusion
Abstract: The fibrous structure of plant protein-based meat analogues, manufactured using high-moisture extrusion, is determined by the flow in the cooling die. However, currently there is little understanding of how the rheological properties influence said flow. In this work, we predict how a soy protein melt flows under changing inlet temperature, cooling temperature, and pH. The model relies on a pH- and temperature-dependent dynamic yield stress and a wall slip equation, parametrised by in situ MRI velocimetry measurements in a circular die. The model predicts that the inlet velocity profile quickly transforms into plug flow for neutral and acidic pH conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is higher. Under alkaline conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is lower, the central core remains flowing, after which it transitions to plug flow. The model was validated by pressure and temperature profiles from a rectangular cooling die, measured along the length of the cooling die. The model provides insight into the link between solidification of the protein melt and the shear stress and the velocity profiles inside the cooling die. Thus, a scalable model was created that can be used to predict the pressure drops and temperature/velocity profiles over different geometries and cooling conditions. This will enable future work to more accurately model flow in the transition zone and cooling die. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Tian M.; Li J.; Du Y.; Shen X.; Wang J.; Sun X.; Yuan Q.
Title: Biosynthesis of vanillin glucoside in Escherichia coli
Abstract: Vanillin is a widely used flavor compound in the food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. Although microbial biosynthesis offers a green alternative to conventional chemical synthesis, challenges such as unstable heterologous enzyme expression, insufficient methyl donor supply, and product cytotoxicity limit de novo production. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli to produce vanillyl alcohol, vanillin, and vanillin glucoside directly from glycerol. Genomic integration of the alcohol dehydrogenase ADH6 and multi-copy of the caffeic acid O -methyltransferase COMT gene eliminated the need for plasmid-based expression, yielding 1.09 g/L vanillyl alcohol in shake flasks. To overcome methylation bottlenecks, we reinforced the S -adenosyl- l -methionine (SAM) cycle by enhancing SAM biosynthesis, accelerating S -adenosyl- l -homocysteine (SAH) hydrolysis, and establishing methionine regeneration, which increased vanillyl alcohol production to 1.95 g/L. Subsequent deletion of four endogenous aldehyde-reduction genes together with removal of heterologous ADH6 enabled vanillin accumulation at 551.6 mg/L. Introduction of the glucosyltransferase UGT72E3/2 converted vanillin into vanillin glucoside, reaching 1.37 g/L in shake flasks and 2.12 g/L in a 3-L fed-batch fermenter. This work establishes a modular platform for efficient production of vanillin and its derivatives in E. coli . © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang Z.; Qiu Y.
Title: Mechanisms and suppression methods of interaction oscillations in complex inverter networks under weak grid conditions
Abstract: Under weak-grid conditions, coupling between grid-connected inverters and grid impedance can excite high-frequency oscillations. This paper develops a modular small-signal model that maps local VSC state-space models to a global dq-domain nodal-admittance matrix. Modal sensitivity and participation factors are used to identify the dominant resonant mode and its contributing components. Based on this diagnosis, a participation-factor-guided HPF active-damping strategy is designed, with an analytical nominal gain and a full-order robust correction accounting for digital delay and grid-impedance uncertainty. Simulations of a three-VSC ring network, including comparisons with CCF-AD and GCF-AD over SCR=1.2–2.5, demonstrate improved high-frequency damping with limited fundamental-frequency error and control effort. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A new power transformer risk modelling considering cumulative surge effects in insulation coordination studies
Abstract: Accurate insulation risk assessment plays a critical role in ensuring the reliability of power transformers, given the significant technical complexities involved in their design. Back flashover failure (BF) caused by lightning overvoltages on incoming substation lines must be considered as an effective stress component in transformer insulation design. These transient surges impose electrical stress on the paper-based insulation system of the transformer. Since such insulation materials are non-self-restoring, the analysis of the voltage–time (V-T) withstand characteristic is essential for insulation risk evaluation. These characteristics are typically derived from laboratory tests on power transformers; however, insulation aging occurring during the testing process may influence the accuracy of the extracted data. In real operating conditions, neglecting aging effects can lead to inconsistencies in insulation coordination. This paper proposes a novel model for correcting aging- deviations in voltage-time (V-T) characteristic curve, enabling a more accurate evaluation of insulation risk. Furthermore, the proposed framework incorporates the cumulative impact of aging in order to estimate the overall insulation risk of the transformer throughout its service life. The findings of this study contribute to safer and more optimized design of power transformers and support improved insulation coordination under realistic operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zeng L.; Tang Y.; Li Y.; Cui W.
Title: Selective ROS generation via engineered electron donor/acceptor sites: Switching photocatalytic oxidation from toxic intermediate to complete mineralization
Abstract: Catalytic oxidation technologies face the challenge of incomplete oxidation, which generates secondary pollutants and undermines environmental benefits. Achieving complete mineralization requires precise steering of reaction pathways, a process fundamentally governed by reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated on the catalyst surface. Herein, we demonstrate that creating localized sites with defined electron-donating or electron-accepting character regulates interfacial charge transfer, thereby directing ROS evolution and final reaction pathway. Using photocatalytic NO oxidation as a model reaction, we engineered ZnO surfaces selectively enriched with donor-type oxygen vacancies (VO) or acceptor-type zinc vacancies (VZn). While both achieved high NO removal efficiency, VZn-rich ZnO produced substantial toxic intermediate NO2 (106.3 ppb), whereas VO-rich ZnO suppressed NO2 to 20.4 ppb. In-situ characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that VZn sites stabilize photogenerated holes, promoting •OH formation and incomplete NO oxidation to NO2. In contrast, VO sites localize electrons, driving O2 activation to •O2− and a deep oxidation pathway to nitrate. The VO-rich catalyst was further immobilized on a porous Al2O3 support, retaining high activity and selectivity with excellent operational stability. This work establishes a fundamental principle for precisely controlling ROS-based reaction pathways, offering a strategy to advance environmental catalytic technologies that maximize conversion efficiency while minimize secondary pollution. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang Y.; Wang H.
Title: Learning Deliverable Wind-Power Capability from Censored SCADA Records for Curtailment-Aware Energy Management
Abstract: Accurate reconstruction of turbine-level available power is essential for active-power dispatch in curtailed wind farms because turbine commands must remain physically deliverable. However, SCADA active power during command-tracking curtailment is constrained by turbine-level set-points and is therefore not an exact observation of available power. This paper formulates reconstruction as a mixed-observation learning problem in which turbine-interval records provide point, lower-bound, interval, or unavailable capability information according to operating state. A wake-coupled spatio-temporal quantile model reconstructs the conditional distribution of latent available power, while local observational support regulates its admission into turbine-level dispatch. The framework is evaluated using 12 months of SCADA, command, status, and event data from three utility-scale wind farms in China. Under 80% controlled censoring, the proposed method achieves an absolute bias of 0.33% and a CRPS of 1.19% of capacity, compared with 0.79% and 1.63% for standard quantile learning. In real curtailed replay, the infeasible-command rate decreases from 7.8% to 4.2% and the non-deliverable ratio from 0.72% to 0.46%. This corresponds to approximately 260 MWh of avoided non-delivered energy per 100 GWh requested and a scenario-based value of CNY 52,000–130,000 (USD 7,700–19,200) under assumed energy values of CNY 200–500/MWh (USD 29.5–73.7/MWh), based on the official RMB central parity rate on 28 August 2026. Release-event, high-curtailment, ablation, and cross-farm experiments further confirm robustness and transferability. The results show that information-consistent treatment of censored SCADA improves capability reconstruction, dispatch reliability, renewable-energy utilization, and operational economic value. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Photovoltaic tilt optimization using physics-informed machine learning methods
Abstract: Photovoltaic arrays are typically installed at a tilt angle, measured from the horizontal plane, close to the site latitude; however, this approach can underperform relative to the physics- or data-driven optimum tilt, resulting in suboptimal energy yields. In this work, we introduce a physics-informed machine learning framework to determine the annual fixed tilt that maximizes energy yield for Antalya, Turkiye. To this end, we process daily irradiance records to derive the diffuse fraction and seasonal harmonics. We use the Liu-Jordan isotropic model to generate a physics-based reference curve and obtain an annual optimum array tilt of 34.75∘. Afterward, we apply machine learning algorithms to a tilt-augmented dataset (0-60∘, in steps of 0.25∘). The best-performing machine learning model yields an incident irradiation of 1,850kWhm−2year−1, which corresponds to an electrical specific yield of 1.57MWhkWp−1year−1 (assuming a performance ratio of 0.85). Finally, all the results provide a robust way to select the tilt angle for optimal system design and to compare data-driven with physics-based models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Energy management systems for hybrid AC/DC microgrids: a problem-oriented review of system challenges and control architectures
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources introduces several system-level challenges for hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs), including power coordination, voltage regulation, uncertainty management, load–demand balancing, and energy storage coordination. Energy management systems (EMS) play a key role in addressing these challenges and ensuring reliable and efficient MG operation. Existing review studies mainly focus on methods and optimization techniques, while system challenges are not always clearly identified or examined from a structured perspective. This paper reviews studies that support system design and the mitigation of operational challenges and presents a comprehensive classification of MGs and EMS. Review and research studies are compiled in separate tables and categorized according to system challenges and the applied EMS approaches. System challenges are identified and related to the control layers responsible for addressing them across primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The proposed classification explicitly covers rule-based, method-based, and objective-based EMS strategies and presents a multi-dimensional framework that links system challenges, control structures, and energy management approaches. The resulting framework provides a consolidated and problem-oriented perspective and supports future research toward the development and evaluation of effective energy management solutions for hybrid AC/DC MGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Sensitivity-factor-based local flexibility market clearing for mixed P-Q services
Abstract: The rapid expansion of distributed photovoltaic generation in low and medium voltage networks is causing increasing voltage limit violations and congestion problems, which distribution system operators must handle. This paper presents a simulation framework for locationally differentiated procurement of flexibility services at distribution level. We demonstrate how controllable active devices connected to low-voltage networks (residential photovoltaic systems, distributed energy storage, flexible consumers) can support voltage control through combined active and reactive power services, and how the bid prices and activation of such flexibility services can be determined by combining bid prices assumed equal to the marginal costs of flexibility assets with network sensitivity factors in a pay-as-bid local flexibility market clearing algorithm. The results demonstrate how the success of market participants in distribution-level clearing depends on their location relative to the network constraints. By embedding sensitivity factors into mathematical optimization, bids are evaluated not only by price but also by their network impact, producing location-dependent bid selection outcomes that reflect physical contribution. This paper highlights how the proposed sensitivity factor framework can provide a computationally efficient mechanism for locational flexibility procurement within the validity range of the applied sensitivity factors, without requiring centralized optimal power flow computations during market clearing. © 2026 The Authors

Title: A physics-informed multi-source signal fusion method for excitation transformer fault diagnosis
Abstract: Excitation transformers are key components of generator excitation systems in power plants and operate under heavy loads, strong electromagnetic interference, and coupled thermal-mechanical stresses, making reliable diagnosis of mechanical loosening, partial discharge, and DC bias faults challenging. To overcome the limitations of conventional single-signal methods in noisy and non-stationary environments, this paper proposes a physics-informed multi-source signal fusion method for excitation transformer fault diagnosis, termed EM-APMSF. The proposed method integrates enhanced Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient features, temperature information, and mechanism-guided relevance information within a unified diagnostic framework. A weighting strategy combining mechanism-guided relevance and entropy-based confidence is introduced to coordinate the relative contributions of acoustic and temperature features during cross-modal fusion. The method was validated using field monitoring data and historical fault records from excitation transformers in a power plant. Comparative and ablation results show that EM-APMSF achieves a diagnostic accuracy of over 95% with an average F1-score of 0.954, outperforming conventional methods by >8% in accuracy. These results support the feasibility of EM-APMSF as an effective framework for excitation-transformer condition monitoring and fault diagnosis under the field conditions represented in the current dataset. © 2026

Title: Simulation-based deep learning for lightning localization using convolutional autoencoder and multilayer perceptron
Abstract: Lightning-induced overvoltages are a major cause of faults and outages in overhead transmission systems, significantly affecting the reliability and operational continuity of power networks. Accurate and timely localization of lightning strikes is therefore essential for improving system monitoring, fault diagnosis, and post-event analysis. In this paper, a simulation-based data-driven approach for two-dimensional lightning localization is proposed using voltage signals induced on transmission lines and evaluated at limited sensor locations. The method combines a convolutional autoencoder (CAE) for feature extraction with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for regression, forming a hybrid deep learning architecture (CAE-MLP) tailored to the nonlinear nature of the localization problem. The framework uses Rusck's analytical formulation to generate waveforms for six line configurations, enabling assessment of topology effects on localization accuracy. No field-measured transmission-line records were used. Compared with CNN, LSTM, and standalone MLP, CAE-MLP achieves the lowest coordinate RMSE in 10 of 12 configuration/axis cases. Across six configurations, its RMSE ranges from 121 to 758 m in the x-coordinate and from 123 to 610 m in the y-coordinate; median two-dimensional error ranges from 150 to 427 m. The results demonstrate in-distribution feasibility using two sensor waveforms under assumptions of an infinite, lossless, single-conductor line above perfectly conducting ground. Archived SNR tests indicate lower sensitivity than comparison models over 5–40 dB. However, because training and testing data were generated by the same idealized model, the results do not establish practical deployment readiness. Validation with measured records or an independent, higher-fidelity electromagnetic model remains necessary. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Directed biosynthesis of the designer peptidyl nucleoside antibiotics featuring a simplified azetidine-containing moiety
Abstract: Fungal and fungal-like pathogen infections pose escalating threats to the global one-health, thus underscoring the urgent need to reverse this trend by accelerating the development of novel antifungal drugs. Polyoxin (POL), a group of structurally related nucleoside antibiotics, is an eco-friendly fungicide targeting fungal cell wall biosynthesis. However, the chemical diversity and therapeutic potential of this antibiotic has remained underexplored. Here, we report the rational design of a series of POL analogs that feature a simplified azetidine-containing moiety, and we have further realized the directed biosynthesis of them using an industrial POL producer as cell factory. Notably, three analogs (POL-AX, POL-HX, and POL-KX), featuring a l -A2CA ( l -azetidine-2-carboxylic acid) moiety, exhibit enhanced inhibitory activity against Candida albicans and even the oomycete plant pathogen Phytophthora sojae . Moreover, systematic molecular docking analyses reveal that the three POL analogs can be better accommodated to the active pocket of the chitin synthases, directly contributing to the improved inhibitory activity of the designer POL analogs. The study provides the basis for the rational access of next-generation agents targeting chitin biosynthesis. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Wu S.; Wang X.
Title: Permanent magnet synchronous motor parameter identification considering nonlinearities based on harmonic suppression and an improved black-winged kite algorithm
Abstract: Aiming at the loss of accuracy and stability in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) parameter identification under voltage source inverter (VSI) nonlinearities, this study develops an improved black-winged kite algorithm with PIR harmonic suppression. First, a PIR controller is used to suppress the sixth-order harmonics of the d-q axis currents. This reduces the adverse effect of VSI nonlinearities on the quality of identification data. Second, a snowmelt factor is introduced to adaptively adjust the position update step in the attack phase, which improves both exploration and exploitation. Finally, a cooperative migration strategy based on Bezier curves is designed to enhance convergence stability and speed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable identification performance under the tested operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Electrostatic and Radio Frequency Performance Optimization of a Triple Metal Gate Hybrid Nanowire Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This paper presents a simulated study on a 2D Asymmetric Gate Stack-Triple Metal Gate-All-Around (AGS-TM-GAA) Nanowire MOSFET with a SiGe-Ge-InGaAs hybrid channel, multi-work function metal gates, and optimally structured high-k dielectric stack (TiO₂/Hf O₂/Si₃N₄). The device has lightly p-doped source/drain, the highly n-doped channel and gate work functions 4.0 eV, 3.9 eV, 4.4 eV to have a greater threshold voltage stability, to lower the potential barriers and to have a better carrier injection. This has been demonstrated to be excellent electrostatic integrity, with steep conduction-band bending ≈-1.5 eV, uniform distribution of fields in the mid-channel ≈1.3-1.5×10⁶ V/m and constant electron mobility ≈8-10 cm2/Vs with ATLAS simulator. The proposed device has the following highest gate-to-drain and gate-coupling capacitances Cgd ≈ 7.5×10-18-2.4×10-19 fF/μm and Cgg ≈ 4.8×10-19 fF/μm, maximum drive current Ids ≈ 5×10-3 A, subthreshold slope 2.2×10-8-1.45×10-9 mV/dec and drain conductance  1×10-9 μS/nm. Short-channel effects, including the variation in threshold-voltage, and degradation of mobility and enhancement of leakage, are substantially reduced due to the GAA, asymmetric gate stack and enhanced quantum confinement. Cut-off frequency (ft), robust FTP behaviour and peak current density are high-frequency metrics that verify the suitability of the architecture to high-speed and Radio Frequency applications. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Zhang R.
Title: Emotional preferences in LoRA-driven AI-generated urban vitality spaces: A study using discrete choice models
Abstract: China's transition toward urban stock renewal has heightened the focus on the emotional quality of urban vitality spaces. While AI generative design offers new approaches, whether AI-generated images as visual representations for specific spaces can meet people's emotional needs remains insufficiently examined. This study examines whether AI-generated visual representations of such spaces evoke image-based emotional preferences comparable to those for real photographs, and identifies which spatial attributes drive these preferences. Using THE BOX in Beijing as a case, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models generated visual representations of seven chosen scenes. Emotional preferences were measured through validated scales completed by 115 participants. A discrete choice model was used to compare participants' preferences between photographs of the real space and AI-generated images and identified influential attributes. Results showed that participants with design-related backgrounds preferred real photographs. Positive affect toward AI-generated images was the strongest predictor of preference. Real-scene color, natural elements, and uniqueness reduced the odds of choosing AI-generated versions, whereas AI-generated form and structure, natural elements, and changeability increased them. The study contributes a replicable workflow linking generative AI with emotional preference measurement, offering a structured approach for evidence-based design review. The findings are preliminary due to the single case, modest sample, and reliance on static images. Future work should extend to diverse urban contexts and multimodal evaluation. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Chen C.; Du L.; Hu Z.; Fang B.; Wan W.; Harada K.; Yuan J.
Title: AVT: Adhesive visual tactile sensor for anthropomorphic and precise manipulation of tiny mechanical components
Abstract: Grasping and manipulation of tiny objects have always been a significant challenge in manufacturing and industrial automation, especially in tasks such as small-part sorting, kitting, and assembly preparation. The tiny size makes it hard for vision systems to detect and locate small pieces with high accuracy. And they offer only limited contact regions for robotic hands to pick. Thus, this study proposes a non-prehensile manipulation method for tiny components based on a developed adhesive visual tactile sensor. This sensor incorporates a transparent adhesive layer with a visual tactile sensor, enabling the picking of multiple pieces using adhesive force while detecting the object types and locating the positions. We developed a two-fingered dexterous robotic hand that mimics intuitive human behavior, utilizing one finger to adhere a tiny component and another finger nail to detach it. The proposed sensor is equipped on the sensor finger, while the other fingertip features a nail structure. Inspired by human behavior, the hand can stick and detect objects using the sensor finger, and detach the picked objects from the adhesive surface to the target positions using the nail finger. We also propose the associated planning methods for finger and robot motions. Experimental results show that the method can effectively classify and organize various scattered tiny components with a classification accuracy of 96.4% and an average positioning error of 0.51 mm, validating the proposed method for manipulating tiny mechanical components in manufacturing applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Dynamic event-triggered hierarchical coordination for TSO-DSO systems: Communication-efficient optimization under practical constraints
Abstract: The proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) demands scalable, communication-efficient coordination between transmission and distribution system operators (TSOs and DSOs). Existing hierarchical methods rely on periodic or iterative exchange, inducing excessive overhead and failing to accommodate network imperfections such as heterogeneous delays and packet dropouts. This paper proposes a three-layer dynamic event-triggered hierarchical coordination (DETHC) framework that transforms TSO-DSO interaction from time-driven to event-driven. An ordinary differential equation (ODE)-governed saturated dynamic threshold determines when DSOs transmit flexibility information, provably eliminating Zeno behavior; flexibility envelopes become event-driven objects refreshed upon state-, prediction-error-, and constraint-proximity triggers; and an event-triggered analytical target cascading (ATC) algorithm with distributed nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) solves the coordination asynchronously within a user-specified iteration bound. Under the assumptions of Section 6 (Lipschitz-bounded flexibility variation, second-order-cone-convexified subproblems, bounded delays, and bounded independent dropouts), Lyapunov analysis establishes practical bounded-error stability for communication delays up to 500 ms and stochastic dropouts. The analysis isolates two findings: a saturated threshold bounds worst-case staleness and the minimum inter-event time by design constants regardless of gain ordering—decoupling suppression aggressiveness from closed-loop stability—and the event-triggering protocol hard-limits the signal exchanged between the communication and optimization layers, so that input-to-state stability certifies the coupled scheme without any small-gain condition. Evaluated on a modified IEEE 30-bus system interconnected with five distribution feeders, DETHC achieves 73.3% communication reduction with only 0.06% optimality gap versus the SOCP-convexified centralized benchmark at the nominal five-DSO operating point, while remaining stable and—under this fixed five-DSO-tuned policy—scalable to 20 DSOs, for which the optimality gap remains below 3.2%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Shen X.; Liu S.; Zhang Y.
Title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. By leveraging large language models to quantify complex external influences and semantic relationships, this framework provides a new perspective for improving the accuracy and interpretability of tourism flow forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang A.; Dong H.
Title: An embedded uncertainty quantification architecture for fuel cell degradation prediction
Abstract: Accurate prediction and credible reliability evaluation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC) performance degradation are critical for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of their integrated energy system. To address the limitations of existing methods, which often employ tightly coupled architectures with poor flexibility and inadequate uncertainty quantification, this study proposes an Embedded Uncertainty-quantification Architecture (EUA). With a modular design, the EUA serves as a plug-and-play module that can be integrated into deep learning time-series models (as baselines) without structural modifications, thereby enhancing local feature extraction and enabling uncertainty quantification. Specifically, the front end of the EUA incorporates a Multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Network (MSTCN) module to extract multi-granularity local features, while the back end employs a Sparse Gaussian Process Regression (SGPR) module to perform efficient probabilistic modeling of the baseline model outputs, thereby generating well-calibrated predictive confidence intervals. An experimental assessment of dynamic PEMFC datasets demonstrated that integrating the EUA with various baseline models not only significantly improved point prediction accuracy (reducing the RMSE by 28 %-49 %) but also provided reliable and tight confidence intervals. The strong generalization and robustness of the EUA were further validated through experiments under multiple load conditions, cross-condition scenarios, and unseen noisy environments. This study provides a plug-and-play prediction framework with built-in uncertainty quantification for PEMFC health management, effectively bridging the uncertainty quantification gap inherent in high-performance point prediction models. © 2026

Authors: Lim S.-S.; Kim G.-H.; Lee J.-O.
Title: Comparative analysis of loss-aware optimal power flow considering droop-controlled inverters
Abstract: The rapid integration of renewable energy sources into distribution networks necessitates advanced voltage regulation strategies, such as smart inverter Volt-VAR droop control with dead-bands. However, conventional linearized optimal power flow (OPF) models frequently overlook network losses, resulting in suboptimal reactive power allocation. This study presents a comparative analysis of three loss-aware OPF formulations tailored for inverter-dominated grids employing piecewise linear droop control. The iterative mixed-integer linear program (MILP) linearizes quadratic loss terms using successive Taylor expansions within a trust-region framework. The mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic program (MIQCQP) relaxes nonconvex loss equalities into convex quadratic inequalities, incorporating a reactive loss penalty. The two-stage MILP + AC-OPF enforces the full nonlinear AC power flow equations as optimization constraints. These formulations are evaluated on a combined IEEE 30-bus and 33-bus transmission–distribution system under four scenarios that vary photovoltaic (PV) capacity, flexible AC transmission system (FACTS) device availability, and inverter reactive power limits, and on a modified 250-bus T118D4 system with 40 PV inverters. The iterative MILP and MIQCQP converge to nearly identical generation costs. The AC-OPF achieves 1.0–2.3% lower generation costs and 5–20% lower reactive power losses through different reactive power allocations. All three formulations yield AC-feasible dispatches, but their reactive power allocations differ substantially, highlighting that AC feasibility alone does not ensure dispatch optimality. On T118D4, the MIQCQP more closely reproduces the AC-OPF voltage and reactive power dispatch, whereas the iterative MILP solves faster, revealing a tradeoff between agreement with the AC-OPF benchmark and computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yu X.; Liu M.
Title: Short-term load forecasting using an improved PatchTST model with time–frequency feature fusion
Abstract: To address the challenges of strong nonlinearity, non-stationary fluctuations, and multi-scale coupling in short-term power load forecasting, this paper proposes MSTF-PatchTST, a novel time–frequency feature fusion model built on the PatchTST framework. The model consists of a wavelet transform convolution (WTConv) frequency branch, a multi-scale temporal convolution (MSTCN) time branch, an improved PatchTST-based encoder, and a feature fusion prediction module. Specifically, the frequency branch captures periodic and multi-scale spectral characteristics through discrete wavelet decomposition and convolutional feature extraction, while the time branch learns local fluctuations and long-term trends via multi-scale temporal convolutions and patch-based global dependency modeling. Subsequently, the representations from both branches are adaptively fused and mapped to the forecasting targets through the TCFNN-based prediction head, enabling effective complementarity between time-domain dynamics and frequency-domain periodicity. Experiments on the Tetouan City power consumption dataset across 1–3 day rolling forecasting horizons demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms GRU, LSTM, TCN, Transformer, Informer, TimesNet, Autoformer, FEDformer, and iTransformer in terms of MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2. The predicted load trajectories closely follow the ground-truth series across all tested horizons, demonstrating both high accuracy and robust generalization as the forecasting horizon extends. © 2026

Title: Direct electron transfer-mediated flow-through electrochemical reductive dechlorination over a 3D self-supporting Co-N3O1 single-atom membrane electrode
Abstract: Electrochemical reductive dechlorination (ERD) represents a sustainable route for eliminating halogenated pollutants, yet its practical application is fundamentally limited by insufficient intrinsic catalytic activity and sluggish interfacial mass transport. Herein, a three-dimensional (3D) self-supporting flow-through membrane electrode incorporating atomically dispersed Co-N3O1 sites (CoSAC-FEM) was developed to synergistically regulate the electronic structure of catalytic sites and convective mass transport, thereby promoting direct electron transfer (DET)-dominated dechlorination. Under microfiltration-coupled electroreduction, the CoSAC-FEM attained > 95% tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP) removal within 60 min, while membrane-thickness optimization enabled a single-pass dechlorination efficiency of 98.3% and a 77-fold enhancement in the mass-normalized rate constant compared with the conventional flow-by electrodle systems. Mechanistic investigations deried from membrane transport analysis, finite-element simulation and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that convective flow-through substantially compresses the diffusion boundary layer to maximize single-atom utilization, while the asymmetric Co-N3O1 coordination optimizes the electronic structure to enhance TCEP adsorption affinity (-0.33 eV) and reduce the C-Cl bond cleavage barrier to 0.17 eV, thereby facilitating DET-dominated dechlorination and simultaneously suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Together with its excellent stability, broad matrix adaptability, negligible Co leaching (0.163 μg L−1) and low operating cost (2.4 CNY t−1), the as-fabricated CoSAC-FEM exhibits a carbon footprint 54.07% lower than that of the flow-by process. This work establishes a general design strategy that integrates electronic-structure engineering with interfacial mass-transfer enhancement for sustainable electrochemical remediation of persistent halogenated micropollutants. © 2026

Title: Harnessing metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs) to regulate the digestive kinetics and enhance gel properties of whey protein gel: The influence on intermolecular interaction force and microstructure
Abstract: Whey protein (WP) has significant applications in the fields of food and nutrition. However, WP has the characteristics of fast digestion rate and a wide range of different gel properties depending on processing history, which limits its application in industrial production. Therefore, in this study, proanthocyanidins and calcium ions were introduced as model polyphenols and metal ions to form a versatile novel material, metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs). MPNs with strong adhesive properties were added to whey protein isolate gel (GWPI) to form MPNs-enhanced GWPI (GWPI@MPNs). This experiment first elucidated the mechanisms by which proanthocyanidins and calcium ions form MPNs and the molecular interactions between MPNs and WP. Then, the effects of adding different proportions of MPNs on the digestion kinetics and gel properties of GWPI@MPNs were determined. The indicators of digestion rate included degree of hydrolysis, digital image of the digestion process, SDS-page, and distribution of polypeptide molecular weight. Gel properties encompassed texture properties, rheological properties, denaturation behaviours, low-field nuclear magnetic resonance, and water-holding capacity. It was found that adding an appropriate amount of MPNs was an effective method to control the digestion rate and enhance the gel properties of GWPI. The mechanism might be that MPNs could enhance the intermolecular forces of WP and make the GWPI form a dense and uniform microstructure. The novel method developed in this research has the potential to contribute to overcoming the inherent limitations of WP and adding a new digestion related functional value for its application in the food industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Norouzi K.; Xu H.; Liu W.
Title: Discrete-time capability-aware multi-rate frequency control of fast and slow distributed energy resources in microgrids
Abstract: This paper presents a discrete-time multi-rate frequency control scheme for a single-bus system comprising a synchronous generator (SG) and an inverter-based resource (IBR). The proposed method coordinates the fast IBR response with the slower SG dynamics using a discrete-time signal derived from the frequency evolution, which captures the required rate of active power variation for frequency regulation. The IBR reference is defined as a combination of frequency-deviation feedback and a rate-dependent term modulated by a smooth activation function, while the SG is governed by a ramp-limited integral control law updated at a slower sampling rate. The resulting control architecture is implemented in a multi-rate framework with distinct fast and slow update loops. A discrete-time model of the closed-loop system is derived and formulated as a singularly perturbed system, in which the IBR tracking dynamics form a contractive fast subsystem and the SG–frequency dynamics evolve on the slow time scale. Practical stability is established by combining a contraction property of the fast subsystem with an input-to-state stability characterization of the slow sampled dynamics. The analysis characterizes the influence of IBR tracking bandwidth, sampling-rate separation, and SG ramp-rate constraints on the closed-loop frequency response. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Similarity-based strategic data allocation for robust PD defect identification in MV cable terminations
Abstract: This paper investigates overfitting caused by overly idealized datasets that fail to capture real-world variability. Four common installation defects in underground cable terminations—improper overlapping of the stress control tube, voids within the insulation layer, carbon tracking on the insulation surface, and irregular edges of the outer semiconductive layer—were physically simulated. Three samples of each defect were fabricated to preserve inherent physical variations. Partial discharge (PD) signals were acquired and transformed into unipolar and bipolar phase-resolved PD (PRPD) patterns. A Residual Neural Network (ResNet-18) was employed for feature extraction and classification. By performing image similarity analysis to strategically allocate training datasets, the model effectively overcomes high intra-class variability, particularly in irregular edge defects. The results demonstrate that bipolar PRPD patterns provide superior diagnostic features compared to unipolar patterns, enabling the optimized ResNet model to improve classification accuracy from 69.81% to 96.50%. This study validates a highly robust, non-intrusive diagnostic framework suitable for practical condition monitoring of field-installed cable terminations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Non-covalent interactions between Lycium barbarum polysaccharides and goat whey protein isolate: Structural changes, odor mitigation and application in yogurt
Abstract: This study investigated the non-covalent interactions between Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP) and goat whey protein isolate (GWPI), as well as the structural modifications of LBP-GWPI complexes, their effects on volatile release associated with goaty flavor, and their application performance in yogurt. The results demonstrated that LBP bound to GWPI via hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions, inducing conformational rearrangement and a more compact microstructure of GWPI. The complexation process disrupted the ordered secondary structure of GWPI without altering its primary structure, with the complexes formed at pH 3 exhibiting stronger intermolecular binding and more compact microstructures. Electronic nose analysis indicated that the complexes modulated the release of volatile compounds associated with goaty flavor, with a greater effect observed at pH 3 than at pH 7. Furthermore, application of the optimized LBP-GWPI complex in goat milk yogurt revealed that it effectively maintained structural stability while significantly improving product quality; the optimal ratio was LBP-GWPI = 1:1, which increased yogurt viscosity by 424% at a shear rate of 0.01 s−1 and water-holding capacity by 18.57% relative to the control group. This study elucidates the structure-function relationships of LBP-GWPI complexes in modulating volatile release, providing a feasible green modification strategy and robust theoretical support for quality enhancement and high-value utilization of goat dairy products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Barrier-Function-Constrained Residual RL-Based Current Control for LCL-Filtered NPC Inverters under Weak-Grid Operation
Abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to grow, grid-connected inverters are increasingly required to operate reliably under weak-grid conditions, where low short-circuit ratios, changing grid impedances, and rapid disturbances reveal the limitations of conventional fixed-gain PI current controllers. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a more adaptive control approach; however, its application to fast inner current loops remains limited by stringent safety requirements and practical rediness challenges. This paper presents a control framework that combines a model-free Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based residual reinforcement learning controller with a model-based Control Lyapunov Function–Control Barrier Function (CLF–CBF) quadratic-program (QP) safety filter for an LCL-filtered three-phase neutral-point-clamped (NPC) grid-connected inverter. Although residual RL and CLF–CBF safety methods have been explored independently, this work integrates a model-free PPO-based residual controller with a model-based CLF–CBF safety filter within a unified architecture for fast inner-loop current control under varying grid-strength and operating conditions. Instead of replacing the conventional PI controller, the residual policy generates bounded corrective voltage commands that complement a fixed PI baseline, while the CLF–CBF–QP safety filter provides analytical enforcement of stability and operational constraints independently of the learned policy. A two-stage training strategy, consisting of unconstrained warm-start followed by safety-constrained fine-tuning, enables efficient policy learning while maintaining safe operation. Evaluated across eight representative operating scenarios with five independent trials per condition, the proposed framework achieves a maximum total harmonic distortion (THD) reduction of 49.7% under extreme thermal stress and 44.2% under nominal operation, with an average THD reduction of 25.7% across all scenarios. The framework also reduces aggregate constraint violations by 35.7% across the evaluated conditions, indicating that the integration of model-free residual reinforcement learning with a model-based CLF–CBF safety layer can improve harmonic performance while providing model-based supervision of current and voltage operating constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Incorporating renewable reactive-power capability curves into multi-objective AC optimal power flow: a comparative assessment of cost, voltage performance, and reactive flexibility
Abstract: In current power systems, the rising use of inverter-based renewable energy sources (RESs) is altering voltage control and reactive-power management. Although photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation units can provide substantial reactive-power support through their power-electronic interfaces, their actual reactive-power capabilities depend on operating conditions and are frequently overlooked or oversimplified in traditional optimal power flow (OPF) formulations. This paper presents a multi-objective AC-OPF framework that explicitly integrates renewable reactive-power capability curves into power-system operation studies. Seven representative capability-curve models are systematically compared within a common optimization framework. The proposed framework simultaneously minimizes generation operating cost, active-power losses, and voltage deviation while maximizing renewable reactive-power flexibility through a Reactive Flexibility Index (RFI). The approach is validated using a modified IEEE 30-bus system with three RESs. The results reveal that renewable reactive-power capability curves greatly influence operational cost, transmission losses, voltage performance, upward and downward renewable reactive-power reserves, and renewable reactive-power flexibility. The Constant Reactive-Power model attains the lowest operating cost and active-power losses, the Triangular model provides the lowest voltage deviation, and the Oversized-Inverter model offers the highest upward and downward renewable reactive-power reserves, the highest RFI, and the highest TOPSIS score. Parameter-sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the principal capability-curve conclusions and demonstrates increasing reactive flexibility with inverter oversizing. These results highlight the importance of accurately representing renewable reactive-power capability when assessing the operational flexibility and voltage performance of renewable-integrated power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A multi-mode active frequency support strategy for a grid-friendly integrated PV-ES system
Abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage (ES) is an effective solution to mitigate PV output fluctuations and enhance solar energy utilization. However, existing PV-ES coordination schemes are often limited by insufficient consideration of source-side support capability, grid-side frequency demands, and source-grid interaction. These systems typically operate in a passive manner, merely complying with grid codes rather than actively supporting the grid, thereby limiting the development of power systems with high penetration of renewable energy. To address these limitations, this paper makes the following contributions. First, theoretical analysis reveals that the dual-stage PV system possesses inherent advantages in active frequency support due to its wide-range power regulation capability, which provides a topological guideline for designing grid-friendly integrated PV-ES systems. Second, the active frequency support performance of the PV-ES system is enhanced by optimizing the reserved capacity of the energy storage system. It is theoretically proved that state-of-charge (SOC) balancing among ES units can maximize the system's transient frequency support capability. Third, a multi-mode active frequency support strategy that simultaneously considers grid-side and source-side requirements is proposed. It enables a coordinated and flexible interaction between the grid and PV-ES system, achieving a balance between active support and economic operation. Experimental validation confirms that the proposed control strategy is both feasible and effective. © 2026

Title: A tri-objective goal programming approach to generator maintenance scheduling
Abstract: The generator maintenance scheduling problem is a key decision-making task in power system planning, requiring schedules that ensure reliability while controlling operational costs. Motivated by reliability challenges and financial constraints in systems such as South Africa's, this paper proposes a tri-objective optimisation framework that simultaneously minimises generator failure probability, production cost, and reserve margin. The model is formulated using goal programming to balance these competing objectives and is solved using simulated annealing and constraint programming. It is evaluated on the IEEE reliability test system and a large-scale Eskom-inspired system with 157 generating units. The results characterise trade-offs among reliability, cost, and reserve margin objectives, approximate a Pareto frontier, and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a decision-support tool for practical generator maintenance planning. © 2026 The Authors
